On the law of value, Fuchs extends Marx to fill the "labour blind spot" in the political economy of communication, whereas Hardt and Negri hold that unified labour time has dissolved and value cannot be fixed in time units. Mo judges that "immaterial labour" is the broader concept, while digital labour faces the difficulty of explaining how the digital generates labour. The two approaches represent the objective and subjective dimensions of Marxism's development. Mo calls for drawing on and criticising both to analyse new labour forms, exploitation, resistance and the possibilities of sharing. Read the original if you want a brief Chinese-language comparison of Fuchs with Hardt and Negri on labour and value.
quoteEn: In terms of approach, the two reflect the difference between the objective dimension and the subjective dimension in the development of Marxism.
quoteZh: 从进路上看，两者又体现了马克思主义发展过程中客体向度和主体向度的区别。

t: Digital labour from the perspective of Marx's view of labour
zh: 马克思劳动观视域下的数字劳动
source: Chinese Social Sciences Today (Zhongguo shehui kexue bao), 22 August 2024
paras: Li Suiyue takes up a dispute in the study of digital labour: what the concept includes and excludes, and whether such labour is productive. The article argues that Marx's view of labour, applied through dialectical and historical materialism, can fix the concept's boundaries. Without this, Li warns, digital labour is stretched, trivialised or treated as play, and the common features of labour and its essence are lost.

This short commentary, first published in a Chinese newspaper, has three parts. It begins by criticising two Western approaches to defining digital labour. It then sets out four general features of labour that any digital activity must meet. Finally it describes what is distinctively digital about this form of labour and offers a typology of real digital workers.

Li identifies two errors in Western scholarship. Tiziana Terranova's line of thought, which Li links to terms such as audience labour and play labour, treats internet users' online consumption as labour and so produces the error of "going online is labour". Christian Fuchs's approach counts everything tied to the digital value chain, including mining and hardware manufacture, and drifts towards "all labour is digital labour". Against both, Li draws on Marx to say that an activity is labour only if it is purposeful, productive, work-like and creative. Users' browsing traces are, in Li's account, a "behavioural surplus" outside any purpose, whereas annotators and programmers labour purposefully. On the digital side, the means of labour must be substantively digital rather than merely related to digital technology. Gig workers such as delivery riders and ride-hailing drivers therefore remain traditional labourers.

Li concludes that real digital labour falls into two types. The first is the work of software engineers, algorithm designers, game developers, web designers and system maintainers. The second is cultural creation by digital means, such as an online novelist writing and uploading a novel. Only by grasping both the labour character and the digital character of this work, Li argues, can scholarship avoid the theoretical and practical confusion of a "pan-digital labour". Read the original if you want a compact Chinese Marxist argument for narrowing the definition of digital labour, set against Terranova and Fuchs.
quoteEn: Digital labour stresses substantive \"digitalisation\" rather than merely associated \"digitalisation\".
quoteZh: 数字劳动强调的是实质性“数字化”而非关联性“数字化”。

t: Two dimensions of the fusion of horizons between Marxism and biopolitics
zh: 马克思主义与生命政治学视域融合的两个维度
paras: Why can Marxism and biopolitics (the study of how power takes human life and populations as its object) be brought into a shared horizon? In this short piece, first published in China Social Sciences Today in September 2024, Lin Qing argues that the two share an underlying logic: both centre on the capitalist mode of production and the governmentality it requires.

The article is organised around two dimensions. The first concerns how the internal requirements of capitalist production, in particular the shift from absolute to relative surplus value, produce a politicisation of life. The second concerns the 'materiality' of power, drawing on Michel Foucault's reading of Marx.

On the first dimension, Lin notes that Foucault ties biopolitics to liberalism, but holds that its original context lies in capitalist production. Absolute surplus value, obtained by lengthening the working day, meets natural limits of the body. Relative surplus value therefore requires care for population and labour-power, including raising workers' quality, and Lin cites Marx's remark that the state must legislate to force basic sanitation on capitalism. For Lin, Capital does not treat this theme explicitly but supplies the premise for understanding biopolitics. On the second dimension, Foucault criticises analyses that locate power in the state apparatus and ideology as 'Rousseauising' Marx, and Lin links this to Marx's Critique of the Gotha Programme. Foucault finds in Capital four features of power: plural, not derived from sovereignty, productive rather than prohibitive, and technical, as in the factory.

Lin concludes that biopolitics cannot be understood from its own concepts alone, and that changes in the capitalist mode of production explain its emergence. Power's materialism, in Foucault's reading of Marx, lies in concrete sites such as the factory rather than the state apparatus. Read the original if you want a brief account of how a Chinese scholar connects Foucault's biopolitics to Marx's analysis of relative surplus value and factory power.
quoteEn: Without the needs of relative surplus value production, the attention to, care for and regulation of the population that biopolitics displays could not have emerged.
quoteZh: 如果没有在相对剩余价值生产维度的需要，生命政治学所展示的对人口的关注、呵护与调整就不可能出现。

t: A dialectical view of the relationship between Marx's philosophy and biopolitics
zh: 辩证地看待马克思哲学与生命政治学的关系
paras: As biopolitics has become a popular topic in Chinese scholarship on Western left theory, this short commentary (first published in China Social Sciences Today, 2024) asks how it relates to Marx's philosophy. Wang Haifeng argues that the relation should be seen dialectically, by comparing the two in theme, content and orientation. In Wang's view, biopolitics continues Marx's critique of capitalism but takes a different path and offers a different solution.

The article is organised in three steps, each matching one point of comparison: the shared theme of capitalist critique, the different understanding of "life", and the proposed routes to human emancipation. It draws mainly on Foucault, Hardt, Negri, Agamben and Esposito for biopolitics, and on Marx's 1844 Manuscripts, The German Ideology and Capital.

Wang holds that, following Althusser's idea of a "problematic", biopolitics shares Marx's underlying problem even though its authors rarely cite him. It extends critique to micro-level power over populations, health and birth rates beyond the factory. For Marx, by contrast, life is always social and historical, tied to wage labour, surplus value and the logic of capital. This leads to different solutions. Agamben looks to a messianic "remnant" and Negri to irreducible singularity, whereas Marx locates the root of power over life in capital and calls for overturning capitalist social relations in favour of communism.

Wang concludes that biopolitics widens the critical path Marx opened and enriches world Marxist theory. The article adds that the issues, resources and methods of Western Marxism offer lessons for building a contemporary Chinese Marxist philosophy able to address problems of Chinese modernization. Read the original if you want a brief Chinese Marxist assessment of how biopolitics is positioned against Marx.
quoteEn: Rather than saying that Marx valued "life", it is better to say that he valued the sociality and historicity of life.
quoteZh: 与其说马克思重视的是“生命”，不如说重视的是生命的社会性和历史性。

glossary.explanation: An official concept for China's path of modernization, promoted by the Communist Party especially since the 20th Party Congress (2022) as distinct from Western models.
A field of theory associated with Michel Foucault that studies how modern states manage populations and bodies through health, birth rates and similar mechanisms.

t: Extending and exceeding: biopolitics and political philosophy
zh: 拓展与跃出：生命政治学与政治哲学
source: China Social Sciences Today (Zhongguo shehui kexue bao), 19 September 2024
paras: Zheng Yuchen asks how biopolitics, the field Michel Foucault developed, relates to political philosophy, a question on which scholars disagree. Citing Roberto Esposito, Zheng notes that Foucault's work shifted the whole framework of political philosophy. The article argues that biopolitics extends the classical framework and in part exceeds it. This newspaper essay appeared in 2024.

The piece has three parts. It first outlines biopolitics' micro and macro dimensions and the debate over its status. It then compares the basic questions of biopolitics and political philosophy, and ends by assessing biopolitics' philosophical significance. Thinkers discussed include Foucault, Antonio Negri, Michael Hardt, Giorgio Agamben, Jacques Rancière and Esposito.

Zheng argues that Anglo-American and continental political philosophy share one basic question, what a good common life is, but stress different mechanisms: coordination (rights, justice) versus coercion (sovereignty, the state of exception). With capitalism, the economy became central to politics, turning politics into biopolitics. Zheng contends that biopolitics finds hidden coercion inside liberalism's soft coordinating mechanisms, which are guaranteed by a sovereign 'night-watchman' able to declare exceptions. Biopolitics therefore belongs to the continental tradition. Its micro dimension carries power analysis into non-political fields such as medicine, culture and technology.

Zheng concludes that the macro dimension joins classical debates by deconstructing them. The micro dimension leans towards social theory, and whether it counts as political philosophy remains contested and unresolved. Read the original if you want a compact Chinese-language map of how biopolitics is positioned against political philosophy, including the positions of Chinese scholars such as Lan Jiang and Xia Ying.
quoteEn: Biopolitics focuses on the coercive operation of power, and with a new research paradigm it extends and goes beyond the existing framework of classical political philosophy.
quoteZh: 生命政治学着重考察了权力的强制性作用，以新的研究范式拓展并跃出了经典政治哲学的既有框架。

t: Marx's view of machines in the perspective of the history of philosophy
zh: 哲学史视域中的马克思机器观
paras: Deng Pan asks where Marx's view of machines came from and what it added to earlier philosophy. The article, originally published in the Chinese Social Sciences Today in August 2024, argues that this view was both a product and a scientific summing-up of nineteenth-century technological development. It also contends that the view is closely tied to Aristotle, Descartes and Hegel, and that Marx ultimately went beyond all three.

The piece has two main parts. The first traces the philosophical history of tools and machines. It runs from Aristotle's treatment of the hand, stage machinery and mechanics, through medieval and early modern clock metaphors (Nicholas of Cusa, Ficino, Comenius, Descartes, La Mettrie, Christian Wolff), to Hegel's natural philosophy and his early and late social writings. The second part turns to Marx's treatment of tools and machines in Capital, his reading of contemporary engineering literature, and his Notebooks on Machinery and Technology.

Deng argues that Aristotle did not clearly separate tool from machine, that Descartes turned the body into an automaton, and that Hegel distinguished the two. On Deng's reading, Hegel's Jena manuscripts criticise machines for making labour abstract and devalued, whereas the Philosophy of Right credits them with raising productivity. For Marx, by contrast, tools and machines are first of all means of producing surplus value, so their analysis rests on the social and historical conditions of their use. Deng reports that Marx divided developed machinery into motive machine, transmission mechanism and tool machine, and compared this scheme with Moritz Rühlmann's 1862 textbook. For Marx a true machine system exists where a series of complementary tool machines is driven by a central automaton, and Deng calls this the most developed form of machine production. Unlike manufacture, such a system fixes the production process by the machine rather than by the worker's habits, and runs continuously and automatically.

Deng concludes that Marx drew on Aristotle and Hegel but surpassed them. Marx moved from Aristotle's technical analysis based on the circle to a view grounded in relations of production, and his conditions for building machines are said to have prepared the ground for later modular, geometric-constraint design associated with Reuleaux. The article adds that Capital set out these ideas systematically and went on to influence German philosophy of technology in the second half of the nineteenth century. Read the original if you want a compact account of the philosophical lineage behind Marx's concepts of the tool machine and the machine system.
quoteEn: The core of Marx's discourse on machines is a detailed examination of the social and historical conditions under which tools and machines are used.
quoteZh: 马克思的机器话语核心要义是详细考察使用工具和机器的社会历史条件。

t: The self and the subject from the perspective of the materialist conception of history
zh: 唯物史观视域中的自我与主体
paras: Since the beginning of idealist philosophy, the question of the self and the riddle of the subject, especially the problem of their inner consistency, have remained a persistent difficulty. In this short piece, first published in the Chinese Social Sciences Today in August 2024, Sun Lin argues that only Marx, through the materialist conception of history, unified self and subject on real ground, both historically and logically. In Sun's reading, Marx's critique of idealism is at the same time a critique of the modernity of capital.

The article traces a sequence of idealist attempts to join self and subject: Descartes, Kant, Fichte and Hegel. Each section sets out the thinker's position and then gives the verdict of the materialist conception of history. The final section turns to Marx's own solution, built around the self-activity of the real subject.

Sun's account runs as follows. Descartes places self and subject together in a spiritual substance, but his dualism of mind and body leaves them split. Kant separates self-consciousness (theory) from free will (practice), so the subject can encompass the self but not the reverse. Fichte derives the categories from the self's own positing and so merges the two principles, but his self cannot explain concrete, varied reality. Hegel makes the externalisation and reclaiming of self-consciousness in social interaction the basis of subjectivity. For Sun, however, this unity is wrapped in the 'absolute' and so turns illusory.

Sun's central move is to read Hegel's logic of objectification as homologous to the logic of capital: capital goes outwards, captures profit and surplus value, and returns to itself as self-valorising capital, which is the subjectivity of things. The consistency of self and subject in Hegel is therefore, Sun argues, a false unity produced by fetishism, in which relations between people become relations between things. The materialist conception of history instead raises the speculative subject to a real subject whose self-activity achieves historically conditioned consistency. Sun concludes that under capitalist private ownership this requires raising productive forces to break through fetishism and raising labour capacity to overcome objectified labour, moving towards a society of the free and all-round development of every person. Read the original if you want a concise Chinese Marxist account of how the materialist conception of history positions itself against Descartes, Kant, Fichte and Hegel on selfhood and subjectivity.
quoteEn: The materialist conception of history raises the speculative subject to a real subject that always lies beyond mere appearance, and through its own objectifying activity, that is, the self-activity of the real subject, achieves a historically conditioned inner consistency of subject and self.
quoteZh: 唯物史观把思辨的主体提升为始终浮现在表象之外的实在主体，通过自身的对象化活动也就是实在主体的自我活动，实现主体与自我有历史条件的内在一致性。

glossary.explanation: The Marxist theory that social life and historical change are grounded in material production and social relations. In Chinese scholarship it is the usual term for historical materialism.
The Chinese term for philosophical idealism, here covering German idealism and its Cartesian precursors.
Marx's term for the way social relations between people appear as relations between things, as with the commodity and capital.
A term used in Chinese Marxist scholarship for modernity as shaped by the logic of capital, which Marx's critique is read as targeting.

t: Hegel's thought on labour examined from the standpoint of historical materialism
zh: 黑格尔劳动思想的唯物史观考察
source: Chinese Social Sciences Today (中国社会科学报), 8 August 2024
paras: Zhang Donghui and Li Chunxiao ask what Hegel's account of labour contributed to the later materialist critique of political economy, even though his philosophy remained objective idealism. Their answer is that, in analysing modern civil society through labour, Hegel grasped the essence of labour from the standpoint of modern political economists. The authors argue that his treatment of the division of labour, tools and machines, and value and money shows clear tendencies towards historical materialism. They note that Lenin and Lukács also saw it as laying groundwork for Marx's social critique.

The article, a short piece first published in a Chinese newspaper in 2024, proceeds in four sections: labour and the division of labour; labour and machines; value as abstract labour; and a closing assessment of Hegel's limits. It draws on Hegel's Jena writings (the System of Ethical Life and the First Philosophy of Spirit) and the Philosophy of Right. It also reads him alongside Adam Smith, Adam Ferguson and Marx's 1844 manuscripts.

The authors argue that Hegel, following Smith, saw the division of labour making labour and needs increasingly abstract. In their account he saw that it separated labour from its purpose, simplified work into mechanical routines and shaped human subjectivity. Hegel also held that tools mediate between humans and nature and that machines make labour 'lifeless', turning workers into appendages and producing alienation and extreme poverty. The authors say he optimistically expected machines to free up time. On value, they report that Hegel distinguished use-value from value, treated value as abstract labour and as a social relation among private labours, and saw money as a social relation, which Lukács read as anticipating fetishism. They add that he proposed state regulation of civil society, for example through taxation, to counter the pursuit of wealth.

The authors conclude that Hegel's limits are plain next to Marx. In their reading, he never entered the terrain of political economy or distinguished concrete from abstract labour. He therefore described alienated labour only empirically, did not see all labour under commodity production as alienated, and did not grasp capital's domination over labour. They add that he did not understand labour as a mode of production through which social formations and historical laws can be grasped. Read the original if you want a concise account of how Hegel's views on labour, machinery and value are read as precursors to Marx's critique of political economy.
quoteEn: Nor did he understand labour as a mode of production, and so grasp social formations and historical laws through the mode of production.
quoteZh: 他也没有把劳动当作生产方式来理解，进而通过生产方式来把握社会形态和历史规律。

t: François Furet on historical materialism and the French Revolution
zh: 傅勒论唯物史观与法国大革命
paras: This short commentary, first published in China Social Sciences Today in August 2024, introduces François Furet's book Marx et la Révolution française (Marx and the French Revolution). Zhu explains that Furet, a leading twentieth-century French historian, wrote it to rebut the simplified, dogmatic and teleological historiography of the dominant French school of Albert Soboul, Claude Mazauric and others. Zhu's account is that Furet sought to show a basic difference between Marx and his later French followers.

The article follows Furet's collection and analysis of Marx's main statements on the Revolution from 1842 to 1871. It is organised around two questions: how Marx understood the relation between the French Revolution and social revolution (the problem of the 'second revolution'), and the autonomy of politics. It takes in the young Marx, the period after the formation of historical materialism, and the years of Capital.

In Zhu's reading of Furet, the young Marx derived the idea of the Revolution as the 'matrix' of social revolution from his own reading and from German backwardness. He did not revere Jacobin dictatorship, and he recognised the state's independence only in the form of 'alienation' or 'illusion'. After his turn to historical materialism, Furet finds a tension: in theory the Revolution was the necessary product of social production, but in practice revolutionary action itself becomes decisive. Furet also finds that Marx reduced the many regimes of France to different bourgeois class fractions, and that his analysis of the Second Empire deduced economic and social evolution from political history.

Zhu concludes that the young Marx's views and his later ones do not contradict each other, and that Marx grounded the 'second revolution' in revolutionary practice. Historical materialism, Zhu argues, cannot be applied mechanically but must be tied to concrete historical situations. Zhu also calls for keeping socio-economic development and the productive forces as the starting point of all undertakings. Read the original if you want a brief Chinese-language introduction to Furet's critique of Marx's account of the French Revolution.
quoteEn: On important questions such as social revolution, historical materialism cannot be applied mechanically to historical explanation, and analysis must proceed from the concrete historical situation.
quoteZh: 在诸如社会革命等重要问题上，唯物史观不能机械地运用到历史解释之中，而必须根据具体的历史情境展开分析。

t: Engels's late-life guidance of the British workers' movement
zh: 恩格斯晚年指导英国工人运动的实践历程
paras: This short commentary, published in China Social Sciences Today in August 2024, asks how Engels, who led no national or international organisation in his last years, still shaped the British workers' movement. Liu argues that he acted as an intellectual and practical mentor to its most advanced figures, chiefly in two areas: the New Unionism and the founding of an independent working-class party.

The article opens with Britain's place in the history of socialism and the decline of Chartist radicalism into trade unionism. It then treats two cases in turn: Engels's 1881 articles and the Marxist-led New Unionism of the late 1880s, and his advice on party-building to figures such as Mahon, Burns, Mann, Hardie and Aveling.

Liu argues that Engels identified the limits of trade unionism, which sought only a "fair day's wage" and favoured a labour aristocracy. In his Labour Standard articles he named wage labour itself as the root of the problem and called for workers' ownership of the means of labour and for independent political organisation. Liu credits Marxists with leading the 1889 London dock strike, after which union membership is said to have risen from 860,000 to nearly two million. On party-building, Liu holds that British labour's dependence on the Liberals was the main obstacle. The Independent Labour Party (1893) later drifted into reformism, which Liu reads as proof that a workers' party cannot succeed without scientific socialism.

Liu concludes that Engels guided British workers by indirect means: letters, newspaper articles and programmatic advice. He thereby carried on the work he and Marx had begun, and Liu says he deserves the title of the modern proletariat's most outstanding scholar and teacher. Read the original if you want a brief overview of Engels's correspondence with British labour leaders and the Chinese framing of his late role.
quoteEn: The development of the Independent Labour Party proves that, without accepting scientific socialism as its theoretical basis, establishing a working-class party will not succeed.
quoteZh: 独立工党的发展证明了如果不接受科学社会主义作为理论基础，建立工人阶级政党是不会成功的。

t: The scholarly logic of Engels's research on scientific socialism
zh: 恩格斯科学社会主义研究的学理逻辑
paras: This short commentary, first published in the Chinese Social Sciences Today in August 2024, asks how Engels studied scientific socialism and what that method offers present-day research. Zhang argues that Engels upheld Marxism's basic method while building specific methodological principles suited to scientific socialism, and so carried Marxism a considerable step forward.

The article distinguishes two levels of Engels's method. One concerns scientific socialism as theory, including its place within the whole of Marxism. The other concerns it as practical movement and institutional form, including the general laws, principles and paths of social development. Zhang adds a third element, the personal qualities Engels demanded of researchers.

On the theoretical side, Zhang says Engels treated dialectics, epistemology and logic as identical, required full command of concrete material, and warned against quoting out of context. Each principle of scientific socialism, in this reading, must be linked historically to other principles and to concrete experience, so that dogmatism is avoided. On the practical side, Engels made historical materialism the foundation and dialectics the mediation for grasping capitalism's tendency towards self-negation. Zhang adds that class analysis, with class struggle as the main thread, stayed central for Engels even late in life. Engels also asked that researchers be diligent learners rather than hunters of new phrases.

Zhang draws five lessons for research on adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times. They are to start from the changed principal contradiction in Chinese society, to keep a people-centred stance, to study the logical starting point of Chinese Marxism, to document its methodology, and to adopt a rigorous, truth-seeking attitude. Read the original if you want a brief Chinese-language statement of how Engels's methodological remarks are mobilised for current theoretical work.
quoteEn: Class analysis, especially taking class struggle as a main thread for observing class society, was a basic methodological principle to which Engels consistently adhered.
quoteZh: 阶级分析法尤其是以阶级斗争作为观察阶级社会的一条主要线索，是恩格斯始终坚持的基本方法论原则。

glossary.zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化
glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
glossary.explanation: Official formula for the Party's project of fitting Marxist theory to China's conditions and contemporary requirements. The article itself uses the shorter form "Sinification of Marxism".

t: Engels's critique of erroneous currents of thought
zh: 恩格斯对错误思潮的批判
paras: This short commentary, first published in China Social Sciences Today in August 2024, argues that the history of Marxism is also a history of struggle against erroneous theories. Zhang and Zhou contend that many of Marxism's classic ideas took shape through polemics, and that Engels was not only a founder and developer of Marxism but also its loyal defender.

The article reviews four of Engels's critiques in turn: Proudhonism, Bakuninism (anarchism), Dühringism and dogmatism about economic determination. It follows them from the 1840s to the late nineteenth century.

On Proudhon, the authors say Engels exposed reformist schemes that left capitalism intact and prepared the ground for Marx's The Poverty of Philosophy and for Marxism's guiding role in the First International. Against Bakunin, Engels held that the state would fall once capital was abolished and the whole mode of production transformed, and that urging workers to abandon politics was mistaken. The Hague Congress of 1872 expelled Bakunin. In Anti-Dühring, the authors write, Engels attacked Dühring's philosophy, economics and socialism, and thereby set out Marxism's three component parts as one organic whole. Against the dogmatists, Engels held that the economic factor is decisive only "in the last instance", and he affirmed the relative independence of ideology.

The authors conclude that Engels defended and developed Marxism after Marx's death by taking on non-Marxist currents. They hold that surveying these critiques helps consolidate Marxism's guiding position in the ideological sphere and is the best way to commemorate Engels. Read the original if you want a brief, Party-oriented overview of Engels's polemics and the lessons Chinese scholars draw from them.
quoteEn: Engels was not only a founder and developer of Marxism, but also its loyal defender.
quoteZh: 恩格斯不仅是马克思主义的创立者、发展者，更是马克思主义的忠诚捍卫者。

t: A scientific understanding and grasp of Engels's view of authority
zh: 科学理解与把握恩格斯权威观
paras: This short commentary, published in the Chinese Social Sciences Today in August 2024, asks what Engels's view of authority offers for upholding the authority of the Party Central Committee. Li argues that Engels, in struggles against erroneous ideas inside and outside the working class, set out why authority matters for production and revolution, what it scientifically means, and how it relates to obedience and autonomy. Li holds that this has direct significance for the current stage of building a modern socialist country.

The article draws mainly on Engels's Anti-Dühring and "On Authority". It is organised in three sections: why upholding the Central Committee's authority is the basic guarantee of building a modern socialist country; why the key lies in the leader's core position; and why the root lies in combining institutional authority with the authority of the rule of law.

Li reads Engels as showing that authority is an objective necessity of social development, illustrated by cotton mills and railways, and as criticising anarchists who reject all authority. Li links this to the 14th Five-Year Plan period, when a complex environment calls for the Central Committee to supply guidance, leadership and mobilisation. Li treats "core" and "leader" as closely related, quoting Engels's ship-in-danger example, and argues that a party gains cohesion only by establishing and defending its leading core, namely Xi Jinping. Li adds that obedience increasingly rests on consent, with democratic and consultative elements.

Li concludes that Central Committee authority depends on the Four Consciousnesses, the Four-sphere Confidence and the Two Upholds, and above all on institutions and law. Perfecting the basic political system and the constitution-centred legal system would embed legal authority in political authority. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Engels's "On Authority" is used in Party-theoretical argument for upholding central leadership.
quoteEn: The key to upholding the authority of the Party Central Committee lies in upholding the leader's core position.
quoteZh: 维护党中央权威的关键在于维护领袖的核心地位。

glossary.explanation: A Party formula, prominent since 2018, calling on members to uphold Xi Jinping's core position on the Central Committee and in the Party as a whole, and to uphold the Central Committee's authority and centralised, unified leadership.
Confidence in the path, theory, system and culture of socialism with Chinese characteristics.
A Party slogan urging members to keep political awareness, to think in terms of the big picture, to follow the leadership core and to keep in line with the Central Committee.
China's national economic and social development plan for 2021–2025, issued together with the long-range objectives to 2035.

t: Three important documents in "Engels on China" and their theoretical value
zh: “恩格斯论中国”的三篇重要文献及其理论价值
paras: Wang Donghong, in a short commentary first published in the Chinese Social Sciences Today in 2024, argues that research on what Marx and Engels wrote about China needs a full inventory of the texts. Existing thematic compilations, the author says, are selections rather than complete collections. Wang counts at least 80 works by Engels on China between 1839 and 1894, and presents three that are absent from the 2015 edition of Marx and Engels on China and have not been studied.

The article is organised around three texts. These are the early political essay Letters from the Wuppertal (1839), the dictionary entry "Burmah" (1858) written for The New American Cyclopaedia, and "A Newly Discovered Case of Group Marriage" (1892). Wang also notes Engels's passing references to China in letters of 1840 and in the 1842 work on Schelling.

Wang reads the 1839 essay's mention of Chinese script as the earliest sign of Engels's interest in China, earlier than the 1845 Elberfeld speech that scholars usually cite. On "Burmah", Wang summarises its account of the China–Burma border, trade goods and religious differences. Wang adds that Engels's letters to Marx show how laborious the short entry was, which Wang takes as evidence of a scientific and rigorous approach. In the 1892 piece, Engels translated a Russian report that described the Giliak people as long subject to "China-ised" Manchus. Wang suggests this anthropological use of "China-ised" may help trace the origin of the concept of adapting Marxism to the Chinese context.

Wang concludes that these texts enrich research on Engels's life and work and on the Marx–Engels relationship. The author also draws from the 1892 translation, with its more than ten alterations for German readers, an image of Engels as a translator. Wang presents the "Burmah" entry as relevant to the history and prospects of the Southwest Silk Road. Read the original if you want a bibliographic pointer to little-studied Engels texts that mention China.
quoteEn: The term "China-ised" thus appears in Engels with an anthropological and ethnological meaning, directly linked to the thought of Marx and Engels, and this offers guidance and even a signpost for tracing the origin of the concept of the "sinicization of Marxism".
quoteZh: “中国化”一词就在恩格斯那里以人类学、民族学的含义直接与马克思、恩格斯的思想联系到了一起，这为溯源“马克思主义中国化”概念提供了导引乃至路标。

glossary.zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化
glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context
glossary.explanation: Official formula for applying Marxism to Chinese conditions and developing it there. The article speaks of the earlier form "Marxism's sinicization" and looks for its conceptual origin in Engels.

t: On Engels's "three greats"
zh: 论恩格斯的“三个伟大”
paras: Marking the 200th anniversary of Friedrich Engels's birth, this commentary (first published in China Social Sciences Today, 18 August 2024) proposes three headings for understanding him: a great life, a great character and great contributions. Wang Yonghe argues that Engels, together with Marx, supplied the proletariat and humanity with Marxism as their strongest intellectual weapon.

The piece is short and organised under the three headings. It first outlines Engels's biography (1820–1895) and his path from a bourgeois family in the Rhine Province to the workers' movement. It then turns to his friendship with Marx and his modesty, and finally lists his theoretical contributions.

On life, Wang stresses his two years living among workers in Manchester, which produced The Condition of the Working Class in England (1845). On character, Wang points to his financial support for Marx, his postponement of work on Dialectics of Nature to edit Marx's manuscripts, and his remark that he played "second violin". Wang cites Lenin on the friendship. On contributions, Wang names five: co-founding Marxism's basic theory; editing volumes two and three of Capital; systematising Marxism by integrating historical and dialectical materialism and naming "scientific socialism"; original work in philosophy, political economy and socialist theory; and defending Marxism against dogmatic readings and economic determinism.

Wang concludes that Engels's life, character and contributions deserve remembrance, study and respect. Read the original if you want a brief, Lenin-based overview of how Chinese commentary presents Engels's role beside Marx on his bicentenary.
quoteEn: Engels's life was a life of exploring and founding scientific theory for the liberation of the proletariat and humanity, of unceasing struggle to transform the old world and build a new one, and of giving everything to seeking and defending truth.
quoteZh: 恩格斯的一生，是为无产阶级和人类解放探索创立科学理论的一生，是为改造旧世界建立新世界战斗不止的一生，是为追求真理捍卫真理奉献所有的一生。

t: Rethinking the Marxist view of progress
zh: 重新认识马克思主义进步观
source: Chinese Social Sciences Today (中国社会科学报), 11 May 2024
paras: Zhao Song takes up the charge, made by some Western scholars, that Marx was a "progressivist" whose view of history is metaphysical. The article, a short commentary from the Chinese Social Sciences Today, argues that this reading misrepresents Marxism. Zhao contends that the Marxist view of progress is neither an eschatological "end of history" thesis nor a linear theory, because it is built on real human beings and their activity.

The article first sets out two Western readings. Fukuyama is presented as equating Marx with Hegel in positing a final historical goal, with communism as Marx's endpoint. Sean Sayers is cited as treating Marx's theory as linear, a succession of stages each replaced by a higher one. Zhao then answers each reading in turn, drawing on passages from Marx and on Fredric Jameson.

On the first point, Zhao concedes that Marx's images of a "free association" and a "realm of freedom" suggest a goal. Even so, Zhao argues that history has no preset purpose of its own: purposes belong to human activity, so history cannot end while people exist. Communism is therefore a new beginning, the end of "prehistory", as Jameson puts it. On the second point, Zhao holds that Marx's late study of "Eastern societies" and his reply to Mikhailovsky rejected a single path for all nations. The article also argues that linear progress presupposes a super-historical subject such as Hegel's spirit, whereas Marx made real, living people the agents of history. Zhao describes the Marxist view as a spiral that unites the diversity of historical paths with general laws.

Zhao concludes that equating Marxism with these forms of progressivism betrays its human-centred starting point. A correct understanding, Zhao argues, has to begin from the human dimension and recognise the irreplaceable position of real people in historical progress. Read the original if you want a concise Chinese-language rebuttal of Fukuyama-style and linear readings of Marx, along with the passages from Marx it relies on.
quoteEn: Therefore, the purpose Marx speaks of is not a purpose of history itself, but human activity.
quoteZh: 因此，马克思所说的目的并非历史本身的目的，而是人的活动。

t: The dual logic of Marx's theory of social progress
zh: 马克思社会进步理论的双重逻辑
source: China Social Sciences Today (Zhongguo shehui kexue bao), 11 May 2024
paras: This short piece in China Social Sciences Today asks how Marx's theory of social progress relates to the Enlightenment philosophy of history from which it grew. Zhang argues that the theory contains a dual logic. The first is the grounding of history in "material relations of life". The second is the understanding of social progress as a "natural history". Together, the author contends, the two logics turn the philosophy of history into a science of history.

The article first sketches the Enlightenment background, taking Kant and Hegel as its examples. It then sets out the shared premises and the decisive break with that tradition. The two main sections are headed "Understanding history through 'material relations of life'" and "Social progress as 'natural history'". The piece closes by drawing the two logics together.

Zhang reads Kant's "hidden plan of nature" and Hegel's "absolute spirit" as cases where history becomes a footnote to reason. Marx, in this account, replaces reason with practice, meaning the material production of life by real human beings, as the measure of history. The constant element that makes a science of history possible is the contradictory movement of the productive forces and the relations of production, which Zhang presents as the "driving force" of social progress. The second logic draws on Marx's remark in Capital about the development of the economic formation of society as a process of natural history. Zhang uses it to show that society shares the materiality of nature, so that progress follows laws independent of human will. Yet society also transforms nature into a "humanized nature", which gives progress a subjective dimension. Human initiative can grasp the laws and speed up progress, as in the "Caudine Forks" leap, without negating the priority of nature.

Zhang concludes that the two logics are not split apart but unified in material production and in the core theme of practice. On this reading, Marx's theory is a rigorously logical system. It breaks with idealist approaches to history and offers what the author calls the best account of the laws of social progress, in which progress unfolds as the working-out of the contradiction between productive forces and relations of production. Read the original if you want a concise, Chinese-language statement of how Marx's break with Enlightenment philosophy of history is currently presented in Chinese academic commentary.
quoteEn: Taking \"material relations of life\" as the root, it re-establishes the constancy of history itself and so identifies the \"driving force\" of social progress; this is the fundamental logic of his theory of social progress.
quoteZh: 以“物质的生活关系”为根源，重新确立历史自身的恒定性，从而明确了社会进步的“动力源”，这是其社会进步理论的逻辑根本。
keywords: productive forces and relations of production

t: Rereading Marx's aesthetic notebook
zh: 重读马克思的美学笔记
paras: Li Suogui, writing in Guangming Daily (29 July 2024), revisits Marx's excerpt notes on Friedrich Theodor Vischer's multi-volume Aesthetics, or the Science of the Beautiful, prompted by a new Chinese translation published in 2023. Li argues that the notes, written in June 1857, show Marx's real command of philosophical aesthetics and that they fed into his later writing.

The piece first describes the notes' fate. Li says they went unpublished in full until a Russian version appeared in 1990, and that the new translation corrects earlier mistranslations and omissions. It then follows the notes' order: definitions of aesthetics, Kant's aesthetic judgement, the "elements of the beautiful", natural beauty, fantasy and myth, and the classification of the arts. Li ends with how the notes were used.

Li identifies three purposes for the notes: an invited encyclopedia entry on aesthetics, material for the 1857 Introduction to the Critique of Political Economy, and a theoretical basis for judging Lassalle's drama Franz von Sickingen. Li reads Marx's selections as deliberate. Marx recorded the sublime in detail, the tragic and comic more briefly, and fantasy and myth in full, but skipped the volumes on sculpture, painting, music and poetry. The entry was declined, yet the material on myth reappears in the Introduction's question about Greek art and modern machinery. It also shaped Marx's view of Lassalle's play as tragedy, following Vischer's idea that revolution is tragedy's true theme.

Li concludes that the notes were not wasted, and that Marx's closing classification table shows how far he accepted Hegelian-school aesthetics. Read the original if you want a brief account of how Marx's 1857 aesthetic notes are structured and how they connect to his later writings.
quoteEn: Marx's notes were not made in vain.
quoteZh: 马克思所做的笔记没有白费。
keywords: Introduction to the Critique of Political Economy

t: The synthesis of reality in Marxist philosophy
zh: 马克思主义哲学的现实综合
paras: Lan Jiang asks what it takes to understand Marxist philosophy beyond its familiar concepts such as materialism, contradiction, productive forces and practice. The commentary, published in the China Social Sciences Journal in July 2024, argues that Marxism must be read as a comprehensive truth and placed within the real world. Theory and practice are to be brought together there, which the author calls the "synthesis of reality".

The piece moves from Marx's break with German idealism to the demands placed on Marxist philosophers today. It draws on the Theses on Feuerbach and The German Ideology, then turns to Chinese modernization, big data, artificial intelligence and automated production.

Lan contends that Marx's notion of practice is a real force for changing the world, not an abstract category. Citing The German Ideology on the steam engine and the spinning jenny, the author stresses that liberation depends on industrial, commercial and agricultural conditions. Marx studied the science and technology of his day, the article says, and this knowledge underpinned historical materialism and Capital, so Marxist philosophy was interdisciplinary from the start. For today's researchers this implies learning mathematics, physics, economics, law, communication studies and more. Lan adds that autonomous agents such as coordinating warehouse robots should be counted as subjects within social relations, which challenges politics, sociology and law.

Lan concludes that Marxist philosophy today must break disciplinary barriers and follow changes in industry, agriculture, commerce and communication. It should also be combined with China's concrete realities and with traditional Chinese culture, as the Two Integrations require. The aim is a more humane, flexible, orderly and ecological community with a shared future for mankind under intelligent technology. Read the original if you want a short example of how Chinese philosophers link Marx's practice to AI and interdisciplinary research.
quoteEn: Marxist philosophy achieves a synthesis of reality on an interdisciplinary basis, and carries out practical revolution on the basis of that synthesis.
quoteZh: 马克思主义哲学就是在跨学科的基础上实现对现实的综合，并在这个综合的基础上进行实践性的革命。

glossary.explanation: A formula in Party theory: combining Marxism's basic principles with China's concrete realities and with fine traditional Chinese culture.
The official term for China's path of modernization under Party leadership, prominent in Party discourse since the 20th Party Congress (2022).

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: A concept promoted by Xi Jinping since 2012–13 describing the Chinese vision of international relations and global governance.

t: The inherent unity of the integrity of Marxism and the disciplinary character of political economy
zh: 马克思主义整体性与政治经济学学科性的内在统一
paras: Zheng Jiwei takes up a tendency in Chinese scholarship to stress the integrity (整体性) of Marxism while neglecting political economy as a distinct academic discipline. The article, a short commentary from the Chinese Social Sciences Today of July 2024, argues that the two are inherently unified and that, in the new era, achieving this unity is an objective need for systematising and giving scholarly grounding to the latest results of adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times.

The piece first recalls Marx's turn to political economy from late 1843 and the emergence of political economy as an independent discipline. It then turns to the present, discussing the establishment of Marxist theory as a first-level discipline and Xi Jinping's 2023 call to make theory systematic and rooted in scholarly principle.

Zheng reads Marx's forty-year turn to political economy as compatible with the wholeness of Marxism, citing Marx's description of his works as an artistic whole. Zheng objects to the view that each discipline generates its own Marxism and so dissolves the whole, calling it open to question. Systematisation, in Zheng's account, requires understanding Marxism as an integrated whole, including Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era. Giving the theory a scholarly basis requires the disciplinary character of its parts. For political economy, this aids popularisation and deeper research, and Zheng holds that Xi Jinping's economic thought can be understood in its logic only from a political-economy perspective.

Zheng concludes that systematisation and scholarly grounding reinforce each other, and that integrity and disciplinarity are not opposed. Read the original if you want a brief example of how Chinese academic commentary links Marxist disciplinary debates to the Party's theoretical-innovation agenda.
quoteEn: The establishment of Marxist theory as a first-level discipline does not conflict with the long-standing treatment of political economy as an important discipline; rather they complement and promote each other.
quoteZh: 马克思主义理论一级学科的成立与长期以来将政治经济学作为重要学科并不矛盾，反而相得益彰，相互促进。

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017 and 2018.

glossary.zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化
glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
glossary.explanation: The official formula for applying Marxism to Chinese conditions and contemporary circumstances, and developing it in the process.
The official name for the economic component of Xi Jinping Thought, presented as a development of Marxist political economy.

t: Marxist philosophy's interpretation of "the human being" and its contemporary implications
zh: 马克思主义哲学对“人”的阐释及其当代启示
paras: Yang Qiaorong asks what Marxist philosophy means by "the human being" and what that understanding offers today. The article, a newspaper commentary first published in Guangming Daily in July 2024, argues that Marxism treats the human being not as an isolated abstraction but as a practical subject embedded in social relations and historical development. On this view, the concept gives people a way to see the deeper forces behind social change and to act consciously to push society towards greater justice.

The piece has three parts. The first traces how Marx and Engels built the concept through critical engagement with German classical philosophy (Hegel and Feuerbach), British classical political economy and French utopian socialism. The second sets out three dimensions of the Marxist account: the web of social relations, the human being as a dynamic subject of history, and the ideal of complete human emancipation. The third draws three contemporary lessons, with reference to economic globalization and rapid information technology.

In Yang's account, Marx replaced a transcendent, ahistorical human nature with the thesis that the human essence is the ensemble of social relations. Through the theory of alienated labour, developed in the Economic and Philosophic Manuscripts of 1844 and in Capital, Marx showed how workers lose their subjectivity under capitalism. Yang then links this to the contradiction between productive forces and relations of production. Emancipation, in this reading, requires abolishing private ownership and class oppression, so that labour becomes a means of all-round self-realization.

For the present, Yang calls for attention to how social structures shape individuals, for deepening reform, fairer distribution of wealth and more equal educational opportunity. Citing Xi Jinping, the author says socialism with Chinese characteristics, led by the Communist Party, has put a "logic of the people" above a "logic of capital". Yang also urges debate on technology ethics in the digital age, so that artificial intelligence and data technologies do not become new tools of oppression and alienation. Read the original if you want a concise example of how a Party-aligned newspaper commentary links Marx's theory of the human being to current policy themes.
quoteEn: The free and all-round development of the human being is the highest ideal and value pursuit of social progress.
quoteZh: 人的自由而全面的发展是社会进步的最高理想和价值追求。

glossary.explanation: The official name for the Chinese Communist Party's model of socialism since the reform era. Party theorists present it as Marxism applied to Chinese conditions.

glossary.literal: the logic of the human person
glossary.explanation: The article's rendering of 人的逻辑, which it contrasts with the 'logic of capital'. It presents production as aimed at meeting people's needs for a better life rather than at maximizing profit.

t: A philosophical interpretation of high-quality development
zh: 高质量发展的哲学解读
paras: Qiu Gengtian takes up high-quality development, which Xi Jinping has called the theme of China's economic and social development during the 14th Five-Year Plan period and beyond. The article, a short newspaper piece, argues that Marxist philosophy lets readers grasp it as a whole and see its essence and laws. Qiu holds that this grasp has three logical dimensions: epistemological, axiological and methodological.

The article takes the three dimensions in turn. The epistemological one asks what kind of development China should pursue. The axiological one asks why high-quality development is needed. The methodological one asks how it can be achieved.

On epistemology, Qiu argues that social development moves through a contradictory interplay of low-quality and high-quality development, driven by two mechanisms: demand rising to higher levels, and problems that force a transformation. This makes high-quality development historically necessary and calls for a consensus that gives it a foundational status. On values, Qiu presents it as both end and means. It is the primary task of building a modern socialist country, and it is the basic route to resolving the principal contradiction between people's growing need for a better life and unbalanced, inadequate development. On method, Qiu proposes three principles: fully applying the new development philosophy, accelerating new quality productive forces as the material basis, and staying problem-oriented by moving from high-cost, low-quality development to low-cost, high-quality development.

Qiu concludes that these three perspectives give a clear theoretical reference for why and how to pursue high-quality development in the new era. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Chinese scholars frame current economic policy in philosophical terms.
quoteEn: High-quality development is a unity of end and means.
quoteZh: 高质量发展是目的和手段的统一。

glossary.explanation: An official economic policy goal, prominent since the late 2010s. It stresses quality, efficiency and innovation over speed of growth.
Xi Jinping's framework of innovative, coordinated, green, open and shared development, announced in 2015.
A concept Xi Jinping introduced in 2023. It refers to advanced productive forces driven by technological innovation.

t: Advancing the development of Marxism through China's vivid practice
zh: 用中国鲜活的实践推进马克思主义发展
source: China Social Sciences Today (Zhongguo shehui kexue bao), 25 June 2024
paras: Han Xiping asks how Marxism can keep developing and how China's philosophy and social sciences should be built on it. The short commentary, first published in China Social Sciences Today in June 2024, argues that scientific theory guides social progress while living practice is the source that enriches and renews theory. Han holds that Marxism must be used to observe, interpret and lead the times, and that contemporary Chinese practice is the ground on which it advances.

The piece has three parts. The first treats Marxism as a constantly developing science, tracing this from Engels and Lenin to the Communist Party of China's adaptation of Marxism to the Chinese context. The second takes up Marxism as the fundamental guide for philosophy and social sciences with Chinese characteristics. The third sets out how an autonomous Chinese knowledge system in these fields should be built.

Han first argues that Marxism's vitality comes from keeping pace with the times. Citing Engels and Lenin, Han presents the Chinese Party's Marxism as the three leaps of Marxism's adaptation, ending in Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, which Han calls twenty-first-century Marxism. From there Han maintains that building China's own philosophy and social sciences means taking this thought as the basic guide. Han cites Xi's remark that the field's capacity in concepts, discourse and standards does not yet match China's national strength and international standing.

Han proposes four routes for building the autonomous knowledge system. Marxism should serve as the worldview and methodology across disciplines. Research should be problem-oriented and turn China's experience into theory, with policy and experience given scholarly description and argument. The "new liberal arts" should break down disciplinary barriers in response to technological and industrial change. A new explanatory paradigm should also address the sense that Chinese discourse is absent from some disciplines, textbooks and forums, and should offer original concepts that international audiences can understand. Han concludes that this would strengthen the subjectivity, originality and competitiveness of Chinese scholarship. Read the original if you want a concise statement of how Chinese academic commentary links Marxist theory, Xi Jinping Thought and the building of an autonomous knowledge system.
quoteEn: Raise China's experience to the level of Chinese theory, so as to better promote knowledge innovation, theoretical innovation and methodological innovation in philosophy and the social sciences.
quoteZh: 把中国经验上升为中国理论，更好地推动哲学社会科学知识创新、理论创新、方法创新

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018. Official texts present it as the latest stage of adapting Marxism to China.

glossary.zh: 中国特色哲学社会科学
glossary.en: philosophy and social sciences with Chinese characteristics
glossary.explanation: An official goal, stressed by Xi Jinping from 2016, of building a Chinese system of disciplines, scholarship and discourse guided by Marxism.
A slogan from Xi Jinping's 2022 and 2023 speeches calling for Chinese social science to rest on its own concepts and theories, rather than on Western frameworks.
An education policy initiative promoting interdisciplinary reform of the humanities and social sciences in response to new technology and industry.

t: Marx's scale of thought
zh: 马克思的思想尺度
paras: Liu Tongfang asks what the macro-level "scale" (chidu) of Marx's thinking looks like, setting it beside the attention to concrete and particular matters that Marx also showed. The article argues that, viewed as a whole, Marx's intellectual development rests on three macro-level moves: a grand view of history that divides human social development into stages, a systemic way of thinking that defines the nature and forms of production, and an overall value standard for judging social progress.

The piece is organised in three sections that follow these moves and are presented as a logical shift "from outside to inside" and then to evaluation. The first treats the periodisation of history, drawing on the Grundrisse, the Economic and Philosophic Manuscripts of 1844 and Marx's late anthropological and historical notebooks. The second analyses alienated labour and the structure of human production. The third turns to the criteria of social progress. Liu presents the first two as scientific description of social history and the third as scientific value judgement.

In the first section, Liu argues that Marx divides history by two criteria. The objective one is the level of the productive forces and the form of production relations. The "inner" one is the state of human subjectivity: dependence on persons, dependence on things, and free individuality. The disappearance of antagonistic production relations marks the end of "prehistory", and Liu reads Marx's late notebooks as moving beyond Eurocentrism. In the second section, Marx treats production as human "life activity" and as "species life", not merely as economic activity. Liu describes a structure with material production and the production of human beings as the "foundational level", the production of social relations as the "intermediary level" and spiritual production as the "highest level". In the third section, Marx is said to reject single standards such as productive-force growth alone. He treats material abundance as basic but not sufficient, and adds spiritual culture, harmony in social relations and harmony between humans and nature, all measured by whether they promote all-round human development.

Liu concludes that clarifying this scale shows the breadth and depth of Marx's thought and strengthens research on its wholeness. The article calls on Marxist theorists to pursue multi-dimensional, integrated study of Marx and to develop a conscious sense of academic mission in doing so. Read the original if you want a concise Chinese-academic account of how Marx's periodisation of history, theory of production and criteria of progress are linked into one framework.
quoteEn: To evaluate social progress is to present as a whole all the meanings that progress contains.
quoteZh: 评价社会进步就是要整体性地呈现进步所包含的全部意义

t: Evaluation of historical figures must adhere to the materialist conception of history
zh: 历史人物评价必须坚持唯物史观
source: Chinese Social Sciences Today (Zhongguo shehui kexue bao), 29 January 2024
paras: Sun Qinmei takes up a long-standing question in historical scholarship: how historical figures should be judged. The commentary argues that correct evaluation depends first on the underlying view of history, and that the materialist conception of history is the only scientific basis for it. Sun treats this as a precondition for building a discourse system of Marxist historical materialism today, and as a response to what the author sees as distorted reassessments of historical figures.

The piece has three parts. The first sets out why historical materialism supplies the methodological basis for evaluating individuals. The second analyses historical nihilism, which Sun describes as a political current rather than a scholarly one. The third proposes three ways of applying historical materialism in current research on historical figures.

Sun sets historical materialism against idealist views such as the "heroic" and "genius" conceptions of history, and draws three principles from it: place a figure within given historical conditions, examine the class interests and national relations the figure represents, and seek truth from facts. Historical nihilism, in Sun's account, errs in four ways: it denies the unity of subjectivity and objectivity in evaluation, judges the past by present standards, replaces class analysis with abstract human nature in "above-class" reassessments, and distorts main facts through fragmentary detail. The proposals follow. Historical materialism should be restored to its original meaning, stripped of dogmatism and misreadings. The several evaluative standards (class, productive forces, progress, morality) should be used with awareness of their limits, with moral judgement resting on factual judgement. And the principle of wholeness should be upheld, which means historicism, distinguishing mainstream from tributary, and rejecting claims such as "farewell to revolution".

Sun concludes that if historical materialism does not occupy the field of historical research, historical nihilism will, and cites Xi Jinping on the need to master Marxism in order to resist it. Strengthening the explanatory power and influence of historical materialism is presented as the proper theoretical self-awareness of historians in the new era. Read the original if you want a concise statement of the official Chinese Marxist case against historical nihilism in the assessment of historical figures, and of the criteria it proposes.
quoteEn: It flies the banner of scholarship, yet it is not an academic trend of thought but a political one.
quoteZh: 它打着学术旗号，却并非学术思潮，而是一种政治思潮。

glossary.explanation: In Chinese Party discourse, a label for interpretations seen as denying or belittling the revolutionary and socialist past and its leading figures. Party leaders have repeatedly criticised it as a political current.

The Marxist theory that material production and social relations shape historical development; it is also called historical materialism. Chinese authors treat it as the guiding method of historical research.
The Marxist method of explaining people and events through class position and interests. The article defends it against claims that it is outdated.

t: Global neoliberal capitalism and its alternatives
zh: 全球新自由资本主义及其替代方案
paras: The article, attributed to David Lane and carried by the Chinese Social Sciences Today in June 2024, asks why neoliberalism became dominant after the 1980s and whether Margaret Thatcher's claim that "there is no alternative" holds. Lane doubts it. He argues that a viable alternative exists for advanced capitalist states, which he calls regulated market socialism.

The text opens with the strength of socialism between the 1950s and the mid-1970s and its retreat by the early twenty-first century. It then defines neoliberalism as an economic doctrine that became a social theory, covering legal, psychological, economic and political dimensions. Next it lists six problems it attributes to neoliberal capitalism. It then surveys alternatives in three groups: reformist options within capitalism, socialist options, and hybrid forms, before setting out Lane's preferred model.

Lane draws on Hayek, Keynes and Myrdal. He argues that neoliberalism spread because governments of different parties saw it as a cure for stagnation, not only through coercion or media persuasion. Its legal order, individualism and monetisation of social exchange, he says, also shifted the Western left from class analysis to identity politics. The six problems are cyclical crises, inherited income inequality, social and political turmoil, ecological damage, inequality between core and peripheral states, and the threat of war. He cautions against blaming all of them on neoliberalism alone. His own model combines state-level planning with micro-level markets. Large firms would be moved gradually into public ownership, small and medium enterprises would stay private, and personal savings and earned assets would be protected. Pluralist electoral politics would continue, and the aim would be to end class exploitation and reduce inherited wealth without civil conflict.

Lane concludes that this model would reduce exploitation and inequality, avoid civil war and pose no threat to other states. He says it applies to developed countries such as the United States and Britain, not to emerging economies. He accepts that it currently has no support from any Western party and attributes this to ideological inertia. Quoting Milton Friedman on keeping alternatives alive until the politically impossible becomes inevitable, he expresses confidence that socialism will become politically inevitable in the West. Read the original if you want a Western Marxist-leaning typology of alternatives to neoliberalism and a concrete proposal for transition in advanced capitalist countries.
quoteEn: I believe that, as Friedman put it, socialism, which now looks \"politically impossible\" in the West, will in the end become a \"politically inevitable\" reality.
quoteZh: 我相信，如弗里德曼所言，现在在西方看起来“政治上不可能”的社会主义终将成为“政治上不可避免”的现实。

t: Advancing the development of Marxism through China's vivid practice
zh: 用中国鲜活的实践推进马克思主义发展
paras: Han Xiping asks how Marxism can keep developing and how it should guide the building of Chinese philosophy and social sciences. The commentary, which first appeared in China Social Sciences Today in June 2024, argues that Marxism is a theory that grows with practice and that contemporary Chinese practice is its present source of renewal. Han bases this on Xi Jinping's call to use Marxism to observe, interpret and lead the times.

The piece has three parts. The first treats Marxism as a continuously developing science, running from Marx and Engels through Lenin to the successive stages of adapting Marxism to Chinese conditions. The second addresses Marxism as the fundamental guide for philosophy and social sciences with Chinese characteristics. The third sets out how to build an autonomous Chinese knowledge system in these fields.

Han's central move is to link theory to practice in both directions. Citing Engels and Lenin, Han holds that Marxism stays alive by keeping pace with the times, and that Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era is an original system formed by combining Marxism with China's realities and its fine traditional culture. Han contends that the Chinese social sciences still lag behind the country's overall strength and international standing in academic propositions, ideas, standards and discourse. The remedy is to build the disciplinary, academic and discourse systems on this Thought, turning Chinese experience into Chinese theory.

Han proposes four routes to an autonomous knowledge system: let Marxism guide every discipline as worldview, method and standard of testing; adopt a problem-oriented approach that gives scholarly expression to the experience of socialism with Chinese characteristics; pursue the "new liberal arts" by breaking down disciplinary barriers; and construct a new explanatory paradigm. The last aims to end the "absence" of Chinese discourse in some disciplines, textbooks and forums, and to produce concepts that international audiences can understand. Read the original if you want a concise statement of the official line on Marxism's development and on the construction of an autonomous Chinese social science system.
quoteEn: In building an autonomous knowledge system for Chinese philosophy and social sciences, one must proceed from practice, take the times as the point of reference, and keep advancing innovation in knowledge, theory and method through practice.
quoteZh: 建构中国哲学社会科学自主知识体系，要立足实践，以时代为观照，在实践中不断推进知识创新、理论创新、方法创新。

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Communist Party of China's current official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018. Official texts present it as the Marxism of contemporary China and of the twenty-first century.
The standard Chinese official category covering the humanities and social sciences. Party documents set it as a field to be guided by Marxism and to serve national development.
An official goal, stressed by Xi Jinping, of building Chinese-originated disciplinary, academic and discourse systems rather than relying on Western frameworks.
An education policy initiative promoting interdisciplinary reform of the humanities and social sciences in response to technological and industrial change.

t: Deng Xiaoping's exploration of and contribution to the theory of Chinese modernization
zh: 邓小平对中国式现代化理论的探索与贡献
source: Research on Marxist Theory Education in Colleges and Universities (高校马克思主义理论教育研究), 2024 no. 3
paras: Yu asks what Deng Xiaoping contributed to the basic framework of the theory of Chinese modernization. The article argues that Deng, as chief architect of reform and opening up and of socialist modernization, put forward a series of ideas that laid that framework and deepened understanding of modernization. Yu holds that summing up these contributions matters for building the theory system and for advancing Chinese modernization in practice.

The article is organised around six contributions. They are the concept of a "Chinese-style modernization", the goal of common prosperity, the "three-step" development strategy, the thesis that science and technology are the primary productive force, opening up to the outside world, and the theory of the socialist market economy. Yu draws on Deng's talks and speeches from 1978 to 1988, on Marx's analysis of capitalism and the world market, and on modernization theory, dependency theory, Stalin and Mises.

Yu first argues that Deng's 1979 concept challenged the equation of modernization with Westernization promoted by classical modernization theory, which Yu says the United States sponsored. The concept takes socialism and the primary stage of socialism as its coordinates and reflects Deng's reflection on the "Left" errors before reform. Yu reads it as treating socialist and capitalist modernization as two particular forms of a shared universal process. On common prosperity, Yu says modernization brings wealth but not necessarily shared wealth, so only socialism can secure the latter. On opening up and markets, Yu argues that globalization follows the logic of capital and risks Westernization and dependency, so opening must keep to the socialist road and the Four Cardinal Principles. Yu adds that the market is a means of allocating resources, not the preserve of capitalism, and that Deng's separation of the market economy from capitalism freed it to serve socialism.

Yu concludes that these ideas covered the concept, essential requirements, strategic arrangements, direction and principles of Chinese modernization. Deng also stressed Party leadership, spiritual as well as material civilization, and socialist democracy. In Yu's view, this enriched Chinese modernization theory and deepened the Party's understanding of general and Chinese laws of modernization, laying a foundation for later theoretical and practical innovation. Read the original if you want a systematic account of how Deng's statements are presented as the origin of Chinese modernization theory, with extensive quotations from his speeches.
quoteEn: In putting forward the concept of Chinese-style modernization, Deng Xiaoping had already seen that socialist modernization and capitalist modernization are two particular forms, and that China can have its own pace, path and goals.
quoteZh: 邓小平提出中国式的现代化概念，就是已经看出，社会主义现代化和资本主义现代化都是两种特殊，中国可以有自己的节奏、路径和目标。

glossary.explanation: The official term for China's path of modernization under Party leadership. Deng Xiaoping used the phrase in 1979, and it has been developed as a full theoretical concept in the Xi Jinping era.
The policy course launched in 1978 under Deng Xiaoping. It introduced market-oriented economic reforms and opened China to foreign trade and investment.
A socialist goal of prosperity shared by all, as opposed to polarization. Deng linked it to the essence of socialism, and it has been revived as a major policy goal since the 2020s.
The official judgement that China is in a long early phase of socialism marked by underdeveloped productive forces. The Party formally adopted it in 1981 and 1987.
Deng Xiaoping's 1979 formula: keep to the socialist road, the people's democratic dictatorship, Party leadership, and Marxism-Leninism and Mao Zedong Thought.

keywords: science and technology as primary productive force

t: Mao Zedong and the development of philosophy and social sciences in China
zh: 毛泽东与中国哲学社会科学事业发展
paras: Song and Zhou ask what Mao Zedong contributed to laying the foundations of Marxist philosophy and social sciences in China, and what that legacy offers for building philosophy and social sciences with Chinese characteristics today. They argue that Mao explored the laws and features of this field, set out guiding policies for it, and left a body of historical experience that bears directly on current tasks.

The article has four parts. The first treats Mao's adaptation of Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times as the path that opened the field. The second examines his formulas "weeding through the old to bring forth the new" and "making the past serve the present". The third covers the "Hundred Flowers" and "Hundred Schools" policy. The fourth draws lessons for the present, citing Xi Jinping's statements throughout.

The authors argue that Mao's theoretical works, from the theory of New Democratic revolution to the writings on contradictions among the people, themselves embody the stance and method of Marxist social science, whose living soul they identify as seeking truth from facts, the mass line and independence. On tradition, they trace the formula from Mao's 1938 call to inherit China's historical legacy critically, through the 1942 inscription for the Yan'an Peking opera institute, to postwar projects: the Academy of Sciences' philosophy and social sciences division (1955) and the new punctuated edition of the Twenty-Four Histories (completed 1978). On the "Hundred Flowers" policy, they stress three features: it operates under Marxist guidance, which Mao held would strengthen rather than weaken Marxism's leading position; it upholds academic democracy by separating political from academic questions; and it is inclusive, rejecting both xenophobia and uncritical borrowing from abroad. Examples include the founding of Historical Research (1954), Mao's 1957 logic seminars and his remark on the Lanting Preface debate.

Drawing on Mao, the authors call for problem-oriented research on major practical questions, with Marxism as guidance and the people as the research standpoint. They also want an independent Chinese knowledge system, with discipline, academic and discourse systems built on Chinese conditions rather than copied from abroad. They add a call for talent programmes and incentives for scholars. They present Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era as the current guide. Read the original if you want an official-academic account of how Mao's cultural and scholarly policies are being drawn on in current discussions of China's philosophy and social sciences.
quoteEn: The \"Double Hundred\" policy advocated by Mao Zedong also champions academic democracy.
quoteZh: 毛泽东所提倡的“双百”方针，也是高扬学术民主的。

glossary.literal: let a hundred flowers bloom, let a hundred schools of thought contend
glossary.explanation: A policy Mao announced in 1956–57 encouraging diverse artistic styles and scholarly schools under Party leadership. It is often abbreviated as the "Double Hundred" policy.

glossary.en: weeding through the old to bring forth the new
glossary.literal: push out the old, bring forth the new
glossary.explanation: Mao's formula for critically sifting traditional culture, discarding what is outdated and building new forms on what is inherited.

glossary.en: making the past serve the present
