glossary.explanation: A cultural principle associated with Mao, under which ancient heritage is used selectively and critically to serve contemporary socialist needs.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology since 2017, written into the Party and state constitutions.
Mao's term for the stage of the Chinese revolution before socialism, led by the Communist Party and aimed at imperialism, feudalism and bureaucrat-capitalism.

t: Engels's The Condition of the Working Class in England and the study of Britain's modernization: a visual analysis
zh: 《英国工人阶级状况》关于英国现代化进程研究的可视化分析
paras: Liu Nana rereads Engels's The Condition of the Working Class in England as a study of Britain's modernization, which Engels traces from the Industrial Revolution. The article argues that Engels's data and field observations expose a set of paradoxes in capital-driven modernization. From these Liu draws lessons for seeing how Chinese modernization goes beyond the Western path.

The article has three parts. The first sets out the temporal and spatial features of British modernization, using figures and charts on population movement, transport, city growth and the world market. The second analyses three paradoxes that Liu finds in Engels's text. The third draws theoretical implications for Chinese modernization.

In Liu's account, Engels treats industrialization and urbanization as mutually reinforcing, and sees British capitalism as opening world history through the division of labour, new technology and the world market. Liu identifies three paradoxes. Workers become appendages of machines and are harmed in body and mind. Urban space develops unevenly, with housing shortages, town–country opposition and the loss of public leisure space. Free trade benefits capital, not labour: it intensifies competition among workers, lowers their purchasing power and extends exploitation worldwide. Liu stresses that Engels traces these outcomes to the capitalist system itself and not to incidental causes.

Liu concludes that Chinese modernization surpasses Western modernization in three ways. First, it is a modernization of people, in contrast to what Liu calls the Western modernization of things, and it aims at free and all-round human development under a people-centred approach. Second, it builds socialist town–country relations through "people's cities" and rural revitalization. Third, it widens its space through a new pattern of domestic and international dual circulation. Liu describes it as both open and endogenous, and as rejecting plunder and colonial expansion. Read the original if you want a data-driven rereading of Engels's early work that is tied to current Party discourse on Chinese modernization.
quoteEn: That Western modernization is a modernization of things means that it sees \"things\" but not \"people\".
quoteZh: 西方式现代化是物的现代化意味着见“物”不见“人”

glossary.explanation: The official Party concept of a distinctive path of modernization, set out prominently since the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is presented as an alternative to Western models.

glossary.literal: taking the people as the centre
glossary.explanation: A guiding principle in Xi Jinping-era Party discourse. It holds that development should be for, and rely on, the people and be shared by them.

A slogan from Xi Jinping, repeated in the 20th Party Congress report: "people's cities are built by the people and for the people". It stresses residents' participation and benefit in urban development.
A national strategy launched in 2017 and elaborated in the 2018–2022 plan. It seeks to develop rural industry, ecology, culture and governance and to narrow the town–country gap.
An economic strategy put forward in 2020. It takes the domestic cycle as the main body while the domestic and international cycles reinforce each other.

keywords: The Condition of the Working Class in England

t: The "logic of Capital" as critique and transcendence of Hegel's speculative logic
st: A methodological inquiry based on the relation between logic and history
zh: “《资本论》的逻辑”对黑格尔思辨逻辑的批判与超越
zhSub: 基于“逻辑与历史”关系的方法论探究
paras: Liu Daoyi asks how Marx's principle of the unity of logic and history arose from, and went beyond, Hegel's opposite principle that history is unified within logic. The article argues that Hegel's inversion of the relation between thought and reality necessarily inverted the relation between logic and history. In Liu's account, Marx overcame this inversion in what Lenin called the "logic of Capital", where materialist logic, dialectics and epistemology are applied to a single science.

The article has four parts. It first reconstructs Hegel's principle through his treatment of the history of philosophy and of world history, and lists its defects. It then sets out Marx's counter-principle, drawing on the 1857–58 manuscripts and Engels. The last two parts follow the "logic of Capital" through two movements of concepts: from the concrete to the abstract, which Liu locates in Marx's critique of the history of political economy (chiefly Theories of Surplus-Value), and from the abstract to the concrete, which Liu locates in the three volumes of Capital.

Liu identifies three defects in Hegel's approach. Its transitions are conceptual deduction that cannot be verified against facts. It leaves his material thin, as in his treatment of China, and so feeds Eurocentrism. It cannot grasp the role of economic factors. Marx, by contrast, starts from real contradictions in capitalism and gathers extensive factual material. He holds that the order of categories follows their relations within modern bourgeois society, not their historical order of appearance, although simple categories such as money or labour in general often did exist earlier. In Liu's reading, Marx's critique of political economy runs from the mercantilists through Smith and Ricardo to the vulgarisation of the Ricardian school. It shows how all economists studied surplus-value only in the special forms of profit and rent.

On Liu's reading, the structure of Capital embodies the same unity. Volume I runs from commodity and money to the tendency of capitalist accumulation, which ends in the negation of the negation. Volume II treats the circuits and reproduction of capital. Volume III moves from profit to merchant capital, interest-bearing capital and ground-rent, each with a historical review. The article concludes that this method negated and surpassed Hegel's speculative logic, raised dialectics to a new level and offers a scientific methodological basis for social change and theoretical innovation today. Read the original if you want a detailed, text-based account of how the structure of Capital is read as applying the unity of logic and history against Hegel.
quoteEn: Marx's principle of the unity of logic and history was thereby established and systematically carried through in Capital and its manuscripts, negating and surpassing Hegel's speculative logic through dialectical research and exposition and raising dialectics to a new level.
quoteZh: 马克思的“逻辑与历史相统一”原则由此确立，并在《资本论》及其手稿中系统贯彻，以辩证的研究和论述否定并超越了黑格尔的思辨逻辑，将辩证法提升到一个新的高度

glossary.explanation: A methodological principle in Chinese Marxist scholarship, drawn from Engels's remarks on Marx's method. It holds that the order of theoretical exposition corresponds in essence to the real course of historical development, though not in a simple one-to-one way.
A phrase from Lenin's Philosophical Notebooks. He wrote that Marx left no 'Logic' but did leave the logic of Capital, in which dialectics, logic and theory of knowledge coincide.
The article's label for Hegel's principle that history, both of philosophy and of the world, is an unfolding of the logical determinations of the Idea or Absolute Spirit.

t: Plekhanov's critique of the "religious quest" and his exposition of Marxist atheism
zh: 普列汉诺夫对“宗教探寻”的批判和马克思主义无神论的阐释
paras: Zhang Jiansong asks what Georgi Plekhanov's long essay "On the So-called Religious Quest in Russia" offers for religious theory and for ideological struggle today. Zhang argues that, after the defeat of the 1905 revolution, Plekhanov used historical materialism to expose the "God-seeking" and "God-building" currents as theoretically weak and politically harmful. The article presents the essay as a model of Marxist criticism that still has practical meaning for religious work and for the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation.

The article follows the three parts of the essay that Plekhanov completed, using the texts in volume three of his selected philosophical works. Part one, "On Religion", sets out a basic theory. Part two, "Religion Again", criticises Tolstoy, Lunacharsky and Gorky. Part three deals with the "decadents" Merezhkovsky and Minsky. Zhang opens with the Stolypin reaction and closes with lessons for China.

Zhang's central claim is that Plekhanov grounds religion in social being. His definition has three elements: ideas, feelings and ritual. Myth and animism arise from the low productive forces of hunting peoples, who reasoned by analogy. Totemism gave way as humanity gained control over nature, and later gods took on the shape of rulers and judges. Applying this framework, Plekhanov argues that every religion needs spirits, so the "atheist religion" of Tolstoy, Lunacharsky and Gorky is a verbal game. Zhang reports that Plekhanov attributes the quest to intellectuals who lost faith in revolution and turned to individual consolation. Against the decadents, Plekhanov defends the proletariat's economic struggle and argues that their individualism and fear of death drive their mysticism. He appeals to Feuerbach and Engels, and holds that only dialectical materialism resolves the problem of freedom and necessity.

Zhang concludes that readers should learn two things. The first is to remain firm Marxists. Zhang cites the Soviet Union's collapse under Gorbachev's ideological pluralism and the Chinese Communist Party's adaptation of Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times. The second is to dare to struggle against erroneous trends. Zhang lists historical nihilism, constitutional democracy, "universal values" and neoliberalism, along with abnormal religious phenomena in some regions, as targets. Read the original if you want a detailed Chinese reading of Plekhanov's religious theory and of how it is used in current Chinese ideological discussion.
quoteEn: Plekhanov's spirit of drawing the sword and of struggle in the face of erroneous trends of thought deserves our study.
quoteZh: 普列汉诺夫面对错误思潮的亮剑精神、斗争精神，值得我们学习。

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A long-standing Party goal of restoring China's national strength and international standing, closely associated with Xi Jinping's leadership.
In official Chinese usage, a label for views that question or negate the Party's account of revolutionary and socialist history.

t: New developments in the ideological sphere under new technological conditions
zh: 新技术条件下意识形态领域新变
paras: Writing in a newspaper commentary (China Social Sciences Today, May 2024), Huang Xianghuai asks how ideological work must change under new technological conditions. Huang credits the Party Central Committee since the 18th Party Congress (2012) with a fundamental turnaround in the ideological sphere. The author nevertheless stresses, citing the report to the 20th Party Congress (2022), that "quite a few challenges" remain and that the work must keep renewing itself.

The piece examines three new features: the changed communication landscape of the all-media era, a new form of struggle in the age of cognitive warfare, and the greater difficulty of safeguarding ideological security in the post-truth era.

On the first, Huang argues that mainstream media are squeezed by self-media and capital, and that a dominant position is earned through influence, not held by default. Mainstream outlets should therefore be judged by what they achieve, not by whether they discharge their duties, and any outlet that sustains this function could be recognised as mainstream. On the second, the author says openly hostile statements have largely disappeared, but contention has shifted from disputes over doctrine to disputes over specific issues, using insinuation and incremental pressure that the author calls cognitive warfare. Responses must follow what works. On the third, Huang contends that narrative matters more than fact, that non-ideological problems turn into ideological ones, and that blocking and deleting content are losing effect.

Huang proposes raising the ideological capacity and literacy of Party members and officials, alongside technical and legal measures, so that erroneous views lose influence. Huang also calls for a more open, inclusive attitude towards media outside the traditional mainstream. Read the original if you want a brief statement of how a Chinese Party-affiliated scholar frames online ideological work in 2024.
quoteEn: The mainstream is earned, not self-proclaimed; it is gained by expanding influence, not by taking up some position and resting on it.
quoteZh: 主流是获得的而非自得的，是通过扩大影响力而获得的，而非通过占据某种地位自得的

glossary.explanation: The Party's work of shaping thought, culture and public opinion, including media management and ideological education. It is treated as a core responsibility of Party organisations.
A term for contests over perception and thinking, seen here as an upgrade of earlier information, propaganda and public-opinion warfare.
A period in which, as the author describes it, narratives about facts carry more weight than the facts themselves.

t: The historical-materialist implications of building a modern Chinese civilization
zh: 建设中华民族现代文明的历史唯物主义意蕴
paras: Dong Jianming asks what historical materialism contributes to understanding the "new cultural mission" put forward by General Secretary Xi Jinping: building a modern civilization of the Chinese nation. The article argues that this mission is firmly grounded in Marx's theory of history and is both required by the times and an inevitable step in historical progress. It presents the mission as part of Xi Jinping's thought on culture and as a source of theoretical guidance for creating a new culture for the present era.

The piece is a short commentary, originally published in the China Social Sciences Today (中国社会科学报) on 5 June 2024. It is organised in three parts: the historical necessity of the mission, the role of culture in social development, and the intellectual and cultural traditions accumulated by the Chinese nation. Dong draws on Marx, Engels, Mao Zedong's \"On Contradiction\", the report to the 20th Party Congress (2022) and statements by Xi.

First, Dong applies the principle that the economic base ultimately determines the superstructure. In this account, modern China's cultural subjectivity crisis stemmed from underdeveloped productive forces, while the Party-led advance from \"standing up\" to \"becoming rich\" to \"becoming strong\" and the progress of Chinese modernization now provide the material basis for cultural confidence. Second, citing Engels, Dong rejects economic determinism: culture interacts with the base and other superstructural elements. Cultural subjectivity does not grow automatically from economic growth but must be consciously built. Dong contends that in Western capitalist societies culture is dominated by capital and serves exploitation and accumulation, becoming a fetter on the productive forces. Third, Dong stresses the relative independence of forms of social consciousness, so that Chinese civilization's inherited traditions matter alongside economic factors.

Dong concludes that shouldering the new cultural mission requires taking the Two Integrations, especially the \"second integration\" of Marxism with fine traditional Chinese culture, as the basic guide. Marxism, in this view, activates the genes of Chinese civilization, while traditional culture enriches Marxism, producing a new cultural life-form. Dong presents this as both an application and a further development of historical materialism. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Chinese commentators ground Xi Jinping's cultural thought in the classical Marxist base–superstructure framework.
quoteEn: Cultural subjectivity does not grow up spontaneously in the course of economic development.
quoteZh: 文化主体性并不会在经济发展的过程中自发地生长出来

glossary.explanation: Formula associated with Xi Jinping: integrating the basic tenets of Marxism with China's concrete realities (the first) and with fine traditional Chinese culture (the second).
The official term for China's own path of modernization, prominent in Party documents since the 20th Party Congress (2022).
A concept in recent Party discourse referring to a nation's self-conscious, autonomous standing in its own culture, associated with Xi's remarks on consolidating cultural subjectivity.
The body of Xi's statements on culture, officially formulated in 2023, covering cultural confidence, the new cultural mission and the integration of Marxism with Chinese tradition.
Xi Jinping's 2023 formulation of the cultural task of the new era, including building a modern civilization of the Chinese nation.

t: Holding firmly to the soul and the root of adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
zh: 坚守好马克思主义中国化时代化的魂和根
paras: Taking up Xi Jinping's statement that Marxism must not be abandoned as the "soul" and fine traditional Chinese culture must not be abandoned as the "root" of the process, Wu Haijiang and Jiang Hao ask what it means to hold to both. Their thesis is that doing so is the foundation and precondition of theoretical innovation in adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times. The piece appeared in the China Social Sciences Today (Zhongguo shehui kexue bao) in February 2024.

The commentary has three parts. The first treats Marxism as the soul (hunmai, the "soul vein"). The second treats fine traditional Chinese culture as the root (genmai, the "root vein"). The third argues that the two must be integrated, and lists what this integration brings. Throughout, the authors rely heavily on Xi Jinping's speeches and the report to the 20th Party Congress (2022).

On Marxism, the authors argue that it is a scientific truth with lasting vitality, resting on historical materialism and the theory of surplus value. They also present it as the guiding ideology on which the Party and the state were founded, and as the "spiritual calcium" of the Party's new journey. They say Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era has made original contributions to it. On the cultural root, they identify five features of Chinese civilization: continuity, innovation, unity, inclusiveness and peace. They claim each of these shapes the Chinese path. In their account, for example, unity makes national unification the core of China's core interests, and peace explains why China imposes neither its values nor its political system on others.

The authors conclude that the soul and the root must be "connected" so that the Party's theoretical innovation continues. They say this means injecting Chinese concepts, spirit and wisdom more deeply into Marxism. It also means building China's own autonomous knowledge system, with Marxism activating living elements of traditional culture. Finally, it means building a modern Chinese civilization as the cultural form of Chinese modernization. They present this as a contribution to human civilization with world-historical significance. Read the original if you want a concise statement of how Party theorists in 2024 framed the relationship between Marxism and traditional culture, and which Xi Jinping formulations they drew on.
quoteEn: Theoretical innovation must speak in new terms, but it cannot lose sight of its ancestors; forgetting one's origins amounts to severing the soul vein and the root vein, and in the end leads to the subversive error of losing both.
quoteZh: 理论创新必须讲新话，但不能丢了老祖宗，数典忘祖就等于割断了魂脉和根脉，最终会犯失去魂脉和根脉的颠覆性错误。

glossary.zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化
glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
glossary.explanation: A formula for the Party's project of fitting Marxism to China's conditions and to each new era. The "times" element was added to the older "sinicization of Marxism" in recent Party documents.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018.
The official term for China's own path to modernization, which the Party presents as distinct from Western models. It was elaborated at the 20th Party Congress (2022).
A goal Xi Jinping set for Chinese philosophy and social sciences in 2022. It calls for theories and concepts rooted in China's own experience and tradition.

t: The historical-materialist grounding of the new form of human civilization
zh: 人类文明新形态的唯物史观根据
paras: Ding Kuangyi asks what historical materialism contributes to understanding the "new form of human civilization" that Xi Jinping associates with Chinese modernization. The article opens from Xi's statement that Chinese modernization is rooted in traditional Chinese culture, embodies the essence of scientific socialism and shows a path different from Western modernization. Ding argues that this new civilizational form has a deep basis in historical materialism, and that the basis can be traced along three lines.

This short commentary, published in the Chinese Social Sciences Today on 11 April 2024, is organised in three sections. They cover innovation in the mode of production, the dialectical relation between material and spiritual civilization, and the idea of a "true community". Each section sets out the Marxist principle first and then applies it to Chinese modernization, with Western modernization as the contrast.

In the first section, Ding restates that the mode of production, the unity of productive forces and relations of production, underlies culture and civilization. The contradiction between the two drives changes in the economic base and superstructure, and so the rise and fall of civilizational forms. On this basis Ding presents new quality productive forces, technological innovation and adjustments to relations of production (public ownership, a mix of distribution principles, common prosperity) as innovations that reshape civilization. In the second section, Ding cites Marx, Engels and Lenin on the mutual influence of material and spiritual life. Ding describes Western modernization as pursuing abstract material wealth, producing consumerism, instrumental rationality, utilitarianism and individualism. Chinese modernization is portrayed as grounded in a "logic of the human being" rather than capital, with material growth as a means, not an end. The third section describes capitalist community as mediated by money, capital and the market, which Ding calls an inverted and alienated form producing atomised, lonely individuals. Ding contrasts this with Marx's "true community", the association of free individuals.

Ding concludes that Chinese modernization builds community at home through a governance community of shared construction, governance and benefit. Abroad it does so through a community with a shared future for mankind. The "true community" thus points, in Ding's account, to a civilization of equality, harmony and mutual help. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Chinese commentators link Xi Jinping's formulations on civilization to classical Marxist categories in a short newspaper format.
quoteEn: Chinese modernization is a development in which material and spiritual civilization are coordinated; it enhances the universality of people's needs, abilities and enjoyment, and shapes a new form of human civilization.
quoteZh: 中国式现代化是物质文明与精神文明相协调的发展，提升人的需要、才能、享用等的普遍性，塑造人类文明新形态。

glossary.explanation: The official concept of China's path to modernization, promoted by the Party leadership since the early 2020s as distinct from Western models.
A formulation in Party discourse describing Chinese modernization as creating a civilizational form different from Western modernization.
A concept introduced by Xi Jinping in 2023 for productive forces driven by technological innovation, strategic emerging industries and future industries.
An official goal of shared wealth for all people, stressed by the Party leadership as a requirement of socialism.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's concept for China's vision of international relations, presented as a guide for global governance.

t: Is the socialist ideal being reborn in the West?
st: Starting from the sharpening internal contradictions of the Western "elected system"
zh: 社会主义理想是否在西方重生？
zhSub: 从西方“民选体制”内部矛盾的激化谈起
paras: Zheng Ruolin asks whether the Western consensus that socialism died with the Soviet Union still holds. The author starts from Thomas Piketty's 2020 book Vivement le Socialisme!, in which the author of Capital in the Twenty-First Century says he now sees socialism as the best name for an alternative to capitalism. Zheng argues that Western capitalism's inequality is undermining the Western "elected system", and that this could lead either to a turn towards socialism or to a new era of conflict.

The short commentary takes Piketty's two conditions for capitalism's survival, equality and the environment, and concentrates on inequality. It then analyses the split between national industrial capital and transnational financial capital, and uses the United States as its main case. It compares the present to the situation a century ago.

Zheng cites Piketty's figures: the top 1% own 38.8% of global assets and the bottom 50% own 2%. In Zheng's account, the Western "democratic system" is really an "elected system" that depends on continuous growth and on economic superiority over other systems. Both conditions are eroding because of polarisation and China's rise. The author argues that globalisation once united the interests of the two forms of capital, but industrial capital now backs de-globalisation, with working-class support, while financial capital wants free movement. Zheng reads Trump's election and the Capitol riot as signs of this conflict and as a growth of the far right resembling the pre-war period.

Zheng concludes that it is unclear whether the present will produce a Western move towards socialism, as Piketty hopes, or a conflict of "all against all", perhaps war or nuclear war. The author notes that the West has historically tried to resolve internal crises through external war, and that this needs serious study. Read the original if you want a short Chinese-language view that links Piketty's turn to socialism with a class-fraction analysis of Western politics.
quoteEn: The so-called Western "democratic system" is in essence an "elected system", far removed from the genuine ideal of government of the people, by the people and for the people.
quoteZh: 西方所谓的“民主体制”实质上是一种“民选体制”，与真正的“民有、民治、民享”的理想差之远矣。

t: The historical-materialist basis of the new form of human civilization
zh: 人类文明新形态的唯物史观根据
paras: This short commentary, published in the Chinese Social Sciences Today in April 2024, asks what grounds in historical materialism support the claim that Chinese modernization amounts to a new form of human civilization. Starting from Xi Jinping's statement that Chinese modernization is a wholly new form of human civilization, different from the Western model, Ding argues that the concept rests on three historical-materialist foundations.

The article is organised in three short sections: innovation in the mode of production, the dialectical relationship between material and spiritual civilization, and the "true community". Each section first sets out the relevant principle from Marx, Engels or Lenin, then contrasts Western modernization with Chinese modernization as the author presents them.

In the first section Ding argues that civilizational forms ultimately derive from the mode of production, the unity of productive forces and relations of production, so that transforming productive forces is key to renewing civilization. Chinese modernization is said to advance this through technological innovation and new quality productive forces, and through adjusting relations of production: public ownership as the base, distribution combining work and factors of production, narrower income gaps and common prosperity. In the second section Ding holds that Western modernization pursues abstract material wealth, reduces rationality to instrumental reason and makes utilitarianism and individualism the basis of its spiritual life. Chinese modernization, by contrast, is said to coordinate material and spiritual civilization, treating wealth as a means rather than an end. In the third section Ding describes the capitalist "community" as mediated by money, capital and the market, producing atomised individuals and a lonely mass society, whereas Marx's "true community", the association of free individuals, overcomes this.

Ding concludes that Chinese modernization advances community-building domestically, through a social governance community built, governed and shared by all, and internationally, through a community with a shared future for mankind. In this account, the new form of human civilization points towards equality, harmony and mutual aid. Read the original if you want a compact example of how Chinese commentary derives the concept of a new form of human civilization from classical Marxist texts and contrasts it with Western modernization."
quoteEn: The transformation and upgrading of productive forces is the key to innovating human civilization.
quoteZh: 生产力的转型升级是创新人类文明的关键所在。

glossary.explanation: The official name for China's path of modernization, which Party leaders present as distinct from the Western model. It has been elaborated especially since the 20th Party Congress (2022).
A formulation that Xi Jinping and the Party use to describe the civilizational significance of Chinese modernization, as an alternative to Western modernization.
A concept promoted by Xi Jinping from 2023 for productive forces driven by technological innovation, strategic emerging industries and future industries.
An official goal of socialism with Chinese characteristics, stressing prosperity shared by all and narrower gaps between regions, urban and rural areas and income groups.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's foreign-policy and international-relations concept, calling for common development and cooperation among countries.

t: Holding fast to the soul and the root of adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
zh: 坚守好马克思主义中国化时代化的魂和根
paras: Wu Haijiang and Jiang Hao, in a commentary first published in China Social Sciences Today in February 2024, take up Xi Jinping's statement that the project of adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times rules out abandoning either Marxism, the "soul", or excellent traditional Chinese culture, the "root". The authors argue that holding fast to both is the foundation and precondition of theoretical innovation. Their thesis is that the two must be fused, not merely kept side by side.

The piece has three parts. The first sets out why Marxism must remain the soul. The second lists the features of the root in traditional culture. The third explains what follows in practice from joining the two. It leans throughout on Xi Jinping's speeches and the report to the 20th Party Congress (2022).

In the authors' account, Marxism is a scientific truth with lasting vitality: historical materialism and the theory of surplus value reveal the laws of social development and of capitalism. It is also the Party's fundamental guiding thought, linked to the Two Integrations. The authors credit Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era with a new leap in adapting Marxism. The root, they say, has five features: continuity, innovation, unity, inclusiveness and peace. They claim these features explain why China keeps to its own path and peaceful development, and why it imposes neither values nor political systems on others. Wu and Jiang warn that forgetting one's ancestors severs both soul and root and leads to a "subversive" error.

The authors conclude that Marxism's core ideas and the best of traditional culture must be linked, and name three outcomes. The first is continued Party theoretical innovation, with the nation's core ideas and wisdom injected more deeply into Marxism. The second is building China's own independent knowledge system, in which Marxism activates living elements of tradition. The third is building a modern Chinese civilization, a new cultural form for Chinese modernization, which they say carries world-historical significance. Read the original if you want a concise example of how official Party-theory commentary frames the relationship between Marxism and traditional culture.
quoteEn: Theoretical innovation must speak new words, but it cannot discard the old ancestors; forgetting one's origins amounts to severing the soul and the root, and ends in the subversive error of losing both.
quoteZh: 理论创新必须讲新话，但不能丢了老祖宗，数典忘祖就等于割断了魂脉和根脉，最终会犯失去魂脉和根脉的颠覆性错误。

glossary.zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化
glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
glossary.explanation: The official formula for the Party's project of fitting Marxism to China's conditions and to contemporary developments. The "times" element was added in recent years to the older notion of "sinification" of Marxism.
Xi Jinping's formula for combining Marxism's basic principles with China's concrete realities and with China's excellent traditional culture.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's current official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions and presented as the latest stage of Marxism adapted to China.
The official term for China's own path to modernization, which the Party says differs from Western models. It has been central to Party discourse since the 20th Party Congress (2022).
A metaphor in Xi Jinping's recent speeches. The "soul" is Marxism and the "root" is excellent traditional Chinese culture, and neither may be abandoned.

t: New changes in the ideological sphere under new technological conditions
zh: 新技术条件下意识形态领域新变
paras: This short commentary, first published in the Chinese Social Sciences Today in May 2024, asks how new technology is changing ideological work in China. Huang Xianghuai argues that, despite what the author describes as a fundamental turn for the better since the 18th Party Congress (2012), the 20th Party Congress report (2022) acknowledges many remaining challenges. The author calls for study of their new forms so that ideological work becomes more targeted, proactive and effective.

The article takes three features of the present in turn: the all-media communication landscape, the era of cognitive warfare, and the post-truth era. For each, Huang describes how the terrain of ideological contestation has shifted and what this requires of media organisations, institutions and Party members.

In Huang's account, self-media and capital have squeezed traditional mainstream media, so that mainstream opinion no longer holds its lead automatically: it is earned by expanding influence, not by occupying a position. Media should therefore be judged by whether they achieve their function, not merely by whether they discharge their duties. Huang describes non-mainstream ideologies as shifting from doctrinal disputes to disputes over specific issues, using insinuation and individual cases to unsettle public perception. The author calls this cognitive warfare, an escalation of earlier information and propaganda battles. In the post-truth era, Huang argues, narrative outweighs fact, and non-ideological problems readily acquire ideological content, so blocking and deleting lose effect.

Huang concludes that mainstream media should adopt a more open and inclusive attitude, matching tactics to how problems appear, and that Party members and cadres need stronger ideological ability and literacy, alongside technical and legal measures. Read the original if you want a brief, official-line view of how Chinese Party scholars frame ideological risk in the internet age.
quoteEn: The mainstream is earned, not self-proclaimed; it is gained by expanding influence, not assumed by occupying some position.
quoteZh: 主流是获得的而非自得的，是通过扩大影响力而获得的，而非通过占据某种地位自得的

glossary.explanation: The Party's efforts to shape thought, culture and public opinion in line with its official ideology, covering media, propaganda and education.
A term for efforts to influence how people perceive and judge events, here presented by the author as an upgrade of information, propaganda and public-opinion warfare.
A term for the integrated media environment combining traditional outlets, online platforms and self-media.

t: The historical-materialist implications of building a modern Chinese civilization
zh: 建设中华民族现代文明的历史唯物主义意蕴
source: Chinese Social Sciences Today (中国社会科学报), 5 June 2024
paras: This short commentary asks what historical materialism contributes to understanding the new cultural mission that General Secretary Xi Jinping has set out: building a modern civilization of the Chinese nation. Dong Jianming argues that the mission rests firmly on Marx's historical materialism and is both required by the times and an inevitable result of historical progress. Grasping this, the author says, helps readers understand the core of Xi Jinping's thought on culture and take up the mission.

The article is organised in three sections. The first treats the historical necessity of the mission through the base–superstructure relationship. The second discusses culture's role in social development. The third turns to the intellectual and cultural traditions that the Chinese nation has accumulated over its history. Dong draws on Marx, Engels and Mao Zedong's essay "On Contradiction", together with Xi Jinping's statements and the report to the 20th Party Congress (2022).

Dong's first move is that the economic base determines the superstructure only "in the last instance". In this reading, China's modern humiliation and its crisis of cultural subjectivity came from underdeveloped productive forces. The Party's leadership from "standing up" to "becoming prosperous" and "becoming strong", and the advance of Chinese modernization, now supply the material foundation for cultural confidence and independence. Second, citing Engels's letters, Dong rejects economic determinism: culture reacts on the economy and other superstructural elements. The author adds that cultural subjectivity does not grow spontaneously out of economic growth and must be built consciously. Dong characterises Western capitalist culture as dominated by capital, serving exploitation and eventually fettering the productive forces. Third, Dong invokes the relative independence of forms of social consciousness. Chinese civilization's "five outstanding features" (continuity, innovation, unity, inclusiveness and peacefulness) and the "Second Integration" of Marxism with fine traditional Chinese culture are presented as developing this point.

Dong concludes that the Two Integrations, especially the Second, must guide the mission. Marxism is said to activate the genes of Chinese civilization, while traditional culture enriches Marxism's cultural life, producing a new cultural organism. The article presents this as both applying and further developing historical materialism, and as a way to create a new culture for the present era. Read the original if you want a brief, Party-line account of how Xi Jinping's cultural thought is linked to classical Marxist texts on base, superstructure and relative autonomy.
quoteEn: Cultural subjectivity does not grow spontaneously in the course of economic development, nor does culture automatically promote the coordinated development of all areas of society as the economy grows; both depend on people's conscious construction.
quoteZh: 文化主体性并不会在经济发展的过程中自发地生长出来，文化本身也并不会在经济发展的过程中自动地发挥促进社会各领域协调发展的功能，这都有待人们的自为性建构。

glossary.explanation: A body of ideas on culture and ideology associated with Xi Jinping, formally put forward at a national work conference on propaganda and ideology in October 2023.

The formula of combining Marxism's basic tenets with China's concrete realities (the first) and with fine traditional Chinese culture (the second). The 'Second Integration' was stressed by Xi Jinping in 2023.
The idea that a nation holds a self-conscious, independent cultural identity and agency. In current Party discourse it is linked to cultural confidence and consolidating that identity.
The official term for China's path of modernization, set out in the report to the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is presented as distinct from Western models.

t: Plekhanov's critique of the "religious quest" and his exposition of Marxist atheism
st: A reading of "On the So-Called Religious Quest in Russia"
zh: 普列汉诺夫对“宗教探寻”的批判和马克思主义无神论的阐释
paras: Zhang Jiansong studies Georgi Plekhanov's long essay "On the So-Called Religious Quest in Russia", written after the defeat of the 1905 revolution under Stolypin's reaction. The article asks how Plekhanov used Marxist theory to answer the mystical currents of the time: "God-seeking" among bourgeois thinkers and "God-building" inside the Social-Democratic movement. Zhang argues that Plekhanov's rebuttal was theoretically sound and timely, and that it still offers lessons for religious work and ideological struggle in China today.

The article follows the three finished parts of the essay, as collected in the third volume of Plekhanov's selected philosophical works. It first treats "On Religion", the theoretical introduction. It then covers "Religion Again", which criticises Tolstoy, Lunacharsky and Gorky. Finally it covers the section on the Decadents, chiefly Merezhkovsky and Minsky. Zhang notes that a planned fourth article on the Vekhi group was never written. A short closing section draws contemporary lessons.

In Zhang's account, Plekhanov first defines religion as a fairly coherent system of ideas, feelings and activities, and traces animism, myth, totemism and the gods to the level of the productive forces and the hunting way of life. Zhang reads this as an application of the principle that social being determines social consciousness, and stresses that Plekhanov also allowed for interaction between consciousness and being. Armed with this, Plekhanov argues that every religion, including the "atheist religion" of Tolstoy, Lunacharsky and Gorky, necessarily involves spirits and the supernatural. He treats these quests as a response to the despair of the intelligentsia after defeat. Zhang adds that Plekhanov attacks the Decadents for individualism, fear of death and contempt for the workers' economic struggle, and for substituting a consolation that Feuerbach had already dismissed as illusion.

Zhang concludes that Plekhanov's critique steadied revolutionary morale and holds two lessons. One is to stay firmly Marxist, which Zhang contrasts with the Soviet collapse under Gorbachev and links to adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times. The other is to dare to struggle against erroneous trends, such as historical nihilism and certain abnormal religious phenomena in parts of China. Read the original if you want a detailed Chinese reading of Plekhanov's religious theory, or want to see how the history of Marxism is used to frame current ideological work.
quoteEn: Plekhanov's sword-drawing, fighting spirit in the face of erroneous trends of thought deserves our study.
quoteZh: 普列汉诺夫面对错误思潮的亮剑精神、斗争精神，值得我们学习。

glossary.zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化
glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
glossary.literal: the Sinicisation and modernisation of Marxism
glossary.explanation: Official formula for the continuing process of fitting Marxist theory to China's conditions and to the contemporary era. It is used in Party documents on theoretical development.
A current among some Russian Marxists, including Lunacharsky and Gorky, after 1905. It proposed a humanist "religion of socialism", and Plekhanov and Lenin opposed it.
The religious-philosophical search for God among Russian intellectuals after 1905, often tied to idealist and mystical thought.

t: Class-based environmental analysis
st: A new reading of The Condition of the Working Class in England
zh: 基于阶级的环境分析
zhSub: 《英国工人阶级状况》的一种新解读
paras: Liu Li asks how Engels's The Condition of the Working Class in England (1845) should be read now that class analysis and environmental analysis of the book usually run on separate tracks. The article argues that the work's distinctive contribution was to join the two for the first time, treating capitalist exploitation through an environmental lens. On this reading, Engels remained committed to Marxist class analysis, in contrast to the stratification, race, community and identity frameworks that Liu says dominate environmentalism since the 1960s.

The article draws on Engels's observations of Manchester, London, Liverpool and other industrial towns in 1842–1844. It is organised in four parts: how capital reshapes the environment in its natural, social and individual dimensions; class-based environmental differentiation and opposition; the environmental discipline and control of the working class; and a concluding section with four points. Liu sets Engels against Weber, Bourdieu, Giddens, Foucault and Braverman, and cites Ted Benton on Engels as an early ecological political thinker.

Liu's central claim is that the environment is neither external nor neutral under capitalism but distributes class positions. Four mechanisms are identified: environmental stratification, such as the concentric layout in which factory zones, middle-class streets and bourgeois suburbs are ranked by exposure to pollution; environmental identification by housing, occupation, age and sex; closure and segregation, including the hiding of slums behind respectable streets; and a classification of disease, with occupational illness and shortened lifespans. The author then argues that capital controls workers through sanitary policing, workhouses and the factory system, which operates through space, time and the body.

Liu concludes that labour exploitation and environmental exploitation are linked, and that housing and factories were the first and main sites of class segregation and control. In the author's reading, Engels traced the "social murder" of workers to the capitalist system itself and not to incidental abuses. The article also holds that environmental debates, including urban ecology and spatial justice, should not lose this class standpoint. Read the original if you study Engels's early work, Marxist ecology or class-based environmental justice and want a detailed reading of the book's environmental themes alongside Foucault and Weberian stratification theory.
quoteEn: The environment is not an external, neutral entity; in capitalist society it breeds, creates, uses and distributes the relations between people.
quoteZh: 环境不是一种外在的、中立的存在物，在资本主义社会，环境孕育、创造、使用和分配了人与人之间的关系
keywords: Condition of the Working Class in England

t: The deep logic and forms of cultural imperialism in Western left-wing discourse
zh: 西方左翼话语中文化帝国主义的深层逻辑与样态
paras: Du Min asks what lies beneath cultural imperialism as Western left-wing and postcolonial writers describe it, and how it works in the contemporary world. The article argues that its core is a "spiritual interest–control" logic, which goes beyond the profit logic of trade in cultural goods. Du holds that this logic appears in two forms, "knowledge imperialism" and "spiritual imperialism".

The article draws on thinkers including James Petras, Harold Innis, Syed Hussein Alatas, Syed Farid Alatas, Edward Said, Samir Amin, David Harvey and the Sri Lankan scholar Susantha Goonatilake. It first sets out the "commodity profit–capital" and "spiritual interest–control" dimensions. It then treats knowledge imperialism through intellectual property, research funding and academic dependence. Spiritual imperialism is traced from religious imperialism to non-governmental organizations, with cases from Africa, Central Asia and Sri Lanka.

On knowledge imperialism, Du argues that developed countries hold superiority in knowledge production and use patent regimes, such as TRIPS, to monopolise technology and extract excess profit. Du sets this "knowledge–hegemony–rent" logic against Lenin's "finance–monopoly–excess profit" logic. Dependent countries are said to suffer intellectual subordination, a "captive mind" and brain drain. On spiritual imperialism, Du contends that since the 1990s religious bodies and other NGOs have served as covert channels of Western values. The 2004 tsunami relief in Sri Lanka is offered as a typical case. Du also cites American legislation on international religious freedom and funding for training journalists as ways of legitimising this influence at home.

Du concludes that the two forms are complementary routes by which imperialism pursues its strategic interests under neo-colonial conditions. The article also holds that China's catching-up in knowledge and innovation has alarmed the United States. It notes that states such as Pakistan, Russia and Hungary have responded by expelling or banning foreign NGOs and strengthening ideological safeguards. Du presents these as forms of resistance to spiritual infiltration. Read the original if you want to see how a Chinese Marxist scholar draws on Western left and postcolonial sources to build a typology of cultural imperialism.
quoteEn: The "spiritual interest–control" logic is the core meaning of the structural system of cultural imperialism.
quoteZh: “精神利益-控制”逻辑才是文化帝国主义结构体系的核心要义。

glossary.explanation: The extension of imperialist domination into culture, through unequal relations in cultural power, media, knowledge and values. In this article it is analysed mainly through Western left-wing critics.
The article's term for the dominance of imperialist countries over knowledge and technology production. Intellectual property rules and academic dependence maintain it.
The article's term for ideological and religious penetration of other countries, in the author's account carried out increasingly through religious bodies and NGOs.
The author's name for the deep logic of cultural imperialism, which pursues strategic interests through ideological and intellectual control rather than direct trade profit.

t: Marx's thought on the "machine system" and its methodological implications
zh: 马克思的“机器体系”思想及其方法论意蕴
paras: Prompted by the rise of ChatGPT and debates over machines, technology and the fate of civilisation, Chen Zhong asks how artificial intelligence should be understood and what Marx would make of it. The article argues that Marx was not the first thinker to discuss the "machine system", but offered the most historically grounded and penetrating analysis of it. Its value, Chen contends, lies less in knowledge content than in method.

The article has three parts. The first reconstructs Marx's account of the machine system from The Poverty of Philosophy, the Communist Manifesto, the 1857–58 and 1861–63 manuscripts and Capital, drawing on commentary by Mumford, An Qinian, Zhang Yibing and Gao Qiqi. The second extracts the methodological features of that account. The third applies them to artificial intelligence and digitalisation.

Chen reads Marx's machine system in four dimensions: automated machinery, a society interconnected through machine industry, the replacement of workers' skills by machines (making workers appendages of capital-owned fixed capital), and the growing role of science. Methodologically, Marx starts from real historical processes and living relations rather than abstract concepts, as in his critique of Proudhon. He also judges machinery by its historical trend, as both progress in productive forces and a source of harm to labourers under capital. Applying this, Chen treats AI as an advanced "working machine" that externalises higher mental skills. In Chen's reading, its general progressive effect must be separated from the distribution of interests under particular institutions, and the idea of AI wholly replacing humans is science fiction rather than science.

Chen draws three points for the intelligent age: the machine system is the systematisation of civilisation, and humanity increasingly forms a community with a shared future; conscious public adjustment of institutions is needed to civilise it; and people should become the conscious core of the system, with institutions that let all parties share its gains equally. Chen speculates that Marx would use ChatGPT for routine textual work but would still study the intelligent machine system from "real life relations". Read the original if you want a Marxist-methodological framework for AI that draws closely on Marx's texts on machinery.
quoteEn: Artificial intelligence is merely a tool for mental labour with ever-growing functions; its wholesale replacement of humans is a literary proposition and a science-fiction concept, not a scientific proposition.
quoteZh: 人工智能只是一种功能日益增强的脑力劳动的工具而已，其对人的全面替代只是一个文学命题、科幻概念，而不是科学命题。

t: Upholding the socialist market economy is the necessary path for comprehensively deepening reform
zh: 坚持社会主义市场经济是全面深化改革的必由之路
source: Chinese Party and Government Cadres Forum (中国党政干部论坛), 2024 no. 6
paras: Writing in mid-2024, after Xi Jinping's 23 May symposium with entrepreneurs and experts, Dong Zhiyong asks why the socialist market economy must remain the basis of further comprehensively deepening reform. The article argues that, as reform enters what it calls a "deep-water zone", only unwavering adherence to the socialist market economy can keep consolidating the institutional strengths of Chinese modernization and drive reform forward.

The article has five parts. It first treats the socialist market economy as a product of adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times. It then presents it as a great creation of the Communist Party, traced through successive Party congresses from the 12th to the 15th. Next it credits the system with China's economic achievements, then sets out what upholding it implies for deepening reform, and ends with a short conclusion.

Dong contends that classical Marxism and Western neoclassical economics both assumed socialism and the market to be opposed, and that both drew mainly on Western experience. China, proceeding from the primary stage of socialism, held that planning and the market are both means of allocating resources and that the market economy is not the same as capitalism. Dong contrasts this with the Soviet model, whose partial reforms the author calls short-lived, and with the Soviet and East European turn to privatisation, which the author links to the collapse of those systems. The article credits the market's "decisive role" in resource allocation, citing shifts from planning targets to prices, from state protection to property-rights protection, and from officials to entrepreneurs, but insists that this role is not the "whole role". Party leadership, medium- and long-term planning and cross-cyclical macroeconomic regulation are presented as distinctive strengths.

Dong concludes that building a high-level socialist market economy is the necessary path for deepening reform and advancing Chinese modernization, and that the qualifier "socialist" must never be forgotten. Upholding it is said to mean shifting growth towards innovation and new quality productive forces, pursuing common prosperity, reforming ownership structures, balancing development with security, and expanding institutional opening up, which the author says offers a reference for other developing countries. Read the original if you want an official-line account of how Party theorists link the market economy, reform and Chinese modernization after the 20th Party Congress (2022).
quoteEn: We are developing the market economy under the overriding premise of Communist Party leadership and the socialist system, and we must never forget the qualifier "socialist".
quoteZh: 我们是在中国共产党领导和社会主义制度的大前提下发展市场经济，什么时候都不能忘了“社会主义”这个定语。

glossary.explanation: The Party's official term for China's own path to modernization, prominent since the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is presented as distinct from Western models.
The economic system formally adopted as the reform goal at the 14th Party Congress in 1992. It combines market mechanisms with public ownership as the main body and Party leadership.
An official thesis that China is still in an early, long phase of socialism with underdeveloped productive forces. It is used to justify market reforms and mixed ownership.
A concept introduced by Xi Jinping in 2023 for advanced productive forces driven by scientific and technological innovation rather than factor inputs.

glossary.zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化
glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
glossary.explanation: The official formula for developing Marxism in light of China's conditions and contemporary demands.
An official goal of broadly shared wealth, stressed under Xi Jinping, involving narrowing income gaps.

t: The peaceful character of Chinese civilisation and its world significance
zh: 中华文明的和平性及其世界意义
paras: Luo Wendong takes up a thesis from Xi Jinping's speech at the symposium on cultural inheritance and development: that the peaceful character of Chinese civilisation fundamentally determines China's role as a builder of world peace, contributor to global development and defender of the international order. The article, published in the China Social Sciences Today in July 2024, argues that peace is a defining trait and basic value of Chinese civilisation. In Luo's account, it has shaped China's own history and also bears on world peace and development.

The piece moves in three steps. It first traces the cultural roots and historical record of Chinese peacefulness, from classics such as the Book of Documents, the Book of Songs, the Doctrine of the Mean and Sunzi's Art of War to the Silk Road, Zhang Qian and Zheng He. It then turns to the People's Republic, covering the Five Principles of Peaceful Coexistence, Deng Xiaoping's reform-era foreign policy and Mao Zedong's statements against aggression. Finally it considers China's peace concepts and policies since the 18th Party Congress (2012).

Luo's central claim is continuity: values such as "harmony in diversity" and "winning without fighting" are said to have guided exchange through trade and cultural influence rather than conquest. Luo cites Bodde, Bertrand Russell and Jomo Kenyatta as outside observers who recognised this, and says China did not expand even when its economy was a third of world output. The article presents the Communist Party as inheriting this tradition. In its telling, China's rise to the second-largest economy came through hard work and opening-up cooperation, not colonial plunder. For the present, when it describes a world of conflict, hegemonism and deficits in peace, development, security and governance, Luo lists China's initiatives as its answer. These are the community with a shared future for mankind, the Belt and Road Initiative and the Global Development, Security and Civilization Initiatives.

Luo concludes that peace is the foundation of national stability and prosperity, and that China will keep to peaceful development and help build a community with a shared future for mankind. It is said to reject cultural hegemony, imposing its values or political system on others, and bloc politics. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party-affiliated scholars link classical Chinese culture to contemporary foreign-policy doctrine.
quoteEn: Loving peace and seeking development are valuable experience that the Chinese nation has drawn from historical laws, and are also the foremost common value it contributes to all humanity.
quoteZh: 爱和平、谋发展是中华民族从历史规律中总结出来的宝贵经验，也是贡献给全人类的首要的共同价值。

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: A concept promoted by Xi Jinping since around 2012–2013 as China's vision for international relations, stressing cooperation, shared security and common development.
An infrastructure and economic cooperation initiative launched by Xi Jinping in 2013, invoking the ancient Silk Road.
Principles of mutual respect for sovereignty, non-aggression, non-interference, equality and mutual benefit, and peaceful coexistence, jointly advanced by China, India and Myanmar in the 1950s.

glossary.zh: 全球发展倡议、全球安全倡议、全球文明倡议
glossary.pinyin: Quánqiú Fāzhǎn Chàngyì, Quánqiú Ānquán Chàngyì, Quánqiú Wénmíng Chàngyì
glossary.en: the Global Development, Security and Civilization Initiatives
glossary.explanation: Three initiatives put forward by Xi Jinping in 2021–2023 as China's proposals for global governance.

t: A panoramic examination of Mao Zedong's promotion of the innovative development of Chinese Marxist philosophy in the Yan'an period
zh: 延安时期毛泽东推进中国马克思主义哲学创新发展的全景式考察
source: Journal of Hunan University of Science and Technology (Social Sciences Edition), 2024 no. 3
paras: Wang Yan asks how Mao Zedong, during the Yan'an period (1935–1947), built Chinese Marxist philosophy and gave Marxist philosophy a 'Chinese form'. The article argues that Yan'an was the most important stage of this work. In Wang's account, Mao created the first theoretical form of Chinese Marxist philosophy by combining Marxist principles with China's concrete realities and with fine traditional Chinese culture.

The article has four main sections plus a conclusion. It begins with the two foundational texts, 'On Practice' and 'On Contradiction'. It then turns to Mao's account of what Chinese Marxist philosophy means and how it is generated, and to his philosophical work in three fields: military, political and methodological. It ends with the Rectification Movement, the establishment of the line of seeking truth from facts, and the Party's adoption of Mao Zedong Thought at the Seventh Congress (1945).

Wang first argues that the two essays gave a systematic philosophical basis to the ideological line of seeking truth from facts, in response to the dogmatism that had cost the revolution heavily. They drew critically on Soviet textbooks, for example by Mitin and Shirokov, while reorganising and extending their content. They also absorbed Chinese traditions, such as the unity of knowing and acting and the dialectics of the Book of Changes. Second, Wang reads Mao's call to 'sinify Marxism' (issued in 1938) as a two-way process: applying theory to Chinese conditions and raising Chinese revolutionary experience into theory. On the cultural side, Mao is said to have distinguished the feudal from the non-feudal in tradition, given old terms such as 'seeking truth from facts' new Marxist meanings, and translated Marxist language into national forms. Third, Wang shows Mao applying this philosophy to a Marxist military philosophy ('On Protracted War'), a political philosophy ('On New Democracy') and a methodology of thought, leadership and work.

Wang concludes that Chinese Marxist philosophy belongs to the Marxist philosophical tradition while taking a form distinct from Marxism elsewhere. It emerged from repeated struggle against dogmatism, from reflection on the Chinese–Western cultural debate, and from the summing up of experience in making Marxism concrete. Wang says it thereby 'realised the modern ideological enlightenment of the Chinese people'. Read the original if you want a detailed, source-based account of how the Yan'an texts and the Rectification Movement are presented in Chinese scholarship as the origin of Chinese Marxist philosophy.
quoteEn: Chinese Marxist philosophy is the theoretical result of the unity of the two processes of 'making'.
quoteZh: 中国马克思主义哲学就是两个“化”之过程相统一的理论结果。

glossary.explanation: An old Chinese phrase from textual scholarship that Mao Zedong redefined in 1941 as a Marxist principle. It became the core of the Chinese Communist Party's ideological line.

Mao Zedong's call, made at the Sixth Plenum of the Sixth Central Committee in 1938, to apply Marxism to Chinese conditions and give it Chinese forms. The Party now uses it in the wider formula 'adapting Marxism to the Chinese context'.
An ideological campaign in the Party in Yan'an from 1942 that targeted dogmatism, subjectivism and 'Party stereotype' writing. It consolidated Mao Zedong's leadership and line.
Mao Zedong's theory, set out in 1940, of a transitional stage of revolution led by the proletariat and aimed at imperialism, feudalism and bureaucrat capital. It was to precede socialism in China.
The Party's term for the Sinified Marxism-Leninism associated with Mao. The Seventh Party Congress in 1945 wrote it into the Party constitution as a guiding ideology.

t: Soft narratives of historical nihilism: endogenous mechanisms and countermeasures
zh: 历史虚无主义软性叙事：内生机制与应对策略
paras: Luo Hongjie takes up a shift in how historical nihilism, which the article treats as a harmful erroneous trend and a political problem, is spread. Since the 18th Party Congress (2012), Xi Jinping has repeatedly called for resisting it openly, and scholars and mainstream media have criticised it widely. Luo argues that, with digital technology, it has moved from "hard" to "soft" and from explicit to implicit narratives, which makes it harder to recognise and more likely to be believed. The article sets out to describe these forms, explain how they work and propose responses.

The article moves in four steps. It first identifies two shifts: from grand narratives to micro-level "playful retellings" (personal memoirs, trivial details), and from abstract sophistry to embodied, audiovisual "performance" (short videos, newly compiled histories). It then describes four soft forms: everyday agenda-setting, emotive discourse, covert images and immersive audio-visual embedding. Next it analyses three internal mechanisms, and finally it sets out countermeasures.

For the mechanisms, Luo proposes a sequence of "concealment–attraction", "consumption–stirring" and "interpellation–alienation". Nihilist content attaches to media that are easy to hide in and attractive, such as memes, short videos, games and murder-mystery role-play. Consumption then moves audiences from receiving to accepting the content. Drawing on Althusser's notion of interpellation, Luo holds that repeated exposure turns spontaneous reactions into conscious ones. Audiences are then "alienated" in their values and view of history, and become carriers of the trend themselves. Examples include the claim that burning the soldier Qiu Shaoyun alive contradicts physiology, jokes about Lu Xun's portrait and game versions of historical figures.

Luo's response has three parts: effective identification, rational criticism and active construction. Identification means reviewing topics, discourse, images and audio-visual content, including platform screening and regulation of films, lyrics and games. Criticism means refuting the essence, the implicit mechanism and typical cases. Construction means establishing a Marxist view of history and a scientific view of "perceptual activity", and building the mainstream ideology's own soft narrative system at national, institutional and individual levels. Read the original if you study how Chinese scholars frame digital media, popular culture and ideological work in the fight against historical nihilism.
quoteEn: Soft narrative methods, to a certain extent, increase the likelihood that people wrongly believe historical nihilism and make it harder for us to identify it.
quoteZh: 软性化的叙事方式在一定程度上增加了人们误信历史虚无主义的可能性，增添了我们识别历史虚无主义的难度。

glossary.explanation: In official Chinese discourse, a label for views that are said to distort or negate the Party's history, its leaders and its achievements. Xi Jinping has repeatedly called for opposing it.
The author's term for indirect, entertaining, everyday-style ways of conveying a message, as opposed to openly argued "hard" ones.
The officially promoted Marxist and Party-led value system, which the author says must occupy the ideological field.
Louis Althusser's concept (Chinese translation of interpellation) for how ideology addresses individuals and turns them into subjects.

t: A theoretical analysis of new quality productive forces and paths for cultivating them
zh: 新质生产力的学理分析与培育路径
source: Shanghai Economic Review (Shanghai Jingji Yanjiu), 2024 no. 5
paras: Since Xi Jinping first raised the term in Heilongjiang in September 2023, "new quality productive forces" has become a central economic concept. Cheng Enfu and Liu Meiping take up three questions: what the concept means, what institutional conditions it requires, and how it can be cultivated. Their answer is that new quality productive forces are defined by new production factors, new science and technology, and strategic new industries. They say these can develop properly only within socialist relations of production under Party leadership.

The article is organised in three main parts. The first analyses new quality productive forces along the three dimensions of factors, technology and industry. The second discusses the relations of production that support them: the dialectic between productive forces and socialist relations of production, the roles of government and market, and state-owned enterprises. The third sets out cultivation paths: new mechanisms, new fields of application, and a peaceful world environment. A short conclusion follows.

On factors, the authors argue that information, data and networks have become core production factors. In their account these factors produce "intelligent labourers" and a digital economy that can steer traditional factors, including capital. On technology, they hold that new quality productive forces arise from cultural, institutional, basic-science and industrial revolutions together, and that frontier basic research is the source of original innovation. They say China needs a full group of high technologies, to be developed through a new national system, to resist external "chokehold" pressures. On relations of production, they hold that public ownership as the mainstay, a government that regulates markets, and strong state-owned enterprises keep capital under control and guide the new forces towards common prosperity. They cite platform monopolies and the real-estate sector as areas needing regulation, and Huawei's Mate60 Pro and its 5.5G chips as evidence of industrial upgrading.

The authors also argue that war and the "new imperialism" obstruct new quality productive forces, while these forces in turn promote just exchange and peace. They conclude that new quality productive forces are the most important route to Chinese modernization and to catching up with the developed West. They call for Party leadership, full use of the socialist economic system, and coordination of new factors, technologies and industries. Read the original if you want a political-economy reading of new quality productive forces that links technology and industrial policy to public ownership, state enterprises and anti-hegemony arguments.
quoteEn: New quality productive forces are productive forces whose core factors are informatised and which are able to steer capital.
quoteZh: 新质生产力是核心要素信息化并且能够驾驭资本的生产力。

glossary.explanation: A concept Xi Jinping first used in September 2023. It refers to advanced productive forces driven by technological breakthroughs, new industries and new factors of production, and is presented as a basis for high-quality development.
The official name for China's path of modernization, set out by the Party since the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is presented as distinct from Western models.
An official goal of shared wealth for all, stressed under Xi Jinping as a defining feature of socialism with Chinese characteristics.

t: Lenin's critique of non-Marxist currents of thought in Russia and its implications for contemporary China
zh: 列宁对俄国非马克思主义思潮的批判及其对当代中国的启示
paras: Jia Shupin asks how Lenin identified and refuted the non-Marxist currents that flourished in Russia around the turn of the twentieth century, and what this offers China today. The article argues that such currents typically present themselves as 'developing' Marxism, which makes them more deceptive. Studying Lenin's critique, in Jia's view, helps in recognising the harm of present-day currents in a complex ideological struggle.

The article has three parts. The first describes four currents the author treats as Russian variants of Bernstein's revisionism: Menshevism, economism, Narodism (populism) and Machism. The second sets out Lenin's criticism of each. The third draws lessons for contemporary China.

Jia reads Lenin's critiques as defences of Marxism's organisational, political, economic and philosophical foundations. Against the Mensheviks, Lenin upheld a centralised party of committed members, with democratic centralism in place of a loose, self-governing association. Against the economists, he argued that socialist consciousness must be 'instilled' from outside the spontaneous labour movement by an organisation of revolutionaries. Against the Narodniks, he held that capitalism's development in Russia was objectively necessary and historically progressive, and against Mach's followers he defended the partisanship of philosophy and the primacy of matter. Jia adds that Lenin kept the party close to the masses, warning that separation from them was among its gravest dangers.

For China, Jia calls for upholding Marxism's guiding position and the Party's leadership over ideology and culture, drawing on the lessons of the Soviet collapse. The author names historical nihilism, neo-liberalism, the 'end of ideology' thesis and online-driven currents as threats. Jia proposes better discernment among social trends, firm and open rebuttal of erroneous views, and stronger theoretical education, including study of the 'Four Histories' and of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era. Read the original if you want to see how a Chinese Marxist journal draws on Lenin's polemics to frame current ideological work.
quoteEn: Only by arming its mind with Marxism and building a solid ideological safeguard can the proletarian party fundamentally eliminate the harmful influence of bourgeois ideas and act as a good ideological leader.
quoteZh: 无产阶级政党只有用马克思主义武装头脑，筑牢思想保障体系，才能从根本上破除资产阶级思想观念的不良影响，做好思想领导者

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018.
In official Chinese usage, a label for views that question or negate the Party's revolutionary history and established historical narratives.
The Leninist organisational principle, combining discussion with binding unity of action and subordination of minority to majority.
A Party education term for the history of the Party, of the People's Republic, of reform and opening up, and of socialist development.

t: The essence of law: examining the relations between law, state and society
st: Rereading Marx's Critique of Hegel's Philosophy of Right
zh: 法的本质：从法与国家及社会关系 层面进行的审视
zhSub: 再读马克思《黑格尔法哲学批判》
paras: Xiong Guangqing asks what Marx's early Critique of Hegel's Philosophy of Right reveals about the essence of law. The author argues that earlier readings often overlooked Marx's legal concerns, and that the work is Marx's first exploration of the nature of law. In Xiong's account, it marks the start of his critique of bourgeois legal thought and a turn towards historical and dialectical materialism.

The article reads the text from a legal angle, drawing also on philosophy and political science. After a section on Hegel's Philosophy of Right and Marx's reasons for criticising it, four parts follow. They treat the relation of state and society, the class character of the state, the internal links among law, state and society, and the state as the embodiment of class and civil society. Xiong draws on the Introduction to the Critique, the Communist Manifesto, The German Ideology and Engels to show how Marx's views developed.

Xiong's central claim is that Marx corrected Hegel's inversion of the relation between state and civil society. Hegel derived the state from the absolute Idea. Marx held instead that family and civil society are the presuppositions of the state, which in the author's reading establishes law's objectivity. Xiong then argues that Marx exposed the class nature of the Prussian state and of Hegel's defence of constitutional monarchy, since the state protects private property and law expresses the will of the ruling class. Marx's treatment of monarchy, bureaucracy and legislature as unreconciled elements of the state is read as showing law's material determination. Law, in this reading, is a product of class and society, conditioned by material life and not a tool the ruling class can use at will.

Xiong concludes that the work set the intellectual foundation for Marxist theory and for Marx's later deepening of his account of law. It also helped move Marx from revolutionary democracy towards communism. The author highlights Marx's preference for democracy, in which the people create the constitution and popular sovereignty is realised, and reads it as pointing towards a "new state system", which Xiong identifies with the dictatorship of the proletariat. Read the original if you study the early Marx, Marxist jurisprudence or Chinese scholarly readings of the Critique of Hegel's Philosophy of Right.
quoteEn: One of the most brilliant achievements of the Critique of Hegel's Philosophy of Right is that Marx put forward the view that civil society determines the state and law.
quoteZh: 《黑格尔法哲学批判》这部著作最光辉的成就之一就是，马克思提出了市民社会决定国家和法。

glossary.explanation: Hegel's term (bürgerliche Gesellschaft) for the sphere of private economic and social relations between family and state. Marx treats it as the material basis that determines the state and law.
Hegel's supreme spiritual substance, which the article presents as the core of his idealist system and the source from which he derives state and society.

keywords: Critique of Hegel's Philosophy of Right

t: Comparing the "two systems": three patterns of modernization theory and practice
zh: “两制”比较：现代化理论与现代化实践的三种样态
source: Reform and Strategy (Gaige yu Zhanlüe), 2024 no. 2
paras: Zheng Yifan and Zhou Miao ask how modernization theory and practice have developed under capitalism and socialism, and what this means for Chinese modernization.
