Read the original if you want a representative example of how official Party commentary justifies China's democratic criteria and contests Western democratic standards.
quoteEn: Whole-process people's democracy works and is truly effective precisely because it has grown out of China's own social soil; to keep thriving in future, it too must be deeply rooted in that soil.
quoteZh: 全过程人民民主之所以行得通、真管用，就是因为它是从中国的社会土壤中生长起来的，未来要继续茁壮成长，也必须深深扎根于中国的社会土壤。

glossary.explanation: A concept put forward by Xi Jinping after the 18th Party Congress (2012). The Party presents it as a form of socialist democracy in which people take part in every stage of governance, not only in elections.
China's fundamental political system, a hierarchy of congresses from the National People's Congress down to local levels, which the constitution makes the organs of state power.

glossary.en: the people being masters of the country
glossary.literal: the people act as masters of the house
glossary.explanation: A standard Party formulation for the essence of socialist democracy, meaning that the people hold state power.

t: Learning dialectics from Comrade Mao Zedong
zh: 向毛泽东同志学习辩证法
paras: Marking the 130th anniversary of Mao Zedong's birth, Qu Qingshan asks what Mao's dialectical thought contributed and why Party members should study it today. Taking its cue from Xi Jinping's speech of 26 December 2023, the article argues that Mao's dialectics forms a core part of Mao Zedong Thought and gave the Chinese revolution and construction a "spiritual weapon". Qu holds that learning it remains necessary for advancing Chinese modernization and the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation.

The article has three parts. The first surveys how Mao's dialectics guided the New Democratic Revolution, socialist construction, Party building, and the making of strategy and tactics, drawing on texts such as On Protracted War, On the Ten Major Relationships and the 1939 preface to The Communist. The second assesses its place in the Party's intellectual history. The third turns to what studying it means in the era of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era.

Qu's central claim is that Mao's dialectics has three sources: the basic tenets of Marxism, fine traditional Chinese culture, and the concrete realities of China. Qu says Mao developed the law of the unity of opposites and the principle of the universality and particularity of contradiction, which laid a methodological basis for adapting Marxism to Chinese conditions. The article presents Mao's use of terms such as "contradiction" and "unity of knowing and doing", and of proverbs and stories, as creative transformation of Chinese tradition. It also describes Mao's dialectics as a "dialectics of practice" drawn from the experience of victories and defeats.

Qu calls for the Party to treat Marxist philosophy as its "essential skill", study materialist dialectics, and make the "six musts" from the 20th Party Congress (2022) the Party's new "common language". Qu also argues that the Two Integrations, especially the second, open a new horizon for dialectics and continue the adaptation of Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times. Read the original if you want an official Party-journal account of how Mao's philosophy is presented as a source for current ideological campaigns and for Xi Jinping Thought.
quoteEn: Comrade Mao Zedong's dialectical thought is a dialectics of practice, the crystallisation of thought that unites knowledge with practice, theory with reality, and the transformation of the subjective world with that of the objective world.
quoteZh: 毛泽东同志的辩证法思想，是实践的辩证法，是认识与实践相结合、理论与实际相联系、改造主观世界与改造客观世界相统一的思想结晶。

glossary.explanation: Formula in Xi Jinping-era Party theory: combining the basic tenets of Marxism with China's concrete realities (the first) and with fine traditional Chinese culture (the second).
Official term for the Party's path of modernization, set out prominently at the 20th Party Congress in 2022 as distinct from Western models.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.literal: great revival of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: Official goal of restoring China's national strength and international standing, central to Party discourse since the 18th Party Congress (2012).
Six principles summarising the stand, viewpoint and method of Xi Jinping Thought, set out in the report to the 20th Party Congress in 2022.

t: Zhou Enlai and the Nanchang Uprising of 1 August
zh: 周恩来与八一南昌起义
source: Studies on the History of the Chinese Communist Party (Zhonggong dangshi yanjiu), 2024 no. 1
paras: Written for the 126th anniversary of Zhou Enlai's birth, this article asks how to understand Zhou's part in the 1 August 1927 Nanchang Uprising and how to assess the uprising's historical standing. Zhou had neither Mao Zedong's years in the new army nor Zhu De's formal military training. Shi argues that his earlier experience made him the natural leader of the uprising. Shi also argues that the uprising should be seen as part of the Party's exploration of a Chinese revolutionary road, not as a mere failure of 'urban-centred' thinking.

The article has four parts. The first traces Zhou's career from 1924 to 1927: Guangzhou, the Whampoa Academy's political department, the two Eastern Expeditions, four months administering the East River region, the Ye Ting Independent Regiment, the Shanghai workers' uprising and the response to Chiang Kai-shek's coup. The second narrates the uprising, the southward march, the defeats around Shantou, Zhu De's 'three reorganizations' in southern Jiangxi, and Zhou's escape to Hong Kong. The third reassesses the uprising's status. The fourth follows Zhou's later work in the central leadership.

Shi's central move is to separate historical evaluation from historical lessons. In 1927 no choice existed between urban insurrection and encirclement of the cities from the countryside, so Shi says the uprising cannot be faulted for lacking a later insight. Shi treats it as exploration, comparing failures to a red traffic light that warns 'no road this way'. Shi lists its significance as the first armed resistance to the Kuomintang, the beginning of an independent Party-led army, and the start of the agrarian revolutionary war. Quoting Zhou's own later self-criticism, Shi accepts that the main error was marching far south instead of carrying out land revolution locally.

Shi concludes that the uprising belongs to the opening of the sinicization of Marxism, citing Hu Jintao's 2007 remark, and that Zhou was one of the great explorers of that road. After 1927, Shi says, Zhou guided the remnants of the uprising troops towards Jinggangshan and the Hailufeng base, and opposed 'putschist' leftism. Shi also credits Zhou with promoting Mao and Zhu's armed base-building and arguing the case for rural revolution to the Comintern. Read the original if you want a detailed Party-history account of Zhou's military role and of how current Chinese scholarship reframes the Nanchang Uprising within the Party's search for its revolutionary road.
quoteEn: Since it was exploration, that is, 'crossing the river by feeling the stones', there would be successes and also failures.
quoteZh: 既然是探索，也就是“摸着石头过河”，就会有成功的，也有不成功的。

glossary.explanation: The Party's term for applying Marxism's basic principles to China's concrete conditions and developing them in Chinese form. The article presents the Nanchang Uprising as part of its opening phase.
The early Party line, modelled on the Russian October Revolution, that revolution should rest on urban workers' uprisings. Later Party history contrasts it with the rural road associated with Mao.
The Party's programme of redistributing land from landlords to peasants. It gave its name to the 'agrarian revolutionary war' period of 1927–1937.
Zhu De's ideological, organizational and military consolidation of the surviving uprising troops in late 1927. Party history treats it as a model of 'political army-building'.

t: Mazyar and Marxist historiography in Republican China
zh: 马札亚尔与民国马克思主义史学界
source: Historical Theory Studies (Shixue lilun yanjiu), 2024 no. 2
paras: Li Ziqiang asks how the Hungarian-born Comintern scholar Ludwig Madyar (Mazyar, 1891–1937), the best-known exponent of the Asiatic mode of production, was received by Chinese Marxist historians in the Republican period, and why he has become a marginal and silenced figure in Chinese scholarship. The article argues that a political-history framework has reduced Madyar to a Trotskyist label. Li holds that a scholarly reassessment shows his work prompted Chinese historians to deepen their grasp of historical materialism and to rethink the particularity of China's path.

The article has three parts. The first surveys the translations of Madyar's Chinese rural economy study and his later Outline of the Chinese Economy, along with the publishers' promotion, reviews and varied reactions of Chinese scholars. The second traces how his image shifted from international authority to Trotskyist and finally "counter-revolutionary", through the 1931 Leningrad discussion, the 1930s and the 1940s. The third weighs the weaknesses of his theory and the ways Chinese Marxist historians sublated it.

Li argues that Chinese reactions mixed political, scholarly and national-sentiment factors. Trotskyist sympathisers tended to back Madyar, while Lü Zhenyu, Jian Bozan and others criticised him, often with real engagement. After the Soviet verdict of 1931 and the consolidation of a unified historical-materialist paradigm around 1938–39, criticism became ideological, and from 1949 Madyar was fused with the Trotskyists. Li identifies his fatal flaw as a contradiction between his Asiatic theory and his own evidence, which pointed to landlord–peasant exploitation and thus to feudalism. He also sees an over-reliance on natural-environment explanations and a European yardstick. Yet Li credits Madyar with prompting agrarian-economy research by Chen Hansheng and others and with forcing a rebalancing of the general and the particular, which led Lü Zhenyu and Hou Wailu beyond the "variant" theory.

Li concludes that the Asiatic mode of production may be a "false problem", but a century of debate has left a rich scholarly legacy. He calls for abandoning binary thinking, recognising the historical relativity of orthodoxy and heresy, and avoiding a mechanical match between the Asiatic mode and the Chinese road. Li presents this clearing-up of the legacy as a necessary step in adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times. Read the original if you study the Asiatic mode of production debate, the Chinese social history controversy or the intellectual history of Chinese Marxist historiography and want detailed sources on Madyar's reception.
quoteEn: Madyar's theory spurred Chinese scholars to rebalance the relationship between the general and the particular, and in doing so advanced the adjustment and deepening of Chinese Marxist historiography.
quoteZh: 马札亚尔学说促使中国学者对于一般性与特殊性关系作出再平衡的努力，进而推动着中国马克思主义史学研究的调整与深化。

glossary.explanation: A term from Marx's 1859 Preface for a distinct pre-capitalist social form, often linked to state landownership, village communities and despotism. Whether it applies to China was long disputed among Marxists.
A debate of the late 1920s and 1930s among Chinese intellectuals over the nature of Chinese society and its stages of historical development, closely tied to disputes over revolutionary strategy.
The Chinese rendering of Hegel's Aufhebung: to criticise and discard a theory while preserving and developing its useful elements.

glossary.zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化
glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
glossary.explanation: An official formula for applying Marxism to China's conditions and to the present era. The term 'of our times' was added in recent Party documents.

t: An interpretation of Marx and Engels's methodology of investigation and research
zh: 马克思恩格斯的调查研究方法论阐释
paras: Liu Ying asks what methodological principles guided Marx and Engels's investigation and research (diaocha yanjiu), and what they offer to present-day practice. The article starts from the Party's description of investigation and research as its "family heirloom" and from Mao Zedong's remark that scientific communism was reached only after a lifetime of such work. Liu argues that, although Marx and Engels never used the term, each step towards scientific socialism was in substance investigation and research, and that their methods still give guidance in the new era.

Published in Theoretical Exploration in 2024, the article sets out five principles in turn and then a short conclusion. They are: standing on the proletarian position; combining problem awareness with a problem orientation; combining typical with general surveys; combining investigation with research; and organising and institutionalising the work. Liu draws on Marx's articles on the Moselle, his 1880 Workers' Inquiry, Engels's Letters from the Wuppertal and The Condition of the Working Class in England, the Brussels Communist Correspondence Committee and the International Working Men's Association.

In Liu's account, investigation as such has no class position, but its use does. Marx and Engels worked for proletarian liberation in their aims, objects and findings, whereas bourgeois scholars, in Liu's view, distorted facts to hide class contradictions. Liu argues that Marx and Engels focused on fundamental questions of their era rather than isolated social problems. They treated England as the typical site of mature capitalism, while the International's statistical committees pursued general surveys of workers' conditions. Liu stresses that gathering evidence, from fieldwork and from libraries and blue books, was only a first step: the decisive stage was analysis, summed up in the saying "three parts investigation, seven parts research". Liu also emphasises the correspondence committees and the International's rules as ways of making investigation collective and regular.

In the conclusion Liu draws lessons for today. Investigation must be people-centred, and Liu cites Xi Jinping's 1988 inquiry in Ningde and the "Four Down to the Grassroots" system as examples. Liu adds that it must be problem-oriented, combine breadth with typical cases, and turn scattered impressions into systematic understanding, as with the more than fifty inquiries Xi made before the "targeted poverty alleviation" approach. Liu also endorses the Party Central Committee's call to make investigation a long-term mechanism and routine work. Read the original if you want a concise, Party-line overview of how Chinese scholars link Marx and Engels's research practice to current calls for investigation and research.
quoteEn: Investigation establishes the truth of a problem; research grasps its essence.
quoteZh: 调查的是问题的真相，研究的是问题的本质。

glossary.explanation: A Party working method that combines fact-finding on the ground with analysis, strongly associated with Mao Zedong. It is regularly promoted in official campaigns, including the 2023 call to step up such work across the Party.
A work system that Xi Jinping is said to have introduced in Ningde, Fujian, in the late 1980s. It has officials go to the grassroots to hear public views, handle petitions and solve problems.
The approach to poverty reduction associated with Xi Jinping from 2013, which identifies poor households individually and designs measures for each.

keywords: The Condition of the Working Class in England

t: The logic behind the formation of Marx's philosophical discourse: a discourse perspective
zh: 从话语视角看马克思哲学的生成逻辑
source: Journal of Zhengzhou University of Light Industry (Social Science Edition), 2024 no. 1
paras: Liu Ying and Yang Yi ask how Marx's philosophical discourse was formed and what logic it followed. They treat Marx's philosophical revolution as also a revolution in discourse, which they define as a system of linguistic signs organised by a certain logical structure. Starting from Xi Jinping's calls to build a philosophy and social science discourse system with Chinese characteristics, the authors argue that returning to the original context of Marx's discourse can support that task. Their thesis is that its formation rests on four paired logics, each a unity of two sides.

The article is organised in four sections: speculative and realist logic; implicit and explicit logic; critical and constructive logic; and revolutionary and practical logic. It follows Marx's path from his doctoral dissertation and the Rheinische Zeitung period, through the Hegelian Philosophy of Right critique, the Economic and Philosophic Manuscripts of 1844 and The Holy Family, to the Theses on Feuerbach and The German Ideology. It draws on Hegel, Feuerbach, Deleuze and Althusser's symptomatic reading as points of reference.

The authors argue that Marx moved from Hegelian speculation, through Feuerbach's humanism, to a realist logic grounded in practice. They hold that this shift appears on the surface as changes in terms and categories, for example from 'alienated labour' to 'relations of production'. Beneath it runs an implicit line, which the authors identify as the era's question of capital's appropriation of labour and the emancipation of the proletariat. In their account, terms sometimes lagged behind thought: 'human essence' and 'species' were kept while their meaning changed. They contrast Hegel's self-determining concept, as in his idealised notion of labour, with Marx's concepts drawn from real productive life. They conclude that Marx's discourse is both critical of the world and put into practice, unlike the Young Hegelians' 'phrase-revolution'.

The authors conclude that Marx's discourse differs from speculative philosophy in one respect: practice. They say it works as a material force aimed at changing the world and guiding the proletariat. They present this as theoretical support for building a Marxist-guided academic discourse system in contemporary China. Read the original if you want a close, text-by-text account of how Marx's categories changed between 1841 and 1846, as seen by Chinese scholars of the history of Marxism.
quoteEn: The formation of Marx's philosophical discourse is a process of continual movement from speculative logic to realist logic, and also a process in which the two are brought into unity.
quoteZh: 马克思哲学话语的生成是从思辨逻辑不断向现实逻辑转变的过程，也是二者实现统一的过程。

t: The deep logic and forms of cultural imperialism in Western left discourse
zh: 西方左翼话语中文化帝国主义的深层逻辑与样态
paras: Du Min asks what lies beneath cultural imperialism as it is analysed by Western left and critical scholars. The article argues that, besides a "commodity profit–capital" logic, cultural imperialism rests on a deeper logic of "spiritual interest–control", in which cultural exchange serves the strategic interests of imperialist states and ideological domination matters more than trade volumes.

Drawing on James Petras, Harold Innis, Edward Said, Syed Hussein Alatas, Syed Farid Alatas, Samir Amin, David Harvey and others, Du divides this logic into two forms. The first is "knowledge imperialism", based on technological hegemony and control. The second is "spiritual imperialism", based on ideological penetration. The article treats each form in turn, with examples from Asia, Africa, Latin America and the former Soviet space.

On knowledge imperialism, Du describes a sense of civilisational superiority inherited from colonial rule and a monopoly over knowledge production backed by intellectual property regimes such as the TRIPS agreement. Du also cites figures on patents and research spending. On this account, a "knowledge–hegemony–rent" logic differs from Lenin's finance-capital monopoly. It leaves dependent states with intellectual dependence, a brain drain and what Alatas calls the "captive mind" and the intellectual "comprador". Spiritual imperialism is traced from religious imperialism to non-governmental organisations, which Du says have become agents of Western values since the 1990s. Du cites Soros-funded foundations, the post-tsunami conversions and Sinhala Buddhist backlash in Sri Lanka, and US measures such as the International Religious Freedom Act. Du argues that this penetration is more concealed than old colonial methods.

Du concludes that the two forms are complementary routes to imperialist strategic interests in the post-colonial world. Du adds that China's catch-up in knowledge production has, in this reading, alarmed the United States. Spiritual penetration, the article claims, tends to provoke resistance, and Du points to Pakistan's expulsion of international aid organisations in 2018 and Russia's 2015 bans on US foundations. Read the original if you want to see how a Chinese Marxist scholar draws on Western and postcolonial critics to frame knowledge, religion and NGOs as instruments of imperialism, with case material from Sri Lanka and Central Asia.
quoteEn: The "spiritual interest–control" logic is the core essence of the structural system of cultural imperialism.
quoteZh: “精神利益-控制”逻辑才是文化帝国主义结构体系的核心要义。

glossary.explanation: The extension of imperialist domination into culture, through the export of media, values and knowledge and through asymmetries in cultural status between powerful and weaker states. The article treats it as cultural hegemony and exploitation.

The article's term for imperialist dominance in knowledge production, technology and intellectual property, which leaves other countries dependent on the West for knowledge. It draws on the work of Syed Hussein Alatas and Syed Farid Alatas.

The article's term for ideological and religious penetration of other countries, increasingly through religious bodies and non-governmental organisations, aimed at shaping values and cultural structures in line with imperialist strategic interests.

In the Chinese context, a local intermediary serving foreign commercial interests under colonial-era conditions. The article extends it to intellectuals in dependent countries who act as local partners of Western academia.

t: Cybernetic proletarianisation
st: Spiralling devaluation and conflict in digitalised production
zh: 控制论无产阶级化
zhSub: 数字化生产中螺旋式的贬值与冲突
source: Foreign Theoretical Trends (国外理论动态), 2024 no. 1
paras: This text is a Chinese translation, abridged, of an article by Simon Schaupp first published in Capital & Class (2022). Schaupp asks how digitalisation affects manual labour and argues that, rather than mainly polarising jobs, it produces a spiral of devaluation that he calls "cybernetic proletarianisation". Algorithmic control, he claims, both expels living labour from production and reintegrates it in devalued form. Workers are caught in digital feedback loops, and part of their work is to make themselves superfluous.

The article combines Marxist class analysis with empirical labour-process research in Germany, a leading economy in production digitalisation. It draws on participant observation from 2017 to 2019 in four anonymised firms: a mechanical engineering company, a food-delivery platform, a chemicals manufacturer and an online retailer. The author took assembly work and bike-courier work and attended works-council meetings. The study rests on 55 interviews with workers, engineers and managers. After a theoretical reconstruction of proletarianisation, drawing on Marx's Theories of Surplus Value and on Nick Dyer-Witheford's "cybernetic vortex", the empirical sections cover expulsion, reintegration and conflict.

Schaupp identifies three mechanisms of expulsion. First is "deskilling flexibilisation": workers encode their know-how into digital systems, which then equip low-skilled replacements and allow flexible scheduling. Second is cybernetic intensification: real-time measurement and feedback induce workers to "self-adjust" and eliminate idle time. Third is data-based automation: data gathered from workers is used to automate their tasks, such as robotic picking or driverless vehicles. Expulsion does not produce technological unemployment. It is followed by reintegration into labour-intensive, low-paid, precarious work, often by migrants, which starts the next cycle. Against views that algorithmic management atomises workers, Schaupp describes "technopolitics from below": technological disobedience, oppositional worker cultures and organised action. He reports informal resistance, strikes and platform-courier protests, and finds that union strength was weaker where cybernetic proletarianisation was more advanced.

Schaupp concludes that cybernetic proletarianisation is a dynamic process rather than a fixed social group. It is defined by computer-issued instructions, digital performance evaluation, use of collected data to replace labour, and precarious pay, and it is shaped by shared subjective experiences of lost autonomy and dignity. The four stages form a spiral, and the four firms are placed at different turns of it. Whether the process becomes a general trend, he says, depends on workers' own technopolitical action, which has in some cases halted or reversed devaluation. He notes that the qualitative design cannot measure its full extent. Read the original if you study digital labour, algorithmic management or the Marxist theory of proletarianisation and want an empirically grounded German case study.
quoteEn: Part of the work of the cybernetic proletariat is to produce the very data that will be used to replace them entirely in production, thereby making themselves superfluous.
quoteZh: 控制论无产阶级的部分工作就是通过生产被用来在生产过程中完全取代自己的数据，从而让自身变得多余。

t: Examining the global digital divide in the 21st century and China's solution
zh: 21世纪全球数字鸿沟审视与中国方案
paras: Chen and Nie ask why a gap in digital capacity has opened between developed and developing countries, and how it might be closed. Drawing on Marxist political economy, they argue that the digital divide, understood mainly as the "third divide" (unequal outcomes from using digital technology), is a product of digital capitalism, neoliberal policy and the digital hegemony of the United States and other Western states. They present the "Digital Silk Road" as China's solution, one that would help build a community with a shared future for mankind in the digital age.

The article has three parts. The first sets out the conditions that produced the divide. The second classifies it into four kinds (access, capability, output and talent), explains its logic of generation, and diagnoses obstacles to governing it. The third explains the content and scope of the Digital Silk Road and the governance subjects and mechanisms needed to build it. The authors cite figures on 2021 internet penetration, 4G coverage and broadband, and examples such as the Japan–US semiconductor disputes, Huawei sanctions and control of root servers.

The authors argue that digital capitalism leaves capitalism's exploitative essence unchanged. In their account, developed countries export digital capital, monopolise technology and data, and appropriate "digital surplus value" from paid and unpaid digital labour. They say these countries restrict latecomers on grounds of "national security" once those latecomers approach core standards. Governance fails, the authors say, for lack of a cooperative environment, effective actors and workable security and cooperation mechanisms. The Digital Silk Road, which they describe as combining China's digital economy with the Belt and Road Initiative, is presented as non-zero-sum cooperation. It rests on joint consultation, respect for digital sovereignty and the non-competitive character of digital networks.

The authors call on China to strengthen its digital technology and cyber security, and to build digital government, society and individuals. They also call for aligning top-level design with partner countries, cooperating across institutional, technical, material and commercial dimensions, and admitting willing developed countries. They add that the divide does not show a flaw in digital technology itself: under capitalism it serves a few, under socialism it could serve the majority. Read the original if you want a Chinese academic account that links digital-divide theory to digital hegemony and the Belt and Road Initiative.
quoteEn: The emergence and widening of the digital divide are closely related to digital capitalism, neoliberal policies and Western digital hegemony.
quoteZh: 数字鸿沟的产生、扩大与数字资本主义、新自由主义政策、西方数字霸权都有密切的关系。

glossary.explanation: The digital dimension of the Belt and Road Initiative, covering digital infrastructure, digital economy and technology cooperation between China and partner countries.
A Chinese initiative launched by Xi Jinping in 2013 to promote infrastructure, connectivity and economic cooperation across Eurasia, Africa and beyond.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: A foreign-policy concept promoted by Xi Jinping that calls for shared development and cooperation among states.
The authors' term for a monopoly position in digital technology that a state uses to restrict other countries and impose its values or interests.
The authors' extension of Marx's surplus value to profit extracted from digital labour, paid and unpaid, and from digital infrastructure and data.

t: Restless hegemony: the US far-right political movement and its impact
zh: 躁动的霸权：美国极右翼政治运动及其影响
paras: Zhao Minghao examines the rise of the far-right political movement in the United States and asks what it means for American politics, for the wider world and for China. The article argues that, amid social division, ethnic antagonism and political polarisation, far-right ideas have moved towards the mainstream. In Zhao's account the movement has become a national security threat, is linked to far-right forces in Europe and elsewhere, and has a strongly anti-China hawkish tendency that drives US China policy.

The article has three parts. It first describes the movement's ideology, membership, characteristic features and likely future threats, citing the Biden administration's own assessments and episodes such as Charlottesville (2017) and the 6 January 2021 Capitol attack. It then explains why the movement is growing, tracing it from the Ku Klux Klan through the Tea Party to the Trump era. Finally it turns to the movement's international networks and its effect on US–China relations.

Zhao offers four causes of growth: widening inequality and economic distress among lower-middle-class whites; ethnic tension and white 'survival anxiety' over projected demographic change; social media and 'tribalism', which spread conspiracy theories; and defects in the electoral system and polarised parties, aggravated by Trump's tolerance of groups such as the Proud Boys. Zhao says the movement links with European populists, notably through Steve Bannon's foundation 'The Movement', on shared anti-elite, nationalist and anti-immigrant positions. On China, the author contends that far-right propaganda shapes Republican voters' hostile views, that politicians then gain by taking a tough line, and that this vicious circle was worsened by 'China virus' rhetoric during the pandemic.

Zhao concludes that the movement's influence deserves close attention and could reach a new high if Trump wins the 2024 election. Zhao warns that US political turmoil will spill over into relations with China, and calls on China to guard against it and to respond properly to the growing 'restlessness' of American hegemony. Read the original if you want a Chinese scholarly view of how American domestic extremism is linked to US foreign policy and to Sino-American relations.
quoteEn: The worsening of America's political disorder will spill over into China–US relations, and China needs to take the initiative to guard against this and respond properly to the growing inner restlessness of American hegemony.
quoteZh: 美国政治乱局的加剧将对中美关系带来溢出性影响，中国需要主动加以防范，妥善应对美国霸权越发增强的内在躁动性。

t: From the realm of necessity to the realm of freedom: the practical direction of AI development
zh: 从必然王国到自由王国：人工智能发展的实践指向
source: Teaching and Research on Marxist Theory, 2023 no. 4
paras: Chen and Zhang ask how artificial intelligence (AI) should be understood from a Marxist standpoint, given that its capitalist application deepens exploitation and traps workers in what Marx called the realm of necessity. They argue that AI's own contradictions point its development towards the communist realm of freedom, and that the article demonstrates the historical necessity of a leap from the one to the other.

The article has three sections. The first describes how AI operates within the realm of necessity under capitalism. The second presents AI as a historical opportunity for escaping that realm. The third sets out the real possibility that AI carries human society into the realm of freedom. The authors draw mainly on Capital and the 1857–58 manuscripts (the Grundrisse), together with contemporary commentators such as Yuval Noah Harari.

In the first section, the authors argue that capitalist ownership turns AI into a tool for extracting surplus value. In their account it displaces both manual and mental labour, creates a 'useless class' of surplus population, concentrates wealth in the hands of owners of intelligent machines, and enables intensive surveillance of workers. In the second section they draw on Marx's Grundrisse passage on the 'explosive' conditions that capital itself creates. As automation reduces living labour towards zero, they contend, value cannot be measured by labour time, exchange value and the money form come under strain, and the basis of capitalist value relations erodes. The same process shortens necessary labour time and expands free time, which they treat as the precondition of free labour.

In the third section the authors contend that AI dissolves the opposition between labour and leisure, makes labour a first need of life rather than a means of survival, and allows all-round individual development. Disposable time, not surplus labour time, becomes the measure of wealth, which they link to common prosperity and distribution according to need. They conclude that the social practice of AI increasingly breaks through capital's constraints, which raises the likelihood that society enters the realm of freedom. They add that individuals must keep learning to meet the new demands. Read the original if you want a systematic reading of AI through Marx's Grundrisse theory of labour time, value and free time.
quoteEn: The social practice of AI development is increasingly breaking through the constraints of capital's logic and increasingly eliminating capital's alienated labour and monopolisation of material wealth, while helping to liberate human labour.
quoteZh: 人工智能发展的社会实践在日益突破资本逻辑束缚，日益消灭资本异化劳动和霸占物质财富的同时，助力了人类劳动获得解放

glossary.explanation: A Chinese policy goal of shared wealth for all members of society, prominent in official discourse under Xi Jinping. Here the authors link it to the wealth-sharing they expect from AI-based production.
Marx's term in Capital, volume 3, for the sphere of material production, where labour is determined by necessity and external purposes.
Marx's term for the sphere beginning beyond necessary material production, where human powers develop as an end in themselves.

t: Building a community with a shared future for mankind and opposing the future of hegemonism and power politics
zh: 构建人类命运共同体反对霸权主义和强权政治未来
paras: This text is a Chinese translation of a speech by Rossana Duron Cambron, co-chair of the Communist Party USA, delivered at the 13th World Socialism Forum. Cambron argues that science and production already allow humanity to end hunger, homelessness and poor education and healthcare, and that only the capitalist system prevents this. In her view, building a community with a shared future for mankind therefore means confronting the minority that controls resources and power.

The speech moves from a diagnosis of US hegemony to the domestic situation in the United States. It then surveys the left in Latin America, and finally describes her party's ideological and peace work. She cites labour struggles, polling of young Americans, and the electoral record of left governments in Mexico, Colombia, Brazil, Chile, Bolivia and Cuba.

Cambron describes the United States as an imperialist power abroad that presents itself as a democracy at home. She claims the greatest domestic threat is fascism, advanced by an extreme right that grew under Reagan and gained strength with Donald Trump's election in 2016. Against this she points to rising worker militancy, including auto workers, UPS drivers, and Amazon and Starbucks workers, and to polls showing most Americans under 35 prefer socialism. She also points to a new Latin American "pink tide", with 12 countries governed by the left in 2023. She says the struggle against hegemonism is above all ideological: it must counter "American values" of individualism and competition, which she links to high depression, suicide and drug-use rates. She also links it to military spending of over 900 billion dollars and more than 800 overseas bases.

Cambron reports that her party held a peace conference in November 2023. It put forward proposals for a ceasefire in Gaza, cuts to military spending, a ban on nuclear war, and measures against poverty. She holds that peace means achieving justice rather than the absence of conflict, and that all struggles are linked, so funds must shift from the military to the people. She welcomes the Chinese comrades' call for a new society built on more advanced values and cooperative international relations, and says she is convinced that the new form of human civilization will be socialist civilization. Read the original if you want a US communist's view of hegemonism, US politics and Latin American left governments, and of the community with a shared future for mankind.
quoteEn: We firmly believe that the new form of human civilization will be a socialist civilization.
quoteZh: 我们坚信，人类文明新形态将是社会主义文明。

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: A foreign-policy and theoretical concept promoted by Xi Jinping since around 2012–13. It calls for shared development, cooperation and opposition to hegemony in international relations.
An annual international forum on socialism, organised by the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences. Its proceedings are published in World Socialism Studies.

keywords: community with a shared future for mankind

t: An assessment of the new wave of socialist thought in the United States
zh: 美国新一轮社会主义思潮评析
paras: Gao Jianming asks what the revival of socialism in the United States since Bernie Sanders's 2016 and 2020 campaigns amounts to intellectually, and where it may lead. The article argues that four current programmes (liberal socialism, twenty-first-century socialism, class-struggle social democracy and new anarchism) share enough ground to make a lasting revival possible, but only if their advocates play down ultimate disagreements.

After framing socialism as one of three competing ideologies alongside liberalism and conservatism, the article takes each programme in turn. Liberal socialism is associated with James Livingston, Ira Katznelson and Michael Walzer. Twenty-first-century socialism is associated with Fred Block, Erik Olin Wright and Nancy Fraser. Class-struggle social democracy is drawn from the Jacobin circle (Bhaskar Sunkara, Vivek Chibber). New anarchism is represented by David Graeber's "prefigurative politics". Gao then compares similarities and differences and ends with the prospects for American socialism.

Gao identifies two shared features. First, all the currents reject revolutionary socialism: they renounce violent revolution and comprehensive planning and keep markets, even where, as with Sunkara and Chibber, they treat Soviet experience more sympathetically. Second, they absorb left populism in the sense of Chantal Mouffe. They stress direct or participatory democracy and fold class struggle together with new social movements, and Sunkara and Chibber use a widened notion of the working class that blurs into "the people". The differences lie in vision and method. Liberal socialists want to tame capitalism, twenty-first-century socialists to end it while keeping some private ownership, class-struggle social democrats to abolish private ownership, and anarchists to oppose the state. They also differ over whether electoral, class or prefigurative politics should lead.

Gao concludes that the prospects are unclear. Factional dispute could weaken the left, and Gao cites the split and falling membership of Democratic Socialists of America after its 2021 peak of 95,000. Alternatively, the other currents could treat liberal socialism as an intermediate stage, which would broaden its social base and let Wright's strategy of eroding capitalism from above and below be put into practice. Gao holds that toning down ultimate conflicts and attending to present common ground is an indispensable subjective condition for the revival to continue. Read the original if you want a Chinese scholar's map of post-2016 American socialist currents, their key texts and their disagreements.
quoteEn: That the various socialist currents play down ultimate conflicts and attend to present consensus is an indispensable subjective condition.
quoteZh: 各社会主义流派淡化终极冲突、关注当下共识，是必不可少的主观条件。

t: Raising high the banner of building a community with a shared future for mankind and working together for a better world
zh: 高举构建人类命运共同体的鲜明旗帜 携手建设更加美好的世界
paras: This is a speech by Guo Yezhou, then Deputy Head of the International Department of the CPC Central Committee, delivered at the 13th World Socialism Forum and published in World Socialism Studies, 2024 no. 1. Guo argues that Xi Jinping's idea of a community with a shared future for mankind, together with the Global Development, Global Security and Global Civilization Initiatives, answers the question of what to do in a world undergoing great changes unseen in a century.

The speech first sets out three Marxist qualities that Guo attributes to these ideas: scientific character, popular character and practical character. It closes with a call to communists worldwide and a statement of what the Chinese Communist Party will do in its party-to-party diplomacy.

On scientific character, Guo contends that the ideas rest on dialectical and historical materialism and develop Marx and Engels's theory of world history, replacing confrontation with peaceful development and zero-sum games with mutual benefit. On popular character, Guo traces them to traditional Chinese ideas such as "all under heaven is shared by all" and cites the Belt and Road Initiative, which the speech says has drawn nearly 1 trillion US dollars in investment, produced over 3,000 projects and helped lift nearly 40 million people out of poverty. On practical character, Guo reports that the idea has appeared for six consecutive years in UN General Assembly resolutions, that over 100 countries support the development and security initiatives, and that China has built various communities of shared future with dozens of countries and regions.

Guo calls on communist parties and progressive forces to follow a new type of inter-party relations based on seeking common ground, mutual respect and mutual learning. The Party, Guo says, will hold more bilateral and multilateral exchanges, such as the forum of the Communist Party of China with Marxist parties. Read the original if you want an official statement of how Chinese party diplomacy presents this concept to foreign communists.
quoteEn: The idea of a community with a shared future for mankind and the \"three global initiatives\" inherit and develop the Marxist theory of world history.
quoteZh: 人类命运共同体理念和“三大全球倡议”继承并发展了马克思主义世界历史理论

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: A concept put forward by Xi Jinping from 2012–13 as the aim of China's foreign policy. It stresses interdependence among states and shared responsibility for global challenges.

glossary.en: Global Development, Global Security and Global Civilization Initiatives
glossary.explanation: Three initiatives announced by Xi Jinping in 2021–2023 on development, security and civilizational exchange. The Chinese leadership presents them as concrete ways of building a community with a shared future.
A Chinese programme launched in 2013 for infrastructure and economic cooperation across Asia, Europe, Africa and beyond.

keywords: community with a shared future for mankind

t: Why Western economic models no longer work
zh: 西方经济学模型为什么不灵了
paras: This short commentary, first published in Economic Daily in February 2024, asks why Western economic models increasingly fail to forecast or explain the world economy and China's economy. Ye argues that these models suffer from a serious "explanatory deficit" because they strip out historical, cultural and humanistic factors.

The piece opens with recent doubts voiced in the West: ECB president Christine Lagarde's remark that some economists form a closed "tribe", Esther Duflo's joke about economists' standing, and central banks in Britain and Canada reviewing their forecasting systems after failing to predict inflation. It then turns to Western media coverage of China and closes with a prescription.

Ye contends that traditional Western economics starts from an abstract, homogeneous "economic man" and treats history, values and institutions as "interference". In Ye's account, globalisation and technological revolution have produced diverse national development models and non-linear relations that linear formula-based thinking cannot capture. China is presented as the typical case the models cannot explain: Western economists have repeatedly predicted its collapse, yet reforms that mainstream theory judged mistaken succeeded. Ye cites Zhu Tian's finding that Confucian culture, especially its emphasis on saving and education, helped drive growth alongside distinctive institutions and policies.

Ye concludes that understanding China's economy requires more humanistic "parameters", returning the abstract economic man to a concrete social and cultural person. Only then, Ye says, can one grasp why the state can be a "necessary good", why some loss-making high-speed railways are built, and why rural revitalisation, dual-carbon policy and the Belt and Road Initiative are pursued. Read the original if you want a brief example of how Chinese official-media commentary criticises Western mainstream economics and frames China as its test case.
quoteEn: To understand China's economy, more humanistic "parameters" need to be introduced.
quoteZh: 读懂中国经济，需引入更多人文“参数”。

glossary.explanation: A China-led international infrastructure and economic cooperation programme launched by Xi Jinping in 2013.
A national strategy announced in 2017 to develop agriculture, villages and rural incomes.
China's goals of peaking carbon emissions before 2030 and reaching carbon neutrality by 2060.

t: Upholding financial services for the real economy as the fundamental purpose
zh: 坚持把金融服务实体经济作为根本宗旨
paras: Writing in Red Flag Manuscript in 2024, Huang Maoxing takes up Xi Jinping's instruction, given at a study session for provincial and ministerial leaders on high-quality financial development, that finance must make serving the real economy its fundamental purpose. Huang argues that the real economy is the foundation of finance. Cut off from it, finance becomes "water without a source", and the sector should therefore treat service to the real economy as its starting point and goal.

The commentary has three sections. The first sets out why serving the real economy is finance's central mission. The second names priority areas for high-quality financial services. The third proposes five ways to strengthen financial service functions: the monetary and financial environment, financial infrastructure, multi-level capital markets, high-standard financial opening up, and regulatory effectiveness.

Huang's core reasoning rests on three claims, each presented as following from Marxist political economy. First, finance arises from an industrial-capital-centred real economy, so the two form a dialectical unity, summed up in Xi's image of the economy as the body and finance as its blood. Second, finance concentrates dispersed money capital and so supports a modern industrial system. Third, Huang says some capitalist countries, driven by financialised capital, let finance circulate apart from the real economy. In Huang's account this produced excessive virtual-economy expansion and crises, and only a real-economy orientation can prevent systemic risk under the socialist market economy. The priority areas Huang lists are product and service innovation, a better structure of funding supply, support for manufacturing upgrading, and credit access for private firms. Huang adds that funding should favour science and technology, green development, inclusive finance, pension finance and digital finance.

Huang calls for steady monetary policy with structural tools, better financial infrastructure and credit-reporting systems, deeper equity financing and institutional investors, and opening up that keeps a floor of financial security. Huang also calls for stronger Party leadership over financial work and regulation that covers all financial activity, including local government debt and real-estate firms. Since 2012, Huang says, the financial system has made progress in these areas. Read the original if you want a concise statement of how Party-affiliated scholarship in 2024 linked Marxist political economy to concrete financial policy priorities.
quoteEn: Finance is the lifeblood of the real economy; serving the real economy is finance's bounden duty and its purpose.
quoteZh: 金融是实体经济的血脉，为实体经济服务是金融的天职，是金融的宗旨。

glossary.explanation: The part of the economy that produces goods and non-financial services, as opposed to financial and speculative activity. Official texts treat it as the base on which finance should rest.
Financial services extended to small firms, rural households and other groups with limited access to credit. It is one of the "five major articles" of financial work.

t: Deepening supply-side structural reform and expanding effective demand in tandem
zh: 坚持深化供给侧结构性改革和着力扩大有效需求协同发力
paras: This commentary, published in Red Flag Manuscript in early 2024, interprets one of the "Five Musts" set out by the Central Economic Work Conference: that China must deepen supply-side structural reform and work to expand effective demand at the same time. Xu Kangning argues that the two should be pursued together, not separately. In Xu's account, doing so would balance demand and supply dynamically, draw on China's ultra-large market and strong productive capacity, and advance the new development pattern and high-quality development.

The article has four sections. The first explains why expanding domestic demand and optimising supply must move together and why a unified national market is needed. The second sets out the theoretical relation between supply and demand. The third calls for innovation-led measures on both sides, covering consumption, investment, rural markets, strategic emerging industries and the digital economy. The fourth extends the argument to the international circulation, using examples from foreign trade.

Xu's central claim is that demand and supply are mutually dependent: demand pulls supply, and supply creates demand. Managing only the demand side, Xu holds, cannot reach deep structural problems. Smartphones and online music serve as examples of new supply generating new demand. Xu describes overcapacity in some industries as structural, not absolute, because high-quality supply still sells, citing domestic phones and new-energy vehicles. On this reading, technological innovation drives industrial and market innovation, and new quality productive forces, strategic emerging industries and future industries are the key directions for improving supply.

Xu also proposes extending demand-side measures to the countryside through rural logistics, e-commerce and infrastructure investment, alongside institutional reform and support for private investment. On trade, the article cites the shift from the "old three" exports (clothing, appliances, furniture) to the "new three" (new-energy vehicles, lithium batteries, photovoltaics), and calls for more digital trade and higher-standard opening up. Xu concludes that this combined approach fits Chinese modernization and raises the quality of both domestic and international circulation. Read the original if you want an official-line reading of the Central Economic Work Conference's supply-and-demand guidance, with the examples and policy priorities used to support it.
quoteEn: Demand pulls supply, and supply creates demand.
quoteZh: 需求牵引供给,供给创造需求。

glossary.explanation: An economic policy line introduced by Xi Jinping in 2015. It aims to improve the structure and quality of supply, for example by cutting overcapacity and upgrading industries, instead of relying mainly on demand stimulus.
A strategy put forward in 2020 that makes the domestic circulation the mainstay of the economy, with domestic and international circulations reinforcing each other.
A concept Xi Jinping put forward in 2023. It refers to advanced productive forces driven by technological breakthroughs, emerging industries and the digital economy.
An official goal, adopted in 2017, of shifting from high-speed growth to growth based on quality, efficiency and innovation.
The official term for China's path to modernization, described by the Party as distinct from Western models. It is associated with common prosperity and a very large population.
An annual meeting of top Party and state leaders, usually held in December, that sets the economic policy agenda for the coming year.

t: Upholding positive interaction between high-quality development and high-level security
zh: 坚持高质量发展和高水平安全良性互动
paras: Han Xiping takes up the relationship between development and security, and argues that high-quality development and high-level security must interact positively and keep a dynamic balance. The author starts from Xi Jinping's statement at the Central Economic Work Conference (December 2023) that this is a regular pattern to follow in economic work in the new era. In Han's account, security is the precondition of development and development is the guarantee of security.

The article, published in Qiushi's Red Flag Manuscript (Hongqi Wengao) in 2024, has three parts. The first explains why the principle matters. The second sets out its basic requirements. The third proposes practical paths: one for achieving high-quality development and one for achieving high-level security.

On significance, Han presents the principle as an inherent requirement of building a modern socialist country in all respects. The author also treats it as a strategic response to a changing international and domestic environment, citing great-power rivalry, a setback for economic globalisation, uneven development and "chokepoint" technologies. Han further calls it a theoretical innovation within Xi Jinping's economic thought. On requirements, the author stresses seeing how the two interact, making them support each other, and continually reassessing the balance through early identification and handling of risks. On paths, Han calls for speeding up the new development pattern by expanding domestic demand, achieving technological self-reliance and opening up at a higher level. Han also calls for a stronger national security system covering food, energy, finance and the ecological environment.

Han concludes that the holistic approach to national security must be implemented so that the "two miracles" of rapid economic growth and long-term social stability become more sustainable, and so that the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation proceeds smoothly. The author says development results should be turned into security capacity, while security should create a stable environment for development. Read the original if you want a concise statement of the official Party-line reasoning on development and security, together with its policy checklist for key sectors.
quoteEn: Development and security are two wings of one body and two wheels of one drive.
quoteZh: 发展和安全是一体之两翼、驱动之双轮。

glossary.explanation: An official economic goal since about 2017, stressing quality, efficiency and innovation over speed and scale of growth.

glossary.en: the holistic approach to national security
glossary.explanation: A concept Xi Jinping put forward in 2014. It treats security as covering many fields, including politics, economy, technology and ecology, and traditional and non-traditional threats alike.
An official strategy formulated in 2020 that takes the domestic market as the mainstay, with domestic and international circulation reinforcing each other.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The official goal of restoring China's national strength and international standing, closely tied to the Chinese Dream.

The official name for the body of economic ideas attributed to Xi Jinping. It was formally presented in 2017 and described as the latest achievement of Marxist political economy with Chinese characteristics.

t: An action guide for advancing comprehensive rural revitalization effectively
zh: 有力有效推进乡村全面振兴的行动指南
paras: Huang Chengwei offers a study-and-implementation commentary on Xi Jinping's important instruction on "agriculture, rural areas and farmers" (the "three rural issues"), issued around the 2023 Central Rural Work Conference. Huang argues that the instruction sets out the strategic requirements and main thrust of comprehensive rural revitalization. In this reading it is the fundamental guide and action guide for pushing revitalization forward "effectively" in the new era, and it ties accelerated agricultural and rural modernization to Chinese modernization.

The article, published in the Party journal Red Flag Manuscripts in 2024, is organised in five parts. These cover the positioning of rural revitalization as the overall lever of rural work, lessons from the "Thousand Villages Demonstration, Ten Thousand Villages Renovation" project, the two bottom lines plus the twin drivers of technology and reform, three "levels" of improvement with farmers' income, and Party leadership.

Huang's first move is to present rural revitalization as the "overall lever" of rural work, assessing achievements and new difficulties such as rising production costs and market volatility. Huang lists favourable conditions: Party leadership, national strength, rural potential and accumulated experience. The second move is to treat the Zhejiang "Thousand Villages" experience as a teaching model with three features: a people-first value orientation, a systematic and coordinated approach, and tailoring policy to local conditions. The third move is a package of measures. These aim to guarantee grain security and prevent large-scale return to poverty, to drive rural development through science and technology and reform, and to raise rural industry, construction and governance while strengthening measures to raise farmers' incomes.

Huang concludes that the Party's overall leadership is the fundamental guarantee. This includes the principle that the Party manages rural work, a responsibility system running from the central level to counties and townships, grass-roots Party organisations, rural talent and risk prevention. The article is an authoritative-style reading of the policy line, not an independent empirical study. Read the original if you want a systematic outline of how official commentary framed the priorities of rural policy in early 2024, including the specific measures listed for grain security, poverty-return monitoring and rural reform.
quoteEn: Achieving the two "assurances" is a complex systematic undertaking that requires a package of strategic measures to be advanced in an integrated way.
quoteZh: 实现两个“确保”是复杂的系统工程，需要采取一揽子战略措施一体化推进。

glossary.explanation: A standard shorthand for agriculture, rural areas and farmers, used in Chinese policy to refer to rural development as a whole.
The rural development strategy launched at the 19th Party Congress (2017), covering industry, ecology, culture, governance and living standards in the countryside.

glossary.en: Thousand Villages Demonstration, Ten Thousand Villages Renovation
glossary.explanation: A rural environmental and development programme begun in Zhejiang in 2003, when Xi Jinping was provincial Party secretary. It is now promoted as a national model.
The official term for China's path of modernization, which the Party presents as distinct from Western models.
The prospect of many households falling back below the poverty line after the 2020 declaration of victory in poverty alleviation. Preventing it is an official bottom-line task.

t: The logical starting point of the political economy of socialism with Chinese characteristics is the primary stage of socialism
zh: 中国特色社会主义政治经济学的逻辑起点是社会主义初级阶段
source: Observation and Reflection (Guancha yu sikao), 2023 no. 9
paras: Chinese scholars have proposed many different logical starting points for the political economy of socialism with Chinese characteristics, and Yu Bin asks why they disagree and which answer is correct. The article's thesis is that the starting point is the primary stage of socialism. Yu treats Chinese modernization as the logical main line that unfolds from this point.

The article first diagnoses four causes of the disagreement. It then reviews candidate starting points for general socialist political economy, among them socialist commodities, public ownership, quotas, funds, associated labour and "socially organised commodities". It then turns to a long list of proposals specific to China: commodities, productive forces, economic resources, consumption needs, Party leadership, the basic economic system, the "people as principal body" theory, surplus product, capital, ownership, "labour for the people", the "real person" and the principal contradiction. Yu criticises each in turn.

Yu traces the disagreement to four causes: neglect of results already achieved by Marxist political economy, interference from bourgeois economics, one-sided attention to economic reality, and treating the starting point in isolation from the logical main line that must develop from it. Using Capital as the model, Yu argues that a starting point must be able to generate the whole system, must not be a result or a means, and must not presuppose what it has yet to explain. Yu holds that for general socialist political economy the starting point is associated labour on the basis of common ownership of the means of production, as in Marx's "negation of the negation" passage. Because socialism with Chinese characteristics is socialism at its primary stage, its political economy must first show why it differs from general socialist political economy. On Yu's reading, Deng Xiaoping's remarks on the primary stage and on Chinese modernization make that stage the starting point of the main line, which is the movement of Chinese socialism towards higher stages.

Yu concludes that, since a mature socialist political economy does not yet exist, a textbook could proceed from general political economy to socialist political economy and then to the Chinese case, and would then begin with political economy in general. If socialist principles are already presupposed, the logical starting point is the primary stage of socialism. Yu also argues that early PRC practice after the 1950s should be analysed critically, because it ran ahead of the primary stage. Read the original if you want a detailed critical survey of Chinese debates on the starting point of socialist political economy, argued from Capital's method.
quoteEn: Chinese modernization is the logical main line of the political economy of socialism with Chinese characteristics. The logical starting point of this main line is the starting point of Chinese modernization, and that starting point is precisely the primary stage of socialism.
quoteZh: 中国式现代化是中国特色社会主义政治经济学的逻辑主线。这条主线的逻辑起点也就是中国式现代化的起点。这个起点恰恰就是社会主义初级阶段

glossary.explanation: An official thesis, formalised in the 1980s, that China remains at an early, underdeveloped stage of socialism. It is used to justify market mechanisms and a mixed ownership structure.
The Party's official name for China's path since reform and opening up, associated with Deng Xiaoping's formulation of building socialism suited to Chinese conditions.
The official term for China's own path of modernization under Communist Party leadership. It was stressed by Deng Xiaoping and developed further under Xi Jinping.

The first, simplest category from which a theoretical system is derived step by step, as commodity is in Marx's Capital. Chinese debates over it concern how to structure a political economy of socialism.

t: Collective force: on the logical foundation of common prosperity
zh: 集体力：论共同富裕的逻辑基础
paras: How can common prosperity be achieved under a socialist market economy, where the law of value tends to produce polarisation? Li Fenghua and Yi Xilin argue that Western welfare-state and market-failure remedies cannot answer this, since they rest on individualism and private ownership. They find the answer in the concept of "collective force" (jitili) from Marx's Capital, which they present as the logical and economic-philosophical foundation of common prosperity.

The article has three parts. The first defines collective force and shows how it operates across modern industrial society: in material production, knowledge production (science, patents, platform economies) and social interaction (markets and political institutions). The second examines how capitalism privatises collective force, through global plunder, appropriation of audience labour, technological hegemony and international financial dominance. It also notes partial public ownership, in public utilities and welfare states. The third sets out how making collective force public leads to common prosperity.

The authors read Marx's passage on cooperation as showing that cooperation and division of labour create a productive force that cannot be reduced to individuals. Since this force is social in origin, they hold that it should belong to society, and that capital's unpaid appropriation of it is the main source of surplus value and of wealth gaps. They argue that collective force exists at several levels, from workshop and city to nation and world. This yields "multi-level ownership", combining public ownership at each level with respect for individual ownership of individual contributions. They claim this fits Marx's twin formulas of abolishing private ownership and re-establishing individual ownership, and that it covers mixed-ownership economies in the primary stage of socialism.

The authors conclude that distribution theory has focused on labour versus production factors and neglected the contribution of collective force, which they say has let a few individuals capture it as factor income. They propose identifying the collective component of outputs and returning it through taxes and public accumulation, citing inheritance, property and windfall taxes as useful precedents. This, they argue, is a Pareto-improving, gradual path of socialist "self-reform" rather than violent expropriation. Read the original if you want a Chinese political-economy attempt to ground common prosperity in a reading of Marx's Capital and in ownership theory.
quoteEn: Multi-level ownership of collective force will provide an economic-philosophical foundation for common prosperity, and a political-economy proof of the common prosperity proposition.
quoteZh: 集体力的多级所有将为共同富裕提供一个经济哲学基础，为共同富裕命题提供政治经济学的证明。

glossary.explanation: A long-standing socialist goal in China, stressed in official policy since 2021, of prosperity shared by all rather than a few. Official discourse says it does not mean egalitarianism.

A term from the Chinese translation of Marx's Capital, for the productive force created by cooperation and division of labour. The authors extend it into a general category for social productive power.
The official characterisation of China's present stage of development, in which public ownership is dominant and several ownership forms coexist.
The authors' proposed ownership model, in which collective force is publicly owned at levels from workshop to world, alongside private ownership of individual contributions.
An official Party term for the Party correcting itself. The authors use "self-reform" of the socialist system for non-violent change.

t: Showing the dual character of Chinese modernization through the "big history" perspective
st: The distinctive features of Chinese modernization and the common features of modernization across countries
zh: 从大历史观展示中国式现代化的双重属性
zhSub: 中国式现代化的特色与各国现代化共同特征
paras: Every country's path to modernization, Li Jie argues, must follow the general laws of modernization while also fitting national conditions. Chinese modernization therefore has both features shared with other countries and features of its own, and the universal lives within the particular. Li proposes that a "big history" perspective (dà lìshǐ guān) can show this dual character. The piece appeared in Beijing Daily on 22 April 2024.

The commentary goes through five features of Chinese modernization: a huge population, common prosperity for all, coordinated material and cultural-ethical progress, harmony between humanity and nature, and a path of peaceful development. For each, Li sets the Chinese case against how Western capitalist modernization handled the same problem. The text also draws on Marx on machinery, Mao Zedong on the value of people, Deng Xiaoping on the essence of socialism, Xi Jinping on ecology and culture, and the report to the 20th Party Congress (2022).

In Li's account, each Chinese feature answers a problem that every modernizing country faces. Western countries met labour shortages through land enclosure, the slave trade and factory machinery, which Li says sacrificed workers and peasants to capital accumulation. China instead treats its population as a resource rather than a burden. Li argues that capitalist modernization can create wealth but cannot distribute it fairly, and that it fosters hypocritical morality, ecological damage and colonial expansion. Socialist modernization is presented as a remedy, through distribution and social security systems, balancing efficiency with fairness and vitality with order, combining material and spiritual wealth, and rejecting the logic that a strong country must seek hegemony.

Li concludes that the Chinese features and the common features of modernization are inseparable and highly unified. He attributes this unity both to the dual nature of modernization itself and to the historic achievements and changes of socialism with Chinese characteristics in the new era. Li also presents China's experience as a model for developing countries seeking non-capitalist paths and cultural confidence. Read the original if you want a short, official-style statement of how Party-aligned scholars frame Chinese modernization against Western modernization.
quoteEn: This inherent and high degree of unity stems both from the dual character of modernization itself and from the historic achievements and changes that socialism with Chinese characteristics has brought about in the new era.
quoteZh: 这种内在的高度统一，既源自现代化本身的双重属性，也源自中国特色社会主义在新时代取得的历史性成就、发生的历史性变革。

glossary.explanation: A term used in Party discourse for viewing events across long historical spans and in a global context. It was emphasised by Xi Jinping and is used here as an analytical lens.
The official name for China's development path, set out by Xi Jinping and the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is described as having both common features and distinctive Chinese characteristics.
A goal of socialism in Party theory, meaning prosperity shared by all rather than by a minority. It has been stressed again in policy since 2021.
The official name for China's system since the reform era. It combines Marxism with Chinese conditions and is the Party's central theoretical framework.

glossary.literal: harmonious coexistence of humans and nature
glossary.explanation: A principle of the Party's ecological civilization policy, which holds that economic development and environmental protection should go together.

t: Re-examining the labour theory of value in the age of artificial intelligence
zh: 人工智能时代劳动价值论再审视
source: Studies of the Marxist Theory Discipline (马克思主义理论学科研究), 2024 no. 3
paras: Li Nan takes up the doubts that "machines replacing humans" and "unmanned factories" have raised about Marx's labour theory of value. The article asks how artificial intelligence (AI) reshapes labour, whether the theory still applies, and how it should be put into practice. Li answers that AI changes the forms of labour and the realisation of value without displacing living labour as the sole source of value, so the theory remains a scientific guide.

The article has three parts. The first describes how AI reshapes labour and shifts value. The second clarifies three points of dispute: the uniqueness of the source of value, the standing of the worker as subject, and the nature of capital. The third sets out how to uphold the theory in practice, and cites Xi Jinping on AI as support for the Party's people-centred orientation.

In the first part, Li argues that the relation between living and objectified labour grows more complex, with objectified labour taking a larger share. New forms such as digital labour appear, and working time and space extend. Higher organic composition of capital and falling value per commodity make use-value and value move in opposite directions. In the second part, Li rejects autonomist and knowledge-theory claims that intellect or knowledge creates value. Following Marx's view of labour as a totality, Li says unmanned factories must be assessed together with the upstream and downstream work of R&D, assembly, maintenance and distribution, where living labour adds value. AI is still a "technical being" created by human labour, and humans still supply the purposes of labour. Li also rejects the accelerationist hope that AI can transcend capitalism. In Li's account, AI intensifies the opposition between capital and labour, monopoly, and exploitation, and makes exploitation less visible, for instance through users' unpaid "non-employment labour" that trains models.

Li calls for three things. The first is to uphold the monistic view of living labour as the source of value while broadening the concept to cover digital labour. The second is to keep the worker's subject status, through innovation-oriented training, AI education and all-round human development. The third is to treat capital and AI dialectically, using the basic economic system, fair distribution and anti-monopoly and data regulation to curb the disorderly expansion of capital. Read the original if you want a Chinese Marxist defence of the labour theory of value against claims that AI makes living labour obsolete, together with the policy proposals Li draws from it.
quoteEn: AI cannot eliminate the exploitative nature of capital; it merely makes exploitation more concealed.
quoteZh: 人工智能无法消除资本的剥削性质，只是将剥削行为变得更加隐蔽。

glossary.en: monistic view of living labour as the source of value
glossary.explanation: The position that living labour alone creates value and surplus value, so that machines, knowledge or data cannot do so independently. The article defends it against pluralist theories of value.

glossary.literal: taking the people as the centre
glossary.explanation: A guiding principle of Xi Jinping-era Party discourse that development should serve the people's interests and wellbeing. The article uses it to frame the proper relation between AI and workers.
An official phrase, prominent since about 2020, for unregulated growth of private capital, especially in platform and technology sectors. It is used to justify regulation and anti-monopoly measures.
The official framework of China's socialist economy, with public ownership as the mainstay alongside diverse forms of ownership, and distribution according to work as the main mode alongside others.

t: Uncovering the critical dimension of the labour theory of value
zh: 发掘劳动价值论的批判性维度
paras: Niu Ziniu takes up a gap in how the labour theory of value is read. Chinese Marxist scholars, the author says, have long stressed its constructive dimension: labour creates value, capitalism's main defect is the unpaid appropriation of surplus value, and a post-capitalist order should distribute value fairly. This is a kind of 'distributive justice' reading. Niu argues that Western left scholars, citing Moishe Postone, now stress a critical dimension. On this view, 'labour appearing as value' already contains a degree of alienated labour, so the problem goes beyond unjust distribution. Niu presents recovering this dimension in Capital as a task for today's Marxist scholars.

The piece appeared in the China Social Sciences Today in March 2024. It has four sections: the social constructedness of categories, the historicity of the labour theory of value, the organic object and dialectical method of Capital, and the relation between the labour theory of value and the theory of surplus value. It draws mainly on Marx's Grundrisse and Capital. It closes by linking the argument to present-day labour conditions.

First, Niu argues that 'labour' and 'value' are historical categories. Marx asked why labour appears as value, which the classical economists never did. Niu distinguishes the early, ontological concept of labour as sensuous object-activity from the Capital concept tied to abstract labour, which belongs to capitalist wage labour. Second, Niu rejects a 'linear logic' reading in which the labour theory of value is an axiom from which capitalism is deduced. Capitalism is an 'organic totality' in which each element is both condition and result. The ascent from the abstract to the concrete reproduces that totality in thought; it is not a historical genesis. Third, value rests on money and capital, and capital on surplus value. So 'labour creates value' in reality means 'wage labour creates profit'. Niu adds that, on Marx's Grundrisse argument, abolishing capitalism means abolishing the value form, so that labour time is no longer the measure of wealth.

Niu concludes that the labour theory of value is neither a pure premise of Capital nor a standard of critique that exists independently of capitalism. It is an abstract aspect of the capitalist totality and holds the seeds of labour alienation. Niu notes that deepening contradictions have brought intensified labour, unstable labour relations, sharper competition and meaningless work. Grasping the critical dimension, Niu argues, would revive the value of Capital and give a philosophical account of these problems.
