The essay then traces how the relation between civil society and the state changed: from identity in ancient Greece and the Middle Ages to separation after the French Revolution. It next follows how the concept of civil society narrowed from a bourgeois political community to a system of needs, and closes with Marx's critical route and its present value.

Sun contends that Hegel rebuilt the concept of civil society on Adam Smith's account of labour, division of labour and exchange, but did so in order to surpass Smith. Where Smith relied on the "invisible hand" and laissez-faire, Hegel held that individual reason is mastered by civil society, so that the state's collective reason must overcome its antinomies. In Sun's reading, Hegel's philosophy of the state is therefore itself a critique of political economy. Marx, by contrast, first criticised the "copy" (Hegel's speculative philosophy of the state) and then the "original" (the modern representative state). Marx saw this state as a regime of private property, so Hegel's state could only reinforce civil society's dominant logic. Sun adds that Marx at this stage had not yet studied classical political economy or the civil-society section of Hegel's text.

Sun concludes that, despite their disagreements, Hegel and Marx agree on the evolution of modern Western society, with civil society as the basis of Western modernity. Marx's further step was to carry the narrow concept of civil society to a critique of the capitalist mode of production. Sun notes the irony that state intervention, as Hegel envisaged it, later appeared in the New Deal, Keynesianism and the welfare state, yet as a bourgeois political state. Neither Smith's nor Hegel's logic resolved civil society's paradoxes. Read the original if you want a compact Chinese account of how Hegel's civil society and state, and Marx's early critique of them, are linked to the critique of Western modernity.
quoteEn: It is not the state that determines civil society, but civil society that determines the state!
quoteZh: 不是国家决定市民社会，而是市民社会决定国家！

t: Drawing theoretical innovation wisdom from the creations of the people
zh: 从人民群众的创造中汲取理论创新智慧
paras: Ai Silin takes up Xi Jinping's call, made at the sixth collective study session of the 20th Politburo (2023), to "draw theoretical innovation wisdom from the creations of the people". The article reads the call as an application of the Marxist theory of knowledge and the mass view of history, and as a summary of the Party's historical experience. It argues that the call fixes the standpoint, direction and route for advancing the Party's theoretical innovation.

The commentary is organised in three parts. The first sets out why the people's creative practice is the inexhaustible source of Marxist theoretical innovation. The second reviews the Party's history, from the New Democratic Revolution through socialist construction and reform and opening up to the new era. The third turns to practical measures for following the mass line in theoretical work.

Ai's core reasoning starts from the primacy of practice in Marxist epistemology and the people-centred nature of Marxism. Practice is a social activity carried out by the masses, so the masses are the decisive force in changing the world and a source of theory. The article presents the rural investigations behind Mao Zedong's strategy of surrounding the cities from the countryside, and the household contract responsibility system and township enterprises under reform and opening up, as examples. It treats Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era as rooted in the people's practice. On method, Ai calls for large-scale investigation and research in which cadres learn humbly from the people. Investigation gathers raw material, and research must then distil from it theory that applies generally. Ai describes investigation without research as a "broken bridge".

Ai concludes that the Party should build long-term mechanisms for following the mass line. These include education in the Marxist mass viewpoint, stronger research skills with incentives for evaluating research results, and open channels for suggestions, criticism and supervision. They also include a body of theorists who learn from the people and "write their papers on the land of the motherland". Ai ties this to the current study campaign on Xi Jinping Thought and to a period of rapid change, which is said to call for respecting the people's initiative. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party theorists justify theoretical innovation as coming from the masses and how they link it to investigation and research methods.
quoteEn: The practice of the people is the raw material of theoretical innovation, and our Party bears the responsibility of integrating, systematising, perfecting and elevating it.
quoteZh: 人民群众的实践是理论创新的原材料，我们党承担着将其整合起来、系统起来、完善起来、升华起来的责任。

glossary.explanation: A Party working method associated with Mao Zedong: leaders gather the views and experience of ordinary people, consolidate them into policy, and then take them back to the people. It remains a standard element of Party doctrine.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The official guiding ideology of the Communist Party of China, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018. It is presented as the latest stage in adapting Marxism to China.
The policy of economic reform and opening to the outside world launched in 1978 under Deng Xiaoping.

A method of fieldwork and analysis, associated with Mao Zedong, in which cadres investigate conditions at the grassroots and then analyse the findings to guide policy. Xi Jinping promoted it as a campaign in 2023.
A phrase used in Party discourse for the claim that ordinary people originate new practices, such as rural reforms, which the Party later adopts and generalises.

t: Hegel's reconciliation and the young Marx's revolution
zh: 黑格尔的和解与青年马克思的革命
paras: Why did Hegel counsel reconciliation with social reality while the young Marx demanded revolution? Zhang Donghui argues that the difference rests on how each understood 'essence'. Hegel, in Zhang's reading, takes an anti-essentialist stance that dissolves and weakens essence, and so views social contradiction and historical change through becoming and reconciliation. The young Marx tends towards essentialism, which is the premise of his theory of alienation, and he chooses revolution in order to sublate alienation.

The article, a short piece first published in the China Social Sciences Today newspaper in November 2023, has three parts. The first compares the two thinkers' conceptions of essence, drawing on Hegel's Phenomenology of Spirit and Science of Logic and on the young Marx's critique of Hegel's philosophy of right and his determinations of religion, money, labour and the human being. The second sets Marx's alienation against Hegel's 'becoming' (Werden). The third turns to reconciliation versus revolution as practical attitudes.

Zhang defines essentialism as grasping the laws and essence of things from empirical phenomena. The young Marx, on this account, presupposes an essence, reads the actual state of things as alienation from it, and then uses revolution to return things to their ideal state. Hegel, by contrast, treats essence as the reflection of thought in itself and as a transitional moment on the way to the absolute Idea, so alienation in Marx's sense cannot arise for him. Becoming is a broader concept that contains alienation. Reconciliation is not an excuse for existing evils: Zhang notes that Hegel allows for reform and even revolution when social contradictions, such as extreme inequality, make society unworthy of reconciliation. Zhang describes Hegel's stance as present-oriented realism and Marx's as future-oriented idealism.

Zhang adds that Marx moved from political towards social revolution, stressing the material conditions and development of productive forces, as in The German Ideology. That emphasis, Zhang says, links his theory of revolution to Hegel's dialectic of becoming and gives it some compatibility with reconciliation. Zhang concludes that Hegel's anti-essentialism remains entangled with essentialism, that Marx's revolution partly destroys essentialism, and that the essentialism lens is only one angle of reading. Read the original if you want a brief, concept-focused comparison of Hegel and the young Marx through the essence/alienation framework.
quoteEn: Hegel's reconciliation inherently carries a realist perspective grounded in the present, whereas the young Marx's revolution has an idealist dimension directed towards the future.
quoteZh: 黑格尔的和解内在地具有立足当下的现实主义视角，而青年马克思的革命则具有指向未来的理想主义维度。

t: Carl Schorlemmer and the Marxist philosophy of chemistry
zh: 肖莱马与马克思主义化学哲学
source: Chinese Social Sciences Today (Zhongguo shehui kexue bao), 4 December 2023
paras: This short piece asks what the work of the German chemist Carl Schorlemmer (1834–1892), a close associate of Marx and Engels, contributes to a Marxist philosophy of chemistry. Yu Ping and Li Xuechen present him as a scientist who consciously applied materialist dialectics to research and as a committed communist. They argue that his achievements show the value of theoretical thinking for natural science and of natural science for Marxism.

The article has four parts: Schorlemmer's work in chemistry and the philosophy of chemistry; his work on the history of chemistry; the character of his scientific conduct; and the lessons the authors draw for today. It draws on Engels's judgements of Schorlemmer, on his textbook and history of organic chemistry, and on a letter from Marx to Engels of 3 January 1868.

The authors argue that Schorlemmer borrowed the method of Marx's Capital and treated aliphatic hydrocarbons as the "cell" from which all organic compounds derive. On this basis he did experimental and theoretical work on hydrocarbons and their derivatives. In the authors' account he also traced a dialectical path from inorganic chemistry through organic chemistry and biochemistry to biology, and showed how chemistry rests on physics and mechanics, which they say matches Engels's view of the transformation of forms of motion. In the history of chemistry, his 1871 textbook, the first organised by chemical structure, and his 1879 history of organic chemistry are presented as pioneering works shaped by historical materialism. The authors add that he came from a poor family, lived frugally, was generous to friends and students, and thus models the spirit of the scientist.

The authors draw two lessons. Natural scientists should actively learn and use Marxist theoretical thinking in their research. Adapting Marxism to the needs of our times also requires drawing on new natural-science results and on study of Marx's theory of science and technology, in order to keep Marxism vital. Marx's request, passed through Engels, for Schorlemmer's advice on agricultural chemistry while writing on ground rent is cited as evidence that Marx valued natural science. Read the original if you want a brief, officially oriented introduction to Schorlemmer and to how Chinese Marxist scholars link the history of science with the adaptation of Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times.
quoteEn: Research in the natural sciences should attach importance to methods of theoretical thinking.
quoteZh: 自然科学研究应当重视理论思维方法。

glossary.explanation: The Marxist method that treats nature and society as material and as developing through contradiction and interconnection. The article presents it as Schorlemmer's guiding method in chemistry.

t: How Marx transcended Rousseau's Romantic view of science and technology
zh: 马克思对卢梭浪漫主义科学技术观的超越
paras: Rousseau, the Romantic thinker, acknowledged the importance of science but dwelt mainly on its harmful effects, holding that it corrupted social customs and degraded human nature. Zhu argues that Marx inherited Rousseau's critical spirit but placed science and technology within historical materialism. In this account Marx revealed their social and humanistic character and treated them as a revolutionary force for progress, thereby overcoming Rousseau's Romantic imagination.

The short commentary, which first appeared in the Chinese Social Sciences Today in December 2023, is organised around three themes: the essence of science and technology, their alienation, and their revolutionary power. It ends with three lessons for promoting scientific and technological innovation in the new era.

On essence, Zhu contrasts Rousseau's claim that science springs from moral vice (astronomy from superstition, mathematics from greed) with Marx's view that curiosity and desire are only drivers. For Marx, the real basis of natural science is labour practice, and the value of the human being and that of science and technology are unified. On alienation, Zhu says Rousseau saw science's damage to morals but not its root. Marx traced the harm to workers' bodies, minds and individuality to the capitalist production process, and located the cause in the capitalist application of machinery rather than machinery itself, which in itself lightens labour and shortens working time. On revolutionary power, Zhu says Marx rejected Rousseau's anti-science stance. He saw technology as raising productivity, saving labour time and enlarging free time, and he regarded alienation as a necessary stage on the road to communism.

Zhu draws three lessons for innovation in the new era: keep a human-centred orientation aimed at the people's aspiration for a better life; apply dialectics to the 'double-edged sword' of technology, maximising its positive effects and limiting its negative ones; and hold to the historical-materialist position that alienation is avoided by promoting innovation under the system of socialism with Chinese characteristics. Read the original if you want a concise statement of the official Chinese Marxist reading of Marx's relation to Rousseau on technology, and of how it is linked to current innovation policy.
quoteEn: Machinery in itself signifies humanity's victory over nature, but its capitalist application leaves people in a state of enslavement.
quoteZh: 机器本身意味着人对自然的胜利，但它的资本主义应用却使人陷于受奴役状态。

glossary.explanation: The official name for China's current system and path, associated with reform and opening up from the late 1970s and reaffirmed in Party documents since.
The term used since the 19th Party Congress (2017) for the current period of Chinese development under Xi Jinping's leadership.
Marx's theory that material production and social relations shape historical development; here it frames Marx's account of technology.

t: Understanding the great achievements and key lessons of reform and opening up
zh: 深刻认识改革开放的伟大成就和重要启示
authors: Fourth Research Department, Institute of Party History and Literature of the CPC Central Committee
paras: This commentary, written by a research department of the Party's central history and documents institute and published in the People's Daily in December 2023, takes stock of 45 years of reform and opening up. It was issued after the Central Economic Work Conference stressed relying on reform and opening up to strengthen endogenous momentum for development. The authors argue that the record of achievements and the lessons drawn from it matter for deepening reform on the "new journey" and for reaching the second centenary goal.

The article has two parts. The first surveys five areas of achievement: economic strength, socialist democracy and the rule of law, cultural soft power, the sharing of reform outcomes, and ecological progress. The second sets out six lessons for the future. Throughout, the authors link the period since the Third Plenum of the 11th Central Committee (1978) to the new stage opened by the Third Plenum of the 18th Central Committee (2013).

On achievements, the authors cite figures: GDP rising from 368.7 billion yuan at the start of reform to 121.02 trillion yuan in 2022, the world's second largest; the elimination of absolute poverty; the world's most complete industrial system; per capita disposable income up from 171 yuan in 1978 to 36,883 yuan in 2022; and life expectancy of 78.2 years. They also point to whole-process people's democracy, a largely formed framework of law-based governance, a reversal in the ideological sphere, and better air and water quality. From this record they derive their lessons: uphold the Party's centralised and unified leadership, put the people at the centre of development, and keep to the path of socialism with Chinese characteristics. They add that Marxism must continue to be adapted to the Chinese context and the needs of our times, that institutional strengths should become governance effectiveness, and that cultural confidence supplies spiritual strength.

The authors conclude that the practice of reform and opening up proves the correctness of Chinese modernization, which they call the only correct path to national rejuvenation. They call for unity around the Party Central Committee with Xi Jinping at its core and for guidance by Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era. Read the original if you want a compact, officially framed summary of how Party theorists present the achievements and lessons of reform and opening up at the end of 2023.
quoteEn: The practice of reform and opening up fully proves that the socialist system with Chinese characteristics has strong vitality and great superiority, and can continuously drive the progress and development of a large country of over 1.4 billion people.
quoteZh: 改革开放的实践充分证明，中国特色社会主义制度具有强大生命力和巨大优越性，能够持续推动拥有14亿多人口的大国进步和发展。

glossary.explanation: The Party's official concept of China's own path to modernisation, set out prominently since the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is presented as distinct from Western models.
An official term for China's democratic system, promoted under Xi Jinping. It stresses people's participation across all stages of decision-making, not only elections.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's current guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018.
The official name for the Party's path, system and theory since the reform era began under Deng Xiaoping.

t: Forever remember Comrade Mao Zedong's great achievements and noble example
zh: 永远铭记毛泽东同志的丰功伟绩和崇高风范
authors: Party History and Literature Research Institute of the CPC Central Committee
paras: Written for the 130th anniversary of Mao Zedong's birth, this commemorative piece by the Party History and Literature Research Institute of the CPC Central Committee asks what the Party should draw from Mao's legacy today. Its answer is that remembering Mao means deepening understanding of the Two Establishes, adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times, holding to the socialist road, pursuing Chinese modernization, and continuing full and rigorous self-governance of the Party.

The article opens with an assessment of Mao as a founder of the Party, the army and the People's Republic. It then proceeds in four sections, each introduced by the phrase "today, to cherish the memory of Comrade Mao Zedong, we must…". These cover his role as the core of the first generation of central leadership, his pioneering role in adapting Marxism to China, the socialist path, and modernization and Party building. Each section links Mao's record to Xi Jinping's leadership and thought. The piece draws on quotations from Mao, Deng Xiaoping and Xi.

The authors argue for continuity across eras. They hold that the Zunyi Meeting established Mao's leadership and that Deng judged the revolution would have groped in darkness longer without him. They present the Two Establishes as the major political outcome of the new era. In their account Mao Thought was the first historic leap in adapting Marxism to China, and Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era is a further leap. They say it keeps the "living soul" of Mao Thought (seeking truth from facts, the mass line, independence) and carries it forward through the Two Integrations. The article acknowledges that Mao took detours in exploring socialist construction. It insists that the periods before and after reform and opening up are linked, and that the achievements of each must not be negated. It credits Mao's era with the industrial base and the "two bombs, one satellite" breakthroughs, and treats Chinese modernization as confirming his forecasts.

On Party building, the authors present Mao's "two musts" and his answer to the historical cycle of rise and decline (letting the people supervise the government) as forerunners of the Party's self-reform. They conclude that the best commemoration is to carry forward his cause, to follow a path that is neither rigid nor a change of banner, and to unite around the Party Central Committee with Xi Jinping at its core. Read the original if you want to see how the Party's central research institute frames Mao's legacy in relation to Xi Jinping Thought and current slogans in an official anniversary text.
quoteEn: Today, the best way to commemorate Comrade Mao Zedong is to carry forward and develop well the great cause that he and his comrades-in-arms laid the foundations for and pioneered through arduous struggle and painstaking effort, and to write a new chapter of history from a new historical starting point.
quoteZh: 今天，对毛泽东同志最好的纪念，就是把他和他的战友们筚路蓝缕、呕心沥血奠基和开创的伟大事业继承好、发展好，在新的历史起点上谱写新的历史华章。

glossary.explanation: A formulation from the 6th Plenum of the 19th Central Committee (2021). It affirms Xi Jinping's position as core of the Party Central Committee and of the whole Party, and the guiding role of Xi Jinping Thought.
The principle of combining the basic tenets of Marxism with China's concrete realities (the first) and with China's fine traditional culture (the second, added by Xi Jinping in 2023).

glossary.zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化
glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
glossary.explanation: The official formula for the Party's ongoing project of applying Marxism to Chinese conditions and updating it to the present era. Mao is credited with first posing the theme of "Sinification of Marxism".

The official term for China's path to modernization under Party leadership, presented as distinct from the Western model. It has been prominent in Party discourse since the 20th Party Congress (2022).

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.explanation: A slogan of the Xi era covering anti-corruption, discipline and organisational reform within the Party.
Xi Jinping's term for the Party's continuing efforts to correct its own faults. The article presents it as the answer to the historical cycle of rise and decline.
Mao's 1949 exhortation that Party members must keep a modest, prudent, hard-working style and the spirit of hard struggle.

t: Mao Zedong's thought of independence and self-reliance and its value for our times
zh: 毛泽东同志的独立自主思想及其时代价值
paras: Writing in Guangming Daily in December 2023, Yang Fengcheng takes up Mao Zedong's idea of independence and self-reliance (duli zizhu), which Yang calls the living soul of Mao Zedong Thought and a key to the success of China's revolution and construction. The article's central claim is that its core is placing national development on the basis of one's own strength and having Chinese affairs decided and handled by the Chinese people themselves. Yang argues that this principle keeps its value in the new era.

The piece has five numbered sections. The first traces the idea's sources in Marxism and in Chinese traditional culture, and the Party's gradual, hard-won grasp of it from the Zunyi Conference onward. The next sections treat independence in choosing a development path, self-reliance in economic and technological work, the relation between self-reliance and openness, and the spirit of struggle. Each section links Mao-era examples to present-day concerns.

Yang holds that independence was not automatic for Chinese communists. Dogmatism and Comintern directives, in Yang's account, bore heavy responsibility for the defeats of the Great Revolution and of the 'Left' line in the land-revolution period. Mao's answers were the path of encircling the cities from the countryside and the 'second integration' of Marxism with Chinese reality after 1949, seen in 'On the Ten Major Relationships'. Yang credits these with building an independent, relatively complete industrial system and avoiding the dependent development of some newly independent states. Self-reliance is illustrated by the Nanniwan production campaign and the 'two bombs, one satellite' programme after the Soviet withdrawal of experts. Yang stresses that it does not mean closing the country: Mao favoured learning critically from all nations, and the article presents reform-era opening up as continuing this.

Yang concludes that no nation has become strong by depending on outsiders or copying foreign models, and that China must keep strengthening confidence in its path, theory, system and culture. Because key technologies still face 'chokehold' problems, the article says they cannot be begged or bought and must be developed independently. Yang also calls for a fighting spirit that is both brave and skilful, citing Deng Xiaoping and Xi Jinping on never being anyone's appendage. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party scholars present Mao's independence principle as a basis for current policy on technology, openness and sovereignty.
quoteEn: Unwaveringly following one's own path is the foundation and precondition of independence and self-reliance, and the basic conclusion of the Communist Party of China's hundred years of struggle.
quoteZh: 坚定不移地走自己的路，是独立自主的根本和前提，是中国共产党百年奋斗的基本结论。

glossary.explanation: A guiding principle of Chinese Communist Party policy, associated with Mao Zedong, that China should decide its own affairs and not depend on foreign direction. It has been applied to revolution, foreign policy and development.
The policy of relying mainly on domestic effort and resources, with foreign aid as a supplement. Mao promoted it from the wartime base areas through the 1950s and 1960s.
Mao's phrase from the 1950s for a second effort to combine Marxism with Chinese conditions, this time in socialist construction. It is the Party's term for the search for a Chinese path to socialism.

t: "What is Chinese communism?": American observers' reflections on the Chinese revolution during the War of Resistance
zh: “何为中国共产主义”:全面抗战时期美国观察家对中国革命的思考
paras: Lu Xiaona asks why American observers who travelled to North China after the full-scale outbreak of war in 1937 kept asking "what is Chinese communism?", how their deep prejudice against the Chinese Communist Party (CCP) dissolved, and how their revised views bore on US Far Eastern strategy. The article argues that field investigation convinced them the CCP was organisationally independent of the Soviet Union and pursued a communist programme rooted in Chinese conditions. Lu presents this as a Marxism adapted to China, which the observers publicised in an effort to shift American policy.

The study follows several groups: the Amerasia group of 1937, Marine officer Evans Carlson (1937–38), missionary Stanton Lautenschlager (1940), and, in 1944, the foreign press party (Harrison Forman, Gunther Stein, Israel Epstein and others) and the US Army Observation Group at Yan'an (John S. Service, John P. Davies, David Barrett, Raymond Ludden and others). Four sections cover the CCP's independence from Moscow, its "own" communism, its wartime economic experiments as a "testing ground for a new China", and Yan'an as a "miniature of China's future". A short conclusion traces the policy consequences.

Lu's central claim is that the observers' changing qualifiers for the party, from Carlson's "so-called" communists to "Yan'an's", "their own" and finally "fitting" communists, reflect the CCP's continuing effort to adapt Marxism to Chinese conditions. The evidence includes interviews with Mao Zedong, Zhu De and Zhou Enlai, Service's report finding no sign of Soviet remote control, and Stein's view that nationalism outweighed doctrine in the party's programme. Lu also examines the policies of rent and interest reduction, encouragement of private capital, and cooperatives and labour-exchange teams built on private holdings. The article contrasts these with Marx's and Lenin's cooperative theories, arguing they did not fit China's unfinished revolution and peasant base.

Lu concludes that the observers' reports improved the CCP's image and for a time encouraged US-CCP military cooperation, with Carlson and Barrett urging closer ties and arms aid. After the failure of Hurley's mediation and Stilwell's recall in late 1944, US policy turned sharply rightward. In Lu's account, decision-makers dismissed the reports as biased because of ideological fixation, which reflected a two-sided American China policy. Read the original if you study US-CCP relations in the War of Resistance, or want a Chinese scholarly account of how American eyewitnesses framed the "Sinification of Marxism".
quoteEn: Whatever the qualifier, its meaning is the CCP's continuing exploration of the Sinification of Marxism, and this is the correct answer to "what is Chinese communism?"
quoteZh: 不论是何种限定，其内涵都是中共中国化马克思主义的持续探索，这便是“何为中国共产主义”之正解。

glossary.explanation: The idea, put forward by Mao Zedong at the Sixth Plenum of the Sixth Central Committee (1938), that Marxism must be applied to and developed from China's concrete conditions. It later became a core formula of Party theory.

A wartime base-area agrarian policy lowering rents and interest while requiring tenants to pay the reduced amounts. It replaced land confiscation in order to keep landlords within the anti-Japanese united front.

t: Capital's critique of capitalist civilisation and its world-historical significance
zh: 《资本论》对资本文明的批判及世界历史意义
paras: Lu Shaochen asks what kind of critique Marx's Capital offers of what the author calls "capital civilisation" (capitalist civilisation), and where it points historically. Lu argues that the work is a political-philosophical critique, not only a critique of capitalist exploitation. It exposes the political preconditions of capitalist civilisation and shows the path from political emancipation to human emancipation, meaning the all-round development of the person. The piece appeared in the Chinese Social Sciences Today in December 2023.

The article is a short essay that sets Marx's argument beside modern Western political thought and contemporary philosophy. It draws on Fergusson, Machiavelli, Hobbes, Hegel, Kant, Tönnies, Weber, Tocqueville and Adam Smith, and on later writers such as Byung-Chul Han, Dorothea Dörmer (Dallmayr-style commentary on subjectivity), Robert Bellah and Habermas. It moves from the totality of the system, through individualism and the loss of community, to poverty and the world system, and ends with Marx's alternative.

Lu's first move is that capitalist civilisation is a total system, not the sum of individual choices, so criticism and transcendence must also be total. Following Marx and Han, Lu describes a rule without a ruler in which competition imposes capital's laws on everyone. Individuals are reduced to egoistic, mutually opposed bearers of exchange relations, and the ideal of self-realisation becomes compulsive "self-exploitation". Lu says this produces narcissism, nihilism and, in the long run, populism, fundamentalism and renewed conflict between nation-states. Lu argues that only Marx showed absolute individualism to be a result of generalised exchange rather than its starting point. A second move is that the logic of reification becomes power, appearing as polarisation of wealth and poverty within states and as a centre–periphery order globally.

Against Hegel's reliance on colonial expansion, Lu says Marx proposed active state governance. Through education it would steer people living by direct labour towards work in invention and artistic creation, and shift production from labour time to free time. Lu adds that this requires treating political economy first as political critique and seeing individuals as community members. Lu concludes that humanity now calls for a new freedom based on community and all-round development, achieved through long-term state governance that gives human relations back to people. Lu also links this to the significance of the Chinese traditional culture of family-and-country feeling and responsibility. Read the original if you want a brief example of how a Chinese scholar reads Capital as political philosophy and ties it to Chinese cultural themes.
quoteEn: Through his analysis of the logic of capital's self-valorisation, Marx revealed a predicament that the proprietary logic of free exchange in modern capitalist civilisation cannot explain or answer.
quoteZh: 马克思则通过对资本增殖逻辑的分析，揭示了现代资本文明自由交换的所有权逻辑难以解释和回答的困局

t: Marx's historical thinking and its contemporary perspective
zh: 马克思的历史性思想及其当代透视
paras: This short commentary, published in the Chinese Social Sciences Today (9 November 2023), asks what is distinctive about Marx's way of thinking historically. Yuan Bei argues that Marx's break with speculative philosophy lay not simply in starting from social reality, but in analysing that reality historically. The piece also asks how Marx's emphasis on objective laws can be reconciled with contingency and the possibility of emancipatory politics.

The article begins with the materialist conception of history of 1845 and the claim in The German Ideology that there is only one science, the science of history. It then contrasts Marx with classical political economy and Hegel, and turns to later disputes: the Second International's economic determinism, the stress on subjectivity from Lukács to the Frankfurt School, and Louis Althusser's "materialism of the encounter", read with Badiou and Žižek on the "event".

Yuan argues that for Marx the social world is a product of industry and social conditions, not something given from the beginning. Historical analysis therefore does two things. It affirms objective laws, grounded in the production and reproduction of material life, and it attends to concrete historical conjunctures, in which elements meet in relations of forces. Classical political economy, in Yuan's account, was "supra-historical" because it treated capitalist production and economic categories as natural and eternal, whereas Marx saw capital as a process and its categories as historical and transitory. Hegel, by contrast, focused on the self-knowledge of absolute spirit, while Marx focused on real individuals engaged in material production, with the aim of breaking the rule of capital and achieving the liberation of the proletariat and humanity.

Yuan holds that Althusser's emphasis on contingency is not groundless, since Marx himself, in his 1871 letter to Kugelmann, said that chance affects the acceleration and delay of development. Yuan concludes that emancipatory politics requires recognising both historical necessity and the contingent event. Drawing on Badiou's two kinds of temporality, Yuan suggests that revolutionary possibility depends on whether individuals can seize fleeting situations opened by an event. Read the original if you want a compact Chinese account of how Marx's historical method is positioned against Hegel, classical political economy and Althusser's aleatory materialism.
quoteEn: All of his philosophical discourse on history points to one clear theme: how to break the domination of the logic of capital and achieve the liberation of the proletariat and of humanity.
quoteZh: 他关于历史的全部哲学言说指向一个明确的主题，这就是如何打破资本逻辑的支配，实现无产阶级和人类的解放。

glossary.explanation: The Marxist theory, set out by Marx and Engels in the mid-1840s, that social being and the mode of material production shape consciousness and historical change. It is often rendered in English as historical materialism.
A late concept of Louis Althusser, who read history as an open process shaped by contingent meetings of elements rather than a predetermined course.

t: The technological (Technologie) import of machinery and large-scale industry in Capital
zh: 《资本论》机器大工业的工艺学意旨
paras: Li Jiayi asks how Marxist political philosophy can grasp the political essence of modern capitalism in an age of highly developed machine industry. The short piece, published in the Chinese Social Sciences Today in December 2023, answers that the route is Marx's 'technology' (工艺学, the study of how production is carried out) in Capital. Li contends that this approach exposes how bourgeois power relations are built into both material and mental production, 'from below'.

The article has three parts. The first distinguishes the general and the specific meanings of technology in Capital: the general study of humanity's active relation to nature, and the study of the direct production process under a particular social form. The second examines how machine industry builds the modern logic of technology, through the replacement of the human organism by an objective productive organism and through the principle of decomposition and synthesis. The third turns to political philosophy and to how technology works as a form of power.

Li argues that under capitalism the machine becomes capital and makes the labour process subordinate to it. Machinery creates no value but yields surplus value by shortening the part of the working day the worker spends for themselves. Workers, owning nothing but their labour-power, must be merged into the machine system, so that, in Marx's words, the means of production use the worker. Li lists four features of this domination by things: capitalist ownership of means of production and products; the machine as a screen that makes capital's power less visible; the machine as objectified general intellect and the separation of manual from mental labour; and a shift of workers' struggle from direct to indirect confrontation. Technology then reproduces itself as management science, culture and ideology. Li, drawing on Foucault, reads management technology as a 'political anatomy' and 'mechanics of power' that disciplines bodies and measures even leisure time.

Li concludes that analysing the labour process behind the value-expansion process reveals the historical character of capitalist power. Because modern industry's technical basis is revolutionary, Li holds, it must come into irreconcilable conflict with the logic of capital's valorisation and eventually undermine it. Compared with deriving power relations from political economy, Li claims, the technological route better reveals the micro-mechanisms of capitalist power. Read the original if you want a concise Chinese-language reading of Marx's technology concept as a bridge between political economy and political philosophy, including its use of Foucault.
quoteEn: Machine industry has reshaped the logic of power, and the direct domination of people by things has become a new form of rule in capitalist society.
quoteZh: 机器大工业重塑了权力的统治逻辑，物对人的直接统治成为资本社会统治的新形式和新形态。

t: The three dimensions of Marx's critique of political economy
zh: 马克思政治经济学批判的三重维度
paras: Liu Yiwen asks in what sense Marx's critique of political economy is a critical theory, and answers that it is at bottom a critique of justice. Drawing on Gould's remark that in this critique Marx revealed the ethical substance of his theory of justice, Liu argues that the critique carries Marx's thinking on justice. It exposes a substantive injustice behind capitalism's apparent justice in exchange and distribution.

The article takes up the debate on "Marx and justice" that began in the 1970s, including the "Tucker–Wood thesis". It works through three dimensions of Marx's critique in turn: alienation, exploitation and crisis. For each, it asks why the phenomenon should count as a cause of capitalism's injustice, since Liu says no self-evident link joins them. The text appeared in the Chinese Social Sciences Today on 21 December 2023.

On alienation, Liu reads it as capital's structural, self-perpetuating domination over labour, a relation that labour itself produces. Free and equal exchange hides this relation, and it generates fetishism that naturalises historical social relations. It also exposes a contradiction between the spheres of exchange and production, since capitalism violates the justice standard it set for itself. Exploitation is treated as the other side of the same process: capital appropriates the product of labour without payment, in a coercive and permanent way. For crisis, Liu argues that treating it as a purely economic matter hides its link to the system. The injustice lies in the logic of capital that causes, conceals and tries to sustain comprehensive social breakdown, not in the breakdown itself. Following Marx, crises end only with capitalism's collapse from within and proletarian revolution from outside.

Liu concludes that alienation, exploitation and crisis are each grounds for Marx's justice critique, but the final target is the operating logic of the capitalist system. In Liu's account, the shift from the laws of commodity production to the laws of capitalist appropriation serves unlimited capital accumulation and the system's perpetuation. The critique is therefore a distinctive holistic, comprehensive and developmental theory. Read the original if you want a concise Chinese-language account of how Marx's critique of political economy can be read as a theory of justice.
quoteEn: Marx's critique of political economy is a critique of justice.
quoteZh: 马克思的政治经济学批判是一种正义批判。

t: Capital's critique of Locke's labour theory of property
zh: 《资本论》对洛克劳动所有权理论的批判
paras: Cheng Tong asks what exactly Marx criticised in John Locke's theory that labour gives rise to ownership. The article takes issue with a widely held scholarly view that Marx simply pointed to a 'separation of ownership and labour' in capitalism, which supposedly made Locke's 'identity of ownership and labour' obsolete. Cheng argues instead that Marx's real objection is that this identity still holds formally under capitalism but has changed its content, so that it now serves the capitalist rather than the labourer.

The piece opens with Locke's Two Treatises of Government and the 'identity of ownership and labour' at the core of his argument. It then reviews the 'separation' reading, citing the Japanese scholar Mochizuki Seiji and Marx's well-known formulations in the 1857–58 and 1861–63 manuscripts and in the German editions of Capital, Volume I. The article then turns to textual evidence from the French edition and to Marx's own concepts in Capital and its manuscripts.

Cheng's first move is philological. The famous passage on the separation of ownership and labour was deleted from the French edition of Capital, Volume I, the last version Marx revised, and replaced by a sentence about the disappearance of the appearance of equivalent exchange. Marx's lists of revisions and his annotated copy of the second German edition confirm that later editions were to follow the French text. 'Separation of labour and product' became 'separation of product and producer'. Cheng reads this as Marx recognising that the earlier wording was imprecise or erroneous.

The second move is conceptual. Marx distinguishes the 'bearer' of labour from its 'owner'. Once the capitalist buys labour-power, its use-value, which is labour itself, belongs to the capitalist, and so does the product. Ownership and labour are therefore identical in the capitalist, which entails the separation of ownership from the labourer. Cheng concludes that Locke's error lies not in ignoring a separation but in applying a pre-capitalist, small-producer identity to capitalist property, thereby defending it with an ideology of labour-based property. Read the original if you want a close textual argument, drawn from the Marx manuscripts and the French edition, on how Marx answered Locke.
quoteEn: What truly belongs to Marx is the view that in capitalist society ownership and labour have not separated; on the contrary, the 'identity of ownership and labour' still holds in form.
quoteZh: 真正属于马克思的观点是，在资本主义社会中，所有权与劳动并未分离，相反，“所有权与劳动的同一性”在形式上仍然成立。

t: Taking the right path of modernization for a large country with an enormous population
zh: 走好人口规模巨大的大国现代化道路
paras: Taking up Xi Jinping's statement that Chinese modernization is modernization of a huge population, Ouyang argues that population scale is a defining feature of the Chinese path and the basic starting point for decision-making. The article contends that three tasks follow from this feature: promoting common prosperity, building a leading country in education, and driving growth mainly through domestic demand.

The commentary is organised under three headings, one for each task. It draws on World Bank figures for 2021, national statistics on educational attainment, and Xi's remarks on China's market size and population.

On common prosperity, Ouyang notes that China's roughly 1.41 billion people moving into modernity would, in the author's figures, raise the number of people in high-income countries by 1.28 times. The author proposes coordinated regional development and rural revitalization to address regional and urban–rural imbalances. On education, Ouyang argues that population size is an asset rather than a constraint. Having turned labour quantity into an advantage in early reform and opening up, China now needs a human-capital dividend, built through equalised basic education, vocational training, diversified higher education and lifelong learning. On demand, the author says the export-oriented model suited the period of low incomes, whereas rising incomes make a domestic-led model, a unified national market, secure industrial and supply chains and technological self-reliance the best choice.

Ouyang concludes that these three priorities are the urgent requirements for realising Chinese modernization under conditions of huge population scale. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Chinese official commentary links population size to policy priorities in distribution, education and domestic-demand-led growth.
quoteEn: This population scale is not a constraint on achieving modernization, but a positive factor that can be turned to its advantage.
quoteZh: 这种人口规模不是实现现代化的掣肘,而是可以转化为实现现代化的积极因素。

glossary.explanation: The official term for China's path to modernization, which Party documents describe as having distinctive features, including a huge population, common prosperity and socialist orientation.
A stated goal of socialism with Chinese characteristics, meaning prosperity shared by all rather than a few, and prominent in official policy since 2021.
A national strategy announced in 2017 to modernize agriculture and rural areas and narrow the urban–rural gap.
The policy of economic reform and opening to the outside world begun in China in 1978.

t: The transformation of the Marxist view of history in the new era and its intellectual effects
zh: 新时代马克思主义历史观变革及其思想效应
paras: Jin Xingyu takes up the many references to "history" in the report to the 20th Party Congress (2022) and asks what view of history lies behind the achievements of the decade since 2012. The article argues that this view, built on dialectical and historical materialism, enriches and deepens the Marxist conception of history. It also claims that the view lays a cultural foundation for building China into a modern socialist country.

The article is organised in three parts that follow the classic division of a theory into ontology, epistemology and methodology. The first part treats the ontology of history through four features: essence, process, driving force and form. The second treats the epistemology of history through five forms: historical time, position, mission, experience and spirit. The third treats historical methodology through five practices, from the "big view of history" to taking historical initiative in the world.

Jin's core claim is that Xi Jinping's statements turn the Marxist view of history into a framework for understanding the Party's own record. On ontology, history is presented as a practical history centred on the mode of production. It is a comprehensive history spanning the histories of the Party, New China, reform and opening up, socialism and the Chinese nation. It is driven by the principal contradiction, which the 19th Party Congress (2017) redefined, and it is written by the people. On epistemology, the author places the Party at a "critical moment" between the first and second centenary goals. The third historical resolution (2021) draws ten lessons from the past century. On methodology, Jin links the big view of history to assessing the two periods before and after reform and opening up as continuous in essence. The author also links it to judging historical figures within their conditions and to opposing historical nihilism, which the article says aims to deny Marxism's guiding role and the Party's leadership.

Jin concludes that the three theoretical dimensions form an organic whole within socialism with Chinese characteristics. The author says this view strengthens historical confidence and the authority of the Party Central Committee and its core leader. Jin calls on the Party to keep "historical clarity" and to take historical initiative in advancing the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. Read the original if you want a systematic, officially aligned account of how Party theorists organise Xi-era statements on history into ontology, epistemology and methodology.
quoteEn: The big view of history fits the methodological requirement of grasping the \"theme, main thread and mainstream essence\", helps avoid a metaphysical view of history that cuts history apart, and ensures the correct direction of historical development.
quoteZh: 大历史观契合把握“主题主线、主流本质”的方法要求，有助于避免割裂历史的形而上学历史观，确保历史发展的正确前进方向。

glossary.explanation: A term Xi Jinping has promoted since around 2021. It asks the Party to analyse events across long historical sweeps, the tide of the times and global developments, and to grasp their themes and mainstream essence.

In official Chinese usage, a label for views that question or negate the Party's historical narrative, its leaders or the historical necessity of socialism in China. Party texts treat it as an ideological threat.
The 2021 Central Committee resolution on the Party's major achievements and historical experience over its first century. It follows the resolutions of 1945 and 1981.

A Marxist-Leninist concept used by the Party to define the central task of each period. The 19th Party Congress (2017) restated it as the contradiction between people's growing need for a better life and unbalanced, inadequate development.
The goals of building a moderately prosperous society by the Party's centenary (2021) and a modern socialist country by the centenary of the People's Republic (2049).

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The official overarching goal of Party policy, presented as overcoming the humiliations of modern China and restoring national strength and standing.

t: Reform and opening up and the founding and development of socialism with Chinese characteristics
zh: 改革开放与中国特色社会主义的开创和发展
paras: Marking 45 years since the Party's decision to launch reform and opening up, Qin Gang asks how that policy and socialism with Chinese characteristics relate to each other. The article argues that the two form a single, integrated process: reform and opening up gave rise to socialism with Chinese characteristics and keeps driving its development, while the latter displays the achievements of reform. Qin holds that the policy's greatest historical contribution is precisely the founding and growth of this form of socialism.

The article has three parts. The first sets out four ways reform and opening up contributed: it laid a foundation, opened space for innovation, gathered strength and supplied lasting momentum. The second describes innovative development in the new era under Xi Jinping, in five respects: faster pace, demonstrated superiority, governance effectiveness, contributions to the world and a demonstration effect. The third distils six lessons from experience.

Qin's central reasoning is that freeing thought led to reform, and reform in turn moved socialism beyond rigid thinking and rigid institutions. The article credits two historic shifts, from a highly centralised planned economy to a socialist market economy and from a closed to an open country, with reshaping ownership and distribution structures. For the new era, it cites poverty alleviation, ecological protection, ethnic unity, the Belt and Road Initiative, whole-process people's democracy and Chinese modernization as evidence of governance capacity and wider influence. Qin also reports 2022 per capita GDP of 12,741 US dollars and a middle-income group of over 400 million.

The six lessons are: theoretical innovation grounded in practice; independent exploration; putting people's rights and interests first; giving society stable expectations through phased goals and five-year plans; actively integrating national development into world development; and the Party's leading role. Qin presents the last as a distinctive strength, arguing that the Party represents the whole of society rather than any interest group. Qin also acknowledges remaining problems, such as entrenched interests and institutional defects, and calls for deeper reform and opening up. Read the original if you want an official-line overview of how Party theorists link reform and opening up to socialism with Chinese characteristics and to the new era.
quoteEn: The historical contributions of reform and opening up are many-sided, and the greatest of them is that it promoted the founding and development of socialism with Chinese characteristics.
quoteZh: 改革开放的历史贡献是多方面的，其中，最大的贡献就是促进了中国特色社会主义的开创和发展。

glossary.explanation: The policy of economic reform and opening to the outside world launched under Deng Xiaoping from the Third Plenum of the 11th Central Committee in December 1978.
The official name for China's path, theory and system since the reform era, combining Party leadership and public ownership with a market economy.

glossary.zh: 社会主义市场经济体制
glossary.explanation: The economic system adopted as the official reform goal in 1992, combining market mechanisms with a basic socialist system and a leading public sector.
Official term for China's democratic model, presented by the Party as covering every stage of political life rather than only elections.
The official concept of China's own path to modernization, which Party texts contrast with Western models.
China's international infrastructure and economic cooperation initiative, launched by Xi Jinping in 2013.

t: A model of combining general principles with historical conditions
st: A theoretical interpretation of the prefaces to the Communist Manifesto
zh: 一般原理和历史条件相结合的典范
zhSub: 《共产党宣言》序言的理论阐释
source: China Social Sciences Today (Zhongguo shehui kexue bao), 14 November 2023
paras: This short commentary asks what the seven prefaces that Marx and Engels wrote for later editions of the Communist Manifesto show about how Marxism should be applied. Jiang Tianlun argues that, although the prefaces were written at different times, for different audiences and about different problems, together they exemplify combining the general and basic principles of Marxism with historical conditions and concrete realities. The author treats this combination as the methodological core running through them.

The piece first sketches the Manifesto's drafting for the Communist League in 1848, its predecessor drafts by Engels and its four-part structure. It then argues that the prefaces re-elaborate scientific socialism in light of conditions in particular countries. Jiang organises the discussion around three themes: the terminology of communism versus socialism, the path of development for non-Western societies, and the relation between the unity of the world's proletarians and national independence.

On terminology, Jiang follows Engels's explanation in the 1888 and 1890 prefaces. In 1847 socialism was a bourgeois movement and communism a working-class movement, so the Manifesto could not be called a socialist manifesto. Jiang adds that the choice also criticised the petty-bourgeois socialist currents of later decades, such as Lassalleanism, Proudhonism and Fabianism. On Russia, Jiang reads the 1882 Russian preface and Marx's reply to Vera Zasulich as refusing to apply the Western sequence of social formations mechanically. The rural commune could become a starting point for communist development if a Russian revolution signalled, and complemented, proletarian revolution in the West. On the Polish and Italian prefaces, Jiang reads Engels as holding that international proletarian cooperation requires each nation's independence, so that "Workers of the world, unite!" is tied to national industrial development and the socialist movement.

Jiang concludes that Marx and Engels never set an abstract, rigid "law" or single path for historical development. In the author's account, their attention to each nation's circumstances and traditions, also seen in Engels's remarks on the English and German workers' movements, is a model of applying and innovating theory. Jiang also suggests that the communism–socialism distinction offers a methodological basis for understanding the unity of the common ideal of socialism with Chinese characteristics and the lofty ideal of communism. Read the original if you want a compact Chinese account of how the Manifesto's prefaces are used to support the principle of integrating general theory with specific conditions.
quoteEn: This means that the requirement that the practical application of Marxism's general principles "everywhere and at all times depend on the historical conditions of the day" inherently includes concern for the concrete realities and historical traditions of each nation.
quoteZh: 这就意味着，马克思主义一般原理的实际运用，“随时随地都要以当时的历史条件为转移”这一要求内在包含着对各个民族的具体实际和历史传统的关切。

glossary.explanation: The official name for the Chinese Communist Party's model of socialism, associated with reform and opening up from the late 1970s. It presents China's path as Marxism applied to Chinese conditions.
The international workers' organisation founded in 1847 for which Marx and Engels drafted the Manifesto.

t: The context and mechanism of social self-criticism
zh: 社会自我批判的语境与机制
source: Chinese Social Sciences Today (中国社会科学报), 14 November 2023
paras: Lü Jingmei takes up "social self-criticism" as a theoretical and practical problem, arguing that it must be approached through a historical-materialist reading of the classic texts. The article holds that notions such as social self-adjustment, self-development, self-improvement and self-transcendence all belong to this category and are in essence processes of society's self-movement. To grasp it systematically, Lü proposes to clarify its context, its concept and its mechanism.

The piece is a short commentary in three parts: the context in which the topic arises, a conceptual clarification, and an analysis of mechanism. It draws chiefly on the Communist Manifesto, Marx's 1857 Introduction to the Critique of Political Economy and the Preface to A Contribution to the Critique of Political Economy. It also looks at the transformations of capitalism since the nineteenth century and at socialism with Chinese characteristics.

On context, Lü sets the Manifesto's optimistic judgement of the two inevitabilities beside the Preface's more cautious point that new relations of production never appear before their material conditions mature. Capitalism, in Lü's account, has moved from free competition to organised, welfare-state and neoliberal forms without resolving its basic contradiction. On concept, Lü argues that "social self-criticism" fits better than "social criticism" because society is both the object and the subject of critique, and finds the idea implicit in Marx's phrase "self-criticism of bourgeois society". It has a real form (the "criticism by weapons") and an ideal form (the "weapon of criticism"). On mechanism, Lü argues that it starts from concrete individuals whose critique spreads into a collective effect, and that it needs an objective condition (deep-rooted contradictions) and a subjective one (a class-conscious proletariat). It also needs a reference frame of social reality and social ideal, and a unity of retrospect, tracking of the present and prospect.

Lü concludes by distinguishing three routes of social self-criticism according to the relation of individual, society and state: an individualist route starting from the atomised individual, a statist route starting from the nation-state, and a socialist route starting from concrete individuals in social relations. The author presents the third as going beyond the other two, since it holds that the free development of each is the condition for the free development of all. Read the original if you want a concise conceptual framing of Marx's "self-criticism of bourgeois society" and its link to contemporary questions about capitalism and socialism with Chinese characteristics.
quoteEn: The subject of social self-criticism is society itself.
quoteZh: 社会自我批判的主体是社会本身。

glossary.explanation: The official name for China's path of socialist development since reform and opening up, combining Party leadership with a market-oriented economy.
The author's concept of society acting as both subject and object of critique, derived from Marx's phrase "self-criticism of bourgeois society".
A shorthand for the Manifesto's claim that the bourgeoisie's fall and the proletariat's victory are equally unavoidable. It is often paired with the "two never" of the 1859 Preface.

keywords: Introduction to the Critique of Political Economy

t: Locke's theory of property rights and its influence on Marx
zh: 洛克财产权理论对马克思的影响
source: Chinese Social Sciences Today (Zhongguo shehui kexue bao), 9 November 2023
paras: Marx read Locke's Two Treatises of Government and his economics closely, yet Zhang observes that Chinese Marxist theory has paid little attention to how Locke shaped Marx's social and political philosophy. The article argues that Locke is both an important source of that philosophy and the starting point from which Marx criticised and went beyond liberalism and classical political economy. Zhang takes property rights as a preliminary case, offered as an opening for further discussion.

The piece, a short newspaper article, first sets out the essence of Locke's property theory, then turns to Marx's reflections on property, and finally to the ways Marx surpassed Locke. Hegel and Rousseau appear as intermediaries, and Adam Smith as the thinker who raised labour to a principle of political economy. Zhang draws on Marx's Economic and Philosophic Manuscripts of 1844 and Theories of Surplus-Value.

Zhang reads Locke's politics as a defence of property because property is the concrete form of freedom. Government is secondary and instrumental, and Locke grounds property both in natural law and in labour being "mixed" with nature. Marx inherited two things: labour as the justification of property, and the link between property and human freedom. He also saw Locke as a spokesman of the rising English bourgeoisie, progressive against feudal claims but conservative in presenting private property as natural and eternal. Marx's break comes through his distinction between objectified labour and alienated labour, and between "private property as labour" and "private property as capital". Zhang argues that Locke missed this distinction and so treated capitalist property as the product of objectified labour. For Marx, property in Locke's sense is property as capital. It springs from alienated labour, is therefore historical rather than natural, and has its own emergence and demise.

Zhang concludes that Marx did not justify private property as the basis of individual freedom, as Locke did, but exposed the capital relation as an obstacle to self-realisation. Marx treated property as an economic and social question of human emancipation, not a matter of natural right or political emancipation. On this reading, property and ownership can be settled only through social and political revolution that abolishes private property as capital. Read the original if you want a concise account of how Locke, Hegel and Rousseau figure in Marx's early critique of property.
quoteEn: Marx grasped it as a major economic and social question, the question of \"human emancipation\".
quoteZh: 马克思把它把握为重大的经济和社会问题（“人类解放”问题）。

t: The scientific disclosure of the inherent laws of the innovative development of Marxism in the new era
zh: 新时代对马克思主义创新发展内在规律的科学揭示
paras: Liu Jianjun and Qiu Anqi ask whether the innovative development of Marxism follows identifiable laws, and argue that it does. In their account, since the 18th Party Congress (2012) Xi Jinping and the Chinese communists around him have not only created Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era but also scientifically disclosed the basic laws governing how Marxism develops through innovation. The authors present this as a major new theoretical contribution and a research topic that scholars should take up.

The article first justifies speaking of laws of 'innovative development' rather than of Marxism's development in general. It cites Marx, Engels and Lenin, then Mao Zedong, Deng Xiaoping, Jiang Zemin and Hu Jintao, before tracing Xi's statements from 2013 to 2023. From these the authors distil four basic laws, each treated in its own section: the dialectical unity of upholding fundamental principles and innovation; the cross-fusion of localization and adaptation to the times; the organic combination of differentiated and fusion development; and the benign interaction of theoretical and practical innovation.

On the first law, the authors argue that 'upholding what is correct' (shouzheng) is the precondition of innovation, because of Marxism's truth content and its guiding role for Party and state; it means keeping its core, not its letter. They cite Bernstein's revisionism and Wang Ming's dogmatism as failures to hold the two together, and Lenin and Mao as models. On the second, localization (spatial) and adaptation to the times (temporal) are inseparable, and the Two Integrations are presented as the Chinese form with wider applicability. On the third, innovation either unfolds from within an existing proposition (for example from one integration to two) or fuses with other thought, as Xi puts it, in a 'chemical reaction' rather than a 'platter'. On the fourth, practice supplies the basis for theory and theory guides practice, provided practice does not violate theoretical logic and theory does not outrun practice.

The authors conclude that these laws are embodied in the formation of Xi Jinping Thought, described as contemporary Chinese Marxism and Marxism of the twenty-first century. They call for upholding fundamentals without wavering and innovating without pause, for continuing the Two Integrations, and for advancing Chinese modernization so that theory and practice enrich each other. Read the original if you want a systematic statement, in the official Chinese framework, of how Party theorists conceptualise the rules of Marxist theoretical innovation under Xi.
quoteEn: Upholding what is correct does not mean clinging to the old, nor holding to the books and articles of Marxism, but strictly adhering to its core, essence and soul.
quoteZh: 守正不是守旧，不是守马克思主义的本本、条条，而是要恪守其核心、本质和灵魂。

glossary.literal: guarding what is correct and innovating
glossary.explanation: A formula stressing that Marxist theory must keep its core truths while innovating. It appears among the 'six musts' in the 20th Party Congress report (2022).
The principle of combining Marxism's basic tenets with China's concrete realities and with China's fine traditional culture. The second integration was added under Xi Jinping.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The official guiding ideology of the Chinese Communist Party, written into the Party constitution in 2017.
The official term for China's own path of modernization, promoted by the Party especially since the 20th Party Congress (2022).

t: Lenin's theory of the new-type proletarian party and its contemporary value
zh: 列宁的新型无产阶级政党理论及其当代价值
source: Journal of Changshu Institute of Technology, 2023 no. 6
paras: Yuan and Ma ask what Lenin's theory of the new-type proletarian party consists of and why it still matters. They argue that the theory, developed against Bernstein's revisionism and Russian 'Economism', remains a basic principle and scientific guide for proletarian parties today. In their account, whether a socialist country correctly assesses and keeps to this theory, and to the party's leadership, determines its future.

The article has three parts. The first sets out why Lenin judged a new-type party necessary and urgent in Russia around 1900. The second reconstructs the theory itself, in six elements: Marxism as guiding ideology, an organisation of revolutionaries, the core role of leaders and a leading group, the 'inculcation' of socialist consciousness, the party programme, and the party rules with democratic centralism. The third turns to Xi Jinping's statements on party-building and to the Soviet collapse.

In the authors' reading, Lenin answered a workers' movement that was growing but led by a disorganised, 'amateurish' party whose Economist wing separated economic from political struggle and celebrated spontaneity. Lenin held that workers alone produce only trade-union consciousness, so socialist consciousness must be brought from outside. He also held that the party must be a disciplined vanguard distinct from the whole class, and that centralism, binding rules and discipline were needed against federalism and autonomy. For the present, the authors argue that upholding the authority of the Party Central Committee and centralised, unified leadership is a major principle of a mature Marxist governing party. They reject the view that these principles suit only a revolutionary party seeking power, citing Xi's statement that the Communist Party of China is both a Marxist governing party and a Marxist revolutionary party.

The authors take Gorbachev's reforms as a negative case. In their account, 'unrestricted openness' and radical democratisation, together with the amendment of Article 6 of the Soviet constitution in 1990, ended the party's leading position and led to the party's collapse and the Soviet Union's disintegration. They conclude that the Communist Party of China must keep to Marxist-Leninist party-building principles, defend its leadership and long-term governing position, and resist calls for multiparty or Western-style systems. Read the original if you want to see how a Chinese Party-affiliated scholarly article uses Lenin's party theory and the Soviet case to justify centralised Party leadership today.
quoteEn: The party's leading position and role in the state is a fundamental question bearing on the survival or demise of the socialist system.
quoteZh: 党在国家中的领导地位及作用是关系社会主义制度存亡的根本问题。

glossary.explanation: The organisational principle of Leninist parties, combining discussion and election with binding decisions, discipline, and subordination of lower bodies to higher ones and the minority to the majority.
A tendency in the Russian Social-Democratic movement around 1900 that stressed workers' economic struggle over political struggle. Lenin attacked it in What Is To Be Done?.
Lenin's thesis that socialist consciousness does not arise spontaneously from workers' struggles but is brought to the working class from outside by the party.
A formula in contemporary Chinese Party discourse for the Central Committee's authority over the whole Party, often linked to the Party's overall leadership of all work.

t: The practical logic of building a modern civilization of the Chinese nation
zh: 建设中华民族现代文明的实践逻辑
paras: This commentary, published in Guangming Daily in January 2024, asks how the new cultural mission of building a modern civilization of the Chinese nation is to be carried out in practice. Zhang and Guo argue that the task follows from the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation and must be guided by Xi Jinping's thinking on culture, which they present as the cultural component of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era.

The article is organised around four elements: the leading force, the spiritual foundation, the fundamental method and the path of advance. Each is introduced with extensive quotation from Xi Jinping's speeches and addressed in turn: Party leadership over culture, cultural confidence, the Second Integration, and the unity of local rootedness with openness to the world.

The authors first argue that culture is part of the superstructure and carries a class position, so the Party's leadership over cultural work and Marxism's guiding role in ideology secure the right direction. In their reading, the "modern" in the new civilization comes from Marxism's scientific truth, which "activates" traditional civilization. They then treat the Second Integration, the combination of Marxism with fine traditional Chinese culture, as the core method. It is described as a chemical reaction rather than a mechanical joining: Marxism gives tradition a modern form, and Chinese wisdom makes Marxism "Chinese". The authors say this process rebuilds the cultural subjectivity damaged in the modern era. Finally, they hold that Chinese modernization supplies the practical ground, and that the civilization must be both national and global, overcoming the polarised debate between wholesale Westernization and conservative revivalism.

The authors conclude that building the new civilization requires unwavering Party leadership, cultural confidence and independence in theory, deepening the Second Integration, and combining "upholding the ancestors" with "speaking new words". They add that this means drawing on the achievements of all human civilizations while creating a new form of human civilization. Read the original if you want a concise example of how official Party-aligned commentary in early 2024 framed Xi's cultural thought and the Second Integration.
quoteEn: Building a modern civilization of the Chinese nation is neither a return to the study to "sort out the national heritage" nor a simple recasting of traditional cultural forms in modern concepts. It requires fine traditional Chinese culture to be adapted to modern production and connected with modern life.
quoteZh: 建设中华民族现代文明不是复归书斋的“整理国故”，也不是简单用现代概念改造传统文化表达形式，而是要使中华优秀传统文化与现代生产相适应、与现代生活相贯通。

glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's formula, set out in 2023, for combining the basic tenets of Marxism with fine traditional Chinese culture. It follows the First Integration, which combined Marxism with China's concrete realities.
The official name for China's path of modernization, presented as distinct from Western models. It has been a central slogan since the 20th Party Congress (2022).
Confidence in China's own cultural values and vitality. Xi Jinping presents it as the foundation of confidence in the path, theory and system of socialism with Chinese characteristics.
The idea that Chinese culture should stand on its own position and identity. Official discourse presents it as a necessary basis for civilizational renewal.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology since 2017, written into the Party and state constitutions.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The official national goal of restoring China's strength and standing, closely associated with Xi Jinping's Chinese Dream.

keywords: modern civilization of the Chinese nation

t: Guiding the practice of reform and opening up in the new era with the grand view of history
zh: 以大历史观指导新时代改革开放实践
source: Party Building Research for Government Organs (Jiguan dangjian yanjiu), 2023 no. 12
paras: Xiong Daohong and Cai Ziwei ask how the grand view of history that Xi Jinping has urged the whole Party to adopt can be used to understand 45 years of reform and opening up and to guide its continuation. Their answer is that reform and opening up should be read within a wider frame of time and space, and that doing so strengthens historical consciousness and historical confidence. In their account it also supports a spirit of historical initiative in deepening reform and opening up in the new era.

The article has three parts. The first sets out the foundations: historical materialism, the correct view of Party history, and the Central Committee's repeated summings-up of reform and opening up, from the 1981 historical resolution to Xi's 2018 speech marking 40 years. The second says that grasping the history means grasping its theme, its main thread, its position and its relation to the world. The third turns to practice in the new era.

In the authors' account, the theme is upholding and developing socialism with Chinese characteristics, and the main thread is theoretical innovation, running from the truth-criterion debate through Deng Xiaoping Theory, the Three Represents and the Scientific Outlook on Development to Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era. They place reform and opening up within the "five histories" (Party, New China, socialism, the Chinese nation, and reform and opening up itself). The periods before and after 1978 are treated as a unified whole, not as opposites. For the new era the authors identify three features: continuity, as Chinese modernization is advanced and the people remain the subject of history while the country stays in the primary stage of socialism; particularity, because the principal contradiction has changed and reform now means harder institutional construction; and a worldwide dimension.

The authors conclude that the experience of 45 years must be carried into current practice. They call for a firm grasp of historical trends and the world situation, a people-centred approach, and a more active attitude toward change and openness. They also call for explaining China to the world and promoting mutual learning among civilizations. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party-affiliated scholars apply the grand view of history to reform and opening up, and how that history is periodised and framed in official discourse.
quoteEn: The history of reform and opening up is a concentrated expression, over a historical period, of the Party's worldwide vision and global outlook.
