quoteZh: 改革开放史是党的胸怀天下与世界眼光在历史时段上的集中体现。

glossary.explanation: A concept Xi Jinping has urged cadres to adopt, asking them to analyse events across long historical spans, the tide of the times and global developments. It is presented as an application of historical materialism.
The policy course launched at the Third Plenum of the 11th Central Committee in 1978, which introduced market-oriented reforms and opened China to the outside world.
The official name for the Party's path, theory and system since 1978, said to combine the basic principles of scientific socialism with China's conditions.
The official term for China's own path of modernization, stressed since the 20th Party Congress (2022) and presented as an alternative model to Western modernization.
The official judgement that China, though socialist, is still in an early and long stage of development. It underpins the Party's policy line.
A formula that groups the history of the Party, of New China, of reform and opening up, of socialist development and of the Chinese nation as the content of Party education.

t: Intelligent international communication of the concept of a community with a shared future for mankind: significance, communication system and pathways
zh: 人类命运共同体理念的智能化国际传播：意义向度、传播体系与路径
source: Social Science Journal (Shehui kexue jikan), 2023 no. 6
paras: Taking up the 20th Party Congress (2022) call to build a community with a shared future for mankind and to strengthen international communication capacity, Xu asks how artificial intelligence can help spread this concept abroad. The article argues that intelligent communication, driven by big data, computing power and algorithms, can turn the concept from a "Chinese discourse" into a "world discourse". It holds that this requires both exploiting the technology's advantages and overcoming political and cultural obstacles.

The article has five parts. It first describes how data, computing power and algorithms form a new platform for international communication. It then sets out the value dimensions of intelligent communication, namely discursive effectiveness, discursive confidence and discursive appeal, and the bottlenecks that limit it. The last two parts propose a communication system built on "warmth", "breadth" and "precision", and six practical choices. Xu draws repeatedly on Xi Jinping's statements on international communication.

Xu's core argument is that AI-based translation, virtual reality, agenda-setting and metaverse narrative networks can lower cultural barriers and let the concept reach audiences through immersive, personalised, point-to-point delivery. Against this, the author identifies three constraints. Western capital and Western-dominated opinion are said to intensify profit-driven competition over communication rules. Nationalist approaches to AI governance are said to breed ideological bias against the concept. Differences in values are said to open a "discourse gap" and to keep developing countries "voiceless". Xu portrays the concept's call for a fairer international order as in direct conflict with Western monopoly capital's interests.

Xu proposes six measures: adopting scene-based thinking, strengthening value guidance, building a dual-track mechanism of intelligent technology plus value concepts, using algorithms to identify friendly, neutral and hostile audiences for point-by-point communication, using blockchain to build trust, and raising intelligent communication to a strategic communication system with trained specialists and theoretical research. The author also warns against over-reliance on technology and calls for filtering ideas such as neoliberalism, populism and historical nihilism. Read the original if you want to see how a Chinese Marxist scholar links AI, algorithms and the metaverse to official goals for international discourse power.
quoteEn: Artificial intelligence, as a technology, has no values of its own; its practical needs and value concepts all come from the countries that are developing and using it.
quoteZh: 人工智能作为一项技术，自身并不具有价值观念，它的现实需求和价值理念全部来自于正在开发和利用这项技术的国家

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: A concept associated with Xi Jinping since 2012–13 that presents China's vision of global governance based on cooperation and shared interests. It is now a core element of Chinese foreign-policy discourse.

The capacity to shape agendas, narratives and rules in international public opinion. Chinese official texts say China's discourse power should match its comprehensive national strength and international standing.
A top-level, state-planned framework for international communication, which Xi Jinping has called on China to build with distinctive Chinese features.

keywords: community with a shared future for mankind

t: The philosophical code of the creative transformation and innovative development of excellent traditional Chinese culture
st: A historical-materialist perspective
zh: 中华优秀传统文化创造性转化和创新性发展的哲学密码
zhSub: 唯物史观的视角
paras: Zhang Ruitao and Guo Binbin take up the policy of the "creative transformation and innovative development" of excellent traditional Chinese culture, abbreviated as the "Two Creations". They note that existing scholarship mostly discusses its background, mechanisms, value and practical paths, and that its inner logic is under-examined. The authors ask what the Two Creations are, why they are "inevitable" and how to deepen them. Their answer is that, read through historical materialism, they follow necessarily from the relation between social being and social consciousness.

The article has four parts. It first defines the philosophical meaning of the two terms and the logical relation between them. It then sets out the historical logic, covering practice, human agency and the Chinese Communists' changing attitudes to tradition from Li Dazhao and Chen Duxiu to Mao Zedong, Deng Xiaoping and Xi Jinping. The third part gives the theoretical logic, and the fourth the practical logic: who carries it out, in what direction, and by what means.

The authors treat "creative transformation" as the dialectical unity of cultural continuity and change, an enlarged reproduction of culture, and an interplay of content and form. "Innovative development" is the replacement of old cultural forms by new ones, the absorption of modern and foreign culture, and the extension of culture's essential content. They argue that cultural change follows changes in material production. Culture's historical inheritance, its uneven development relative to the material base, and the mutual influence of the elements of social consciousness all require traditional culture to be remade. Examples include turning the idea of family-and-nation sentiment into a basis for patriotism and a sense of community while discarding its patriarchal and autocratic elements. They also cite the concept of "harmony and unity" (hehe) as a guide for relations between people, nature and civilizations.

In practice, the authors name the people as the decisive force and Party leadership as the political guarantee. They set four directions: scientific truth under Marxism, "Chinese characteristics", conformity to the times, and openness to the world. They propose four paths: coordinating cultural time and space through media; building a discourse system; improving legal protection of heritage and intellectual property; and improving national education. Read the original if you want a detailed account of how Chinese scholars ground the Two Creations in historical materialism and in the Party's evolving view of tradition.
quoteEn: The Two Creations are both what ought to be, constrained by society's material production, and what is in fact so, continuing the historical tradition.
quoteZh: “两创”既是受社会物质生产制约的“应然”，也是延续历史传统的“实然”。

glossary.zh: 创造性转化和创新性发展
glossary.explanation: A Party formula, abbreviated "Two Creations" (两创), for treating excellent traditional culture. Old forms are given new content, and the culture is then developed within contemporary socialist cultural construction. It has been emphasised since the 2010s, notably under Xi Jinping.
The Marxist theory that material production and social relations ultimately shape political and cultural life. The article uses it to explain why culture must change with society.

A Marxist pair of concepts: social being is society's material life, and social consciousness is its ideas and culture. The authors treat their relation as the basic question of historical materialism.

t: Learning from Mao Zedong's strategic foresight
zh: 学习毛泽东的战略远见
source: Chinese Leadership Science (中国领导科学), 2023 no. 6
paras: Bi Jingjing, a retired senior officer of the PLA National Defence University, takes up Mao Zedong's strategic foresight (zhanlüe yuanjian) as a core element of strategic leadership. Bi argues that Mao made a pioneering contribution to shaping the Chinese Communist Party's capacity for foresight. Studying it, in the author's view, is of major strategic significance for building a modern socialist country and advancing the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation amid a complex international situation.

The article has three parts. The first explains how Mao's foresight formed: as a product of adapting Marxism to the Chinese context, as a cognitive outlook drawing on Marxism and traditional Chinese culture, and as guidance for revolution and construction. The second sets out its practical structure in six aspects. The third discusses its philosophical basis. Examples run from the Jinggangshan base area and the Anti-Japanese War to the Civil War, the Korean War and early socialist construction.

Bi's central claim is that foresight is a combined quality of aspiration, belief, prediction, decision, patience and vigilance. The six aspects are national rejuvenation as aspiration, anticipation of the future, willingness to make trade-offs, confidence in victory, patience and wariness in times of safety. Illustrations include On Protracted War, the decision to give up Yan'an in 1947 to win all of China, the decision to enter the Korean War, and the 'going to the capital to take the examination' remark. Bi then roots these in dialectical materialism and historical materialism, in five unities: seeking truth from facts with far-sighted vision, a bright future with a tortuous road, strategic resolve with tactical flexibility, summing up history with opening the future, and individual with collective wisdom.

Bi concludes that Mao's foresight is a model for the Party's strategic thinking. The author states that, with instability and uncertainty rising in the external environment, understanding it should help the Party broaden its strategic horizon, strengthen strategic thinking and create new achievements. The text draws on Xi Jinping's assessments of Mao's decisions as reference points. Read the original if you want a Party-military view of how Mao's strategic thinking is presented as a resource for current leadership training and Party history education.
quoteEn: Strategic foresight is a strategic realm formed by the fusion of strategic aspiration, strategic conviction, strategic prediction, strategic choice and strategic clear-headedness.
quoteZh: 战略远见是由战略志向、战略信念、战略预见、战略抉择、战略清醒等融会而成的战略境界。

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A central Party goal, closely associated with Xi Jinping, of restoring China to national strength and prosperity after what the Party describes as a 'century of humiliation'.

glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context
glossary.explanation: The Party's term for applying Marxism's basic principles to China's concrete conditions, traditionally traced to Mao Zedong.
A principle taken from classical Chinese and made central to Mao Zedong Thought; it stresses starting from actual conditions rather than dogma.

t: Mao Zedong and the historical evolution of the modern civilisation of the Chinese nation
zh: 毛泽东与中华民族现代文明形态的历史演进
source: Ideological and Theoretical Education (思想理论教育), 2023 no. 12
paras: Written for the 130th anniversary of Mao Zedong's birth (26 December 2023), the article asks how Mao contributed to the formation of a modern civilisation of the Chinese nation. That is the task the Party set itself in the new era. Tian argues that Mao, by combining the basic principles of Marxism with China's concrete realities, made an indelible contribution to the creative transformation of Chinese culture from tradition to modernity. In Tian's account, this laid the theoretical foundation for the present call to build a modern Chinese civilisation.

The article has three parts. The first sets out the historical context: the clash between Western capitalist civilisation and traditional Chinese civilisation, and the failed attempts to find a path forward before the Communist Party. The second examines Mao's contributions in politics, the economy and culture. The third draws four lessons for today and links them to statements by Xi Jinping.

Tian's core argument is that Mao's contribution rested on three tasks: breaking down the old order and building a new one. In politics, this meant the people's democratic dictatorship, the system of people's congresses, multi-party cooperation under Party leadership, and regional ethnic autonomy. In the economy, it meant socialist transformation of ownership and industrialisation, which Tian credits with building a fairly complete independent industrial system. In culture, it meant the New Democratic cultural programme (national, scientific, mass), a selective attitude towards tradition, and the 'Hundred Flowers, Hundred Schools' policy. Tian presents these as the political premise, material basis and cultural roots of the modern civilisation of the Chinese nation. Earlier attempts, from 'Chinese learning as the base, Western learning for use' to 'wholesale Westernisation', are said to have failed because they did not handle the relation between Chinese and Western civilisation correctly.

Tian draws four lessons from Mao: keep to the standpoint of the Chinese nation, rely on the strength of the Chinese people, unswervingly follow China's own path, and treat the achievements of human civilisation with openness. Tian concludes that the Party must make building this civilisation its cultural mission, uphold the Two Integrations, and promote the coordinated development of material, cultural-ethical, political, social and ecological civilisation. Read the original if you want to see how a Chinese Party-school scholar links Mao's cultural thought to current official discourse on civilisation.
quoteEn: Mao Zedong's important idea of always building a new culture of the Chinese nation from the standpoint of the Chinese nation still has great practical guiding significance today.
quoteZh: 毛泽东始终立足于中华民族立场建设中华民族新文化的重要思想，在今天依然具有重大的现实指导意义。

glossary.explanation: Official formula for combining the basic tenets of Marxism with China's specific realities and with China's fine traditional culture. It was elaborated under Xi Jinping.

glossary.en: modern civilisation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A concept put forward by Xi Jinping in 2023 for a civilisation that combines the Chinese cultural tradition with modernisation under Party leadership. Tian uses it in a broad sense covering material, spiritual and institutional dimensions.
The official definition of the Chinese state system, in which democracy for the people is combined with dictatorship over reactionary forces. The formula was set out in the late 1940s.

glossary.literal: Let a hundred flowers bloom, let a hundred schools contend
glossary.explanation: A policy announced in 1956 encouraging diversity in the arts and academic debate under socialism. Tian notes that its implementation was later set back.
Mao Zedong's theory of a transitional stage of the Chinese revolution led by the proletariat, directed against imperialism and feudalism, before the move to socialism.

t: Mao Zedong and seeking truth from facts
zh: 毛泽东与实事求是
paras: This short commentary, published in Study Times in December 2023, examines the place of "seeking truth from facts" in Mao Zedong's thought. Zhang argues that it is one of the three basic aspects of the living soul of Mao Zedong Thought and its starting point, and that Mao created that body of thought by applying the basic tenets of Marxism-Leninism to Chinese realities.

The article is built in three parts. The first traces Mao's path from his youth to the post-Mao period: the Hunan tradition of practical statecraft, his early social investigations, the Jinggangshan base and the Central Soviet Area, the Yan'an-era writings and Rectification campaign, the early People's Republic, and the return to the principle after the Third Plenum of the 11th Central Committee (1978). The second part sets out Mao's original ideas on the subject, and the third draws lessons for the present.

Zhang's central argument is that Mao made seeking truth from facts the basis of the Party's ideological line. In the author's account, Mao insisted that theory must come from practice and be proved in practice, that Marxism must be "concretised" in China and developed rather than treated as dogma, and that dogmatism and subjectivism must be opposed. Zhang gives particular weight to investigation and research: Mao's slogan that without investigation there is no right to speak, his 1930 essay on opposing book worship, and his 1961 call for a year of investigation after the losses of the Great Leap Forward. The article also presents Mao as a lifelong reader of Marxist classics, especially the Communist Manifesto, and quotes Mao's remark that Chinese problems can only be solved by the Chinese.

Zhang concludes that Communists must remain models of seeking truth from facts, and ties this to Xi Jinping's description of the principle as the Party's basic method of thinking, work and leadership. The author calls for raising theoretical level, upholding the Two Integrations, linking theory with practice, and using investigation and research as a family heirloom. Read the original if you want a concise, officially oriented account of how Mao's approach to investigation and theory is presented to Party cadres today.
quoteEn: Mao Zedong made investigation and research the primary task of leadership work and the basis for deciding policy.
quoteZh: 毛泽东把调查研究作为领导工作的首要任务和决定政策的基础

glossary.explanation: A classical Chinese phrase that Mao Zedong gave a Marxist meaning in the 1940s. It became the core of the Party's ideological line, and was revived after 1978.
A formula in current Party theory: integrating the basic tenets of Marxism with China's specific realities and with its fine traditional culture.
A Party-wide movement launched by Mao in 1942 in Yan'an against subjectivism, sectarianism and "Party formalism" (stereotyped writing).
The Party's official term for Mao's theory and practice as an adaptation of Marxism-Leninism. It was written into the Party constitution at the 7th Party Congress in 1945.

t: Hegelian elements in Marxism outside China
zh: 国外马克思主义中的黑格尔思想元素
source: Chinese Social Sciences Today (中国社会科学报), 12 September 2023
paras: Lu Shaochen asks how Marxism outside China has dealt with Hegel, and why its relation to him has produced a mismatch. The article argues that these thinkers criticise modern society in a "near-Hegelian" way, drawing on Hegel's work on the state and national spirit. When they turn to practice and reconstruction, however, they fall back on a "near-Kantian" position that predates Hegel. Lu proposes a new Marxist scheme that stays Hegelian in method of critique and practice but replaces Hegel's ontology with the "positive existence" and "positive essence" of human beings.

The piece, a short newspaper article, moves through foreign Marxist thinkers in roughly chronological order. It starts with Georg Lukács and Antonio Gramsci, then covers Herbert Marcuse, Theodor Adorno, Jürgen Habermas and Axel Honneth. It cites Martin Jay, Allen Wood, Michael Feola, Kurt Leidecker and Perry Anderson as commentators. It ends with Hegel's own limits and Marx's critique of him.

Lu's central claim is that Hegel's lasting achievement was to explain the substantive spirit of Western modern society through the state idea and national spirit. Any serious critique of that society must therefore engage him. In Lu's reading, Lukács inherited the category of totality but detached the revolutionary subject from building the state idea and national spirit. Gramsci enriched Hegel on civil society and hegemony but did not grasp that national spirit is the state idea reproduced downward. Marcuse defended Hegel against the charge of proto-Nazism but could not show how a totalising revolution was possible. Adorno rejected totality altogether, and Habermas and Honneth retreated towards communicative and social-liberal solutions that Lu finds weak on objectivity. Lu treats Hegel as neither a plain statist nor a liberal.

Lu concludes that Hegel's real flaw was to treat Western capitalist state ideas as the only form of world history, a distortion that Lu says especially affects his reading of the East. Lu finds Marx's critique of political economy the way past Hegel, because it reveals that humans generate themselves through labour and addresses the problem of poverty that Hegel could not solve. Lu endorses Anderson's complaint that foreign Marxism neglects labour and the reproduction of human beings, and says that refuting Hegel in a Kantian way was doomed to fail. Read the original if you want a concise Chinese-language assessment of how Lukács, Gramsci, the Frankfurt School and Habermas relate to Hegel, framed by the state and national spirit.
quoteEn: When they tried to refute Hegel in a Kantian or near-Kantian way, their failure was already sealed.
quoteZh: 当他们用一种康德与近康德的方式来驳倒黑格尔时，已然注定了其失败的结局。

t: Practical lessons of Lenin's historical analysis for the Party in formulating correct policies and tactics
zh: 列宁的历史分析法对党制定正确的政策策略的现实启示
source: Observation and Thinking (Guancha yu sikao), 2023 no. 9
paras: Liang asks how Lenin's method of historical analysis helped the Bolsheviks set policy and tactics, and what it offers the Communist Party of China today. The article argues that Lenin treated dialectics as inseparable from historicity, and that this method let him adjust policy to each specific stage and set of conditions. In Liang's view, it remains a methodological reference for Party policy-making in the new era.

The article, published in 2023, has two parts. The first defines Lenin's historical analysis and traces its use in three areas: flexible tactics through the 1905 and 1917 revolutions, firm struggle to consolidate Soviet power, and the critique of mistaken currents. The cases include Narodism, the Economists, Machism and revisionism. The second part draws three lessons for the Chinese Party.

On Lenin, Liang's central claim is that he derived tasks from the actual course of events rather than from fixed principles. Examples include rejecting the Mensheviks' copying of Western bourgeois revolution in 1905, the April Theses and the decision for armed uprising in 1917, the Brest-Litovsk peace, and the wartime policy toward peasants. Liang also says Lenin's critiques rested on extensive historical research, as in The Development of Capitalism in Russia and Materialism and Empirio-criticism. The Chinese lessons follow from this. The Party should study history seriously, citing Marx and Engels, Mao Zedong and Xi Jinping. It should respect historical stages and conditions and draw on past failures. Liang names Chen Duxiu's compromise with the Kuomintang, Wang Ming's and Bo Gu's errors, and the Great Leap Forward. It should also adopt the "grand view of history" (da lishi guan), which Liang describes as long-term, broad and steady in direction.

Liang concludes that Lenin's method is a tested scientific worldview and methodology. Studying history, learning from experience and holding a long-term global perspective will help the Party formulate correct lines. In this reading it will also support Chinese modernization and the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation, and strengthen confidence in socialism's eventual victory. Read the original if you want a Chinese-language account of how Lenin's historical method is used to justify Party history study and the Xi-era "grand view of history".
quoteEn: Lenin's method of historical analysis combines materialist dialectics with specific historical stages, conditions and phenomena. It analyses social problems scientifically, applies policy and tactics flexibly, draws lessons from experience in good time, and firmly guides practice.
quoteZh: 列宁的历史分析法，是一种将唯物主义辩证法，同特定历史阶段，特定历史条件，特定历史现象相结合，科学分析社会问题，灵活运用政策策略，及时总结经验教训，坚定指导实践的研究方法

glossary.explanation: The Party's official formula, developed under Xi Jinping, for China's own path of modernization, presented as distinct from Western models.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.literal: great revival of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A central Party goal, associated with Xi Jinping's "Chinese Dream". It means restoring China to national strength and prosperity by mid-century.
A phrase promoted by Xi Jinping in the Party history study campaign. It calls for assessing events across long historical spans and in a global context.

t: Interpreting the young Marx's Paris text cluster
zh: 青年马克思的巴黎文本群解读
source: Chinese Social Sciences Today (中国社会科学报), 9 October 2023
paras: Zhang Yibing takes up the long dispute over the young Marx's Paris writings, namely the Economic and Philosophic Manuscripts of 1844 and the contemporaneous Paris Notebooks, which together form a "Paris text cluster". The article argues that the key to reading this cluster is what Zhang calls the "labour-alienation construct", which bears on the sources of Marx's thought and on his later economic thinking.

Zhang first explains why the cluster is contested: Marx's thinking was unsettled, with Hegel, Feuerbach, political economy and Enlightenment history competing in his mind. The texts were also found only after his death, and their interpretation is tied to ideological struggles over the legitimacy of historical materialism. The article then reconstructs the order of writing and traces the construct from On the Jewish Question through the Paris Notebooks to the 1844 Manuscripts and later economic manuscripts.

Zhang holds that the Paris Notebooks contain a complete research plan: Say, Smith and List, then the Mill excerpts, then the Hegel excerpts. Since Marx did not normally excerpt and write at once, Zhang concludes that the Notebooks preceded the 1844 Manuscripts. Zhang distinguishes three stages: a first construct in the Mill notes, based on "need" and alienated exchange; a second in Notebook I of the Manuscripts, drawing on Hegel and Smith; and a scientific third construct in the later economic manuscripts. Zhang reads the construct as Marx's first systematic "critical epistemology", Hegelian phenomenology applied to social materialism. It sees relations behind visible commodities and property, yet still ends in Feuerbach's human species-being, which Zhang calls implicitly idealist.

Zhang concludes that Marx abandoned this humanist epistemology from the Theses on Feuerbach onwards, and that a new critical epistemology emerged in the 1857–58 and 1861–63 manuscripts, completing two shifts in his epistemology. Read the original if you want a concise statement of Zhang Yibing's periodisation and reading of the young Marx's alienation theory.
quoteEn: Unless we explain well where it came from, it is hard to settle where it is going; this is precisely the significance of a text-based reading of this text today.
quoteZh: 不解释好“何所来”的问题，就很难解决“何所往”的问题，这正是我们当下对这一文本进行文本学解读的意义所在。

t: The concept of class in the "Introduction to A Contribution to the Critique of Hegel's Philosophy of Right"
zh: 《〈黑格尔法哲学批判〉导言》中的阶级概念
paras: Huang Du and Liu Ling start from the observation that the concept of class is receding from politics, sociology and even philosophy, where "stratum" has largely replaced it. They argue that treating class as an empirical ranking of wealth or social status is the greatest misreading of Marx. Their thesis is that Marx's concept of class can be grasped fully only by returning to his early texts, above all the 1843–44 Introduction to the Critique of Hegel's Philosophy of Right, where the proletariat first appears in a philosophical determination that underlies his later theory.

The article, originally published in the Chinese Social Sciences Today in October 2023, reconstructs why and how the concept enters this text. It does so through three "logics": textual, practical and theoretical. The authors also address the common scholarly view that the Introduction is immature because Marx had not yet mastered political economy or formed historical materialism.

On the textual side, a word-frequency count in the Marx–Engels Collected Works (Chinese second edition, vol. 1) shows "class" appearing 41 times in the Introduction, 13 of them as "proletariat", against one occurrence in the Critique itself. The authors read this as a turning point. In the practical account, Marx's work on the Rheinische Zeitung, especially the debates on wood theft, confronted him with the "perplexing questions" of material interests and left Hegel's rational state unconfirmed. In the theoretical account, Marx moves from seeking a political solution to the split between state and civil society towards the interior of civil society. There he turns that split into the antagonism between proletariat and bourgeoisie, using a transformed Hegelian dialectic.

The authors conclude that class concerns human "species being" and real freedom, not merely poverty or ownership of the means of production. They offer three initial propositions. The proletariat is a product of history and of industrial, modern capitalist society. It marks the loss of human universality and is not simply observable workers or paupers. It is a special class with self-negating and transcending character, since it must abolish the bourgeoisie and thereby itself. Without this framework, they warn, the later notion of the working class risks empiricism and Lukácsian reified consciousness. Read the original if you want a compact, text-based argument for a philosophical rather than sociological reading of Marx's class concept.
quoteEn: Class points to human "species being"; the emergence of the proletariat is a sign that humans have lost their universality, so the proletariat is by no means merely the workers and paupers seen in empirical observation.
quoteZh: 阶级指向人的“类存在”，无产阶级的出现就是人丧失普遍性的标志，因而无产阶级绝非仅仅是经验直观到的工人、贫民
keywords: Critique of Hegel's Philosophy of Right

t: The three-dimensional historical foundations of historical materialism
zh: 历史唯物主义的三维历史底蕴
source: Chinese Social Sciences Today (Zhongguo shehui kexue bao), 21 September 2023
paras: This short theoretical piece asks what gives historical materialism its character as a totalizing philosophy of history. Jin argues that it inherits, criticises and goes beyond the "general philosophy of history" represented by Hegel. Its break, in Jin's account, is to "return the content of history to history": it grounds history in the productive practice of "real individuals" and so offers a scientific answer about history in general. The article claims that this is built on three dimensions.

Jin takes the dimensions in turn: natural history and human history, past and future, and national history and world history. Each is tied to texts by Marx and Engels, mainly The German Ideology, Engels's account of natural evolution, and their late reflections on Russia. The piece is a compact exposition rather than a survey of secondary literature, with a brief nod to E. H. Carr on the link between past and future.

On the first dimension, Jin argues that natural history and human history are structurally parallel on the basis of practice. Externally, both show diverse forms. Internally, both are governed by laws rooted in the metabolism between humans and nature. In capitalism, Jin says, the logic of capital makes human history move blindly, like natural history, which bourgeois ideology then defends. Overcoming this alienation requires a return to active practice. On the second, historical materialism is described as a philosophy oriented to the future. It links "interpretation–critique–prediction" and uses a "practical reflection" that works backwards from developed forms. It ties historical logic to the real movement of communism. On the third, Jin says Marx and Engels went beyond a Eurocentric view of history. They treated world history as a system of mutually dependent nations. Their late attention to Russia's possible path past the "Caudine Forks" of capitalism, Jin argues, shows that varied national paths do not negate general laws.

Jin concludes that these three dimensions give historical materialism's totality a unified, diverse and open character. Jin presents this "big view of history" as an important intellectual resource for the Communist Party of China's governance. In Jin's reading it fits the theme of a century of Party history, supports Chinese modernization and the building of a new form of human civilisation, and opens a new stage in adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times. Read the original if you want a brief statement of how Chinese theorists currently frame the historical-materialist "totality" of nature, time and world history, and how they link it to Party doctrine.
quoteEn: In terms of historical content, historical materialism achieves an internal isomorphism of \"natural history–human history\"; in historical time, a two-way connection of \"past–present–future\"; and in historical space, a two-way determination of \"nation–world\".
quoteZh: 历史唯物主义在历史内容上实现“自然史—人类史”的内在同构，在历史时间上实现“过去—现在—未来”的双向贯通，在历史空间上实现“民族—世界”的双向规定

glossary.explanation: The official name for the Communist Party of China's model of national development, prominent in Party discourse since the 20th Party Congress (2022).

glossary.zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化
glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
glossary.explanation: The official formula for the Party's ongoing effort to combine Marxist theory with Chinese conditions and contemporary developments.
A phrase in recent Party discourse for placing events within long historical sweeps and the whole course of world history. Here the author links it to historical materialism.

t: Advancing Chinese modernization requires strengthening strategic thinking
zh: 推进中国式现代化必须强化战略思维
paras: This commentary, published in Red Flag Manuscript in 2023, argues that Chinese modernization can only be advanced by cadres who are good at strategic thinking and at viewing problems from a strategic standpoint. Cheng Zhangchun takes as the framework a speech by Xi Jinping at the study seminar on Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era and the spirit of the 20th Party Congress (2022). In Cheng's account, the speech identifies four qualities of strategy that cadres must strengthen.

The article is organised in four sections that follow these qualities: foresight, a global (whole-picture) perspective, stability, and the combination of strategic principle with tactical flexibility. Each section explains what the quality means and what Party members and cadres are expected to do in practice. The text relies heavily on quotations from Xi Jinping and on the documents of the 20th Party Congress rather than on external cases.

On foresight, Cheng contends that strategy concerns the long term and the general trend, so that cadres must move from passively "encountering" risks to actively "foreseeing" them, guided by scientific theory and by knowledge of historical laws. On the global perspective, the author holds that planning must start from the "two overall situations" (the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation and profound changes unseen in a century), grasp the principal contradiction, and use systems thinking, including the nine essential requirements of Chinese modernization and the five-sphere integrated plan. On stability, Cheng calls for historical patience, strategic resolve and a broad mind among leading cadres, who should be willing to build on predecessors' work and avoid frequent policy reversals.

The final section argues that strategy and tactics form a dialectical unity: firm principles must be kept in line with Party theory and the Party line, yet need not become rigid, and strategy should be adjusted as conditions change. Cheng notes that the content of the current period of strategic opportunity has changed profoundly and calls for new strategic responses, together with flexible, locally adapted policies, bottom-line thinking and the capacity for struggle. Read the original if you want a compact example of how Party-school-style writing translates Xi Jinping's formulation of strategic thinking into concrete expectations for cadres.
quoteEn: Strategy means making judgements and decisions from the standpoint of the overall situation, the long term and the general trend; tactics serve strategy under its guidance, and a correct strategy needs correct tactics to carry it out.
quoteZh: 战略是从全局、长远、大势上作出判断和决策，策略是在战略指导下为战略服务的，正确的战略需要正确的策略来落实。

glossary.explanation: The official term for China's own path to modernization, elaborated by the Party especially since the 20th Party Congress in 2022. It is presented as distinct from Western models.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018.

Official formulation referring to the strategic whole of the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation and the world's profound changes unseen in a century. The Party says all planning should be viewed in light of both.
The Party's overall plan for advancing economic, political, cultural, social and ecological development together, adopted at the 18th Party Congress (2012).

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The Party's central national goal, associated with the Chinese Dream, of restoring China to national strength and prosperity by mid-century.

t: New displays of the appeal of Chinese civilisation in the new era and a new realm for research on the "Two Integrations"
zh: 新时代中华文明魅力的新展示与“两个结合”研究的新境界
source: Mao Zedong Deng Xiaoping Theory Studies, 2023 no. 7
paras: Writing after the 20th Party Congress (2022), Liu Shulin asks what Chinese civilisation shows in the new era and what that implies for research on the Two Integrations: combining the basic principles of Marxism with China's concrete realities and with China's fine traditional culture. Liu argues that Chinese civilisation has regained a leading position, and that Marxist scholars now have a new mission to realise the Two Integrations through adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times.

The article has three parts. The first describes three new aspects of Chinese civilisation's appeal: an expanded historical timeline supported by archaeology, its continuity, and an endogenous dynamic arising from interaction between centre and periphery. The second examines how the civilisation passed through a low point in modern times and revived. The third sets out three requirements of the Two Integrations in the new era. Liu draws on Xi Jinping's speeches, Chinese historians such as Bai Shouyi and Lei Haizong, and Arnold Toynbee.

Liu's central argument concerns historical regularity. Early advance in the feudal stage, Liu holds, gave China a durable institutional shell, which later made the transition to new social formations harder. Citing Lei Haizong, Liu says countries that enter a new social formation first are usually relatively backward in the previous one, and that China's modern humiliation is explained by two lacks: guiding ideas and a unifying organisation. Marxism-Leninism and the Communist Party, in Liu's account, supplied both and 'activated' the civilisation's vitality, so that China is again at the starting point of leading development. Liu rejects cultural revivalism and historical nihilism, and endorses 'creative transformation and innovative development' of tradition under Marxist guidance.

Liu concludes that Marxist scholars must carry forward the tradition of adapting Marxism, keep Marxism firmly in the guiding ideological position, and use tradition to educate people, especially the young. Liu frames this as a contest of soft power with hegemonic forces and calls for building academic, disciplinary and discourse systems on Chinese civilisation. Read the original if you want a Party-theory account of how the Two Integrations are tied to claims about civilisational continuity and the social-formation sequence.
quoteEn: This is the secret of how the Chinese nation passed through the humiliation and obscurity of modern times, emerged from the trough and moved towards rejuvenation.
quoteZh: 这就是中华民族穿越近代受辱蒙尘，走出低谷、走向崛起的秘密所在。

glossary.explanation: Formula stressing the combination of Marxism's basic principles with China's concrete realities and with China's fine traditional culture. The second 'integration' was added to the older formula in Xi Jinping's 2021 speeches.

glossary.zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化
glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
glossary.explanation: Official term for the continuing project of fitting Marxist theory to Chinese conditions and to contemporary circumstances.

glossary.zh: 创造性转化、创新性发展
glossary.explanation: Official principle for treating traditional culture: reworking its elements to fit present conditions rather than simply restoring them.
Term used in Party discourse for views said to negate the Party's revolutionary history and socialism by denigrating the past.

t: The inner connection and practical orientation of firm historical confidence and steadfast ideals and convictions
zh: 坚定历史自信与坚守理想信念的 内在关联与实践指向
paras: Mei Ping and Chen Jiao take up a pairing first put forward by Xi Jinping at the Second Plenary Session of the Sixth Plenum of the 19th Central Committee (2021): that Party members should "stand firm in historical confidence" and "consciously hold to ideals and convictions". The authors argue that the two are highly coupled. Both aim to unify thought and action around the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation, though they differ in content: historical confidence rests on a scientific grasp of historical laws and achievements, while ideals and convictions mean belief in Marxism, communism and the common ideal of socialism with Chinese characteristics.

The article has three parts. The first treats the inner connection between the two; the second, their active role in the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation; the third, four practical orientations for the "new journey of examination". It draws mainly on Xi Jinping's speeches, the 2021 Party resolution on history and the Marxist classics, and relates the argument to the Party's centenary history.

On the connection, the authors contend that historical confidence affirms and supports ideals and convictions. It affirms them because it is confidence in the "two inevitables" and in a century of achievements, and it supports them because Party history supplies facts, heroes and collective memory. In return, steadfast conviction gives historical confidence its rational self-awareness, since it is grounded in Marxist truth, and its deepest source of strength, the aim of seeking happiness for the Chinese people and "great harmony" for the world. On their active role, historical confidence strengthens historical consciousness and initiative, while conviction supplies socialist direction and gathers the people's strength through the common ideal.

The practical orientations are strengthening the Party's self-confidence and upholding its overall leadership, including the Two Establishes and the Two Upholds; consolidating the spiritual foundation through the Party's spiritual genealogy to advance Chinese modernization; clearing ideological fog by opposing historical nihilism, with the collapse of the Soviet Union cited as a warning; and honing the capacity for struggle against risks and challenges. The authors conclude that, amid the interplay of the "two overall situations", the whole Party and people must keep both qualities to advance national rejuvenation. Read the original if you want a detailed example of how Party theorists link historical confidence, ideological conviction and the Party's political tasks.
quoteEn: Firm historical confidence, in the end, is a high affirmation of the gradual confirmation and continuous realisation of the "two inevitables" in the course of pursuing ideals and convictions.
quoteZh: 坚定历史自信说到底就是对追求理想信念过程中“两个必然”的逐渐确证和不断实现的高度肯定。

glossary.explanation: A concept stressed in Party documents from 2021, meaning confidence in the laws and trend of history and in the Party's historical achievements, experience and fighting spirit.
Marxist propositions that capitalism inevitably perishes and socialism inevitably triumphs, treated here as the core law of historical development.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.literal: great revival of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The official overarching national goal of the Party, linked to the Chinese Dream and to the centenary targets.

glossary.literal: new road of sitting an exam
glossary.explanation: A metaphor from Mao Zedong in 1949, revived by Xi Jinping, presenting governing as an ongoing exam taken before the people.
The official series of "great spirits" formed in Party history, with the great founding spirit of the Party as its source.
In Party usage, a label for views that negate the Party's history or the socialist path, treated as an ideological threat.
A formula adopted in 2021 affirming Xi Jinping's core position in the Party and the guiding role of his thought.
The requirement to uphold Xi Jinping's core position and the authority of the Party Central Committee.

t: Hegelian elements in foreign Marxism
zh: 国外马克思主义中的黑格尔思想元素
paras: Lu Shaochen asks how Marxism outside China has dealt with Hegel, and why its theoretical results have been uneven. The article, a short commentary first published in China Social Sciences Today in September 2023, reads the relationship through Hegel's notions of the state idea and the national spirit. Lu argues that these thinkers criticised society in a largely 'near-Hegelian' manner but drew back to a 'near-Kantian' position when it came to practice and constructive proposals. Lu holds that this mismatch deserves study, and proposes a new Marxist approach that stays Hegelian in method and critique but replaces Hegel's ontology with 'the positive existence and positive essence of the human being'.

The article moves through foreign Marxism roughly in sequence. It begins with the inheritance of the totality method in Georg Lukács and Antonio Gramsci. It then turns to Herbert Marcuse's defence of Hegel and to Theodor Adorno's rejection of totality, followed by Jürgen Habermas and Axel Honneth, who Lu says retreat towards social liberal democracy. A final section sets out how one might return to Hegel and then go beyond him, drawing on Marx and on critics of Hegel such as Kurt Leidecker and Perry Anderson.

Lu's central claim is that Hegel's strength lay in explaining the substantial spirit of Western modernity through the state idea and national spirit, and that any critique of that modernity must therefore pass through him. In Lu's reading, Lukács's proletarian subject floats free of state idea and national spirit, Gramsci enriches Hegel on culture and hegemony but underrates the contest for state power, and Marcuse speaks only abstractly of historical reason. Adorno's negative dialectics and Habermas's communicative paradigm, Lu argues, give up totality and fall back on contractarian contingency. Lu also contends that Hegel is neither a simple statist nor a liberal, since he insisted that totality and individuality must be united. His real flaw, on this account, is treating Western capitalist forms as the only pattern of world history.

Lu concludes that Marx's critique of political economy supplies the way forward. Marx located the secret of human history in people producing themselves through labour, and so could address the poverty and 'rabble' problem Hegel could not solve. Lu endorses Anderson's complaint that foreign Marxism neglects labour and the reproduction of human beings, and judges that refuting Hegel in a Kantian manner was bound to fail. Lu also links this to the values of Eastern civilisation, such as attention to humaneness and labour. Read the original if you want a compact, Chinese-authored assessment of how Lukács, Gramsci, Marcuse, Adorno, Habermas and Honneth relate to Hegel, and of the case for a Marx-based return to him.
quoteEn: Hegel was not a philosopher who stressed only totality, substantiality and the state and national spirit; this is precisely where he differs fundamentally from Plato.
quoteZh: 黑格尔并不是只强调总体性、实体性和国家与民族精神的哲学家，这正是他与柏拉图的根本区别之所在。

glossary.explanation: A Chinese academic field covering Marxist currents outside China, broader than Western Marxism in the strict sense. It includes the Frankfurt School, Gramsci and others.

glossary.literal: the idea of the state and the spirit of the nation
glossary.explanation: The author's rendering of Hegelian categories of the state and the substantial spirit of a people. The author treats them as the core of Hegel's 'totality' category.

A Hegelian-Marxist category, stressed by Lukács, in which the whole determines how its parts are understood. The article treats it as the method that foreign Marxism inherited and then partly rejected.

t: The Mill Notes in the context of political economy and the evolving logic of alienation
zh: 政治经济学语境中的《穆勒笔记》及其异化逻辑演进
source: China Social Sciences Today (Zhongguo shehui kexue bao), 9 October 2023
paras: Zhang Fugong examines the Mill Notes, the young Marx's first extended encounter with political economy, and asks how the logic of alienation develops within them. Drawing on MEGA2, the article argues that the Mill Notes should be read against the economic literature Marx was excerpting, and that this reading helps settle current scholarly disputes. Originally a newspaper article from 2023, it is a short piece.

The article first reviews the long debate over the Mill Notes' date and status relative to the Economic and Philosophic Manuscripts of 1844. It identifies three positions: written before the Manuscripts, between Notebook I and Notebooks II–III, or after Notebook III. It then follows the Paris Notes on Say, Skarbek, Smith and Ricardo to trace how Marx moves from alienated exchange to alienated labour.

Zhang rejects the claim that the Mill Notes' alienation of communication (交往异化) is more advanced than the alienation of labour in Notebook I. In Zhang's reading, the social relations in the Mill Notes are mainly exchange relations, whose freedom and equality are an ideological appearance concealing the exploitation behind private property. From Say, Skarbek and Smith, Marx obtains the picture of a commercial society and treats money as the alienated mediation of human activity. He then turns to wage labour for subsistence through the line division of labour, labour machine and exploitation-based private property, which he takes from Ricardo.

Zhang concludes that Marx's early theory of alienated labour grows out of this political-economy context. Its four forms are already sketched, and attention to capital–labour exploitation begins to break the exchange framework. The theory still lacks sublation of alienation, which Zhang says Marx later supplies by drawing on Hegel's negative dialectic. Read the original if you study the young Marx's development or the dating debate over the Paris writings and want a source-based argument against treating alienation of communication as the higher stage.
quoteEn: This shows that tracing the sources of Marx's theory cannot rely only on direct textual quotations, but must also take account of the clues implicit in Marx's excerpt notebooks.
quoteZh: 这表明，对马克思的理论渊源的追溯不能只依据直接的文本引述，还需要结合马克思的摘录笔记隐含的线索。

glossary.explanation: Marx's 1844 excerpts from and comments on James Mill's work, part of the Paris Notes. They contain his discussion of money and alienated exchange.
The alienation of human exchange and social interaction, which Marx discusses in the Mill Notes through money and exchange. It contrasts with the alienation of labour.
Labour performed only to earn a livelihood under private property. Some scholars propose translating it as 'profit-making labour', which the author rejects.
Marx's excerpt notebooks on political economy from 1844, covering authors such as Say, Smith and Ricardo.

t: The internal structure of the young Marx's theory of alienation
zh: 青年马克思异化理论的内在结构
paras: Kong Weiyu asks how the many theoretical sources of the young Marx's theory of alienation (political economy, Hegelian philosophy, Feuerbach's humanism) were arranged in his thinking. The author treats this as a foundational question to settle before any original interpretation. The thesis is that two logics coexisted in Marx's mind in a structured field of forces, which polyphony theory and field theory together can describe. The piece appeared in the Chinese Social Sciences Today in October 2023.

The article first reviews the "two logics" reading of the Economic and Philosophic Manuscripts of 1844, associated with Sun Bogao, Zhang Yibing and Tang Zhengdong. It then borrows the concept of polyphony from musicology and from Mikhail Bakhtin's account of Dostoevsky's novels, and adds Pierre Bourdieu's theory of the field.

Kong reads the two logics as polyphonic: an objective logic starting from economic reality and an alienation logic starting from humanism, each independent yet jointly forming a whole. Because polyphony leaves the whole unfinished, Kong suggests, it helps explain why later scholars interpret the young Marx so openly. Field theory is then used to show how the logics relate. The objective logic is explicit, since the Manuscripts use terms close to those of the political economists, and even production, practice and communism appear. The humanist alienation logic stays implicit but dominates, so that the return point for overcoming alienation remains human species-essence. Kong argues that this changed only after Marx's Brussels and Manchester notebooks and his encounter with large-scale machine industry.

Kong adds that each logic has mixed sources. The objective one draws on Smith and Ricardo and also on the humanist economist Schulz-type thinkers such as Skarbek, while the alienation logic draws on Feuerbach and on Hegel's Phenomenology of Spirit. Kong concludes that opening up this structural field is difficult but rewarding, and requires sustained work on the texts. Read the original if you want a short methodological sketch of how the young Marx's thought can be modelled with polyphony and field theory.
quoteEn: In terms of how they exist, the young Marx's intellectual space contains an explicit logic and an implicit logic.
quoteZh: 从存在方式来看，青年马克思的思想空间中存在着显性逻辑和隐性逻辑。

t: Rethinking the totality of Marx's concept of "history"
zh: 重新理解马克思“历史”概念的总体性特征
paras: Wu Meng asks how the totality of Marx's concept of "history" should be understood, and argues that the influential reading by Georg Lukács needs to be revised. The article, first published in the Chinese Social Sciences Today in September 2023, holds that this concept shapes both the horizon of historical materialism and our theoretical attitude towards contemporary life. Wu's thesis is that the totality of Marx's "history" is a historical feature tied to the capitalist mode of production. It is not a whole that contains and determines its parts.

The piece has three parts. The first sets out Lukács's account in History and Class Consciousness. The second identifies three internal inconsistencies in it. The third presents Wu's own reading of Marx's dialectic and of totality in the critique of political economy.

In Wu's account, Lukács treats method as the core of Marxist orthodoxy. He reads Marx through a Hegelian dialectic of part and whole and of subject and object. Reification, on this reading, is a partial appearance, and the proletariat can grasp the social totality behind it. Wu credits the insight that history is more than a set of empirical facts but argues that the logic fails on three counts. Part–whole dialectics work in Hegel's logic because the Absolute Idea unites individuality and totality, whereas capitalist social structure is not an individual phenomenon alongside others. Lukács's mediating concepts, the "structural principle of construction" and the "real tendency of development", are vague and hard to operationalise. Reading Marx's move from the abstract to the concrete as a move from part to whole also turns Marx's historically specific concept into an abstract one applicable to any era. Wu locates the root of these problems in equating Marx's dialectic with Hegel's, although Marx called his method the direct opposite of Hegel's.

Wu's positive proposal is that totality is the capitalist mode of production itself. It is not a ready-made entity but a structural operation that gives phenomena their "mode of givenness". It is a functional whole that accompanies objects yet cannot be objectified, a "collusion" of human and material factors. Totality is therefore a historical feature belonging only to capitalism, where universal relations between persons and between things arise. Marx, Wu argues, begins from this universality, which classical political economists took to be eternal, and asks about its historical preconditions. Read the original if you are interested in Western Marxism's debates over totality and in a Chinese critique of Lukács's use of Hegel in reading Marx.
quoteEn: Rather, this totality dimension of history presents itself precisely as the "mode of givenness" of phenomena.
quoteZh: 毋宁说，历史的这种总体性维度正是作为诸现象的“给出方式”而展现自身的

t: Resolving the dilemmas of global governance through the Silk Road spirit
st: Dilemmas and pathways
zh: 论以丝路精神破解全球治理的困境与路径
paras: Yin Xuepeng and Xu Xiujun ask how global governance can be improved at a time of what they call accelerating changes unseen in a century. Their answer is that the Silk Road spirit, defined as peace and cooperation, openness and inclusiveness, mutual learning among civilisations, and mutual benefit and win-win outcomes, can offer ideological guidance for building a more just and reasonable global governance system.

The article first traces how Xi Jinping formulated the Silk Road spirit between 2013 and 2017 and sets out its four meanings: a driving force of the ancient Silk Road, a system of ideas with a practical basis, the guiding principle for high-quality development of the Belt and Road Initiative, and the spiritual core of a community with a shared future for mankind. It then analyses four conflicts of governance ideas, assesses the spirit's value for resolving each, and ends with four practical paths.

The authors describe global governance as split between confrontation and cooperation, protectionism and openness, decoupling and connectivity, and zero-sum thinking and win-win outcomes. They attribute the first term of each pair mainly to the United States and its allies, citing tariffs, sanctions, withdrawal from the TPP and 'conscious decoupling', and the second to China and other emerging economies. Each principle of the Silk Road spirit is then matched to one problem. Peace and cooperation counter Cold War thinking, openness counters protectionism, mutual learning counters the 'clash of civilizations', and mutual benefit counters zero-sum games.

The four paths are to promote the common values of all humankind, to practise the global governance outlook of extensive consultation, joint contribution and shared benefits, to practise 'true multilateralism', and to innovate governance ideas through initiatives such as the Global Development Initiative and the Global Security Initiative. Yin and Xu conclude that the Silk Road spirit, which they say is the only foreign-affairs spirit included in the spiritual genealogy of Chinese Communists, summarises China's diplomatic thinking in the new era and helps move the international order towards greater justice and reason. Read the original if you want a detailed, officially aligned account of how Chinese scholars link the Belt and Road Initiative to global governance and to the idea of a community with a shared future for mankind.
quoteEn: Mutual benefit and win-win outcomes are the basic principle for sustaining long-term cooperation among countries: without mutual benefit, cooperation cannot continue; without win-win outcomes, cooperation lacks confidence.
quoteZh: 互利共赢是世界各国之间维持长远合作的基本原则，离开了互利，合作难以为继；离开了共赢，合作没有底气。

glossary.explanation: A formula used in official discourse since Xi Jinping's speeches of 2013–2017. It summarises the ancient Silk Road's legacy as peace and cooperation, openness and inclusiveness, mutual learning and mutual benefit, and it is linked to the Belt and Road Initiative.
An infrastructure and economic cooperation initiative launched by Xi Jinping in 2013, comprising the Silk Road Economic Belt and the 21st-Century Maritime Silk Road.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: A foreign-policy concept promoted by Xi Jinping since 2012–13. It calls for countries to take account of one another's legitimate concerns and to pursue common development.
A formula proposed by Xi Jinping in 2015 listing peace, development, equity, justice, democracy and freedom. Official sources present it as an alternative to Western 'universal values'.

glossary.zh: 共商共建共享的全球治理观
glossary.pinyin: gòngshāng gòngjiàn gòngxiǎng de quánqiú zhìlǐ guān
glossary.en: global governance outlook of extensive consultation, joint contribution and shared benefits
glossary.literal: global governance view of joint consultation, joint construction and joint sharing
glossary.explanation: An official Chinese principle of global governance. It holds that all countries should take part equally in making and benefiting from international rules.
An official economic and policy goal stressing quality, efficiency and sustainability over speed of growth. It is applied here to Belt and Road cooperation.

keywords: community with a shared future for mankind

t: The growing overseas influence of Mao Zedong Thought and its lessons
zh: 毛泽东思想海外影响力的提升与启示
source: China Leadership Science (Zhongguo lingdao kexue), 2023 no. 5
paras: Ding Yi asks how Mao Zedong Thought, which the article presents as the theoretical result of the first historic leap in adapting Marxism to the Chinese context, built up its influence abroad, and what that history teaches about promoting Chinese theory and culture internationally today. The author argues that the process passed through three stages and that its experience offers practical guidance for taking Chinese theory "global" in the new era.

The first half is a historical periodisation. The early stage (to 1949) covers translations and publications through the Comintern, the Paris-based Salvation Times and a Yan'an English edition of On Coalition Government. It also covers foreign journalists, above all Edgar Snow and his Red Star Over China. The second stage (1949–1978) covers state-organised multilingual publishing of the Selected Works, with the article citing 18 languages and 48 editions in the 1960s and 70s. It also covers dissemination in Asia, Africa and Latin America. The third stage (1978 to the present) is described as a calmer, scholarly phase with research centres in South Korea, Australia, the United States and Japan.

The second half draws four lessons from this record, organised by the elements of communication. On communicators, Ding argues that state leadership must be complemented by media, enterprises, think tanks, universities and non-governmental bodies, because politicised or state-led channels in some Soviet-bloc countries limited the effect. On channels, the author calls for combining traditional publishing with internet-based and other new media. On content, Ding stresses adapting to local cultures and the role of translation, citing the audience-aware Japanese translations of the Selected Works. On methods, the author points to cultural diplomacy and soft power.

Ding concludes that cultural diplomacy, supported by the country's "hard power", helps shape a positive national image and a favourable international opinion climate. The author calls for Chinese theory to be communicated through a global system based on a community with a shared future for mankind, using new concepts that connect Chinese and foreign audiences, and for translation of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era to be standardised. Read the original if you want a Chinese official-academic account of how Mao Zedong Thought's overseas reception is used to frame current international communication strategy.
quoteEn: Overseas dissemination of Mao Zedong Thought gradually shifted from the fervent peak of around the 1960s to a calm and rational phase, with a wave of research enthusiasm for Mao Zedong Thought appearing in countries abroad.
quoteZh: 毛泽东思想海外传播逐步由20世纪60年代左右的狂热高潮转变为平静理性，海外国家纷纷出现毛泽东思想研究热的现象。

glossary.zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化
glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context
glossary.explanation: The official formula for the Party's project of fitting Marxism to China's conditions and to the needs of each era. Mao Zedong Thought is presented as its first major theoretical result.

glossary.zh: community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: A foreign-policy concept promoted by Xi Jinping since the early 2010s, calling for shared development and cooperation among states.
Borrowed from Joseph Nye, the term is used in Chinese official discourse for the influence of culture, values and image, in contrast to "hard power" of economic and military strength.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018.

t: Lenin's New Economic Policy thought from the perspective of reform and its contemporary value
zh: 改革视角下的列宁新经济政策思想及其当代价值
source: Observation and Reflection (Guancha yu sikao), 2023 no. 9
paras: Zhang Wei asks what Lenin's New Economic Policy (NEP) can teach about reform in a socialist state. The article argues that the shift from War Communism to the NEP was a major reform in the history of socialism. In Zhang's reading, Lenin was both an advocate and a practitioner of that reform, and his thinking on it holds lessons for China's drive to comprehensively deepen reform.

The article has three parts. The first traces how NEP thought took shape, from early ideas on state capitalism in 1918, through the crisis of War Communism and the peasant revolts, to the Tenth Party Congress (1921), Lenin's essay "On the Tax in Kind" and the later acceptance of markets and money. The second part organises Lenin's thinking under five headings: the motives, methods, risk prevention, implementation and safeguards of reform. The third part draws five lessons for present-day China.

In Zhang's account, Lenin held that War Communism had become detached from Russia's conditions, with a small-peasant economy and little large-scale industry. It damaged the peasants' incentive to produce and worsened the lives of workers and peasants. Lenin therefore turned to using private capitalism and state capitalism, including the tax in kind and concessions to foreign capital, to promote socialism. He also treated the NEP as a retreat that needed a limit: capital had to stay under Soviet power's "supervision and calculation", with the commanding heights in state hands. Zhang adds that Lenin required Communists to learn management, even from bourgeois specialists, and to keep the Party united.

Drawing on Xi Jinping's statements, Zhang proposes five lessons for comprehensively deepening reform: stay problem-oriented, lead with theoretical innovation, hold to bottom-line thinking, build cadres' capabilities, and strengthen Party leadership. The author argues that the contrast between reform in China and in the Soviet Union and Eastern Europe turned largely on whether Party leadership was kept. Zhang concludes that the NEP and today's reform face similar questions, such as how to treat capital and how to build socialism in a backward country, and urges continued study of Lenin's NEP thought. Read the original if you want to see how a Chinese Party-theory journal links Lenin's NEP to the current reform agenda.
quoteEn: Lenin likened the New Economic Policy to a retreat within an offensive, and the key to guarding against its risks lay in setting a \"limit\" to the retreat.
quoteZh: 列宁将新经济政策比喻为进攻过程中的退却，防范新经济政策风险的关键在于设定退却的“度”。

glossary.explanation: The emergency economic system of Soviet Russia during the Civil War (1918–1921), involving compulsory grain requisitioning, nationalised industry and restricted trade.
The policy Lenin introduced in 1921 to replace War Communism. It allowed a tax in kind, limited free trade and concessions to foreign capital under state control.
In Lenin's usage, capitalism operating under the supervision of the proletarian state. He saw it as a step forward and a bridge towards socialism in a backward country.
A slogan launched at the Third Plenum of the 18th Central Committee (2013). It denotes a broad programme of reform across the economy, politics, society and Party-building.
A mode of reasoning promoted by Xi Jinping. It asks policymakers to identify limits that must not be crossed and to prepare for the worst-case risks.

t: Mechanisms by which high-quality Party building in universities can lead high-quality development of ideological and political work among university students
zh: 高质量党建引领大学生思想政治工作高质量发展的机制研究
source: School Party Building and Ideological Education (学校党建与思想教育)
paras: Zhang Yao, a university Party official, asks how Party building in Chinese universities can guide and raise the quality of ideological and political work among students. The article argues that the two are unified in the practice of running socialist universities rooted in Chinese soil, and that both serve the mission of educating people for the Party and talent for the country. Zhang's answer is a set of four mechanisms: organisational management, coordination and linkage, evaluation and assessment, and support and guarantees.

The article has three parts. The first sets out why high-quality Party building leading high-quality ideological and political work matters. The second explains the internal logic linking the two. The third proposes the four mechanisms and illustrates them with examples from Huazhong University of Science and Technology and other unnamed universities. Zhang quotes Xi Jinping repeatedly, on ideological and political work as the lifeline of all work, on the Party's overall leadership of education, and on moral education as the fundamental task.

On significance, Zhang points to three pressures: the traits of present-day students, who are described as capable and public-spirited but still forming their values and so open to competing currents of thought and online influence; new demands on student Party work; and external challenges. In this last point the author says Western countries, led by the United States, are containing China and attempting ideological infiltration, so universities must hold their ideological ground. On internal logic, Zhang says Party building guides ideological work politically, organisationally and culturally. Ideological work in turn gives Party building its goals, working models and teaching staff, and both share the aim of cultivating a new generation for the era.

The four mechanisms are concrete. Party committees would join decision-making and oversight, and the student affairs department would take the lead. Platforms and teams would be integrated through one-stop student communities, unified Party-Youth League-class organisation and "walking ideological and political classes". Student Party members would be assessed over their whole membership cycle, with results used for rewards and discipline. Support would come from political-leadership requirements, standardised student Party branches and a strengthened staff of counsellors and class advisers. Read the original if you want a practitioner's account of how a university leader frames Party building and student ideological work, with institutional examples from Huazhong University of Science and Technology.
quoteEn: University Party building is an important guide for ideological and political work among students, and that work is an important part of university Party building.
quoteZh: 高校党建是大学生思想政治工作的重要指针，大学生思想政治工作是高校党建的重要内容

glossary.explanation: The Party's work of shaping people's political views and values through education and organisation. In universities it covers political courses, counsellors and student Party activities.
Official term for the fundamental task of education in the Xi Jinping era: building moral character while training talent.
The work of strengthening the Party's organisations, membership and ideological discipline, here applied to universities and student Party branches.
Practice-based teaching in which students learn about national conditions through fieldwork and social practice outside the classroom.

keywords: Huazhong University of Science and Technology

t: Building the new development pattern and seizing the initiative in future development
zh: 构建新发展格局把握未来发展主动权
paras: Writing in the Party-state newspaper Economic Daily in October 2023, Wang Tinghui asks why the Party Central Committee under Xi Jinping decided to build a new development pattern and how it should be built. The pattern is defined as one with the domestic circulation as the mainstay and the domestic and international circulations reinforcing each other. Wang argues that it is a strategic response to changes in China's stage of development, environment and conditions. In this reading it will secure China's economic foundations and its "initiative" in future development.

The commentary has two parts. The first sets out three aspects of the pattern's strategic significance. The second identifies four priority areas for systematic deployment. Throughout, Wang draws on Xi Jinping's statements and on the official framing of the principal contradiction in society and of the "two overall situations".

On significance, Wang argues that the pattern fits the new stage of development and the changed principal contradiction. It also helps coordinate the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation with what the article calls the world's "great changes unseen in a century", at a time of rising unilateralism, protectionism and weakened traditional international circulation. Finally, it draws on China's changing comparative advantages: rising labour costs and resource constraints on one side, a very large market, a middle-income group of over 400 million and a complete industrial system on the other. On priorities, Wang calls for stronger endogenous momentum in the domestic circulation through expanded domestic demand and deeper reform. Wang also urges a modern industrial system built on high-level scientific and technological self-reliance and a real-economy focus. Further proposals are coordinated urban–rural and regional development with a unified national market, and a higher-quality international circulation through high-standard opening up.

Wang concludes that making the domestic circulation the mainstay does not mean closing the door. Instead, domestic demand potential should be used to link domestic and international markets more closely and to attract global resources. This, Wang says, will strengthen China's capacity to allocate resources globally and keep the strategic initiative. Read the original if you want a concise, officially aligned account of how Chinese policy writers justify and operationalise the dual circulation strategy.
quoteEn: Making the domestic circulation the mainstay is by no means closed-door operation, but uses the potential of domestic demand to connect domestic and international markets better.
quoteZh: 以国内大循环为主体，绝不是关起门来封闭运行，而是通过发挥内需潜力，使国内市场和国际市场更好联通。

glossary.explanation: A strategy put forward by the Party leadership in 2020. It makes the domestic circulation the mainstay, with domestic and international circulations reinforcing each other, and is often called "dual circulation".

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A central goal of Party discourse since the 18th Party Congress (2012). It refers to restoring China's national strength and international standing by mid-century.

glossary.zh: 世界百年未有之大变局
glossary.pinyin: shìjiè bǎinián wèi yǒu zhī dà biànjú
glossary.en: great changes unseen in a century
glossary.explanation: A phrase used by Xi Jinping to describe shifts in the global balance of power, technology and the international order. Official texts pair it with the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation as the "two overall situations".
A policy aim of removing regional barriers so that goods, factors and resources move freely across China under common rules.

t: Innovating the research paradigm of foreign Marxism
zh: 创新国外马克思主义研究范式
paras: Writing in the China Social Sciences Today in September 2023, Lan Jiang argues that Chinese research on foreign Marxism, which has been productive since the 1980s, has reached a turning point. In the author's view, the field must move beyond translating and analysing foreign Marxist thinkers. It should reinterpret them through a Chinese discourse system, be guided by problems, and contribute to building China's own independent knowledge system.

The piece first describes the historical mission of the field after reform and opening up. It then reviews three decades of expansion, from individual thinkers to schools and national traditions, and to new areas such as ecological, postcolonial and feminist Marxism. It next sets out two current problems and closes with a proposal for a new research structure. Lan names early Chinese translators and the main figures introduced, from Lukács, Gramsci and the Frankfurt School to French and analytical Marxists.

Lan identifies two weaknesses. Early work concentrated on texts and ideas and neglected their historical setting. Lan argues that figures such as Horkheimer, Adorno, Marcuse, Baudrillard and John Bellamy Foster responded to specific stages of capitalism, so reading text against text is like buying the casket and returning the pearl. Lan also holds that these thinkers often read Marx through Western ideological discourse. Fromm's humanist reading, which sets the young Marx against the Marx of Capital, is the example given. Lan then describes Chinese scholarship as a coordinate system.
