The views set out in 1925 by the Kuomintang theorist Dai Jitao, who grounded Sun Yat-sen's doctrine in Confucian benevolence, rejected class struggle and urged Communists to leave their party. Communist writers treated it as the ideological preparation of the KMT right wing.

A political grouping around the Young China Party (founded 1923) and the weekly Xingshi (Awakened Lion), which preached 'statism' and an all-class revolution and opposed communism and the Soviet Union.

t: Understanding the genesis and logic of the "grand historical view"
zh: 深刻认识和把握大历史观的生成逻辑
paras: This short commentary, published in Guangming Daily in June 2023, asks where the "grand historical view" (da lishi guan) put forward by Xi Jinping comes from. Wang Guang argues that the concept, which Xi has advanced since the 18th Party Congress (2012) as a scientific way of understanding, drawing on and grasping history, rests on three sources: Marxist historical materialism, China's fine traditional culture, and the practice of socialism with Chinese characteristics in the new era.

The article is organised in three parts, one for each source. It moves from theoretical origins to historical grounding to practical basis, quoting Xi's remarks throughout, together with a line from Liang Qichao on Chinese historiography.

In the first part, Wang presents the grand historical view as a development of historical materialism, the \"only scientific view of history\". Faced with what Xi calls changes unseen in a century, it calls for analysing events within the long flow of history, the tide of the times and global currents. In the second, Wang treats it as a creative transformation of Chinese historiographical tradition, citing the continuity of Chinese civilization and the practical, statecraft orientation of Chinese historical writing. In the third, Wang says the concept is a theoretical summing-up of the new era's practice. Xi has asked that work on philosophy and social sciences, the \"three rural issues\" and literature and art all be viewed within it.

Wang concludes that the ten years of change in the new era supplied the practical foundation for the concept and, in turn, enriched its content. Firmly establishing the view, Wang says, helps draw experience and wisdom from a broad historical perspective for building the future. Read the original if you want a brief, official-line account of how Chinese scholars trace the intellectual sources of the grand historical view.
quoteEn: The grand historical view is the development of historical materialism for our times.
quoteZh: 大历史观是唯物史观的时代发展

glossary.explanation: A concept Xi Jinping has promoted since the 2010s, urging that the Party's history and current affairs be assessed within long-term historical, epochal and global perspectives.
The Marxist theory that material conditions and social relations drive historical development; in Chinese official discourse it is the foundation for the Party's reading of history.
The official name for the Chinese Communist Party's path and system since reform and opening up.

t: The historical and theoretical logic of the modern civilization of the Chinese nation
zh: 中华民族现代文明的历史与理论逻辑
source: China Social Sciences Today (中国社会科学报), June 2023
paras: Luo Wendong offers a commentary on Xi Jinping's speech at the symposium on cultural inheritance and development (2023), which called for taking on a new cultural mission and building a modern civilization of the Chinese nation. Luo argues that the speech shows the Party's understanding of cultural construction and the laws of civilizational development has reached a new height. In Luo's reading, it also makes an original contribution to Marxist cultural theory and is a milestone in the history of both the Chinese nation and human civilization.

The article is organised in three parts. The first sets out the historical roots and cultural foundation of Chinese civilization. The second traces the distinctive path and essential character of the modern civilization the Party is building, from the late Qing to the new era. The third turns to the guiding ideas and fundamental principles for building it, drawing on Xi's cultural thought since the 18th Party Congress (2012).

Luo first presents the five outstanding features of Chinese civilization that Xi identifies: continuity, innovation, unity, inclusiveness and peacefulness. Luo holds that these features explain why China must follow its own path and why understanding them is a precondition for grasping the historical inevitability of the Chinese path. Next, Luo recounts how failed attempts to revive national heritage or imitate the West gave way to Marxism-Leninism and the Party's efforts at civilizational modernization. The Two Integrations, of Marxism with China's concrete realities and with its fine traditional culture, are presented as producing a new organic cultural entity, strengthening cultural subjectivity and opening room for innovation. Luo describes the resulting civilization as socialist, as combining material and spiritual advance and harmony between humans and nature, and as oriented to common prosperity and a community with a shared future for mankind. Luo claims it goes beyond both ancient Chinese and modern Western civilization.

Luo concludes that building this civilization is a long, exploratory undertaking that cannot be done quickly. Luo urges philosophers and social scientists to link their work to the current thematic education campaign, to apply the Two Integrations, and to deepen research on the laws and major questions of cultural and civilizational development. Read the original if you want a concise official-line academic account of how Party scholars frame Chinese civilization, the Two Integrations and the modern civilization of the Chinese nation after Xi's 2023 speech.
quoteEn: The modern civilization of the Chinese nation is a great creation that surpasses both ancient Chinese civilization and modern Western civilization.
quoteZh: 中华民族现代文明是既超越中国古代文明又超越西方近代文明的伟大创造。

glossary.explanation: A formula in Party theory for combining the basic tenets of Marxism with China's concrete realities and with its fine traditional culture. The second integration was added to the formulation in 2021–2023.
A goal of shared wealth for all the people, presented in official discourse as an essential requirement of socialism.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's concept for international relations, stressing shared interests and joint development among countries.

glossary.en: modern civilization of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A term foregrounded in Xi's June 2023 speech on culture, referring to a socialist civilization said to combine Chinese tradition with modernity.

t: Chinese modernization amid the predicament of world modernity: a systemic-structural response
zh: 世界现代性困境下的中国式现代化：系统结构性应对方案论析
source: Socialism Studies (《社会主义研究》), 2022 no. 6
paras: Zhu Wenting asks how Chinese modernization can be understood as a Chinese response to the current predicament of world modernity. The article argues that its effectiveness lies in its "systemic-structural" character, a term Zhu takes from materialist dialectics to describe the interaction of a thing's internal elements. In Zhu's account this character runs through three levels: values, institutional principles and practical forms.

The article opens with the nature of world modernity and its three predicaments, as Zhu describes them: deepening value alienation, institutional divergence, and the entanglement of modernization with de-globalization. It then reviews Western-centric modernity theory and several "multiple modernities" approaches: neo-Marxist theory, developmentalism and dependency theory, and world-systems theory. It next sets out the three-level structure of Chinese modernization, and ends with the mechanisms Zhu draws from it.

Zhu judges the alternative theories inadequate. Western-centric models only adjust capitalism, and the multiple-modernities schools remain within capitalist market logic or neglect the agency of late-developing countries. Chinese modernization, by contrast, is presented as moving from "value ideals" (the all-round development of the person, common prosperity, a community with a shared future for mankind) through the institutions of socialism with Chinese characteristics to practical forms. Those forms are the deepening of the socialist market economy and the parallel advance of new-type industrialization, informatization, urbanization and agricultural modernization. Zhu then names three mechanisms: a Party–people–humanity pattern of multiple actors that gathers modernizing forces; a handling of the socialist–capitalist relationship that, Zhu argues, releases the advantages of the socialist system; and the creation of a new form of human civilization through improved relations between humans and nature, society and the world.

Zhu concludes that Chinese modernization offers a reliable model for escaping the predicament of world modernity. In this reading it also enriches modernity theory and supports the idea of a new form of human civilization. Zhu treats capitalism as the root of the predicament and presents socialism with Chinese characteristics as correcting capital-centred, polarising and expansionist modernization. Read the original if you want a systematic, Party-theory account of how Chinese modernization is positioned against Western modernity theories, dependency theory and world-systems theory.
quoteEn: The unity of values and institutions constitutes the intrinsic determination of Chinese modernization.
quoteZh: 价值和制度的统一构成中国式现代化的内在规定性。

glossary.explanation: The official name for China's path to modernization, elaborated by the Communist Party from the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is presented as distinct from Western models.
An official goal of prosperity shared by all the people, which the Party describes as an essential requirement of socialism.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's concept for China's vision of international relations and global governance.
The official name for the Party's theory, system and path of socialism since the reform era.

glossary.en: a new form of human civilization
glossary.explanation: An official formulation, used from 2021, for the civilizational achievement Chinese modernization is said to create.

t: The new form of human civilization sublates the paradox of capitalist civilization
zh: 人类文明新形态扬弃资本文明悖论
paras: Taking its cue from the report to the 20th Party Congress (2022), which calls for regulating and guiding the healthy development of capital by law, Zhao Ruize asks how the new form of human civilization deals with capital's contradictory effects. The author argues that this civilization, a new type oriented towards socialism, distinguishes capital's dual nature as a relation of production and as a factor of production. It thereby uses capital's positive role while avoiding its negative limits, and in doing so sublates the paradox of capitalist civilization. The piece appeared in China Social Sciences Today in May 2023.

The article moves in four steps. It first sets out how capitalist civilization arose through capital's civilizing role, then the paradox built into that form. It next places the new form of human civilization in Marx's account of the succession of civilizational forms, and finally draws out the significance of continuing to enrich and develop it. Zhao relies mainly on Marx and Engels, including the Grundrisse's three social forms and the Communist Manifesto.

In Zhao's reading, capital's civilizing role consists in the rapid growth of productive forces and the universalization of social exchange, which opened world history. Yet capital's aim is self-valorization, and its drive to expand keeps pressing against natural and social limits. The result, the author argues, is ecological crisis and social crisis, rooted in private appropriation set against socialized production and in domination of the periphery by the centre. Zhao presents the new form of civilization as a transitional socialist form between capitalist and communist civilization. It absorbs capitalism's material achievements while carrying communism's requirements, and it is the product of integrating Marxism with China's concrete reality and its fine traditional culture. Under it, socialist relations of production dominate, so capital's factor-of-production attributes can be used while its valorizing attributes are held in check.

Zhao draws three implications. First, "traffic lights" for capital (green for its civilizing function, red for its valorizing drive) are a way to "harness" capital, with the final aim of "eliminating" it in a higher mode of production. Second, material, political, spiritual, social and ecological civilization are coordinated, in contrast to what the author calls capitalism's one-dimensional civilization. Third, respect for civilizational diversity and the building of a community with a shared future for mankind show that capitalist modernization is not the only road and that capitalist civilization is not the final form. Read the original if you want a compact statement of how Chinese commentary links Marx's theory of capital's civilizing role to Chinese modernization and the policy of regulating capital.
quoteEn: The process of sublating the paradox of capitalist civilization is a process of continually creating conditions for communism.
quoteZh: 扬弃资本文明悖论的过程，就是不断为共产主义创造条件的过程。

glossary.en: the new form of human civilization
glossary.explanation: A concept in Party discourse, prominent since Xi Jinping's 2021 speech on the Party's centenary. It describes the civilizational type said to be created by Chinese modernization.
The official name for China's path of modernization, set out in the report to the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is presented as an alternative to Western modernization.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's formulation of the aim of Chinese foreign policy, stressing cooperation, shared development and respect for civilizational diversity.

t: Marx's philosophy establishes a scientific concept of practice
zh: 马克思哲学确立科学的实践概念
paras: This short piece, published in the Chinese Social Sciences Today in May 2023, asks how Marx's concept of practice became a scientific one and why it matters. Gao Juan argues that practice is the pivot by which Marx broke with the idealist philosophical tradition. In Gao's reading, it is also essential for grasping the scientific system of Marxist philosophy and the coherence of Marx's thought as a whole.

The article follows the concept from The German Ideology back to its origin in the Theses on Feuerbach. It first traces a movement from the abstract to the concrete in Marx's treatment of practice. It then examines the "five kinds of production" that The German Ideology treats as the main forms of practice. It closes by placing practice as the starting point of Marx's philosophy.

Gao contends that the Theses on Feuerbach fixed practice as the mark separating new materialism from old materialism. There Marx criticised Feuerbach's humanism, redefined the human essence as the ensemble of social relations, and made sensuous human activity the logical starting point. In Gao's account, The German Ideology deepened this into material production, so that "object-related activity" became concrete. The five kinds of production are the production of material means of life, their reproduction, the production of human beings themselves, of social relations and of social consciousness. Gao says the first three are basic and that new needs arising from satisfied ones drive history. Social consciousness is derived from the other four. Gao notes that the word "practice" appears in The German Ideology mostly indirectly, through terms such as "sensuous activity" and "industry and commerce".

Gao concludes that the German Ideology filled the gap of abstraction left at the time of the Theses, grounded the new view of history in real individuals and production, and marked an essential break with Feuerbach. Practice is described as the core of the universal principles of Marxism. Gao calls for understanding, inheriting and developing Marx's scientific conception of practice so that it can be combined with China's realities to address practical difficulties. Read the original if you want a compact Chinese account of how the Theses on Feuerbach and The German Ideology are linked through the concept of practice.
quoteEn: Practice is the starting point of Marxist philosophy, and the formulation of the scientific conception of practice marks an essential difference between the new materialist philosophy Marx founded and the old materialism represented by Feuerbach.
quoteZh: 实践是马克思主义哲学的起点，科学实践观的提出则标志着马克思创立的新唯物主义哲学与费尔巴哈为代表的旧唯物主义哲学有了本质区别。

t: The complex context of the young Marx's turn to materialism
zh: 青年马克思唯物主义思想转变的复杂语境
paras: Zhang Yibing, in a piece first published in the Chinese Social Sciences Today (6 June 2023), returns to the young Marx's first intellectual shift, from idealism to materialism. The article asks three questions: how this shift should be studied, why Marx made it, and where its theoretical sources lay. Zhang argues that the shift was driven by the "problem of material interests" and that it drew on more sources than Feuerbach alone.

The article starts from Lenin's 1914 account of Marx's turn during the Rheinische Zeitung period and the Deutsch-Französische Jahrbücher, and from Sun Bokai's "two shifts" thesis, which separates general materialism from historical materialism. Zhang divides the first shift into five stages. They run from the 1842 Rheinische Zeitung articles, through the 1843 Critique of Hegel's Philosophy of Right and the Kreuznach notebooks, and the Deutsch-Französische Jahrbücher texts, to the 1844 Paris Notebooks and Economic and Philosophic Manuscripts of 1844. The fifth stage is the second shift after 1845, toward historical materialism, together with Marx's later explicit and implicit returns to the first shift.

On method, Zhang sets three principles. These are working from the German, French and English originals and the MEGA2 manuscripts; tracing the genesis of Marx's ideas; and reconstructing his thought in its own context without teleological projection. Zhang's example is that reading the 1843 "civil society" as the "economic base", or reading alienated labour through Capital, mistakes later concepts for earlier ones. On motive, Zhang holds that Marx's encounter with material interests, as in the debates on wood theft, shook his Hegelian faith in state reason. The problem was only partly resolved in 1843–44, when Marx turned to economics. It persisted through the theory of alienated labour and later through the "sachlich" forces and "Versachlichung" of historical materialism, and it shaped his critical sequence from civil society to bourgeois society to the capitalist mode of production.

On sources, Zhang accepts Feuerbach's importance but, following Sun Bokai, stresses that Marx never accepted him without reservation and sublated his humanism through Hegelian dialectics. Zhang adds Eduard Gans, whose Hegel edition and remarks on class opposition left a lasting mark. Zhang also names Engels and Moses Hess, who supplied economic critique and the notion of "economic alienation". The last source is the classical economists excerpted in the Paris Notebooks, who in Zhang's view brought Marx to what Zhang calls "social materialism". Read the original if you study the young Marx's intellectual development, MEGA2-based textual method, or the Chinese scholarly debate following Sun Bokai's "two shifts" thesis.
quoteEn: The \"problem of material interests\" was both the motive for the young Marx's turn to materialism and an important factor in the formation and deepening of his critical discourse.
quoteZh: “物质利益难题”既是青年马克思唯物主义转变的动因，也是马克思批判话语形成和深化的重要因素。

glossary.explanation: An interpretation of the young Marx's development proposed by Sun Bokai of Nanjing University. It distinguishes a first shift to general materialism from a second shift to historical materialism.

glossary.literal: the difficult problem of material interests
glossary.explanation: The puzzle Marx met in 1842 when he found that real material interests, not rational principles, determined law and the state. Chinese scholars commonly treat it as the practical spur to his turn to materialism.
Zhang's own term for the materialist view of social life that Marx reached through classical political economy in 1844, before historical materialism.

t: Reflections on building an autonomous knowledge system for Chinese historiography
zh: 对构建中国历史学自主知识体系的思考
source: Historical Theory Studies (Shixue lilun yanjiu), 2023 no. 3
paras: Chen Qitai asks how Chinese historical scholarship can build its own autonomous knowledge system under the guidance of the materialist conception of history. The article argues that historiographical theory guides the whole discipline, and that the task requires two things: drawing together the theoretical achievements of the reform era and drawing out the theoretical value of traditional Chinese historiography.

The article opens by presenting China's long, continuous history, its developed feudal society, the modern revolution and the decades since 1949 as a source of theoretical problems. Chen then credits two forces for the vitality of historical theory since reform and opening up: clearing out dogmatism and returning to Marxism's founding principles, and developing the materialist conception of history to match new conditions. Section two lists 13 theoretical achievements of the period and discusses several in detail. Section three takes the history of historiography as a test case.

Among the 13 achievements, Chen examines Fei Xiaotong's theory of the pattern of diversity in unity of the Chinese nation, the cultural-identity thesis in Qu Lindong's five-volume work, and Liu Danian's 'two basic problems' (national independence and modernization) as the main thread of modern Chinese history. He presents the last as an integration of earlier approaches centred on revolutionary high tides and on modernization. In section three, Chen argues that historical compilation is not a mere technical matter. He identifies 'compilation thought' as its core, and takes Sima Qian's Shiji as an example. Its five-part form embodies what Chen calls a 'multi-dimensional historical vision', later adapted in Bai Shouyi's multi-volume General History of China.

Chen concludes that creative use of the materialist conception of history is the unshakeable direction. He calls for more systematic summaries of theoretical results, both across the discipline and within its branches such as political, economic, intellectual and cultural history. In his view this would strengthen cultural confidence. Chen describes his list of 13 achievements as a personal and incomplete selection. Read the original if you want a Chinese historian's survey of reform-era historical theory, including the debates on ethnic relations and modern history, and of how traditional historiography is being reframed for a contemporary Chinese knowledge system.
quoteEn: China is fertile soil for the development of historiography, and it should also be fertile soil for the creation of historical theory.
quoteZh: 中国是史学发展的沃土，也应该是史学理论创造的沃土。

glossary.explanation: The Marxist theory of history, which explains social change through material production and class relations. In Chinese scholarship it is the stated guiding principle of historical research.
The policy of economic reform and opening to the outside world launched in 1978. Chinese scholars often use it to mark the start of a new period of academic freedom and creativity.

glossary.zh: 中华民族多元一体格局
glossary.en: pattern of diversity in unity of the Chinese nation
glossary.literal: pluralistic-unitary configuration of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A theory proposed by the anthropologist Fei Xiaotong in 1988. It holds that the 56 officially recognised ethnic groups form one Chinese nation at a higher level of identity.
The branch of history that studies how history-writing has developed, including its methods, genres and thinkers.
A slogan stressing confidence in China's own cultural tradition and socialist culture. It was promoted prominently under Xi Jinping.

t: Mastering Marxism's "essential skill": study, practice and the theme education campaign
zh: 把马克思主义看家本领学到手
paras: This newspaper commentary, first published in the China Social Sciences Today on 27 April 2023, takes up the Party's theme education campaign on studying and implementing Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era. It was written after a work conference on the campaign held in Beijing on 3 April 2023. Ling argues that the campaign is a means of improving the Marxist level of the whole Party and that it demands effort in three areas: ideological study, linking theory to practice, and concrete action.

The piece is organised under three headings that follow this scheme. It begins with Xi Jinping's remarks at the conference about the goals of national rejuvenation and the need to strengthen theoretical armament. It then discusses the campaign's general requirements and its fundamental task, citing Xi's formulations at length. It closes with the call to read original texts and to turn theory into practical results.

Ling's core claim is that the campaign's requirements, "learn the thought, strengthen Party spirit, emphasise practice, build new achievements", embody the Marxist theory of knowledge, which joins understanding with practice and the remaking of the subjective world with the remaking of the objective one. On this reading, the unity of study, reflection and application and of knowing, believing and acting expresses the Two Integrations and keeps Marxism vital. Ling also presents ideals and convictions as the Party's spiritual "calcium", and holds that Party members must use the thought to face contradictions, analyse them and resolve them. The author further links this to the Party's self-reform, with members urged to take political check-ups, accept public supervision and correct deviations at once.

Ling concludes that the Party's success rests on Marxism and that rising challenges in reform, development and governance require cadres to apply the thought to major risks and problems, in pursuit of Chinese modernization and the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. Each step in theoretical innovation, the author says, must be followed by theoretical armament and then practice, and cadres should read original works to grasp the thought as a whole. Read the original if you want a compact example of how the 2023 theme education campaign was justified in Marxist epistemological terms in the Party-aligned press.
quoteEn: The unity of study, reflection and application, and of knowing, believing and acting, carries through the theoretical character of dialectical and historical materialism, which combines Marxism's basic principles with China's concrete realities and with China's fine traditional culture, and it is the fundamental principle for keeping Marxism vigorous and full of vitality.
quoteZh: 学思用贯通、知信行统一贯彻了马克思主义基本原理同中国具体实际相结合、同中华优秀传统文化相结合的辩证唯物主义和历史唯物主义的理论品格，是保持马克思主义的蓬勃生机和旺盛活力的根本原则。

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The official guiding ideology of the Communist Party of China, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018. It is presented as the latest stage of adapting Marxism to China.
A Party-wide political study and rectification drive organised around a set theme. The 2023 campaign focused on studying and implementing Xi Jinping Thought.
The formula that Marxism must be combined with China's concrete realities and with its fine traditional culture. It is used officially to describe adapting Marxism to China.
An official term for the Party's efforts to discipline, purify and improve itself. It is often paired with full and rigorous self-governance of the Party.
The official name for China's path to modernity, set out by Xi Jinping and the 20th Party Congress (2022) as distinct from Western models.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.literal: the great revival of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The Party's central national goal, associated with the Chinese Dream, of restoring China to a position of strength and prosperity by the mid-twenty-first century.

t: Truly mastering Marxism as the essential skill
zh: 真正把马克思主义看家本领学到手
paras: Writing in Red Flag Manuscripts (2023, no. 9), Gong Yun takes up Xi Jinping's call, made at the work conference for the thematic education campaign on studying Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, that Party members and cadres should "truly master" Marxism as their essential skill (看家本领). Gong argues that doing so means, above all, studying and applying Xi Jinping Thought in depth, and that theoretical armament has been a constant priority of the Party for over a century.

The commentary has two parts. The first sets out why Marxism is the soul and banner of the Communist Party of China. It draws on Marx, Lenin, Mao Zedong, Deng Xiaoping and Xi Jinping. The second explains how to deepen the study and implementation of Xi Jinping Thought, under three headings: comprehensive study, comprehensive grasp and comprehensive implementation.

In the first part Gong presents Marxism as a unity of truth and values, with the people as its essential attribute. Gong describes it as a scientific, practical and open theory whose fate is bound up with that of the Party, the Chinese people and the Chinese nation. In Gong's account it supplied the ideological weapon for revolution, construction and reform, and cadres who master it gain stronger political judgement, understanding and execution. The second part calls Xi Jinping Thought "contemporary Chinese Marxism" and "Marxism of the twenty-first century". Gong says it should be studied as a complete system rather than in fragments, with attention to its worldview, methodology and the "six musts" set out in the report to the 20th Party Congress (2022), and applied in practice.

Gong concludes that study must lead to action, linking theory with practice, so that learning is turned into results that advance the work of the Party and state. Gong calls on cadres to use the Thought to remould their own outlook, to resolve problems and defuse major risks, and to advance Chinese modernization, in service of the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party-affiliated theorists frame Marxist study for cadres during the 2023 thematic education campaign.
quoteEn: The whole purpose of studying Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era lies in applying it, in turning this thought into a powerful ideological weapon for transforming both the subjective and the objective world.
quoteZh: 学习习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想的目的全在于运用，在于把这一思想变成改造主观世界和客观世界的强大思想武器。

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The official name for the Party's guiding ideology associated with Xi Jinping, written into the Party constitution in 2017. Official texts present it as the latest stage of adapting Marxism to China.
The official term for China's path to modernization, set out at the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is presented as distinct from Western models.
A Party-wide political education drive organised around a set theme. The 2023 campaign focused on studying Xi Jinping Thought.

Six methodological principles in the report to the 20th Party Congress: put the people first, stay confident and independent, uphold fundamental principles while innovating, be problem-oriented, apply systems thinking, and have a global vision.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: An official goal of restoring China's national strength and international standing, central to Party discourse since 2012.

t: Applying historical wisdom to create great undertakings in the new era
zh: 运用历史智慧开创新时代伟业
source: China Social Sciences Today (Zhongguo shehui kexue bao), posted 25 May 2023
paras: Writing after the 20th Party Congress (2022), Zhang Yanguo takes up the report's call to "firm up historical confidence, strengthen historical initiative". The commentary asks how studying history can help the Party and people achieve great undertakings in the new era. Zhang's answer is a sequence: a correct view of history leads to historical cognition, then to historical confidence, historical consciousness and historical initiative, and finally to great historical undertakings.

The piece is organised under five headings. These cover the origin of historical confidence in a correct view of history, historical cognition as its basis, and confidence as the deepest and most fundamental form of confidence. They continue with historical consciousness as the route to initiative, and the creation of new-era undertakings. Zhang draws throughout on Xi Jinping's remarks, on Marx, Engels, Mao Zedong and Deng Xiaoping, and on the Party's official summaries of its historical experience.

Zhang distinguishes fragmentary, emotional perception of history from rational cognition that works from facts, from surface to essence. Historical confidence, in this account, rests on the second kind, guided by dialectical and historical materialism and on the history of the Chinese nation, the Party, New China, reform and opening up and the past decade. Zhang calls it the foundation of the Four-sphere Confidence and says it should also become confidence that others share. The author also sets confidence against two threats: domestically, historical nihilism that denies the Party's achievements, and abroad, "hostile forces" promoting Western-centred views of history, "universal values" and "Westernization". Zhang urges the Party to answer these ideological struggles directly.

Zhang concludes that historical confidence is the Party's greatest source of assurance, historical consciousness its distinguishing feature, and historical initiative its particular strength. The Party's "five historical significances", "ten historical experiences" and "six musts" are presented as the grand narrative that roots the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation in history. As challenges grow more complex, Zhang calls for firmer historical resolve and a fresh "answer sheet" for history and the people. Read the original if you want a representative example of how Party-aligned scholars present historical confidence and the struggle against historical nihilism after the 20th Party Congress.
quoteEn: Historical confidence becomes deeper and more powerful only when it is rooted in the deepest layers of one's own history.
quoteZh: 历史自信只有植根于自己历史的最深处，才更加深沉有力

glossary.explanation: A concept stressed by Xi Jinping and in the 20th Party Congress report, referring to confidence in the Party's and the nation's historical path and achievements. It is often linked to the study of Party history.
The idea of actively grasping historical laws and trends to shape events, rather than reacting to them. Official texts pair it with historical confidence and historical consciousness.
An official label for views that Party theorists see as denying or distorting the Party's and the socialist path's historical record. Its use is a recurring theme in Chinese ideological discourse.
Confidence in the path, theory, system and culture of socialism with Chinese characteristics. It is an official formula associated with Xi Jinping's leadership.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The official long-term national goal of restoring China's strength and standing, closely tied to the Chinese Dream.

t: Beware of overseas regional history's attempts to deconstruct historical China
zh: 警惕海外区域史研究解构历史中国的企图
paras: Kong Yingchuan takes up a trend in recent American China studies: regional histories of China's frontiers that claim to be "region-centred" but, in the author's view, end up deconstructing historical China. The article, a critical commentary first published in Historical Review in 2022, argues that this work uses Western concepts to cut the frontiers out of Chinese history. Kong says the real intent behind it deserves vigilance.

The piece first sketches the development of American regional-history writing on China, from Fairbank, Lattimore and Wittfogel in the 1930s and 1940s, through the "China-centred approach" of the 1960s and Skinner's regional systems theory, to a post-1990 shift under postmodern and postcolonial influence. It then examines specific works on Taiwan, Guizhou, Yunnan and Xinjiang, by authors including Teng Emma Jinhua, Laura Hostetler, Bin Yang, Peter Perdue, James Millward and Michael Clarke. Kong closes by setting these works against what the article presents as the historical record of a unified multi-ethnic China.

Kong contends that these works label ancient China an "empire" and treat the Yuan and Qing as non-Chinese "conquest dynasties". On this reading, Qing map-making, ethnography and frontier governance are equated with Western colonialism, and Yang's account of Yunnan is said to make its Chinese identity depend on a provincial identity. Kong answers that such claims ignore the long Chinese traditions of cartography and local gazetteers. The author adds that they also ignore the institutional continuity of the province system, which Kong traces back to the Wei–Jin, Sui and Tang dynasties. Kong further cites the gradual fusion of nomadic and agrarian peoples.

Kong concludes that the "colonial empire" framing plays down modern Western colonial aggression against China and serves a political aim. In the article's reading, "decolonisation" of the regions amounts to "de-Sinicisation", a return to a Han-only China acceptable to the West, or a "China history without China". Kong insists that China's unity came from the natural coalescence of its peoples and was settled in the modern struggle against colonial invasion. Read the original if you want an example of how Chinese historians of the frontiers respond to the "New Qing History", Inner Asia approaches and postcolonial scholarship in the United States, and which books they single out.
quoteEn: A unified multi-ethnic China and a pluralistic yet integrated Chinese nation were formed through the natural coalescence of the peoples living on Chinese soil over thousands of years of history.
quoteZh: 统一多民族的中国、多元一体的中华民族，是中华大地上生活的各民族在千百年来的历史长河中自然凝聚而形成的

t: The elements, models and evolution of Chinese modernization
zh: 中国式现代化的要素、模式与变迁
source: Journal of Beijing Administration Institute, 2023 no. 2
paras: Tong Dezhi and Wang Xu ask what elements make up Chinese modernization, how those elements relate, what models they form and how these have changed across periods. Taking up the 20th Party Congress (2022) call to advance the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation through Chinese modernization, they argue that it is best defined as the strategic goal of the Communist Party leading the people, through reform and opening up, to promote development and build socialism. They contend that it has passed through three successive models and moves from the inheritance of core principles to innovation, and from emphasis on a centre to comprehensiveness.

The study builds a corpus from five sets of leaders' writings: Mao Zedong, Deng Xiaoping, Jiang Zemin, Hu Jintao and Xi Jinping's Governance of China. It extracts the words adjacent to "modernization", about 320,000 characters, and checks the results against a supplementary corpus of Party document compilations since 1978. Using Nvivo 11 coding, co-occurrence and coverage statistics, the authors combine quantitative and qualitative analysis. The article sets out the elements, then three models, then patterns of change.

From the most frequent co-occurring words, the authors derive four features: modernization led by the Party and carried out by the people, socialist modernization, modernization driven by reform and opening up, and modernization aimed at development. They trace the shift in the notion of development from rapid growth to high-quality development. They then periodise three models. The first is the "four modernizations" (industry, agriculture, national defence, science and technology), whose frequency peaks in Deng's writings and then drops. The second is a moderately prosperous society (xiaokang), and the third is the modern socialist country. In the authors' reading, this sequence shows social and state-level modernization converging.

The authors conclude that Chinese modernization combines continuity, meaning Party leadership, socialism and common prosperity, with innovations such as whole-process people's democracy and a community with a shared future for mankind. They say its scope has widened from key sectors to an overall layout, the three-in-one to five-in-one arrangement, culminating in the 20th Congress's account. They concede that word-frequency analysis assumes frequency equals importance and that conclusions rest on texts alone and need further empirical testing. Read the original if you want a corpus-based, quantitative reading of how Party leaders' modernization discourse has evolved from Mao to Xi.
quoteEn: Chinese modernization is a process of continual inheritance and innovation, moving from a centre of emphasis towards comprehensive development.
quoteZh: 中国式现代化是一个不断传承创新、由中心走向全面发展的过程。

glossary.explanation: The Party's official term for China's own path of modernization, given a systematic statement in the report to the 20th Party Congress in 2022.
A national goal of modernizing industry, agriculture, national defence, and science and technology, formulated under Mao and Zhou Enlai and taken up by Deng Xiaoping.
A development goal from Deng's era, written into Party Congress reports from 1997. It was declared achieved in 2020 under the label of a moderately prosperous society in all respects.

Official concept describing China's democracy as covering every stage of the political process, from elections to consultation, decision-making, management and oversight. It was put forward by Xi Jinping in 2019.
Official term for a shift from high-speed growth to growth stressing quality, efficiency and innovation.
The policy of economic reform and opening to the outside world launched in 1978 under Deng Xiaoping.
The goal of prosperity shared by all the people, presented in official discourse as an essential requirement of socialism.

t: Three dimensions of Marx's conception of civilization
zh: 马克思文明观的三重维度
paras: This short commentary, first published in the Chinese Social Sciences Today in April 2023, asks how Marx understood civilization. Huang and Xue argue that his view rests on three basic dimensions: human practice as the basis for analysing civilization, human development as the yardstick for assessing it, and human emancipation as the ideal pursued by communist civilization.

The article is organised in three sections, one for each dimension. It begins by contrasting Marx with modern Western research on civilization, citing Guizot's historical work and Morgan's anthropology. It then turns to Marx's assessment of capitalist civilization, and ends with his picture of a communist stage of civilization.

On practice, the authors say Enlightenment-influenced scholarship asserted human agency against theology but grasped the human being as an abstract generality. In their account, this led it into idealism, treating civilization as a product of ideas and desires. Marx instead started from material production, so that civilization is, in Engels's words quoted by the authors, a matter of practice. Productive forces are its ultimate determining force, and practice makes civilization a practical, historical and social category. On development, Huang and Xue say Marx credited capitalism's "civilizing side": vast productive forces, world-wide interaction, mastery over nature and free time for workers. He also condemned its "anti-civilizing side": exploitation for the sake of valorising capital, workers reduced to appendages of machines, and a dependence on things that leaves people as capital's "sacrificial victims".

The authors conclude that Marx's aim in studying civilization was human liberation and the free and all-round development of the individual. They describe communist civilization as unifying three pairs: individual and others' development, labour and human development, and all-round human development and social progress. Labour there becomes self-realisation rather than a compulsory means of livelihood. Read the original if you want a compact, quotation-based outline of how Marx's account of civilization links practice, capitalism's contradictions and communist emancipation.
quoteEn: Civilization is, in the final analysis, the product of the practice of people situated within specific social relations.
quoteZh: 文明归根到底是处在各种特定社会关系当中的人的实践创造物。

t: Marx and Engels's critique of the paradoxes of capitalist society
zh: 马克思恩格斯对资本主义社会悖论的批判
paras: Liu Shuhui, writing in the Chinese Social Sciences Today (23 February 2023), asks how to understand the claim in the Communist Manifesto that the fall of the bourgeoisie and the victory of the proletariat are "equally inevitable". The article argues that the claim can be understood through three paradoxes of capitalist society that Marx and Engels identify: wealth, freedom and civilization. Each, in Liu's reading, is an opposition produced by capitalism itself, and together they make bourgeois rule unsustainable.

The piece is a short commentary on the history of Marxism, organised under three headings, one for each paradox. Liu draws mainly on the Manifesto and links it to other works by Marx and Engels, including The Poverty of Philosophy, Wage Labour and Capital, Capital, Engels's Outlines of a Critique of Political Economy and Marx's speech on free trade. A closing section ties the three paradoxes back to the Manifesto's thesis.

On wealth, Liu describes the opposition between the accumulation of wealth and the accumulation of poverty. The bourgeoisie must guarantee workers at least a bare subsistence in order to rule, yet cannot do so, and in that sense society can no longer live under its rule. On freedom, Liu reads Marx's analysis in Capital as showing that freedom of buying and selling presupposes workers who have no means of production and are compelled to sell their labour-power. Free competition is likewise described as the highest form of private property, so that the worker's only freedom is the freedom to choose by whom to be exploited. On civilization, Liu follows Marx and Engels in holding that the bourgeoisie draws all nations into "civilization" while forcing them to adopt its mode of production and subordinating the East to the West through colonialism. The result, the article says, is a lopsided world.

Liu concludes that the first two paradoxes lead workers to unite against their own national bourgeoisie, while the third leads the proletarians of the world to unite against the bourgeoisie as a class. In this sense the fall of the bourgeoisie and the victory of the proletariat are, as the article presents it, equally inevitable. Liu notes that the opposition between wealth and ecological destruction is not treated in the Manifesto and is therefore left aside. Read the original if you want a concise, text-based outline of how Chinese commentary reads the Manifesto's thesis of bourgeois collapse through the themes of wealth, freedom and civilization.
quoteEn: The civilized world that the bourgeoisie creates for itself in its own image is a seriously unbalanced and deformed world.
quoteZh: 资产阶级按自己的面貌为自己创造的文明世界，是一个严重失衡的畸形世界。

t: Upholding and developing Marxism requires integrating it with China's fine traditional culture
zh: 坚持和发展马克思主义，必须同中华优秀传统文化相结合
paras: This short commentary, first published in the People's Daily on 18 April 2023, explains the statement in the report to the 20th Party Congress (2022) that upholding and developing Marxism requires combining it with China's fine traditional culture. Zhang argues that this integration deepens the Party's understanding of how to adapt Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times, and expresses the Party's cultural confidence and cultural self-awareness.

The piece opens with Xi Jinping's remarks that traditional culture is the "root" of the Party's theoretical innovation. It then moves through the historical reasons for the integration, the influence of traditional culture on China's path, theory and institutions, and the tasks ahead on the "new journey".

Zhang's central claim is that Marxism took root in China because it resonated with values the Chinese people had inherited over millennia and held without always noticing. In this account, the values of fine traditional culture are highly compatible with those of scientific socialism, which is the precondition for the integration. Citing Xi, Zhang holds that socialism with Chinese characteristics carries a "genetic code" from traditional culture, and that the national governance system draws on it. Since the 18th Party Congress (2012), the article says, ideas such as "the world belongs to all" and "the people are the foundation of the state" have been reinterpreted as sources for the core socialist values. The relationship is presented as mutual: Chinese Marxism gains Chinese style, while tradition gains new content from Marxism's truth.

Zhang calls for stronger historical and cultural confidence and a deeper grasp of the Two Integrations. The article urges drawing out the philosophy, humanism, values and moral norms of traditional culture, so as to give the Party's innovative theory distinct Chinese characteristics. Read the original if you want a concise, official-line statement of why the Chinese Communist Party links Marxism to traditional culture.
quoteEn: The values of China's fine traditional culture are highly compatible with the values advocated by scientific socialism, and this provides the precondition for integrating the basic principles of Marxism with fine traditional Chinese culture.
quoteZh: 中华优秀传统文化的价值观念同科学社会主义价值观主张具有高度契合性，这为马克思主义基本原理同中华优秀传统文化相结合提供了前提条件。

glossary.explanation: Formula referring to combining the basic tenets of Marxism with China's concrete realities and with China's fine traditional culture. The second integration was added in official discourse in 2021–2023.
Official term for confidence in the value and vitality of China's own culture, listed by Xi Jinping alongside confidence in the path, theory and system.
A set of twenty-four characters in twelve values at the national, social and individual levels, promoted by the Party since the 18th Party Congress.
The Party's official name for its path, theory and system of socialism, dating from the early 1980s reform era.

t: Is there "civil society" in the Critique of Hegel's Philosophy of Right?
zh: 《黑格尔法哲学批判》中存在“市民社会”吗？
paras: Kong Weiyu starts from Engels's 1885 claim that it is civil society that conditions and determines the state, and from the habit of reading that claim as the state of the young Marx's thought in 1843–44. The article asks what Marx meant by "civil society" in his manuscript Critique of Hegel's Philosophy of Right, which Engels had not seen. Kong's answer is that the concept there is ambiguous and unfinished, and is neither Hegel's concept nor the later historical-materialist one.

The piece is a short theoretical commentary first published in the Chinese Social Sciences Today in April 2023. It is organised around four questions: whether the concept exists at all in the manuscript, whether it exists in Hegel's sense, whether it exists as an "economic base", and whether it exists in a humanist sense. Kong draws on Marx's German terminology, the structure of Hegel's Elements of the Philosophy of Right, and Marx's later retrospective remarks.

On terminology, Kong notes that the manuscript is loose in its wording. Marx sometimes replaces "civil society" with "the individual", which Kong reads as showing that he then conceived civil society as made up of individual rights. Kong also distinguishes the French-derived term for aristocratic "society" from "bürgerliche Gesellschaft", and argues that the former is pejorative and must not be confused with civil society. On Hegel, the surviving manuscript begins at the "State" section (§261), and Kong argues that no lost part could have treated the long civil-society chapter, so no sustained analysis of it exists. Marx's civil society is a flat, non-structured body of private citizens held together by marriage, contract and legally conceived property. In Kong's view, this is why Marx could not carry out a materialist inversion of Hegel's structured "state–civil society–family" system and "only turns in circles within abstract right". Political economy had not yet been studied systematically, so the concept only emerges properly in the 1844 Economic and Philosophic Manuscripts.

Kong concludes that the manuscript's civil society has a humanist side: it must first sublate the feudal political state, and in the future it would itself be sublated, so that the "true human being" appears. Kong sees this as an expression of Marx's humanist materialism of the time. Read the original if you study the young Marx's development, the translation of bürgerliche Gesellschaft, or the gap between his 1843 manuscript and Engels's later reading of it.
quoteEn: That civil society goes beyond the political state is only the first step; more important is that Marx here puts forward a forward-looking logic of civil society's development.
quoteZh: 市民社会超越政治国家只是第一步，更重要的是马克思在这里提出了面向未来的市民社会发展逻辑。

glossary.explanation: Rendering of the German bürgerliche Gesellschaft, the sphere of private individuals and interests distinct from the state. The article argues that it should be translated this way rather than as "bourgeois society" for the young Marx.

keywords: Critique of Hegel's Philosophy of Right

t: The succession of early Chinese Marxists' theories on the evolution of social formations
zh: 我国早期马克思主义者关于社会形态演变理论的递嬗研究
paras: Wang Xiangqing and Liang Yanli ask how early Chinese Marxists understood the evolution of social formations, a core category of historical materialism, and how their successive studies built up Marxist theory on the subject in China. They argue that, guided by historical materialism, these thinkers moved from borrowed general schemes towards a theory fitted to Chinese conditions. In the authors' account, the work spread Marxism and helped answer the question of where China was heading.

The article has three parts. The first sets out the background: the debates over "ancient and modern, China and the West" and over "problems versus isms", plus the intellectual sources, namely the Marxist classics, Japanese and Soviet Marxism, and traditional Chinese philosophy. The second traces five stages through five figures: Cai Hesen, Zhang Bojian, Fan Shoukang, Li Da and Mao Zedong. The third draws out the general features of this body of work.

The authors assess each figure by his periodisation and its limits. Cai's Social Evolution (1924) used Morgan's three-stage scheme and is judged pioneering but vague. Zhang's eight-stage scheme is described as more concrete and accessible, though some of its divisions are called contentious. Fan and Li are credited with a five-stage division and with attention to China's specificity. Mao is credited with stressing class struggle and analysing China's semi-colonial, semi-feudal formation. Three features are identified. Historical materialism was used to criticise evolutionism. Attention shifted from general theory, through the study of ancient society, to the present reality of China. Diverse views gave way to acceptance of the five-formation theory, which the authors say was consolidated by the Stalin-edited History of the CPSU(B) in 1938 and Mao's praise of it.

The authors conclude that this research moved from spontaneous to conscious, from individual to collective and from theory to practice. They say it promoted a shift from an idealist view of heroes to a materialist view of the masses. In their view it also strengthened the Communist Party's leadership by gathering mass support for socialism, and revolutionary practice confirmed the theory. Read the original if you want a detailed, Party-historiographical account of how Chinese Marxists periodised history before 1949 and how the five-formation scheme became orthodox.
quoteEn: In studying the development and evolution of social formations with historical materialism, China's early Marxists achieved a shift from the spontaneous to the conscious, from the individual to the collective, and from theory to practice.
quoteZh: 我国早期马克思主义者在以唯物史观研究社会形态的发展与演变时，实现了从自发到自觉、由个体到群体、从理论到实践的转变

glossary.explanation: A historical materialist category for the concrete unity of an economic base and its superstructure at a given level of the productive forces. Chinese scholarship uses it for stages such as primitive, slave, feudal, capitalist and socialist society.
The Marxist theory that material production and the relations of production shape social structure and historical change.

t: The Western tradition, core orientation and intellectual effects of Marx's thought on community
zh: 马克思共同体思想的西方传统、核心指向与思想效应
paras: Shen Jiangping and Ding Yaopeng ask how Marx's thought on community (gongtongti) relates to the long Western lineage of such thinking, and what it can still contribute today. Marx never defined the term, and his remarks are scattered across his career. The authors argue that he sublated earlier Western ideas of community, that his core contribution lies in a revolutionary path to a "true community", and that this thought should not be read as a fixed dogma.

The article, published in Nanjing Social Sciences in 2023, has three main parts. It first surveys pre-Marxian thought: the "moral community" of Socrates, Plato and Aristotle, the contract community (Augustine, Hobbes, Rousseau), the rational communities of Kant, Hegel and Feuerbach, and utopian socialists such as Saint-Simon, Owen and Fourier. It then reconstructs Marx's own position from early writings to Capital and the Critique of the Gotha Programme. Finally it turns to later developments: Lenin, Western critics, Michael Hardt and Antonio Negri, and the Chinese idea of a community with a shared future for mankind.

The authors identify three structural themes in the earlier tradition: the relation of individual to community, the gradual separation of "community" from "state" (clearest in Kant), and the projection of an ideal society. In their reading, Marx developed the first into two relations and three principles, drawn from his early journalism and philosophy. He treated the capitalist state as an "illusory community" and the "association of free individuals" as the true community. The authors say this involves abolishing private ownership, the withering of the state and free, all-round individual development. Marx's route there is the "re-establishment of individual property" on the basis of cooperation and common possession. The authors also hold that the community/state distinction still needs defending against Fukuyama, Berlin and Hayek, and they criticise Hardt and Negri for stressing political "exodus" while neglecting economic revolution.

The authors argue that the community with a shared future for mankind should not be read as a linear continuation of Marx's true community. In their view it addresses a different level, namely coexistence of different systems in the long period before communism, when Marx allowed the state to persist. They hold that the ultimate aim of abolishing private ownership and building the true community remains the Communists' highest programme. They also call for adapting Marx's thought to changed conditions. Read the original if you want a Chinese scholarly account of how Marx's community concept is positioned against both the Western tradition and the current Chinese diplomatic concept.
quoteEn: It cannot be understood as a linear inheritance of Marx's thought on community in the new era merely because it involves the word "community".
quoteZh: 不能因为其涉及到了“共同体”，就将其理解为马克思共同体思想在新时代的线性继承

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: A foreign-policy and theoretical concept associated with Xi Jinping since around 2012. It advocates cooperation among states with different systems on the basis of shared interests and values.
Marx's term, used in The German Ideology, for a community in which individual freedom is realised, as opposed to the "illusory community" of the bourgeois state.
Chinese rendering of Marx's "association" in which the free development of each is the condition for the free development of all. The authors treat it as equivalent to the true community.
A phrase from Capital, volume 1. It refers to restoring individual property on the basis of cooperation and common possession of the means of production, after the expropriation of the expropriators.

keywords: community with a shared future for mankind

t: Upholding the Marxist standpoint in research on ideology
zh: 坚持意识形态问题研究的马克思主义立场
paras: This short commentary, first published in China Social Sciences Today in December 2022, asks why research on ideology must be conducted from a Marxist standpoint. Shi and Song argue that ideology is vital to the survival of a party, a state and a nation. They hold that a Marxist standpoint supplies both a scientific analytical perspective and a practical necessity for China.

The authors begin with the place of ideology in the history of Marxism. They list classic works, Second International theorists and Western Marxists such as Lukács, Gramsci, the Frankfurt School and Althusser as evidence of its importance. They then trace the Chinese Communist Party's handling of ideological work from the New Democratic Revolution to the period since the 18th Party Congress (2012).

Their central theoretical move concerns Marx's own legacy. Many scholars treat ideological critique as the core of Marx's theory. Shi and Song accept this partly, but say that treating ideology as "false consciousness" is only the logical starting point. In their reading, the deeper purpose is to build a "proletarian system of ideas", so the critical and the functional dimensions together make up the whole doctrine. Their second move is practical: because Marxism is the guiding thought of the Party and the state, ideology research must keep to it.

The authors credit the Party with clarifying ideological confusion through the debate on the criterion of truth and the Four Cardinal Principles. They also credit it with a mature ideological theory in the twenty-first century. Since 2012, they say, the leadership has secured Marxism's guiding position, strengthened responsibility systems for ideological work, and criticised historical nihilism. They conclude that a Marxist standpoint is both extremely important and urgent. Read the original if you want a brief example of how Party-affiliated scholars frame ideology work and its Marxist lineage.
quoteEn: "Critique" is not the only tendency in Marx's doctrine of ideology.
quoteZh: “批判性”并不是马克思意识形态学说的唯一倾向

glossary.explanation: A term used in Party discourse for views that are seen as denying or distorting the Party's history and the revolutionary and socialist record. It has been a frequent target of official campaigns since the 18th Party Congress.
Principles set out by Deng Xiaoping in 1979: keeping to the socialist road, the people's democratic dictatorship, Communist Party leadership, and Marxism-Leninism and Mao Zedong Thought.

glossary.zh: 真理标准问题的大讨论
glossary.pinyin: zhēnlǐ biāozhǔn wèntí de dà tǎolùn
glossary.en: debate on the criterion of truth
glossary.explanation: A 1978 debate which held that practice is the sole criterion of truth. It helped to loosen dogmatic adherence to Mao-era positions and to prepare for reform and opening up.

t: The place of the theory of human development in Marxism
zh: 人的发展理论在马克思主义中的地位
source: Studies on the Marxist Theory Discipline (马克思主义理论学科研究), 2023 no. 3
paras: Chen Xinxia asks what position the theory of human development holds within Marxism as a whole. The article argues that the complete emancipation and free and all-round development of the human being is the core value of Marxism. The theory that expresses this value orientation is, in Chen's account, an important part of Marxism: it rests on Marxism and is generated and developed within it.

The article has three parts. The first shows that the theory of human development is grounded in Marxist philosophy, political economy and scientific socialism. The second argues that human development is the core value running through all three components. The third sets out the theoretical and practical significance of making this position explicit, including for contemporary China.

Chen's central moves are as follows. Philosophically, the practical standpoint and historical materialism define the human subject, the meaning of development and its social conditions. Political economy, through the theory of surplus value, explains why capitalism blocks development and why free time and shorter working hours matter. Scientific socialism supplies the path of emancipation, and Chen treats emancipation as the premise of development: emancipation is the task of revolutionary periods, development that of periods of construction. Chen then argues that Marxism's components are usually seen as unified in their scientific understanding, while their unity of value orientation gets too little attention. Recognising human development as the shared value would confirm Marxism as, in Lenin's phrase, a single 'piece of steel'.

On the practical side, Chen holds that the point strengthens Marxism's capacity to answer deep questions of social life and to guide social progress. In China, where the principal social contradiction has shifted, the article proposes human development as a higher value standard for relating the two problems of unbalanced and inadequate development. Chen argues that inadequate development is addressed through further growth and unbalanced development through adjusting social relations, and that both should be judged by whether they benefit human development. Read the original if you want a systematic, text-based account of how human development links Marxist philosophy, political economy and scientific socialism, and how one Chinese scholar applies it to current policy.
quoteEn: The condition of human development is the fundamental yardstick and ultimate indicator for judging the success or failure of social systems and policies.
quoteZh: 人的发展状况是判定社会制度和政策成败得失的根本尺度和终端显示

glossary.explanation: A strand of Chinese Marxist scholarship that systematises Marx's and Engels's remarks on the free and all-round development of the individual into a theory. It is treated as part of Marxist philosophy and related fields.
Marx's ideal of every individual developing their abilities, relations and personality fully in a communist society. Chinese official discourse treats it as the ultimate goal of socialism.
The term for the socialist doctrine founded by Marx and Engels, set against utopian socialism. In Chinese textbooks it is one of the three components of Marxism.

The Party's official definition of the central problem of the current stage. Since the 19th Party Congress (2017) it has been the contradiction between unbalanced and inadequate development and the people's growing need for a better life.

t: The intellectual sources and original theoretical contributions of the "Two Integrations"
zh: “两个结合”的思想渊源和原创性理论贡献
paras: Jin Minqing asks where the thesis of the Two Integrations came from and what is original about it. The thesis, put forward by Xi Jinping, calls for combining the basic tenets of Marxism with China's specific realities and with fine traditional Chinese culture. Jin argues that it distils a century of Party theoretical innovation, reveals the laws of adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times, and makes an original contribution to that process.

The article has three parts. It first traces the history of attempts to link Marxism with Chinese conditions and culture, from Liang Qichao, Zhu Zhixin and Wang Zichen to Li Dazhao, Cai Hesen, Chen Duxiu and the early Party. It then follows the Party's accumulated experience from Mao Zedong's sinification of Marxism through Deng Xiaoping Theory, the Three Represents and the Scientific Outlook on Development, up to Xi's formulation at the Party's centenary (2021) and the 20th Party Congress (2022). The third part lists the original contributions of the new era.

Jin's central claim is that the two integrations were pursued unevenly. Earlier generations, facing national independence and construction, concentrated on the first integration, while the second was relatively underdeveloped; Mao spoke of a "deep integration" with culture but never turned it into a clear proposition. Jin holds that the new era's historic mission made the second integration especially important. Jin then argues that Xi's theory joins Marxist principles to Chinese tradition at specific points. Marxism's view of the people as makers of history is joined with the minben (people-as-foundation) tradition, and the communist ideal of a "true community" with the ideal of "all under heaven as one family", yielding a community with a shared future for mankind. Marxist views on nature are joined with the unity of heaven and humanity, yielding ecological civilization, and Party purity with traditions of self-examination, yielding the Party's self-reform. Jin also credits Xi with analysis of the contemporary epoch, the "new contradiction" of the new era, Chinese modernization and a Marxist stance toward traditional culture.

Jin concludes that the Two Integrations work in both directions. Marxism takes root in Chinese culture and in popular values, and traditional culture is raised to the level of Marxism through creative transformation and innovative development. Jin presents Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era as the exemplar of this process and as a new leap in adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times. Read the original if you want a detailed, officially aligned account of how Chinese scholars trace the lineage of the Two Integrations from the early twentieth century to Xi's thought.
quoteEn: Through this two-way transformation, the basic tenets of Marxism are linked with fine traditional Chinese culture and merged with the shared values that people live by every day without noticing.
quoteZh: 通过双向转化，马克思主义基本原理同中华优秀传统文化贯通起来，同人民群众日用而不觉的共同价值观念融通起来

glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's formula of combining the basic tenets of Marxism with China's specific realities and with fine traditional Chinese culture. The second integration was stressed in his 2021 centenary speech and at the 20th Party Congress.

glossary.zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化
glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
glossary.explanation: The official phrase for the Party's long-running project of adapting Marxism to Chinese conditions. The term "of our times" was added in recent years.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's concept for international relations and global governance, stressing dialogue, shared development and cooperation.
The Party's term for its own continuous self-correction and discipline. Xi presents it as the second answer to the question of how to escape the historical cycle of rise and fall.
Hu Jintao-era guiding concept stressing people-centred, comprehensive and sustainable development.
Jiang Zemin's theory that the Party represents advanced productive forces, advanced culture and the fundamental interests of the people.
The official name for China's path of modernization, defined at the 20th Party Congress as socialist modernization led by the Party, with features such as a huge population and common prosperity.

t: Displaying the mighty power of the manned spaceflight spirit on the new journey of the new era
zh: 在新时代新征程上彰显载人航天精神的磅礴伟力
paras: This commentary, published in Guangming Daily in April 2023, asks how the spirit forged in China's manned spaceflight programme can serve the Party's central task after the 20th Party Congress (2022). Xu Chuan argues that the manned spaceflight spirit, part of the Party's spiritual lineage that begins with the great founding spirit, will supply strong spiritual power for advancing Chinese modernization.

The article is organised around the four components of the spirit as Xu presents them: being especially able to endure hardship, to fight, to tackle key problems, and to dedicate oneself. Each section follows the same pattern. It first explains how the quality arose in the spaceflight workforce, then traces its roots in Chinese civilisational tradition and the Party's history, and finally says how it should be carried forward in the new era. Xu draws heavily on speeches by Xi Jinping and on classical Chinese verse.

In Xu's account, endurance of hardship came from harsh conditions and a weak technical base, and fighting spirit from the scale and risk of the project. Tackling key problems relied on the nationwide system of concentrated effort, which Xu says filled technological gaps, and dedication meant generations giving up personal interests, even their lives. Xu presents each trait as both a legacy of the Chinese nation and a reflection of the Communist Party leading the people. The author links them to present tasks: young cadres should be tempered at the grassroots and in hard regions, struggle is needed amid mounting risks, key core technologies cannot be bought or begged, and selflessness is needed in a turbulent world.

Xu concludes that these four qualities should be promoted on the new journey, and calls for turning spiritual wealth into inexhaustible material creativity. The piece calls for a new, improved nationwide system for science and technology, for more breakthroughs "from 0 to 1", and for dedication that ties personal development to the country's fate. Read the original if you want an example of how official Chinese commentary links a specific national project to the Party's spiritual lineage and to the goals of Chinese modernization.
quoteEn: The "especially able to endure hardship" of the manned spaceflight spirit means that the more one faces difficulties, risks and challenges, the less one may retreat or yield, and the more one must stir the resolve and courage to overcome, defeat and master hardship.
quoteZh: 载人航天精神中的“特别能吃苦”就是越面对困难、风险、挑战，越不能退缩让步，越要激发克服艰苦、战胜艰苦、驾驭艰苦的决心和勇气。

glossary.explanation: One of the named spirits in the Party's official 'spiritual lineage', summed up as being especially able to endure hardship, fight, tackle key problems and dedicate oneself. It is associated with the Chinese manned space programme.
The official term for China's path to building a modern socialist country, set out as the Party's central task at the 20th Party Congress in 2022.
An approach that mobilises resources across the country for major projects, such as space and key technologies. It is often described in official texts as an institutional advantage.

t: "Human emancipation" in the perspective of community theory
zh: 共同体理论视域中的“人的解放”
paras: Zhao Zixu and Wang Shirun argue that "community" (gongtongti) was long dismissed as an immature element of the early Marx under the influence of the Soviet system of Marxist theory. Reflection on that system, translations of Marxist scholars from abroad, and Xi Jinping's idea of a community with a shared future for mankind, they say, offer a chance to reread the concept. Their thesis is that community runs through Marx's whole thought as a changing category: if "human emancipation" is the theme and aim of Marx's philosophy, community theory is its foundation and guarantee.

The article, first published in the Chinese Social Sciences Today in March 2023, follows Marx's treatment of community through four stages. These are his rejection of Hegel's view in the early writings, the community thinking of the Economic and Philosophic Manuscripts of 1844 and The German Ideology, the historical account of pre-capitalist forms in the Grundrisse manuscripts of Capital, and the "time economy" through which capital prepares the restoration of community. Hegel, Feuerbach, Aristotle, Kant and Gramsci appear as reference points.

The authors read Marx's development as a triad of thesis, antithesis and synthesis. In the 1844 Manuscripts, they say, the unalienated "species life" is lost through private property and alienated labour, and communism as community restores it. The German Ideology supplies the "false community" (antithesis) and the "true community" (synthesis) but leaves the thesis missing. The authors hold that the Grundrisse fills this gap with the "original community", in which labour and ownership are undivided. They describe Marx's three forms of ownership (Asiatic, ancient, Germanic) and argue that only the Germanic form, resting on individual ownership, contained the conditions for free labour and wage labour.

Once civil society emerged and the world market formed, the authors say, capital seemed to make emancipation impossible. They contend, however, that Capital shows capital's civilising role: by creating surplus labour and shortening necessary labour, it makes possible a "time economy" under workers' own control, which supports the return of community. They conclude that Marx's vision of community will be realised in the move from theory to reality, and they link this to Xi Jinping's idea of a community with a shared future for mankind. Read the original if you want a concise Chinese account of how community underpins Marx's idea of emancipation, from Hegel's critique to the Grundrisse.
quoteEn: If "human emancipation" is the theme and aim of Marx's philosophy, then the theory of "community" is the solid foundation and guarantee for achieving that aim.
quoteZh: 如果说“人的解放”是马克思哲学的主题和目的，那么“共同体”理论则是其实现这个目的的坚实基石与保证。

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: A foreign-policy and theoretical concept promoted by Xi Jinping since around 2012–2013. It calls for countries to share interests and responsibilities in global affairs.
The term used to translate the German Gemeinschaft and related concepts in Marx. In the article it covers forms of collective life from the original community to the communist association.

t: The historical-materialist foundations of Marx's thought on the "real community"
zh: 马克思“真正的共同体”思想的唯物史观基础
paras: Sang Mingxu asks how Marx's idea of the "real community" ("true community", 真正的共同体) should be understood and used.
