The article, a short piece first published in the China Social Sciences Today in March 2023, argues that the idea did not arrive as a finished scientific theory. In Sang's account it passed from a humanist (anthropological) position to historical materialism, and only the later, historical-materialist formulations should serve as the main basis for research.

The article follows the concept through three texts. It begins with the 1844 critique of "The King of Prussia and Social Reform", then turns to The German Ideology, and finally to the 1857–58 manuscripts (the Grundrisse). It then sets out eight features of the real community as Marx developed it on a historical-materialist basis. The last section draws out three implications for present-day theory and practice.

Sang reads the 1844 formulation, "the essence of man is the true community of man", as a humanist proposition shaped by Feuerbach's influence. It defines human essence abstractly, apart from concrete social relations. In The German Ideology the real community is contrasted with the illusory communities of the past, which rest on the division of labour and private property. It presupposes highly developed productive forces, universal intercourse and the disappearance of private property and the division of labour. In the Grundrisse Marx ironically calls money and capital the inverted "community" of capitalism. Sang's eight features cover the community's definition, its historical position beyond the capitalist mode of production, its characteristics, its subjects (real individuals), its inner principle (free association), its ownership basis (individual ownership rebuilt on common possession of the means of production), its dialectical structure and its means of realisation.

Sang distinguishes the real community from a community with a shared future for mankind. In Sang's account the latter is a global community of development that stands on this side of capitalism, with nation-states as its subjects and a mixed global ownership structure, while the former is its long-term goal. For building contemporary communities, such as communities of social governance, Sang proposes four principles: realism, dialectics, historicity and agency. Sang warns that citing Marx's humanist-stage statements as the main evidence weakens Marxism's explanatory power. Read the original if you want a compact, text-based outline of how Marx's concept changed and how a Chinese scholar links it to the community with a shared future for mankind.
quoteEn: The "real community" is not an abstract human essence or an abstract generic community; it transcends all the false and illusory communities of the past and is the community of the future communist society.
quoteZh: “真正的共同体”不是抽象的人的本质，不是抽象的类共同体，它超越了过去一切虚假共同体、虚幻共同体，是未来共产主义社会的共同体。

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: A foreign-policy and theoretical concept promoted by Xi Jinping since around 2012–13. It calls for shared development, common interests and common values among countries.

Marx's term for the future communal form in which individuals freely associate, in contrast to earlier "false" or "illusory" communities based on class division and private property. It is also rendered "true community".

The Marxist theory that holds that history develops through changes in material production, productive forces and social relations. The article treats it as the scientific turning point in Marx's thought.
A term in recent Chinese Party and government discourse for a collaborative model of social governance in which many actors take part in building and sharing governance.

keywords: community with a shared future for mankind

t: Adhering more consciously to the Two Integrations as the fundamental path for adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
zh: 更加自觉地坚持“两个结合”推进马克思主义中国化时代化的根本途径
paras: This short commentary, published in the People's Daily on 22 March 2023, takes up a question raised by Xi Jinping's report to the 20th Party Congress (2022): by what path is adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times to be advanced? Liu Dehai answers that the fundamental path is the Two Integrations, meaning the combination of Marxism's basic principles with China's concrete realities and with excellent traditional Chinese culture. Liu presents this as the reason the tree of sinicised Marxist theory is deeply rooted and leafy.

The piece is organised in three sections. The first treats the Two Integrations as a summing-up of experience and a revealed regularity in the Party's history of more than a century. The second turns to the new era, and the third to what the Party must do on its new journey.

Liu argues that Marxism is a guide to action rather than a dogma, and that the Party's rejuvenation path grew from drawing on both China's realities and its traditional culture. In Liu's account, Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era was formed through the Two Integrations. Liu describes it as contemporary Chinese Marxism and twenty-first-century Marxism, and as a new leap in adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times.

Liu calls for more conscious adherence to the Two Integrations, so as to produce theoretical innovation on the basis of practice. This means answering new practical problems, deep-seated issues and pressing public concerns. It also means promoting the creative transformation and innovative development of traditional culture, and linking Marxism with the values of ordinary people. Read the original if you want a concise, official-style statement of how the Two Integrations were presented in the press after the 20th Party Congress.
quoteEn: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era was formed through adherence to the Two Integrations; it is contemporary Chinese Marxism and twenty-first-century Marxism, the essence of Chinese culture and the Chinese spirit for our times, and it has achieved a new leap in adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times.
quoteZh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想是在坚持“两个结合”中形成的，是当代中国马克思主义、二十一世纪马克思主义，是中华文化和中国精神的时代精华，实现了马克思主义中国化时代化新的飞跃。

glossary.explanation: The principle of combining the basic tenets of Marxism with China's concrete realities and with excellent traditional Chinese culture. The second integration was added to the Party's formula in 2021–22 and written into the 20th Party Congress report.

glossary.zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化
glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
glossary.literal: the sinicisation and modernisation (timeliness) of Marxism
glossary.explanation: The Party's official formula for developing Marxist theory in line with Chinese conditions and the demands of the era. The 20th Party Congress report added the 'times' element to the older 'sinicisation' formula.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018.

t: A deeper understanding of "ultimately, it is Marxism that works — Marxism adapted to the Chinese context and the needs of our times"
zh: 深刻理解“归根到底是马克思主义行，是中国化时代化的马克思主义行”
paras: This commentary, first published in Guangming Daily in March 2023, interprets a formulation from the report to the 20th Party Congress (2022): why the Communist Party of China "can", why socialism with Chinese characteristics is "good", and why, ultimately, "Marxism works", specifically Marxism adapted to the Chinese context and the needs of our times. Bai argues that the three claims form a dialectical chain and that the formulation expresses the internal logic and historical necessity of adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times.

The article is organised in four numbered sections. The first draws out the basic Marxist principles contained in the formulation. The second presents it as the historical wisdom of the Party's century of struggle. The third sets out the fundamental route by which Marxism takes effect, and the fourth outlines directions for Party-building and the cause of socialism with Chinese characteristics in the new era.

Bai's central reasoning rests on three claims about theory and practice. Theory guides practice, so Marxism is fundamental to the Party's revolution, construction and reform. Its value is realised only in concrete, historical conditions, so what actually guided the Chinese revolution, in Bai's account, was not dogmatic, book-bound Marxism but a Marxism that had been adapted to China. Marxism also does not "work" spontaneously: it needs the Communist Party as its practical agent, the integration of its basic principles with China's realities and fine traditional culture, and mastery by the people. Bai accordingly states three conditions: Marxism must be applied in practice, localised and updated, and taken up by the masses. The author also reads the Party's century of struggle as a unity of theoretical innovation, Party leadership and the Chinese path.

Bai concludes that the new era requires firm theoretical confidence, strengthening the Party through theory, and a stronger conscious commitment to applying Marxism to major practical problems. The author calls for arming the whole Party with the latest results of Marxism, and for using the worldview and methodology of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era to pursue Chinese modernization and the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. Read the original if you want a concise example of how official Party commentary explains the link between Marxism, Party leadership and the Chinese path after the 20th Party Congress.
quoteEn: Marxism can "work" only if it is localised and keeps pace with the times.
quoteZh: 马克思主义只有实现本土化时代化才能“行”。

glossary.zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化
glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
glossary.literal: Sinicisation and modernisation (of the age) of Marxism
glossary.explanation: The official formula for fitting Marxist principles to China's conditions and to each new historical period. The 20th Party Congress added the "needs of our times" element to the older idea of Sinicising Marxism.
The Party's official term for China's own path to modernisation, which it presents as distinct from Western models. It was given prominence in the report to the 20th Party Congress.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018. It is presented as the latest stage of adapting Marxism to China.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A long-standing official goal of restoring China's national strength and international standing, closely tied to the Chinese Dream and the "second centenary goal" of 2049.
The official name for the Party's model of socialism since reform and opening up. It combines Party leadership and public ownership with market mechanisms.

keywords: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context

t: The worldview and methodological significance of adhering to systems thinking
zh: 坚持系统观念的世界观和方法论意义
paras: This commentary, first published in Guangming Daily in February 2023, starts from the report to the 20th Party Congress (2022), which says the Party must adhere to systems thinking (系统观念). Yang Hongyuan asks how this idea should be understood and used to guide the work of the Party and state. The answer is that systems thinking is both a worldview and a method, and that the Marxist classics help to explain it.

The piece has three parts. The first traces the idea in Marx, Engels and Lenin. The second shows how the Chinese Communist Party has applied it, from Mao Zedong to the period since the 18th Party Congress (2012). The third takes up current conditions and the demands they place on systems thinking.

Yang argues that dialectical materialism treats the material world as universally connected, so that every thing is an organic whole, or system. In Yang's account, Marx's idea of the organic system and his analysis of bourgeois society in Capital, and Engels's use of the concept of system in his writings on nature, are foundational, and Lenin summarised the method. Yang holds that making systems thinking part of the worldview and methodology of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era is an original contribution to Marxism. It is linked to strategic, historical, dialectical, innovative, rule-of-law and bottom-line thinking.

Yang concludes that, given the strategic opportunities and risks at home and abroad, systems thinking is needed to advance high-quality development and Chinese modernization. Yang calls for balancing domestic and international affairs, development and security, central and local initiative, and the short and long term. Read the original if you want a concise, official-register account of how Party theorists ground systems thinking in Marx and Engels.
quoteEn: Systems thinking is both a fundamental view of how the objective world exists and an important method for understanding and transforming the external world, embodying the organic unity of worldview and methodology.
quoteZh: 系统观念既是对于客观世界存在方式的根本看法，又是认识和改造外部世界的重要方法，体现着世界观与方法论的有机统一。

glossary.explanation: A principle stressing that things are interconnected wholes and should be handled comprehensively. The 20th Party Congress report (2022) listed it among the guiding principles for the Party's work.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party constitution in 2017 and the state constitution in 2018.
The official name for China's path to modernization, set out by the 20th Party Congress (2022) as distinct from Western models.
An official goal, in place since about 2017, that moves the economy from speed and scale towards quality, innovation and balance.

t: Chinese modernization raises human civilization to a higher dimension and level
zh: 中国式现代化促进人类文明升维提级
paras: Taking Xi Jinping's speech at the study session on the spirit of the 20th Party Congress (2022) as its starting point, this short commentary, published in the China Social Sciences Today in March 2023, asks what Chinese modernization means beyond China. Liu argues that its proposal, its successful advance and the first construction of its theoretical system mark a step up in dimension and level (shengwei tiji) on three fronts: in Chinese civilization's understanding of itself, in the world concept of modernization, and in human thinking. Liu expects these to lead in practice to a similar step up in the form of human civilization.

The piece first reviews the paradigm that has governed Chinese self-understanding since the mid-nineteenth century, then turns to each of the three upgrades in turn. It draws on classical Chinese sources (the Book of Songs, the Analects, Zhou Dunyi) and sets Western critiques of modernity, from postmodernity to multiple modernities, against Chinese experience. It closes with a reflection on Hegel's and Fukuyama's views of history.

Liu describes the old paradigm as 'modernization equals Westernization': China learned first techniques, then institutions, then ideas, in a process assumed to follow a single line with the West ahead. In this account the more closely China imitated the West, the more it lost itself. Chinese modernization, Liu argues, breaks this myth by showing world history as simultaneous advance at many points, and recasts China's modern renewal as an interaction of Western and Chinese civilizations that produces a new civilization that is both Chinese and universal. Western thinkers have criticised Eurocentric modernity but, Liu says, they seldom recognise a Chinese form as independent and in some respects pointing to the future. As an example Liu cites harmony between humanity and nature, which Liu sets against a Western faith in conquering nature, drawing on the Chinese debate on heaven and humanity. On thinking, Liu invokes the idea of the unity of substance and function (ti-yong buer) to argue that no single universal standard of modernization exists apart from its varied concrete forms.

Liu concludes that Chinese civilization should take on, with confidence, the mission of bringing forth a new form of human civilization. This requires creative transformation of tradition rooted in living practice. Liu holds that history has neither been completed in Prussia nor ended in the West, and that people everywhere will take part in making it. Read the original if you want a compact example of how Chinese scholars present Chinese modernization as a philosophical and civilizational claim with world significance.
quoteEn: Chinese modernization breaks the myth that 'modernization equals Westernization' and presents another picture of modernization: world history does not advance along a single line through time, but moves forward simultaneously at many points.
quoteZh: 中国式现代化打破了“现代化=西方化”的迷思，展现了现代化的另一幅图景：世界历史并非单线历时演进，而是多点共时并进。

glossary.explanation: The official name for the Party's account of China's path to modernity, given prominence at the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is presented as distinct from Western models and as having world significance.

glossary.en: step up in dimension and level
glossary.explanation: The author's phrase for a qualitative advance in how something is understood or organised. It is used here for civilization, the concept of modernization and human thinking.

glossary.literal: substance and function are not two
glossary.explanation: A concept from Chinese philosophy holding that underlying principle (ti) and concrete manifestation (yong) are inseparable. The author uses it to argue that a general idea of modernization exists only in its varied concrete forms.

t: The historical logic of "daring to struggle and being good at struggle" and its contemporary value
zh: “敢于斗争、善于斗争”的历史逻辑及其当代价值
paras: Writing in 2023, shortly after the 20th Party Congress (2022), Xiao Guiqing and Liu Jiarong take up the injunction in Xi Jinping's report that the whole Party must "dare to struggle and be good at struggle". The article argues that this principle is a consistent historical logic running through the Communist Party's first century, and that it remains a guiding requirement for building a modern socialist country and reaching the second centenary goal.

The article moves chronologically. It first reviews the Party's experience in the new-democratic revolution, in socialist revolution and construction, and in the reform period. It then turns to the "great struggle" of the new era since the 18th Party Congress (2012), covering its meaning, its "new historical characteristics" and its achievements. A final section looks ahead to the new journey towards the second centenary goal.

The authors' central move is to split the principle into two parts: daring to struggle is a matter of courage and spiritual drive, while being good at struggle is an art of strategy. Drawing on Mao Zedong, they cite the policy of "both unity and struggle" and the criteria of being justified, advantageous and restrained, and on Deng Xiaoping the strategy of "hiding our capabilities and biding our time", which they say did not mean abandoning struggle on core interests. For the new era, they present Xi's view that struggle must keep to the leadership of the Party and the socialist system, and that it spans political, economic, cultural, social and ecological security. They credit it with the Party's centenary, the entry of socialism with Chinese characteristics into a new era, and poverty alleviation. They describe the external environment as marked by Western containment, trade and technology wars, and a US that they say will not tolerate Chinese modernization.

The authors conclude that the second centenary goal will be accompanied by long and complex struggles, and that the key lies in the Party and in its cadres. They call for cultivating a fighting spirit, strengthening fighting skills through ideological, political and practical training, and holding the initiative in struggle, while stressing that the Party has no wish to make enemies. Read the original if you want a representative example of how Party-affiliated scholars after the 20th Party Congress trace the concept of struggle through Party history and apply it to current domestic and international tasks.
quoteEn: Daring to struggle is a form of courage; being good at struggle is an art.
quoteZh: 敢于斗争是一种勇气，善于斗争则是一门艺术。

glossary.en: dare to struggle and be good at struggle
glossary.explanation: A formula stressed in Xi Jinping's report to the 20th Party Congress as one of three things the whole Party must uphold. It pairs willingness to confront challenges with skill in strategy and tactics.

A concept introduced at the 18th Party Congress in 2012, which spoke of preparing for a great struggle with many new historical characteristics. Xi Jinping links it with the great dream, great cause and great project of Party building.

glossary.en: hiding our capabilities and biding our time
glossary.explanation: A foreign policy approach associated with Deng Xiaoping after 1989, which counselled a low profile and concentration on development. The authors read it as a strategy of struggle, not its abandonment.
The aim of building a modern socialist country by the centenary of the People's Republic in 2049. The first centenary goal, a moderately prosperous society, was declared achieved in 2021.
The official name for China's path to modernization, set out prominently at the 20th Party Congress. It is presented as distinct from Western models.

t: The purpose and significance of Marx's "commentary on Greek art"
zh: 马克思“希腊艺术评论”的目的和意义
paras: Marx's well-known remarks on Greek art in the Introduction to A Contribution to the Critique of Political Economy have usually been read within aesthetics and art studies. Zhou and Zhou argue that their purpose and significance go well beyond this. In the authors' view, the commentary is a large-scale social theory about the future direction of human society and the ideal mode of human existence and development.

The short piece, first published in the Chinese Social Sciences Today in 2023, reads the commentary through its textual structure and logic of argument. It takes up the several "difficult problems" Marx names and draws out their methodological meaning. It treats Greek art, Greek myth, the critique of capitalist production and Marx's late turn to anthropology and history in turn.

The authors make three moves. First, Marx insists on rising "from the abstract to the concrete": the general principle that material production determines spiritual production is not enough, and Greek art must be tied to Greek myth and to the conditions of low productive forces. Once nature is actually mastered, myth disappears, so Greek art's decline in modern society is unavoidable and imitation of it is bound to fail. Second, the commentary is part of Marx's critique of capitalism. The authors say it refutes the bourgeois belief that material and artistic production advance in balance, and shows that capitalist production, which seeks exchange value, is hostile to art as free spiritual production. Third, studying ancient society offers a "prototype" for predicting modern trends.

The authors conclude that Marx answers the puzzle of Greek art's "eternal charm" by turning an artistic question into one of social development. For them, Greek society, as humanity's childhood, serves as a "norm" and "model". Its simple original relation between humans, nature and society, its "natural individuality" and its imaginative power still instruct modern people. Read the original if you want a concise argument for treating Marx's remarks on Greek art as social theory and not only as aesthetics.
quoteEn: Marx's main purpose in commenting on Greek art lies not in Greek art itself or in the development of art in general, but in using that commentary to reveal the "unequal relation between the development of material production and that of art".
quoteZh: 马克思评论希腊艺术的主要目的不在于希腊艺术本身或一般艺术发展问题，而是试图通过对希腊艺术的评论，揭示“物质生产的发展同艺术发展的不平衡关系”。

t: Whole-process people's democracy: the unity of discursive construction and practical path
zh: 全过程人民民主：话语建构与实践路径的统一
paras: Chen Chengxin asks what distinguishes whole-process people's democracy from other democratic forms and answers that its main comparative advantage is the unity of democratic discourse and democratic practice. In Chen's account it is a democracy in which words and deeds agree. The piece first appeared in the China Social Sciences Today newspaper in February 2023, and the author attributes this unity to three constants: a people-centred logical starting point, the running of people's democracy through every stage of political life, and Party leadership as the fundamental guarantee.

The commentary has three parts. The first treats the people-centred starting point, the second the comparative advantages of whole-process people's democracy, and the third the Party leadership that Chen presents as its basic guarantee. Chen draws on the Constitution, the revised Organic Law of the National People's Congress, the basic political institutions, and examples of recent democratic innovation such as NPC oversight and the People's Daily Online "message board for leaders".

Chen argues that "the people" in this democracy is a systemic "all-subject" concept that includes respect for individual rights but unifies them within the whole people. The author also stresses coverage of "all domains", from the struggle for independence to poverty alleviation and Chinese modernization. Compared with electoral democracy, which Chen portrays as a formal system of "one election decides all", the author presents whole-process people's democracy as resting on two kinds of completeness: complete institutional procedures and complete participatory practice, the latter described as covering the whole chain, all fields and the whole process. It is oriented towards whether problems are effectively solved rather than towards votes alone, and Chen says it applies consultation, supervision and public input throughout decision-making and an official's whole term.

Chen concludes that Party leadership secures the direction, order and efficiency of this democracy, through institutional mechanisms, the mass line, rule of law and consultative governance. In this reading, the Party both constructs the democratic discourse and leads its practice, and people's evaluation is the standard by which discourse is tested against practice. Chen adds a caution that "whole process" applies within a given context and scope, so the discourse has boundaries and operating limits. Read the original if you want a concise statement of how Chinese scholars present the comparative case for whole-process people's democracy against electoral democracy.
quoteEn: Whole-process people's democracy is not oriented solely towards \"votes\" but towards results, namely \"whether problems can be effectively solved\".
quoteZh: 全过程人民民主不以“选票”为唯一导向，而以“是否能够有效解决问题”为实绩导向。

glossary.explanation: A concept put forward by Xi Jinping in 2019 and developed in later Party documents. It describes the Chinese political system as democratic across all stages of political life, not only at elections.

glossary.literal: taking the people as the centre
glossary.explanation: A guiding principle of Party discourse under Xi Jinping, holding that governance and development should serve the people's fundamental interests.
A Party working method, associated with Mao Zedong, of drawing on the views of the masses and returning them as policy, and of staying in close contact with the people.
The Party's official term for China's own path to modernization, prominent since the 20th Party Congress (2022).

t: The civilisational implications of the Communist Manifesto
zh: 《共产党宣言》的文明意蕴
paras: Wang Jing reads the Communist Manifesto, the programmatic document marking the public emergence of Marxism, through the lens of civilisation. The short piece, first published in the China Social Sciences Today in February 2023, argues that the Manifesto applies historical materialism to reveal both the historical significance and the inherent defects of modern capitalist civilisation, and to explain why humanity must move on to a new communist civilisation. In Wang's formulation, the text is at once a critique of modern capitalist civilisation and a manifesto for a new communist one.

The article has two main sections. The first, on the Manifesto as a critique of capitalist civilisation, sets out what Marx and Engels credit to the bourgeoisie and then the contradictions they trace to capital. The second, on the Manifesto as a declaration of a new civilisation, draws chiefly on the third part of the Manifesto, on socialist and communist literature, and on its account of the communist future.

Wang argues that Marx and Engels recognised the bourgeoisie's revolutionary role: the expansion of productive forces, the replacement of feudal and patriarchal ties by wage-labour relations, and the creation of a world market and world history. The defects, Wang says, stem from the logic of capital's self-valorisation, which produces three imbalances: unequal social standing between bourgeoisie and proletariat, uneven development between nations, and strained relations between humans and nature. Wang then explains that the Manifesto rejects reactionary, conservative and critical-utopian socialisms as not genuinely communist, because they leave the relation of capital and wage labour intact or refuse revolutionary action.

Wang concludes that, for Marx and Engels, communist civilisation is a sublation of capitalist civilisation: it must absorb capitalism's positive achievements while overcoming its defects. It abolishes bourgeois property rather than property in general, reverses the rule of the past over the present, and ends the subordination of living labour to accumulated labour. Wang adds that, in the Manifesto's account, this requires a communist revolution that breaks radically with traditional property relations and leads to an association in which the free development of each is the condition for the free development of all. Read the original if you want a concise Chinese statement of how the Manifesto can be read as a theory of civilisation, in the context of official discussion of civilisation.
quoteEn: It can be said that the Manifesto is both a critique of modern capitalist civilisation and a declaration of a new communist civilisation.
quoteZh: 可以说，《宣言》既是一部现代资本主义文明的批判书，又是一部共产主义新文明的宣言书。

glossary.explanation: The Chinese rendering of Hegel's and Marx's Aufhebung: a transition that cancels a prior form while retaining and elevating its positive elements.

t: The problem consciousness and theoretical tensions of classical Western Marxism
zh: 经典西方马克思主义的问题意识与理论张力
paras: Gao Xiaoxi, in a short piece first published in China Social Sciences Today in January 2023, asks what questions drove classical Western Marxism, the current running from Lukács to Althusser between the 1920s and 1960s, and what tensions it left behind. Gao argues that its problem consciousness grew out of the dispute over how to make socialist revolution in advanced capitalist countries, and that this dispute took the form of a rethinking of the nature of Marx's philosophy.

The piece first sets out the conditions of twentieth-century capitalism: oligopoly, a divided working class including a "labour aristocracy", and a shift from direct repression to ideological control through consumerism and mass culture. It then contrasts classical Western Marxism with the Second International, divides the tradition into humanist and scientistic camps, and traces its afterlife in later foreign Marxism.

Gao contends that the Second International read Marxism as determinism, treating historical laws like statistical natural laws and falling into dogmatism. Classical Western Marxists, in Gao's account, instead took Marx's philosophy as a subject-centred theory of practice and urged a revolution grounded in cultural and psychological change and class consciousness. The tension lay in uniting ideological critique with revolutionary practice, which Gao says exposed subjectivist and romantic tendencies. Humanists such as Lukács, Korsch, Gramsci and the Frankfurt School followed Hegelian elements in Marx; Althusser's structuralism, with its "theoretical anti-humanism", is judged to have lapsed into theoretical monologue.

Gao concludes that ecological Marxism, post-Marxism and later Marxist themes such as space and the body descend from this problem consciousness, and that foreign Marxism can be read through paired tensions such as history–structure and time–space. Without grasping this, Gao warns, one may misjudge the history of Western Marxism and weaken the contemporary and global outlook of sinicized Marxism. Read the original if you want a compact Chinese overview of how classical Western Marxism is positioned within the wider field of foreign Marxism.
quoteEn: Classical Western Marxism occupies an important place in the theoretical map of foreign Marxism.
quoteZh: 经典西方马克思主义在国外马克思主义理论版图中占据重要位置。

glossary.explanation: The tradition running from Lukács, Korsch and Gramsci through the Frankfurt School to Althusser, centred on culture, ideology and philosophy. Chinese scholars treat it as one part of the broader field of foreign Marxism.
The Chinese academic label for all Marxist currents outside China, broader than Western Marxism.
Marxism adapted to Chinese conditions, as developed in Chinese Party theory since Mao Zedong.

t: The new form of human civilization as a continuation and innovation of Marx and Engels's theory of civilization
st: An analysis from the perspective of world history
zh: 人类文明新形态对马克思恩格斯文明理论的守正创新
zhSub: 基于世界历史视域的分析
paras: Liu Hao asks how the "new form of human civilization" created through Chinese modernization relates to the theory of civilization that Marx and Engels developed in the nineteenth century from a world-historical perspective. The article argues that the Communist Party of China has both preserved the core of that theory and innovated on it, and that this is visible in three areas: historical trend, path of development and mode of interaction between peoples. The author presents this as opening a new chapter of Marxist civilization theory.

The article is organised in three parts that follow these three areas. The first treats the historical trend from capitalist to socialist civilization and the Chinese case. The second takes up Marx's late idea of bypassing the "Caudine Forks" of capitalism and Chinese modernization as a distinct path. The third examines Marx's idea of the "meeting of extremes" in his writing on the Taiping rebellion and the proposal of a community with a shared future for mankind. Liu closes with a summary of the significance of these contributions.

In the first part, Liu reads Marx and Engels as showing the dual character of capitalist civilization: historically progressive, yet trapped in contradictions rooted in capital, so that socialist civilization must replace it. The author contends that the new form of civilization puts "the people first" against capitalism's primacy of capital, and that, by combining public ownership as the main body with a socialist market economy, it governs capital without abolishing it, something Marx and Engels did not address. In the second part, Liu argues that Marx's late writings reject a linear view of history and allow backward countries distinct paths, which Chinese modernization is said to confirm and extend by showing how to consolidate socialism after such a leap. In the third part, Liu holds that Marx foresaw China as one pole of world history, and that a community with a shared future for mankind and the Belt and Road Initiative turn this antagonistic interaction into mutual benefit and replace the claimed superiority of Western civilization with coexistence.

Liu concludes that the new form of civilization answers the questions of where socialism and socialist civilization are heading, and points a direction for how human civilization should be built. The author presents it as altering the pattern of world development and as carrying universal world-historical significance. Read the original if you want to see how a Chinese academic frames current Party theory as a continuation of Marx and Engels's writings on civilization, world history and the East–West relationship.
quoteEn: The community with a shared future for mankind, as a creative application and development of Marx's dialectical idea of the "meeting of extremes", is the Chinese wisdom that Chinese communists, by rationally grasping the general trend of world development, contribute to the sustainable development of human civilization.
quoteZh: 人类命运共同体作为马克思“两极相联”辩证思想的创造性运用与发展，是中国共产党人理性把握世界发展大势，为推动人类文明可持续发展贡献的中国智慧

glossary.explanation: A concept used in Party theory, notably in Xi Jinping's 2021 speech marking the Party's centenary, for the civilization said to arise from Chinese modernization and socialism with Chinese characteristics.
The official name for China's path to modernization, set out at the 20th Party Congress (2022) with a list of defining features.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: A foreign-policy and global-governance concept promoted by Xi Jinping since 2012–13, stressing interdependence, cooperation and mutual benefit among states.
An infrastructure and economic cooperation initiative launched by Xi Jinping in 2013, linking China with countries across Eurasia, Africa and beyond.

keywords: community with a shared future for mankind

t: The Western tradition, core orientation and intellectual effects of Marx's thought on community
zh: 马克思共同体思想的西方传统、核心指向与思想效应
paras: Marx never defined "community" (Gemeinschaft, Gemeinwesen) explicitly, and his remarks on it are scattered across his works. Shen and Ding ask how his thought on community grew out of the Western tradition, what its core is, and how it should be read today. They argue that Marx sublated earlier Western ideas of community, and that his idea of a "true community" is a scientific theory but not a fixed dogma. It has to be developed in step with changing historical conditions.

The article has three main parts. The first surveys pre-Marxian Western thought: the moral community of Socrates, Plato and Aristotle, the contract communities from Augustine and Hobbes to Rousseau, the rational communities of Kant (right), Hegel (ethical life) and Feuerbach (love), and the utopian socialists Saint-Simon, Owen and Fourier. The second reconstructs Marx's own account from his early journalism to Capital and the Critique of the Gotha Programme. The third follows later developments: Lenin on the state, Western critics such as Hayek, Hardt and Negri's "multitude", and the idea of a community with a shared future for mankind.

Shen and Ding identify three persistent themes in the tradition: the relation of individual to community, the gradual separation of "community" from "state", and the anticipation of an ideal society. Marx, in their account, turns the first into two relations (individual and whole, self-consciousness and universal consciousness) and three principles (freedom, unity of collective and private interest, human emancipation beyond political emancipation). He treats the capitalist state as an "illusory community" and the "association of free individuals" as the true one. He proposes to reach it by abolishing bourgeois private property and "re-establishing individual property". The authors judge Hardt and Negri's call for the multitude to "exit" capital and state to be right about capitalism's property form but without an economic basis. They also argue that the community with a shared future for mankind, part of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, is not a linear development of Marx's true community. In their view it answers a different question: coexistence among states and systems in a long period before communism, when Marx allowed the state to persist.

The authors conclude that the true community will be realised only in a future communist society. Until then, Marx's thought offers resources for handling individual-community relations, coexistence between differing systems and ideologies, and the question of ownership reform grounded in the productive forces. They warn that merging the two ideas would undermine the scientific character of Marxism. Read the original if you want a systematic Chinese-language account of how Marx's community concept is placed within Western intellectual history and how it is distinguished from the community with a shared future for mankind.
quoteEn: It cannot be understood as a linear inheritance of Marx's thought on community in the new era merely because it involves the word "community".
quoteZh: 不能因为其涉及到了“共同体”，就将其理解为马克思共同体思想在新时代的线性继承

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: A foreign-policy and theoretical concept associated with Xi Jinping since 2012–13. It stresses interdependence and cooperation among countries regardless of social system.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The official name of the Party's guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018.
Marx's term, from the Communist Manifesto, for the future communist society. The article treats it as his "true community".
Marx's contrast, in The German Ideology, with the "illusory community" of the state. The measure of a true community is the realisation of individual freedom.
A formula from Capital, vol. I. It refers to restoring individual property on the basis of cooperation and common possession of land and means of production after capitalism.

keywords: community with a shared future for mankind

t: Upholding the Marxist standpoint in the study of ideology
zh: 坚持意识形态问题研究的马克思主义立场
paras: This short commentary, first published in the China Social Sciences Today in December 2022, argues that research on ideology must keep to a Marxist standpoint. Shi and Song hold that ideology is vital to the survival and development of a party, a state and a nation, and that it occupies a central place in the whole history of Marxism.

The authors first survey the classical texts and later thinkers in which ideology is discussed, from The German Ideology, the Communist Manifesto and Capital to the Second International theorists, Western Marxism (Lukács, Gramsci, the Frankfurt School) and Althusser. They then turn to the Chinese Communist Party's own record on ideological work, from the new-democratic revolution through the reform era to the period after the 18th Party Congress (2012).

Their central claim is that ideology has two sides in Marx. Critique of ideology as "false consciousness" is, in their account, only the logical starting point, shaped by Marx's materialist reworking of Kant's critical philosophy and by the needs of proletarian struggle. The more important purpose is a "functional" one: to build an ideological system for the proletariat. Together, critique and function make up what the authors call Marx's "ideological legacy".

On the practical side, Shi and Song say Marxism is the guiding ideology on which the Party and state were founded. They credit the Party with reaching a mature ideological theory and, since 2012, with strengthening Marxism's guiding position, criticising "historical nihilism" and promoting core socialist values. They conclude that studying ideology from a Marxist standpoint is both extremely important and urgent. Read the original if you want a concise statement of the official Chinese view of how Marx's theory of ideology links to current ideological work.
quoteEn: In fact, treating ideology as an object of critique and defining it as "false consciousness" or "inverted ideology" is only the logical starting point of building Marxist ideological theory; there is a more important aspect, namely that ideology also has "functional" value.
quoteZh: 实际上，把意识形态作为批判的对象，定义为“虚假的意识”或“颠倒的意识形态”，这只是马克思主义意识形态理论建构的逻辑起点，还有更为重要的一个方面，那就是意识形态还具有“功能性”价值。

glossary.explanation: A term used in Party discourse for views that are seen as denying or distorting the Party's revolutionary history and socialist achievements. It is mainly used in official campaigns on ideological work.
A set of 24 characters in twelve values, at national, social and individual levels, promoted by the Party since the 18th Party Congress (2012) as the basis of cultural and ideological work.

t: Several features of how Gongjin spread Marxism
zh: 《共进》传播马克思主义的若干特点
paras: Gongjin (Advancing Together) was one of the earliest progressive periodicals to spread Marxism in Shaanxi province. The authors ask how it did so and identify five characteristics of its dissemination work. Originally a magazine that reported popular suffering and attacked warlord rule, it turned towards Marxism in June 1922, when its 17th issue carried the Chinese Communist Party's statement on the political situation.

The short article, first published in the Chinese Social Sciences Today in February 2023, belongs to the history of Marxism in China. It works through the five features in turn, citing individual articles and issue numbers from the journal as evidence.

The first two features concern interaction. Gongjin answered letters from young intellectuals on questions such as gradualism versus radicalism and the Kuomintang–Communist cooperation, and it worked alongside other red periodicals, notably Gongxian, run by Shaanxi students away from the province. It also reprinted pieces on the October Revolution and Lenin from New Youth, The Guide and China Youth. The next two features concern occasions and topics. The journal used anniversaries of the October Revolution, Marx's birth and Lenin's death to explain class struggle, surplus value and the Communist Manifesto, and it commented on local issues, such as a warlord's massacre of peasants in Xingping, to argue for national revolution with peasants as its main force.

The fifth feature, according to the authors, was adjusting content to readers. Articles for progressive youth and educators gave theoretical argument on surplus value and Leninist imperialism theory. Pieces for ordinary readers used plain language, for example a simplified five-stage account of social development. The authors present these methods as the reason Gongjin advanced Marxism in Shaanxi. Read the original if you want a concise, source-based account of early Marxist propaganda in a regional Chinese periodical.
quoteEn: Gongjin had a wide readership, whose theoretical level and cultural education varied widely.
quoteZh: 《共进》的读者群体广泛，理论水平和文化素养参差不齐。

t: Basic experiences and lessons of the early adaptation of Marxism to the Chinese context
zh: 早期马克思主义中国化的基本经验及启示
paras: This short commentary, first published in the Chinese Social Sciences Today in February 2023, asks what the Communist Party of China learned during the early exploration of adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times (1919–1938). Liu argues that the Party then lacked experience and struggled to combine Marxism-Leninism with Chinese revolutionary practice. Its setbacks, in Liu's view, yield lessons relevant to the Two Integrations today.

The article is built around four "persistent" principles drawn from the early period: applying Marxism's basic tenets to China's concrete realities; combining them with fine traditional Chinese culture; upholding the principal position of the people; and actively guiding currents of social thought. Liu illustrates each with episodes such as the Long March, Mao Zedong's early writings and the debates of the 1920s.

On the first point, Liu holds that treating Comintern directives as sacred and copying Soviet experience produced Chen Duxiu's "Right" error, the failure of the Great Revolution and the near-collapse of the Long March. The Party then reflected, and the Tongdao and Liping meetings under Mao's leadership changed the route. Liu presents Mao's "no investigation, no right to speak" as the outcome of that reflection. On thought, Liu describes three major debates, including Li Dazhao's reply to Hu Shi that "problems" and "isms" cannot be separated. They are said to have drawn a line between Marxism and liberalism, guild socialism and anarchism.

Liu concludes that early progress came from independence in solving China's problems, a dialectical stance towards tradition, firm Party leadership with reliance on the people, and struggle against erroneous trends. Liu offers these as the main inspiration for adapting Marxism in the new era. Read the original if you want a brief, official-style summary of how Party scholars draw lessons from the 1919–1938 period for current theory.
quoteEn: The key to deepening the adaptation of Marxism to the Chinese context is to hold consistently to the principal position of the people.
quoteZh: 马克思主义中国化的深化发展，关键在于始终坚持人民主体地位。

glossary.explanation: A formula in Party theory for combining the basic tenets of Marxism with China's concrete realities and with fine traditional Chinese culture. It is associated with Xi Jinping's leadership.

glossary.zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化
glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
glossary.explanation: The official name for the Party's project of applying Marxism to China's conditions and updating it for each era. The article uses the shorter form 'Sinicization of Marxism' for the early period.

glossary.en: the principal position of the people
glossary.explanation: A Party principle that the people are the main agents of history and of the Party's work. It is often stated as 'everything for the people, everything relying on the people'.

t: The qualities behind the early successful spread of Marxism in China
zh: 马克思主义在中国早期成功传播的品质
paras: Why did Marxism spread successfully in China in the early twentieth century? This short commentary, first published in the China Social Sciences Today newspaper in February 2023, argues that the answer lies in qualities of Marxism itself and in how Chinese communists handled it. Ling and Zhu distinguish a necessary condition, Marxism's advanced character, from sufficient conditions: its fit with the needs of the Chinese revolution and the Party's scientific attitude towards it.

The article opens with the rise of Leninism and the October Revolution, which it says strengthened the confidence of Chinese intellectuals seeking a way to save the nation. It then sets out four qualities in turn: Marxism as the proletarian ideology that fits the trend of social development; its capacity to keep pace with the times; its integration with Chinese conditions and with fine traditional Chinese culture; and the role of the Communists who carried it.

The authors contend that Confucian ideology collapsed with its feudal base, while the Three Principles of the People lost popular support once, in their account, they served a minority and were reshaped under Chiang Kai-shek. Marxism, by contrast, took the people's standpoint. Ling and Zhu also hold that its aim of free and all-round human development matches the traditional ideals of great harmony and shared wealth. In the New Democratic Revolution, they say, dogmatism weakened Marxism's social base until Mao Zedong and others established the line of seeking truth from facts.

The authors conclude that Marxism's advanced and revolutionary character became effective because Communists applied it to China's realities. They present this as the foundation of the adaptation of Marxism to Chinese conditions. Read the original if you want a concise statement of the official Party-history explanation of why Marxism, rather than rival ideologies, won acceptance in early twentieth-century China.
quoteEn: For a newly emerging ideology to win popular recognition, it must possess cultural qualities that people accept psychologically.
quoteZh: 一种新生的意识形态能为民众所认同，必须具备民众心理认同的文化品质。

glossary.en: adaptation of Marxism to Chinese conditions
glossary.explanation: The Party's term for applying Marxism to China's concrete circumstances and culture, associated with Mao Zedong's writings from the late 1930s.
Mao Zedong's term for the Chinese revolution of roughly 1919–1949, led by the proletariat and the Communist Party, as a stage preceding socialism.
A principle of basing policy on actual conditions, adopted by the Party as its ideological line and associated with Mao Zedong in the 1940s.
Sun Yat-sen's political doctrine of nationalism, democracy and people's livelihood, later the ideology of the Kuomintang.

keywords: early spread of Marxism in China
adaptation of Marxism to Chinese conditions

t: The influence of Japanese Marxism on the early adaptation of Marxism to the Chinese context
zh: 日本马克思主义对早期马克思主义中国化的影响
paras: This short piece, first published in China Social Sciences Today in February 2023, asks how Japanese Marxism shaped the early adaptation of Marxism to the Chinese context. Li and Zhang argue that Chinese students in Japan and exiled reformers or revolutionaries translated Japanese-language Marxist texts. In their account, this had an important effect on early Marxism in China.

The authors move through three themes. They describe how Japanese socialists coined Marxist terminology, why Japan became China's main channel for absorbing it, and how much Japanese-channel literature reached China. They then turn to the formation of a Chinese Marxist discourse.

Li and Zhang say Japanese translators either gave new meanings to classical Chinese words or coined new terms from Chinese characters. They contend that shared characters and a common cultural sphere made Japan a shortcut for Chinese translators. The authors cite 231 translated works between 1902 and 1949 and a peak around 1919. They also cite a German scholar's count of 35 Marxist terms borrowed directly from Japanese, such as 'capitalism' and 'socialism'. Terms were not borrowed uncritically: 'means of production' was first rendered through the Japanese 'means of production' wording in the 1938 Capital, then revised in 1957 after the German original.

The authors conclude that China's understanding was at first passive but not slavishly imitative. Japanese terminology spared Chinese translators the difficulty and inconsistency of working directly from the originals or English translations, so it sped up the spread of Marxism in China. Read the original if you want a concise overview of the Japanese route by which Marxist vocabulary and texts entered China.
quoteEn: Without the mediating role of Japanese Marxist terminology, it would have been much harder for China to translate Chinese terms directly from the original Marxist works or English translations.
quoteZh: 如果没有日文马克思主义术语的中介作用，中国直接从马克思主义原著或英译本翻译成中文术语的难度将会大大增加

t: The founding of Marx's materialist conception of history seen from the perspective of discourse transformation
zh: 话语变革的视角看马克思唯物史观的创立
source: Marxist Philosophy (马克思主义哲学), 2022 no. 5
paras: Most studies of Marx's materialist conception of history stress that it uncovered general laws of human history and revolutionised the understanding of history, but Liu Ying observes that few approach its founding through discourse. Opening with Xi Jinping's repeated calls to study historical materialism, the article argues that Marx's philosophical discourse passed through three forms: an early Hegelian speculative discourse, a humanist discourse with Feuerbachian colouring, and a new materialist discourse. In Liu's account, the change of discourse was the formation of the materialist conception of history itself.

The article follows Marx's texts in chronological order across three sections. The first covers the Doctoral Dissertation and the Rheinische Zeitung period. The second covers the Critique of Hegel's Philosophy of Right, the Deutsch-Französische Jahrbücher, the Paris manuscripts and The Holy Family. The third covers the Theses on Feuerbach and The German Ideology. Liu tracks logic, narrative mode, terminology and field of problems in each, drawing on Plekhanov, Althusser, McLellan and Engels.

Liu argues that each stage already held elements pointing beyond it. In the speculative period, "real factors" appear: Marx criticises Epicurus's freedom detached from the world and begins to speak of "objective relations" independent of individual will. In the humanist stage, Marx reverses Hegel on civil society and the state, introduces the proletariat, and in The Holy Family first uses "mode of production". He still derives economic categories and communism from alienated labour, which Liu reads as a logic of alienation rather than historical necessity. The decisive shift comes with the Theses on Feuerbach, which drop "species" and "alienation" and put practice at the centre. The German Ideology then makes real production practice the starting point, replacing "self-consciousness" and "human essence" with productive forces, forms of intercourse and material production, and so completes the new materialist discourse.

Liu concludes that the Theses were a rehearsal of the new discourse and The German Ideology marks its formation and the founding of the materialist conception of history. Liu concedes that some terms in the latter remain imprecise, for example "forms of intercourse" where later texts say relations of production. The Poverty of Philosophy and the 1859 Preface are presented as refinements within this framework. Liu also suggests that this view can inform building a discourse system for contemporary Chinese philosophy and social science under Marxist guidance. Read the original if you want a close, text-by-text account of how Marx's vocabulary shifted on the way to historical materialism, as seen by a Chinese scholar.
quoteEn: Discourse is a reflection of thought; the transformation of Marx's philosophical discourse was in fact also the process by which the materialist conception of history took shape.
quoteZh: 话语是思想的映射，马克思哲学话语的变革过程其实也是唯物史观的形成过程。

glossary.explanation: The Chinese term for historical materialism, Marx and Engels's theory that material production and social relations underlie history and ideas.
Marx's term in The German Ideology for the social forms in which people produce and exchange. Liu reads it as the forerunner of "relations of production".

t: Artificial intelligence and the transformation of the capitalist mode of production
zh: 人工智能与资本主义生产方式的变迁
source: Foreign Theoretical Trends (Guowai lilun dongtai), 2022 no. 6
paras: This article reviews recent work by scholars outside China on how artificial intelligence is changing the capitalist mode of production, and analyses it through Marxist political economy. Wang's thesis is that AI has not altered the essential features of capitalism. In the author's reading, it has reshaped machine systems, forms of work and the capital–labour relation in ways that deepen capital's control and exploitation of labour and sharpen class contradictions.

The review begins with Marx's definition of the capitalist mode of production in Capital and a sketch of successive technological revolutions, from steam to electricity to computers and then AI. It is organised in three parts: AI's remaking of the machine system, its effects on workers, and new features of the capital–labour relationship. The sources are mainly Western and other foreign scholars, including Nick Srnicek, Jamie Woodcock, Mary L. Gray and Siddharth Suri, Christian Fuchs, Shoshana Zuboff, Bernard Stiegler and Janine Berg.

Wang first argues that AI is essentially the intelligent upgrading of the 'control machine' added by automation to Marx's three-part machine. This produces platforms as a form of production organisation and the 'gig economy', including 'ghost work'. On labour, the review reports digital labour, the polarisation of the workforce as middle-skill jobs are replaced, and weakened worker solidarity. On the capital–labour relation, it identifies three tendencies: stronger control through what Zuboff calls surveillance capitalism, including remote control, monopoly over data and absolute power in the labour market; heavier exploitation through longer hours, lower pay, reduced autonomy and new forms such as 'playbor' and affective labour; and the concealment of the contradiction behind algorithms, platform 'neutrality' and the 'algorithmic black box'.

Wang concludes that, under the logic of capital, AI raises productivity but also reshapes organisation, employment and labour forms so that exploitation of surplus labour intensifies. The review holds that this confirms Marx's claim that capitalist development strengthens exploitation of the individual worker. It adds that the capitalist use of AI re-intensifies the conflict between bourgeoisie and working class and is brewing a general crisis within capitalist society. Read the original if you want a Marxist-framed map of Western and other foreign scholarship on platforms, digital labour and AI-era exploitation.
quoteEn: Artificial intelligence has not changed the essential features of the capitalist mode of production; rather, it has used new technologies and means to strengthen capital's control and exploitation of labour.
quoteZh: 人工智能并没有改变资本主义生产方式的本质特征，而是用新的技术和手段强化了资本对劳动的控制与剥削。

t: A political-economy critique of "algorithmic capitalism"
zh: “算法资本主义”的政治经济学批判阐释
paras: Sun Liang asks why algorithms have become central to contemporary capitalism, how they exercise control, and whether they leave any route to emancipation. The article argues that algorithms should not be equated with control: algorithms in general are an anthropological, accumulated human skill, and their coercive, profit-seeking features come from the capitalist form that has captured them. Critique should therefore target the capital form of algorithms, not algorithms as such.

The article has three parts. The first describes how algorithms embedded in capitalism produce a paradox with modern civilisation, at the levels of cognition, governance and production. The second identifies three mechanisms by which designers' interests and the capital principle shape algorithmic operation. The third turns to Marx's critique of political economy to propose a direction for correcting algorithmic capitalism. Sun draws on Lessig, Deleuze, Han Byung-chul, Zuboff, Hardt and Negri, Virno and others.

On cognition, Sun argues that algorithms promise an accurate picture of the world but breed a cartographic, computational belief that erodes subjects' capacity to imagine the future. On governance, they open a space of freedom that becomes biopolitical regulation. On production, they are meant to enable shared resources but become a means of capital valorisation, since they make social and affective activity measurable and so subject to value form. The three mechanisms are: algorithms embody designers' interests and are not neutral; data-guidance capacity reproduces the inequalities of private ownership; and ownership of platforms and servers is capitalist in character, producing data monopoly and what Sun calls "data colonialism". Against Virno and Negri's "crisis of measure" reading of the "Fragment on Machines", Sun argues that they read Marx's labour theory of value in a Ricardian way. In Sun's account, value-form analysis shows that algorithms cannot change the social character of exchange value, and the Grundrisse's collapse thesis was superseded by the dual character of labour in Capital.

Sun concludes that general intellect can serve human development only if it is withdrawn from capital's possession, which requires changing the ownership structure of the means of production. Algorithms should be steered towards regulation and "de-capitalisation" under a tension between suffering from algorithmic development and suffering from its absence. Sun suggests that, under socialism's drive to develop the productive forces, algorithms can support Chinese modernization. Read the original if you want a Marxist value-form rebuttal of post-operaist and Western left optimism about digital technology, set against critical theories of surveillance and biopolitics.
quoteEn: Algorithms cannot simply be equated with control; once this is understood, the object of transformation can be directed more fully towards capitalism as a social form.
quoteZh: 不能够简单地将算法直接等同于控制，明白了这一点，才能更多地将变革的对象朝向资本主义这一社会形式。

glossary.explanation: The official name for the Party's model of national development, promoted especially since the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is presented as distinct from Western modernisation paths.
A term from Marx's Grundrisse, in the "Fragment on Machines", for socially accumulated knowledge and science embodied in production. Italian post-operaist thinkers such as Virno have developed it.

Marx's concept of the social form in which labour appears as the value of commodities. Sun uses it to argue that analysis should explain why labour takes this form, not just measure labour quantities.

t: The value implications, strategic design and development path of building a modern socialist country in all respects
zh: 全面建设社会主义现代化国家的价值意蕴、战略设计及发展路径
source: Journal of Xinjiang Normal University (Philosophy and Social Sciences Edition), 2023 no. 3
paras: Taking the report to the 20th Party Congress (2022) as its starting point, this article asks what kind of modern socialist country China is to build and how. Li Nan and Zeng Lihua argue that building a modern socialist country in all respects carries a distinct set of values. They also argue that it rests on a systematic strategic design and requires a coordinated set of development paths, which they regard as necessary for Chinese modernization in the new stage of development.

The article has three parts. The first sets out four value implications: moving people from "one-dimensional" to all-round development, putting into practice the Party's original aspiration and founding mission, securing the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation, and opening a new realm of modern civilization. The second reviews the strategic design: eight goals for 2035, five guiding principles, the staged steps from the Two Centenary Goals onward, and six methodological choices. The third proposes six paths, covering Party leadership, high-quality development, whole-process people's democracy, cultural confidence, common prosperity and harmony between humanity and nature.

The authors' central claim is that this modernization differs in kind from the Western model. They describe the Western model as capital-centred, built on plunder and exploitation, and equating "modernization" with "Westernization". Chinese modernization, in their account, rests on people-centred development and an all-round development of the person, with material, cultural and ecological foundations. They say it turns the model of world modernization "from singular to plural". Leadership by the Party is presented as the fundamental guarantee, and the authors offer evidence for readiness to advance, including per capita GDP of 12,551 US dollars in 2021 and China's climb in the Global Innovation Index from 34th in 2012 to 11th in 2022.

The authors conclude that the two-step plan, basic modernization by 2035 and a strong modern socialist country by the middle of the century, should be pursued through stronger Party leadership. They also call for deeper reform and opening up, for the Two Unwaverings, for a rounded income distribution structure and for green, low-carbon development. They add that the struggle in the ideological and cultural sphere must be sustained. The article is a systematic exposition of the congress report's themes in official terms, not a critical or comparative study. Read the original if you want a detailed, source-based overview of how Chinese academics organise the 20th Party Congress's modernization agenda around values, strategy and policy paths.
quoteEn: Building a modern socialist country in all respects fundamentally rejects the fixed mindset of "modernization equals Westernization", turns the model of world modernization from singular to plural, offers countries a wholly new option for achieving modernization, and contributes Chinese wisdom to the construction of a paradigm of modernization.
quoteZh: 全面建设社会主义现代化国家从根本上否认了“现代化=西方化”的思维定式，将世界现代化模式由单数变为复数，为世界各国提供了实现现代化的全新选择，贡献了现代化范式建构的中国智慧。

glossary.explanation: The official term for China's own path of modernization, given prominence in the 20th Party Congress report (2022). It is presented as distinct from Western models, with features such as a huge population and common prosperity.
A long-standing socialist goal of prosperity shared by all, given renewed policy emphasis since the 2010s. It is linked to narrowing regional, urban–rural and income gaps.

A concept first put forward by Xi Jinping in 2019 to describe China's socialist democracy as covering every stage of political and policy processes. Official texts present it as distinct from Western electoral democracy.
The official principle of unwaveringly consolidating and developing the public sector and unwaveringly encouraging, supporting and guiding the non-public sector.
The official economic goal, adopted around 2017, of shifting from rapid growth to growth stressing innovation, efficiency, balance and sustainability.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.literal: great revival of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The Party's overarching national goal, tied to the Chinese Dream and to the Two Centenary Goals for 2021 and 2049.

t: Accelerating the improvement of the socialist market economy system
zh: 加快完善社会主义市场经济体制
paras: Writing in Guangming Daily in February 2023, after the 20th Party Congress (2022), Yang Jing asks how the socialist market economy system should be understood and further improved. The commentary argues that, since the 18th Party Congress (2012), the Party Central Committee with Xi Jinping at its core has accelerated this improvement, treating the system as an important part of the basic socialist economic system. Yang holds that this has deepened understanding of market-economy laws, extended Chinese modernization and enriched Marxist political economy on the market economy.

The piece has three sections. The first places the socialist market economy system within the basic socialist economic system. The second discusses letting the market play the decisive role in allocating resources while the government plays its role better. The third concerns correctly understanding and handling the characteristics and behavioural laws of capital. It draws throughout on statements by Xi Jinping and on the 20th Party Congress report's call to build a high-standard socialist market economy system.

Yang first notes that the Fourth Plenum of the 19th Central Committee (2019) placed the system alongside public ownership as the main body and the primary role of distribution according to work. Together these form a \"three-in-one\" framework. In Yang's reading, combining the basic socialist system with the market lets ownership, distribution and economic operation form an organic unity. Yang argues that this serves people-centred development, the principal contradiction and common prosperity, by enlarging the \"cake\" and then dividing it well. Second, Yang traces the Party's evolving view of the state–market relation to the Third Plenum of the 18th Central Committee (2013). The author calls for less direct government interference in micro-level activity and for better macroeconomic governance, regulation and public services to remedy market failure. Third, Yang acknowledges the many forms of capital in China today. The author argues that capital's profit-seeking can cause disorder if unchecked, and calls for equal access, orderly competition and legal oversight with \"traffic lights\".

Yang concludes that perfecting the system in this way conforms to the law that relations of production must suit the state of the productive forces. The author contends that it frees and develops the productive forces and meets people's needs for a better life. Capital should be guided to promote productive forces, wealth creation and livelihood protection, and kept from drifting away from the real economy. Read the original if you want a concise, official-line statement of how Chinese commentary in early 2023 framed the state, market and capital relationship after the 20th Party Congress.
quoteEn: Developing a market economy under socialist conditions is a great pioneering undertaking of our Party; it has achieved an organic combination of the basic socialist system and the market economy, and has advanced the improvement and development of the basic socialist economic system.
quoteZh: 在社会主义条件下发展市场经济，是我们党的一个伟大创举，实现了社会主义基本制度和市场经济的有机结合，推动了社会主义基本经济制度的完善和发展。

glossary.zh: 社会主义市场经济体制
glossary.explanation: China's economic system combining market mechanisms with public ownership and Party leadership. The concept was adopted at the 14th Party Congress in 1992.

glossary.zh: 社会主义基本经济制度
glossary.explanation: The core economic framework of the Chinese state. The Fourth Plenum of the 19th Central Committee (2019) defined it as public ownership as the main body, distribution according to work as the main body, and the socialist market economy system.
The official term for China's own path of modernization, prominently set out at the 20th Party Congress in 2022.
A goal of shared wealth for all the people, which Party documents present as an essential feature of socialism.

t: Letting Marxism take firm root in China
zh: 让马克思主义在中国牢牢扎根
paras: This short commentary, first published in the People's Daily on 6 February 2023, interprets a passage in Xi Jinping's report to the 20th Party Congress (2022). The passage calls for giving scientific theory distinct Chinese characteristics and consolidating the historical and popular foundations of adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times. Zhao argues that this passage explains why Marxism has taken root in China and how it can keep doing so.

The piece begins with Marx's remark that a theory is realised in a country to the degree that it meets that country's needs. It then treats the two foundations in turn, historical and popular, and ends by relating them to each other. It uses the Party's record since its founding and examples from the period after the 18th Party Congress (2012).

On the historical foundation, Zhao holds that Marxism must be applied to China's concrete conditions in each period, so that practical and theoretical innovation reinforce each other. The article lists Mao Zedong Thought, Deng Xiaoping Theory, the Three Represents, the Scientific Outlook on Development and Xi Jinping Thought as products of this process. On the popular foundation, Zhao stresses the Two Integrations, in particular combining Marxist principles with fine traditional Chinese culture. As examples, the author cites the people-centred development philosophy, said to draw on ideas such as "the people as the foundation of the state", and the idea of a community of life for humanity and nature.

Zhao concludes that the two foundations support each other dialectically. A firmer historical foundation strengthens the people's historical self-awareness and confidence in Marxism. A firmer popular foundation lets the people understand and apply the theory, and so turn it into a material force. Read the original if you want a brief example of how official Party commentary presented the 20th Congress's line on Marxism and Chinese tradition.
quoteEn: Only by combining the basic tenets of Marxism with the Chinese nation's history and culture, modes of thinking and national psychology can Marxism be accepted and mastered by the people, steadily consolidating the popular foundation for adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times.
quoteZh: 只有把马克思主义基本原理同中华民族的历史文化、思维方式、民族心理结合起来，才能让马克思主义为人民群众所认同、所掌握，不断夯实马克思主义中国化时代化的群众基础。

glossary.zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化
glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
glossary.explanation: Official formula for the Party's project of applying Marxism to Chinese conditions and updating it for the present era. The "times" element was added in the 2020s to the older "sinification of Marxism".
Xi Jinping's formula for combining the basic tenets of Marxism with China's concrete realities and with fine traditional Chinese culture.
Theory associated with Jiang Zemin, introduced around 2000. It holds that the Party represents advanced productive forces, advanced culture and the fundamental interests of the people.
Guiding concept associated with Hu Jintao, stressing people-centred, comprehensive and sustainable development.

t: Linking the essence of Marxist thought with the best of traditional Chinese culture
zh: 把马克思主义思想精髓同中华优秀传统文化精华贯通起来
paras: Taking its cue from Xi Jinping's report to the 20th Party Congress (2022), this commentary asks how the essence of Marxist thought can be connected with the finest elements of traditional Chinese culture. Shang argues that this requires understanding Marxism's core, continually drawing out the ideas in traditional culture, and studying the inner logic that joins the two. The text first appeared in the People's Daily in February 2023.

The piece has three parts. The first treats Marxism as open to all the achievements of human civilisation and as a method rather than a dogma. The second traces how Marxism's adaptation in China has drawn on Chinese historical culture. The third sets out tasks for the present.

Shang holds that Marxism's three components built on German classical philosophy, British classical political economy and French utopian socialism, and that Engels described it as a method, not a doctrine. Applied in China, it met an ancient culture, and the Party has advanced the Two Integrations through successive theoretical achievements. Shang cites Mao's "seeking truth from facts", Deng's "xiaokang", Hu Jintao's "harmonious society" and, under Xi, the people-centred idea and a community with a shared future for mankind as examples of Marxism and traditional culture combined. In this account Marxism gains a Chinese flavour while dialectical materialism gives traditional culture new vitality.

Shang calls for firmly grasping the essence of Marxism, digging out the best of traditional culture with Marxist standpoint and method, and pursuing continued integration in content, method and values. Shang presents this as a historical responsibility of today's Communists and as a sign of the Party's cultural confidence. Read the original if you want a short, official-line statement of how Party theorists justify combining Marxism with traditional culture.
