quoteEn: Grasping the essence of Marxist thought ultimately means seizing what is fundamental, central and essential within the Marxist theoretical system.
quoteZh: 把握马克思主义思想精髓，说到底是要在马克思主义理论体系中抓住根本、抓住核心、抓住实质。

glossary.explanation: The principle of combining the basic tenets of Marxism with China's concrete realities and with its fine traditional culture. The second integration was added to the formula in 2021–2023 Party documents.
A goal of social development promoted under Hu Jintao in the mid-2000s, drawing on the traditional ideal of harmony.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's concept for international relations, which the article links to ideas such as "all under heaven as one family".

t: The Communist Party of China's historic contributions to enriching and developing scientific socialism
zh: 中国共产党丰富和发展科学社会主义的历史贡献
paras: Writing after the 20th Party Congress (2022), Huang asks how the Communist Party of China (CPC) has enriched and developed scientific socialism over its century-plus history. The article argues that the Party, by combining Marxist fundamentals with Chinese conditions, has become the mainstay of the international communist movement in the twenty-first century. Huang presents its contributions as original ones in theory, in practice and in institutions.

The article is organised in three parts. The first treats theory: the path to power, stages of socialist development, the essence of socialism, and Chinese modernization. The second treats the practice of the socialist movement, from the New Democratic Revolution through socialist transformation and reform to the new era. The third treats institutional innovation, from the Chinese Soviet Republic to the system of socialism with Chinese characteristics. Huang repeatedly contrasts Marx, Engels, Lenin and Stalin with the Party's own responses.

Huang's central move is to show that each Chinese innovation filled a gap left by the classics. Marx and Engels gave no concrete guidance for semi-colonial countries, and saw peasants as incapable of representing themselves. Mao Zedong's New Democratic Revolution, relying on the peasantry and encircling cities from the countryside, is described as a second model after the October Revolution, later borne out in Vietnam, Korea and Cuba. Huang likewise credits the theory of the primary stage of socialism, Deng Xiaoping's definition of socialism's essence (liberating and developing the productive forces, eliminating exploitation and polarisation, reaching common prosperity), and the break from the Soviet model as moving socialism from one model to many.

Huang concludes that Chinese modernization, led by the Party, breaks the Western equation of modernization with capitalism and offers developing countries a path of independent exploration. The author also holds that China's governance experience and the proposal of a community with a shared future for mankind show the advantages of socialist governance. The article ends by listing the Party's theoretical achievements, from Mao Zedong Thought to Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, as results of adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times. Read the original if you want a systematic account of how Party scholars frame China's relation to the classics of scientific socialism and to the Soviet experience.
quoteEn: The Party's theoretical and practical innovation in Chinese modernization has greatly expanded the content of scientific socialism's account of socialist development, and has further widened the road toward the goal of every person's free and all-round development.
quoteZh: 中国共产党对中国式现代化的理论与实践的创新，大大拓展了科学社会主义关于社会主义发展的内涵，在追求实现每个人的自由而全面发展的目标上，进一步拓宽了前进道路。

glossary.explanation: The official name for China's path of modernization under Party leadership, elaborated at the 20th Party Congress (2022) with five characteristic features and a set of essential requirements.
A Party judgement, systematically set out at the 13th Party Congress (1987), that China is in a long, underdeveloped initial phase of socialism. It underpins reform-era policy.
An official goal of prosperity shared by all the people. Deng Xiaoping included it in his definition of socialism's essence, and it has been stressed again in the Xi Jinping era.

Mao Zedong's theory of a revolution against imperialism and feudalism led by the proletariat, as a stage preceding socialist transformation. It is the Party's official account of the revolution before 1949.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's concept for international relations and global governance, presented officially as China's contribution to world order.

glossary.zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化
glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
glossary.explanation: The official formula for the Party's project of fitting Marxist theory to Chinese conditions and contemporary circumstances. The phrase is used of successive Party theories from Mao Zedong Thought onward.

t: The scope and boundaries of intelligent labour
zh: 智能劳动的范围与边界
paras: Writing in a newspaper commentary in January 2023, Shang and Chen ask how far AI-driven "intelligent labour" can replace human labour. They note the pessimistic view that machines will displace workers and usurp their status as labourers. They argue instead that Marxist labour theory remains valid and that intelligent labour has clear limits.

The piece first describes what intelligent machines already replace, such as cash machines, unmanned warehouses, automatic ticketing and securities-analysis software. It then explains how an intelligent machine system (algorithms, data and robotic arms) takes over functions of the brain and muscles. Finally it sets out three boundaries drawn from Marx's historical materialism and his view of labour.

According to the authors, replaceable work is repetitive, patterned and programmable. Human knowledge is objectified in machines, turning living labour into objectified labour. The first boundary is that AI cannot produce something from nothing, because it depends on data supplied by humans. The second is that AI creates no value: living human labour remains the only source of value, and the machine is only a "measurer" and "indicator" of social relations. The third is that AI lacks emotion, will and aesthetic sense, so it cannot respond to unexpected situations and its output lacks uniqueness.

The authors conclude that AI remains a tool and cannot shed its character as a thing. They still regard it as a historical advance over handicraft and mechanical tools, one that produces new forms of labour alienation but also holds positive significance for the liberation of human labour. Read the original if you want a brief Marxist-labour-theory answer to fears of AI replacing human work.
quoteEn: Artificial intelligence in essence does not create value; the sole source of value remains the living labour of human beings.
quoteZh: 人工智能本质上不创造价值，价值的唯一源泉仍然是人的活劳动。

t: The problem consciousness and theoretical tensions of classical Western Marxism
zh: 经典西方马克思主义的问题意识与理论张力
paras: Gao Xiaoxi, in a short piece for the Chinese Social Sciences Today (January 2023), asks what question drove classical Western Marxism, the current running from Lukács to Althusser between the 1920s and 1960s. Gao argues that its core concern was how to make socialist revolution in advanced capitalist countries, and that this strategic dispute was expressed as a debate over the nature of Marx's philosophy.

The article first sketches twentieth-century capitalism: oligarchic monopoly, a divided working class including a "labour aristocracy", and a shift from open repression to softer ideological control through consumerism and mass culture. It then contrasts classical Western Marxism with the Second International, divides the former into humanist and scientistic wings, and traces its afterlife after the events of May 1968.

Gao contends that the Second International read Marx in a deterministic, dogmatic way and so could not meet these changes. Classical Western Marxists, by contrast, treated class consciousness as decisive and understood Marxism as a philosophy of subjective practice joining philosophy, history and politics. Its central tension, in Gao's account, is how to unite critique of capitalist ideology with revolutionary practice, which exposes a subjectivist and romantic tendency. The humanist wing (Lukács, Korsch, Gramsci, the Frankfurt School, existentialist Marxism) is set against Althusser's structuralist "theoretical anti-humanism", which Gao says slides into theoretical monologue.

Gao concludes that Marxism outside China can be read as shaped by tensions such as history–structure and liberation–disengagement, which trace back to classical Western Marxism. Without grasping this problem consciousness, Gao warns, one risks misjudging the interpretation and reception of Western Marxism and weakening the contemporary and global outlook of Marxism adapted to the Chinese context. Read the original if you want a compact Chinese account of how classical Western Marxism is positioned within the wider field of foreign Marxism.
quoteEn: We may even regard the theoretical map of Marxism outside China as the outcome of a problem consciousness originating in classical Western Marxism, governed and shaped by tensions such as history–structure, time–space, substance–discourse, class–individual, construction–deconstruction and liberation–disengagement.
quoteZh: 我们甚至可以将国外马克思主义的理论版图，看作以经典西方马克思主义的问题意识为源，经由“历史—结构、时间—空间、实体—话语、阶级—个体、建构—解构、解放—解脱”等张力结构统摄与形塑的结果。

glossary.zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化
glossary.en: Marxism adapted to the Chinese context
glossary.explanation: Official formula for the Party's project of adapting Marxism to Chinese conditions and the needs of the times. The article refers to it in the earlier form 中国化马克思主义 (Marxism adapted to China).
A broad field in Chinese scholarship covering Marxist currents outside China, including Western Marxism, ecological Marxism and post-Marxism.
The article's term for Western Marxist theory from Lukács to Althusser, c. 1920s–1960s.

t: Firmly grasping the theme, main thread and mainstream essence of the history of New China
zh: 牢牢把握新中国史的主题主线、主流本质
paras: Marking the 30th anniversary of the Chinese Society for the History of the People's Republic, Xi Jinping sent a congratulatory letter urging historians to firmly grasp the theme, main thread and mainstream essence of the history of New China. This commentary, published in Guangming Daily on 15 February 2023, sets out how Song Yuehong reads that instruction. Song argues that studying the letter requires an objective, comprehensive and accurate account of the course, achievements and experience of New China, and a deeper understanding of these three categories.

The piece moves in three steps. It first defines the theme and the four main threads of New China's history, tracing the Party's changing statements of its goals across the socialist revolution and construction period, the reform and opening up period and the new era. It then sets out the mainstream and essence of that history, including how the author treats its setbacks. Finally it draws out tasks for research on the history of New China.

In Song's account, the theme is the adaptation of Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times, together with building and developing socialism with Chinese characteristics and rejuvenating the Chinese nation. The four threads are safeguarding sovereignty and promoting a community with a shared future for mankind; upholding Marxism and the Party's self-reform; advancing Chinese modernization and common prosperity; and achieving national reunification. Song admits that the path was not smooth and that mistakes and serious setbacks occurred. The author nonetheless holds that the exploratory achievements of the early period prepared the ground for later reform, so the mainstream is founding, enriching and strengthening the country, taking its own path and benefiting the people. The essence is a history of socialist development, of the people's united struggle and of national rejuvenation.

Song calls for research to explain the historical logic of the socialist path with Chinese characteristics and the course of Chinese modernization. It should also build a disciplinary, academic and discourse system for the history of New China, combine source collection with theory, and openly oppose historical nihilism. Studies should foster historical confidence and the Four-sphere Confidence. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party-affiliated historians frame the periodisation and interpretive guidelines for studying the People's Republic after Xi's 2023 letter.
quoteEn: The mainstream of the history of New China can be put as follows: founding, rejuvenating and strengthening the country, walking its own path, bringing benefits to the people, promoting the building of a better world, with brilliant achievements and broad prospects.
quoteZh: 新中国史的主流可表述为，立国兴国强国，走自己的路，为民造福，推动建设美好世界，成就辉煌、前景广阔。

glossary.en: theme, main thread and mainstream essence
glossary.explanation: A framework from Party historiography for interpreting the history of the People's Republic. It identifies an overarching theme, guiding threads, and the principal character of that history, as distinct from its setbacks.
The Party's official term for China's own path to modernization, which it presents as sharing features with other countries but as distinct in its Chinese characteristics.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: A foreign-policy concept promoted by Xi Jinping that calls for shared development, security and cooperation among nations.
An official term for the Party's efforts to discipline and renew itself, which it presents as a precondition for leading social transformation.
An official goal of prosperity shared by all the people, emphasised in the Xi era.
In official usage, a label for interpretations of Chinese revolutionary and socialist history that are seen as denying or belittling its achievements.
Official slogan calling for confidence in the path, theory, system and culture of socialism with Chinese characteristics.

t: The historic contributions of the Party Constitution adopted at the Seventh Party Congress
zh: 中共七大党章的历史性贡献
paras: This short commentary, published in Guangming Daily in February 2023, asks what the Constitution of the Communist Party of China adopted at the Seventh Party Congress (Yan'an, 23 April to 11 June 1945) contributed to Party history. Huang Wei argues that it was the most complete and detailed Party constitution of the democratic revolution period, a summary of the 17 years of struggle since the Sixth Congress (1928), a mark of the Party's maturity and a milestone in the development of Party constitutions.

The article is organised around three contributions. The first is the constitution's statement that Mao Zedong Thought is the Party's guiding ideology. The second is its full presentation of the programme of the New Democratic revolution. The third is its strengthening of the Party's own building, through organisational principles, institutions, work style and discipline. Huang draws heavily on Liu Shaoqi's report on revising the Party constitution (published as "On the Party") and on the constitution's text.

On the first point, Huang notes that the general programme defines Mao Zedong Thought as the unity of Marxism-Leninism with the practice of the Chinese revolution and the guide to all of the Party's work, and makes studying it a duty of every member. In Huang's reading, this reflected the Party's ideological and political maturity and led to the first historic leap in adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times. On the second, Huang stresses that the constitution for the first time placed a general programme before the articles, a practice later followed. It defined the Party's nature, its goal of New Democracy and its final aim of communism, and set out the revolution's character, leading force, tasks and targets.

On Party building, Huang cites a 1943 decision on strengthening Party spirit, which criticised members who acted without consulting the centre, as the background. Huang lists a series of "firsts" in the constitution: codified duties and rights of members, the mass line and the aim of serving the people wholeheartedly, criticism and self-criticism, democratic centralism, admission by conduct rather than class origin, the powers of national conferences, and graded disciplinary measures. Huang concludes that these show the constitution's pioneering character and its place linking past and future in Party history. Read the original if you want a brief, officially aligned account of how Chinese scholars present the 1945 Party constitution and its place in Party-building history.
quoteEn: The Seventh Congress Party Constitution was a revolutionary programme guiding the whole Party in leading the Chinese nation and people to win national independence and the people's liberation.
quoteZh: 七大党章是一部指引全党带领中华民族和中国人民夺取民族独立和人民解放的革命纲领

glossary.explanation: The Party's term for Mao's body of ideas as the adaptation of Marxism-Leninism to Chinese conditions. It was first written into the Party constitution as the guiding ideology in 1945.
Mao Zedong's theory of a transitional revolutionary stage in a semi-colonial, semi-feudal country, led by the proletariat and aimed at preparing the way for socialism.

glossary.zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化
glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
glossary.explanation: The official formula for fitting Marxism to China's conditions and to the era. The Party describes Mao Zedong Thought as its first historic leap.
A Party principle that cadres must stay in close contact with the people, listen to their demands and act on them. It was developed in the Yan'an period.
The Leninist organisational principle of centralism on the basis of democracy and democracy under centralised leadership. Minorities obey majorities and lower bodies obey higher ones.

t: The translation and dissemination of the Communist Manifesto in China
zh: 《共产党宣言》在中国的翻译与传播
paras: Writing in the Chinese Social Sciences Today (22 December 2022 issue dated 29 December), Li Xinhao traces how the Communist Manifesto reached and was rendered in China over roughly 120 years. The article argues that this translation history is also the history of Marxism taking root in China and of the Communist Party's pursuit of truth and its self-reform. It treats the Manifesto's reception as part of adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times.

The piece is a short historical overview in three parts. The first divides the Chinese versions into three stages: excerpts and quotations (1899–1919), full-text translations (1920–1949) and revised editions (1949 to the present). The second takes the opening sentence about the "spectre" as a case study of translators' deliberations. The third turns to how Chinese scholars have interpreted the text and what the 20th Party Congress (2022) implies for its continued dissemination.

Li's central example is the rendering of the German words Gespenst and umgehen. Chinese translators tried many renderings, and Cheng Fangwu revised his several times over decades, from "huge shadow" to "demon shadow" to "demon". The Central Compilation and Translation Bureau fixed "youling" (spectre) and "youdang" (to wander) in 1964 and 1995, checking the German original against other-language versions. Li also reads Marx's choice of the pejorative term as ironic self-description that opens the Manifesto like a theatrical monologue. On interpretation, Li distinguishes three levels: terminological translation studies, annotated readings, and evidential scientific exegesis that links the text to present Chinese practice. Li holds that readings screened by revolutionary and construction experience become part of adapting Marxism to China.

Li concludes that Manifesto scholarship now includes histories of its dissemination, discourse and ideas, and treats this as a creative use of the classic. Citing the 20th Party Congress's stress on the Two Integrations and on the Manifesto's own preface, which says application of its principles depends on historical conditions, Li calls for drawing out ideas that were previously neglected but matter for current practice. Read the original if you want a compact account of the Chinese editions of the Manifesto and of how Party-aligned scholarship frames their significance.
quoteEn: The translation history of the Manifesto is also the history of the spread of Marxist truth in China; the translations and editions of different periods together bear witness to Marxism taking root, sprouting and continually developing in China.
quoteZh: 《宣言》的翻译史也是马克思主义真理在中国传播的历史，不同时期的《宣言》译本、版本共同见证了马克思主义在中国生根、发芽，不断创新发展的历程

glossary.zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化
glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
glossary.explanation: The official formula for fitting Marxist theory to China's conditions and to the current era. The "times" element was added in recent Party documents.

A Party formula stressing the integration of Marxism's basic tenets with China's concrete realities and with China's fine traditional culture. It was highlighted in the 20th Party Congress report (2022).
The Party institution responsible for authoritative Chinese translations of Marxist classics and Party documents.

t: The people-centred character of the Communist Manifesto
zh: 《共产党宣言》的人民性品格
paras: This short commentary, first published in the China Social Sciences Today (Zhongguo shehui kexue bao) on 29 December 2022, asks in what sense the Communist Manifesto embodies the 'people-centred' (renminxing) character that Shao Xiaoqiu treats as the essential attribute of Marxism. Shao argues that the Manifesto grew out of the practice of the masses and aims at the liberation of humanity, so that it shows this character in an exemplary way.

The piece has two main parts. The first traces how the Manifesto arose from the proletariat's struggles and from Marx and Engels's own practice. It also covers the seven prefaces added over later decades. The second part examines the Manifesto's account of the Communist Party's relation to the people and of the stages leading to human emancipation.

Shao contends that nineteenth-century workers' uprisings, such as those in Lyon, Silesia and the Chartist movement, all failed and so called for a scientific theory. In Shao's reading, Marx and Engels distilled these experiences, with Engels spending over twenty months among factory workers. The prefaces then adjusted the text to new conditions after the 1848 revolutions, the First International and the Paris Commune. On emancipation, Shao sets out three steps drawn from the Manifesto: establishing proletarian rule, socialist transformation of ownership, and developing production towards communism. Shao stresses that the Party has no interests apart from those of the proletariat as a whole.

Shao concludes that the Manifesto's people-centred essence has contemporary value across time. Its insistence on keeping theory abreast of the times reflects the 'people-centred' idea that the Chinese Communist Party has consistently upheld. Read the original if you want a brief example of how Chinese commentary links the Manifesto's prefaces and its idea of emancipation to current Party language about the people.
quoteEn: It can thus be seen that it was precisely the proletariat's unremitting struggle that gave birth to the Communist Manifesto, this people-centred fighting manifesto.
quoteZh: 可见，正是无产阶级坚持不懈的斗争催生了《共产党宣言》这一人民性的战斗檄文。

glossary.literal: taking the people as the centre
glossary.explanation: A guiding principle in Party discourse since Xi Jinping's leadership began, holding that policy and theory should place the people's interests first.

t: Marx's theory of "world history" and the international workers' movement
zh: 马克思的“世界历史”理论与国际工人运动
paras: Liu Enzhi asks how Marx's concept of "world history" differs from the idealist versions in German classical philosophy, and what it implies for proletarian politics. The article, first published in the Chinese Social Sciences Today in October 2022, argues that Marx grounded world history in the real economic relations of capitalism. On this basis he drew a practical programme, world revolution, and a conception of peace opposed to Kant's.

The piece opens by contrasting Marx with Kant and Hegel. Kant's "perpetual peace" and Hegel's absolute spirit as ruler of world history are treated as speculative constructions with no historical reality. Two sections follow. The first, on how world history is presented, deals with the world market and world revolution. The second, on world history and proletarian emancipation, compares Kant's and Marx's routes to peace and ends with the First International.

In Liu's reading, Marx treats the world market opened by the bourgeoisie as the material carrier of world history. Capital globalises its own contradictions, so world revolution is both possible and necessary. It is possible because crises spread everywhere and because Eastern countries are drawn into the market. It is necessary because an isolated crisis can be exported through war or colonial expansion, and because local communism would be swallowed by expanding capitalism. Liu then argues that Kant's perpetual peace is a transcendental, abstract imperative, and that his league of states would remain bourgeois. Marx instead sought elements of peace within objective conditions. For Marx, lasting peace rests on the revolutionary union of the proletariat, which abolishes bourgeois states, classes and war together.

Liu concludes that world revolution is the concrete practical form of Marx's concept of world history, aiming at abolishing bourgeois rule globally. The First International is presented as Marx's key attempt to unite workers across countries, with Marx as its guiding figure. According to Liu, it fostered the international workers' and world socialist movements that pressed on bourgeois rule and shaped world history. Read the original if you want a short, source-based account of how Chinese Marxist scholarship distinguishes Marx's world history from German idealism and links it to internationalism.
quoteEn: But communism is by no means this kind of transcendental, abstract, powerless moral imperative; it is rooted in empirical real relations and is a concrete conclusion generated from the actual possibilities of material economic relations and class relations.
quoteZh: 但共产主义绝不是这种先验的、抽象的、软弱无力的道德命令，它深植于经验的现实关系之中，它是从物质经济关系和阶级关系的实际可能性中生成而出的具体结论。

t: The historical significance of Engels's "Outlines of a Critique of Political Economy"
zh: 《国民经济学批判大纲》的历史意义
paras: This short commentary, first published in the China Social Sciences Today in October 2022, asks what Engels achieved in his 1844 Outlines of a Critique of Political Economy. Sun argues that Engels did more than expose the alienation of economic categories. In Sun's reading, he found a logical starting point that undoes the mystical system of Hegel's speculative philosophy, moving from an undetermined immediacy to the reality of concrete human beings, and so laid a foundation for the materialist conception of history.

The article has two main parts after a discussion of the logical beginning of the text: Engels's critique of capitalist production, and his critique of the essence of capitalist private ownership. Sun draws on Engels's passages on factors of production, capital as accumulated labour, price and value, overproduction and crisis, and the concentration of property. Feuerbach's influence is traced through Engels's remarks in the Outlines and in The Holy Family.

Sun's central claim is that Engels, like Feuerbach, inverted Hegel's logic and replaced it with a starting point of the sensuous and objective ("感性—对象性"). On this basis, Sun says, Engels could enter bourgeois society and analyse the alienated realities of private ownership. Sun credits Engels with identifying nature and humans as the two factors of production, treating capital as accumulated labour, finding hidden theft in the price-value gap, and tracing crises to overproduction. For Sun, private ownership is the source of exploitation and class polarisation, since living labour is ruled by dead capital.

Sun concludes that Engels held that the evils of private ownership can be removed only by abolishing it, and that he pointed to public ownership as the future direction of social development. Read the original if you want a brief, Chinese-language account of how the Outlines is read as a bridge between Feuerbach's critique of Hegel and the materialist conception of history.
quoteEn: The ills brought by private ownership can be removed only by abolishing private ownership.
quoteZh: 私有制带来的弊端唯有通过消灭私有制才能解除。

glossary.explanation: The Marxist theory that material production and social relations shape historical development. Marx and Engels set it out most fully from The German Ideology (1845–46) onwards.

keywords: Outlines of a Critique of Political Economy

t: The decline of Western European parties and the rise of populism
zh: 西欧政党衰败与民粹主义的崛起
paras: Why have populist parties surged in Western Europe in recent years? In this short commentary, first published in the Chinese Social Sciences Today in September 2022, Zeng Sen argues that the decay of mainstream parties is the basic precondition for that rise. Since the 1970s, the author notes, Western European countries have entered post-industrial society, with major shifts in class structure and values, and parties have declined over the long term as a result.

The article is organised around three aspects of this decline, which Zeng presents as the political setting for populism: the weakening of party organisation, the ideological convergence of mainstream parties, and growing electoral volatility. It draws mainly on Britain, France and Denmark, and on the scholarship of Richard Katz and Peter Mair, Robert Putnam, Arend Lijphart, Francis Fukuyama and others cited in passing.

On organisation, Zeng reports that membership of the main Western European parties fell by almost half between 1980 and 2008, that activism and party identification weakened, and that parties became 'cartels' reliant on state resources, which cut their ties with voters and produced a crisis of representation. On convergence, the author argues that the centrist 'Third Way' consensus politics left left and right parties alike embracing European integration, globalisation and immigration. This is said to have neglected the grievances of blue-collar workers and allowed populists to claim to be the only true voice of the people, especially in consensus-style systems. On volatility, Zeng argues that the postwar 'frozen' party system has thawed. The article cites a fall in the average mainstream vote to 72% in 2015 and the exit of both main French parties in the first round of the 2017 presidential election.

Zeng singles out centre-left parties, which in the author's account turned from economic equality to the identity politics of marginal groups and lost working-class voters to right-wing populists. The article concludes that populist parties have partly reshaped Western Europe's political map, and says it is still an open question whether they act as a corrective or a threat. Read the original if you want a compact Chinese-language overview of party-system explanations for European populism and of how it is framed for Chinese readers.
quoteEn: It is precisely the growing similarity among mainstream political forces that has provided fertile soil for the rise of populism.
quoteZh: 而正是主流政治力量越来越相似，为民粹主义的兴起提供了肥沃的土壤。

t: New developments in contemporary ecological Marxism
zh: 当代生态马克思主义研究新进展
source: China Social Sciences Today (Zhongguo shehui kexue bao), 27 October 2022
paras: This short review in a Chinese social-science newspaper surveys how ecological Marxism has developed since the start of the twenty-first century. Lin Zhaoxia presents it as one of the most influential current schools of thought, arising from the worsening ecological crisis and from Marxism's practical mission. The review's central claim is that these scholars treat the ecological crisis as in essence a crisis of the social system, to be resolved only through a thoroughgoing critique and transcendence of capitalism.

Lin reviews work by André Gorz, John Bellamy Foster, Grundmann, James O'Connor, Paul Burkett, Joel Kovel, Saito Kohei and others on the causes, forms, critical dimensions and ways beyond ecological crisis. The text is organised in four sections: capital accumulation as the direct cause of crisis; the rift in metabolism as its form of appearance; the critical dimensions of ecological Marxism; and a renewed construction of historical materialism. A short conclusion places the school in the history of Marxist research since the 1960s.

On causes, Lin reports that capital's endless accumulation demands raw materials and energy. O'Connor's 'second contradiction' sets capitalism's unlimited production against the limited conditions of production, while Foster describes accumulation as producing a rift in the metabolism between society and nature. On forms, the review describes three features: the contradiction between use-value and exchange-value, alienated consumption and commodity fetishism, and the estrangement of people from nature. On critique, Gorz is said to seek a 'paradigm shift' that frees use-value from exchange-value, and Kovel to locate the crisis in social relations and to stress restoring producers' control over production. Foster, Peter Dickens-type thinkers such as Pepper, and Grundmann are said to argue that historical materialism has an ecological dimension, which Saito systematically reconstructs as continuous with Marx's critique of political economy.

Lin concludes that ecological Marxism is both a value orientation for social development and a critical theory of capitalism's internal contradictions. The review adds that these scholars treat ecological problems as common to all human society, and cites the Russian scholar Shevchenko's remark that capitalism's development model is 'a dead end'. In this account the ecological crisis can be overcome only by a complete critique and transcendence of capital and capitalist society. Read the original if you want a concise Chinese-language overview of how ecological Marxist thinkers are presented to a Chinese readership.
quoteEn: The capitalist ecological crisis is not only a problem in the ecological sphere, but also the inevitable result of the essence of the capitalist system.
quoteZh: 资本主义生态危机不仅是生态领域的问题，而且是基于资本主义制度本质的必然结果。

glossary.explanation: A current of Marxist thought, prominent since the 1960s–70s, that analyses environmental destruction as a product of capitalist social relations and accumulation.
A concept drawn from Marx's idea of the metabolism between humans and nature, developed by Foster to describe how capitalist production disrupts natural cycles.
In Marx's analysis, the usefulness of a good in satisfying human needs, as opposed to its exchange-value in the market.
The Marxist theory of history that explains social development through material production and social relations; the review argues it has an ecological dimension.

t: Viewing the new thought of the new era from a historical perspective
zh: 从历史角度看新时代的新思想
source: Journal of Shanghai Normal University (Philosophy and Social Sciences Edition), 2023 no. 1
paras: Following the 20th Party Congress (2022), which declared that Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era marks a new leap in adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times, Zhou Liangshu asks how the new thought should be understood. The author argues that it must be placed inside the Party's own history, as a relationship of adherence and development, inheritance and innovation. Zhou takes this reading from Xi's own remarks that socialism with Chinese characteristics is a "big essay" which each generation of leaders continues to write.

The article proceeds chronologically through four stages. It begins with Mao Zedong's founding of China's socialist cause, then turns to Deng Xiaoping and the 1981 Resolution on Party history as the basis for continuity and development. It then covers the exploration of a new path under reform and opening up, and finally the contributions of Jiang Zemin, Hu Jintao and Xi Jinping. At each stage Zhou draws on speeches and Party documents.

Zhou's first move is to trace methods of thought across generations. Mao's 1956 "Ten Relationships" and his 1957 analysis of contradictions among the people are said to survive in Jiang's twelve relationships, Hu's Scientific Outlook on Development, Xi's call for a systems approach, and the identification of the principal social contradiction. The second move concerns Deng. The article describes his handling of Mao's legacy as evaluating a figure through the whole of history rather than a fragment of it, and presents "socialism with Chinese characteristics" as a unity of inheritance and development. Zhou also rejects both a return to a "closed and rigid" old road and a "wrong road" of abandoning socialism, and links Deng's combative style and leadership method to Xi's "great struggle" and emphasis on the "key minority".

Zhou concludes that the Three Represents, a harmonious society and the Scientific Outlook on Development each answered problems that history had made ripe for solution, and warns against judging predecessors with hindsight. The article credits the new era with three achievements: Xi's thought, the Party's self-reform as a second answer to the historical cycle of rise and fall, and the launch of a new journey toward a modern socialist country. Zhou presents these as continuous with earlier generations' work. Read the original if you want a Party-history account of how Chinese scholars link Xi's thought to Mao, Deng, Jiang and Hu.
quoteEn: The Communist Party of China views development on the basis of inheritance, and speaks of development on the basis of inheritance.
quoteZh: 中国共产党是在继承基础上看发展的，是在继承基础上谈发展的。

glossary.zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化
glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
glossary.explanation: The official formula for the Party's project of fitting Marxism to China's conditions and to each era. The 20th Party Congress described Xi's thought as a new leap in this process.
Hu Jintao's guiding concept from the early 2000s, stressing people-centred, comprehensive, coordinated and sustainable development.
Jiang Zemin's theory of 2000, holding that the Party represents advanced productive forces, advanced culture and the fundamental interests of the majority.
Hu Jintao's goal of building a socialist harmonious society, which added attention to fairness and the wealth gap to the pursuit of efficiency.
Xi-era term for the Party's efforts to purify and renew itself. It is presented as the answer to the historical cycle of rise and fall.

t: Getting off to a good start in building a modern socialist country in all respects
zh: 为全面建设社会主义现代化国家开好局起好步
paras: Writing in the People's Daily in January 2023, Wang Changlin interprets the Central Economic Work Conference held at the end of 2022 and the speech Xi Jinping gave there. The article's thesis is that China's economy has withstood severe tests, that its long-term fundamentals remain sound, and that the conference's priorities can bring about an overall recovery in 2023. In Wang's account, this recovery would mean an effective improvement in quality and a reasonable growth in quantity, and so a good start to building a modern socialist country in all respects.

The piece has three parts. It first reviews the 2022 economic record, then assesses short-term and long-term prospects, and finally sets out how to carry out the conference's tasks. The review cites figures on growth, high-tech manufacturing, investment, exports, prices, employment and food output. It compares China's inflation and trade performance with that of the United States, the eurozone and Japan.

Wang argues that, despite a growth dip to 0.4% in the second quarter, a package of stabilising measures produced annual growth of 3.0% and GDP above 120 trillion yuan. For 2023 the author sees favourable conditions in the recovery of contact consumption, continued infrastructure and manufacturing investment, policy effects and a low 2022 base. Over the longer term Wang points to a working-age population of nearly 900 million, a large middle-income group, a complete industrial chain and room for fiscal and monetary policy, and puts potential growth at 5%–6%. The author also admits that three pressures remain: shrinking demand, supply shocks and weakening expectations.

Wang calls for coordinated management of several pairs of tasks and for improving social expectations and confidence. The priorities are expanding domestic demand, especially consumption; building a modern industrial system with key technology breakthroughs and food and energy security; implementing the Two Unwaverings; attracting more foreign investment; and defusing financial and property-sector risks. Read the original if you want a concise official-economist reading of the 2022 Central Economic Work Conference and the policy priorities it set for 2023.
quoteEn: Insufficient aggregate demand, especially declining consumer demand, is the prominent contradiction facing the economy at present.
quoteZh: 总需求不足尤其是消费需求下降是当前经济运行面临的突出矛盾。

glossary.explanation: The policy formula of unwaveringly consolidating and developing the public sector and unwaveringly encouraging, supporting and guiding the non-public sector. It is used to express equal treatment of state-owned and private firms.
An annual meeting of the Party and state leadership, usually held in December, that reviews the year's economy and sets the policy direction for the next year.

glossary.zh: 全面建设社会主义现代化国家
glossary.en: building a modern socialist country in all respects
glossary.explanation: The task set by the 20th Party Congress (2022) for the period after the completion of a moderately prosperous society, with the aim of making China a modern socialist country by 2035 and by mid-century.

t: The normative dimension of Marxism
zh: 马克思主义的规范性维度
paras: Marxism's standard self-descriptions include practicality, class character, criticality, revolutionary character and scientific character, but not "normativity". Xu Mengqiu argues that the concept should now be introduced, both to answer Western Marxism and Western scholars who criticise or misread Marxism and to widen the field of Marxist research. Xu's thesis is that Marxism has a normative dimension and normative content, and that its normative basis is fairly clear. The piece appeared in Guangming Daily on 26 September 2022.

The article has two parts. The first defines the "normative dimension" and contrasts it with a "cognitive dimension", using examples from Mencius, Confucius, daily life and engineering acceptance checks. The second turns to Marxism. It reports Habermas's claim that Marxist social theory lacks a clear normative basis, and the view of Allen Wood and Richard Miller (named in the text as Wood and Miller) that Marx was not concerned with justice and morality. It then answers these claims with passages from Marx and Engels.

Xu defines the normative dimension as starting from an "ought" grounded in some value outlook. From that position one affirms or negates what actually exists, then defends, corrects or reconstructs it. Xu groups description, explanation and empirical verification under a "cognitive dimension", and holds that the normative dimension also includes practical action. On Hume's problem of deriving "ought" from "is", Xu argues that the two activities arise together in practice, so neither is logically prior. Against Habermas, Xu holds that Marx's critical standpoint shifted with his worldview and his target, but two features run throughout. The first is a value foundation in the fundamental interests of the proletariat and working people, combined with a scientific grasp of historical laws, which together yield a revolutionary ideal. The second is a critique of capitalist reality and bourgeois ideology by both theoretical and material weapons, in the service of socialism and communism. Xu cites the Economic and Philosophic Manuscripts of 1844, the Theses on Feuerbach and Capital as evidence of this dimension.

Xu concludes that Marxist normativity is the unity of its value outlook and its sense of the "ought", with proletarian interests and historical laws as its ground. It joins the value yardstick to the scientific yardstick. Normativity and scientific character are essentially different but mutually dependent. Without science, Marxism would fall into utopian or ethical socialism. Marxists, Xu adds, do not claim value-neutrality, and openly present their doctrine as the proletariat's intellectual weapon. Read the original if you want a concise Chinese-language reply to Habermas and to the debate on Marx and justice, and a view of how Chinese Marxist theory is starting to adopt the vocabulary of normativity.
quoteEn: Marxism's normativity and its scientific character are two properties that differ in essence yet depend on each other.
quoteZh: 马克思主义的规范性与它的科学性是既有本质区别又相互依存的两种性质。

t: Guidance by Marxist scientific theory as the Chinese Communist Party's distinctive political character and powerful political strength
zh: 马克思主义科学理论指导是中国共产党的鲜明政治品格和强大政治优势
paras: Writing in Guangming Daily on 16 September 2022, shortly before the 20th Party Congress, Ruan Huarong and Chen Shuguang take up Xi Jinping's statement that being guided by Marxist scientific theory is the Party's distinctive political character and powerful political strength. They argue that the Party's achievements and the merits of socialism with Chinese characteristics come down, in the end, to the fact that Marxism works.

The commentary is organised in three parts. The first presents the adoption of Marxism as the choice of history and the people in modern China. The second reviews four historical periods: the New Democratic Revolution, socialist revolution and construction, reform and opening up, and the new era. The third turns to the continuing task of developing Marxism in China.

The authors first claim that after 1840 many programmes and isms were tried and failed, including reformism, liberalism, anarchism and pragmatism, and that only Marxism could resolve the nation's historic problems. They then describe a mutual relationship: Marxism did not fail the Party, and the Party did not fail Marxism. In their account Marxism gave rise to the Party and armed it, while the Party upheld and developed Marxism, defended it during a low ebb of world socialism and put it into practice in the largest developing country. Period by period, they link Mao Zedong Thought, Deng Xiaoping Theory, the Three Represents, the Scientific Outlook on Development and Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era to the successive leaps from 'standing up' to 'becoming prosperous' to 'becoming strong'.

The authors conclude that the adapting of Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times is far from finished. They hold that Marxism is a guide to action, not dogma, and that China's present practical innovation requires further integration of its basic principles with China's realities and with fine traditional Chinese culture. Theoretical innovation, they say, will let Marxism show greater persuasive force in China. Read the original if you want a concise example of how the Party's official narrative of Marxism's role in its history was presented to a general readership on the eve of the 20th Party Congress.
quoteEn: Without Marxism there would be no Communist Party of China today; without Marxism there would be no tomorrow for it either.
quoteZh: 没有马克思主义，就没有中国共产党的今天；离开了马克思主义，也没有中国共产党的明天。

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology associated with Xi Jinping, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018.
The guiding concept associated with Hu Jintao, stressing people-centred, comprehensive and sustainable development.
The theory associated with Jiang Zemin, holding that the Party represents advanced productive forces, advanced culture and the fundamental interests of the majority.

t: A community with a shared future for mankind: inheritance and innovation of Marx and Engels's theory of world history
zh: 人类命运共同体：马克思恩格斯世界历史理论的继承与创新
source: Journal of North China University of Water Resources and Electric Power (Social Sciences Edition), 2022 no. 5
paras: Marking the 90th anniversary of the publication of The German Ideology in 2022, Gong Liuji and Li Jing ask how the idea of a community with a shared future for mankind relates to the theory of world history that Marx and Engels developed in that work. They argue that the idea, put forward by Xi Jinping, upholds the core of the theory while innovating on it. In their view, understanding the link requires first grasping the theory's main content and then identifying what the idea adds.

The article has three main parts. The first reconstructs the theory of world history in The German Ideology: world history as an objective process, productive forces and universal intercourse as its basic drivers, and communism as its direction of development. The second shows how the idea of a community with a shared future for mankind inherits the theory in three dimensions: theoretical, practical and value. The third sets out three innovations, in development path, development method and development subject.

On inheritance, the authors say the idea follows the historical trend in a period of what they call great change unseen in a century, and keeps the theory's concern for harmony between humanity and nature, including green and sustainable development. They also argue that it carries on the value goal of the free and all-round development of the human being, contrasting the "false community" with the "true community" of The German Ideology. On innovation, they claim that Marx and Engels offered a scientific prediction without a concrete programme, whereas the idea supplies a practical plan. They further argue that its method is win-win cooperation rather than the violent revolution Marx and Engels envisaged, and that its subject extends from the proletariat to the peoples of the world. In their account, Marx and Engels were limited by their era in not foreseeing how capitalist societies would adjust themselves and improve welfare systems.

The authors conclude that the theory of world history provides the foundation for the idea, while the idea inherits, develops and renews the theory. They hold that it gives the theory a contemporary spirit and helps in viewing global trends and major problems through a world-historical lens, so as to promote common development. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Chinese scholars present Xi Jinping's concept as a continuation and update of Marx and Engels's world-history theory.
quoteEn: In terms of the development subject, the idea of a community with a shared future for mankind has achieved an innovation from the proletariat to the peoples of the world.
quoteZh: 人类命运共同体思想在发展主体上实现了从无产阶级到世界人民的创新。

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: A concept associated with Xi Jinping since the early 2010s, used to frame China's foreign policy and its vision of global governance around cooperation and shared interests among states.
Marx and Engels's account, set out chiefly in The German Ideology, of how separate national histories become a single world history through capitalism, the world market and universal intercourse.

keywords: community with a shared future for mankind

t: Grasping Marx and Engels's thought on ecology and science and technology
zh: 把握马克思恩格斯的生态科技思想
paras: Yang Xiaobin and Zhang Tian ask how Marx and Engels related science and technology to the natural environment. Writing in a newspaper commentary of 2022, they argue that the two thinkers developed a mature "ecological science-and-technology thought". In it, technology stands in a dialectical unity with humanity and nature, and its ecological effects depend on the social system that controls it.

The piece opens by noting that environmental protection has become a global concern in which technology is central. It then proceeds in three steps: the unity of technology, humans and nature; the damage done when technology is subordinated to capital; and the role of technology under communism.

In the authors' reading, nature is the basis of human activity, and technology emerges from humans' knowledge and transformation of nature. Technology can also open new sources of value by raising resource efficiency and recycling waste, which Marx called production excretions. Under capital, they argue, technology serves profit and accumulation. It leads to over-exploitation, pollution, the transfer of ecological damage worldwide, and a "rift" in the metabolism between humans and nature. Capitalist remedies are described as only temporary and superficial. Under communism, production would aim at use-value and meeting reasonable needs, with the means of production held in common. Technology would then transform nature in accordance with its laws and support the free and all-round development of the individual.

The authors conclude that technology itself does not damage nature and that the root of the problem lies in capitalist control. Only the replacement of capitalism by communism, in their account, can bring a lasting, rational metabolism and a "dual liberation" of humans and nature. Read the original if you want a concise overview of how Marx and Engels's classic passages are used to link ecology and technology.
quoteEn: Technology's damage to nature is not part of its own nature; on the contrary, it is the main path to resolving the ecological crisis.
quoteZh: 科技对于自然的损害并非其自身属性，相反，它是消解生态危机的主要路径。

t: The normative dimension of Marxism
zh: 马克思主义的规范性维度
paras: Jürgen Habermas holds that the normative foundations of Marxism are unclear, and some Anglophone scholars deny that Marx cared about justice and morality. Writing in Guangming Daily, Xu Mengqiu argues that Chinese Marxists must answer this charge. Xu's thesis is that Marxism has a normative dimension and normative content, and that its normative basis is fairly clear.

The article has two parts. The first defines the "normative dimension" and contrasts it with a "cognitive dimension", using examples from the Confucian tradition, daily life and engineering acceptance checks. The second sets out Habermas's critique, replies to it, and reads Marx's own texts, including the Economic and Philosophic Manuscripts of 1844, the Theses on Feuerbach and Capital.

Xu defines the normative dimension as starting from an "ought" grounded in some value outlook. From that standpoint one evaluates what exists, then defends, corrects or reconstructs it. The cognitive dimension, which Xu says covers description, explanation and empirical verification, treats things as they are. Xu holds that the two are interdependent and arise together in practice, so Hume's problem of deriving "ought" from "is" does not arise. Against Habermas, Xu argues that Marx's normative standpoint changed over time and differed by target. Two features run through all of it. The first is a value cornerstone, the fundamental interests of the proletariat and working people, joined to a scientific cornerstone, the grasp of historical laws. Together these yield a revolutionary ideal of the future society. The second is the use of both theoretical and material weapons, meaning the workers' movement, to criticise and deconstruct capitalism and its ideology. Xu cites Marx's critique of alienated labour, his remark that humans build "according to the laws of beauty", and the architect-and-bee passage in Capital as evidence of a normative standard.

Xu concludes that Marxism's normativity expresses its value pursuits and lofty ideals, and that the unity of value and scientific standards is its basis. Normativity and scientific character are distinct yet interdependent. Without science, Marxism would fall into utopian or ethical socialism. Marxists, Xu adds, never claim value neutrality and openly present their doctrine as the proletariat's intellectual weapon. Read the original if you want a Chinese Marxist reply to Habermas's charge about Marx's normative foundations, or a view of how Chinese scholars define "normative" and "cognitive" dimensions.
quoteEn: Marxism's normativity and its scientific character are two qualities that are essentially different yet mutually dependent.
quoteZh: 马克思主义的规范性与它的科学性是既有本质区别又相互依存的两种性质。

t: Reasoned, powerful, effective, useful
st: Reflections on why Marxism works
zh: 有理有力有效有用
zhSub: 关于马克思主义为什么行的思考
paras: Writing in Guangming Daily in September 2022, Ji Zhengju takes up the question of why Marxism "works" (xing). The commentary argues that Marxism's strength rests on four defining traits: it is scientific, rooted in the people, practical and open. On this basis, Ji holds, Marxism has changed the world and China, and it remains a guide for the future.

The piece has four sections. The first sets out the four traits. The second surveys Marxism's effects on world history: human civilisation, the history of socialism, national liberation movements, intellectual history, daily life, party development and the critique of capitalism. The third deals with China, and the fourth looks ahead and rebuts critics. Ji quotes Marx, Engels and Lenin, and also David McLellan and Robert Heilbroner.

Ji argues that Marxism's scientific character, its discovery of laws of history, socialism and proletarian party rule, is joined to a class standpoint that serves working people, so that it carries both truth and moral force. Its practical orientation, summed up in the call to change the world, and its openness to development explain its vitality. Ji traces this development from Lenin's theory of imperialism through to the sinified Marxism of Mao Zedong Thought, Deng Xiaoping Theory, the Three Represents, the Scientific Outlook on Development and Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era. For Ji, the October Revolution, the socialist camp and the rise of socialism with Chinese characteristics show Marxism's effect, and Western disorder shows that contemporary capitalism faces systemic crisis.

Ji concludes that critiques of Marxism, such as the theories that it has failed, is utopian or is outdated, have been refuted by facts. In Ji's view the basic contradictions of capitalism and the "two inevitables" still hold, and we still live in the historical era Marxism identified. Ji calls for continuing to uphold and develop Marxism and to arm minds with its latest sinified achievements. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party-affiliated theorists present the case for Marxism's continuing validity in the Xi Jinping era.
quoteEn: Marxism is not a static, closed and rigid system, but one that keeps innovating and stays open.
quoteZh: 马克思主义不是一个静态、封闭和僵化的体系，而是一个不断创新和开放的体系。

glossary.explanation: The Party's term for combining Marxism's basic principles with Chinese conditions and culture. It is presented as a process that produces new theoretical stages.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The official name for Xi Jinping's body of ideas, written into the Party constitution in 2017. Official texts describe it as the latest stage of sinified Marxism.
A guiding concept associated with Hu Jintao, adopted at the 17th Party Congress (2007). It stresses coordinated and sustainable development.
A theory associated with Jiang Zemin, holding that the Party represents advanced productive forces, advanced culture and the fundamental interests of the majority.
The official name for China's path since reform and opening up. It combines Party leadership and public ownership with market mechanisms.
The Marxist claim that capitalism will inevitably perish and socialism will inevitably triumph.

t: The "concept" mode of thinking in Marx's critique of political economy
zh: 马克思政治经济学批判的“概念”思维
paras: Zi Yang asks what allowed Marx to see through the errors of bourgeois political economy, and answers that it was a mode of thinking built on the "concept" (Begriff). The short essay, first published in the Chinese Social Sciences Today in September 2022, argues that this mode was inherited from Hegel and remade on the basis of historical materialism.

The article begins with Marx's Economic and Philosophic Manuscripts of 1844, where Zi locates the start of the critique of political economy and treats the Rheinische Zeitung period only as its "prehistory". It then moves through three stages: the task of the critique, the forms of empiricism Marx found in political economy, and the formation of the concept-based method. Zi's examples come from Smith, Ricardo and vulgar economics, and from Hegel's Logic and Marx's Capital.

Zi argues that the basic task of the critique is to "comprehend" (begreifen) the laws and categories of political economy. Bourgeois economics fails to do so because it takes private property as given and cannot derive its categories from it or connect them with each other. Zi traces this failure to the ahistorical treatment of the bourgeois mode of production. Zi sorts the resulting empiricism into three types. Smith places inner connections beside surface ones, as in his confusion of labour embodied with labour commanded. Ricardo tries to show directly that categories agree, and so skips the mediations between value, market price and production price. Vulgar economics takes forms of appearance for inner relations, as in its capital–interest formula. Zi then explains Hegel's concept as a subjective form of thought that also expresses the essence of the thing and grounds its truth. Marx, in Zi's reading, grounds it materialistically through Feuerbach's sensuousness and a social account of consciousness. In this sense a concept is a category that grasps the essential determination of a social relation, with "purity" and "inwardness".

Zi concludes that the critique of political economy can be completed only when the essential determinations of social relations are grasped through concepts and then traced through the necessary mediations to surface phenomena. Categories such as "wages" and "circulating capital" are criticised because they either miss the most adequate form of a social relation or confuse it with empirical appearance. Read the original if you want a compact account of the Hegelian roots of Marx's method and of how Smith, Ricardo and vulgar economics are classified as types of empiricism.
quoteEn: The "concept" mode of thinking in the critique of political economy is the result of Marx taking over Hegel's philosophy and reworking it on the basis of the materialist conception of history.
quoteZh: 政治经济学批判的“概念”思维，是马克思从黑格尔哲学承接，在唯物史观的基础上加以改造的成果。

t: The basic character of the materialist conception of history at its inception
zh: 唯物史观形成伊始的基本特征
paras: Was the materialist conception of history, when it first took shape, a "law of development of human history" (Engels's description) or a "guiding thread" for Marx's own research (Marx's description)? Ohmura Izumi, a Japanese Marx-Engels scholar, argues in this short commentary in the Chinese Social Sciences Today (2022) for the second reading. The author holds that Engels and Marx differed here, even though Marx did not object to Engels's name for the theory.

The piece starts from the history of the term. Engels coined "materialist conception of history" in his 1859 review of A Contribution to the Critique of Political Economy, and at Marx's funeral in 1883 he set the theory beside Darwin's theory of evolution. The commentary then turns to The German Ideology, in particular chapter 1 ("Feuerbach") and the dating of the theory's formation.

Ohmura rejects the view, associated with the new historical-critical edition of the Marx-Engels Complete Works (MEGA), that the critique of Stirner in the draft of chapter 3 is the decisive moment. The author identifies three core elements: the base–superstructure relationship, class struggle, and social revolution. Ohmura argues that these appear on manuscript pages 22–24, before the Stirner critique. The later discussion of ideology, on pages 30–35, is read as an extension of that framework, and the author says it also refined the framework itself, notably the thesis that conflicts arise from the contradiction between productive forces and forms of intercourse.

Ohmura concludes that in 1845 the theory was a hypothesis guiding Marx's study of socio-economic history. Surplus-value theory did not yet exist, and the structure of Capital was not yet in view. The author finds it strained to call the theory an evolutionary law at its birth, and calls for further discussion of how its character developed, including whether Engels's formulation is sound. Read the original if you follow the MEGA debate over The German Ideology and want a compact case for dating the theory's formation to chapter 1.
quoteEn: In my view, the basic character of the materialist conception of history at its inception should ultimately be a "guiding thread" for Marx's research on socio-economic history, that is, a hypothesis put forward in order to carry out analysis.
quoteZh: 我认为，唯物史观形成伊始的基本特性，说到底应该是马克思在进行社会经济史研究时的“引导线”，即为展开分析而提出的假说。

t: The basic spirit of Western modernity from a critical perspective
zh: 批判视角下的西方现代性基本精神
paras: What is the basic spiritual condition of Western modernity, and what do its achievements and limits look like when examined critically? Luo Qian argues that in modern society people have become masters of their own lives and no longer submit one-sidedly to external others or transcendent principles. The article holds that the modernity that began in the West rests on five basic aspects of spirit: secularity, individuality, creativity, practicality and positivity. Each marks a great achievement of modern emancipation and also its fundamental historical limit.

This short piece, first published in the China Social Sciences Today newspaper in 2022, takes the five aspects in turn. Luo contrasts each with the pre-modern world, mainly medieval Christian theology. Luo also draws on Nietzsche, Heidegger and Marx, and refers to critiques of instrumental rationality. The closing section turns from the level of ideas to the social and historical foundations of these ideas.

For Luo, secularity removes the transcendent realm as the source of value, so that human reason, interests, rights and desires gain legitimacy, but belief, the sublime and great things fade and value nihilism arrives. Individuality then frees the person from family, caste and rank, and Luo cites Marx on the historical roots of this individual in the dissolution of feudal society and the new productive forces. Creativity makes reality a product of human practice, so that nature, society and life become human artefacts, and Luo warns this may yield a reified world in the human image. Practicality turns relations into calculation, in which human dignity becomes exchange value and reason is reduced to instrumental reason. Positivity makes verifiable science the governing norm and an ideology, which squeezes out the sacred, the mysterious and the poetic.

Luo concludes that interpreting or criticising modernity cannot stop at the level of ideas and must reach its social and historical basis. In this reading, Marx's critique of capitalist modernity supplies the ontological foundation of historical materialism for such criticism. It shows the historical conditions, achievements and limits of Western modernity's spirit. Luo adds that this critique provides the intellectual basis for Chinese modernization and for a new form of human civilisation, and points toward the sublation of Western modernity. Read the original if you want a compact Chinese philosophical account of modernity's five spiritual principles and of how Marxism is used to criticise them.
quoteEn: Viewed critically, the establishment of these five basic spirits of modernity signifies both the great achievement of Western modern emancipation and its fundamental historical limit.
quoteZh: 从批判性的角度来看，这五种现代性基本精神的确立，既意味着西方现代解放的伟大成就，也意味着其根本的历史限度。

glossary.explanation: The official term for China's own path of modernization, promoted by the Party leadership and presented as distinct from Western models.

glossary.en: a new form of human civilisation
glossary.explanation: An official formulation, prominent since 2021, for the civilisational form that Chinese modernization is said to create, in contrast to Western modernity.
The Hegelian and Marxist idea of Aufhebung: to negate something while preserving and transcending its valuable content.

t: The threefold critique of modernity in the Economic and Philosophic Manuscripts of 1844
zh: 《1844年经济学哲学手稿》对现代性的三重批判
paras: Liu Rongjun and Zhang Leiyu ask how Marx criticises modernity in the Economic and Philosophic Manuscripts of 1844. They define modernity as the union of the logic of capital with modern metaphysics, a union that shapes the economy, politics, culture, ecology and the structure of thought. Their thesis is that the Manuscripts mount a threefold critique: an economic-philosophical one, a socio-political one and a critique of the philosophy of subjectivity. The piece first appeared in the Chinese Social Sciences Today in September 2022.

The article moves through the three critiques in turn. The first concerns classical political economy; the second concerns false forms of communism and Marx's own account of communism; the third concerns Hegel's philosophy of the subject and his dialectic. The authors present the three as stages from surface to depth, each sublating the one before. Their starting point is Marx's reading of Hegel's philosophy of right, which led him to treat the relation of industry and wealth to the political sphere as a main problem of the modern age.

On the first level, the authors argue that classical economics defends a "capital justice" that treats the separation of labour from its object as legitimate. In their account it affirms labour in theory while negating the human being in practice, because workers live under fourfold alienation. It never examines private property, the premise of that justice, and so cannot identify capital as the abstract subject governing modern society. On the second level, Marx criticises "crude communism" for levelling private property and so leaving the logic of capital intact. He also criticises a politically minded communism that grasps only capital's negative side. Against these he sets communism as the positive sublation of private property and self-alienation, realised in an "association of free individuals". On the third level, Marx rescues the real, sensuous, objectifying human being from Hegel's abstract subject. The authors argue that he builds a materialist dialectic from Hegel's historical sense and judges that Hegel grasped labour only as abstract mental labour, so that his result is a "revolution inside the skull".

The authors conclude that the three dimensions form a totalising dialectical picture that helped drive Marx's critique of ideology and the founding of historical materialism. Citing Xi Jinping's remark that we still live in the historical epoch Marxism identified, they hold that Marx's way of thinking and method remain useful for reading the present era. They tie this to the generation and development of a new form of human civilisation that sublates capitalist modernity. Read the original if you want a compact, Chinese-language reading of the 1844 Manuscripts as a layered critique of modernity and of its links to Hegel and classical economics.
quoteEn: These three dimensions present a logical progression from the surface to the depths.
quoteZh: 这三重向度呈现为由表层到深层的逻辑递进。

glossary.explanation: The authors' label for the conception of justice that classical economics defends. It treats the separation of labour from its product, and the capitalist's appropriation of that product, as natural and legitimate.

glossary.en: a new form of human civilisation
glossary.explanation: A phrase in official Chinese discourse for the civilisational form that Chinese modernization is said to create. It is presented as going beyond Western capitalist modernity.
The rendering of Hegel's Aufhebung. It means to negate something while preserving and lifting its valid content to a higher level.

t: Capital and the absurd "Sybel debate"
zh: 《资本论》与荒谬的“西贝尔之辩”
paras: Zhang Yibing, in a newspaper commentary first published in the Chinese Social Sciences Today in September 2022, revisits a little-known episode after the publication of Marx's Capital. In March 1872 the Munich historian Heinrich von Sybel gave two public lectures to entrepreneurs, "The Teachings of Contemporary Socialism and Communism", attacking Marx's theory of surplus value and defending capitalists. Zhang calls this the "Sybel debate" and argues that it is absurd and cannot hide the objective laws of the capitalist mode of production that Capital reveals.

Zhang first sets the background. Sybel's attack came mainly in the first lecture, and Marx knew of it. The Russian populist Mikhailovsky later amplified Sybel's views in an 1877 article. In his letter to the editors of Otechestvennye Zapiski, Marx answered only the misreading of his views on paths of social development, not Sybel's claims. The commentary then reports Sybel's two main arguments and answers them in turn.

Sybel first denies primitive accumulation in Germany. Zhang reads this as a cover for his real aim, which is to deny that capitalists appropriate workers' surplus value without payment. Sybel cites Marx's passage on the architect and the bee to argue that purposeful labour belongs to whoever sets the goal. In factories that is the manufacturer, while workers are merely "living tools". Engineers and managers, he says, only serve the owner's goals, so the owner's "mental labour" creates value and surplus value. Zhang replies that Sybel confuses two kinds of purpose: the concrete aim of labour in making use-values, and the capitalist's drive to accumulate profit. The worker's subjective representation of the task cannot be separated from the worker, even on an automated line.

Zhang lists five further flaws. Sybel misreads how the position of workers changes under mechanised production. He ignores the creative role of scientists and technicians. He misses that the factory owner is only a personification of capital relations and a puppet of the law of value. He overlooks that the owner's managerial and coordinating work is in essence capital's appropriation of the social combining power and technological productivity that workers and scientific staff create. Zhang concludes that, over 150 years after Capital, Marx's theory of surplus value remains a powerful tool for analysing contemporary capitalism. Read the original if you want a short Chinese Marxist rebuttal of a nineteenth-century apologist for capital, or an example of how Chinese scholars currently defend the labour theory of value.
quoteEn: The essence of Sybel's argument lies not in opposing Marx's account of primitive accumulation, but in his determined denial of the economic exploitation, revealed in Capital, by which capitalists appropriate without payment the surplus value workers create.
quoteZh: 西贝尔之辩的本质不在于反对马克思的资本原始积累说,而在于他极力否认马克思《资本论》所揭示的资本家无偿占有工人创造的剩余价值的经济剥削。

t: The dialectic of modernity in Capital
zh: 《资本论》的现代性辩证法
source: Chinese Social Sciences Today (中国社会科学报), 13 September 2022
paras: Bai Gang asks how Marx's Capital, as a critique of political economy, offers a comprehensive account of modernity. This short commentary, first published in Chinese Social Sciences Today in 2022, argues that Capital is a 'higher-level' exposition of modernity. In Bai's reading, it identifies capital as the secularised successor to God, and then proposes to limit and transform capital in order to move beyond it.

The article is organised in three parts. The first treats modernity as the process of 'secularising God', drawing on Nietzsche, Weber, Leo Strauss and Scheler. The second examines capital as the 'fetish' that expresses modernity. The third sets out what Bai calls Capital's 'scheme' for modernity: putting 'traffic lights' on capital. Bai draws throughout on Marx, and on Engels's review of Capital.

Bai holds that modernity replaces the medieval order of faith with the rule of capital. Capital moves from commodity capital to money capital to interest-bearing capital, an 'automatic fetish' that Bai says carries the 'spiritual honour' God lost in the modern age. It rules through 'equality' and exchange, not force, which Bai links to the three fetishisms of commodity, money and capital. People gain independence from gods, but remain dependent on things. Bai argues that Marx neither rejects capital nor accepts it as eternal. He recognises its 'civilising side' and seeks to reshape it. Cooperative factories and joint-stock companies, and the replacement of wage labour by cooperative labour, are the means. The aim is the all-round developed individual and the 'realm of freedom'.

Bai concludes that the dialectic of modernity in Capital transcends capitalism and also capital itself, 'surpassing capital through capital'. Marx's remedy for a modernity dominated by capital is a fuller modernity of free, all-round individual development, reached by re-establishing individual ownership and abolishing wage labour. Bai calls Capital the 'highest-level revolution of modernity' and of freedom. Read the original if you want a concise Chinese Marxist interpretation of Capital through the themes of secularisation, fetishism and the limits of capital.
quoteEn: The limits of capital are the limits of modernity.
quoteZh: 资本的界限就是现代性的界限。

t: The international order from the perspective of the philosophy of history
st: On Great-Power Games and the Future World
zh: 历史哲学视域中的国际格局
zhSub: 读《大国博弈与未来世界》
paras: This is a book review, first published in China Social Sciences Today in July 2022. Yang Haifeng reviews Han Zhen's Great-Power Games and the Future World: International Relations from the Perspective of the Philosophy of History (Central Party School Press, 2022). Yang argues that the book treats history, the present and the future as one whole, and so offers a distinctive way of understanding today's global order and the place of socialism with Chinese characteristics within it. Yang credits it with academic and practical value for grasping current upheavals.
