Yang first sets out why a country's development now depends on the global order, since the world has moved from a trend of world history in Marx's day, through the imperialist era and late-twentieth-century globalization, to close interdependence. The review lists the book's eight chapters and concluding remarks. They run from the new development pattern and the North–South and East–West divides, through capitalism versus socialism and geopolitics, to China–US rivalry, future trends and the humanistic basis of a community with a shared future for mankind.

Yang identifies three strengths. First, the book uses a large-scale historical outlook rooted in Hegel's and Marx's philosophy of history. It stresses that geopolitics shifts with changes in economic, political and military strength, and it treats culture as the basis of international relations. Second, it applies contradiction analysis. It traces the internal contradictions of states, for example the economic, political, identity and cultural crises Han attributes to the United States, and it identifies the principal contradictions among powers. In Yang's account, Han reads China–US rivalry as a result of US efforts to keep its post-1991 superpower status against a rising China. Third, Yang presents a community with a shared future for mankind as a solution that moves beyond the contradictions of power balances. In Yang's reading, it develops Marx's idea of an association of free individuals and also draws on Chinese ideas such as harmony and the mean.

Yang concludes that the book takes a pragmatic line. It asks readers to recognise the continuing capacities of advanced capitalist countries as well as their problems, and to weigh these against China's own features and strengths when deciding strategy and pace. This, Yang says, strengthens historical confidence and initiative, and becoming a conscious historical subject is both the core theme of the philosophy of history and the self-understanding China should seek in the global order. Read the original if you want a concise Chinese Marxist assessment of a recent Party School work on geopolitics, China–US relations and the philosophical grounding of the community with a shared future for mankind.
quoteEn: To be a conscious historical subject is both the fundamental theme of the philosophy of history and the rational self-awareness we should strive for when facing the global order.
quoteZh: 做一个自觉的历史主体，这既是历史哲学的根本主题，也是面对全球格局时我们要力求达到的理性自识。

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.literal: community of common destiny for humanity
glossary.explanation: A foreign-policy concept associated with Xi Jinping since around 2012–13. It calls for cooperative, shared-interest international relations and is presented in official discourse as an alternative to power politics.
The official name for China's current political and economic system and the Party's guiding theory. It dates from the early reform era under Deng Xiaoping.
An official formulation from 2020 that stresses the domestic economic cycle while keeping domestic and international circulation mutually reinforcing.

keywords: community with a shared future for mankind

t: Grasping the materialist conception of history through the dual character of labour
zh: 从劳动的双重属性把握唯物史观
paras: How should labour be understood, and what place does it hold in the materialist conception of history? Li Jili, in a newspaper article from the Chinese Social Sciences Today (2022), argues that the question decides the future of historical materialism. The article contends that Marx's concept of labour has a natural and a social aspect, and that this dual character is the key to the materialist conception of history as a whole, not only to political economy.

The article begins with two rival misreadings. Li says Jürgen Habermas, a figure of Western Marxism, reduces Marx's labour to Weberian purposive-instrumental action and so proposes to reconstruct historical materialism. Moishe Postone, in Li's account, treats labour as a form peculiar to capitalism and so cuts Marx's thought in two. Li then moves from labour as a philosophical concept, through the concepts of productive forces and relations of production, to the objective laws of social development, and finally to Capital.

Li first argues that Marx's labour is a philosophical concept, taken from Hegel's insight into labour and then freed of its idealism. Labour in this sense is the real social labour of a whole society, not that of an isolated individual. It therefore contains both the object-relation between people and nature and the social relations among people. Second, Li holds that the productive forces come from labour's natural side and the relations of production from its social side. Productive forces and relations of production are not two independent things that interact. They are two aspects of material production. Li maintains that productive forces determine relations of production by way of objectified labour, in which "dead labour" becomes the material carrier of objectified social relations. Third, Li says the same route explains why the products of human activity can harden into an objective material force that escapes human control. This force has its own logic, which is why historical laws can count as objective laws unlike natural ones.

Li concludes that Marx's remark in Capital that the dual character of labour is "the pivot" for understanding political economy has long been read too narrowly. In Li's view the dual character is equally the pivot for understanding the materialist conception of history. If it is treated only as a feature of capitalism, Li warns, historical materialism is denied universal validity, and it cannot then guide socialist practice. Read the original if you want a short, philosophically oriented Chinese reply to Habermas and Postone on labour and historical materialism.
quoteEn: The dual character of labour is not only the pivot for Marx's critique of political economy and for understanding his political economy, but also the pivot for understanding the materialist conception of history.
quoteZh: 劳动的双重属性不仅是马克思展开政治经济学批判和理解其政治经济学的枢纽，也是理解唯物史观的枢纽。

glossary.explanation: The Chinese term for Marx and Engels's theory of history, also called historical materialism. It explains social change through material production and the relation between productive forces and relations of production.

In Marx's Capital the term refers to the concrete and abstract aspects of commodity-producing labour. Li uses it in a wider sense, for labour's natural aspect (people and nature) and its social aspect (people and people).

A tradition of Marxist thought in Western Europe that began with Lukács, Korsch and Gramsci and includes the Frankfurt School. Chinese scholars often discuss it critically, as the article does with Habermas.
Chinese translations use the term for Marx's objectification and for reification in Lukács's sense. Li uses it to say that social relations take material form in accumulated past labour.

t: Marx's concept of cooperation and its contemporary significance
zh: 马克思的协作概念及其当代意义
source: Chinese Social Sciences Today (中国社会科学报), 25 August 2022
paras: Pan Shenyang asks what Marx's concept of cooperation (Kooperation) contributes to his critique of capitalism and to his vision of socialism. The short commentary argues that cooperation is the footing of Marx's critique and, in later work, the basis of his account of a practical path towards communism.

The article draws on Capital and its manuscripts, Engels's letter to Bebel, and Marx's engagement in the 1860s with Lassalleanism, the International Workingmen's Association, Owen and the Chartist Ernest Jones. It first sets out four features of cooperation, then turns to its role in the critique of capitalism, and finally to cooperative production under socialism.

Pan holds that under capitalism the social productive power created by cooperation is appropriated without payment and appears as the productive power of capital. Two further critiques follow: capitalist management presents itself as neutral while concealing exploitation, and workers within cooperative labour are reified into mere parts. Marx and Jones, Pan says, criticised isolated, competing cooperatives such as Rochdale while valuing features of others, and Marx called cooperatives "possible" communism. Marx gave no detailed blueprint but two principles: proletarian dictatorship as the political precondition, and drawing on new social elements generated within capitalism, such as the factory and credit systems.

Pan concludes that Marx's cooperative conception stresses both subjective self-emancipation and objective conditions, so it avoids being either utopian or blindly activist. The piece offers little explicit discussion of present-day application beyond this. Read the original if you want a compact guide to how Marx's notion of cooperation links his critique of capitalism to the cooperative form.
quoteEn: Cooperative production is one of the principled stipulations that Marx and Engels laid down for socialism.
quoteZh: 协作生产是马克思恩格斯对社会主义的原则规定之一。

glossary.explanation: Marxist term for working-class political rule during the transition from capitalism to communism. Pan presents it as the political precondition for workers' self-management.

t: Continuously advancing the adaptation of Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
zh: 不断推进马克思主义中国化时代化
paras: Published in the China Social Sciences Today in August 2022, this commentary takes up Xi Jinping's speech at the study session for provincial and ministerial-level leading cadres on implementing the sixth plenary session of the 19th Central Committee (2021). Wang and Wang aim to explain why Marxism "works", why it works specifically through being adapted to the Chinese context and the needs of our times, and how that adaptation should continue. Their answer is that Marxism's scientific and practical character requires constant adaptation, which they say the Party's history confirms.

The article follows the three questions in three sections. The first treats the nature and mission of Marxism, drawing on Xi's 2018 speech marking Marx's 200th birthday. The second argues that Marxism has to be adapted to China, citing Marx, Lenin and Mao Zedong and then surveying the Party's theoretical stages from Mao Zedong Thought to Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era. The third sets out requirements for the new era.

In the authors' account, Marxism works because it reveals the laws of social development, is the first system of thought for the people's own liberation, and is an open theory that develops with the times. They hold that since Marxism supplies only general principles, applying them in a country means examining national particularities, and that adapting Marxism to China combines upholding it with developing it. On this reading, the Party's history is one of successive adaptations: Mao Zedong Thought, the theoretical system of socialism with Chinese characteristics, and Xi Jinping Thought. The authors say this success has shifted the contest between socialism and capitalism in socialism's favour.

For the new era, the authors call for continuing the Two Integrations, combining Marxist principles with China's concrete realities and with its fine traditional culture, so that China makes original contributions to adapting Marxism to the times. They also call for a global outlook, citing the idea of a community with a shared future for mankind, and say that answering questions such as how to rebuild the post-pandemic world requires effort from Marxists worldwide. Read the original if you want a compact example of how official commentary in 2022 framed the logic and history of adapting Marxism to China.
quoteEn: Adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times is both an objective need for solving China's problems and an inherent requirement for moving Marxism forward.
quoteZh: 马克思主义中国化时代化既是解决中国问题的客观需要，又是推动马克思主义向前发展的内在要求。

glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's formula (2021) for combining Marxism's basic tenets with China's concrete realities and with its fine traditional culture.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into its constitution in 2017 and presented as the latest stage in adapting Marxism to China.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's concept of international relations and global governance, promoted since 2013 as a framework for shared development and cooperation.

keywords: sixth plenary session of the 19th Central Committee
community with a shared future for mankind

t: Creative theoretical contributions to the socialist market economy
zh: 对社会主义市场经济的创造性理论贡献
paras: Writing in the Party-run Economic Daily in September 2022, Gu Hailiang argues that Xi Jinping's economic thought makes creative theoretical contributions to the socialist market economy. Gu identifies three areas: the government–market relationship as the core issue of economic reform, the basic economic system as the defining character of the socialist market economy, and the nature and behavioural laws of capital. In Gu's account, these contributions enrich the political economy of socialism with Chinese characteristics and give Marxist political economy a new content for the twenty-first century.

The article follows the Party's changing positions from the Third Plenum of the 11th Central Committee (1978) to the Third Plenum of the 18th Central Committee (2013) and the Fourth Plenum of the 19th Central Committee (2019). It then turns to the methodology Gu finds in Xi's thinking and ends with a section on capital under socialism. It is built as four sections, each pairing documents and Xi's statements with Gu's commentary.

Gu first traces a progression from adjusting economic mechanisms, to reforming the economic structure, to settling the system. Along the way, the market's role moved from supplementary to "basic" and then, in 2013, to "decisive" in allocating resources. Gu reads this as a shift from the market being merely compatible with socialism to being combined with it. Second, Gu holds that treating the socialist market economy as part of the basic economic system is an original contribution: public ownership as the mainstay, distribution according to work and Party leadership give the market economy its socialist character, and "dialectics" and "two-sidedness" govern the state–market and public–private relationships. Third, Gu notes that Marx, Engels, Lenin and Stalin did not address capital under socialism. Gu presents Xi's approach as recognising several forms of capital, state, collective, private, foreign and mixed, whose positive role should be used and whose negative effects controlled. This means curbing the disorderly expansion of capital and setting "traffic lights" for it.

Gu concludes that upholding the direction of socialist market-economy reform is a key principle of the political economy of socialism with Chinese characteristics. Gu also concludes that Xi's economic thought gives that theory a new content in the sense of adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times. Read the original if you want a concise, officially aligned account of how Party theorists trace the doctrinal stages of the socialist market economy and frame the Party's approach to capital.
quoteEn: Establishing the basic-economic-system character of the socialist market economy is a great pioneering step by our Party in the theory and practice of scientific socialism, and a notable theoretical creation of Xi Jinping's economic thought.
quoteZh: 确定社会主义市场经济体制的基本经济制度性质，是我们党对科学社会主义理论和实践的一个伟大创举，也是习近平经济思想显著的理论创造。

glossary.explanation: The Party's official description of China's economic system, adopted as the reform goal at the 14th Party Congress in 1992. It combines market allocation of resources with public ownership and Party leadership.

The body of economic ideas attributed to Xi Jinping, formally presented as part of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era. It was first named as a guiding framework in 2017.

glossary.zh: 社会主义基本经济制度
glossary.explanation: The Party's formula for the core structure of the economy. The Fourth Plenum of the 19th Central Committee (2019) defined it as public ownership as the mainstay alongside diverse forms of ownership, distribution according to work as the mainstay alongside other forms of distribution, and the socialist market economy.

glossary.zh: 马克思主义政治经济学中国化时代化
glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
glossary.explanation: The official formula for the Party's claim that it develops Marxist theory by fitting it to Chinese conditions and to contemporary circumstances.

t: Understanding "Marxism works" through the essence of the epoch
zh: 从时代精华角度读懂“马克思主义行”
paras: This short commentary in Guangming Daily takes up Marx's dictum that every true philosophy is the spiritual quintessence of its time. Jia Yingjian argues that the line explains why Marxist philosophy keeps pace with the demands of the epoch. The author presents Marxism as an innovative, open body of theory and an intellectual forerunner of social progress.

The piece begins from Xi Jinping's reaffirmation of the saying at a Politburo study session of the 18th Central Committee. It then sets out four claims about how Marxist philosophy relates to its era, and closes with the task of building a modern socialist country.

Jia argues that Marxist philosophy is a scientific theory grounded in its epoch and develops historically as social being and social life change. It advances through answering the questions of the age, and the author credits the Party leadership since the 18th Party Congress (2012) with answering the questions of what kind of socialism with Chinese characteristics to uphold and how. Marxist philosophy also marks the height of the spirit of the age, and the author says the Party has combined it with the creative transformation of traditional Chinese culture. Finally, it drives change in the epoch and shows the power of "changing the world".

Jia concludes that applying contemporary Chinese Marxist theory in practice will let the Party meet the "great test" of building a modern socialist country. The author calls for stronger ability to grasp and steer the times. Read the original if you want a brief example of how official commentary links Marx's view of philosophy and the epoch to Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era.
quoteEn: Marxist philosophy is adept at advancing innovation by answering the questions of the age.
quoteZh: 马克思主义哲学善于在回答时代之问中推进创新。

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018.
The official name for China's path and system of socialism since reform and opening up.

t: "People make their own history"
zh: “人们自己创造自己的历史”
paras: Ye Zexiong and Zhao Ting, in a commentary first published in Guangming Daily in August 2022, ask what Marx and Engels meant by history and who makes it. Starting from Xi Jinping's statement that the people are the creators of history, they argue that the formulation in The Holy Family, that history is nothing but the activity of human beings pursuing their own aims, offers a worldview and a method for grasping the direction of historical development.

The piece has three sections. The first sets the masses as creators of history against idealist history. The second treats history as practical activity with purposes and an orientation. The third turns to the Chinese Communist Party's mass-line view of history, from Mao Zedong and Deng Xiaoping to Xi Jinping.

The authors contend that idealist history, which credits emperors, generals and heroes, errs epistemologically by taking ideas and motives as causes, and errs in class terms by serving exploiting classes. Historical materialism instead starts from "real individuals" and the resultant of many wills (Engels's "parallelogram of forces"), and holds that the masses create material and spiritual wealth and decide social change. Ye and Zhao add that history is practice, and that its purposes are set by people from their own needs and the possibilities reality offers, not by "reason" or the "absolute spirit".

They conclude that since the 18th Party Congress (2012) the Party has pursued a people-centred approach to development and has relied on the people to eliminate absolute poverty, build a moderately prosperous society and fight Covid-19. Reaching the second centenary goal of a modern socialist country, the authors say, requires fuller use of the masses' initiative and creativity. Read the original if you want a short, official-style statement of how the mass-line view of history is derived from Marx and Engels and applied in Party discourse.
quoteEn: In the course of human social history, practice, as the endogenous driving force of historical development, keeps pushing the productive forces forward.
quoteZh: 在人类社会历史进程中，实践作为推动社会历史发展的内生性动力，促使生产力不断向前发展

glossary.explanation: The Party's term for the view that the people, not elites, are the decisive force in history. It is presented as an application of historical materialism and ties into the Party's "mass line".

glossary.zh: 以人民为中心的发展思想
glossary.pinyin: yǐ rénmín wéi zhōngxīn de fāzhǎn sīxiǎng
glossary.explanation: A slogan associated with Xi Jinping since the 18th Party Congress (2012), stating that development should serve and rely on the people.
A long-standing Chinese goal of general, moderate prosperity. The Party declared it "fully built" in 2021.

t: Grasping the power of thought and drawing on the strength of truth
st: On studying volume four of Xi Jinping: The Governance of China
zh: 感悟思想伟力 汲取真理力量
paras: This commentary, published in Guangming Daily on 25 August 2022, is a study guide to the fourth volume of Xi Jinping: The Governance of China. Wang Rui presents the volume as an authoritative account of how the Party led the people in responding to changed circumstances and opening a new situation. The author argues that studying it closely helps Party members, cadres and the public to understand why the Party has succeeded so far and how it can keep succeeding, and so to understand the Chinese path, Chinese governance and the reasoning behind them.

The piece is organised around five things readers are urged to grasp. They are the essence of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era as a new leap in adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times; the Party's character of confronting risks and waging struggle; the vision of a community with a shared future for mankind; the political resolve to lead a great social revolution through a great self-reform; and the strengthening of historical confidence and a sense of responsibility. Wang draws throughout on the volume, on Xi's statements and on the 2021 Party resolution on the Party's historical achievements and experience.

On theory, Wang follows the resolution in describing Xi's thought as twenty-first-century Marxism that has achieved a new leap, and says the volume sets out the "Ten Clarifications" and explains Chinese modernization. On struggle, the author describes a world of great change, the pandemic and mounting risks, and holds that national rejuvenation will not come easily, so cadres must sharpen their ability to struggle. On self-reform, Wang presents it as the Party's second answer to the question of escaping the historical cycle of rise and fall, after Mao Zedong's 1945 answer of supervision by the people, and links it to full and rigorous self-governance of the Party.

Wang also says the community with a shared future for mankind rejects zero-sum thinking and answers talk of a "China threat". The article ends by calling on cadres to treat the Party's centenary experience as a source of historical confidence, and to see the establishment of Xi's core position and the guiding status of his thought as the most important political outcome of the new era. Read the original if you want a compact example of how the official press framed the study of this volume in 2022.
quoteEn: The Party's vanguard character is not innate; it has been forged through continual self-reform.
quoteZh: 党的先进性不是天生的，是在不断自我革命中淬炼而成的。

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018. It is presented officially as the latest stage of adapting Marxism to China.

glossary.zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化
glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
glossary.explanation: The official formula for the Party's project of combining Marxist principles with Chinese conditions and with contemporary developments. The 'times' element was added in the 2020s to the older phrase 'Sinification of Marxism'.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's foreign-policy concept, promoted since 2012–2013, which calls for shared security, development and global governance. Official texts present it as an alternative to zero-sum international relations.

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.literal: comprehensively and strictly governing the Party
glossary.explanation: A slogan adopted after the 18th Party Congress (2012) for strict Party discipline, anti-corruption campaigns and institution-building within the Party.
The official term for China's own path of modernisation, which the Party contrasts with Western models. It was elaborated especially from 2021–2022.

keywords: Xi Jinping: The Governance of China

t: The German Ideology in the development of Marx's thought
zh: 马克思思想发展中的《德意志意识形态》
paras: Niu Ziniu asks what place The German Ideology should occupy in Marx's intellectual development. The commentary, first published in the Chinese Social Sciences Today in July 2022, argues that the manuscript, now widely seen as a birthplace of the materialist conception of history, represents only a rudimentary form of that theory. In Niu's account, it comes before two decisive turning points and should be assessed with that in mind.

Niu locates the manuscript between the Economic and Philosophic Manuscripts of 1844 and the Theses on Feuerbach on one side, and later works on the other. The first public statement of the materialist conception of history was The Poverty of Philosophy (1847), and its classic formulation is the 1859 Preface to A Contribution to the Critique of Political Economy. The author marks two nodes: the 'historical principle' (every principle has its century) and the completion of the critique of political economy in the Grundrisse and the 1859 work. The text proceeds in three steps: what The German Ideology established, what it left unfinished, and how later work corrected it.

Niu credits the manuscript with establishing the basic content of the materialist conception of history. It brings Marx's critique of German idealism and of Feuerbach's old materialism into a social-historical frame, moving from 'real individuals' and their life-process rather than from abstract categories. It also links this to a revolutionary political stance. Niu then argues that the manuscript does not apply the historicity of categories to itself. Its general concept of 'production' and its use of 'capital' for feudal society treat categories of capitalist society as timeless, and Niu says this shows a residue of Hegelian derivation from abstractions. Marx's own self-criticism in the Grundrisse is cited as evidence. There Marx holds that thought must move from the abstract to the concrete, and that materialism differs from idealism because it treats every abstraction as the product of a given historical concrete totality.

Niu concludes that Marx did not first complete the materialist conception of history and then apply it to political economy. Rather, he built and refined it through the critique of political economy. The Hegelian residue is, in Niu's view, an immaturity and not a distinctive value of the manuscript. By 1859 its content had largely been sublated into the later work, which Niu offers as one reason Marx abandoned publishing it and left it to 'the gnawing criticism of the mice'. Niu grants its philological value but calls for a cautious, realistic assessment of its place. Read the original if you want a short, critical account of why The German Ideology should be read as an early stage in Marx's development and not as his mature statement of historical materialism.
quoteEn: Marx did not first complete the materialist conception of history and then apply it to the critique of political economy; he gradually established and perfected it in the course of unfolding that critique.
quoteZh: 马克思并不是首先完成了唯物史观，尔后将其运用于政治经济学批判，而是在政治经济学批判的展开过程中逐步建立和完善了唯物史观。

glossary.explanation: The Chinese standard term for historical materialism, Marx and Engels's theory that material production and social relations shape history and ideas.
Marx's long-term project of analysing capitalism by criticising classical political economy, running from the 1850s manuscripts to Capital.

The idea, which Marx puts forward in The Poverty of Philosophy, that every category and principle belongs to a particular historical period. The article treats it as one of two turning points in Marx's development.
The Chinese rendering of Hegel's and Marx's Aufhebung: to negate while preserving and carrying forward in a higher form.

t: Practical materialism from the perspective of the reconciliation of body and mind
zh: 从肉体与精神和解的视角看实践唯物主义
paras: Since reform and opening up, Chinese Marxist philosophy has given weight to the foundational status of practice and has often understood itself as "practical materialism". Writing in the Chinese Social Sciences Today in July 2022, Wang Xiaosheng notes that scholars still disagree on how to read this, chiefly over whether practice or matter comes first. Wang argues that neither side can settle the dispute, because both assume that body and mind are separate, and that this assumption itself needs to be examined. The article's answer is that Marxism seeks a reconciliation of body and mind, and that practical materialism is best understood on that basis.

The article is a short philosophical commentary in three parts. It begins with Engels's account of the basic question of philosophy and its roots in early humanity's belief that thinking is the activity of a soul. It then turns to Adorno and Horkheimer's Dialectic of Enlightenment and to Marx's Economic and Philosophic Manuscripts of 1844 and The German Ideology. Finally it applies the reading to Marx's critique of the Young Hegelians, to the notion of "reality", and to the theory–practice relation.

Wang argues that the opposition of body and mind is a basic fact of human survival, not merely a mistaken idea. Drawing on the Odysseus and Sirens episode in Dialectic of Enlightenment, Wang holds that humans must restrain their bodily nature to survive, and that this opposition underlies civilisation and the modern subject–object split. Fixing the opposition as the only mode of existence is also mistaken, in Wang's view, because it yields an instrumental reason that drives the body to self-harm. Body and mind are neither naturally unified nor wholly opposed; Wang reads Marx's account of communism as resolving the conflict between humans and nature, including their own nature, as pointing to a dialectical unity-in-opposition, or reconciliation. On this basis Wang treats dialectical and practical materialism as essentially the same: material priority is granted within the opposition, but thought is carried into practice, and Marx's "practical subject" is the reconciled living person.

Wang concludes that Marx's critique of the Young Hegelians, his idea of "reality" as distinct from Hegel's, and his words as bound to reality all depend on this reconciliation. Wang warns that purely spiritual "love" can turn cold and even justify killing. In Wang's view, practical materialism overturns the body–mind and subject–object framework, marking a major change in the history of philosophy and offering guidance for present-day social practice. Read the original if you want a compact Chinese argument that links the debate over practice versus matter to the Frankfurt School and the early Marx.
quoteEn: The premise of Marx's thought of practical materialism is the reconciliation of body and mind.
quoteZh: 马克思的实践唯物主义思想的前提是肉体与精神的和解。

glossary.explanation: A reading of Marxist philosophy, prominent in Chinese scholarship since the 1980s, that treats practice as its foundation and cites Marx's phrase "practical materialists" in The German Ideology. Scholars dispute how it relates to the priority of matter.
The policy of economic reform and opening to the outside world launched in China in 1978.

t: The polyphonic character of Marx's early intellectual development
zh: 马克思早期思想发展的复调性特征
paras: Li Yaxi questions the standard account that Marx turned to Bruno Bauer's philosophy of self-consciousness in 1837 and wrote his doctoral dissertation on that basis. The article notes that Bauer only built his self-consciousness system after reaching Bonn in 1840, which leaves a gap in the history of ideas. Drawing on Marx's early notebooks in MEGA2, Li argues that Marx's early thought and dissertation are "polyphonic", combining heterogeneous and conflicting intellectual sources.

The piece, first published in the Chinese Social Sciences Today in 2022, is short. It begins with Marx's letter of November 1837 and his law studies in Berlin, then covers the dispute between the historical school and the rationalist school of jurisprudence, and Marx's teachers Savigny and Eduard Gans. It then turns to Marx's contact with the Doctors' Club and Bauer, and to the Epicurus Notebooks, the Berlin Notebooks and the Bonn Notebooks.

Li argues that in 1837 Marx was still mainly absorbed in law, and that his move to philosophy extended the jurisprudential debate between Savigny and Gans. Bauer, then still a Hegelian of the right, had not yet developed his own system. In the Epicurus Notebooks Marx criticised a subjective spirit detached from substance and wanted to ask how philosophy relates to the world. Bauer rejected this in letters of 1841, and Marx probably compromised because he hoped for Bauer's help with the teaching-qualification exam. In the Bonn Notebooks Marx treated art through "social connection", which Li traces to the objective rationalism of Gans.

Li concludes that the background of the time, independent research and practical needs left Marx's writing with incompatible sources, which form the polyphonic character of his texts and thought. Li also finds in Gans the roots of the rationalist view of the state Marx held at the Rheinische Zeitung. Read the original if you study the young Marx, the Bauer–Marx relationship or the MEGA2 notebooks and want a concise argument against a straight line from Bauer to the dissertation.
quoteEn: Thus, between Marx's turn to philosophical research and Bauer's creation of the philosophy of self-consciousness, there appears a gap in the history of ideas that needs to be filled.
quoteZh: 于是，在马克思转向哲学研究到鲍威尔创立自我意识哲学之间便出现了一段需要填补的思想史空白。

t: The theoretical responsibility of historical materialism
zh: 历史唯物主义的理论担当
source: Chinese Social Sciences Today (Zhongguo shehui kexue bao), 30 June 2022
paras: This short commentary, published in a Chinese newspaper in 2022, asks why Marx and Engels's The German Ideology deserves repeated reading today. Chen Lixin argues that the work gave the first relatively systematic statement of historical materialism's basic principles. In Chen's account, the doctrine shows a distinctive "theoretical responsibility" (lilun dandang) in how it faces both thought and the real world.

The piece opens by noting that major world events send people back to Marxism, and cites Derrida's remark that failing to read and discuss Marx would be an error of the age. It then moves through three headings: raising philosophical ontology through the historical principle, entering the real life-process, and revealing the dialectical movement of modern society. Chen traces the lineage from Vico through Kant and Hegel to Marx.

Chen's central claim is that Marx brought history into the ontology of philosophy. Earlier philosophy started from consciousness or self-consciousness and proved being through the deduction of categories. Marx, by contrast, started from real individuals and their sensuous activity, explained ideas from practice and ended the philosophy of conceptual deduction. Chen adds that historical materialism holds that the production and reproduction of real life is decisive in history. Because human activity is social by nature, the author says, individuals develop only in community, and the contradiction between productive forces and forms of intercourse drives history. Chen holds that Capital, by showing the relation of capital and labour as the axis of modern society, extends this insight.

Chen concludes that the historical principle, the demand of reality and the movement of society together display the unmatched theoretical responsibility of historical materialism. Chen argues that the doctrine helps people grasp the nature and likely course of the logic of capital today. It can also answer a modern "spiritual hunger" amid material abundance. Re-reading The German Ideology with this awareness is, for Chen, indispensable. Read the original if you want a brief Chinese statement of why the classic text is still treated as central to Marxist philosophy.
quoteEn: Historical materialism ended the philosophical approach driven by conceptual deduction and returned philosophy to the real world of life, so that it achieves its own development and self-confirmation.
quoteZh: 历史唯物主义终结了以概念演绎为动力机制的哲学进路，使哲学回到现实生活世界而实现自我发展与自我确证。

t: The Bonn Notebooks and research on the young Marx's philosophical thought
zh: 《波恩笔记》与青年马克思的哲学思想研究
source: Chinese Social Sciences Today (中国社会科学报), 2 August 2022
paras: Liu Bingjing asks what pushed Marx away from Young Hegelian idealism in 1842–1843. The usual account stresses Feuerbach and the material-interest questions of the Rheinische Zeitung period. Drawing on the Bonn Notebooks as published in MEGA2, Liu argues that an earlier theoretical factor was already at work before the Rheinische Zeitung and prepared Marx's first intellectual turn.

The short newspaper article describes the Bonn Notebooks as the remains of a failed plan to write a critique of religion with Bruno Bauer. Marx abandoned the plan in early 1842 and, from April to May in Bonn, excerpted works on the history of religion and art. These included Charles de Brosses, Karl August Böttiger, Benjamin Constant and Christoph Meiners. Liu concentrates on the Constant excerpts from On the Religion of the Ancients.

Liu identifies two critical threads in Constant that Marx noted. The first is synchronic: religion arises from human society's real need to communicate with the invisible, yet priests monopolise that mediation and turn human-made religious power into domination. The second is diachronic: religious forms harden over time and obstruct religious feeling, so a church claiming to be eternal can be exposed as falsely so. Liu contends that this offered Marx a critique starting from human reality, as opposed to Bauer's self-consciousness, which treats religion as alienated self-consciousness to be overcome by the awakening of a few.

Liu concludes that the Constant excerpts probably moved Marx towards Feuerbach's materialism. Marx's letter on his disagreement with Feuerbach about religion's essence and some materialist statements in his 1842 articles are offered as support. Together with the material-interest question of the Rheinische Zeitung period, the Bonn Notebooks are said to have driven Marx's turn to materialism. Read the original if you want a brief account of how the MEGA2 Bonn Notebooks bear on the debate over Marx's break with Bauer.
quoteEn: It is not the self-consciousness of a few, but human reality itself, that holds the critical power to refute European religious domination.
quoteZh: 不是少数人的自我意识，而是人类现实本身具有证伪欧洲宗教统治的批判力量。

t: Mao Zedong's idea of people's constitution-making in the 1954 Constitution and its implications
zh: “五四宪法”中毛泽东人民立宪思想及其启示
source: Studies on Mao Zedong and Deng Xiaoping Theory, 2022 no. 4
paras: Marking the 40th anniversary of the current 1982 Constitution, Zhang Xiaoshuai asks what the 1954 Constitution (the "Five-Four Constitution") reveals about Mao Zedong's idea of people's constitution-making (renmin lixian). The author argues that existing scholarship relies too heavily on hindsight or Western constitutional theory, and that the 1954 text should be read within Mao's own thought and the historical evolution of China's constitutional system. The article is a research article published in 2022.

Zhang does not examine the Constitution's detailed provisions. Instead the article considers three aspects of how Mao's thought shaped it: its foundations (the creation of "democratic facts" and of "the people" as the constituent subject), its purposes (the state system, the system of people's congresses and the general line for the transition period), and its drafting methods. A final section draws four implications for implementing the current Constitution in full.

On foundations, Zhang reports Mao's view that a constitution recognises democratic facts already won through revolution, so that earlier documents such as the Provisional Constitution of the Republic of China failed for lack of them. On purposes, the 1954 Constitution established people's democratic dictatorship and wrote the general line for the transition period into its preamble. Zhang contends that the Constitution lost force after socialist transformation was completed in 1956 not because it was instrumental, since all Chinese constitutions set development goals, but because it set only a transitional goal rather than a long-term one. The drafters, in this reading, also neglected constitutional amendment. On methods, Zhang cites Mao's combination of leadership and mass opinion (the author cites over 150 million participants in the draft's discussion), reliance on national conditions, critical borrowing from foreign constitutions, and a balance of principle and flexibility.

Zhang draws four lessons for implementing the current Constitution: stress its legal character, including constitutional interpretation and review; protect human rights, understood through China's conditions and with subsistence and development rights as primary; improve whole-process people's democracy; and combine national conditions, traditional legal culture and critical borrowing from abroad while upholding Party leadership and rejecting Western "constitutionalism". Read the original if you want a Chinese constitutional-law reading of Mao's approach to the 1954 Constitution and the way it is linked to current official discourse on implementing the Constitution.
quoteEn: However, what was finally written into the text of the 1954 Constitution was a transitional goal belonging to the foundation-laying stage, so that once that goal was achieved, the Constitution lost its force for lack of guidance from a long-term goal.
quoteZh: 但是，最终写入“五四宪法”文本的却是属于打基础阶段的过渡目标，这就导致当过渡目标实现后，“五四宪法”就因缺少远期目标的指引而失去效力。

glossary.explanation: Mao Zedong's idea, first put forward in the 1920s Hunan self-government movement, that the people elect representatives to a constitutional assembly that drafts the constitution.
The first constitution of the People's Republic of China, adopted in September 1954 by the First National People's Congress.

glossary.en: general line for the transition period
glossary.explanation: The Party line formulated in 1953 setting the tasks of gradual socialist industrialisation and socialist transformation of agriculture, handicrafts and capitalist industry and commerce.
The official definition of the state system: democracy within the people and dictatorship over enemies, led by the working class and based on the worker-peasant alliance.
China's basic political institution, in which congresses at each level are the organs of state power, topped by the National People's Congress.
A concept promoted by Xi Jinping from 2019, describing socialist democracy as covering all stages of political life, not only elections.

t: A deep understanding of the new stage of development
zh: 深刻理解新发展阶段
paras: Writing in Qiushi in 2022, Qu Qingshan sets out how the new stage of development (xin fazhan jieduan) should be understood. The article presents entering this stage as a major strategic judgement by the Party Central Committee with Xi Jinping at its core. Qu argues that the stage is the period of comprehensively building a modern socialist country and marching towards the second centenary goal, and that studying Xi's statements on it has great practical and historical significance.

The article is organised as a sequence of six topics, each introduced by a question and answered mainly through extended quotations from Xi Jinping. They are the stage's historical position, its material foundation, its goals, its relation to the primary stage of socialism, its relation to the new era, and its relation to Chinese modernization. A last section treats the link between the new stage, the new development philosophy and the new development pattern.

Qu's first move is historical. He traces the quest for modernization from the Opium War, through Sun Yat-sen's plans and the founding of the Party in 1921, to the 1954 and 1964 modernization goals, reform and opening up, and the leap from "standing up" to "becoming rich" to "becoming strong" after 2012. The material basis, he says, is the completion of a moderately prosperous society and the poverty-alleviation campaign, for which he cites 832 counties lifted out of poverty and a GDP above 100 trillion yuan. His second move concerns periodisation: the new stage lies within the primary stage of socialism, which he describes as dynamic and not static, so that quantitative accumulation moves towards qualitative change. The new era and the new stage differ in length but share the same tasks and goals.

Qu concludes that the new stage carries two phased goals: basic socialist modernization by 2035 and a modern socialist country by the middle of the century. This modernization must have Chinese characteristics, which he lists as huge population scale, common prosperity, material and cultural-ethical advancement, harmony with nature and peaceful development. He holds that the new stage supplies the historical position, the new development philosophy the guiding principle and the new development pattern the path for economic modernization. Read the original if you want a compact statement of the official 2022 account of the new stage of development, built on Xi Jinping's formulations, ahead of the 20th Party Congress.
quoteEn: Judged by its historical position and its goals, the new stage of development has not yet gone beyond the historical category of the primary stage of socialism, and this point must be made clear.
quoteZh: 新发展阶段，从其历史方位和奋斗目标看，还没有超越社会主义初级阶段的历史范畴，这一点是必须明确的。

glossary.explanation: A term from the Fifth Plenum of the 19th Central Committee (2020) for the period that began after the moderately prosperous society was completed, devoted to building a modern socialist country by mid-century.
The goal of building a modern socialist country by 2049, the centenary of the People's Republic. The first centenary goal was a moderately prosperous society by the Party's centenary in 2021.
A thesis developed in the 1980s and set out at the 13th Party Congress (1987). It holds that China is socialist but still at an early stage because of its underdeveloped productive forces.
The concept, introduced after 2012, of innovative, coordinated, green, open and shared development as the guiding principle of economic and social policy.
The strategy, announced in 2020, of making the domestic economic cycle the mainstay while domestic and international cycles reinforce each other.
The official term for China's own path to modernization, described as having features such as huge population scale, common prosperity and peaceful development.
A long-standing socialist goal that Party documents describe as prosperity shared by all, and that has been stressed again since the 2010s.

t: Practical materialism from the perspective of the reconciliation of body and mind
zh: 肉体与精神和解的视角看实践唯物主义
source: China Social Sciences Today (Zhongguo shehui kexue bao), 26 July 2022
paras: Since reform and opening up, Chinese research on Marxist philosophy has given the foundational status of practice new weight and has come to read Marxism as "practical materialism". Wang Xiaosheng observes that scholars remain deeply divided over how to understand it, above all over whether practice or matter is primary. In this newspaper essay, Wang argues that the dispute cannot be settled because both sides assume the separation of body and mind, a premise that itself needs reflection. Wang's thesis is that Marxism seeks a reconciliation of body and mind, and that practical materialism and dialectical materialism are essentially the same when read from this angle.

The essay has four parts. It first treats the opposition of body and mind as a basic fact of human existence, drawing on Engels's account of the fundamental question of philosophy and on Adorno and Horkheimer's Dialectic of Enlightenment. It then turns to Marx's pursuit of reconciliation, citing the Economic and Philosophic Manuscripts of 1844 and The German Ideology. A final part applies this reading to Marx's critique of the Young Hegelians, to the meaning of "reality" in Marx and Hegel, and to the unity of theory and practice.

Wang holds that Engels traced the question of thought and being to the "ignorant notions of the age of savagery", yet the separation it names is real: Wang reads the Odysseus and the Sirens episode as showing that survival requires people to bind their own bodies and to control nature. Taken as an absolute, however, this opposition produces an instrumental reason that drives the body to self-harm, and Wang notes that only humans commit suicide. Simple unity of body and mind would be barbarism, so Wang argues that the two stand in a dialectical unity of opposites, which Wang calls reconciliation. Materialism then accepts the priority of matter within the opposition without being confined to it, and reconciliation is possible only in practice, where the "living human being" is the practical subject. On this basis Wang reads the Young Hegelians as thinkers who stayed in words, while Marx's concepts aim to be realised in life.

Wang concludes that practical materialism overturns the philosophical framework that divides body from mind and subject from object. In Wang's view it is both a major transformation in the history of philosophy and a guide to contemporary social practice. Wang adds that purely spiritual "love" can turn cold and has been used to justify killing. Read the original if you want a compact example of a Chinese philosophical reading that tries to settle the "practice first or matter first" debate through the body–mind relation.
quoteEn: Marxist philosophy is dialectical materialism, and its core is to see the unity of opposites between body and mind.
quoteZh: 马克思主义哲学是辩证唯物主义，其核心就是要看到肉体与精神之间的对立统一。

glossary.explanation: A reading of Marxist philosophy that gives practice a foundational role. It became prominent in Chinese philosophy after reform and opening up and remains contested, especially over its relation to the primacy of matter.
The policy of economic reform and opening to the outside world launched in China in 1978.
The philosophical system of Marxism as codified in Soviet and Chinese textbooks. It combines a materialist view of the world with dialectical method.
The author's key notion: neither a natural unity nor an absolute opposition of body and mind, but a dialectical unity of opposites achieved in practice.

t: Reflecting on virtual reality through Baudrillard's philosophy of technology
zh: 于鲍德里亚技术哲学反思虚拟现实
source: China Social Sciences Today (Zhongguo shehui kexue bao), 17 May 2022
paras: Zhang asks what Jean Baudrillard's late philosophy of technology can offer for thinking about virtual reality. The article argues that his concept of the "perfect crime", set out in The Perfect Crime (1995), serves as a prophetic warning. In this crime, a technologically produced "perfect world" kills reality without leaving a trace.

The short commentary first defines virtual reality in a broad sense as a digital world that interpenetrates the physical one. It then outlines three stages of development: digitising reality ("reality + virtual"), virtual–real symbiosis ("reality × virtual") and full fusion ("reality = virtual") through technologies such as brain–computer interfaces. Zhang acknowledges potential benefits, including expanded creativity and, ideally, features resembling a "free association of individuals".

Zhang reads Baudrillard's simulacra and "hyperreality" as a forerunner of the virtual reality concept. At the third stage the author sees a "hyper-hyperreality" in which digital certainty replaces the real, and the real turns from being into nothingness. The same three stages are also read as the killing of illusion, which ends once virtual and real can no longer be told apart. In Zhang's account, people then become nodes in a network, living time becomes labour time, and the result is precise control of individuals, a "pure governance of consciousness".

Zhang calls Baudrillard's thought pessimistically technologically determinist but still valuable as a warning. The author notes that many people already spend more time online than offline and take what they see there as the real world. Whether virtual reality brings a "perfect world" or a "perfect crime" is said to depend on balancing instrumental and value rationality and using technology with "good knowledge" and "good regulation". Read the original if you want a brief Chinese philosophical reading of virtual reality and the metaverse through Baudrillard.
quoteEn: Whether virtual reality in the future brings a \"perfect world\" or commits a \"perfect crime\" depends on whether we can balance instrumental rationality and value rationality, and use technology with \"good knowledge\" and \"good regulation\".
quoteZh: 未来虚拟现实是带来“完美的世界”，还是实施“完美的罪行”，这取决于我们能否平衡工具理性和价值理性，用“善知”和“善制”来使用技术。

t: Applying the Marxist conception of justice to advance social fairness and justice
zh: 运用马克思主义正义观推进社会公平正义
paras: Li Nan asks how Marx's conception of justice can be revived and applied to the tasks of socialism with Chinese characteristics in the new era. The article argues that returning to Marx's view of justice answers rival theories, especially liberal ones, helps defend mainstream values, and offers a way to resolve deep-seated social contradictions and conflicts of interest. In Li's view it should be tied to the modernization of state governance, so that the fruits of development reach all people more fairly.

Published in People's Forum in 2022, the article has three parts. The first sets out four theoretical features of Marx's view of justice. The second explains the significance of applying it today, under four headings: historical position, value orientation, content system and spatial pattern. The third proposes four practical paths: building consensus on fairness, narrowing gaps in distribution, strengthening the rule of law, and improving public services.

On Marx, Li argues that justice belongs to the superstructure and is a historical category, with no eternal justice. Its core is the question of social relations of production, and its ultimate aim is the free and all-round development of the human being. For the present, Li reads Xi Jinping's statement that fairness and justice are an inherent requirement of socialism with Chinese characteristics as the Party's updated position. Justice is said to include both 'getting what one deserves' and 'getting what one needs', with the second protecting vulnerable groups through redistribution. Li presents the 'three fairnesses' (fairness of rights, opportunity and rules) as linking starting point, process and outcome. The article also ties the new development philosophy, the Belt and Road Initiative and a community with a shared future for mankind to justice at home and abroad.

Li's practical proposals include promoting the socialist core value of 'justice' through education and Party media. In distribution, Li calls for distribution according to labour as the main form, fiscal transfers, and charitable 'third distribution'. Li also stresses rigorous law-making and enforcement and fairer education, employment and public services. Achieving justice is described as long-term and complex, to be pursued on the basis of high-quality development. Read the original if you want an example of how Chinese journals link Marx's theory of justice to Xi-era policy on common prosperity, law and livelihood.
quoteEn: The essence of justice is the genuine appropriation of the human essence.
quoteZh: 正义的本质就是对人的本质的真正占有。

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: A foreign-policy concept promoted by Xi Jinping since about 2013. It calls for cooperation and shared security and development among states.
A Chinese infrastructure and economic cooperation initiative launched in 2013, linking China with countries in Asia, Africa and Europe.
A framework put forward in 2015 stressing innovative, coordinated, green, open and shared development.
An official goal of shifting from fast growth to growth that is efficient, balanced and sustainable.
A socialist goal, restated under Xi Jinping, of prosperity shared by all rather than a few.
A formula taken from Xi Jinping: fairness of rights, of opportunity and of rules, as the main content of a social fairness guarantee system.

t: Marx's thought on labour and its contemporary value
zh: 马克思的劳动思想及当代价值
paras: Writing in 2022, Liu Huihui asks what Marx's thought on labour can still offer at a time when modern science and technology have changed the forms and content of labour. The article argues that tracing how Marx's view of labour developed, from his school essay to Capital, yields practical guidance for China's present tasks, including the labour-capital relationship, distribution and common prosperity.

The article follows Marx's intellectual path in stages. It begins with his early views (the essay on choosing a profession, the doctoral dissertation on Democritus and Epicurus, and his work at the Rheinische Zeitung), then turns to alienated labour in the Economic and Philosophic Manuscripts of 1844 against the background of Hegel, Feuerbach and Moses Hess. It next covers the materialist conception of history in The German Ideology, and finally the labour theory of value in The Poverty of Philosophy, Wage Labour and Capital, the 1857–58 manuscripts and Capital.

Liu's central claim is that labour runs through Marx's whole development. Contact with material interests at the Rheinische Zeitung pushed him from idealism to materialism. In the 1844 Manuscripts he described four forms of alienation: from the product, from the act of labour, from species-being and from other people. The German Ideology then made labour and production the basis of history, and the dual character of labour (concrete and abstract) became, in Liu's account, the pivot for understanding political economy and for exposing capitalist exploitation.

Liu draws four lessons for today. These are to respect labour and talent and keep workers as the main body of development; to uphold distribution according to work and tackle uneven distribution in pursuit of common prosperity; to advance a community with a shared future for mankind, presented as a contemporary expression of Marx's theory of labour emancipation; and to combine Marxist principles with the Chinese Dream. Liu stresses that labour's full emancipation belongs to communism. Read the original if you want a concise, textbook-style survey of the stages of Marx's labour thought and an example of how such scholarship is tied to current Chinese policy language.
quoteEn: It has great practical significance for realising people's free and all-round development and for deepening China's reform and development.
quoteZh: 对实现人的自由而全面的发展和深化我国改革发展具有很大的现实启示。

glossary.explanation: A goal of shared affluence for all, long associated with socialism in Chinese official discourse and given renewed prominence under Xi Jinping. It is linked to reducing income gaps.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: A foreign-policy concept promoted by Xi Jinping since around 2012–13. It calls for cooperative global governance and shared development.
A slogan popularised by Xi Jinping from 2012, centred on national rejuvenation and the prosperity of the people.
The socialist distribution principle, drawn from Marx's Critique of the Gotha Programme, under which individuals receive income in proportion to the labour they contribute.

t: The transformation of philosophy and the true task of human philosophy
zh: 哲学之变与人类哲学的真正任务
source: China Social Sciences Today (Zhongguo shehui kexue bao), 19 July 2022
paras: Zhang Nengwei asks whether philosophy is, as Aristotle and Hegel held, a body of theoretical knowledge about the essence and laws of the world. The article, first published in the China Social Sciences Today newspaper in July 2022, answers no. It argues that modern science has ended philosophy's classical role as knowledge of essences. Philosophy survives in a changed form, and its true task is practical philosophy, which reflects on the meaning of human existence and action.

The article is built in three steps, mostly through the work of Hans-Georg Gadamer, with Habermas, Rorty, Kant and Thomas Kuhn's notion of a paradigm in supporting roles. The first step describes how a scientised age and positivist philosophy of science have eroded philosophy's claim to a unified view of the world. The second step follows philosophy's turn towards art and the humanities. The third step proposes replacing the "theoretical paradigm" with a "practical paradigm", drawing on Aristotle's distinction between theoretical, practical and productive knowledge.

Zhang's central move is to separate the end of metaphysics as a theory of knowledge from the end of philosophy itself. Following Gadamer, the author holds that philosophy still pursues an overall understanding of experience, but this "whole" exceeds what science can know. Philosophy therefore resembles art and the humanities: it offers no fixed or absolute answers and is an enterprise of understanding. Zhang then argues that practical philosophy should take the place of "first philosophy". Practice is not the application of scientific theory. Theoretical knowledge and technical capacity should be subordinated to human practice, not the reverse, and this is how the growing self-alienation of modern life can be countered.

Zhang concludes that practical philosophy is the true task of philosophy. It is needed by a scientised present and by a future in which people ask how they ought to exist. The article closes on the claim that philosophy will not end so long as questioning does not end. It does not discuss Marxism explicitly and rests mainly on the hermeneutic tradition. Read the original if you want a concise Chinese-language account of Gadamerian arguments for practical philosophy and their use in rethinking philosophy's task.
quoteEn: Practical philosophy replaces the paradigm of theoretical philosophy, and practical philosophy constitutes the true task of human philosophy.
quoteZh: 实践哲学范式替代理论哲学范式，实践哲学构成了人类哲学的真正任务。

t: Abstraction becomes domination: Marx and Lefebvre
zh: 抽象成为统治：马克思与列斐伏尔
paras: This short commentary, first published in China Social Sciences Today in 2022, asks how Henri Lefebvre extends Marx's critique of the modern paradox that individuals are now ruled by abstractions. Yan argues that Lefebvre takes up Marx's formula of abstraction (capital) becoming dominant and concludes that abstract space has become dominant. Neither thinker, in Yan's reading, falls into despair, since both trust the emancipatory force of historical dialectics.

The piece has three parts: abstract capital as ruler, abstract space as ruler, and the path to breaking abstract domination. It draws mainly on Marx's remarks on money, capital and the bourgeois state, and on Lefebvre's account of the production of space.

For Marx, Yan says, the development of the market makes exchange value an alien power, money its embodiment, and money fetishism a reified social relation in which workers and capitalists alike serve capital's self-expansion. Economic globalisation extends this rule, and capitalist fetishism becomes the ideology of global capital. Lefebvre, Yan explains, moves from the production of things in space to the production of space itself: abstract space becomes the "subject" of social relations and daily life. It is an objective abstraction, understood through the dialectic from the abstract to the concrete. Its closest concrete form is state monopoly capitalism, and urbanisation, nationalisation and globalisation make up a spatial trinity.

Yan concludes that this domination contains its own negation. Capital, for Marx, meets its limit in itself, and abstract space must generate spaces of difference that exist in negative form. The proletariat, in Marx's view, carries the task of liberating humanity, and Lefebvre locates possible spatial liberation in city margins, slums and prohibited spaces of resistance. Read the original if you want a brief overview of how Lefebvre's spatial theory is presented as a continuation of Marx's critique of capital.
quoteEn: In short, the \"self-reflexivity\" of capital links up with the \"self-negation\" of abstract space, signalling the path to the dissolution of abstract domination.
quoteZh: 简言之，资本的“自反性”衔接着抽象空间的“自我否定性”，昭示着抽象统治的瓦解之路。

t: Grasping the milestone significance of the great changes of the new era's first decade
zh: 深刻把握新时代十年伟大变革的里程碑意义
paras: This commentary, published in Guangming Daily in August 2022 shortly before the 20th Party Congress, explains why Xi Jinping described the great changes of the past ten years as having "milestone significance". Zhong Xiaowu takes up Xi's statement that the decade is a milestone in the history of the Party, of the People's Republic, of reform and opening up, of socialist development and of the Chinese nation. The author argues that since the 18th Party Congress (2012) the Party Central Committee with Xi at its core has achieved historic accomplishments and brought about historic change.

The article is organised as a sequence of areas in which the author finds the decade decisive. It covers Party building, economic strength and the first centenary goal, reform and opening up, theory and international influence, and finally national rejuvenation and cultural foundations. Each section lists achievements in the official register, with figures such as GDP passing 100 trillion yuan and nearly 100 million people lifted out of poverty.

On the Party, Zhong claims that the Two Establishes have become a broad consensus, that political awareness of the Four-sphere Confidence and the Two Upholds has risen, and that full and rigorous self-governance of the Party has cleaned up long-standing problems. The author presents the Party's self-reform as a successful path for escaping the historical cycle of rise and fall. On development, Zhong cites a rise in China's share of the world economy from 11.3% to over 18%, a move from 34th to 12th in the Global Innovation Index, the building of a moderately prosperous society, and more than 2,000 reform plans. Zhong then treats Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era as "Marxism of contemporary China and of the twenty-first century". The article holds that Chinese modernization offers developing countries a new path, breaks the equation of modernization with Westernization, and has shifted the contest between socialism and capitalism in socialism's favour.

Zhong concludes that the Chinese nation has entered its best period of development since modern times, and that the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation has become an irreversible historical process. The author links this to a stronger sense of the Chinese nation as a community, to the creative transformation of traditional culture, and to the proposal of a community with a shared future for mankind and the Belt and Road Initiative. Read the original if you want a concise example of how the official 2022 narrative of the "new era" decade was framed for a general readership before the 20th Party Congress.
quoteEn: The ten years of the new era are ten years in which China successfully forged the path of Chinese modernization and created a new form of human civilisation, offering developing countries a new path to modernization.
quoteZh: 新时代十年是成功走出中国式现代化道路、创造人类文明新形态的十年，为发展中国家实现现代化提供了新路径

glossary.explanation: A formula from the Party's 2021 historical resolution: establishing Xi Jinping's position as core of the Central Committee and of the whole Party, and establishing the guiding role of Xi Jinping Thought. It is presented as decisive for the Party's future.

The requirement that Party members uphold Xi Jinping's core position in the Central Committee and the Party as a whole, and uphold the authority and centralised, unified leadership of the Central Committee.
Confidence in the path, theory, system and culture of socialism with Chinese characteristics, a formula promoted in Party discourse since the 18th Party Congress.

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.explanation: The slogan for the Party's discipline and anti-corruption drive since 2012, covering ideological, organisational and conduct requirements for Party members.
Official term for the Party's efforts to correct its own problems, presented as the way to avoid the historical cycle of dynastic rise and decline.
The official name for China's own path to modernization, promoted as an alternative to Western models.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's concept for international relations, stressing common security, development and cooperation among states.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The Party's central national goal, associated with the Chinese Dream, of restoring China to a position of strength and prosperity.

t: Grasping the contemporary significance and essential features of common prosperity
zh: 把握共同富裕的时代意蕴和本质特征
paras: Writing in Guangming Daily in August 2022, Jia Liping asks how common prosperity should be understood as the country begins a new journey towards building a modern socialist country in all respects. Jia argues that common prosperity has its roots in Marxism, expresses the Chinese Communist Party's fundamental values, is an essential requirement of socialism, and is an important feature of Chinese modernization.

The short commentary is organised under four headings, one for each of these claims. It draws on Marx and Engels, on Mao Zedong and Deng Xiaoping, and on Xi Jinping, and it cites the 2021 Party history resolution and the 19th Party Congress (2017) goals for 2035 and the middle of the century.

Jia holds that Marx and Engels pictured a community of free individuals in which each person's free development is the condition for everyone's, so common prosperity is the basic aim of Marxism. In the Party's own history, Jia traces the same aim through Mao's "common" wealth and strength, Deng's statement that common prosperity is socialism's greatest advantage, and Xi's commitment to people-centred development. Jia also reads common prosperity as an institutional requirement tied to the basic socialist economic system and its distribution arrangements, and as a marker of Chinese modernization.

Jia concludes that the Party must coordinate the Five-sphere Integrated Plan and the Four-pronged Comprehensive Strategy, and must pursue high-quality development, so as to meet its goals for common prosperity and all-round human development. Jia presents these goals as having major significance for the history of the Party, of socialism and of human civilisation. Read the original if you want a compact statement of how Party theorists in 2022 linked common prosperity to Marxist classics and to the Party's own tradition.
quoteEn: Achieving common prosperity is the goal the Party has pursued unswervingly.
quoteZh: 实现共同富裕是我们党矢志不渝的奋斗目标。

glossary.explanation: A long-standing socialist goal in Party discourse, meaning prosperity shared by all rather than a few. It was given new emphasis under Xi Jinping from 2021.
The official term for China's own path to modernization, presented as distinct from Western models. Common prosperity is named as one of its features.
An official economic goal, adopted around 2017, that stresses quality, efficiency and balance over speed of growth.
The Party's overall layout for development across the economy, politics, culture, society and the ecological environment.
A strategic framework put forward by Xi Jinping in 2014. It covers building a modern socialist country, deepening reform, governing the country by law and strictly governing the Party.

t: Using digital technology to help comprehensively advance rural revitalization
zh: 以数字技术助力乡村全面振兴
paras: Writing in the People's Daily in August 2022, Chen Fulong asks how digital technology can serve the comprehensive advancement of rural revitalization after the victory in poverty alleviation. Chen argues that digital technology should be deeply integrated with agricultural development, rural governance and farmers' daily life, providing a scientific and technological guarantee for agricultural and rural modernization.

This short commentary opens with Xi Jinping's statements on the shift in the focus of work on agriculture, rural areas and farmers, and on the 14th Five-Year Plan's call to speed up building digital villages. It then proceeds through three headings: modern agriculture, rural governance and farmers' quality of life.

On agriculture, Chen holds that applying digital tools across ploughing, sowing, management and harvest changes business models as well as productivity. Examples include BeiDou positioning, artificial intelligence, QR-code traceability from field to table, and online sales of farm produce. On governance, Chen argues that digital tools suit grid-based management and allow more actors to take part in orderly co-construction, co-governance and sharing, for instance through village affairs posted on WeChat accounts and voting in WeChat groups. On living standards, Chen presents online services such as "at most one visit" and "no-face-to-face approval" as ways to widen the reach and accessibility of rural public services.

Chen concludes that digital technology should drive agricultural modernization while respecting the laws of agricultural production, and should support governance led by Party organizations. Chen also calls for better rural information infrastructure, such as fibre-optic and mobile networks, so that farmers feel the convenience and gain a stronger sense of benefit and security. Read the original if you want a brief, officially aligned statement of how digital villages are framed in the policy discourse on rural revitalization.
quoteEn: To comprehensively advance rural revitalization, digital technology must be given full play as a support, so that digitalised rural governance drives governance that is socialised, law-based, intelligent and professional, helping to build vibrant, harmonious and well-governed villages.
quoteZh: 全面推进乡村振兴，需要发挥好数字技术的支撑作用，以乡村治理数字化驱动乡村治理社会化、法治化、智能化、专业化，助力建设充满活力、和谐有序的善治乡村。

glossary.explanation: A national strategy announced in 2017 to develop rural industry, ecology, culture, governance and living standards. After the poverty-alleviation campaign ended in 2020, it became the main framework for rural policy.
A standard shorthand in Chinese policy for agriculture, the countryside and farmers, treated as a single policy area.
A policy programme to apply information and digital technology to rural production, governance and services. The 14th Five-Year Plan (2021–2025) calls for accelerating its construction.

t: The meaning of Lenin's thought on socialist state governance and its contemporary implications
zh: 列宁社会主义国家治理思想的内涵要义与当代启示
source: Journal of Southwest University (Social Sciences Edition), 2022 no. 4
paras: Zhang Kai and Wang Hongsheng ask what Lenin's exploration of governing the first socialist state can offer China as it works to modernise its system and capacity of state governance. Writing in 2022, with the Third Plenum of the 18th Central Committee (2013) having made this modernisation the overall goal of deepening reform, they argue that Lenin's thought is an important theoretical source for that task. They identify three pillars in it: the dictatorship of the proletariat as the fundamental precondition, proletarian culture as the spiritual consciousness, and participation by all the people as the value orientation.

The article opens with a review of Chinese scholarship, which the authors sort into general accounts of Lenin's governance thought, studies of its essence and principles, and studies of its actors and measures. They say this literature has not examined governance through the proletarian dictatorship, communist culture or forms of popular participation, and has rarely linked Lenin to China's recent experience. Three sections then take Lenin's ideas in turn, and a final section draws four lessons for China.

In the authors' reading, Lenin held that the state remains necessary after the revolution and should be a 'practical' and 'inexpensive' government. It would be led by the vanguard party through political, organisational and ideological leadership, and bound by socialist legality, including supervision through bodies such as the Workers' and Peasants' Inspectorate. Because Russia's backwardness in culture and literacy obstructed governance, he stressed communist morality, political education of cadres and officials, and basic schooling for the masses. He combined direct democracy with party-led indirect democracy, and gave citizens rights of supervision and recall.

The authors conclude that China should uphold the Party's overall leadership, citing the collapse of the Soviet Communist Party as a warning.
