They also call for whole-process people's democracy with a people-centred stance, for rule of law that turns institutional strengths into governance effectiveness, and for Party leadership of ideological work against Western ideological infiltration and historical nihilism. They add that Lenin's wartime communism and the New Economic Policy offer further lessons. Read the original if you want to see how Chinese scholars link Lenin's state-building thought to current Party-state governance doctrine.
quoteEn: Only when the proletariat holds state power can socialist state governance in the true sense be carried out.
quoteZh: 只有无产阶级掌握了国家政权，才能进行真正意义上的社会主义国家治理。

glossary.explanation: A concept put forward by Xi Jinping in 2019 and officially described as democracy covering every stage of political life, from elections to consultation, decision-making, management and supervision.
In official Chinese usage, a label for interpretations that question the Party's historical narrative or the legitimacy of the revolution and socialism.

t: A contemporary interpretation of Marx's thought on world history
zh: 马克思世界历史思想的当代阐释
source: Journal of South-Central Minzu University (Humanities and Social Sciences Edition), online first 15 March 2022
paras: Yu Han takes up a weakness in research on Marx's thought on world history: its core content is often identified imprecisely, so that the idea is understood too broadly and loses its distinctive function. The article argues that the core is Marx's identification of the characteristic of his epoch, "history transformed into world history". It holds that this is a revolutionary weapon of theory rooted in historical materialism, and that its interpretation should also be tied to the Communist Party of China's century of practice.

The article has three parts. The first traces Marx's intellectual sources, chiefly Hegel's philosophy of history. The second examines the epoch characteristic as set out in The German Ideology, Capital and the Economic and Philosophic Manuscripts of 1844. The third discusses the idea's contemporary value, ending with the Party's practice and the present international situation.

Yu's argument turns on two moves. First, Marx inherited Hegel's strong sense of history but sublated it. Marx replaced the self-movement of "impersonal reason" with the practical activity of real human beings, and rejected any general philosophy of history that supplies one abstract formula for all epochs. He also criticised the Eurocentrism of Hegel and Herder as bourgeois ideology. Second, Yu reads the epoch characteristic through large-scale industry and the world market. Capitalism opened the world-historical age and dominated it, but in Marx's view it lacks full world-historical significance, which only communism, aimed at the free and all-round development of the human being, can attain. Yu adds that there is no world-history thought independent of historical materialism.

Yu concludes that Marx's thought on world history completes the aims of his whole doctrine, since it reveals the temporary character of capitalist rule and points to the "changing of the world". For the present, Yu credits the Party's century of practice and Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era with grasping the pulse of the age, and says this practice opens a new world-historical period. Yu also says Marxist philosophy must keep widening its horizons to meet "changes unseen in a century", anti-globalisation sentiment and protectionism. Read the original if you want a Chinese Marxist account of how Marx's world-history thought relates to Hegel, historical materialism and the Party's current self-understanding.
quoteEn: Philosophy cannot be abolished without being made a reality.
quoteZh: 不使哲学成为现实，就不能够消灭哲学。

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017 and 2018. Official texts present it as the latest stage in adapting Marxism to China.

glossary.pinyin: bǎi nián wèi yǒu zhī dà biànjú
glossary.literal: great changes not seen in a hundred years
glossary.explanation: A phrase used by Xi Jinping since about 2017 to describe a shifting global balance of power and rapid change in the international order.

t: Overseas scholarship on the Marxist theory of ownership and its assessment
zh: 海外学界关于马克思主义所有制理论的研究及其评价
source: Frontiers of Foreign Social Sciences (国外社会科学前沿), 2022 no. 7
paras: This literature review surveys how scholars outside China have treated the Marxist theory of ownership and China's ownership reforms. Bao notes that domestic Chinese research on the subject is extensive, whereas overseas work has been little introduced in China. The article argues that overseas research is thin, ideologically conditioned and strongest at the meso and micro levels, and it uses the comparison to propose directions for Chinese research.

Drawing on searches of JSTOR, Web of Science and CNKI, on Chinese translation journals, and on Monthly Review, Historical Materialism and Radical Political Economy, Bao sorts the literature into three blocks. The first covers reflection on classical ownership theory and practice, including the analytical Marxism of G. A. Cohen and John Roemer, Coase-style property-rights theory, and debates on Soviet state ownership and post-Soviet privatisation, where David Kotz is cited as a critic. The second covers China's reforms: the household contract responsibility system, private enterprise and state-owned enterprise reform. The third covers future trends, citing Stiglitz, Samir Amin and comparisons of Chinese and American public enterprises.

Bao credits overseas work with widening the methodological basis for comparing ownership forms and with offering a micro-level path that complements China's macro-level focus on the nature, structure and function of ownership. Two weaknesses are stressed. First, Western mainstream economics has since the marginal revolution taken capitalist private ownership as a given, so Marx's ownership theory has been marginalised; Bao reads Piketty's focus on distribution without ownership in this light. Second, overseas assessments of Chinese reform remain trapped in a Cold War binary of public versus private. In the article's account, they overlook the historical role of state-owned enterprises as the material and political foundation of the state in a late-developing country.

Bao proposes three directions for Chinese research. One is to study contemporary capitalist ownership, including why private ownership has not met the fate Marx foresaw, and to demonstrate the strengths of socialist ownership by comparison. Another is to strengthen research on deepening state-owned enterprise reform in the new era, resisting privatisation and arguing how competitive state firms can become stronger, better and larger. The last is to study the effect of the digital economy and data ownership on traditional ownership relations, drawing on Christian Fuchs and Nick Dyer-Witheford. Read the original if you want a Chinese scholarly map of overseas ownership research and of how Chinese scholars assess and respond to it.
quoteEn: Overseas research on and judgements of China's ownership reform remain deeply shaped by mainstream ideology, so some of its conclusions and evaluations carry an inherent "bias".
quoteZh: 海外学界对于中国所有制改革的研究和判断仍然深受其主流意识形态的影响，因而某些结论和评价上带有先天的“偏见”。

glossary.explanation: The system of ownership of the means of production, a core category of Marxist political economy. In Chinese usage it denotes the basic social form of ownership (public or private), not only legal property rights.
The rural reform from the late 1970s under which collectively owned land was contracted to individual households that farmed it and kept surplus output.

t: Early explorations in building a rural social security system in New China, 1949–1957
zh: 新中国构建农村社会保障体系的初步探索（1949—1957）
source: Studies on Mao Zedong and Deng Xiaoping Theories, 2022 no. 2
paras: How did the Party and state begin to provide social security for China's peasants after 1949, when the country was poor and the countryside vast? Zhou Xiao argues that early New China, lacking the means to copy the urban system, assembled a broad package of measures covering peasants' birth, old age, sickness and death. The author holds that this marked a shift from informal, temporary relief towards a modern social security system, and offers it as historical reference for building a unified urban–rural system and advancing common prosperity.

The article covers 1949–1957 in three parts. The first treats state relief, divided into disaster relief and poor relief, after land reform gave peasants a basis for self-reliance. The second examines collective economy as the main support of rural security after agricultural cooperativization began in 1953. The third turns to rural health and disease prevention, and a closing section compares rural and urban arrangements. Zhou draws on policy documents, leaders' speeches and local cases from provinces such as Zhejiang, Hebei, Hubei and Liaoning.

Zhou's central claim is that the relief approach was set out in the guideline revised in 1954: relying on the collective, mutual aid among the masses and production for self-rescue, with necessary state relief as a supplement. Under it, cooperatives created provident and welfare funds, experimented with cooperative medical care, and from 1956 established the "five guarantees" system for childless and infirm elderly people. In health, the author credits the "patriotic hygiene campaign", county and district health institutions, and campaigns against smallpox, plague and schistosomiasis with rapidly easing the shortage of doctors and medicine. Zhou also notes limits: egalitarianism under the guise of distribution according to work dampened incentives, provident-fund deductions sometimes cut members' incomes, the Great Leap Forward damaged rural health work, and Zhou Enlai acknowledged a marked urban–rural imbalance in medical resources.

Zhou concludes that urban and rural areas ran two different models: urban security was tied to household registration and labour insurance, while the countryside relied on self-rescue, collectives, mutual aid and emergency state aid. The rural system was narrow in coverage, unsystematic, and funded through a single channel. Even so, the author sees collective security and improved rural health as unprecedented changes in China's agrarian history. Read the original if you want a detailed, documented account of how early PRC policy approached rural welfare, cooperative medicine and the five guarantees, from a Chinese official-academic perspective.
quoteEn: In the exploration and practice of building a rural social security system in early New China, the collective economy became the most important breakthrough.
quoteZh: 在新中国初期构建农村社会保障体系的探索与实践中，集体经济成为最为重要的突破口

glossary.explanation: A goal of socialism in Party discourse, stressed since the 18th Party Congress (2012) and especially after 2021, referring to shared prosperity and narrowing of inequalities, including between town and country.
A rural system, begun in 1956, in which the collective guaranteed food, clothing, fuel, education (for children) and burial for elderly, disabled or orphaned villagers without support.
A mass mobilisation launched in the early 1950s to improve sanitation, eliminate pests and prevent epidemic disease.

glossary.literal: public accumulation fund and public welfare fund
glossary.explanation: Deductions from the income of agricultural cooperatives: the former financed expanded production, the latter funded collective welfare, culture, health and relief.

The 1950s process of organising individual peasant households into mutual-aid teams and then cooperatives, part of the socialist transformation of agriculture under the General Line for the transition period (1953).

t: The path of Chinese modernization and a new form of human civilization
zh: 中国式现代化道路与人类文明新形态
paras: Writing in Guangming Daily in July 2022, Hu Boxiang takes up the Sixth Plenum (2021) resolution on the Party's century of struggle. It states that the Party has led the people along the path of Chinese modernization, created a new form of human civilization and widened the routes to modernization open to developing countries. Hu argues that this path is a modernization road without precedent and offers developing countries a new option.

The article is organised in four numbered sections, each naming one "outstanding feature" of the path and of the civilization it produces. These are leadership by the Communist Party and socialism, independence and self-reliance, comprehensive and coordinated development, and peaceful development. Each section sets the feature against a Western theory or model that Hu says Chinese modernization surpasses.

Hu contends that the Western view of modernization as Westernization is overcome by a path that the Party explored independently over a century. In this account China needed the Party's leadership to compress an industrialization that took developed countries centuries into a few decades, and it keeps a socialist orientation. That orientation rests on a public-ownership-based system of mixed ownership, distribution mainly according to work, and common prosperity as the goal. Hu rejects the notion that late developers must depend on imported Western civilization, citing Deng Xiaoping on not copying other countries' experience, while stressing that self-reliance does not mean closing the country. Against "pure economic growth" theory, Hu presents a modernization that coordinates material, political, spiritual, social and ecological civilization and treats human modernization as its essence, pursued through common prosperity and a people-centred rather than capital-centred logic. Against "a strong country inevitably seeks hegemony", the clash of civilizations and zero-sum thinking, Hu describes a path of peaceful development, mutual benefit and the building of a community with a shared future for mankind. Hu says Western modernization was bound up with expansion, colonialism and plunder.

Hu concludes that the path and the new form of civilization come from the Party's grasp of national conditions, from Marxism adapted to Chinese conditions, and from the practice of reform and opening up. Hu presents peaceful development as a considered conclusion, not a diplomatic expedient, and claims it offers "Chinese wisdom" and a "Chinese approach" to global problems. Read the original if you want a concise, officially aligned statement in Guangming Daily of how Chinese modernization is contrasted with Western modernization theory.
quoteEn: The essence of modernization is the modernization of people, and the precondition for the modernization of people is their all-round development.
quoteZh: 现代化的本质就是人的现代化，人的现代化的前提是人的全面发展。

glossary.explanation: The official Party formulation for China's own path to modernization, described as socialist, led by the Party and distinct from Western models. It was elaborated especially from the 19th Party Congress and the 2021 Sixth Plenum resolution onwards.

glossary.en: a new form of human civilization
glossary.explanation: A phrase in the 2021 Party resolution on history. It claims that Chinese modernization creates a form of civilization different from the Western capitalist one.
A socialist goal of prosperity shared by all the people, which Xi Jinping has emphasised as a requirement of socialism and a feature of Chinese modernization.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's concept for international relations based on cooperation, mutual benefit and shared governance, promoted by Chinese diplomacy since 2012.

t: The "group portrait" and "disorder" of contemporary foreign Marxist currents
zh: 当代国外马克思主义思潮的“群像”与“乱象”
paras: Sun Ying and Han Qiuhong, in a commentary first published in the Chinese Social Sciences Today in June 2022, ask how contemporary Marxism outside China should be assessed. They argue that since the 1970s traditional Western Marxism has turned into a plural, fragmented set of currents. In their view this brings both a lively contest of schools and a measure of disorder, so it must be examined objectively from a firm Marxist standpoint.

The article sets out three criticisms in turn. The first concerns method: how these currents describe social criticism and the philosophy of history. The second concerns class standpoint, and the third concerns humanist methods of critiquing capitalism. It draws on Lukács, the Frankfurt School, structuralism, ecological and feminist Marxism, spatial theory, and radical left thinkers such as Rancière, Negri, Agamben, Žižek and Fraser. It also cites Anderson and Harvey as observers who noticed related weaknesses.

The authors contend that these currents coin many labels for new capitalism, such as digital, late and financial capitalism, and for new crises, but rarely analyse the production relations behind them. Mixing in methods from sociology, psychology, geography and ecology, they say, dilutes historical materialism, so claims to "rebuild" it amount to abandoning it. On standpoint, the authors say radical left thinkers replace the proletariat with the multitude and other identity groups, and replace class relations with relations between groups. This, they argue, turns revolutionary emancipation into contingent identity politics. Finally, they say the long reliance on alienation critique rests on a humanist value standpoint rather than political-economic analysis, and ends in utopian or paper solutions.

Sun and Han conclude that foreign Marxist currents do add to Marxism by addressing ecology, gender equality, cyberspace and democracy, and by widening its global and interdisciplinary reach. Yet they judge that fragmentation breaks up the wholeness of Marxist theory and makes consensus and practical unity hard to reach. They call for firmness in Marxism's basic standpoint, reliance on the people and continuing revolutionary practice. Read the original if you want to see how a Chinese Marxist commentary in 2022 sums up and criticises the main trends of Western and foreign Marxism.
quoteEn: At root, contemporary foreign Marxism amounts to a wavering faith in communism and an incomplete adherence to Marxism's basic standpoint, principles and methods; they often treat Marxist theory as a tool for scholarly debate and academic research, not as a scientific guiding ideology for social change.
quoteZh: 究其根本，当代国外马克思主义无外乎对共产主义信仰不坚定，对马克思主义基本立场原则方法的坚持不彻底，他们常常将马克思主义理论作为一种学理争辩、学术研究的理论工具，而非推动社会变革的科学指导思想。

t: The theoretical commitment of historical materialism
zh: 历史唯物主义的理论担当
paras: Why should The German Ideology still be read repeatedly today? In this commentary, published in the Chinese Social Sciences Today in June 2022, Chen Lixin argues that the work first set out the basic principles of historical materialism systematically, and that rereading it shows the theory's radical character, its consistency and its guiding spirit. Chen names this quality the "theoretical commitment" (lilun dandang) of historical materialism.

The piece opens with the claim that Marxism has been consulted at every major turn in world history, because it reveals laws of historical development that contemporary society still lives under. Chen cites Derrida's remark that failing to read and discuss Marx would be an error of the age. The body then takes up three themes under separate headings: raising philosophical ontology through the historical principle, entering the actual life-process, and revealing the dialectical movement of modern society.

On the first theme, Chen traces how history entered philosophy, from Vico's "truth is the made" through Kant's universal history to Hegel's reason and "human passion". In Chen's reading, Marx saw that Hegel's historical sense served the movement of absolute spirit. Marx instead took life as determining consciousness and started from sensuous human activity, so that being is confirmed in real life rather than proved through the deduction of categories. On the second and third themes, Chen holds that Marx fastened on "real individuals" in their social relations, which exposes ideological illusion and locates the ultimate causes of social change in the economy. Because human activity is inherently social, the contradiction between productive forces and forms of intercourse becomes the substance of history, and Capital shows the relation of capital and labour to be the axis of modern society.

Chen concludes that the interaction of the historical principle, the demands of reality and social movement gives historical materialism a theoretical commitment that nothing else matches. Chen adds that in an age when a good life is becoming a global aspiration and material abundance coexists with "spiritual hunger", Marx's account of how the capitalist mode of production is possible helps in grasping the nature and likely course of the logic of capital. Rereading The German Ideology is presented as a necessary exercise in theoretical self-awareness. Read the original if you want a brief, Party-school-style restatement of why Chinese Marxist philosophers treat The German Ideology as a foundational text, and how they link it to current concerns.
quoteEn: Historical materialism ended the philosophical approach driven by conceptual deduction, returning philosophy to the real world of life, where it achieves its own development and self-confirmation.
quoteZh: 历史唯物主义终结了以概念演绎为动力机制的哲学进路，使哲学回到现实生活世界而实现自我发展与自我确证。

t: The materialist conception of history as a historical science
st: Starting from a footnote in The German Ideology
zh: 作为历史科学的唯物史观
zhSub: 从《德意志意识形态》的一个注释谈起
source: Chinese Social Sciences Today (中国社会科学报), 30 June 2022
paras: This short commentary asks what kind of science the materialist conception of history is. Juan takes a deleted passage in the manuscript of The German Ideology, in which Marx says he knows only one science, the science of history, divided into natural history and human history. Juan argues that the passage fixes the difference between historical materialism and the old philosophy and establishes its character as a science of history that is at once a science of man.

The article has three parts. The first sets out Marx's critique of old philosophy, which in Marx's words either distorts human history or leaves it aside altogether. The second presents historical materialism as the science of real human beings, under three headings: its object of study, its basic theoretical logic and its orientation towards the future. The third returns to the unity of natural history and human history.

Juan reads old materialism as leaving human history aside: after Bacon's lively sensuous matter, it turned mechanical and mathematical and became indifferent to human beings. Idealism touched human history but treated it abstractly, as the evolution of spirit. Both, in Juan's account, fail to see that sensuous practical activity is the foundation of the existing world. Historical materialism starts from real individuals and their activity. Production covers the production of life, one's own and others', and so contains both natural and social relations. For Juan this rules out an economic-determinist reading and makes the theory a set of principles and methods, not a formula to be applied everywhere. Its aim is human emancipation, through the common appropriation of social productive forces by associated individuals.

Juan concludes that the nature Marx speaks of is not an absolutely objective nature outside humanity. It is a humanised nature that takes shape through practice, so that natural science will include the science of man and the reverse. Historical materialism is therefore both a science of man and a science of nature, united as the single science of history. Read the original if you want a compact, text-based account of how a footnote in The German Ideology is used to argue against economic-determinist readings of historical materialism.
quoteEn: Historical materialism is the historical science of man: an understanding and grasp of the historical process in which human beings continually generate and create themselves through their own objective practical activity.
quoteZh: 唯物史观就是人的历史科学，是对人通过自身的对象性实践活动不断地自我生成、自我创造的历史过程的理解和把握。

t: Recent advances in German MEGA research
zh: 近年来德国学界MEGA研究的新进展
paras: Kaan Kangal (Kangal Kaan in the Chinese rendering) surveys German-language scholarship on the Marx-Engels-Gesamtausgabe (MEGA) over roughly the past five to six years; the piece first appeared in the Chinese Social Sciences Today in January 2022. The author notes that the 200th anniversaries of Marx (2018) and Engels (2020) produced a surge of publications in Germany. Many of these draw on MEGA2 materials but concern Marx's and Engels's theory in general rather than the edition itself. Kangal's review therefore focuses on debates that deal directly with MEGA.

The survey identifies the main venues of these debates: the Marx-Engels-Jahrbuch, the Marx-Engels-Forschung. Neue Folge and, occasionally, the Zeitschrift für marxistische Erneuerung. It also lists five books bearing directly on MEGA research, among them works by Matthias Bohlender, Hagen Kleemann, Ulrich Pagel and Rolf Hecker. Kangal sorts the debates into four areas: The German Ideology, Marx's political philosophy and conception of critique, the history of MEGA1, and Marx's economic theory of the 1850s and 1860s.

On The German Ideology, Kangal reports that after the MEGA2 volume appeared in 2017, Gerald Hubmann argued that no single work of that name exists. In his account, the manuscripts belonged to a planned journal, and the main target of Marx and Engels was Max Stirner rather than Feuerbach. Pagel and Bohlender develop this line, while Terrell Carver's English edition is criticised by Michael Quante as politically narrow. Lucas Rudolph holds that the text aimed to criticise German philosophy and "true socialism" rather than to construct historical materialism. A second debate concerns Marx's idea of critique as "critique in hand-to-hand combat" and his relation to utopian socialists. The third covers the Marx-Engels-Forschung volume on Boris Nikolaevsky, who helped Ryazanov's MEGA1 project and later the Amsterdam archive. The fourth turns on MEGA2 Section IV notebooks: Soichiro Sumida on the Asiatic form in the London Notebooks, Norman Jakob on Marx's publishing plans, and Kenji Mori and Hecker on the Crisis Notebooks of the 1857 crisis, which Hecker sees as an empirical test of Marx's crisis theory.

Kangal does not offer a single conclusion; the article is a descriptive map of current German MEGA scholarship and its disputes. It shows how new editions and notebooks are reopening questions about Marx's texts, politics and economics. Read the original if you want a guide to the German authors, journals and books driving MEGA debates, particularly on The German Ideology and the Crisis Notebooks.
quoteEn: Over the past five or six years, a wave of research on Marx and Engels has swept German academia.
quoteZh: 最近五六年来，德国学界掀起一股研究马克思和恩格斯的热潮。

t: Abstraction becomes domination: Marx and Lefebvre
zh: 抽象成为统治：马克思与列斐伏尔
paras: This short commentary, first published in the China Social Sciences Today in March 2022, asks how Henri Lefebvre extends Marx's account of modern domination by abstraction. Yan argues that Lefebvre takes up Marx's claim that abstraction (capital) becomes dominant and concludes that abstract space has become dominant in contemporary capitalism. Despite the 'anonymous power' involved, both thinkers are presented as revolutionary optimists who trust the emancipatory force of historical dialectics.

The piece has three parts: abstract capital as ruler, abstract space as ruler, and the path to breaking abstract domination. It draws on Marx's remarks on the second great social form, money, capital and the world market, and on Lefebvre's writings on the production of space, the state and everyday life.

In Yan's reading, Marx shows that exchange value and money become alien powers, so that workers and capitalists alike serve the self-expansion of capital, and that globalisation spreads this rule worldwide. Lefebvre, in Yan's account, shifts the focus from the production of things in space to the production of space itself in abstract space, which codes social relations and admits nothing without exchange value. Its closest concrete form is state monopoly capitalism, and urbanisation, nationalisation and globalisation make up a 'spatial trinity'.

Yan concludes that abstract domination carries its own negation. For Marx capital 'repels itself' and meets its limit in its own nature, and for Lefebvre abstract space must produce differential space that contests homogenisation. Yan notes that Marx locates the force of liberation in the proletariat, while Lefebvre locates it in urban margins, slums and forbidden spaces of resistance. Read the original if you want a brief comparison of Marx's critique of capital with Lefebvre's theory of space.
quoteEn: The 'self-reflexivity' of capital connects with the 'self-negation' of abstract space, pointing to the path along which abstract domination dissolves.
quoteZh: 资本的“自反性”衔接着抽象空间的“自我否定性”，昭示着抽象统治的瓦解之路。

t: Reflecting on virtual reality through Baudrillard's philosophy of technology
zh: 基于鲍德里亚技术哲学反思虚拟现实
paras: This short commentary, first published in China Social Sciences Today in May 2022, asks what Jean Baudrillard's later philosophy of technology can contribute to thinking about virtual reality. Zhang argues that his concept of the "perfect crime" offers theoretical resources for judging whether virtual reality will bring a "perfect world" or carry out a crime against reality itself.

The article first defines virtual reality in the broad sense as a digital world, parallel to and interpenetrating the physical one, in which people live with digital identities. It then sets out Zhang's three-stage model of its development and turns to Baudrillard's works Simulacra and Simulation, The Perfect Crime and others, before returning to present-day online life.

Zhang's three stages run from digitising reality ("reality + virtual"), through symbiosis ("reality × virtual"), to fusion ("reality = virtual") via brain-computer interfaces. Reading Baudrillard, Zhang treats the third stage as a "hyper-hyperreal" condition in which digital certainty replaces the real and illusion disappears, because virtual and original intelligence can no longer be told apart. On this reading the human being becomes a node in a network, existence becomes labour time, and the result is control through "pure governance of consciousness". Zhang sees this as the true perfect crime for a humanity seeking emancipation, while acknowledging that virtual reality might in an ideal case stimulate creativity and resemble the "association of free individuals".

Zhang calls Baudrillard's thought pessimistically technological-determinist but still valuable as a warning about the defects of a highly technologised society. Zhang notes that many people already spend more time online than offline and take what they see there as the real world. Whether virtual reality yields a perfect world or a perfect crime, Zhang concludes, depends on balancing instrumental and value rationality and using technology with "good knowledge" and "good regulation". Read the original if you want a brief Chinese Marxist-oriented application of Baudrillard to debates on virtual reality and the metaverse.
quoteEn: Whether virtual reality in future brings a "perfect world" or commits a "perfect crime" depends on whether we can balance instrumental rationality and value rationality, and use technology with "good knowledge" and "good regulation".
quoteZh: 未来虚拟现实是带来“完美的世界”，还是实施“完美的罪行”，这取决于我们能否平衡工具理性和价值理性，用“善知”和“善制”来使用技术。

t: Focus and breakthrough in Marx's doctoral research
st: A reconstruction based on the MEGA2 edition of the Berlin Notebooks
zh: 马克思在博士论文研究中的聚焦与突破
zhSub: 基于对MEGA2版《柏林笔记》的重构
source: China Social Sciences Today (Zhongguo shehui kexue bao), 28 June 2022
paras: Zhang Yixiu asks how Marx's reading notes from his Berlin years supported the writing of his doctoral dissertation, The Difference between the Democritean and Epicurean Philosophy of Nature. The author argues that MEGA2 gives valuable documents but arranges and names them poorly, splitting Marx's Berlin notes into three parts. Zhang proposes treating all of them as one body, the "Berlin Notebooks", and re-periodising them by date and content.

The article is a short newspaper piece that follows the notes in chronological order, from the winter semester of 1838 to the doctorate granted by Jena in 1841. It covers the Epicurus excerpts of 1839, the later notes and additions on atomism, the lost materials on Democritus and Aristotle, the drafting of the dissertation, and a final group of excerpts from early 1841.

Zhang identifies two moments of focus and breakthrough. In the first group of notes Marx concentrated on Epicurus and engaged his critics, such as Plutarch. He built on Hegel's History of Philosophy but broke with it by valuing Epicurus's natural philosophy and his theory of celestial phenomena as expressions of self-consciousness. From mid-1839 Marx turned to atomism and compared Epicurus with Democritus. Zhang argues that Marx read the atom's swerve as freedom against determinism, in contrast to Hegel, who took it as an emphasis on contingency. According to Zhang, this idea is the core of the dissertation, where the "objectification of self-consciousness" expresses the pursuit of individual freedom.

Zhang concludes that Marx's Berlin notes should be reconstructed as a whole, which would show more clearly how they supported his dissertation. The author also suggests that the last excerpts, from Leibniz, Hume, Spinoza and Rosenkranz, differ physically from the earlier notes and bear little relation to the dissertation. They were more likely preparation for a later teaching qualification examination. Read the original if you work on the early Marx, Marx's relation to Hegel, or the editorial arrangement of MEGA2.
quoteEn: Marx developed a new understanding of this: he held that the significance of Epicurus's theory of the atomic swerve lies in advocating a freedom opposed to determinism.
quoteZh: 马克思对此产生了新的理解，他认为伊壁鸠鲁原子偏斜论的意义在于倡导反决定论的自由。

t: The early intellectual context of the young Marx
zh: 青年马克思的早期思想构境
source: Chinese Social Sciences Today (Zhongguo shehui kexue bao), 28 June 2022
paras: Zhang Yibing asks where the young Marx's early idealism and revolutionary-democratic stance came from, a question he says Chinese scholarship has neglected. Studies have concentrated on the materialist turn and on texts such as the Critique of Hegel's Philosophy of Right, the Economic and Philosophic Manuscripts of 1844 and The German Ideology. Zhang argues that the answer lies in Marx's early reading notes, and that the dominant influence was Bruno Bauer's subjective idealism rather than Hegel's objective idealism.

This short newspaper commentary, published in 2022, proceeds through three questions. It asks first about Marx's initial relation to Hegelian philosophy and the Young Hegelians, then about how the philosophy of his doctoral dissertation took shape, and finally about the change in his thinking between the doctorate and the Rheinische Zeitung period. It draws on the Berlin Notebooks and the Bonn Notebooks.

Zhang holds that Marx came to Hegel largely through the Young Hegelians, above all Bauer, whose concept of self-consciousness recast Hegel's system as subjective idealism and expressed bourgeois individual subjectivity. In the dissertation on Epicurus, Marx used self-consciousness to reinterpret an atomism that had appeared historically in a materialist guise. Zhang calls this Marx's first near-miss with materialism. In the Bonn Notebooks, Zhang sees the subjective idealism loosening. Marx grew dissatisfied with Bauer's detached theological critique, broke off their planned joint work, and first used the concept of fetishism in excerpts from de Brosses. His attention shifted from Hegelian spirit to real history.

Zhang suggests that the fetishism excerpts may be an important source for Marx's later critique of fetishism, up to Capital. Zhang adds that materialist threads in the Bonn Notebooks may already have formed a tacit framework, although the materialist turn was not yet complete. Zhang notes that MEGA2 now publishes these notebooks and letters in full, and hopes for more research. Read the original if you want a brief guide to the early notebooks and to Bauer's influence on Marx before 1843.
quoteEn: Therefore, in the context of the young Marx's early philosophical thought, what held the dominant position was not Hegelian objective idealism but Bauerian subjective idealism.
quoteZh: 因此，在青年马克思早期哲学思想构境中，居支配地位的不是黑格尔式的客观唯心主义，而是鲍威尔式的主观唯心主义。

t: The content and intellectual value of the Berlin Notebooks
zh: 《柏林笔记》的内容及其思想价值
paras: Li Qiankun asks how the young Marx's Berlin Notebooks (1839–1841) should be read and what they are worth. Li argues that they should be treated neither as a finished philosophical statement nor as mere preparatory material. In Li's view they are an indispensable link for understanding the early course of Marx's thought. The piece first appeared in the Chinese Social Sciences Today in 2022.

Li follows MEGA2 in using the title for the eight notebooks of Excerpts from Classical Philosophers. The earlier seven notebooks on Epicurean philosophy and the two groups of Epicurus fragments can count as Berlin Notebooks in a wider sense, but they are already translated and well studied. Li therefore surveys the excerpts section by section: Aristotle's On the Soul, Leibniz, Hume's Treatise, Spinoza's Theological-Political Treatise, and Rosenkranz's history of Kantian philosophy.

Li describes two prior positions. One, represented by the MEGA2 editors and by Alexandre Matheron's French counterpart Lübbert-type studies such as Rubel's Marx Encounters Spinoza (1977), stresses Marx's distinctive philosophical exploration. The other, represented by Michael Heinrich's 2018 biography, reads the excerpts as preparation for a Bonn habilitation, supported by Bruno Bauer's letter of 1840. Li accepts a dialectical view of both. Marx at Berlin still worked within the older philosophical vocabulary, so over-reading is a postmodern textual reading detached from the author.

Li nonetheless finds vivid traces of the period in the notebooks. These include Marx's remarks on Aristotle, his Hegelian vocabulary of consciousness, and his choice to excerpt the later chapters of Spinoza on freedom of thought and democracy first. Li reads these as signs of a preference for Hegel's philosophy of self-consciousness and a democratic political leaning. Read the original if you want a short guide to the contents of the notebooks and to the dispute over their significance.
quoteEn: This set of excerpts is therefore an indispensable link in understanding the intellectual path of the young Marx.
quoteZh: 因此，这一摘录是我们理解青年马克思思想道路不可或缺的一环。

t: An "industrial pathology" examination of the capitalist public health crisis
zh: 资本主义公共卫生危机的“工业病理学”考察
paras: Why do capitalist societies, which have had public health systems since nineteenth-century Britain, still fall into disarray when a pandemic such as COVID-19 strikes? Writing in 2022, Li Ling answers by returning to Marx's use of "industrial pathology" in Capital. The article argues that Marx took an existing medical genre, drawn from physicians' investigations of work-related illness, and recast it through historical materialism. In Li's account, this allows the root of recurrent public health crises to be traced to the capitalist mode of production rather than to administrative failings.

The article draws mainly on Capital, especially the Public Health Reports edited by Dr John Simon, and on Engels, Marx's letters and the Critique of the Gotha Programme. It is organised in four parts: misplaced values, internal contradictions, functional failure of the health system, and a final section on remedies. Each diagnostic part moves from nineteenth-century Britain to the pandemic response in the United States and other Western countries. Li cites New York Times figures from May 2020 on deaths in US elderly-care facilities and higher mortality among ethnic minorities, as well as reports of an early US task-force recommendation rejected over fears for financial markets.

Li's central argument is that capital's self-valorisation takes precedence over human life and health, so that workers, and above all the unemployed, become expendable. Economising on constant capital such as ventilation and housing, and maintaining an industrial reserve army that carries disease, are said to spread epidemics. Li also contends that, in Marx's analysis, doctors are subordinate to the bourgeoisie, medical care is merely the "repair of labour-power", and health spending is an "unproductive cost" to be cut precisely when it is most needed. Hence, Li argues, the health system tends to paralyse itself in a crisis.

As remedies, Li draws on Marx three lessons: change the system of ownership of the means of production, since reform by technocrats and doctors cannot cure a crisis rooted in the mode of production; have doctors serve ordinary people, as the doctors of the poor-law dispensaries did; and respect medical science, as in Marx's proposal that factory inspectors be doctors. Li links these to the Chinese anti-epidemic spirit of putting life first. Read the original if you want to see how a Chinese scholar applies Marx's Capital to the COVID-19 response and to criticism of Western health systems.
quoteEn: The crux of the capitalist public health crisis lies not in public resources or medical technology; its root is the alienated and misplaced value orientation within the capitalist mode of production.
quoteZh: 资本主义公共卫生危机的症结不在于公共资源、医疗技术等问题，其根源是资本主义生产方式中异化和错位的价值导向。

glossary.explanation: A term Marx used in Capital for the study of diseases linked to industrial work, drawing on physicians' reports. Li argues Marx turned it from description into a critique of capitalist relations of production.
Marx's term for the relatively surplus population of unemployed and underemployed workers that capital keeps available to hold down wages and variable capital.

t: The era of the classics and the classics of the era
zh: 经典的时代与时代的经典
paras: Zhou Jiaxin asks how the classic works of Marx and Engels should be read today, and answers that the Two Integrations offer the method. In this commentary, published in the China Social Sciences Today in May 2022, Zhou argues that returning to the classics means returning to the era in which they were written. This shows both their power of truth and their value for the present. Zhou frames the piece with Xi Jinping's call to uphold Marxism as the guiding principle of Chinese philosophy and social science.

The article is organised in three sections, each tied to a stage in the relation between the classics and their time: observing the era and discovering excellent culture; grasping the era and transforming traditional culture; leading the era and shaping cultural tradition. The material covers German classical philosophy, classical political economy and the socialist and communist currents of the nineteenth century. It also covers Marx's and Engels's turn to materialism, their relation to Hegel's dialectic, and Engels's later writings addressed to German, French and British workers.

Zhou's central claim is that Marx and Engels never simply accepted an existing school. In Zhou's account, they critically absorbed the best intellectual achievements of their time and gave them new content. Materialism became dialectical and historical materialism, Hegel's dialectic was changed from a mystical to a rational form in the course of working out the theory of surplus value, and scientific communism joined a new worldview with workers' movements and advanced cultural traditions. Zhou then argues that the two thinkers also shaped cultural tradition. Engels's later works, including Ludwig Feuerbach, Anti-Dühring and his texts on the history of the German and British movements, countered vulgar materialism and petty-bourgeois socialism. They helped workers see their own intellectual lineage.

Zhou concludes that the creation of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era is likewise an innovation that combines Marxism's basic principles with China's realities and with fine traditional Chinese culture. In Zhou's view it also leads the era and preserves and brings out the Chinese nation's excellent cultural achievements. The closing call is to return to the era of the classics, find their value for today and move toward the classics of the era. Read the original if you want a short, Party-theory-oriented example of how Chinese scholars use the Two Integrations to frame the reading of Marx and Engels.
quoteEn: Marxism is not a ready-made theoretical oracle, but the theoretical self-awareness that advanced intellectuals formed by observing their era on the basis of concrete reality.
quoteZh: 马克思主义不是现成的理论谕示，而是先进知识分子，立足具体实际，观察时代所形成的理论自觉。

glossary.explanation: The formula that Marxism's basic tenets must be combined with China's concrete realities and with fine traditional Chinese culture. The 2021 Party history resolution presents it as the method behind Xi Jinping Thought.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017 and 2018. It is presented as the latest stage of adapting Marxism to China.
The term for the communist theory Marx and Engels grounded in historical materialism and the analysis of capitalism, as distinct from utopian socialism.

t: Marx on the relations of private property
st: A reading of Notebook II of Marx's Economic and Philosophic Manuscripts of 1844
zh: 马克思关于私有财产关系的论述
zhSub: 对马克思《1844年经济学哲学手稿》笔记本II的解读
paras: Zhang Na reads Notebook II of Marx's Economic and Philosophic Manuscripts of 1844 to ask how Marx understood private property and what lies at the heart of the opposition between capital and labour. The article argues that, although Notebook II survives only as a fragment, it conveys Marx's central views on private property and is valuable for understanding the critique of political economy and capitalist relations of production. Its thesis is that the opposition of capital and labour is at root an opposition between abstract and concrete labour, which produces alienated labour.

The piece first sets out three aspects of private property in the notebook: the normal relation, in which capital controls the worker's existence; the fixed moment, the struggle between landowner and capitalist; and the necessary process, the three stages of the relation between capital and labour. It then asks what the opposition of capital and labour consists in. Finally it considers how that opposition might be sublated, and where this attempt stops.

Zhang's reading of the third aspect is that capital and labour move from identity, through simple opposition, to an inner opposition. The author links these stages to the emergence, early period and maturity of capitalism, and sees in them Marx's inheritance of Hegelian dialectic. In the mature stage the opposition is hidden inside each side, so that a worker becoming a capitalist is presented as personal fulfilment. Zhang then reasons that capital, as accumulated labour, takes the general form of abstract labour because it can buy any concrete labour at any time. Capital thus confronts concrete labour and gains command over the worker, the product and labour itself. Zhang runs this through the four determinations of alienated labour.

For sublation, Zhang proposes that abstract labour be reunited with concrete labour, with workers taking part in creating and sharing the value of capital. The author describes this as easing the four alienations: products no longer simply confront the worker, labour is partly voluntary, it partly regains its character as an essential human need, and relations with others become less purely those of domination. Zhang adds that this is only a historically specific attempt, comparable to Marx's account of distribution according to labour. Sublating private property is completed only in a communist social form, where people fully appropriate their labour and its relations of production. Read the original if you want a short Chinese commentary that reads Notebook II through the abstract and concrete labour distinction and draws a contemporary conclusion about worker participation in value sharing.)
quoteEn: In short, the opposition of capital and labour is the opposition of abstract labour and concrete labour, and its sharpened form results in alienated labour.
quoteZh: 质言之,资本与劳动的对立是抽象劳动与具体劳动的对立,其尖锐对立的结果是异化劳动。

t: Correctly understanding and grasping the characteristics and behavioural laws of capital
zh: 正确认识并把握资本特性和行为规律
paras: Published in China Social Sciences Today in May 2022, this short commentary responds to Xi Jinping's April 2022 call, at a Politburo study session, to strengthen research on capital theory under new conditions. It also responds to the December 2021 Central Economic Work Conference's call to grasp capital's characteristics and behavioural laws. Zhang and Wang argue that the dual nature of capital is the theoretical basis for doing so, and that practice now requires a theory of capital governance.

The authors start from Marx's dual character of labour and carry it over to capital. They then describe the structure of capital in the primary stage of socialism and set out three practical requirements of governance. The text ends with a short address to leading cadres.

Zhang and Wang hold that capital is both a process of producing use-values, which reflects the productive forces, and a process of producing surplus value, which reflects the relations of production. They argue that this duality yields both capital's positive role as a factor of production and its negative effects. In their account, state-owned, collective and non-public capital are transformed forms of this contradiction, and the public forms decide the direction of the capital structure. On governance, they name three requirements: Party leadership over economic work, the Two Unwaverings, and a new type of government–business relationship. They say the last is needed to curb the pull of non-public capital away from the real economy and its tendency towards monopoly, including data monopoly by internet platforms.

The authors conclude that cadres must master the dual nature of capital and use the "invisible hand" and the "visible hand" correctly. They present this as part of the political economy of Chinese modernization. Read the original if you want a concise statement of how Chinese economists in 2022 framed capital governance in Marxist terms.
quoteEn: Understanding the dual nature of capital is the theoretical cornerstone for grasping the characteristics and behavioural laws of capital.
quoteZh: 认识资本二重性是把握资本特性和行为规律的理论基石。

glossary.explanation: The policy formula of unwaveringly consolidating and developing the public sector while unwaveringly encouraging, supporting and guiding the non-public sector.
The official term for China's path of modernization under Party leadership, promoted prominently since the 20th Party Congress (2022).
The official characterisation of China's present historical stage, which justifies a mixed ownership structure and a socialist market economy.

t: Re-examining the Frankfurt School's paradigm of Enlightenment critique
zh: 审视法兰克福学派启蒙批判范式
source: Chinese Social Sciences Today (中国社会科学报), 28 April 2022
paras: Wang Xiaodong and Li Jingzi ask what Horkheimer and Adorno's critique of the Enlightenment contributes, and where it falls short. Writing in a newspaper piece of April 2022, they argue that the critique offers a valuable view of technological rationality and of domination in advanced industrial capitalism, but that it needs critical scrutiny because it is not consistently historical-materialist.

The article first reconstructs the "cultural critique paradigm" set out in Dialectic of Enlightenment. It then assesses the paradigm's value and sets out three limits. The authors place the paradigm among its influences: the young Marx, Lebensphilosophie, existentialism, Freudianism and early Western Marxism.

In the authors' account, Horkheimer and Adorno reduce the Enlightenment to rationalism, anthropocentrism and progressivism. They analyse it as a threefold alienation: of humans from nature, from one another and from themselves. On this view rationality has turned into instrumental and technical rationality and become a new myth. Wang and Li answer that this picture is partial, because the Enlightenment was plural (French, Scottish, German) and the critique mainly targets the French variety. They also hold that it neglects the Enlightenment's historical progressiveness against feudal absolutism. Above all, they say it wrongly blames reason itself for modernity's crises. Irrational interests and desires, capital and institutional arrangements stand behind instrumental reason, and the authors see Nietzsche, Foucault and the Frankfurt thinkers as rejecting reason instead of criticising these.

The authors conclude that Horkheimer and Adorno accepted Marxism's humanism and its critique of capitalism but did not fundamentally hold to historical materialism. They call for a total historical and practical analysis of the roots of rationality. Read the original if you want a brief Chinese Marxist assessment of the Frankfurt School's critique of the Enlightenment.
quoteEn: The error of the cultural critical theory lies in the fact that it offers no total historical and practical analysis of the true roots of reason.
quoteZh: 文化批判理论的误区在于他们没有对理性的真正根源作出总体性的历史分析和实践分析。

t: The illusion of the technological promise and accelerated capitalism
zh: 科技承诺幻象与加速资本主义
paras: This short commentary, published in China Social Sciences Today in April 2022, asks why technological progress in modern Western capitalism has not freed people from toil. Drawing on Hartmut Rosa's Social Acceleration: A New Theory of Modernity (rendered in Chinese as a critique of the theory of social acceleration), Yu argues that the 'technological promise' is an illusion: technology has been turned from a tool of human liberation into a tool by which capital rules people.

The piece has three main sections: capital logic and technological domination; the 'mission' of technology in accelerated capitalism; and the supposed remedies of 'slow living' and 'resonance'. It begins from Rosa's closed loop of acceleration, in which faster technology speeds social change, social change speeds the pace of life, and the pace of life demands still faster technology.

Yu contends that the loop serves capital's valorisation. Capital stimulates unlimited desires, and satisfying them requires faster production and thus faster technology, so the more technology develops, the busier people become. Technology also lets capital try to push past natural limits, Yu argues, by squeezing more from existing resources and by ecological exploitation of latecomer countries, including through offshore factories and war. The author describes 'slow living' as essentially 'fast', since any pause is repaid with interest, and calls 'resonance' a reformist submission to capital.

Yu concludes that acceleration cannot be undone within capitalism, because it springs from capital's drive to expand without limit. The real task is to dissolve the power of capital and tame capital logic, abolishing its dominance while keeping and transforming its positive elements, in order to move beyond capitalist civilisation. Read the original if you want a brief Chinese Marxist reading of Rosa's acceleration theory and its critique of 'slow life' and 'resonance'.
quoteEn: Technology has been alienated from a tool of human liberation into a tool by which capital rules over people.
quoteZh: 科技由解放人的工具，异化成了资本宰治人的工具。

t: The "first turn" in Marx's philosophical thought
zh: 马克思哲学思想的“第一次转向”
source: China Social Sciences Today (Zhongguo shehui kexue bao), 28 April 2022
paras: Why did the young Marx move from Kant to Hegel? Yu Zaihai argues that Marx's move to the University of Berlin in October 1836 marked the first node in the development of his philosophy, and that the shift was driven by the need to overcome the opposition between the "ought" and the "is". In Yu's reading, Marx turned to Hegel for the same reason Hegel had criticised Kant: to find a way into concrete ethical life.

The piece is a short newspaper essay. It begins with Marx's letter to his father of 10 November 1837, then sets out external and internal causes of the turn. It then reconstructs the difference between Kant's and Hegel's philosophy, covering Kant's theoretical and practical reason, the moral philosophy built on freedom, its dualist flaw, and Hegel's critique. It ends with three inferences about what the turn meant for Marx.

Yu names two external causes. Bonn was dominated by Romanticism, while Berlin was a stronghold of Hegelianism, and Marx absorbed Hegel through Eduard Gans's teaching and the "Doctor Club", where Bruno Bauer and Friedrich Köppen influenced him most. The internal cause is that Marx met an obstacle when he built a philosophy of law on Kant–Fichte lines, namely the opposition between what exists and what ought to be. Yu reconstructs Kant's moral philosophy (duty over happiness, the categorical imperative, the deposit example). Yu then presents Hegel's objection that the universalisation test is purely formal and cannot exclude even the absence of property, so that Kantian morality turns freedom into an "ought" that is never realised. For Hegel, ethical life belongs to objective spirit.

Yu draws three conclusions. The turn was an inner necessity, not a chance interest. It was the key step by which Marx moved from Kant–Fichte idealism toward Hegel. Marx's approach to Hegel was already distinctive: neither the Old Hegelians' fascination with the system nor the Young Hegelians' selective use of it drew him, but Hegel's ending of Kantian dualism, which suggested to Marx a way to "realise" philosophy. Yu holds that this insight separated Marx from the Hegelian schools and set the course of his later work. Read the original if you want a compact account of the intellectual reasons behind Marx's Berlin-period turn from Kant to Hegel, as presented in Chinese scholarship.
quoteEn: It was precisely in order to overcome the dualistic opposition between the "is" and the "ought" that Marx finally decided to turn from Kant to Hegel.
quoteZh: 正是为了克服“实然”与“应然”的二元对立，马克思才最终决定从康德转向黑格尔。

t: The "non-identity" dimension of Marx's empirical research method
zh: 马克思经验研究方法的“非同一性”维度
paras: This short commentary, first published in China Social Sciences Today in January 2022, asks what distinguishes Marx's empirical method from both the speculation of the Young Hegelians and the empiricism of English and French philosophy. Yang argues that Marx combined empirical material with theoretical processing, and that methodologically he rejected metaphysical thinking based on "identity" while stressing the positive significance of "non-identity".

The article is organised under three headings that Yang takes to express this stress: matter (质料, zhiliao), the particular or individual, and difference. It draws mainly on The German Ideology, on Marx's late writings about Russia, and on Hegel's Phenomenology of Spirit.

Yang first argues that Marx grounded theory in material life, so that thought and institutions are historical products of material needs rather than eternal essences. Under capitalism, identity appears as the absolute rule of capital logic, which Marx countered by showing that capitalist production relations are transitory. Second, Yang reads Marx's starting point in living individuals as a critique of capital and metaphysics, which together reduce people to abstract forces. Third, Marx's study of Russia is presented as a case of concrete analysis: Marx rejected turning his account of Western European capitalism into a universal philosophy of history, and held that Russia's path depended on its historical setting.

Yang concludes that, for Marx, experience is not static but expands with time, place and conditions, so it cannot be grasped through fixed concepts. Marx's empirical method is thus aimed at the self-emancipation of concrete, varied individuals and at paths of development that differ by country. Read the original if you want a brief Chinese-language account of how Marx's method is connected to the theme of non-identity.
quoteEn: Because countries differ in historical background, level of development and cultural tradition, the choice of path cannot be one of "identity", but is one of varied and multiform "non-identity".
quoteZh: 由于各个国家在历史背景、发展水平、文化传统等方面存在着差异，因而道路选择不可能是“同一性”的，而是参差多态的“非同一性”。

t: Abstraction becomes domination: Marx and Lefebvre
zh: 抽象成为统治：马克思与列斐伏尔
paras: This short commentary, first published in the Chinese Social Sciences Today in March 2022, asks how Henri Lefebvre carries forward Marx's diagnosis of modern abstraction. Yan argues that Marx criticised the paradox that individuals are now ruled by abstractions, and that Lefebvre took up the formula of abstraction (capital) becoming dominant to conclude that abstract space has become dominant. Yan adds that neither thinker falls into despair, since both rely on the liberating force of the dialectic of history.

The article has three parts: abstract capital as ruler, abstract space as ruler, and the path to breaking abstract domination. It moves from Marx's account of money, exchange value and capital to Lefebvre's theory of the production of space, and ends with their shared view of resistance.

In Yan's reading, Marx shows that money fetishism and the capital relation make people dependent on things, and that economic globalisation spreads this rule worldwide. Lefebvre, in Yan's account, shifts the focus from the production of things in space to the production of space itself. Abstract space becomes the 'subject' of social relations and daily life, erasing lived experience and admitting only objects with exchange value. Yan presents it as an objective abstraction, whose closest concrete form is state monopoly capitalism, and whose urbanisation, statisation and globalisation form a spatial trinity.

Yan concludes that domination by abstraction is not inescapable. Capital's self-negating nature, as Marx describes it, matches abstract space's need to produce spaces of difference, which signals the dissolution of that domination. Yan adds that Marx places the agent of change in the proletariat, while Lefebvre places the possibility of spatial liberation in city margins, slums and forbidden spaces of resistance. Read the original if you want a compact introduction to how Lefebvre's theory of space is linked to Marx's critique of capital.
quoteEn: In short, capital's "self-reflexivity" connects with abstract space's "self-negation", signalling the path to the dissolution of abstract domination.
quoteZh: 简言之，资本的“自反性”衔接着抽象空间的“自我否定性”，昭示着抽象统治的瓦解之路。

t: The contemporary value of the Marxist idea of integrated urban–rural development
zh: 马克思主义城乡融合发展思想的当代价值
paras: This short commentary, first published in the China Social Sciences Today in January 2022, asks how the Marxist idea of integrated urban–rural development can address the urban–rural divide. Yan argues that Western development economics entrenches that divide, while Marxism shows its overcoming to be historically necessary. China's rural revitalization strategy is presented as a new practice that puts this idea to work.

The piece begins with Marx's account in Capital of how capital expropriated rural populations, then turns to Western theories, to Russia after the Soviet collapse, and to Marx and Engels on town and country. It ends with three advantages that Yan attributes to China.

Yan contends that the theories of Lewis, Perroux and Friedmann share a city-centred stance that treats rural sacrifice as inevitable. As the typical case, the author cites Russia's post-1991 "shock therapy", citing figures from Medvedev in 2019 on rural infrastructure. Yan reads Marx and Engels as holding that the town–country opposition can and must be abolished, partly for ecological reasons, and that small peasants should be led towards cooperation rather than expropriated. Yan then names three Chinese advantages: the resolution of private land ownership, long-standing priority for agriculture and rural areas, and the leadership of the Communist Party of China.

Yan concludes that rural revitalization is the opening move towards common prosperity. Success in agricultural modernization and peasant prosperity, the author argues, would resolve the urban–rural opposition and lay the material basis for a higher social form. Read the original if you want a brief example of how Chinese commentary links Marx and Engels on town and country to current rural policy.
quoteEn: China's implementation of the rural revitalization strategy is a new practice that combines the basic principles of Marxism with the concrete realities of China's urban and rural economic development and with fine traditional Chinese culture.
quoteZh: 中国实施乡村振兴战略是马克思主义基本原理同中国城乡经济发展具体实际和中华优秀传统文化相结合的崭新实践。

glossary.explanation: A national strategy announced in 2017 to modernise agriculture and the countryside. Its stated aims are thriving industry, a liveable environment, effective governance, civilised rural customs and prosperous livelihoods.
A long-standing socialist goal of shared wealth, given new emphasis in Party policy since 2021.

t: The theoretical content and practical orientation of Marxist epistemology
zh: 马克思主义认识论的理论内涵与实践旨向
source: China Social Sciences Today (Zhongguo shehui kexue bao), 31 March 2022
paras: Writing in a newspaper commentary, Huang Weijie asks how Marxist epistemology can respond to challenges from twentieth-century Western cognitive science. Huang argues that research should consolidate the basic principles of Marxist philosophy and hold to "proceeding from reality in everything" as the fundamental requirement, attending to the concrete historical relation between knowing subject and object of knowledge.

The article develops three aspects: the content of the "active theory of reflection", the theoretical value of the claim that practice is the source of knowledge, and the practical orientation of the "second leap" in the movement of cognition. It draws on Marx's 1844 and 1857–58 writings, The German Ideology and Engels, and contrasts Marxism with Anglo-American cognitive science and French structuralist epistemology.

Huang contends that Western approaches centre on the individual subject's cognitive structures and drift towards subjective constructivism. Marxism affirms the subject's activity but stresses that the mediating systems, including sense organs, abstract categories and language, are products of social history and practice. Both object and subject are shaped by practice: the sensuous world is a product of industry, and production also produces the subject. The "second leap", from knowledge back to practice, is described as a gap in Western epistemology, which Huang says is therefore confined to speculative debate.

Huang concludes that Marxist epistemology should move beyond purely speculative treatments of the subject–object relation and describe their historical relation under concrete conditions. Huang calls for work based on China's concrete practice, so that narrating Chinese experience and telling China's story become an extension of a practice-oriented epistemology. Read the original if you want a brief statement of how a Chinese scholar uses Marx's texts to answer Western cognitive science and to link epistemology with the aim of telling China's story.
quoteEn: Narrating Chinese experience and telling China's story well is precisely an extended requirement of a Marxist epistemology oriented towards practice.
quoteZh: 叙述中国经验，讲好中国故事，这恰恰是以实践为旨向的马克思主义认识论的延伸性要求。

t: A short philological study of the Paris Manuscripts
zh: 《巴黎手稿》文献学研究小探
source: Chinese Social Sciences Today (Zhongguo shehui kexue bao), 31 March 2022
paras: This short article, first published in a Chinese newspaper in March 2022, takes up three philological questions in research on Marx's Paris Manuscripts (the 1843–45 economic studies). Its aim is to clarify how the Economic and Philosophic Manuscripts of 1844 relate to the notebook of excerpts known as the Comments on Mill. Sheng argues, drawing on the debate among Soviet, Japanese and MEGA editors, that the interleaved order of writing proposed by Nakagawa Hiroshi and Rabin is the more coherent one.

Sheng first describes the structure of the three 1844 manuscripts, most of the second of which is lost. The article then lists the nine excerpt notebooks as published in MEGA1 I/3 (1932) and notes that MEGA2 redistributed them. In MEGA2 IV/2 (1981) seven notebooks stay under the Paris period, while the Lauderdale and Boisguilbert excerpts move to the Brussels notebooks and the Xenophon excerpts are added. The second section reviews the dispute over the order of composition. A closing section turns to alienation, and breaks off after two questions.

Rabin (1969) proposed the sequence Manuscript I, then notebooks IV and V (Ricardo, Mill), then Manuscripts II and III. Nakagawa had suggested something similar in 1968. Their reasons include that Manuscript I cites neither notebook and that Manuscripts II and III cite the Comments on Mill. Taubert, editor of MEGA2 I/2, holds that the Ricardo and Mill excerpts came after the 1844 manuscripts. Sheng finds this unpersuasive, because Marx names Ricardo and Mill in the later manuscripts when denouncing the cynicism of bourgeois political economy. Some scholars use this order to argue that the Comments on Mill, with its 'alienation of exchange', surpasses the 'alienated labour' of Manuscript I. In their view Manuscript I remains in Feuerbach's anthropology and has no social-relational concept of species-essence. Sheng questions this by arguing that Feuerbach's alienation was not one-directional or merely negative, since recognising God as human essence reconciles the believer with the species-essence. Sheng adds that Marx's On the Jewish Question had already identified money as the alienated essence of human labour and existence.

Sheng concludes that the Nakagawa–Rabin sequence is the internationally accepted account and that the question of whether alienated labour or alienated exchange is the higher form needs reassessing. The text ends abruptly after raising this second question, so the full answer is not developed. Read the original if you work on the textual history of the Paris Manuscripts or MEGA and want a compact, citation-rich guide to the editorial and compositional debates.
quoteEn: In sum, as regards the order in which the Paris Manuscripts were written, the inferences of Nakagawa Hiroshi and Rabin are logically coherent and are also the view widely accepted in the international scholarly community.
quoteZh: 总而言之，关于《巴黎手稿》写作顺序，中川弘和拉宾的推论逻辑自洽，也是为国际学界广泛接受的学说。

t: Showing the truth-power of Marxism in the unity of theory and practice
zh: 在理论和实践的统一中展现马克思主义真理力量
paras: This short commentary, first published in Guangming Daily on 17 March 2022, takes as its starting point a passage in the Party's 2021 historical resolution. The passage says that Marxism will show greater truth-power in China if the Party advances theoretical innovation through new practice and guides that practice with new theory. Xue argues that this expresses the dialectical unity of theory and practice, and that Marxism's truth-power depends on grasping the essence, source and destination of theoretical innovation.

The article is organised around three questions: what theoretical innovation is in essence, where it comes from, and where it should go. Each is answered from the standpoint of Marxist epistemology and illustrated with quotations from Marx, Lenin, Mao Zedong and Xi Jinping.

On essence, Xue holds that cognition is the active reflection of practice, so innovation must uphold the primacy of practice and also the basic principles of Marxism. These two commitments, in Xue's account, are not in conflict. On source, innovation comes from practice in three dimensions: China's concrete conditions, the world situation, and the future. Xue presents Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era as the product of such practice. On destination, theory must return to practice through the unity of knowing and doing: a true grasp of what is changing and unchanging, and real problem-solving in reform and development.

Xue concludes that if the Party keeps Marxism as its guide and continues adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times, Marxism will shine more brightly in China. Read the original if you want a compact example of how official commentary frames theoretical innovation in epistemological terms.
quoteEn: Only when the results of theoretical innovation return to new practice and serve it can they play a major guiding role.
quoteZh: 理论创新成果只有回到新的实践中去、服务于新的实践,才能发挥重大先导作用。

glossary.zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化
glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
glossary.explanation: An official formula for the Party's ongoing effort to fit Marxist theory to China's conditions and to contemporary developments.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018.

t: The "difference analysis" method of Western "Marxology" and its contemporary reassessment
st: With a discussion of the Marx–Engels relationship question
zh: 西方“马克思学”的差异分析方法及其当代反思
zhSub: 兼论马克思恩格斯关系论问题
paras: Writing after the bicentenary commemorations of Marx and Engels, Zhao and Zhang argue that the method Western "Marxology" used in the twentieth century, "difference analysis", is still alive. They cite recent work by Norman Levine, Terrell Carver and Gareth Stedman Jones as examples. The authors hold that the method is a legitimate, "neutral" tool of the history of ideas, but that some Western scholars have pushed it past its proper limits. In their view this has a covert negative effect on Marxist research in China and calls for vigilance.

The article first traces three stages in the Western use of the method: Sidney Hook's partial analysis of dialectics from the 1930s; the systematic analysis of Maximilien Rubel and Levine from the 1960s; and Carver's hermeneutic version from the 1980s. It then sets out four limits on the method: its premise, its historical limit, its role limit and its human limit. A closing section on each limit ends with the authors' own response to the Marx–Engels relationship question.

Zhao and Zhang contend that Western Marxology starts from a "presumption of guilt" against Engels. They accept that two individuals with different backgrounds and styles will differ, and that these differences helped their collaboration. But they say "opposition" theorists inflate such differences into essential ones. The authors also argue that Marx's and Engels's thought developed through three historical periods, so the late Engels, writing after 1883, cannot be set against the earlier Marx. They describe the Marxology of the 1844 Manuscripts as an anachronistic comparison. The two men divided theoretical labour, with Marx on political economy and Engels on science, military affairs and the workers' movement. The authors argue that this division still left them in agreement in spirit and essence. They call the idea that Engels "invented" Marxism a politically motivated conspiracy theory, and insist the question is political as well as academic.

On the human limit, the authors defend the Marx–Engels friendship and Engels's editing of volumes II and III of Capital against the doubts raised by Rubel and Carver. They also reject the claim that the friendship rested on financial dependence. They conclude that comparing differences between Marx and Engels is academically legitimate. Such work must, however, begin from a scientific understanding of their relationship, respect historical context, and refuse sensational exaggeration. Read the original if you want a Chinese Marxist critique of Levine, Rubel, Carver and Hook on the Marx–Engels question, and a view of how Chinese scholars frame its political dimension.
quoteEn: Therefore, correctly positioning the relationship between Marx and Engels is the methodological premise for using the difference analysis method.
quoteZh: 因此，正确定位马克思恩格斯的关系是使用差异分析方法的方法论前提。

t: On Mao Zedong's original contributions to Marxist philosophy
zh: 论毛泽东对马克思主义哲学的原创性贡献
source: Journal of Hunan University of Science and Technology (Social Science Edition), 2022 no. 2
paras: Zhao Shifa and Zhang Hao ask in what sense Mao Zedong's philosophical thought is an original contribution to Marxist philosophy. They write against dogmatist and empiricist denials of this originality, and against Western-centric views that reject a distinctively Chinese path to modernity. Their thesis is that Mao's contribution was not ordinary theoretical innovation but originality in the strict sense. In their account it achieved the first historic leap in adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times, in its philosophical dimension.

The article has three parts. The first defines originality and sets out the substance of Mao's contribution. The second surveys its content: Mao's theory of modernization and his critique and remaking of the core ideas of Western capitalist modernity, namely science, democracy, freedom, equality and fraternity. The third discusses its theoretical and practical significance, including for Party-building and the international spread of Chinese discourse today.

The authors define originality as building on predecessors, not copying them, and as speaking one's own words through "continuing" or "countering" earlier theory. They also count an originality of theoretical thinking, in which new experience from practice is abstracted into theory. Mao's work shows this in content (the universality and particularity of contradiction, practice and cognition, seeking truth from facts, new-democratic theory) and in form (making Marxist philosophy "speak Chinese" through everyday formulations). It also shows it in transcending dogmatism and empiricism. The central claim is that Mao reworked each Western modern ideal. He treated science as seeking truth from facts, democracy as people's democratic dictatorship and self-criticism, and freedom as knowledge of necessity and transformation of the world.
