He tied equality to labour and the fight against bureaucracy, and replaced "fraternity" with serving the people wholeheartedly. The authors reject Western readings of Mao as a voluntarist or as a nationalist who was not truly Marxist.

The authors conclude that Mao's contribution enabled the modern enlightenment of the Chinese people, laid the theoretical basis for a path of modernization different from the West's, and supports the Party's theoretical innovation today. They also argue it offers a method for countering Western ideological pressure and for communicating Chinese discourse, including in building a community with a shared future for mankind. Read the original if you want a Chinese academic case for Mao's philosophical originality, including his treatment of the Western ideals of science, democracy, freedom, equality and fraternity.
quoteEn: Mao Zedong made Marxist philosophy speak Chinese, expounding it in language the Chinese people could understand, so that it was down-to-earth in expression, grasped by the masses, and thereby achieved the Sinification and popularisation of Marxism.
quoteZh: 毛泽东使马克思主义哲学说中国话，以中国人民能够听得懂的话语进行阐述，使马克思主义哲学在表达上接地气，被大众所理解，进而实现马克思主义中国化与大众化。

glossary.zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化
glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
glossary.explanation: The official formula for the Party's project of fitting Marxism to China's conditions and to each historical period. Mao's thought is described in Party documents as its first historic leap.

A principle of the Party's ideological line, tied to Mao's 1930s–40s writings and later reaffirmed under Deng Xiaoping. It calls for starting from objective reality, not from texts or abstract doctrine.
Mao's formula for the state form of New China. It means democracy for the people combined with coercive rule over those classed as enemies of the people.
A guiding principle of the Party popularised by Mao in 1944. It is presented as the Party's purpose and standard of conduct.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: A foreign-policy concept promoted by Xi Jinping since 2012–13, calling for shared international development and security.

t: Carry forward the spirit of historical initiative and travel well the new-era road of "taking the exam"
zh: 发扬历史主动精神 走好新时代赶考路
paras: This short commentary in Guangming Daily takes up the call by General Secretary Xi Jinping, at the opening of a spring 2022 training course for young and middle-aged cadres at the Central Party School, that Party members and leaders should carry forward the "spirit of historical initiative". Li Hongwei argues that this spirit is a valuable asset formed over a century of Party struggle. In Li's account, it shows historical consciousness, confidence, responsibility and creativity, and it requires acting proactively in the face of opportunities, difficulties and risks.

The piece is organised in three sections that follow Xi's formula: seizing opportunities without hesitating or waiting; confronting difficulties without shifting responsibility or evading them; and responding actively to risks without shrinking back or dodging. Li draws on classical Chinese sayings, the Book of Changes, the Party's history, and the Fourteenth Five-Year Plan proposals. A short closing passage calls on cadres to throw themselves into the new journey.

On opportunity, Li argues that opportunities and crises are dialectically united and can turn into each other. Seizing them requires strategic and systems thinking and the ability to recognise, respond to and initiate change. The author describes the present as a period of important strategic opportunity amid "changes unseen in a century" and the pandemic, and links it to Chinese modernization and a community with a shared future for mankind. On difficulty, Li invokes the Marxist view that contradictions are universal and recounts the Party's achievements across revolution, construction, reform and the new era, naming model figures such as Wang Jinxi, Jiao Yulu and Zhang Guimei. On risk, Li calls for vigilance against "black swan" and "grey rhino" events, bottom-line thinking, balancing development and security, stronger risk-prevention mechanisms and readiness for struggle.

Li concludes that history favours the resolute and does not wait for the hesitant, and that the Party must therefore vigorously uphold the spirit of historical initiative to win greater victories on the new journey. The text is a hortatory piece aimed at cadres, and it shows how the Party's leadership frames historical agency and risk management in 2022. Read the original if you want a compact example of how official commentary translates Xi's call for "historical initiative" into guidance for officials.
quoteEn: The Communist's sense of opportunity is a rational spirit of scientific anticipation, an enterprising quality of keeping pace with the times, and a historical responsibility borne on one's shoulders.
quoteZh: 共产党人的机遇意识，是一种科学预判的理性精神，是一种与时俱进的进取品质，是一种责任在肩的历史担当。

glossary.explanation: A phrase used in Party discourse for the Party's capacity to act proactively and seize the moment in history. Xi Jinping stressed it in 2022 and it was written into the 2021 Party history resolution.
The official term for China's own path to modernization, presented as distinct from Western models. It was elaborated especially after the 19th and 20th Party Congresses.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's concept for China's vision of international relations based on cooperation and shared development.

glossary.en: black swan and grey rhino events
glossary.explanation: Risk metaphors in official language: a black swan is an unpredictable shock, and a grey rhino is a visible but neglected major threat.

t: Writing a new chapter of Marxist political economy
zh: 书写马克思主义政治经济学新篇章
paras: Liu Yuanchun, writing in the People's Daily in April 2022, takes up one passage of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era: its "clarification" of the basic economic system, the market–government relationship, the new development stage, philosophy and pattern, high-quality development, and coordination of development and security. Liu argues that this passage reflects a deep understanding of the laws of China's economic development. In Liu's account it makes an original contribution to the political economy of socialism with Chinese characteristics and writes a new chapter of Marxist political economy.

The commentary is a short theoretical exposition that takes the components of the passage in turn. It covers the basic socialist economic system, the "decisive role" of the market, the triad of the new development stage, the new development philosophy and the new development pattern, then high-quality development, and finally development and security. It closes with economic results since the 18th Party Congress (2012).

Liu's central claim is that each component answers a specific theoretical or practical problem. The basic economic system (public ownership as the mainstay, distribution according to work as the mainstay, the socialist market economy) is said to go beyond capitalist logic by guarding against polarisation, class opposition, monopoly and recurrent crisis, while avoiding the defects of the traditional planned economy. Letting the market play the decisive role in allocating resources while the government plays its role better is presented as China's answer to a worldwide economic puzzle, with the Party's formulation shifting from a "basic" to a "decisive" role. Liu also argues that high-quality development is a general requirement for all regions and for the long term, and that security and development are "two wings of one body", each the precondition of the other.

Liu concludes that the thought has been proved scientific, truthful, people-centred and practical, citing GDP of 114 trillion yuan in 2021 and per capita GDP above 12,000 US dollars. Liu urges unity around the Party Central Committee with Xi Jinping at its core and guidance by this thought. Read the original if you want a concise example of how official commentary frames Xi's economic thought as an advance in Marxist political economy.
quoteEn: Letting the market play the decisive role in resource allocation while the government plays its role better is China's answer to the worldwide economic puzzle of the relationship between government and market.
quoteZh: 使市场在资源配置中起决定性作用，更好发挥政府作用，是对政府和市场关系这道经济学世界性难题的中国解答。

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018. It is presented as the latest stage in adapting Marxism to China.

glossary.zh: 社会主义基本经济制度
glossary.explanation: The official formula combining public ownership as the mainstay with diverse forms of ownership, distribution according to work as the mainstay with other modes, and the socialist market economy. The 4th Plenum of the 19th Central Committee (2019) set out this three-part definition.
The Party's guideline of innovative, coordinated, green, open and shared development, put forward in 2015.
The strategy of making the domestic economic cycle the mainstay while domestic and international cycles reinforce each other. It was put forward in 2020.
The official theme of economic and social development in the 14th Five-Year Plan period, stressing quality and efficiency over speed of growth.

t: Era characteristics of the Party's leadership in building a modern economic system
zh: 党领导建设现代化经济体系的时代特征
paras: Fu Chunyu and Zhao Xinpeng, writing in the China Social Sciences Today in January 2022, ask how the Communist Party of China has led the construction of a modern economic system and what is distinctive about that leadership in the present era. They argue that the Party made top-level design for this task around high-quality development and supply-side structural reform, and then gave it new content and a new yardstick by linking it to the new development pattern.

This short commentary has two main parts. The first covers the top-level design set out at the 19th Party Congress (2017), including the theoretical basis in the new development philosophy and five practical characteristics of the Party's leadership. The second turns to the new stage of development, in which the first centenary goal has been met, and examines how the "dual circulation" strategy of the 14th Five-Year Plan reshapes the task. It draws throughout on Party documents, the Historical Resolution and Xi Jinping's statements.

In the first part, the authors present supply-side structural reform as the response to problems such as a manufacturing sector they describe as "large but not strong", and the new development philosophy as the directional guide. They list five features of Party leadership: long-term planning combined with short-term breakthroughs, theoretical innovation leading practice, comprehensive and coordinated advance, effective concrete policies, and learning from others while keeping Chinese characteristics. In the second part, they argue that the new development pattern serves as both macro-level guidance and an objective test of the modern economic system. They identify two criteria, expanding domestic demand and keeping circulation unobstructed, and four new requirements: demand as the strategic base, smooth internal circulation, better investment structure, and coordination of development with security.

The authors conclude that the new development pattern and the modern economic system are two sides of one task, and that this combination shows the Party "upholding fundamental principles while innovating". In their view, standards have become clearer, the layout more flexible and the paths more concrete. They hold that only continued, centralised Party leadership over economic work, part of Xi Jinping Thought on the economy, can carry the project forward toward a strong modern socialist country and the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. Read the original if you want a compact statement of how Party commentators in early 2022 linked the modern economic system to dual circulation.
quoteEn: The new development pattern is the macro-level guide and objective standard for building a modern economic system.
quoteZh: 新发展格局是现代化经济体系建设的宏观指引和客观标准。

glossary.explanation: A goal set out at the 19th Party Congress (2017): an integrated economic system covering innovation, rural revitalisation, regional coordination, market reform and opening up, intended to support high-quality development.

A policy line launched around 2015 that aims to improve the quality of supply and fix structural imbalances in the real economy. It is associated with the "three cuts, one reduction, one supplement" measures.
The five-part guideline of innovative, coordinated, green, open and shared development, put forward in the 13th Five-Year Plan.
A strategy of "dual circulation" that makes the domestic cycle the mainstay while domestic and international cycles reinforce each other. It was written into the 14th Five-Year Plan.
The official approach, set out at the 19th Party Congress, of shifting from speed of growth to quality and efficiency.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.literal: great revival of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The Party's long-term national goal, usually tied to building a strong modern socialist country by the middle of the century.

t: The roots, essence and way out of de-globalization: a historical-materialist perspective
zh: 逆全球化的根源、本质与出路：基于唯物史观的视角
source: China Social Sciences Journal (中国社会科学报), 1 March 2022
paras: Song Dexiao asks why de-globalization (逆全球化) has emerged and spread, and what could resolve it. Writing in 2022, the author notes that most scholars approach the phenomenon through economics or diplomacy. Song proposes instead a historical-materialist reading tied to the history of capitalism and its globalization. The thesis is that de-globalization is a conflict-laden form of capitalism's own development, essentially a development problem, whose way out is a community with a shared future for mankind.

The short article, first published in the China Social Sciences Journal, traces de-globalization from anti-globalization thought to state policy. It names the 2008 financial crisis, the 2016 Brexit vote and Trump's election, and the Covid-19 pandemic from 2020 as turning points. It then moves through three sections: the roots of de-globalization, its essence, and its trend and way out. Along the way Song draws on Giddens, Arif Dirlik and Fukuyama.

Song first criticises the 'losers of globalization' or 'losers of modernization' theory. In the author's view, it reduces the issue to the distribution of gains and ignores underlying social relations, and the United States, a major beneficiary despite its trade deficits, shows the problem. Song instead locates the roots in the global expansion of the capitalist mode of production: uneven distribution of gains, the internationalization of capitalism's inherent contradiction between socialized production and private appropriation, and clashes between nations over Western-set rules. The article argues that, with war and colonial plunder no longer available, developed countries shift their crises abroad through trade wars and barriers, as the US did after the 2008 crisis. Song reads this as an extension of capitalism's contradictions to the global scale and as a crisis of its governance, politics and values.

Song concludes that de-globalization is a temporary strategic adjustment by developed capitalist states, aimed at a global trading system more favourable to capital, and so it cannot solve capitalism's inherent contradictions or alter the course of world history. The author calls for openly opposing de-globalization, giving up illusions about developed capitalist countries, and pursuing balanced, mutually respectful development that respects each nation's chosen path. Song presents Xi Jinping's idea of a community with a shared future for mankind and the Belt and Road Initiative as the practical answer. Read the original if you want a concise example of how a Chinese scholar applies historical materialism to de-globalization and links it to official foreign-policy concepts.
quoteEn: De-globalization is, in the final analysis, a development problem. To resolve it properly, the key still lies in development: only when all countries and regions around the world develop in a balanced way and progress together can the root problem be solved.
quoteZh: 逆全球化问题归根到底是一个发展问题，要妥善解决这一问题，重点还是在于发展，只有全球范围内各国各地区均衡发展、共同进步，才能解决根源性问题。

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: A concept promoted by Xi Jinping since the early 2010s. It presents the world's countries as interdependent and calls for cooperation, mutual respect and shared development in international relations.
An international infrastructure and economic cooperation programme launched by China in 2013, linking China with Asia, Europe, Africa and beyond.

A term for policies and currents that roll back economic integration, such as trade barriers and protectionism. The article treats it as a stage beyond earlier 'anti-globalization' thought, now carried out by governments.
The Marxist theory that material production and the social relations built on it shape historical development. The article uses it as its analytical method.

keywords: community with a shared future for mankind

t: From the complete Capital to an open "critique of political economy"
st: MEGA² Section II and Marx research in Germany
zh: 从完整的《资本论》到开放的“政治经济学批判”
zhSub: MEGA2第二部分与德国的马克思研究
paras: Zhang Yixiu asks what the completed publication of Section II of the historical-critical edition of the Marx-Engels works (MEGA²) has changed in German scholarship on Marx's critique of political economy. The article, first published in the Chinese Social Sciences Today in January 2022, argues that the edition moves readers away from the image of a single finished Capital and towards an open, unfinished process of research. It adds that recent German scholars use the new material for contemporary critical purposes, unlike the "Marxology" of the twentieth-century West.

Section II ran to 15 volumes (23 books) from 1976 to 2012. Zhang notes that it first published many manuscripts, including parts of the 1861–1863 manuscripts and dozens of manuscripts for Volumes 2 and 3 of Capital. It also publishes the main versions of Capital separately, along with Engels's editorial drafts. The article surveys German research under five headings: periodisation, the status of key texts, method, theoretical content (value theory and crisis theory), and the Marx–Engels relationship.

On periodisation, Zhang reports that Carl-Erich Vollgraf and Hubmann read the manuscripts as belonging to two projects divided around 1863, the critique of political economy and Capital. On this reading, the six-book plan was largely a publishing strategy. Michael Heinrich, Ingo Stützle and others treat the Grundrisse and other texts as having independent themes. Zhang also presents debates on method and content: Haug, Reichelt, Wolf and Backhaus on value as a relational form, and Schefold on value-form theory as a Weberian "ideal type". Kurz and Henning disagree over whether the falling rate of profit was ever settled. The Marx–Engels question is then shown to depend on wider methodological positions. Heinrich stresses Engels's active shaping of Volume 3, Roth defends Engels's caution, and Krätke and Elbe differ over whether his historical reading distorts Marx.

Zhang concludes that German scholars mostly want to free the philosophical wisdom of historical materialism and the method of the critique of political economy from a fixed, dogmatic image of Capital, so as to address present-day capitalism. Zhang says this work is beginning to influence research in China. The article proposes that Chinese researchers, keeping a Marxist standpoint and an open attitude, use the MEGA² materials to move beyond teleological readings and rebuild the path of Marx's critique. Read the original if you want a compact guide to the German scholars and debates around MEGA² Section II, as seen from Chinese Marxist scholarship.
quoteEn: Unlike the conception at the start of publication, MEGA² Section II ultimately records an unfinished process of research, in which Marx kept taking up new objects of study and trying new methods of exposition.
quoteZh: 与出版之初的构想不同，MEGA2第二部分最终记录了一段未完成的研究过程，马克思总是不断涉及新的研究对象，尝试新的论述方法。

t: The "non-identity" dimension of Marx's empirical research method
zh: 马克思经验研究方法的“非同一性”维度
paras: This short piece, first published in the China Social Sciences Today in January 2022, asks what distinguishes Marx's empirical method from both the speculation of the Young Hegelians and the empiricism of English and French philosophy. Yang argues that Marx rejected metaphysical thinking built on "identity" and affirmed the positive significance of "non-identity". On this reading, it is the interaction of subjective and objective, abstract and concrete, experience and theory that gives historical materialism its scientific character.

Yang organises the discussion under three headings: matter (zhìliào), the individual, and difference. Each is tied to a passage or episode in Marx's work, including The German Ideology and Marx's late writings on Russia. Hegel's Phenomenology of Spirit and Dewey's The Quest for Certainty are cited as background.

On matter, Yang contends that Marx started from real individuals and their material conditions of life, which can be confirmed by purely empirical means, and so countered the "old philosophy" of ultimate causes. Under capitalism, Yang says, identity appears as the logic of capital, presented as the only rational reality. On the individual, Yang reads Marx as showing how capital and metaphysics together reduce living persons to servants of abstract powers, and as seeking a path to self-liberation for concrete individuals. On difference, Yang points to Marx's letters on Russia, which reject turning his account of Western European capitalism into a universal philosophy of history. Yang concludes that paths of development are plural rather than uniform.

Yang concludes that Marx valued experience without being confined to it or worshipping it, and that he insisted on concrete analysis of concrete problems. Experience is treated as changing with time, place and conditions, so research cannot rest on fixed concepts. Read the original if you want a compact account of how Marx's anti-metaphysical and anti-universalist stance is framed in Chinese Marxist scholarship.
quoteEn: Marx valued experience, but he was not confined to it and still more opposed superstitious faith in it; he stressed analysing concrete problems concretely on the basis of empirical facts.
quoteZh: 马克思重视经验,但他并不局限于经验,更反对迷信经验,而是强调在运用经验事实的基础上对具体问题展开具体分析。

t: Mao Zedong's thinking and practice on "we must pay attention to economic work" in the Central Soviet Area
zh: 中央苏区时期毛泽东关于“必须注意经济工作”的思考与实践
source: Documents of the Party (Dang de wenxian), 2022 no. 1
paras: Yu Shouping examines the call Mao Zedong made in August 1933, at the economic construction conference of seventeen counties in the south of the Central Revolutionary Base Area, that 'we must pay attention to economic work'. Yu notes that scholarship on this directive is thin and proposes to interpret it through Mao's texts of the period, including 'We Must Pay Attention to Economic Work', 'Our Economic Policy' and 'Show Concern for the Well-being of the Masses and Pay Attention to Methods of Work', set against their historical background. The article argues that the directive guided economic work in the Central Soviet Area, helped break the Kuomintang blockade, improved living conditions and consolidated the base.

The article is organised in five sections: the positioning of economic construction relative to revolutionary war; its key tasks (agriculture, industry, foreign trade, cooperatives); mobilising the masses; training cadres; and leadership style and work methods. Yu draws on Mao's speeches and reports, Soviet government decrees and resolutions, and local examples such as Changgang and Caixi townships and Tingzhou city.

Yu's central claim is that economic construction had to 'revolve around the central task of revolutionary war'. Mao rejected two mistaken views: that economic work was impossible in wartime, and that it had become the centre of all tasks. In Yu's account, Mao placed agriculture first, with land distribution, organised exchange of labour and women's participation. He also sought the planned recovery of handicrafts and some industry, state-directed foreign trade to evade the blockade, and consumer, producer and credit cooperatives. Yu stresses that mobilisation depended on meeting the masses' daily needs and on strengthening the worker–peasant alliance, through measures such as economic construction bonds. Cadres were to be trained as 'commanders on the economic front'. Yu reports that Mao favoured state, cooperative and private enterprise advancing together, held that private economy was needed in the interests of state and people, and criticised bureaucratic leadership.

Yu concludes that Mao's thinking supplied practical guidance and left the Party experience in leading economic work. Rereading it, especially its methods of thought, is said to help in understanding the Party's history and in handling today's economic construction. Read the original if you want a detailed, source-based account of Soviet-period economic policy under Mao, with concrete cases and figures, as presented in Party-history scholarship.
quoteEn: Economic construction must revolve around the central task of revolutionary war.
quoteZh: 经济建设必须是环绕着革命战争这个中心任务的

glossary.explanation: The main Communist-held base area in southern Jiangxi and western Fujian in the early 1930s, centred on Ruijin. It was the seat of the Chinese Soviet Republic's provisional central government, founded in 1931.

t: From a complete Capital to an open "critique of political economy"
st: MEGA2 Section II and Marx research in Germany
zh: 从完整的《资本论》到开放的“政治经济学批判”
zhSub: MEGA2第二部分与德国的马克思研究
source: Chinese Social Sciences Today (Zhongguo shehui kexue bao), 4 January 2022
paras: Zhang Yixiu asks what German scholars have made of the second section of the Marx-Engels-Gesamtausgabe (MEGA2), which covers Marx's economic manuscripts and the editions of Capital, and what Chinese research can learn from them. Published from 1976 and completed in 2012 (15 volumes, 23 books), the section presents all of Marx's surviving manuscripts on the critique of political economy from the late 1850s, together with several editions of Capital and Engels's editorial drafts. Zhang argues that German work based on this material has moved from the image of a finished Capital to that of an open, unfinished process of research.

The article first names the section's two contributions to the sources: first publication of many manuscripts, and separate publication of the main versions of Capital, which allows comparison of Marx's drafts with Engels's edited text. It then surveys German scholarship under five headings: periodisation of Marx's thought, the status of key texts, theory and method, theoretical content (value theory and crisis theory), and the relationship between Marx and Engels. Thinkers discussed include Carl-Erich Vollgraf, Michael Heinrich, Ingo Stützle, Wolfgang Fritz Haug, Helmut Reichelt, Dieter Wolf, Hans-Georg Backhaus, Bertram Schefold, Heinz Kurz, Christoph Henning, Regina Roth and Ingo Elbe.

Zhang's central claim is that the section's original title, "Capital and its preparatory texts", no longer holds. Vollgraf divides the texts at 1863 into two projects, and the editor Gerald Hubmann is reported as saying there is neither a completed Capital nor a body of manuscripts that merely prepares it. Stützle reads the 1857–58 Grundrisse as a self-clarifying text rather than a key to Capital, and Heinrich distinguishes three stages of work on Capital. Scholars also divide over whether Marx's value categories are logical rather than historical (Backhaus, Reichelt, Wolf), over the falling rate of profit (Kurz against Henning), and over whether Engels distorted Marx (Heinrich and Elbe against Roth and Michael Krätke). Zhang notes that the Neue Marx-Lektüre is not treated in detail here.

Zhang concludes that, since the 21st century and especially since the financial crisis, German scholarship differs from twentieth-century Western "Marxology". In Zhang's account, most scholars seek to free the philosophy and method of the critique of political economy from a fixed, dogmatic picture of Capital, not to discredit Marx or Engels. Zhang proposes that Chinese researchers, holding to a Marxist standpoint and an open attitude, use the MEGA2 materials to avoid teleological readings and rebuild the path of Marx's critique. Read the original if you want a concise guide to the main German debates on MEGA2 Section II and on Marx's economic manuscripts.
quoteEn: Unlike the conception at the start of publication, MEGA2 Section II ultimately records an unfinished process of research, in which Marx kept taking up new objects of study and trying new methods of presentation.
quoteZh: 与出版之初的构想不同，MEGA2第二部分最终记录了一段未完成的研究过程，马克思总是不断涉及新的研究对象，尝试新的论述方法。

glossary.explanation: A term for Western scholarly study of Marx's life and texts, often philological. In Chinese writing it is sometimes used for twentieth-century Western work thought to separate Marx from Marxism.
Marx's own name for his project, used as the subtitle of Capital and the title of his 1859 work. The article treats it as a wider and more open project than Capital alone.
A German current from the 1960s onward that reads Marx's value theory as a critique of social forms and categories, not as a labour-substance theory. Backhaus and Reichelt are associated with it.

t: The "non-identity" dimension of Marx's empirical research method
zh: 马克思经验研究方法的“非同一性”维度
paras: This short commentary, first published in the Chinese Social Sciences Today in January 2022, asks what distinguishes Marx's empirical method from both the speculation of the Young Hegelians and British and French empiricism. Yang argues that Marx rejected metaphysical thinking based on "identity" and affirmed the positive significance of "non-identity". In Yang's account, this is what gives historical materialism its scientific footing.

The article is organised around three emphases in Marx's method: matter (质料, the material substrate), the individual, and difference. Yang draws mainly on The German Ideology, Marx's 1877 letter to the editors of Otechestvennye Zapiski, and his reply to Vera Zasulich. Dewey and Hegel are cited as background.

On matter, Yang holds that Marx countered the long Western pursuit of an unchanging "One" by starting from real individuals and their material living conditions, which can be verified empirically. In capitalist society, Yang says, "identity" appears as capital's logic posing as the only rational reality. On the individual, Yang reads Marx as showing that capital and metaphysics together reduce living persons to abstract functions, and that the remedy lies in changing the worldly basis of life. On difference, Yang cites Marx's late study of Russia and his refusal to turn his account of Western European capitalism into a universal philosophy of history. Paths of development, Yang argues, differ with historical setting.

Yang concludes that Marx valued experience without being confined by it or deferring to it. He treated experience as changing, and analysed concrete problems concretely. Marx's aim, Yang says, is the self-emancipation of free, concrete individuals. Read the original if you want a compact reading of Marx's methodology that links empirical research to a critique of conceptual uniformity and to the question of differing national paths.
quoteEn: Marx valued experience, but he was not confined to it and still more opposed superstitious faith in it; he stressed analysing concrete problems concretely on the basis of empirical facts.
quoteZh: 马克思重视经验，但他并不局限于经验，更反对迷信经验，而是强调在运用经验事实的基础上对具体问题展开具体分析。

t: The Chinese Communist Party's exploration of agricultural labour mutual aid in the Soviet areas period
zh: 苏区时期中国共产党关于农业劳动互助的探索
paras: Geng Lei examines how the Chinese Communist Party experimented with agricultural labour mutual aid in the Soviet areas (the rural revolutionary base areas of the late 1920s and early 1930s). The article argues that, alongside land distribution, the Party used mutual aid to pool scarce labour, sustain farming and support the war effort. Geng notes that scholarship on the topic is thin and offers a preliminary survey.

The study draws mainly on the newspaper Red China (Hongse Zhonghua), Soviet government work reports and memoirs. It is organised chronologically and by form: 'Saturday voluntary labour', 'joint cultivation', the 'spring ploughing campaign' with 'ploughing mutual aid', and finally the labour mutual aid societies. Each is set against Soviet Russian precedents, namely Lenin's communist subbotniks and the early collective 'joint cultivation societies'.

Geng's central claim is that the Party adapted Soviet models to local conditions. Saturday labour, carried out by Party members, Youth League members and cadres, helped families of Red Army soldiers with farming, so that soldiers need not be recalled home; it also cultivated public-minded habits. Joint cultivation appeared in two variants, one with shared labour but unequal product shares and one with equal division. From 1931–32 the spring ploughing campaign made mutual aid official policy, but enforcement was uneven because mass mobilisation was weak. The labour mutual aid societies, regularised by the 1933 Outline for Organising Labour Mutual Aid Societies, are presented as the mature form. They widened mutual aid from cadre-to-peasant to peasant-to-peasant, and Geng cites 1934 membership figures such as 18,220 members in 329 societies in Xingguo.

Geng concludes that, though still at an early stage, these practices raised farm output, advanced revolutionary mobilisation and strengthened peasants' identification with the Party and the Soviet regime. They also supplied experience for later production mutual aid movements. The article offers a way to understand mass mobilisation, army–people relations and rural governance in this period. Read the original if you study the early rural economy of the Chinese revolution, Soviet influence on Communist policy, or need the primary-source citations from Red China.
quoteEn: The labour mutual aid society was a relatively mature organisational form of agricultural mutual aid production, formed in the Soviet areas period through continuous exploration and adjustment.
quoteZh: 劳动互助社，是苏区时期农业劳动互助生产模式经过不断探索和调适后形成的较为成熟的组织形态

t: On how historical materialism goes beyond traditional moral philosophy
zh: 论历史唯物主义对传统道德哲学的超越
paras: Zhang Guangquan, in a short commentary first published in China Social Sciences Today in February 2022, asks how historical materialism relates to the split between "is" and "ought" that has troubled traditional moral philosophy. The author argues that Marx and Engels turned this apparently epistemological problem into a practical one, and in doing so went beyond traditional moral philosophy.

The piece begins with Hume's problem, the claimed impossibility of deriving value judgements from factual ones. Zhang traces its consequences in epistemology, in the long dispute over truth and value, and in philosophy of history, where it has fed doubts about the scientific character of historical materialism. The article then sets out three successive transformations of the problem within Marx and Engels's thought.

Zhang holds that traditional approaches treated morality as consciousness detached from the real world, whereas historical materialism derives it from the mode of material production. In the foundational period the problem becomes the unity of the "real human being" (as factual basis) and the "true human being" (as value orientation). In the period of initial establishment it becomes the relation between historical laws and the choice of path. In the period of deepening it becomes the relation between capitalism and communism, where, in Zhang's account, the self-negation of capital's logic drives the transition.

Zhang concludes that historical materialism resolves the dilemma by returning the "is" and "ought" relation to real individuals' practice and to the laws of historical development. The author calls on scholars to discuss this question widely, so as to answer doubts about historical materialism's scientific status and to clarify the relation between the communist movement and communist ideal. Read the original if you want a brief statement of how a Chinese Marxist scholar frames Marx's answer to Hume's problem.
quoteEn: Historical materialism has scientifically resolved the theoretical predicament of traditional moral philosophy.
quoteZh: 历史唯物主义科学地解决了传统道德哲学的理论困境

t: The utopian reconstruction in twentieth-century Western Marxism
zh: 20世纪西方马克思主义的乌托邦重构
paras: Why did some twentieth-century Western Marxists try to rehabilitate utopia, and did the effort work? Xie argues that Ernst Bloch, Herbert Marcuse and others tried to equate utopia with socialism, and that this was both absurd and futile. In Xie's account, any attempt to revive utopia remains a form of feverish fantasy.

The newspaper commentary first sets out the background: early twentieth-century liberal anti-utopianism, which treated utopia and socialism as one and so cast doubt on socialism's legitimacy. It then identifies three ways in which Western Marxists reconstructed utopia, and ends with a critique of all three.

Xie describes the three methods as follows. Bloch's 'ontological' version grounds utopian spirit in hope and drive. Marcuse's 'aesthetic' version calls for a cultural and instinctual revolution to replace proletarian revolution. Russell Jacoby's 'conceptual' version favours an iconoclastic, purely negative utopianism. Xie holds that these versions are idealist, invert the relation between economic base and superstructure, and lead to political apathy. Rather than defending socialism's legitimacy, the author says, they substituted the false question of utopia's legitimacy for the real one. Citing Engels, Xie adds that their utopias lack any means of realisation, which leaves them even less attainable than the classical utopias.

Xie concludes that refuting the liberal charge does not require a road to utopia, and that utopia can be affirmed only if its illusory character is recognised. The author treats these thinkers as well-meaning dreamers whose work is at most a small cultural niche. Read the original if you want a short, polemical Marxist-Leninist critique of Bloch, Marcuse and Jacoby's utopianism, written for a Chinese academic newspaper.
quoteEn: However Western Marxists reconstruct utopia, their basic stance is itself 'utopian', that is, illusory and feverish.
quoteZh: 西方马克思主义者不论以何种方式对乌托邦进行重构，其基本立场都是“乌托邦式”的，即虚幻且狂热的。

t: The evolution of value-form theory: the historical thread of the "New Reading of Marx"
zh: 价值形式理论演进——“新马克思阅读”的历史脉络
paras: This short piece, first published in the China Social Sciences Today (Zhongguo shehui kexue bao) in February 2022, asks how the "New Reading of Marx" (Neue Marx-Lektüre), with its focus on the value form, fits into the longer development of Western Marxism. Li Qiankun argues that value-form theory has advanced along a traceable line in four historical stages, and that tracing it helps clarify the theory's content and significance.

The article moves chronologically. It begins with Marx's own foundation of the theory, then covers the rediscovery of the value form in the 1920s, the wave of research from the 1960s to the 1980s, and the period from the 1990s to the present. Along the way it names neo-Kantian, Soviet and Western Marxist currents, the Frankfurt School, the Uno school, the regulation school and the English-language \"new dialectics\" school.

Li holds that Marx developed the value form in order to find a scientific starting point for presenting the critique of political economy. The author traces this from the 1857–58 and 1861–63 manuscripts to the successive treatments of the value-form text in Capital. Li then argues that the 1920s were a pivotal stage, because Franz Petry, Isaak Rubin, Pashukanis, Lukács, Sohn-Rethel and Pollock each raised basic questions about the theory. The third stage, in Li's account, was driven by criticism of the welfare state as a new form of state monopoly capitalism. In this stage Backhaus and Reichelt defended Marx's philosophical method against marginalist, neo-Ricardian and Habermasian approaches, while Uno, the regulation school and Christopher Arthur pursued parallel lines. For the present stage, Li links the theory to neoliberal monetisation and financial capitalism, and describes it as grasping the most abstract social reality that the theory can reach.

Li draws three conclusions. Value-form theory has always been discussed under concrete historical conditions and for varying theoretical purposes. The foreign Marxist tradition of value-form analysis helps explain the structure of foreign Marxism and its interdisciplinary links with philosophy and sociology. Finally, scholars who debate the theory in speculative, abstract terms risk an ahistorical dead end if they ignore its social and historical grounding. Read the original if you want a compact orientation to the lineage of the New Reading of Marx and value-form theory, as presented by a Chinese scholar of foreign Marxism.
quoteEn: Value-form theory has always been discussed under concrete social and historical conditions and for different theoretical purposes.
quoteZh: 价值形式理论从来都是在具体的社会历史条件下出于不同的理论目的而被加以讨论的

glossary.explanation: A current of Marx interpretation that emerged in West Germany in the 1960s around Hans-Georg Backhaus and Helmut Reichelt. It treats the critique of political economy as a theory of value and social form.
Marx's analysis, in the first chapter of Capital, of why value must appear in the form of exchange-value and money. Later Marxists took it as a key to the critique of capitalist social forms.
The tradition of Lukács, Korsch, Gramsci and the Frankfurt School, which stressed philosophy, culture and critical theory over economics and party politics.

t: Misreadings of Capital in contemporary French critical theory
zh: 当代法国批判理论对《资本论》的误读
paras: Writing in a newspaper commentary (China Social Sciences Today, February 2022), Wang asks how contemporary French critical theory reads Marx's Capital. Wang argues that, although these thinkers treat Marx as a forerunner of the critique of modernity and Capital as a resource that cannot be avoided, their anti-essentialist, anti-reductionist and anti-historicist stance leads them to misread it.

The article covers the French currents that emerged after the May 1968 events and in response to Western Marxism. It sorts their readings of Capital into four paths: a generalised political economy, a scientific epistemology, an expansion of time and space, and a critique of power. Bataille, Lyotard, Baudrillard, Althusser, Badiou, Lefebvre, Bidet and Foucault serve as examples.

Wang's central claim is that these readings detach Capital from its historical-materialist base. Baudrillard's The Mirror of Production, in Wang's account, swaps material production for a sign-based political economy and turns the critique into romanticism. The Althusserian line is credited with restoring Marxism's wholeness but is said to stop at registering complexity without examining Capital's method. Lefebvre's production of space and Foucault's micro-power capture new features of capitalism, Wang says, but explain them through the construction of power, not their social-historical essence.

Wang grants the work some scholarly value and notes shared traits: stress on Capital's contemporary relevance, sensitivity to capitalism's structural contradictions, and interdisciplinary borrowing. Yet Wang concludes that the theory falls back into the "phrase-mongering revolution" Marx criticised. By abandoning class analysis and Marx's internal critique, it ends, Wang says, in fragmentation and utopian revolution. Read the original if you want a concise Chinese Marxist assessment of how French post-structuralist and post-modern thinkers treat Capital.
quoteEn: Whether it is the critique of generalised political economy or the critique of power, once it is cut off from concrete social-historical analysis and sets aside the method of class analysis, any pursuit of a future ideal society becomes rootless duckweed.
quoteZh: 无论是广义政治经济学批判，还是权力批判，一旦脱离了具体的社会历史分析、撇开了阶级分析方法，任何对未来理想社会的追寻都将成为无根之萍。

glossary.explanation: A phrase from Marx and Engels's polemics against the Young Hegelians, meaning radical rhetoric that does not engage with material conditions.

t: The awareness of real-world problems in the study of Marxist texts
zh: 马克思主义文本研究中的现实问题意识
source: China Social Sciences Today (Zhongguo shehui kexue bao), 27 January 2022
paras: Yang Hongyuan asks what textual study of Marxist works should aim at, and argues that it is more than philology. In Yang's view, proper study unites textual-edition verification, interpretation of the text and elucidation of its ideas. Its final purpose, the article contends, is intellectual elucidation, one level of which is solving real problems or revealing a text's real significance. Awareness of real-world problems is therefore integral to such study. The piece, a newspaper commentary, takes Capital as its test case.

The article first redefines what a 'real problem' is and how Capital should be classed. It then examines how changes in real problems shaped the structure of Capital, before drawing out the methodology that emerges from Marx's analysis of such problems. It ends by considering the contemporary value of Capital for present-day problems, including globalization and the significance of the Chinese path.

Yang holds that 'reality' in the philosophical sense is fact plus essence, and that only phenomena expressing the features and trends of an era count as real problems. On this basis Capital is Marx's distillation and analysis of the real problems of his time and an enquiry into the laws of social-historical development, as well as the theoretical expression of Marxism as a current of thought. Yang reads the shifting chapter structures of Capital's editions, and Marx's failure to finish Volumes 2 and 3, as responses to changing realities: the 1873 crisis, the defeat of the Paris Commune, and Marx's turn to capitalism's 'prehistory' and to Russia's village commune. Yang notes Marx's warning against turning his sketch of Western European capitalism into a universal philosophy of history. Methodological lessons are drawn from the analysis of money, commodity and capital as social relations, and from comparison with Hegel, Smith and Ricardo.

Yang concludes that Capital offers no ready-made answers today but remains a methodological resource, since the present era is still within the transition from history to world history. Questions Yang lists as open to its guidance include the nature of capital, how to govern the logic of capital, artificial intelligence, ecological civilization and human free individuality. Yang also calls for placing Capital within the later history of capital critique and for reassessing it in the light of globalization since the 1980s. Read the original if you want a concise statement of how a Chinese scholar links Marxist textual studies to contemporary problem-solving.
quoteEn: It can thus be seen that awareness of real-world problems is an inherent part of the study of Marxist texts.
quoteZh: 由此可见，现实问题意识是马克思主义文本研究的题中应有之义。

t: The logical levels of Marx's category of world history
zh: 马克思世界历史范畴的逻辑层次
paras: Marx and Engels use the term "world history" (shijie lishi) in several senses, and Zhou Kanglin asks how these senses relate. Writing in a newspaper commentary, Zhou argues that the contexts must be separated and their internal connections clarified before the theoretical essence and practical meaning of Marx's category can be grasped. The starting point is the claim that a world of "integrated" universal exchange has confirmed Marx's prediction that history becomes world history.

The article distinguishes three levels in the texts of Marx and Engels. The first is "world-historical significance" as opposed to local, regional or national significance, illustrated by Engels's essay on the condition of England and by The German Ideology. The second is "world history" in the sense of universal history, meaning the whole of human history, which Marx derives from human labour. The third is world history as a form of thought: the transition from closed national history to open, universal intercourse.

On the first level, Zhou reads Engels's remark that English workers' poverty had world-historical significance as tied to modern large-scale industry. Zhou reads the German Ideology passage as a mockery of German philosophers' inflated claims for the dissolution of Hegel's system, which had only local significance. On the second level, Zhou cites Marx's 1844 Manuscripts, in which world history is the process of humanity's birth through labour. Zhou says this goes beyond Feuerbach's "sensuous intuition" and treats labour itself as historically developing: regional handicraft produced a "discrete" world history, capitalist machine production an "alienated" one, and communist "self-activity" would produce a truly free and universal one. On the third level, Zhou holds that large-scale industry "first created world history", so that "history becoming world history" and "intercourse becoming world intercourse" are the same thing.

Zhou concludes that Marx's category differs from both compiled "world history" and the philosophy of universal history, though both fed into it. Marx and Engels needed the empirical material of national histories, especially English social history, to move the idea to the level of historical science. The bourgeoisie, in Zhou's account, is an unconscious instrument of a revolution that remains unfinished, and only the modern proletariat can rebuild the order of world intercourse. Zhou adds that the levels do not form a straight line of development and are often mixed within one text. Read the original if you want a compact guide to the different meanings of "world history" in Marx and Engels and how Chinese scholars separate them.
quoteEn: Clearly, for them, \"history becoming world history\" and \"intercourse becoming world intercourse\" are in fact synonymous; in essence they express the same content, and both take the development of large-scale industry as their real precondition.
quoteZh: 可见，在他们那里，“历史成为世界历史”与“交往成为世界交往”实际上是同义语，它们在本质上表达的是同一内容，它们都是以大工业的发展作为现实前提的。

t: Drawing on intellectual resources, innovating theoretical discourse
st: The internal connection between Marx's theory of world history and a community with a shared future for mankind
zh: 汲取思想养分 创新理论话语
zhSub: 马克思世界历史理论与人类命运共同体的内在联系
source: China Social Sciences Today (Zhongguo shehui kexue bao), 27 January 2022
paras: This short commentary, published in January 2022, asks how Marx's theory of world history relates to the idea of a community with a shared future for mankind. Meng argues that Chinese Communists took the theory as their intellectual basis in offering "Chinese wisdom" and a "Chinese approach" to global problems. In Meng's view, building such a community will move world history towards a peaceful, orderly and equal stage.

The piece has three parts. It first sets out the predictions in Marx's theory, then examines contemporary coordinates of world history, and finally discusses how the community idea is moving from concept to reality, with the Belt and Road Initiative as its main vehicle.

Meng reads Marx's global perspective, including his remarks on a "world literature" and on interdependence among nations, as anticipating today's reality, in which no country can stand apart from global risks. Marx's criticism of Eurocentrism and his view that Eastern societies might take a path different from Western capitalism are linked to socialism with Chinese characteristics, presented as an alternative for developing countries. Meng describes the post-2008 "anti-globalization" current as a Western attempt to rebuild a "selective globalization" that benefits only developed countries, and says leadership now depends on the ability to supply public goods.

Meng concludes that the community with a shared future for mankind makes Marx's distant goal concrete and practicable. It requires recognising that capitalist-led globalization has not ended, while seeking to transcend its constraints through struggle for development and cooperation amid divergent interests. Meng calls it a path from an "illusory community" to a "real community". Read the original if you want a brief, official-style account of how Chinese commentators ground this foreign-policy concept in Marxist theory.
quoteEn: History and facts tell us that a community with a shared future for mankind is a path by which humanity moves from an \"illusory community\" to a \"real community\".
quoteZh: 历史和事实告诉我们，人类命运共同体是人类由“虚幻共同体”走向“真正共同体”的一条路径。

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.literal: community of common destiny for humankind
glossary.explanation: A concept promoted by Xi Jinping since around 2012–2013 as the guiding idea of China's foreign policy and vision of global governance. It stresses interdependence, shared interests and cooperative development.
A Chinese initiative launched in 2013 to build infrastructure and trade links across Eurasia, Africa and beyond. Official discourse presents it as a practical platform for the shared-future idea.
The official name for the Chinese Communist Party's path and system since the reform era, combining Party leadership, public ownership and a market economy.
Marx and Engels' account of how capitalism and expanding exchange link nations into a single global historical process, replacing isolated local histories.

keywords: community with a shared future for mankind

t: The formation of Mao Zedong's materialist conception of history
zh: 毛泽东唯物史观的形成
paras: How did Mao Zedong come to hold the materialist conception of history? Tao Jialing, in a short piece first published in the Chinese Social Sciences Today in July 2021, argues that tracing this process helps explain the origins of the historical outlook of Chinese communists. The article holds that Mao's early materialist conception of history formed in three stages between 1918 and 1921.

The article follows Mao's writings, letters and activities month by month. It covers the "germination" stage (April 1918 to August 1919), the "formation" stage (September 1919 to December 1920) and the "establishment" stage (January to July 1921). Its sources include Mao's articles in the Xiang River Review, his letters to friends such as Cai Hesen, and the debates of the New People's Study Society.

In the first stage, Tao reads Mao's remark that the problem of food is the biggest problem, and his long essay "The Great Union of the Popular Masses", as early signs that social being determines social consciousness and that the people make history. For the second stage Tao lists seven developments: an "economic analysis" of social questions, attention to material production, Mao's sorting-out of competing doctrines through reading the Marxist classics, the spread of Marxist publications through the Cultural Book Society, the decision to found a party, the abandonment of reformism after the failure of the Hunan self-government movement, and a turn to violent revolution. Tao treats his December 1920 rejection of Russell's reformism and of anarchism as the decisive break. In the third stage, Mao's January 1921 letter calling the materialist conception of history the philosophical basis of "our party", and his attendance at the First Party Congress in July 1921, mark its establishment in thought and in practice.

Tao concludes that Mao's outlook arose from a dynamic process of "challenging yesterday's self" and mirrors the wider change in Chinese thought. In this account, Mao moved from revolutionary democracy to communism, driven by patriotism, and became a Marxist in belief and in revolutionary practice. Read the original if you want a compact, dated chronology of Mao's intellectual turn to Marxism in 1918–1921, with the key letters and essays identified.
quoteEn: The formation of Mao Zedong's materialist conception of history was the result of \"today's self challenging yesterday's self\", and it was a dynamic, continually constructed process.
quoteZh: 毛泽东唯物史观的形成乃其“今日之我与昨日之我挑战”的结果，其形成是一个动态的、不断构建的过程。

glossary.explanation: The Marxist theory that material production and economic relations shape social structures and historical development. It is the standard Chinese term for historical materialism.
A study society founded by Mao Zedong and others in Changsha in April 1918. Several members later became prominent in the communist movement.
A weekly journal Mao edited in Hunan in 1919, in which he published essays on popular organisation and social reform.
A bookshop and distribution venture Mao helped set up in Changsha in 1920. It sold Marxist works and new periodicals.

t: An analysis of the success code of a century-old Party
zh: 百年大党成功密码探析
paras: Marking the Communist Party of China's centenary in 2021, the article asks what explains its success. The authors point to the Party's status as the world's largest party by membership, its more than seventy years in power, and what they call the twin miracles of rapid economic growth and long-term social stability, along with lifting nearly 800 million people out of poverty. Their answer is that the Party has "a wise mind, a firm character and rich nourishment".

The article is organised around these three "codes". The first is a wise mind, drawn from arming the Party with scientific theory. The second is a firm character, forged through the Party's self-reform. The third is rich nourishment, supplied by the support of the people. Each section is illustrated with episodes from Party history, from the revolutionary period to the post-2012 era, and with passages from Xi Jinping and Mao Zedong.

On theory, Zhao and Teng argue that Marxism let the Party resolve the basic questions of the Chinese revolution, and that its success also lay in refusing to treat Marxism, Soviet experience or Comintern instructions as dogma. Theoretical innovation, from Mao Zedong Thought to Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, is presented as the result of adapting Marxism to Chinese conditions. On character, they present the Party as one that can face and correct its own mistakes. They argue that its founding mission sustains cohesion, and that anti-corruption since the 18th Party Congress (2012) is vital because corruption could cost the Party its legitimacy, as they say happened to the Soviet Communist Party and the Kuomintang. On the people, they hold that the masses supplied soldiers, grain and practical inventions, such as the household contract responsibility system. They add that popular supervision helps the Party escape the "historical cycle" of dynastic rise and fall.

The authors conclude that the Party's history is one of arming the mind with Marxism, strengthening itself through self-reform, and relying on the people. They call for these codes to be kept as the Party leads the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation and works toward a community with a shared future for mankind. Read the original if you want a compact example of how Chinese Party-affiliated scholarship explains the Party's longevity in the centenary year.
quoteEn: The Communist Party of China's path to success lies in having a wise mind, a firm character and rich nourishment.
quoteZh: 中国共产党的成功之道在于有智慧的头脑、坚定的品格和丰富的滋养。

glossary.explanation: A phrase stressed under Xi Jinping for the Party's efforts to discipline and renew itself, including by fighting corruption. The article treats it as a defining trait of the Party.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A central official goal of national revival, linked to the Chinese Dream and to the Party's stated mission.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's formula for China's vision of international relations and global governance.
The pattern of dynasties rising quickly and collapsing quickly. Mao Zedong discussed it in the 1940s, and Party writers present popular supervision as the way to escape it.

t: The "Ten Upholds" as the key to success running through a century of Party history
zh: “十个坚持”是贯通百年党史的成功密码
source: Ideological and Political Education Research, 2022 no. 2
paras: Xiao Guiqing takes up the ten historical lessons set out in the Resolution on the Party's major achievements and historical experience over the past century, adopted at the Sixth Plenum of the 19th Central Committee (2021). These are: upholding the Party's leadership, putting the people first, theoretical innovation, independence, the Chinese path, a worldview of openness to the world, pioneering spirit, dauntless struggle, the united front, and self-reform. Xiao argues that together these "Ten Upholds" are the code explaining why the Party succeeded in the past and how it can keep succeeding.

The article, published in Ideological and Political Education Research in 2022, has three parts. The first treats the Ten Upholds as a systematic summary of the Party's history and compares the 2021 Resolution with the earlier historical resolutions of 1945 and 1981. The second sets out why the Ten Upholds secure the Party's lasting strength. The third presents them as a guide for future struggle.

Xiao's central claim is that the Ten Upholds are not a stage-specific tally of past policies but an integrated whole. They express the Party's consistent stance, viewpoint and method, and none can be properly understood in isolation: Party leadership, for example, contains the commitments to the people and to theoretical innovation. Following Xi Jinping's four-fold formulation, Xiao says they reveal the fundamental guarantee of success (Party leadership), the source of strength (reliance on the people), the reason the Party holds the historical initiative (theory, independence, innovation), and the way it stays advanced and pure (self-reform). On the last point Xiao presents self-reform as the Party's second answer to the "historical cycle" of rise and decline, after supervision by the people.

Looking ahead, Xiao says the Ten Upholds should serve as an ideological weapon for reading a world of "changes unseen in a century", a practical guide for waging "great struggle", a yardstick for judging political right and wrong, and a guide to Party-spirit cultivation. Xiao calls on the Party to cherish, adhere to and develop them as it pursues the second centenary goal and the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. Read the original if you want a representative Chinese Party-theory reading of the 2021 historical resolution and the logic that links its ten lessons.
quoteEn: The Ten Upholds, as valuable experience the Party has drawn from long practice, are not an isolated and one-sided collection of provisions but a systematic and complete organic whole, and this experience can be grasped accurately only through their mutual connection and mutual illumination.
quoteZh: “十个坚持”作为党在长期实践中得出的宝贵经验，不是孤立片面的条文汇总，而是系统完整的有机整体，只有在相互联系、相互映照中才能实现对这一经验的准确把握。

glossary.explanation: The ten lessons of historical experience summarised in the Party's third historical resolution, adopted in November 2021. They cover leadership, the people, theory, independence, the Chinese path, global outlook, innovation, struggle, the united front and self-reform.
Resolutions in which the Central Committee gives an authoritative assessment of Party history. The three most often cited date from 1945, 1981 and 2021.
A term emphasised under Xi Jinping for the Party's capacity to correct its own errors and purify itself, presented as the means of maintaining its advanced nature.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.literal: great revival of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The official overarching goal of the Party, linked to the Chinese Dream and to the two centenary goals of 2021 and 2049.
The goal of building China into a great modern socialist country by the centenary of the People's Republic in 2049.
The pattern of dynastic rise and decline that Huang Yanpei raised with Mao Zedong in 1945. Party discourse says supervision by the people, and later self-reform, are the answers to it.

t: The philosophization of the world and the worldliness of philosophy
st: An inquiry into the conception of justice in Marx's doctoral dissertation
zh: 世界哲学化与哲学世界化
zhSub: 马克思《博士论文》中的正义观探微
paras: Since the 1970s, Anglo-American philosophers have debated whether Marx had a theory of justice and whether he supported or opposed it. Liu takes up this question by returning to Marx's first systematic theoretical work, the doctoral dissertation on the difference between the natural philosophies of Democritus and Epicurus. The article argues that the dissertation's formula that "the philosophization of the world is at the same time the worldliness of philosophy" contains the starting point of Marx's view of justice. On this reading, the young Marx treats justice as a value norm centred on real human beings.

The article has three parts. The first reconstructs the intellectual context: Marx's early Romanticism and Kant–Fichte idealism, his turn to Hegel, and his closeness to Bruno Bauer's standpoint of self-consciousness, which Liu distinguishes from Marx's own use of the concept. The second part reads Epicurus's doctrine of the atom's swerve as an account of the freedom of self-consciousness. The third part draws out the implications for justice: its subject, its legislator, the role of self-consciousness, and the rights of freedom and equality. A short conclusion places this early view in Marx's later development.

Liu's central move is to read the swerve of the atom against Democritus's rectilinear fall. Democritus, in Marx's reading, subjects atoms to blind necessity, whereas Epicurus's swerve introduces contingency and thus freedom of choice, which Liu extends to human beings as self-conscious social beings. From this Liu derives the two-sided formula. The philosophization of the world means philosophy guides and acts upon reality. The worldliness of philosophy means philosophy criticises injustice in practice and overcomes its own abstraction. Justice, Liu holds, is powerless if confined to theory and must be made real.

Liu concludes that the young Marx makes the real human being, not gods or God, the subject and legislator of justice. Self-consciousness serves as the critic of injustice, such as religious and feudal oppression, and freedom and equality are the rights of that subject. Liu contrasts this with Epicurus, whose freedom is detached from determinate existence, while Marx wants freedom to "shine in" that existence through practice. Liu also notes the view remains idealist and Romantic, and that Marx sublated it later, when he edited the Rheinische Zeitung. Read the original if you are interested in the early Marx, the philosophical roots of the Marxian justice debate, or how Chinese scholars read the doctoral dissertation.
quoteEn: Justice must be \"worldly and made real\"; only then can it be realised.
quoteZh: 正义必须“世界化—现实化”，这才能使正义得以实现。

t: The basic orientation of the new form of human civilization in the course of world history
zh: 人类文明新形态在世界历史进程中的基本定向
source: Marxist Theory Discipline Studies (Makesizhuyi lilun xueke yanjiu), 2022 no. 2
paras: Wu Hongzheng asks how the idea of a community with a shared future for mankind can move from a concept to something with a real foundation. The article's thesis is that Chinese modernization created a "new form of human civilization", and that this civilization supplies the community's "existent basis" (shicun jichu). Together they make up a world-historical sequence: the new path of Chinese modernization, the new form of human civilization, and the community with a shared future for mankind.

Writing in 2022 within Marx's theory of world history, Wu works in three steps. The first sets out what the new civilizational form is and why it is world-historical. The second places the three concepts on a "logical map" of world-historical development. The third explains why the new form of civilization can serve as the community's foundation. Wu draws on Hegel's logic of ground and existence, and cites Piketty, Streeck and Heller to support points about capitalism and political order.

Wu argues that the new civilizational form is not a spontaneous "natural-historical process". In Wu's account it arose under the uncertainty of the "great changes unseen in a century" and aims to sublate the logic of capital and the "clash of civilizations" it produces. Wu holds that Chinese modernization was carrying Marx's world-historical purpose from the start, so it did not "enter" world history only after it began to influence the world. Wu calls the contrary view the "greatest metaphysical way of thinking". Under the coexistence of two social systems, Wu contends, only a socialist-led civilization that matches the direction of world history can ground the community. This civilization works through the principles "seeking common ground while reserving differences" and win-win cooperation, and through "common values of all mankind". Wu distinguishes these values from "universal values", which Wu says impose one country's particular values. Wu also proposes "world relations of production" as an extension of historical materialism.

Wu concludes that the community with a shared future for mankind gains objective necessity from two sources. It is the basic orientation of twenty-first-century Marxist world-history theory, and Chinese modernization and the new civilizational form provide its existent basis. Wu compares this to the way Marx's "two inevitables" established the necessity of communism. Wu also treats the new civilizational form as a transitional stage that will itself eventually be sublated. Read the original if you want to see how a Chinese Marxist philosopher grounds the official concepts of Chinese modernization and the community with a shared future in Hegelian and Marxian world-history theory.
quoteEn: Chinese modernization was placed under the purpose of world history from the outset, so it was world history itself from the beginning, rather than something that later \"entered\" world history as it developed.
quoteZh: 中国式现代化在原初就被置于世界历史目的之下，因而从开端处即是世界历史本身，而不是随着它的发展而后天“走进”世界历史的。

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: A foreign-policy and theoretical concept associated with Xi Jinping since about 2012–2013. It calls for cooperative international relations and shared global development.

The official description of China's own path to modernization, set out by the Party especially since the 2021 centenary and the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is presented as distinct from Western modernization.
A phrase used in Party documents since 2021 for the civilizational achievement said to result from Chinese modernization. It is contrasted with civilizational forms dominated by capital.
Xi Jinping's formulation of peace, development, equity, justice, democracy and freedom as values shared by all. Official discourse contrasts it with "universal values" promoted by the West.

glossary.en: seeking common ground while reserving differences
glossary.explanation: A long-standing diplomatic principle in Chinese foreign policy. It stresses cooperation on shared interests while tolerating differences.

keywords: community with a shared future for mankind

t: Methodological features of Engels's critique of erroneous currents of thought
zh: 恩格斯批判错误思潮的方法论特征
source: Ideological and Political Education Research (思想教育研究), 2021 no. 12
paras: Jin Siyuan asks what methodological features characterise Engels's polemics against erroneous currents of thought, and argues that they show a high degree of methodological self-awareness. The article takes three cases: "true socialism", "socialism of the lectern" (Kathedersozialismus) and the opportunism of the "Young Ones" (Jungen). Jin contends that the critique is marked by scientific rigour, a strongly critical stance and a comprehensive perspective, and that revisiting it has theoretical and practical value for safeguarding mainstream ideological security and improving the governance of social trends of thought.

The article is organised in three parts, one for each feature, and each part works through the three cases. It draws on Engels's writings from 1845 to 1848 on true socialism (including the Communist Manifesto and The German Ideology, co-written with Marx), his 1880s–90s defence of Marx against the charge of plagiarising Rodbertus, and his 1890 reply to Paul Ernst and letters to Bloch, Schmidt, Lafargue and Sombart.

On scientific rigour, Jin shows Engels collecting and analysing sources on a large scale. In the Rodbertus affair he reportedly consulted at least six texts and established that Marx learned of Rodbertus only around 1859, indirectly through Lassalle, when his critique of political economy was already essentially complete. Jin also credits Engels with combining tight logic with vivid, popular language. On critical stance, Engels is said to expose the reactionary class position of true socialism, whose appeal to "love" replaced revolution, and the apologetic reformism of the lectern socialists, who served Bismarck's state socialism. He is also said to refute the Young Ones' economic determinism and adventurism, noting that treating the materialist method as a ready-made formula turns it into its opposite. On comprehensiveness, Engels combines a focus on key arguments with a view of the whole, and uses Ricardian, comparative and historical angles against Rodbertus. He pairs demolition with construction: after criticising the Young Ones he sets out the proper approach to Marxism, namely studying the original works, and treating Marx's worldview as a method rather than a dogma.

Jin concludes that the scientific, critical and comprehensive features of Engels's polemics, together with the methodological self-awareness they reflect, offer practical guidance for studying and researching Marxism today. Read the original if you are interested in Engels's polemical method, in how Chinese scholarship draws on it for contemporary ideological work, or in a compact survey of his critiques of true socialism, lectern socialism and the Young Ones.
quoteEn: Engels stressed that treating the materialist method \"as a ready-made formula\" is a misreading and misuse of that method.
quoteZh: 恩格斯强调将唯物主义方法“当作现成的公式”是对唯物主义方法的误读与误用

glossary.explanation: A 1840s German current, associated with Karl Grün, Moses Hess and others, that presented socialism through abstract philosophy and appeals to humanity and love. Marx and Engels criticised it as petty-bourgeois and politically reactionary.
The label for German professors such as Schmoller and Wagner who advocated state-led social reform to reconcile classes. Engels and others used the term critically (Kathedersozialismus).

A group of young writers and students in the German Social Democratic Party around 1890 who opposed parliamentary tactics and claimed to speak for revolutionary Marxism. Engels attacked their dogmatic use of materialism.

t: Zhou Enlai's 1941 forecast of the Pacific War and his response to it
zh: 1941年周恩来对太平洋战争爆发的预判与应对
paras: Li Tian asks how Zhou Enlai, then head of the Southern Bureau of the CCP Central Committee in Chongqing, read the international situation in 1941 and how he acted on it. The article argues that Zhou weighed the shifting balance between the fascist and anti-fascist camps and correctly predicted the outbreak of the Pacific War. It also argues that his measures after December 1941 helped China's resistance.

Drawing on documents, telegrams and Zhou's commentaries in Xinhua Daily, the article proceeds in four parts. The first follows Zhou's analysis of Japanese–American diplomacy. The second covers his exposure of the 'Eastern Munich plot'. The third examines his assessment of Japanese cabinet changes. The fourth treats the Party's and Zhou's response once the war began, including the evacuation of people from Hong Kong.

In Li's account, Zhou saw the Japan–US talks as a bargaining effort that could sacrifice China and weaken the Kuomintang's will to resist. His June 1941 essays distinguished the 'mainstream' of the war from an 'undercurrent' of compromise, and described Japan's 'two-sided policy' of military pressure and diplomacy. Zhou urged independent resistance, while using contradictions among the imperialist powers and not waiting passively for a clash in the Pacific. After the Tojo cabinet took office in October, he wrote that Japan would pursue a 'Greater East Asia Co-Prosperity Sphere' by force whichever direction it moved first. He also warned Hong Kong-based comrades that war with the United States was possible. On 14 December he described the Pacific War as protracted, expected early setbacks, and put naval power first.

Li concludes that Zhou's analysis and decisions rested on China's national resistance and the global anti-fascist struggle. The article says his commentaries conveyed the Party's position to the public in Kuomintang-ruled areas and gave a strategic basis for the Central Committee's 1942 central task of building strength and consolidating the Party, government, army and people. For Li, the episode confirms that the Party grasps historical trends and was the mainstay of the War of Resistance. Read the original if you want a documented account of Zhou Enlai's wartime assessments of Japan, the United States and the Pacific War, as the CCP presents them today.
quoteEn: Zhou Enlai's forecast was intended to call on the world anti-fascist camp to be vigilant against the reckless adventure that Japanese militarists were about to carry out.
quoteZh: 周恩来的预判意在呼吁世界反法西斯阵营应当警惕日本军国主义分子即将实施的冒险行动。

glossary.explanation: A regional organ of the CCP Central Committee, based in Chongqing during the War of Resistance, responsible for Party work in Kuomintang-ruled areas in the south. Zhou Enlai led it.
The CCP's term for feared deals among Japan, Britain, the United States and the Kuomintang that would sacrifice China, by analogy with the 1938 Munich Agreement.
The CCP's newspaper in Kuomintang-held Chongqing during the war, through which Zhou Enlai published commentaries.

t: The logic behind posing basic theories of the history of the development of Marxism
zh: 马克思主义发展史基础理论提出的逻辑
source: Contemporary World and Socialism (Dangdai shijie yu shehuizhuyi), 2020 no. 5
