Zhu holds that Marx affirmed the justice of exchange under capitalism while sharply criticising its production and distribution. Justice is judged by whether a mode of production fits its historical stage, citing Marx's remark that a transaction is just if it corresponds to the mode of production. Zhu also stresses that Marx sought a real path to a just order, rather than an ideal blueprint. That path runs through public ownership, distribution according to labour, and a higher stage in which free time replaces labour time as the measure of wealth.

Zhu concludes that this thought offers guidance for China's development, and calls for applying historical materialism to current economic relations. The article points to unequal urban–rural public services and collusion between power and capital as problems. It endorses the shared development philosophy and common prosperity, and calls for legal and credit systems, moral self-discipline among economic actors, attention to vulnerable groups, and tax and social security reform to narrow the wealth gap. Zhu presents the aim as social fairness and justice in general, beyond economic justice alone. Read the original if you want a Chinese academic reading of Capital on justice and its application to China's market economy.
quoteEn: Marx never sought to construct an ideal state of justice, but devoted himself to finding the real path to achieving that goal of justice.
quoteZh: 马克思始终并未寻求构建一种正义的理想状态, 而是致力于寻找出实现这种正义目标的现实路径。

glossary.explanation: A Chinese policy goal of prosperity shared by all, in contrast to polarisation of wealth. It has long been a socialist aim and has been given new prominence in recent official discourse.
One of the five development concepts put forward by the Party leadership in 2015. It holds that the fruits of development should be shared by all the people.
The official name for China's economic system, adopted in the early 1990s. It combines market allocation with public ownership and state guidance.
The principle, drawn from Marx's Critique of the Gotha Programme, that in the first stage of communism individuals receive goods in proportion to the labour they contribute.

t: Re-understanding Mao Zedong's dialectics
zh: 毛泽东辩证法的再认识
source: Chinese Social Sciences Today (中国社会科学报), 29 July 2021
paras: Wang Nanshi argues that the originality of Mao Zedong's dialectics has long been overlooked. In Wang's account, the cause lies in two dominant readings of Marxist dialectics, the French-materialist and the Hegelian, which cannot accommodate Mao's distinctive concepts and so trim them to fit. The article's thesis is that Mao's dialectics is a dialectics of practical wisdom, a major innovation in Marxism and a resource for building a Chinese-style system of Marxist dialectics.

The article, a short newspaper piece, has three parts. The first defines in what sense Mao's dialectics is one of practical wisdom, drawing on Aristotle's distinction between theoretical and practical activity and on Mao's essay On Contradiction. The second asks why such a dialectics emerged within a Marxism of Western origin, and turns to Chinese modes of thinking. The third examines Marx's Capital and the contribution Mao's dialectics makes to Marxist philosophy.

Wang reasons that theory deals with eternal objects and therefore uses fixed categories, while practice deals with changeable objects. On Contradiction presupposes a changeable, heterogeneous world, as shown by the distinctions between principal and secondary contradictions, between principal and secondary aspects, and by the theory of uneven development of contradiction. Drawing on Zhang Dongsun, Wang contrasts Western thought, which probes 'behind' things for a single origin, with Chinese thought, which attends to relations among phenomena and to becoming. Mao's categories, Wang holds, grow from the latter. Capital, by contrast, is read as a materialistically reworked Hegelian dialectics of theoretical wisdom, which builds abstract models and ascends slowly to the concrete. Practice cannot wait for that, so practical-wisdom dialectics supplements it by grasping the principal contradiction directly.

Wang concludes that Marxism now contains two dialectics, one for scientific theory and one for forming action plans. They are complementary and mutually determining: theory sets limits on practical wisdom, while practical wisdom supplies the ground for further abstraction. Because practical wisdom has the foundational place and rests on Chinese thinking, Wang holds that a system combining both would be a Chinese-style Marxist dialectics. Read the original if you want a compact philosophical argument for treating Mao's dialectics as a distinct, culturally rooted contribution to Marxism.
quoteEn: Mao Zedong's dialectics is a dialectics that serves as practical wisdom.
quoteZh: 毛泽东的辩证法乃是一种作为实践智慧的辩证法

t: Real-world challenges in building a community with a shared future for mankind and strategies for meeting them
zh: 构建人类命运共同体面临的现实挑战和应对策略
paras: Writing in 2021, Ren Jie asks what obstacles stand in the way of building a community with a shared future for mankind, a concept presented as part of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era. Ren acknowledges the concept's growing international recognition but argues that its realisation is a long and arduous process facing three real-world challenges. The article also proposes four strategies for dealing with them.

The article is organised in four parts. Three sections take up the challenges in turn: differences in strategic thinking and cultural values, gaps in comprehensive national strength, and conflicts over core national interests. A final section sets out responses. Ren draws on Xi Jinping's speeches, Marx on interests, Hedley Bull's idea of international society, UN Secretary-General António Guterres's 2021 debt proposals, and examples from US foreign policy and the Belt and Road Initiative.

On the first challenge, Ren contends that states understand freedom and democracy differently, and that US zero-sum and binary thinking, which Ren says is rooted in a sense of mission, leads Washington to misread China's intentions. Ren cites US think-tank reports and the Biden-era Build Back Better World initiative as attempts to contain or replace the Belt and Road Initiative. On the second, Ren notes that developing countries' collective economic weight is rising, yet argues that China's per capita income, military power and cultural influence still lag behind those of the United States, so claims of a 'Chinese century' are unrealistic and unequal strength undermines extensive consultation, joint contribution and shared benefits. On the third, Ren holds that core interests differ across regions, but that common human interests make a higher-level union of nation-states possible.

Ren proposes four responses: telling the story of the community well, including through accurate translation of the term and stronger discourse power; delivering on commitments to developing countries' development rights and easing their debt burdens; upholding multilateralism and regional cooperation, with RCEP as an example; and promoting a new international political and economic order, with greater solidarity among developing countries. Ren concludes that when humanity's survival is at stake, national interests must yield to common human interests. Read the original if you want a Chinese scholarly account of how the concept is defended against perceived US opposition and of what practical communication and diplomatic measures are recommended.
quoteEn: A community with a shared future for mankind is not a simple aggregation of nation-states, but a union of nation-states at a higher level.
quoteZh: 人类命运共同体不是各民族国家的简单集合,而是各民族国家在更高水平上的联合。

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.literal: community of common destiny of humankind
glossary.explanation: A foreign-policy and global-governance concept put forward by Xi Jinping from 2012–13. The article notes that earlier English renderings such as 'community of common destiny' were replaced by the current official one.
An international infrastructure and economic cooperation initiative launched by China in 2013. The article treats it as a key practical platform for the community with a shared future.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Communist Party of China's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–18.

glossary.pinyin: gòng shāng gòng jiàn gòng xiǎng
glossary.en: extensive consultation, joint contribution and shared benefits
glossary.literal: jointly discuss, jointly build, jointly share
glossary.explanation: An official principle for global governance and Belt and Road cooperation, stressing equal participation by all countries.

keywords: community with a shared future for mankind

t: A century of Chinese Marxist political economy: retrospect and prospect
zh: 中国马克思主义政治经济学百年回顾与展望
source: China Social Sciences Today (Zhongguo shehui kexue bao), 2 September 2021
paras: Marking the centenary of the Communist Party of China in 2021, Tian Pengying reviews how the Party has continuously explored and developed Marxist political economy. The author argues that this history explains how the Party raised its capacity to lead economic development and produced the "two miracles" of rapid growth and long-term social stability. It also, in Tian's view, indicates how new economic achievements can be created and how a 21st-century Marxist political economy can be opened up.

The short newspaper essay has three parts. The first traces the adaptation of Marxist political economy to Chinese conditions from the New Democratic revolution through the Mao Zedong era to reform and opening up. The second sets out seven contributions of the political economy of socialism with Chinese characteristics since the 18th Party Congress (2012). The third looks ahead to the field's prospects.

Tian presents the process as a sequence of theoretical innovations tied to practice. Mao's New Democratic economic programme, his repeated study of Capital and his theory of the basic contradictions of socialist society are followed by Deng Xiaoping's theory of the socialist market economy and of the primary stage of socialism. For the Xi Jinping era, the seven contributions include the Party's overall leadership of economic work, the people-centred development philosophy, the Two Unwaverings, adapting to the "new normal", letting the market play the decisive role in resource allocation, supply-side structural reform, and the new development stage, philosophy and pattern. Tian describes these as turning the regular patterns of China's practice into a systematic theory.

Looking forward, Tian calls for three tasks: summing up great practical experience so that theory and economic practice interact well; grasping major questions of the era, including Chinese modernization and a new form of human civilisation; and engaging with the world governance system amid what the author calls changes unseen in a century. Tian holds that Chinese Marxist political economy offers a "Chinese approach" for other countries' high-quality development and can help guide reform of global governance. Read the original if you want a compact example of how a Party-school-style survey periodises the Sinification of Marxist political economy and lists its official contributions.
quoteEn: To some extent, the hundred-year history of the Communist Party of China's economic development is a history of advancing the innovative development of Marxist political economy.
quoteZh: 一部中国共产党百年经济发展史，在某种程度上是一部推进马克思主义政治经济学创新发展的历史。

glossary.explanation: A policy formula of unwaveringly consolidating and developing the public sector and unwaveringly encouraging, supporting and guiding the non-public sector.
An official description, used from around 2014, of China's economy moving from high-speed to medium-high-speed growth with a changed structure and growth model.
The official term for China's own path to modernization, stressed by the Party leadership as distinct from Western models.
A Party thesis, developed in the 1980s, that China is in a long, underdeveloped initial phase of socialism, which justifies market-oriented reforms.
The policy begun in 1978 under Deng Xiaoping of economic reform at home and opening to the outside world.

t: The Communist Party of China has no special interests of its own: the nature of a Marxist party
zh: 中国共产党没有自己特殊利益 这是马克思主义政党的性质决定的
paras: This newspaper commentary, published in Changjiang Daily in August 2021, takes up Xi Jinping's statement in his speech at the centenary of the Party's founding that the Communist Party of China has no special interests of its own and never represents any interest group, power group or privileged stratum. Xin argues that this claim follows from the nature of a Marxist party and enriches Marxist party theory. In Xin's reading it also sums up the Party's hundred-year history and the rise and fall of parties elsewhere.

The piece is organised around the three negations in Xi's formulation. It first treats interest groups, then power groups, then privileged strata. Xin relies mainly on Xi's speeches since the 18th Party Congress (2012), on the Party Constitution, and on a 2019 Central Committee document on strengthening the Party's political development.

Xin contends that a Marxist party has one interest, that of the people. If it acquired special interests, Xin says, it would breed feudal-style dependence and small cliques, and interest groups inside the Party could change its proletarian character. Xin claims that many parties, especially in Western countries and notably in the United States, serve power groups. On privilege, Xin cites Xi's view that the Soviet Communist Party collapsed partly because it became a privileged bureaucratic group cut off from the people.

Xin calls for open opposition to privileged thinking, conduct and practices, citing Xi's 2013 and 2018 speeches to the Central Commission for Discipline Inspection. Xin also calls for implementing the Party's 2016 norms on intra-Party political life, which require tighter supervision of leaders and rule out unchecked power and unsupervised "special" members. Read the original if you want a short, official-line account of how Party leaders justify the claim that the Party has no interests of its own and frame the Soviet collapse as a warning.
quoteEn: A Marxist party represents the interests of the broadest masses of the people; the Party has only one interest, and that is the interest of the people.
quoteZh: 马克思主义政党代表的是最广大人民群众的利益，党的利益只有一个，那就是人民的利益。

glossary.explanation: A group pursuing its own sectional advantage. Party leaders use the term, including for groups inside the Party, to describe a threat to the Party's nature and political integrity.
A social layer enjoying special rights or advantages through position or power. In Party discourse it is linked to the warning drawn from the fall of the Soviet Communist Party.

glossary.zh: 关于新形势下党内政治生活的若干准则
glossary.pinyin: guānyú xīn xíngshì xià dǎngnèi zhèngzhì shēnghuó de ruògān zhǔnzé
glossary.literal: Several Norms on Intra-Party Political Life under the New Situation
glossary.explanation: A Party document adopted at the Sixth Plenum of the 18th Central Committee in 2016. It sets rules on supervision, discipline and leaders' conduct.

t: On the developmental position of the new era
zh: 论新时代的发展方位
paras: Wei Zhiqi takes up a question he says the literature has neglected: where the "new era" declared at the 19th Party Congress (2017) stands in terms of development, as distinct from its historical position. Most existing studies, Wei argues, treat the two as the same and read the new era only through the history of socialism with Chinese characteristics. His thesis is that the new era is a new stage within the primary stage of socialism and sits in a new developmental position of "after having developed".

The article has three parts. The first argues that the new era remains inside the primary stage of socialism while forming a new stage of it. The second divides the primary stage into two developmental positions, one of "underdevelopment" and one of "after development", and examines what changes and what stays constant in the productive forces and relations of production. The third sets out three features of the new position. Wei draws on Deng Xiaoping, the 13th and 15th Party Congresses, the Fourth and Fifth Plenums of the 19th Central Committee, and statistics on GDP, income, urbanisation and the Engel coefficient.

Wei contends that the primary stage proceeds from quantitative accumulation to "partial qualitative change" and eventually to "comprehensive qualitative change". Four decades of growth have produced a partial qualitative change, a leap in the indicators of the stage's "five" and "nine" characteristics. However, per capita output, regional and urban–rural imbalances, industrial quality and the maturity of institutions show, in Wei's account, that underdevelopment has not fundamentally changed. Its form has shifted from underdeveloped productive forces to unbalanced and inadequate development. The new era is therefore the "second half" of the primary stage, one that partially overcomes, sublates and transcends underdevelopment.

Wei identifies three features of the "after developed" position. The essence of socialism now stresses eliminating poverty and moving toward common prosperity. The principal contradiction has become one between people's growing need for a better life and unbalanced, inadequate development. The central mission has moved from becoming prosperous to becoming strong, through the two-step path to a modern socialist country by around 2050. Wei concludes that becoming strong is the main mission and defining mark of the new position. Read the original if you want a Party-theory account of how the "primary stage of socialism" is periodised into stages and how this underpins the new era's tasks.
quoteEn: Becoming strong is the main mission and fundamental hallmark of the new developmental position.
quoteZh: 强起来是新发展方位的主要使命和根本表征。

glossary.explanation: A Party thesis, developed in the 1980s, that China is in a long, historically necessary early phase of socialism marked by underdeveloped productive forces. It is the official basis for China's basic national conditions.

The 19th Party Congress (2017) declared that socialism with Chinese characteristics had entered a new era, associated with a changed principal contradiction and the goal of building a strong modern socialist country.
The author's term for where the country stands in its developmental stage, contrasted with its "historical position" (历史方位) within the course of socialism with Chinese characteristics.
The goal of prosperity shared by all the people, which Deng Xiaoping linked to the essence of socialism and which Xi Jinping has placed at the centre of current policy.
The Party's official assessment of the main contradiction in society. In 2017 it was redefined as one between the people's growing need for a better life and unbalanced, inadequate development.

t: Always uphold and raise high the banner of historical materialism
zh: 始终坚持和高扬唯物史观理论旗帜
source: China Social Sciences Today (Zhongguo shehui kexue bao), 1 July 2021
paras: Published in China Social Sciences Today on 1 July 2021, the centenary of the Communist Party of China, this commentary asks what theoretical foundation underlies the Party's century of experience. Zhang argues that historical materialism is the Party's "core skill" (kanjia benshi), and that a party's choice between historical materialism, idealist conceptions of history or others is a dividing line for whether its view of history and method is scientific. The Party must therefore keep this banner raised.

The piece opens with the premise that the path a nation takes depends on the theoretical banner its parties raise. It then reviews the Party's own summaries of experience, namely Mao Zedong's "three magic weapons" and Deng Xiaoping's insistence on combining universal Marxist truth with China's concrete conditions. In its second half it sets out three dimensions in which, according to Zhang, historical materialism has guided revolution, construction and reform and opening up.

Zhang's central move is to read the Party's famous experiences as the fruit of applying historical materialism successfully. In this reading, the line of "emancipating the mind and seeking truth from facts" embodies dialectical and historical materialism and has let the Party avoid both wholesale Westernization and ossified closure. The three dimensions are as follows. First, the Party located its historical position and stage, which produced successive general lines from New Democratic Revolution to socialism with Chinese characteristics in the new era. Second, it applied the law that relations of production must suit productive forces and the superstructure the economic base, analysing the nature of Chinese society and the principal contradiction, and describing reform as also emancipating the productive forces. Third, it treated the people as the fundamental social subject, which Zhang links to the mass line, the aim of serving the people wholeheartedly and a people-centred approach to development.

Zhang adds that the Party has also used historical materialism on class struggle, social contradictions, ideology, cultural inheritance and cultural-ethical progress. The author calls on Communists to combine the theory and method with the development of the times, world trends and the people's wisdom, so that it stays a "hard skill" in constant renewal. Doing so, Zhang says, will help the Party grasp the laws and general trend of history and keep the historical initiative. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party-affiliated scholars framed historical materialism as the theoretical core of the Party's centenary narrative.
quoteEn: Therefore, from the standpoint of theoretical consciousness and theoretical confidence, historical materialism is the Communist Party of China's "core skill".
quoteZh: 因此，从理论自觉和理论自信的高度而言，唯物史观是中国共产党的“看家本事”。

glossary.explanation: A colloquial phrase for one's fundamental, signature competence. Zhang uses it to describe historical materialism as the Party's basic strength.
Mao Zedong's formulation of the united front, armed struggle and Party building as the key factors in the Party's revolutionary success.

glossary.en: emancipating the mind and seeking truth from facts
glossary.explanation: A slogan of the Party's ideological line, strongly associated with the reform era under Deng Xiaoping, stressing that policy should start from actual conditions.
The Party's method of work of drawing ideas from the masses and returning them as policy, summed up as "from the masses, to the masses".
The policy of domestic economic reform and opening to the outside world launched in 1978.

t: The glorious course of the century-old Party in advancing the adaptation of Marxism to the Chinese context
zh: 百年大党推进马克思主义中国化的光辉历程
paras: Marking the centenary of the Communist Party of China in 2021, Wang Huxue and He Xiaoxiao take up Xi Jinping's statement that the Party's history is one of continuously advancing the adaptation of Marxism to the Chinese context and of theoretical innovation. The authors argue that every theoretical creation of the Party has depended on the guidance of Marxist theory and on the leadership of successive central collectives. They present the Party's hundred years as an unbroken process of adaptation, with each stage producing a new theoretical form.

The article follows four periods in order: the New Democratic Revolution, socialist revolution and construction, reform and opening up with socialist modernization, and the new era of socialism with Chinese characteristics. For each period it identifies the leading figures, the key meetings and the theoretical results. These run from Mao Zedong Thought through Deng Xiaoping Theory, the Three Represents and the Scientific Outlook on Development to Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era. A short conclusion draws the strands together.

The authors' central move is to read each stage as an answer to a defining question. Early dogmatism, which they link to uncritical reliance on Soviet experience and Comintern resolutions, brought the failure of the Fifth Encirclement Campaign. They credit Mao with the rural-base strategy and with the 1938 formulation of the adaptation of Marxism to the Chinese context, and they describe the 1945 Seventh Congress as the first historic leap. After 1978, they say, Deng's reforms answered what socialism is, Jiang Zemin's Three Represents answered what kind of Party to build, and Hu Jintao's Scientific Outlook on Development answered what kind of development to pursue. For the period after the 18th Party Congress (2012) they list the people-centred approach, the new development philosophy and the "two mountains" ecological idea as new Marxist advances.

The authors conclude that the Party's achievements stem from taking Marxism as its guide while innovating in theory through revolution, construction and reform. They add Xi's 2021 call to combine the best of traditional Chinese culture with the Marxist stance, viewpoint and method. In their view, Marxism adapted to China forms a systematic new theoretical form that serves as a guide to action for the whole Party and people. Read the original if you want a concise, officially aligned periodisation of the Party's theoretical achievements, as presented in the centenary year.
quoteEn: The Party's hundred-year struggle is also a history of Marxism in action, continually advancing the adaptation of Marxism to the Chinese context.
quoteZh: 中国共产党的百年奋斗史也是一部行动着的、不断推动马克思主义中国化的历史。

glossary.en: adaptation of Marxism to the Chinese context
glossary.explanation: The Party's term for applying Marxism to China's concrete conditions and producing new theory from that practice. It was first put forward in 1938 and is now usually paired with 'the needs of our times'.
Mao Zedong's term for the stage of the Chinese revolution, from about 1919 to 1949, led by the proletariat and aimed at ending imperialist and feudal domination before the move to socialism.

Theory associated with Jiang Zemin, introduced around 2000. It holds that the Party represents the development of advanced productive forces, the orientation of advanced culture and the fundamental interests of the overwhelming majority of the people.
Guiding concept associated with Hu Jintao, stressing people-centred, comprehensive, coordinated and sustainable development.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology since the 19th Party Congress (2017), written into the Party and state constitutions.
Official framework, announced in 2015, that centres on innovative, coordinated, green, open and shared development.

keywords: adaptation of Marxism to the Chinese context

t: On the logical path of Marx's critique of commodity fetishism
zh: 论马克思商品拜物教批判的逻辑理路
paras: Sun Xiguo and Mao Fei take up a gap in existing readings of Marx's theory of commodity fetishism. Some scholars reduce it to the 'reification of social relations', but in the authors' view this does not explain why relations between people must appear inverted as relations between things. They argue that the critique operates on two dimensions: a critique of the economic base from which fetishism arises, and a critique of fetishism as an ideological superstructure.

The article, published in Theoretical Journal in 2021, reconstructs the critique as three logical links. It then draws out three implications: against the view that fetishism is merely subjective misrecognition, against the claim that it is obsolete, and for a dialectical view of the commodity. The discussion draws on Capital, Lenin, Lukács, Rubin, Baudrillard, Bailey, Ricardo and Japanese and Chinese commentators.

The first link analyses commodity-producing labour. The authors distinguish household labour (private labour organised privately), enterprise-combined labour (private labour awaiting conversion into social labour) and future socially associated labour (directly social). Because labour in the middle form is private yet social, it must be mediated by value; the authors show this by rejecting the labour-money schemes of Owen and Darimon. The second link follows the movement of the value form, from simple to expanded to general form, through which relations between people come to appear as relations between commodities, producing the illusion of reification. The third link is the belief that commodities are all-powerful, found in Ricardo's classical economics and Bailey's vulgar economics. In the authors' account, Marx gives little space to this ideological layer because his real target is the relations of production behind it.

Sun and Mao conclude that fetishism rests on objective relations of production, so it will not become obsolete while commodity production relations exist. They hold that Baudrillard's 'sign fetishism' stays at the surface of capitalism. They call for a dialectical view of the commodity: recognise that it arose by historical necessity and promotes the productive forces, and also that it is historically transient. Using commodities to develop production would, they say, eventually dissolve commodities and fetishism from within. Read the original if you want a systematic, Chinese-language reconstruction of the value-form argument and a defence of the economic-base reading of fetishism against Baudrillard and 'subjective misrecognition' interpretations.
quoteEn: Marx's critique of commodity fetishism has two dimensions: a critique of the economic base on which commodity fetishism arises, and a critique of commodity fetishism as an ideological superstructure.
quoteZh: 马克思的商品拜物教批判具有两重维度：一是对商品拜物教赖以产生的经济基础的批判；二是对商品拜物教作为观念上层建筑的批判。

glossary.explanation: Marx's concept, set out in Capital, that social relations between producers appear as properties of and relations between things. The article treats it as both an objective economic structure and an ideology.
The way value presents itself, analysed by Marx in Capital through simple, expanded and general forms. The article stresses that it is value itself as form, not an external shell.
The process by which relations between people appear as relations between things. Here it is used in this Lukácsian sense.
Baudrillard's idea that in consumer society the object of worship is the sign value of goods rather than the goods themselves. The authors present it as a rival to Marx's theory.

t: Ultimately, it is because Marxism works
zh: 归根到底是因为马克思主义行
paras: Published in Qianxian (Frontline) in 2021, the year of the Communist Party's centenary, this commentary expands on a formula in Xi Jinping's speech marking the centenary. The formula holds that the Party's success and the merits of socialism with Chinese characteristics are, "ultimately", due to the fact that Marxism works. Wang Chuanli argues that 170-plus years of history and more than four decades of reform and opening up bear this out.

The article has three parts. The first surveys the world history of Marxism from the 1840s: its contest with rival socialist currents, and its adoption in Russia and China. The second considers the Party's century of achievements and credits them to Marxist theory, ideals, method and strategy. The third deals with socialism with Chinese characteristics: its theoretical foundations, the shocks of the early 1990s and the Covid-19 pandemic, and the challenges still ahead.

Wang argues that Marxism proved itself against Proudhonism, Dühringism and Lassalleanism, and that Russia and China each reached it only after long searches through other doctrines. In the author's account, the Party's strength rests on rational conviction in Marxist science and on Marxism as a worldview and method. As evidence, the author cites Mao Zedong's foresight in On Protracted War and the Party's united front, mass line and flexible strategy. The author also traces specific policies to Marxist sources. Marx's Critique of the Gotha Programme is said to underlie the theory of the primary stage of socialism, and the Marxist view of the people as makers of history is said to underlie the commitment to common prosperity. Wang reads the Soviet and East European collapse and the pandemic as tests. The author contrasts Deng Xiaoping's confidence in Marxism after 1991 with what is described as division and failure in Western countries, set against China's pandemic response and its 2020 economic growth.

Wang concludes that history has shown, and will go on showing, that the strength of socialism with Chinese characteristics ultimately rests on Marxism. The author cautions that China still lags well behind developed countries and that national rejuvenation will demand hard struggle. Read the original if you want an example of how Party-affiliated scholars in 2021 framed the case for Marxism's efficacy around the centenary.
quoteEn: The miracles the Chinese Communist Party has created over its 100 years are due to the fact that Marxism is a scientific theory.
quoteZh: 中国共产党100年来创造了无数人间奇迹，就是因为马克思主义是科学的理论。

glossary.explanation: The Party's official judgement that China, though socialist, is still at an early and long stage of development. It was formalised in the 1980s and underpins reform-era policy.
The official name for the Party's path, theory and system since reform and opening up began in the late 1970s.
A goal of shared wealth for all, which the Party presents as a defining feature of socialism. It was given renewed emphasis in the early 2020s.
The policy of economic reform and engagement with the outside world launched in 1978 under Deng Xiaoping.

t: A historical examination of the early spread of Marxism in Shanghai and its present-day implications
zh: 马克思主义在上海早期传播的历史考察及现实启示
source: Ideological and Theoretical Education (思想理论教育), 2021 no. 7
paras: Why did Shanghai become one of the main centres where Marxism first spread in China? Sun Shan argues that the early dissemination of Marxism there supplied advanced Chinese intellectuals with an ideological weapon for national salvation, helped bring about the founding of the Chinese Communist Party in Shanghai, and holds an important place in the course of adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times. The article, published in 2021, aims to enrich the history of Marxist dissemination and of the Party's founding.

The article has three parts. The first analyses the conditions that made Shanghai a hub: its economic development and tradition of political struggle, its divided jurisdictions and migrant culture, and the concentration of intellectuals and workers. The second examines three channels of dissemination: newspapers and journals, classic books, and organised practical activity through schools, trade unions and commemorations. The third draws lessons for the present.

Sun's core argument is that the spread of Marxism in Shanghai resulted from the combined effect of several factors rather than chance. In the author's account, the concession areas offered political 'gaps' and publishing space, while migration produced an open 'Shanghai-style culture'. Sun notes that the city had about 500,000 workers around 1919 and that many students left for study abroad from its port. Dissemination, the article says, moved from the 'clustered' effect of periodicals such as New Youth, Labour World and The Communist, through the 'systematic' publication of classics by firms such as the Commercial Press, to the 'organised' work of workers' schools, unions and commemorations.

Sun draws three lessons for the present. First, Marxism must hold to its principles and engage openly with non-Marxist currents, as it did against pragmatism, reformism and anarchism; the author names liberalism and historical nihilism as present-day counterparts. Second, theory must meet social needs and be supported by practice. Third, discourse must be built and popularised, with theory expressed in everyday language for different groups. Read the original if you want a detailed account of Shanghai's material, social and organisational conditions in early Marxist dissemination, and of how a Chinese scholar draws contemporary ideological lessons from it.
quoteEn: In sum, the founding of various schools created a platform for the 'organised' dissemination of Marxism, made that dissemination more systematic, and considerably raised workers' political consciousness and theoretical literacy.
quoteZh: 综上，各式学校的创办为马克思主义“组织化”传播创建了平台，使马克思主义传播更为系统，较好地提升了工人的思想觉悟和理论素养；

glossary.zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化
glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
glossary.explanation: The official formula for applying Marxism to Chinese conditions and updating it for each era. The 'times' element was added in recent Party documents.
A term for the mixed, cosmopolitan culture that developed in Shanghai through contact between Chinese and foreign influences. The article presents it as open and inclusive.
In Chinese official usage, a label for views seen as denying or distorting the Party's history and revolutionary tradition.

t: The critical dimensions of the young Marx's concept of sensuous consciousness
zh: 青年马克思感性意识概念的批判向度
source: China Social Sciences Today (Zhongguo shehui kexue bao), 24 June 2021
paras: Liu Jianjiang examines the concept of sensuous consciousness (感性意识) that the young Marx developed in the Economic and Philosophic Manuscripts of 1844. The article, a short piece from a Chinese newspaper, argues that the concept carries a double critique and reveals the original, material ground of consciousness.

Liu places the concept within Marx's notion of objective activity, which Marx formed by critically absorbing Feuerbach's principle of sensuous objectivity and Hegel's principle of rational activity. The text is organised around two targets: "pure consciousness" in the tradition of rationalist metaphysics, and Feuerbach's "abstract species-consciousness".

On the first target, Liu reads Marx as holding that pure consciousness has knowledge as its only act and no genuine object outside itself, so that its objects are mere semblance. Consciousness, in Marx's account, is never pure but is "conscious being", rooted in the sensuous life-process of real people. Liu adds that Marx's critique of political economy applies the same logic: categories such as wages, capital and money construct an "economic fact" that hides the real sensuous conflict of interest between capitalists and workers. On the second target, Liu argues that Marx accepts Feuerbach's sensuous grounding of species-consciousness but rejects its abstraction. For Marx the species is not a natural, silent universality but "the sum of all social relations", produced through objective activity.

Liu concludes that sensuous consciousness, as Marx understands it, is pre-conceptual and tied to the language of real life and to human social interaction. It is the consciousness of social being and a confirmation of people's actual social life. Read the original if you want a concise exegesis of how the 1844 Manuscripts link consciousness, sensuousness and social relations against both Hegelian and Feuerbachian positions.
quoteEn: Consciousness is never pure; from the outset it is interwoven with sensuous matter and is \"conscious being\".
quoteZh: 意识从来都不是纯粹的，它从一开始就与感性的物质交织在一起，是一种“被意识到了的存在”。

t: The dialectical moment in Marx's conception of matter
zh: 马克思物质观的辩证环节
paras: Xie Yongkang and Li Jiaqi ask where Marx's materialism comes from and how it fits together with dialectics. Their thesis is that Marx's materialist stance was extracted from Hegel's idealism through a critique of its mystical shell, rather than adopted directly from French materialism or Feuerbach. On this reading, 'materialist' and 'idealist' are two basic moments of dialectics, so the awkward external combination of materialism and dialectics does not arise.

The short piece, originally published in the Chinese Social Sciences Today in 2021, traces a line from Kant's thing-in-itself through Fichte and Hegel to Marx. It then turns to Marx's account of labour-power, the human being as a natural being, the division of labour, and the conditions and structure of freedom, with references to the 1844 Manuscripts, The German Ideology and Capital.

The authors argue that German idealism's core logic is to dissolve the thing-in-itself into the productive activity of mediation, and Marx keeps this logic while defining matter through socially productive labour. Hegel's philosophy has two opposed motives: a demand for the absolute and a longing for substantiality tied to experience. Marx, they say, makes the second motive real, treating the unity of subject and object as a fact of modern productive forces. Labour-power is then a natural force, tools and the division of labour extend the human body and group into nature, and labour always presupposes nature.

The authors conclude that human activity is conditioned and human freedom limited. Freedom has two aspects, appropriating external nature and appropriating one's own generic essence, which promote and restrict each other. Alienated labour, the division of labour and value-producing labour are, in their reading, Marx's forms of mediation, to be overcome in realising freedom. Read the original if you want a concise account of Marx's materialism as continuous with German classical philosophy.
quoteEn: Both Hegel and Marx understand the concept of matter from the standpoint of the subject's mediating activity, and Marx's critical work consists chiefly in bringing out the concept of matter wrapped inside the mystical shell of Hegel's philosophy.
quoteZh: 无论是黑格尔还是马克思，都是从主体的中介活动出发来理解物质概念，而马克思的批判工作主要是将被包裹在黑格尔哲学神秘外壳中的物质概念呈现出来。

t: The community with a shared future for mankind in light of Marx's theory of intercourse
zh: 论马克思交往理论视域下的人类命运共同体
paras: Qian Zhen asks how Marx's theory of intercourse (jiaowang, also rendered "communication" or "interaction") can illuminate the proposal to build a community with a shared future for mankind. Writing in 2021, the author argues that the community is the latest outcome of adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times. In this reading it is a new concept of global intercourse aimed at protecting the common interests of all humanity, and it both inherits and develops Marx's theory.

The article has three parts. The first reconstructs the basic structure of Marx's theory of intercourse, mainly from The German Ideology, through its links to real human beings, to production and to needs. The second sets out the global problems the author sees today: hegemonism, terrorism, ideological struggle and environmental degradation. It then presents the community through five dimensions drawn from Xi Jinping's speeches: partnership, security, economy, culture and ecology. The third part argues for continuity and development in four respects.

In the first part, Qian holds that for Marx people are products of intercourse with nature and with each other, that production is the material basis of intercourse and also depends on it, and that needs drive and shape intercourse. The central claim of the third part is that Marx expected capitalist world history to bring universal and equal intercourse. In the author's account it instead produced unequal subjects and alienated intercourse, with a union of bourgeois interests replacing the "association of free individuals". The community, built on cooperation and win-win outcomes, is said to reshape that pattern and to complete a "second leap" in cognition.

Qian adds further claims. The community expresses harmony among nature, humanity and society, drawing on the Chinese ideas of "unity of heaven and humanity" and "all under heaven belongs to all". It unites truth, goodness and beauty, and it supplies a practical route to Marx's association of free individuals, turning a transcendent ideal into an empirical reality. The author concedes that the idea has attracted doubt and that realising it will take generations. The author nonetheless concludes that it is the necessary path towards the free and all-round development of the human being. Read the original if you want an example of how Chinese Marxist scholarship links Marx's theory of intercourse to Xi Jinping's foreign-policy concept.
quoteEn: Building a community with a shared future for mankind is the necessary path to realising the association of free individuals.
quoteZh: 构建人类命运共同体是实现自由人联合体的必经之路。

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.literal: community of common destiny for humankind
glossary.explanation: A foreign-policy and global-governance concept advanced by Xi Jinping since the 18th Party Congress (2012). It calls for cooperation, shared security and common development among states.

glossary.zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化
glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
glossary.explanation: The official formula for the Party's project of fitting Marxist theory to Chinese conditions and to the current era. New theoretical results are presented as products of this process.
Marx's term for the future communist society in which individuals freely associate. The article treats it as the ideal that the community with a shared future for mankind helps to realise.

keywords: community with a shared future for mankind

t: Lenin's The State and Revolution: a systematic exposition of the Marxist theory of the state
zh: 列宁《国家与革命》：马克思主义国家观的系统阐释
source: Journal of China Jinggangshan Cadre Institute, 2021 no. 3
paras: This article introduces Lenin's The State and Revolution (written in August–September 1917, published 1918) as a systematic statement of the Marxist view of the state. Liu argues that the book answered the major questions of proletarian revolution, guided the Bolsheviks to victory in the October Revolution, and went on to shape the international communist movement and China's revolution, construction and reform. The article also holds that rereading the work still has practical value today.

The piece has three parts. The first sets out the historical background: imperialism and the First World War, the Second International's opportunism (Bernstein, Kautsky), the February Revolution and the reversal of July 1917, and Lenin's preparatory notes (the 'blue notebook' Marxism on the State). The second, the longest, summarises six themes: the origin and essence of the state; smashing the bourgeois state machine by violent revolution; proletarian dictatorship and socialist democracy; the political form of that dictatorship, drawn from the Paris Commune; 'bourgeois right' under socialism; and the withering away of the state. The third part draws three lessons for contemporary China.

In Liu's reading, Lenin shows that the state is an instrument of class rule determined by the economic base, so that even the democratic republic is the best political shell for capitalism and bourgeois democracy is in essence democracy for the propertied few. Liu follows Lenin in holding that, because proletarian revolution replaces private with public ownership, the old military-bureaucratic machine must be smashed rather than taken over. The Commune's measures (an armed people, recallable officials on workers' wages, a working body in place of parliament, democratic centralism) are presented as the model. The article also reports Lenin's view that socialism still carries 'bourgeois right' in distribution by labour, and that the state withers away only as democracy deepens and communism matures. Lenin's criticism of Bukharin is cited as a case of undialectical thinking about using the state.

Liu concludes that the book helps readers reject what the article calls the superstition of Western democracy, citing US figures on money in elections, and affirms socialist democracy with Chinese characteristics and the people's democratic dictatorship. It also underlines the long and arduous course of modernization and communism under the primary stage of socialism, and answers claims that communism is utopian. The article ends by urging readers to strengthen the Four-sphere Confidence and hold to communist ideals. Read the original if you want a compact Chinese-language digest of The State and Revolution and an example of how it is used to defend present-day Chinese political institutions.
quoteEn: Proletarian revolution is a revolution that replaces private ownership with public ownership. It must thoroughly smash the bourgeois state machine, which is determined by the nature and tasks of proletarian revolution.
quoteZh: 无产阶级革命则是用公有制代替私有制的革命。无产阶级革命必须彻底打碎资产阶级国家机器,这是由无产阶级革命的性质和任务所决定的。

glossary.explanation: A formula in Party discourse, popularised under Xi Jinping, calling for confidence in the path, theory, system and culture of socialism with Chinese characteristics.
The official characterisation of China's present development stage, adopted in the 1980s. It holds that China will remain in an underdeveloped phase of socialism for a long time.
The official definition of China's state system in the constitution: democracy for the people and dictatorship over hostile elements, under the leadership of the working class.
An organisational principle of Leninist parties and states combining democratic discussion with centralised, binding decisions. The article contrasts it with bourgeois bureaucratic centralism.

t: "Interdependent social relations" and "concrete justice"
st: A further reflection on the essence of Marx's conception of justice
zh: “互依性社会关系”与“具体的正义”
zhSub: 对马克思正义观实质的进一步反思
paras: Does Marx have a conception of justice, and what is its substance? Zeng Dong and Wang Tiancheng take up this question against the "Tucker-Wood thesis", which holds that Marx rejected a moralistic critique of capitalism from the standpoint of justice and denied justice a normative place in his philosophy. The authors argue that this reading isolates individual passages. In their view Marx criticised the abstractness and formality of the juridical values of freedom, equality and justice under capitalism, not those values as such, and aimed to give justice new content.

The article has three parts. It first distinguishes "dominating" from "interdependent" social relations as the real basis of Marx's thinking on justice, drawing on Marx's three forms of society (personal dependence, objective dependence, free individuality). It then shows how dominating relations underlie Marx's critique of capitalist "abstract justice". Finally it sets out how interdependent relations ground "concrete justice" and summarises three features of Marx's approach.

The core argument runs as follows. Both traditional and capitalist societies, the authors say, are dominating: one person or group controls the conditions of existence of another, and relations between people remain instrumental. Capitalist exchange appears free and equal, but the authors argue that once labour-power enters production, surplus value is appropriated without payment and equality gives way to exploitation, with all individuals subject to capital. Justice under capitalism is therefore, in their words, the "justice" of capital's power. Interdependent relations, which the authors tie to communism, are those in which each recognises and promotes the freedom of others, the community is nothing apart from its concrete members, and the means of production belong to associated producers. Concrete justice then means that everyone controls the conditions of their own survival and development.

The authors conclude that Marx never defined justice systematically but expressed his view through the historical analysis of social relations. His conception is historical, starts from the character of social relations rather than from atomistic individuals (setting it apart from Lockean liberalism), and measures justice by the degree to which domination is eliminated. They hold that the shift from dominating to interdependent relations is its essence, and that this lets one move beyond superficial debates. Read the original if you want a Chinese-language reconstruction of Marx's theory of justice that answers the Tucker-Wood thesis through his theory of social relations.
quoteEn: This conception of justice is a historical and concrete one; its core demand is the transformation from "dominating" to "interdependent" social relations, and this constitutes the essence of Marx's view of justice.
quoteZh: 这种正义观是一种历史的、具体的正义观，其核心内容是要求从“支配性”社会关系转换为“互依性”社会关系，这构成了马克思正义观的实质。

glossary.explanation: The authors' term for a relation in which individuals recognise one another's freedom as an end, which they identify with communism. It is their reading of Marx, not a phrase from Marx's own texts.
Justice understood as a real condition in which everyone controls the conditions of their own development. It is contrasted with the abstract, formal justice of capitalist right.
The view, associated with Robert Tucker and Allen Wood, that Marx did not criticise capitalism as unjust. The authors take it as their main target.

t: Ultimately it is because Marxism works
zh: 归根到底是因为马克思主义行
paras: This commentary, published in Guangming Daily in August 2021, takes up Xi Jinping's statement at the Party's centenary celebration (July 2021) that the Communist Party succeeds and socialism with Chinese characteristics is good "ultimately because Marxism works". Xin Xiangyang reads the line as identifying the fundamental reason for the Party's growth and for China's achievements. The author argues that the Party can keep producing new achievements only by continuing to draw on Marxism and developing contemporary Chinese Marxism and twenty-first-century Marxism.

The piece is organised under four headings. It treats Marxism's role in the national rejuvenation, Marxism as the guiding ideology of the Party and state, socialism with Chinese characteristics as a product of Marxist principles combined with Chinese realities, and the use of Marxism to observe, grasp and lead the times. It draws on quotations from Xi, Mao Zedong, Qu Qiubai and Ai Siqi, and from Marx on avoiding dogmatism.

Xin's central claim is that, after the failures of the Taiping movement, the 1898 reforms, the Boxer movement and the 1911 revolution, Marxism-Leninism gave the Chinese nation a clear direction and moved it "from passivity to initiative" in spirit. Marxism, in this account, changed China, and China in turn enriched Marxism; Xin cites Ai Siqi to say that the seeds of Marxism already lay in Chinese tradition. The author then traces Marxist guidance in four areas: the path, the theoretical system (including Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era), the institutions, and socialist culture with Chinese characteristics. Xin presents these as outcomes of adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times.

Xin concludes that Marxism's truth is open to the future and must not become dogma, so the Party must keep adapting it to Chinese practice. Since the 18th Party Congress (2012), the author says, Party members led by Xi have answered the questions of the times, the people, the Party and the world, and are guiding China towards the centre of the world stage and the building of a community with a shared future for mankind. Read the original if you want a short example of how the official 2021 centenary narrative credits Marxism for the Party's record.
quoteEn: Marxism has profoundly changed China, and China has greatly enriched Marxism.
quoteZh: 马克思主义深刻改变了中国，中国也极大丰富了马克思主义。

glossary.zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化
glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
glossary.explanation: The official formula for the Party's effort to fit Marxist theory to China's conditions and to each era. The 'times' element was added to the older 'Sinicisation of Marxism' in recent Party documents.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology associated with Xi Jinping, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017 and 2018.
The official name for China's path, theory and system since the reform era, introduced under Deng Xiaoping.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: A foreign-policy and global-governance concept promoted by Xi Jinping since 2012–13, stressing shared interests and cooperation among states.

t: Why socialist democracy with Chinese characteristics works
zh: 中国特色社会主义民主为什么行
paras: Writing in Red Flag Manuscripts in mid-2021, Fan Peng asks why socialist democracy with Chinese characteristics succeeds. The author sets the question against what the article describes as disorder in the West: political polarisation, social division, governance failures during the Covid-19 pandemic, and signs of 'democratic deficit' and 'democratic backsliding'. Fan contends that this contrast with 'China's governance' shows that Chinese democracy is a high-quality democracy, sound in concept and workable in practice.

The piece is a commentary organised under five headings. It begins with a short account of China's path to democracy from the semi-colonial period through the founding of the People's Republic, reform and opening up, and the period since the 18th Party Congress (2012). It then discusses people-centred democracy, whole-process people's democracy, the unity of form and substance, democracy that spurs development and builds consensus, and democracy that combines harmony and stability with vitality.

Fan's central claim is that democracy should be judged by substance, practical results and the people's own experience, not by electoral form. The author says Western systems reduce democracy to voting, which leaves citizens passive between elections, and cites George Tsebelis and Mancur Olson to argue that this produces empty procedure and decline. Whole-process people's democracy, by contrast, is said to cover election, consultation, decision-making, management and supervision, with a full chain of mechanisms. Fan's examples are public consultation on draft laws, including the Civil Code, which drew 1.02 million comments from 425,000 people, and grassroots consultation. Fan also argues that the Communist Party, as the highest political leadership force with no special interests, and democratic centralism allow consensus and avoid gridlock.

Fan concludes that Chinese democracy fits China's conditions, answers the people's actual concerns and keeps order and vitality together in a country of more than 1.4 billion people. The author presents the Party's century of struggle as a history of extending democratic rights. Read the original if you want an example of how official-affiliated Chinese scholarship in 2021 framed the case for Chinese democracy against Western models.
quoteEn: Whether a democracy is good depends not only on its form but also on its substance; a high-quality democracy is one in which form and substance are unified.
quoteZh: 民主好不好，不仅要看形式怎么样，还要看内容怎么样，优质的民主是形式与内容相统一的民主。

glossary.explanation: A concept Xi Jinping put forward in 2019 and stressed at the Party's centenary in 2021. It holds that democracy covers every stage of political life (election, consultation, decision-making, management, supervision), not only voting.
The organisational principle of the Communist Party and the state. It combines discussion and democratic input with unified decision-making and discipline.

t: The grounds for confidence in China's ideological system
zh: 我国意识形态制度自信的底气
source: Journal of Yanshan University (Philosophy and Social Sciences), 2021 no. 4
paras: Hou Huiqin takes up the question of why China can be confident in the fundamental system of upholding Marxism's guiding position in the ideological sphere. The 4th Plenum of the 19th Central Committee (2019) established this principle as a basic system of socialism with Chinese characteristics. Hou argues that it follows from the laws governing any ruling party, from the logic of human civilisational progress and from the laws of development of philosophy and the social sciences. The article was published in the Journal of Yanshan University (Philosophy and Social Sciences) in 2021.

The article has three numbered sections. The first treats ideological leadership as a general law of rule and draws lessons from the collapse of the Soviet Union and Eastern Europe. The second places Marxist guidance within a philosophy of history that moves from class society to the free and all-round development of the individual. The third turns to the social sciences and asks what a Marxist-led discipline system should look like in practice.

Hou's core claim is that every ruling class must control the production of ideas as well as material production, so Western charges of 'brainwashing' are, in the author's view, hypocritical. Hou reads the Soviet collapse as beginning with the discarding of Marxist philosophy as 'outdated', which opened the way to historical nihilism, individualism and the removal of Party leadership. In the second section, Hou argues that capitalism's 'abstract individual' is an animal-like, self-interested figure. Genuine individuality, Hou holds, is possible only through the proletariat's conscious liberation and a 'real collective', and so requires cultivating socialist new people. In the third, Hou criticises Western social science for positivism and abstract assumptions about human nature, such as 'economic man', which Hou says serve the existing order. Hou calls for research on objective laws and the whole of society, for Marxist foundations in each discipline's core concepts, and for 'the people' rather than the isolated individual as the subject of knowledge.

Hou concludes that the system of Marxist guidance ensures the healthy development of socialism with Chinese characteristics in the new era and links Chinese experience with world progress. In practice, Hou calls for Marxist worldview training in all disciplines, theory tied to practice, and criticism and debate that unify understanding, rather than debates over how much space to give individual freedom. Read the original if you want to see how a leading Chinese Marxist philosopher grounds ideological leadership in historical materialism and applies it to the social sciences.
quoteEn: Upholding Marxism's guiding position in the ideological sphere is the ideological foundation of upholding Party leadership, and whether this fundamental system is upheld bears on the country's political security.
quoteZh: 坚持马克思主义在意识形态领域的指导地位，是坚持共产党领导的思想基础，是否坚持这一根本制度，关乎国家的政治安全。

glossary.explanation: The official name for China's current path and system, associated with reform and opening up since 1978. Its basic institutions are defined in Party documents.

glossary.zh: 意识形态领域的指导地位
glossary.pinyin: yìshí xíngtài lǐngyù de zhǐdǎo dìwèi
glossary.en: Marxism's guiding position in the ideological sphere
glossary.explanation: The principle that Marxism provides the guiding thought in culture, media, education and scholarship. The 4th Plenum of the 19th Central Committee (2019) named it a fundamental system.
In official Chinese usage, a label for views that negate the Party's history, revolution or socialism. Chinese writers often link it to the Soviet collapse.
A term drawn from Marx's critique of bourgeois thought, meaning an isolated, ahistorical, self-interested person. The author contrasts it with Marx's 'real individual'.
The standard Chinese collective term for the humanities and social sciences. Official policy calls for building these fields with Chinese features under Marxist guidance.

t: Steadily strengthening the political consciousness to achieve the "Two Upholds"
zh: 不断坚定做到“两个维护”的政治自觉
paras: Published in Red Flag Manuscript in 2021, this short commentary asks why the "Two Upholds" are the first task of strengthening the Party's political development. Zhang argues that upholding Xi Jinping's position as the core of the Central Committee and the whole Party, and upholding the authority and centralized, unified leadership of the Central Committee, bear on the success of the Party's cause and its future. Party members, especially leading cadres, are urged to stay in step with the Central Committee politically.

The article first looks back over the Party's century, tracing leadership collectives and cores from Mao Zedong through Deng Xiaoping, Jiang Zemin and Hu Jintao. It then turns to the period since the 18th Party Congress (2012), citing the January 2019 Central Committee opinion on strengthening the Party's political development, and ends with practical requirements for the present.

Zhang's central claim is that establishing and consolidating a leadership collective and core is a mark of political maturity and a long-standing Party tradition and political strength. In this reading, the Party's achievements in revolution, construction and reform owe most to that tradition. The "Two Upholds" are presented as the new era's form of it, resting on a historical choice by the Party and people. Zhang calls for ideological education so that members grasp why central authority matters, and for strict institutional rules governing internal Party political life.

Zhang concludes that making the "Two Upholds" the first task of political development continues the Party's tradition and provides a fundamental political guarantee for building a modern socialist country. Facing a complex international environment and a changed principal contradiction in society, the article calls for a unified Party will. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party media present the Two Upholds in historical and institutional terms.
quoteEn: Establishing and consolidating a leadership collective and leadership core is an important mark of the maturity of the Party's political development.
quoteZh: 确立和巩固领导集体和领导核心，是党的政治建设成熟的重要标志。

glossary.explanation: A Party formula requiring members to uphold Xi Jinping's core position in the Party Central Committee and the whole Party, and the authority and centralized, unified leadership of the Central Committee. It was articulated in 2018–2019.
A Party term for work on political stance, direction, principles and discipline among members. It has been presented as the first task of Party building since the 19th Party Congress (2017).

t: Carrying forward the great spirit of seeking truth from facts
zh: 弘扬伟大的实事求是精神
paras: Published in Hubei Daily in July 2021, in the run-up to the Party's centenary, this commentary argues that seeking truth from facts (shishi qiushi) is the living soul of Marxism and the thread running through the Communist Party of China's hundred years. Jia Lizheng contends that the Party's history is a history of struggle to uphold this ideological line, and that it remains the basic guarantee for national rejuvenation.

The piece is organised in three parts. The first traces the principle through successive stages: Mao Zedong's 1941 Yan'an report 'Reform Our Study', the restoration of the line after the Third Plenum of the 11th Central Committee under Deng Xiaoping, and the period since the 18th Party Congress (2012) under Xi Jinping. The second presents it as the key to why the Party 'can', Marxism 'works' and socialism with Chinese characteristics is 'good'. The third ties it to the 'two centenary goals' and the 'two overall situations'.

Jia argues that the Party has won support and led the move from 'standing up' to 'becoming rich' to 'becoming strong' because it has consistently followed a line of seeking truth from facts, the mass line and a practical work style. Drawing on Marx's remark that theory becomes a material force when it grips the masses by grasping the root of things, Jia answers that the root is seeking truth from facts. In practice this means identifying real rather than false problems, following objective laws and standing with the people. Jia also calls the principle the spiritual core of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, which is said to have developed by answering the questions of the times.

Jia concludes that, as the country begins building a modern socialist country in all respects, the Party must strengthen its stance on seeking truth from facts, implement the line more fully and carry the spirit forward. Doing so is said to help it handle domestic and international situations, manage risks, and advance the Party's self-reform alongside social revolution. Jia calls for cadres to study Xi's remarks, including those at the 120th anniversary of Mao's birth, and apply them in practice. Read the original if you want a representative example of how the Party's official press in 2021 framed seeking truth from facts as a unifying thread of Party history and of Xi Jinping Thought.
quoteEn: The history of the Communist Party of China is a history of struggle and development in upholding the ideological line of seeking truth from facts.
quoteZh: 一部中国共产党党史，就是一部坚持实事求是思想路线的奋斗史、发展史。

glossary.explanation: A classical phrase that Mao Zedong gave a Marxist meaning in 1941. It became the core of the Party's ideological line, meaning that policy should start from actual conditions and be tested in practice.
The Party's basic approach to knowing and handling problems, which guides its policy lines. Since Mao, it has been summarised as seeking truth from facts.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The official guiding ideology of the Party, written into its constitution in 2017 and into the state constitution in 2018.
The goals of building a moderately prosperous society by the Party's centenary in 2021 and a modern socialist country by the People's Republic's centenary in 2049.
An official formula referring to the overall strategy for national rejuvenation and to the profound changes in the world unseen in a century.

t: On the scientific meaning and paths to realisation of socialist modernization
zh: 论社会主义现代化的科学内涵与实现路径
paras: Writing in 2021, the year China began a new journey of building a modern socialist country in all respects, Zhang Jiangang asks what socialist modernization properly means, what experience China has gained in pursuing it, and by what paths it can be achieved. The article argues that socialist modernization is defined by its aim of serving the people's fundamental interests, by the all-round development of the person, and by the advantages of the socialist system. It holds that the Party's leadership and the socialist basic economic system are the decisive conditions for success.

The article has three parts. The first traces the idea of modernization from the late-Qing reformers and the 1911 Revolution, through the Four Modernizations announced by Zhou Enlai in 1964 and 1975, to the contributions of Deng Xiaoping, Jiang Zemin, Hu Jintao and Xi Jinping. The second draws lessons from the historical record. The third sets out four implementation paths.

In Zhang's account, three lessons stand out: a correct development strategy is the precondition, scientific and technological innovation is the internal driving force, and state macroeconomic governance is the fundamental guarantee. Zhang describes modernization in China as a process led by the state, with the market playing a full role, not a spontaneous market-driven one. The paths proposed are: upholding Party leadership, which Zhang says gives the Party the capacity to set strategy, push through reforms, lead the times and set an example through Party building. They also include a people-centred development philosophy, covering education, income distribution and social security. Zhang further stresses the basic economic system, with public ownership as the main body and a socialist market economy. Finally, the article presents the new development pattern of "dual circulation", with the domestic cycle as the mainstay, as the route to basic modernization by 2035.

Zhang concludes that socialist modernization can succeed only if socialism is combined with modernization, under Party leadership and with the people at the centre. The new development stage, the new development philosophy and the dual-circulation pattern together frame the next phase. The article is largely an exposition of official positions, citing Xi Jinping and Party documents. Read the original if you want a concise, officially aligned overview of how Chinese scholars in 2021 defined socialist modernization and linked it to the new development pattern.
quoteEn: China's socialist modernization is not a spontaneous process driven purely by the market, but a process in which the state plays an active leading role and the market is allowed to play its full part.
quoteZh: 我国社会主义现代化不是一个自发的、单纯由市场推动的过程，而是一个由国家积极主导、市场充分发挥作用的过程。

glossary.explanation: The goal of modernizing industry, agriculture, national defence, and science and technology. Zhou Enlai announced it in government work reports in 1964 and 1975, and it was later central to Deng Xiaoping's reform programme.
The Party's guiding framework of innovative, coordinated, green, open and shared development. It was put forward under Xi Jinping in 2015.

A strategy announced in 2020 that treats the domestic economic cycle as the mainstay, with domestic and international cycles reinforcing each other. Official texts call it the new development pattern.

glossary.zh: 社会主义基本经济制度
glossary.explanation: Defined in the Fourth Plenum of the 19th Central Committee (2019) as public ownership as the main body with diverse forms of ownership, distribution according to labour as the main body with diverse modes, and a socialist market economy.

t: Ten essential points of the political economy of socialism with Chinese characteristics
zh: 中国特色社会主义政治经济学十大要义
paras: Cheng Enfu asks what the core tenets of the political economy of socialism with Chinese characteristics should be, and how it can develop as a logically self-consistent discipline. Taking Marx's Capital as the model of theoretical logic, the article sets out ten "essential points" covering guiding thought, object, method, tasks, starting point, central concept, axis, standpoint, purpose and policy orientation. Cheng's thesis is that this political economy must remain anchored in Marxism-Leninism and in public ownership as the dominant element of the economy.

The article is a programmatic essay published in Theory Monthly in 2021. Each of the ten sections states a positive proposition, usually tied to passages from Marx, Engels, Lenin, Stalin or Mao Zedong. Each section then ends with a list of opposing views that, in Cheng's words, do not help the discipline's logical self-consistency. These include dogmatism towards Marx, foreign or ancient authorities, "ownership neutrality", and the substitution of Western economics for socialist market-economy theory.

Cheng's central moves concern object, concept and class relations. The object of study is production relations or economic institutions in the primary stage of socialism, examined together with the productive forces and the superstructure. Cheng proposes beginning, as Capital does, with the commodity, but distinguishes commodities from public and private enterprises. These carry different basic contradictions. Labour is the "meta-concept" and a theory of public surplus value the main thread, with state, collective and cooperative surplus value distinguished from private surplus value. The axis is the relation between public capital and freely associated labour. The article describes methodological pluralism as Marxism as the essence, Western learning as a tool, and Chinese traditional learning as the root.

Cheng concludes that the discipline must take the standpoint of the working class and working people, and must oppose private monopoly and expansion. Its aim is to meet the people's growing needs for a better life, and its policy orientation is to perfect socialist economic relations so as to modernise the productive forces and the superstructure. Cheng warns that if private ownership became dominant, the socialist superstructure would sooner or later change in nature. Read the original if you want a concise statement of one influential Marxist-orthodox position on how Chinese political economy should be built, and on its objections to rival positions.
quoteEn: A political economy of socialism with Chinese characteristics that does not focus on the labour theory of value and the theory of surplus value in the primary stage of socialism can hardly be called an inheritance and development of Capital.
quoteZh: 不重点研究初级社会主义社会劳动价值论和剩余价值论的中国特色社会主义政治经济学，便很难说是对《资本论》的继承和发展。

glossary.explanation: The official name for China's path since reform and opening up, combining Party leadership and public ownership with a market economy.

An official thesis, formalised in 1987, that China is in a long initial phase of socialism with underdeveloped productive forces. Cheng uses the related phrase "primary socialism" for the economic relations of this stage.
Cheng's own concept: surplus value produced by freely associated labourers in publicly owned enterprises, which he distinguishes from private surplus value.
A concept drawn from the Marxist tradition: labour in which producers jointly own and control production. Cheng applies it to public enterprises, in varying degrees.

t: On the intellectual sources of Marx's labour theory of value
zh: 论马克思劳动价值论的思想来源
source: Social Sciences Trends (Shehui kexue dongtai), 2021 no. 6
paras: Where did Marx's labour theory of value come from? Mei Wentao, in an article published in Social Sciences Trends in 2021, follows Lenin's account of classical political economy as one source of Marxism and argues that three strands formed the starting point of Marx's value theory and his economic research. These are the development of classical political economy, the work of Marx's contemporaries, and the shift in Marx's own standpoint, above all his break with Hegel's theory of civil society.

The article is organised in three parts. The first traces the early form of the labour theory of value in British classical political economy through William Petty, Adam Smith and David Ricardo, after setting out the economic and philosophical background (Bacon and Hobbes) and the school's three features. The second looks at contemporaries who shaped Marx before his formal turn to economics: Engels, Moses Hess and Pierre-Joseph Proudhon. The third follows Marx's own path from his journalism on the Rheinische Zeitung to his critique of Hegel.

Mei's central argument is that Marx built his theory by critically absorbing and then overcoming predecessors' limits. Petty located value in labour time but treated gold and silver as the only value form.
