keywords: Outlines of a Critique of Political Economy

t: Class theory in British Marxism
zh: 英国马克思主义阶级理论研究
source: Chinese Social Sciences Today (中国社会科学报), 27 August 2020
paras: Fang Jue asks how British Marxist class theory has developed since the 1950s and what makes it distinctive within Marxism outside China. The article argues that it has passed through three research paradigms: a historical one, a political-science one and a political-economy one. Fang reads these as a distinctively British understanding of historical materialism.

The article first places British Marxism within the two broad concerns of Western Marxism: critique of contemporary capitalism and the search for a revolutionary path. It then takes each paradigm in turn. It covers the historians E. P. Thompson and Eric Hobsbawm after the rise of the British New Left (1956), state theorists such as Ralph Miliband, and Alex Callinicos in the twenty-first century.

Fang describes the historical paradigm as treating class as a relation formed through experience, custom and national cultural tradition, so that class and class consciousness cannot be separated. This paradigm is presented as a historicist reaction against French "rationalist" and scientific Marxism. The political paradigm, in Fang's account, analyses power relations. Miliband held that the state remains an instrument of the bourgeoisie even though it has some autonomy, and he defended the organised working class as the revolutionary subject against "farewell to the working class" arguments. After the neoliberal "end of class" discourse of analytical and post-Marxism, Fang says, the post-2008 turn returned to political economy. Callinicos upholds the labour theory of value and the exploitation of surplus value, and defends the working class as revolutionary subject.

Fang concludes that the three shifts show British Marxists treating historical materialism not as an abstract formula but as grounded in contemporary socialist movements. In this reading Marx's class-struggle approach to capitalism remains valid, because capital's drive to expand is unchanged. Read the original if you want a short overview of how British Marxist class theory moved from history to politics to political economy.
quoteEn: The historical materialism they understand is not an abstract formula but takes the modern socialist movement as its content and foundation.
quoteZh: 他们所理解的历史唯物主义并非抽象的公式，而是以现代的社会主义运动作为自己的内容和基础。

t: Engels's refinement and development of the Marxist theory of ideology
zh: 恩格斯对马克思主义意识形态理论的完善与发展
source: Chinese Social Sciences Today (Zhongguo shehui kexue bao), 14 July 2020
paras: Duan Guangpeng asks what Engels contributed to the Marxist theory of ideology after Marx's death. The article argues that, facing intensifying class struggle over ideological discourse and a proliferation of bourgeois systems of thought in his later years, Engels explained the basic characteristics and active role of ideology in a dialectical way, and so carried the theory further and completed it. This is a short newspaper commentary.

Duan begins with the early Marx and Engels, whose treatment of ideology was mainly a critique of illusory and inverted bourgeois ideology, without a full account of its social functions. The article then proceeds in three parts: how Engels continued while changing the path of interpretation, how he fixed ideology's basic features by reference to the economic base, and how he explained its active role through the dialectic of superstructure and base. Duan draws mainly on Engels's late works and letters, including Anti-Dühring, Ludwig Feuerbach and the End of Classical German Philosophy, and the letter to Joseph Bloch.

Duan rejects the idea that Marx's late disuse and Engels's frequent use of the concept shows anything beyond a division of theoretical labour. In Duan's reading, Engels raised the relation of thinking and being to the basic question of philosophy, separated Hegel's conservative system from his revolutionary method, and recast Hegel's philosophy of nature as a materialist view of nature. Engels also placed ideology in the superstructure, together with legal and political institutions, and ranked its forms by closeness to the economic base: politics and law are nearest, while philosophy and religion are furthest. Against vulgarised readings of historical materialism, Engels stressed the relative independence of ideology, which Duan sums up as historical continuity, uneven development and lack of synchrony. The last is illustrated by Engels's remark that economically backward countries can still play first fiddle in philosophy.

Duan concludes that Engels treated ideology as a basic concept of historical materialism whose content may be false or true and whose function may be conservative or progressive. Ideology also acts back on the economic base as a subjective and creative factor, and Duan names this as Engels's outstanding contribution in his last years. Duan adds that Engels's path of interpretation influenced the treatment of Marxism as a positive science and as a scientific ideology. Read the original if you want a concise Chinese account of how Engels's late writings are used to ground the relative independence and active role of ideology.
quoteEn: Ideology, as the ideal superstructure, acts back through people's conscious historical activity to change the material conditions of social life, and is a subjective and creative factor in the course of historical development.
quoteZh: 意识形态作为观念的上层建筑，通过人们创造历史的自觉活动反过来改变着社会物质生活条件，是社会历史发展进程中的主体性因素和创造性因素。

glossary.explanation: The Chinese rendering of the concept coined by Destutt de Tracy as a 'science of ideas'. In Marxist usage it covers forms of social consciousness such as politics, law, philosophy and religion.
In historical materialism, the totality of relations of production on which the legal, political and ideological superstructure rests.
The legal, political and ideological institutions and ideas that arise on the economic base and in turn act back on it.
The Marxist conception of history, which holds that the production and reproduction of material life is the decisive factor in historical development.

t: On the philosophy of "contradiction"
zh: 论“矛盾”的哲学
source: Journal of Zhengzhou University of Light Industry (Social Sciences Edition), 2020 no. 2
paras: Yu Bin starts from the observation that Marxist textbooks present the philosophy of contradiction almost entirely through Mao Zedong's On Contradiction. The classics of Marx, Engels and Lenin contain no dedicated treatise on contradiction but make many remarks about it, and Yu argues that these are not fully covered by Mao's essay and in places differ from it. The article sets out to collect this classical theory, compare it with On Contradiction and merge the two into a fuller Marxist theory of contradiction.

The article is a long conceptual essay that moves through the main categories of the topic in turn. These are the definition and types of contradiction, the relation between difference, opposition and antagonism, universality and particularity, principal and secondary contradictions, the two aspects of a contradiction, the evolution of contradictions, and their resolution. Yu draws heavily on Marx's Capital, Engels and Lenin. The examples include the commodity and money, planetary orbits, the Chinese revolution and the war against Japan, and socialism with Chinese characteristics.

Yu defines contradiction as a dynamic unity of opposites with an inner connection. Contradictions are of two kinds: those of things, which follow objective dialectics, and those of consciousness, which reflect them as subjective dialectics. On this basis Yu rejects Mao's claim that "difference is contradiction": difference can give rise to contradiction but does not necessarily do so. Yu also separates opposition from antagonism and holds that contradictions can be eased but never reconciled. Principal and secondary contradictions are partly objective and partly dependent on human purposes. The principal contradiction differs from the principal aspect of a contradiction, and the transformation of contradictions (zhuanhua) must be distinguished from their evolution (jinhua) into something new. Yu adds that opposites can also strengthen each other.

Applying this framework to China, Yu says socialism with Chinese characteristics belongs to the universal contradiction of socialism, not capitalism. In Yu's reading, public ownership and distribution according to work are the principal aspect of the principal contradiction, so their dominant position must not waver, while the non-public sector is supported in order to strengthen the public sector. Yu argues that problems arising in reform cannot simply be met with more of the same reform but require removing their causes. The article closes by insisting that contradictions in thought be resolved by seeking truth from facts. Read the original if you want a systematic philosophical reworking of On Contradiction against the classical texts, or an example of how Chinese Marxist philosophers tie dialectics to current debates on ownership and reform.
quoteEn: Clearly, there is contradiction between labour and capital not because they differ, but because there is an inner class connection and an active relationship between them.
quoteZh: 显然，劳资之间有矛盾，不是因为他们有差异，而是因为他们之间有内在的阶级联系和能动的关系。

glossary.explanation: A 1937 philosophical essay by Mao Zedong on dialectical materialism, which has become the standard source for the treatment of contradiction in Chinese Marxist textbooks.
The official name for the Chinese Communist Party's path since reform and opening up, combining a socialist political system with a market economy.

t: Althusser's interpretation of materialist dialectics and its implications
zh: 阿尔都塞对唯物辩证法的阐释及其意蕴
paras: Song Kaixuan asks what separates Marx's materialist dialectic from Hegel's, and how Louis Althusser answered. Against the "philosophy of practice" tradition, which stresses subjective agency and, in the author's view, over-Hegelianises Marx, Song argues that Althusser's scientistic or structuralist reading served as an important corrective, though it has its own limits.

The short piece, first published in a Chinese newspaper in 2020, has three parts. It takes up Marx's "inversion" of Hegel, then Althusser's identification of the dialectic's basic structure, and finally his treatment of the dialectic as a scientific form.

Song reports that Althusser regarded the "inversion" as a metaphor that cannot settle the question. For Althusser, Hegel's "shell" is inseparable from the "kernel", so Marx's inversion must be a fundamental reworking of the dialectic's structure. Song reads Althusser as fixing that structure in the relation between subjective activity and objective structure. This echoes two logics in Marx: an activist logic of changing the world and a determinist logic drawn from modern science. Althusser, with "overdetermination" and "structural causality", contrasts Marx's complex, uneven, structured whole with Hegel's "expressive causality", in which difference returns to the Absolute Idea.

Song concludes that Althusser advanced research on Marxist dialectics by recasting the Marx–Hegel relation as one between agency and structural determination. His flaw, in Song's view, is treating science as the only proper way of grasping the world, which forgets that Marx's critique of political economy aims to change reality. A full interpretation must link the determinist and activist logics. Read the original if you want a brief account of Althusser's reading of Marx's dialectic and a critical assessment from a Chinese perspective.
quoteEn: But its shortcoming is that it regards science as the only proper way of grasping the world, forgetting that the fundamental aim of Marx's critique of political economy was to change the real world.
quoteZh: 但其缺失在于仅将科学视为唯一适当的把握世界之方式，而遗忘了马克思从事政治经济学批判的根本目的在于改变现实世界。

t: Pioneer in building a sinicized Marxist philosophy: a study of Li Da's philosophical thought
zh: 构建中国化马克思主义哲学的拓荒者——李达哲学思想研究
paras: Wang Xinyan asks what Li Da (1890–1966) contributed to the making of a Chinese Marxist philosophy, and argues that he was its pioneering builder. In Wang's account, Li was an encyclopaedic scholar and a founding figure of the Party, whose philosophical work shaped the formation of Mao Zedong's philosophical thought. The text appeared in Guangming Daily in October 2020.

After a short biography, the article is organised in four parts. They cover Li's systematic dissemination of Marxist philosophy from the May Fourth period to the mid-1930s; his theoretical construction of the sinicization of historical materialism; his two attempts at a Marxist philosophical system, the Outline of Sociology and the Outline of Materialist Dialectics; and his exposition of Mao Zedong's philosophical thought.

Wang's core argument has three moves. First, Li moved from critiquing anarchism, revisionism and pseudo-socialism, through the 1926 Modern Sociology, to the Outline of Sociology (1935/1937), which Wang calls the first systematic Marxist philosophy text written by a Chinese author. Second, Li applied historical materialism to economics, history, politics, law and sociology, for example by proposing a 'broad economics' and describing Chinese society as 'semi-colonial and semi-feudal'. Third, the Outline of Sociology presented Marxist philosophy as a 'practical materialism' and as a unified whole, which Wang says anticipated the practical-materialism debates of the 1980s and 1990s and differed from the Soviet textbooks of the time.

Wang describes Li's later work as giving Marxist philosophy a distinctly Chinese style. The Outline of Materialist Dialectics (early 1960s) drew on the experience of the Chinese revolution and socialist construction, and Li's commentaries on Mao's "On Practice" and "On Contradiction" are presented as models of popularising Marxist philosophy. Wang cites Mao's praise of Li's works and his comments on them as evidence. Read the original if you want a concise, appreciative account of Li Da's career and of how Chinese Marxists in 2020 ranked his place in the history of Marxist philosophy in China.
quoteEn: By the mid-1930s Li Da had already explicitly advocated and systematically argued that Marxist philosophy is 'practical materialism' and had built an interpretive system of Marxist philosophy on that basis; this alone suffices to show the depth and creativity of his understanding of Marxist philosophy.
quoteZh: 李达在30年代中期就已明确主张和系统论证马克思主义哲学是“实践的唯物论”并构建了一个“实践的唯物论”的马克思主义哲学阐释体系，仅此一点就足以表明李达对马克思主义哲学理解的深刻性和创造性。

glossary.explanation: The effort to apply and adapt the materialist conception of history to Chinese conditions. It belongs to the broader tradition of 'sinicizing Marxism'.

Li Da's term for Marxist philosophy, which puts practice (centred on labour) at the core of materialism. It is close to the 'practical materialism' (实践唯物主义) discussed in Chinese philosophy in the 1980s.
Li Da's proposal for an economics guided by historical materialism. It would cover both general laws of economic evolution and the particular laws of the Chinese economy.
Two philosophical essays by Mao Zedong, based on lectures from 1937 and revised for publication in the early 1950s. They are treated in China as core texts of Mao Zedong's philosophical thought.

t: Examining Heideggerian Marxism
zh: 考察海德格尔式马克思主义
source: China Social Sciences Today (Zhongguo shehui kexue bao), 24 September 2020
paras: Yang Dong asks how research on contemporary Marxism outside China can take up the legacy of Martin Heidegger's thought. The article, a newspaper piece from 2020, argues that "Heidegger and Marxism" deserves to be treated as a distinct research topic. It also contends that the concept of Heideggerian Marxism should move from a narrow meaning, tied to Herbert Marcuse, to a broad one covering a latent current across the traditional schools.

Yang opens with Gajo Petrović's remark that modern philosophy must choose between Heidegger and Marx, or perhaps start from both. The article separates the topic from "existentialist Marxism" and from "phenomenology and Marxism". It then covers Heidegger's scattered remarks on Marx, Georg Lukács's 1949 Marxist critique of Heidegger, Marcuse's early synthesis, and later scholarship by Jürgen Habermas's contemporaries and others such as Jeffrey Wolin, Poster, Zimmerman and Demmerling.

On the narrow sense, Yang reports that Marcuse in the late 1920s and early 1930s tried to supplement fundamental ontology, which was weak on social and historical questions, with Marxism, centring on "historicity". Marcuse later judged Heidegger's concreteness illusory and found in Marx's Paris manuscripts what he had sought in Heidegger. Wolin and others nonetheless see Heideggerian traits in One-Dimensional Man. For the broad sense, Yang takes Franzen's criterion, that a thinker's reception of Heidegger within Marxism qualifies them, and so includes Schmidt, Axelos, Kosik and Petrović. Yang adds that Marxist critiques of Heidegger, by Lukács, Adorno and Badiou, supply a centrifugal counterpart to this reception and a useful reference point.

Yang concludes that studying Heideggerian Marxism means attending both to Marxism's reception of Heidegger and to its critique of him. Read the original if you want a compact map of how scholars have defined Heideggerian Marxism and which thinkers they place under it.
quoteEn: The concept of Heideggerian Marxism needs to be extended from its narrow to its broad sense, which refers to a latent current in contemporary Marxism outside China that cuts across the traditional schools.
quoteZh: 海德格尔式马克思主义概念有待从狭义扩展为广义，而后者之所指，则是当代国外马克思主义中一股潜藏的、跨越传统派别的思潮。

glossary.explanation: A Chinese academic field covering Marxist thought developed outside China, broader than Western Marxism in the narrow sense.

glossary.zh: 海德格尔式马克思主义
glossary.explanation: A label for thinkers who combine Heidegger's philosophy with Marxism. Traditionally it meant Marcuse's early work; the article proposes a wider use.

t: The dialectics of nature in Anti-Dühring
zh: 《反杜林论》中的自然辩证法思想
paras: Dialectics of nature is widely accepted as a branch of Marxist philosophy, yet a minority who posit an intellectual opposition between Marx and Engels treat it as their key evidence that Engels overstepped Marx's thought. Yang rejects this reading, arguing that Marx and Engels shared the original aim of rescuing conscious dialectics from German idealism and applying it to a materialist view of nature. Because scholarship on Engels's Dialectics of Nature is abundant while studies of the dialectics of nature in Anti-Dühring are few, the article, first published in the China Social Sciences Today in 2020, takes the latter as its subject.

The article has four parts. It first traces how dialectics displaced metaphysical thinking, then examines Engels's critique of Dühring's revival of the old philosophy of nature. It next sets out Engels's positive account of the laws of dialectics. Throughout, Yang follows Engels's own historical sketches and his use of nineteenth-century natural science.

Yang's core argument starts from Engels's account of ancient Greek dialectics as correct but naive, followed by the analytic natural science of the fifteenth century onward. That science, in Yang's account, produced an isolated, static, either-or metaphysics, which German classical philosophy and then modern materialism overcame. Dühring's philosophy of nature, though it attacks Schelling, in Yang's reading still replaces real connections with imagined ones. Engels answers on time, space, matter and motion, the passage from inorganic to organic nature, and the origin of life. He argues that the infinity of the real world differs from a mathematical series with a beginning, and that Dühring's law of determinate number copies Kant's first antinomy. Engels then presents motion as the mode of existence of matter, with mechanical, physical, chemical and biological forms that are distinct yet convertible. The law of contradiction, the law of the interconversion of quantity and quality, and the law of the negation of the negation are presented as universal laws of nature, not mystical formulas.

Yang concludes that Anti-Dühring pursues two aims, refuting Dühring and giving a systematic account of dialectics of nature, so that people can better understand and change the real world. The article implies that this shows the dialectics of nature to be an integral part of Engels's thought, not a departure from Marx. Read the original if you want a concise overview of how Engels builds the case for dialectics of nature in Anti-Dühring, or if you follow the Marx–Engels debate in Chinese scholarship.
quoteEn: Contradiction is the driving force and source of the development of all things, while the interconversion of quantity and quality is the basic form or state of their motion and change.
quoteZh: 矛盾是一切事物发展的动力和源泉，质量互变则为事物运动变化的基本形式或状态。

t: The philosophical significance of the young Marx's turn to the critique of political economy
zh: 青年马克思政治经济学批判转向的哲学意义
paras: Yuan Liguo asks what the young Marx's turn from law and philosophy to political economy, prompted in 1842 at the Rheinische Zeitung by doubts over 'material interests', meant for his philosophy. The article, a newspaper piece in the Chinese Social Sciences Today (2020), argues that in the Paris Manuscripts this first critique of national economics did three things. It sublated idealist 'synthesis of consciousness' into a materialist 'synthesis of labour', moved beyond 'crude communism', and set the theoretical orientation of a new worldview through a 'science of man'.

The text is organised in three sections: the materialist synthesis of labour, the civilizational meaning of communism, and the theoretical orientation of the 'science of man'. Yuan places Marx against Kant, Hegel and Feuerbach, and against the utopian communists Proudhon, Fourier, Babeuf and Blanqui. The argument rests mainly on close reading of the Paris Manuscripts.

In the first move, Yuan holds that Marx saw Feuerbach's naturalism as still abstract, and that Hegel grasped labour's positive essence because he stood on the ground of modern national economics. Through the critique of political economy, labour is deepened from an anthropological category into an epistemological one, so that the synthesis of consciousness rests on the synthesis of labour and not the reverse. In the second move, Yuan reads 'crude communism' as the universalisation of private property, while Marx's communism is the positive sublation of private property. It rebuilds community on humanity's social, species being, avoids setting society against the individual, and yields the 'total man'. Yuan concludes that the degree to which people are socialised measures the advance of civilisation.

In the third move, Yuan presents the 'science of man' as neither philosophical anthropology nor positive social science. It is a phenomenological study of the human, grounded in practice and sensuous experience, in which natural science enters life through industry. Critique of political economy then frees people from 'abstract labour'. Yuan concludes that uniting natural science and philosophy in this way fixed the orientation of Marx's new worldview and foreshadowed historical materialism. Read the original if you want a compact Chinese reading of the Paris Manuscripts that links labour, communism and the science of man.
quoteEn: Therefore, the critique of political economy means liberating human beings from 'abstract labour' and making them once again 'total human beings'.
quoteZh: 因此，对政治经济学的批判就是把人从“抽象劳动”中解放出来，使人重新成为“总体的人”。

t: Marx's theoretical picture of the meaning of life
zh: 马克思理解生命的理论图景
paras: Marx wrote no systematic treatise on the meaning of life. Wu Xiao'an argues that a coherent account can nonetheless be reconstructed from his political economy and historical materialism. The thesis is that, for Marx, life's meaning is neither an object of contemplation nor an abstract philosophical concept. It is a revolutionary question that unfolds in real history and is fully resolved only through the communist movement for human emancipation. The piece is a short newspaper essay, first published in the Chinese Social Sciences Today in 2020.

The article moves in four steps. It first contrasts Marx with Epicurean contemplation, Feuerbach's intuitionism and Hegel's idealist dialectic. It then turns to the Economic and Philosophic Manuscripts of 1844 and to the alienation of life's meaning under capitalism. It next takes up the link between the emancipation of workers and the emancipation of humanity. Finally it treats communism as the realisation of life's full meaning, drawing on the Communist Manifesto, Engels's Socialism: Utopian and Scientific, The German Ideology and the Critique of the Gotha Programme.

Wu's central claim is that Marx builds a double dimension of labour practice and social relations. Human essence and value are realised through free, conscious labour, which is always social production within particular relations of production. Wu notes that Marx does not make material production itself the core of human essence. Under capitalist private property, workers are separated from the means of labour and the product, and wage labour reduces their essence to a means of survival. Wu adds that alienation also corrupts relations among people and affects every class, including capitalists, who are described as instruments of capital's reproduction.

Wu concludes that Marx ties the redemption of life's meaning to the emancipation of workers, because all servitude is contained in the worker's relation to production. This requires abolishing private property and the compulsory division of labour. In the higher stage of communism, labour becomes "life's prime want" and individuals develop freely and all-roundedly. Read the original if you want a concise, text-based outline of how Marx's early and later works can be read together on the question of life's meaning.
quoteEn: In Marx's view, the meaning of life is not an abstract and isolated problem of philosophical theory, but a revolutionary problem that unfolds in real history around the double dimension of labour practice and social relations.
quoteZh: 在马克思看来，生命意义不是一个抽象和孤立的哲学理论问题，而是在现实历史中围绕劳动实践与社会关系的双重维度展开的革命问题。

t: The scientific form of Marx's philosophy
zh: 马克思哲学的科学形式
source: China Social Sciences Today (Zhongguo shehui kexue bao), 30 April 2020
paras: Wang Shizhong asks how Marx's philosophy, understood as a philosophy of practice, can be given a scientific form. Since the early 2000s, Wang notes, some scholars have reinterpreted Marxist philosophy from a practice-philosophy standpoint, aiming to go beyond traditional research and to bring Chinese, Western and Marxist resources into dialogue. Wang argues that practice must be expressed in a scientific theoretical form, and proposes an open, two-level structure for that purpose.

This short newspaper piece has three parts. It first explains why practice philosophy needs scientific form, then examines the boundary between natural and social science, and finally turns to Hegel, Croce and Wang's own proposed structure. Along the way it draws on Carl Menger's Austrian school and on game-theoretic institutional economics.

Wang's central move is a method of "reverse compulsion": tracing the internal limits of the natural sciences, and then of economics, to show where a further philosophical breakthrough is required. Natural science handles relations between humans and nature, whereas social science handles relations between people, who are purposive and free and so cannot be reduced to relations between things. Economics, in Wang's view, faces a paradox: without history it lacks legitimacy, and with history its scientific status is weakened. Hegel's dialectic offers a breakthrough, but Wang follows Croce in holding that it confuses opposites with distinct concepts. Croce's own scheme is, in Wang's judgement, a closed circuit.

Wang proposes remodelling Croce's circuit into an open "double-layer, three-dimensional" structure: theoretical and practical activity form two layers, practical activity combines higher and lower levels, and space is left for human freedom. Wang offers it as an interpretive framework and a workable scientific scheme for Marx's philosophy. Read the original if you want a compact sketch of one Chinese attempt to link practice philosophy, the philosophy of science and Croce's dialectic.
quoteEn: Hence \"science\" should be used as the theoretical form that represents \"practice\", rather than remaining within a \"philosophical\" interpretation of practice.
quoteZh: 故要以“科学”作为表征“实践”的理论形式，而不能停留在关于实践的“哲学”阐释之中。

t: Lenin's in-depth study of Marxist texts
zh: 列宁对马克思主义文献的深入研究
paras: Zhao Yulan, in a short piece for Guangming Daily, asks how Lenin related to the textual legacy of Marx and Engels. The article argues that Lenin was not only the leader of the October Revolution and the theorist who developed Marxism into Leninism, but also a careful student of the classics. In Zhao's account, he was the driving force behind the first large-scale collection, editing and systematic publication of Marx and Engels's writings, which gave the international workers' movement a theoretical weapon.

The article follows Lenin's engagement with the texts in three stages. It begins with his early study and first translation work in the 1890s and 1900s, moves to the overview of Marx's works that he gave in 1914, and ends with his support after 1917 for the institutional collection and publication of the legacy. Zhao relies on Lenin's own writings, prefaces and letters, including his notes to David Riazanov.

Zhao's core argument is that Lenin's reading shows a command of the whole corpus long before 1917. In his 1894 polemic against the Narodniks, written at 24, Lenin cited Capital, the 1859 Preface and even the then little-known manuscript of The German Ideology. In 1907 he revised the Russian edition of Marx's letters to Kugelmann and wrote a preface to the Sorge correspondence. In his 1914 encyclopaedia entry on Marx, Lenin listed Marx's works and repeatedly noted that many newspaper articles and International Workingmen's Association documents had never been collected, reissued or translated. Zhao reads this as an early recognition of the gap in the sources.

After the revolution, Zhao says, Lenin acted on this recognition. In 1920–21 he oversaw the creation of the Marx-Engels Institute under Riazanov, and sent him a note with seven questions that Zhao treats as a working programme. He also approved an extra 75,000 gold roubles for buying the Mautner and Grünberg libraries in Vienna, and kept following the collection work. Zhao concludes that study of the texts equipped Lenin to lead the revolution, and that Soviet power let him lay the intellectual foundation for world socialism through systematic editing. Read the original if you want a brief, source-based account of Lenin's role in founding the Marx-Engels textual project and the Marx-Engels Institute.
quoteEn: Lenin had already keenly perceived that Marx and Engels's writings were incompletely collected, insufficiently published and insufficiently studied.
quoteZh: 列宁就已经敏锐地觉察到马克思恩格斯著作文章搜集不全、出版不够、研究不足的现状

t: Grasping the broad trends of world and Chinese development: a guide to Marx and Engels on China
zh: 把握世界和中国的发展大势——《马克思恩格斯论中国》导读
paras: This reading guide, published in Red Flag Manuscripts (Hongqi Wengao) in 2020, introduces the collection Marx and Engels on China (《马克思恩格斯论中国》). Wang Yi asks what Marx and Engels wrote about China and why it still matters. The guide argues that their judgements help readers understand Marxist standpoint and method, the main course and lessons of modern Chinese history, and why China should unwaveringly keep to the path of socialism with Chinese characteristics.

The guide has three parts. The first sets out the historical conditions in which Marx and Engels came to study China. The second summarises five groups of their judgements on Chinese society and events. The third turns to the present and draws lessons for understanding contemporary China.

Wang gives three reasons for the two thinkers' interest in China. China was the last piece of the capitalist world market, forced in by the Opium Wars. It also became part of their search for revolutionary prospects after the defeat of the European revolutions. And Marx wrote about it as a correspondent for the New-York Daily Tribune, with Engels helping to translate and contributing pieces of his own. Wang then reports their analyses. They described a social structure built on small-scale agriculture combined with household industry, which in Wang's account underpinned centralised despotism and 2,000 years of stability. They exposed the opium trade and the aggressions of Britain, France and Russia, and they backed the Chinese people's resistance, including the Taiping uprising. They predicted that the old order would collapse, that China would affect world civilisation, and that it would eventually take a socialist road, even naming a future 'Chinese Republic'.

Wang draws three present-day lessons. First, China must be understood within world history. Wang cites the 19th Party Congress (2017) on what has and has not changed in China's position, and calls for balancing change and continuity amid what the guide calls great changes unseen in a century. Second, comprehensive deepening of reform should proceed with correct direction and keep economic development central. It should aim at modernising the system and capacity of national governance. Third, China should help build a community with a shared future for mankind, rejecting hegemonism and Cold War thinking while staying alert to Western interference. Read the original if you want a concise, officially oriented overview of Marx and Engels's writings on China and of how they are used in current Party discourse.
quoteEn: Marx and Engels's views on China are not only of important guiding value for correctly understanding modern Chinese history; today, as socialism with Chinese characteristics enters a new era, they still have major practical significance.
quoteZh: 马克思、恩格斯的中国观不仅对我们正确认识近代中国历史具有重要的指导价值，在中国特色社会主义进入新时代的今天，依然有着重要的现实意义。

glossary.explanation: The official name for the Chinese Communist Party's model of socialism since the reform era, combining Party leadership with a market-based economy.
A policy slogan launched at the Third Plenum of the 18th Central Committee (2013), calling for reform across economic, political, social and other fields.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's foreign-policy concept, promoted since about 2013, which presents international relations as based on cooperation and shared interests.

glossary.en: great changes unseen in a century
glossary.explanation: A phrase used in official discourse since about 2017–2018 to describe a major shift in the global order, including the rise of emerging economies.

keywords: community with a shared future for mankind

t: Engels's construction of the system of Marxist philosophy
zh: 恩格斯对马克思主义哲学体系的建构
paras: This short commentary, first published in Guangming Daily in June 2020, asks what Engels contributed to building Marxist philosophy into a system. Yang argues that Engels contributed in both form and content. In form, he helped break down the closed logic of older philosophical systems and made philosophy an open structure and dynamic thought. In content, he started from a renewed reading of philosophy's basic question and joined ontology, dialectics and the conception of history into one whole.

Yang first notes that systematising an existing theory is as hard as creating one, and cites Engels's editing of volumes two and three of Capital and works such as Anti-Dühring, Ludwig Feuerbach and the End of Classical German Philosophy, Dialectics of Nature and The Origin of the Family, Private Property and the State. The piece then moves through four themes: the basic question of philosophy, the ontological foundation, dialectics, and the relations among historical factors.

On ontology, Yang says Engels located the unity of the world in its materiality, abstracted the concept of matter from particular material things, and examined matter, motion, time and space. On dialectics, Yang presents it as the main thread running through Engels's work. Engels is credited with showing its role as worldview and method in nature, history and thought, and with distilling its laws. On history, Yang argues that Engels corrected the one-sided stress on economic determination, which Marx and Engels had sometimes made in polemic. Engels stressed the relative independence and interaction of political, legal and ideological factors, so that economically backward countries can still "play first fiddle" in philosophy.

Yang concludes that these achievements make Engels's description of himself as "second fiddle" fully deserved. The text is a brief appreciation, not a detailed textual study.

Read the original if you want a compact Chinese overview of how Engels's role in systematising Marxist philosophy is presented in official-academic commentary.
quoteEn: Engels's indelible contribution to constructing the system of Marxist philosophy makes his self-description as \"second fiddle\" fully deserved.
quoteZh: 恩格斯对马克思主义哲学体系的建构所作出的不可磨灭的功绩，使其“第二小提琴手”的自我认同实至名归。

t: Engels and Marx's "turn to political economy"
zh: 恩格斯与马克思的“政治经济学转向”
paras: Published in Guangming Daily in July 2020, this short piece asks how Marx came to turn to political economy. Liu argues that Engels played a key role in prompting and shaping that turn.

The article first outlines Engels's early observations of capitalist society in Barmen, Bremen and Manchester, and the works he wrote between 1843 and 1845. It then looks at Marx's "tormenting doubts" arising from his work on the Rheinische Zeitung, and at how Engels's writings bore on his first economic studies.

Liu contends that Marx's studies had shown him that civil society determines the political state, but he did not yet grasp civil society's economic relations. Engels's Outlines of a Critique of Political Economy, read while Marx was preparing the Deutsch-Französische Jahrbücher, showed the importance of political economy and recast its basic categories. Liu then identifies three links with the Economic and Philosophic Manuscripts of 1844: the aim of criticising classical economics, the empirical material on workers' conditions drawn from Engels's The Condition of the Working Class in England, and a historically grounded critique of private property. The two men's ten days of discussion in Paris in 1844 are said to have strengthened these links.

Liu concludes that Engels's close attention to concrete social problems and empirical evidence helped Marx resolve his early doubts. It also pointed him towards a deeper inquiry into capital. Read the original if you want a brief account of Engels's influence on Marx's early economic thought.
quoteEn: Engels's writings made Marx feel both the importance and the urgency of such research, and directly brought about his "turn to political economy".
quoteZh: 恩格斯的论著既让他感到这种研究的重要性和紧迫性，更直接促成了他的“政治经济学转向”。
keywords: Condition of the Working Class in England

t: New features of monopoly in modern capitalism
zh: 现代资本主义垄断的新特征
paras: Writing in 2020 amid trade disputes, Tan Peiwen and Chen Yao argue that capitalist monopoly is not confined to the financial monopoly stressed in Lenin's theory of imperialism. They contend that earlier research neglected Marx's treatment of monopoly in production, consumption, distribution and exchange, and that today's trade frictions repeat the pattern Marx analysed in the Grundrisse in the 1850s.

The short commentary, first published in the Chinese Social Sciences Today, works through four spheres in turn, drawing on passages from the Grundrisse. It then turns to practical conclusions for China's response.

In the authors' reading, monopoly over the production of exchange value disrupts the industrial and value chains that produce use values, and in the world market appears as unilateralism, prohibitive tariffs and protectionism. Capital's monopoly of the labour market makes the exchange of money for labour-power formally equal while real inequality persists, so that equality and freedom become empty ideas. Consumption serves only capital's accumulation, not people's all-round development, and distribution by capital leaves workers impoverished. The authors read recent US tariff increases as an internationalisation of this power over distribution.

They conclude that capitalism is not the same as the market economy and has an anti-market side. China should use the strengths of the socialist market economy, rebuild fair value chains, pursue common prosperity, and guard against systemic financial risk while opening up further. Read the original if you want a brief Chinese Marxist reading of the US–China trade conflict through Marx's Grundrisse.
quoteEn: Capitalist monopoly is not only concentrated in financial monopoly, but also shows new features of monopoly in the spheres of production, consumption, distribution and exchange.
quoteZh: 资本主义垄断不仅突出集中表现为金融垄断，而且还表现出生产、消费、分配和交换等领域垄断新特征。

glossary.explanation: China's official economic system since the early 1990s, combining market mechanisms with public ownership and state macro-control.
A Chinese policy goal of prosperity shared by all, stressed in Party documents and especially under Xi Jinping.

t: The narrative features of Engels's theory of nature's revenge
zh: 恩格斯“自然报复论”的叙事特征
paras: Marking the 200th anniversary of Engels's birth, Li Heliang and Zhang Xu revisit his theory of nature's revenge, a short newspaper essay on how Engels built his dialectics of nature around the human–nature relation. The authors argue that the theory carries its background, rhetoric and purposes implicitly within the text, and that it prepares the idea of the "two reconciliations": between humanity and nature, and within humanity itself.

The essay is organised around five features: the stages in which the theory took shape, its writing context, its intended targets, its rhetorical strategies, and its bearing on the present. It draws on Engels's early reports on pollution, Anti-Dühring, "On Authority", "The Part Played by Labour in the Transition from Ape to Man" and Dialectics of Nature.

The authors contend that Engels aimed to settle accounts with several rival outlooks. These were naturalism and anthropocentrism, vulgar materialism and social Darwinism, and metaphysical views of nature together with idealist dialectics. Li and Zhang say Engels placed nature as the prior material basis of human activity, which people change and use by knowing its laws. His rhetoric relied on personification, analogy and model abstraction from cases such as deforestation and soil erosion. The authors conclude that, for Engels, nature's revenge is in essence people's revenge on themselves. They hold that it arises from the limits of human knowledge, from capitalist production for profit, and from consumer desires stimulated by capital.

The authors conclude that, on Engels's account, only communism can resolve these contradictions at root. They link the theory to the Fourth Plenum of the 19th Central Committee (2019), calling for Xi Jinping Thought on Ecological Civilization, ecological red lines and a "Beautiful China". Read the original if you want a brief Chinese official-academic reading of Engels's ecological thought and its link to current ecological civilization policy.
quoteEn: Engels held that the defects of human understanding, and the flaws of social production and of consumption and distribution under the capitalist system, inevitably give rise to nature's revenge, and make it ever more severe.
quoteZh: 恩格斯认为人类的认识缺陷、资本主义制度下的社会生产和消费分配弊端必然会导致自然报复的产生，并会越来越严重

glossary.explanation: A label for Engels's argument that nature reacts against human conquest of it, drawn mainly from "The Part Played by Labour in the Transition from Ape to Man" and Dialectics of Nature.
Shorthand for the reconciliation of humanity with nature and of humanity with itself, an idea Chinese scholars derive from Engels's early writings.
A Chinese official concept for a model of development that seeks harmony between people and nature. It is a stated national goal since the early 2010s.

glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Ecological Civilization
glossary.explanation: The part of Xi Jinping's thought that deals with environmental protection and ecological civilization, formally articulated in 2018.
Officially designated limits and protected zones within which development is restricted to safeguard ecological functions.

t: A classic for understanding the origin and withering away of the state: a reader's guide to The Origin of the Family, Private Property and the State
zh: 理解国家起源与消亡的经典著作——《家庭、私有制和国家的起源》导读
paras: This is a reader's guide, published in Red Flag Manuscripts (Hongqi Wengao) in 2020, to Engels's The Origin of the Family, Private Property and the State (1884). Ming presents the book as a work that applies historical materialism to the state. In this account, it explains how family, private property and class relate to the emergence of the state, and so enriches Marxist political theory.

The guide is organised in four parts. It first sets out the book's background: Marx's plan to interpret Lewis Henry Morgan's Ancient Society, Engels's use of Marx's notes on it, and the need to answer bourgeois scholars and opportunists. It then summarises the contents (a preface, nine chapters and an 1892 appendix) and the book's main ideas. It closes with the book's theoretical and historical significance and its relevance for China in the new era.

On the core argument, Ming reports Engels's theory of the two kinds of production, the production of the means of life and the production of human beings themselves. Engels uses these to trace the move from kinship relations to class relations. The state, in Ming's reading, is a historical category produced by the third great division of labour, which dissolved the gentile order. Ming lists three routes to the state (Athenian, Roman and Germanic) and three features of the state: territorial division of the population, a public power backed by force, and taxation. Its essence is class rule, even where it appears as the representative of the public interest. Its forms are slave-owning, feudal and bourgeois, and it will wither away once private property and classes are abolished on the basis of highly developed productive forces.

Ming draws contemporary lessons. Capitalist democracy is described as an indirect and concealed form of bourgeois class rule. China's socialist state, resting on public ownership and the people's democratic dictatorship, is said to represent the fundamental interests of the great majority. Ming adds that abolishing private ownership is a long process that depends on conditions. As long as socialism and capitalism compete, the author argues, state functions must be strengthened and not weakened, and class struggle still exists in China to a certain extent. Ming also points to implications for family-building and for the modernization of the system and capacity of state governance. Read the original if you want to see how a Party journal in 2020 presents Engels's theory of the state and its application to current Chinese policy.
quoteEn: The Origin tells us that in an era when socialism and capitalism are still in competition, the functions of the state must by no means be weakened but must be strengthened.
quoteZh: 《起源》告诉我们在社会主义与资本主义仍然处于竞争的时代，国家职能决不能削弱，而是要加强。

glossary.explanation: The constitutional description of China's state system: led by the working class and based on the worker–peasant alliance. It means democracy for the people and dictatorship over those regarded as hostile to it.

glossary.en: modernization of the system and capacity of state governance
glossary.literal: modernisation of the state governance system
glossary.explanation: A goal set out in the Party's 2013 Third Plenum decision, referring to improving institutions and the ability to govern.
Engels's idea that history is determined by the production of the means of life and by the production of human beings themselves, that is, reproduction.

t: Engels's critique of capital and its characteristics
zh: 恩格斯的资本批判及其特征
paras: Nie Jinfang's short piece, published in Guangming Daily in 2020, asks what Engels's own critique of capital consisted of and what marks it out. Nie argues that Marxism is bound up with the critique of capital and the search for human emancipation. In Nie's account, Engels and Marx were highly consistent in analysing capitalist society and the position of the working class, and they completed the theoretical construction of Marxism in complementary ways.

The article is organised around three features of Engels's critique. The first is his lived experience of the "suffering and ills" of the age of capital in Barmen, Bremen, Manchester and London. The second is his grasp, through years in business, of the historical formation and present workings of the capitalist system. The third is his editing of Marx's manuscripts for the second and third volumes of Capital.

On the first point, Nie draws on The Condition of the Working Class in England, which Engels wrote after 21 months of direct observation. It documents workers' physical, intellectual and moral degradation, and Nie notes the contradiction between Engels's position as a "cotton king" and his siding with labouring people. On the second, Nie traces how improved spinning machinery, from the spinning jenny to the steam engine, produced the factory system, which split society into capitalists and proletarians and fostered working-class consciousness. On the third, Nie holds that Engels was more than a technical editor of the fragmentary manuscripts of Volumes II and III. In Nie's reading he was an interpreter and in some sense a constructor of their ideas, which cover circulation, reproduction, profit, production prices, commercial and interest-bearing capital.

Nie concludes that Engels moved from sensory experience of the age of capital to rational dissection of it, and that Marx's political-economic theory could not have been presented in complete form without Engels's labour. Nie closes with Marx's own letter of thanks for Engels's sacrifices. Read the original if you want a brief Chinese-language overview of Engels's role in the critique of capital, and of how a Guangming Daily author presents Engels's part in completing Capital.
quoteEn: He was also an interpreter of the ideas and theoretical system of these two volumes, or in a certain sense their constructor.
quoteZh: 他也是这两卷所关涉的思想内容和理论体系的阐释者，或者从某种意义上讲是建构者。
keywords: Condition of the Working Class in England

t: Marx's philosophical mode of expression
zh: 马克思的哲学表达方式
paras: Twentieth-century declarations of the "end of philosophy", especially in French philosophy, have amplified the anti-philosophical strain in Marx and cast doubt on whether "Marx's philosophy" is a legitimate concept. Xia Ying, in a short piece first published in the Chinese Social Sciences Today in April 2020, argues that Marx did not abandon philosophy. In Xia's reading, the historical materialism he built is itself a new way of expressing philosophy, a philosophical revolution suited to its era.

The article begins with the "Korsch problem", the early twentieth-century question whether Marxism is a philosophy at all. Xia treats it as a pointer to a tension between theory and practice rather than a question to be settled. It then turns to Marx's well-known mockery of "philosophers" in the Theses on Feuerbach and The German Ideology. Next it sets out two features of historical materialism, and finally it places Marx within the line of German classical philosophy from Kant to Hegel.

Xia contends that the philosophy Marx rejected around 1845 was specific: the Hegelian speculative system and its one-sided Young Hegelian heirs, which equate conceptual construction with practice. Historical materialism, by contrast, has a practical orientation. It examines the logical preconditions of history, namely the material conditions of real individuals' activity, so that objectivity takes logical priority. It also looks forward: the analysis of past forms of ownership is guided by a vision in which the division of labour and alienated labour disappear and individual freedom is realised within social freedom. For this reason Xia calls it less a "scientific study" of history than a "philosophical study" of the possibility of human freedom.

Xia concludes that Marx's questions, the first causes of being and the conditions of freedom, remain within the traditional problem field of philosophy. What changes is the mode of expression. Drawing on the "strong sense of history" of German classical philosophy, Marx adds historical qualifiers to his categories and takes up questions such as the workings of capitalist economic structures. The difference between Marx and earlier Western philosophy is therefore one between old and new modes of philosophical expression, not between non-philosophy and philosophy. Read the original if you want a concise argument, from within Chinese Marxist philosophy, that historical materialism counts as philosophy, and if you are interested in how it answers the Korsch problem.
quoteEn: The difference between Marx's philosophy and all earlier Western philosophy is less a difference between non-philosophy and philosophy than one between a new mode of philosophical expression and the modes of expression of an older age.
quoteZh: 马克思的哲学与此前全部西方哲学的差异，与其说是非哲学与哲学的差异，不如说是新的哲学表达方式与旧有时代的哲学表达方式之间的差异。

t: The value implications of the good life in the Communist Manifesto
zh: 《共产党宣言》中美好生活的价值意蕴
paras: Ouyang Qi and Jin Xingyu read the Communist Manifesto, published more than 170 years ago, as a "political manifesto" of the good life as well as a founding document of scientific socialism. This short commentary, first printed in the Chinese Social Sciences Today in 2019, argues that its theoretical core and practical implications can inform the theory and practice of the good life in the new era.

The authors organise the piece in three parts. The first covers the Manifesto's picture of the good life, the second its paths to realisation, and the third how it presents the good life through historical materialism. They note that the word "life" appears 28 times in the text, and that Engels's 1888 note defines the proletariat through the need to live by selling labour-power.

Ouyang and Jin argue that the Manifesto answers the proletariat's material and spiritual oppression with an "association of free individuals", which they describe as uniting rich material life, elevated spiritual life and harmonious ecological life. They derive this from its critique of capitalism's overproduction, its stripping of the sacred, and its strain on the environment. Three paths follow: leadership by communists, whose interests they say coincide with the whole proletariat's; labour as the real means of achieving the good life; and uniting all possible forces internationally. The authors add that the Manifesto rebuts bourgeois accusations and corrects feudal, bourgeois and utopian socialism.

The authors conclude that, despite the changed era, the Manifesto's account remains relevant. They cite the 19th Party Congress report (2017) pledge to take the people's longing for a better life as the Party's goal. Combining the Manifesto's meaning with meeting "needs for a better life" is, in their view, an effective route to adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times. Read the original if you want a brief, Party-line reading of the Manifesto's treatment of life and labour linked to new-era policy language.
quoteEn: With historical materialism as its core, the Manifesto, in condensed and spirited language, presents to the world from both positive and negative sides its design and vision of the good life.
quoteZh: 《宣言》以唯物史观为核心内容，通过凝练豪迈的语言形式，从正反两方面向世人呈现了对于美好生活的设计与构想。

glossary.zh: 马克思主义时代化、中国化
glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
glossary.explanation: Official formula for the ongoing effort to apply and develop Marxism in light of Chinese conditions and contemporary circumstances.
A key phrase from the 19th Party Congress report (2017), which spoke of the people's growing needs for a better life as the Party's goal.
The Chinese rendering of the Marxian image of a future communist society in which each person's free development is the condition for the free development of all.

t: Western Marxism's decoding and critical study of capitalism
zh: 西方马克思主义对资本主义的解密与批判性研究
paras: Feng Wangzhou, in a short commentary first published in China Social Sciences Today in September 2019, asks how Western Marxism has studied capitalism and what its critique achieves. The author argues that Western Marxism continues Marx's critical tradition and has tracked capitalism's changes, but only partly inherits that tradition because its remedies stay inside the capitalist system.

The article divides Western Marxism's roughly ninety years into three periods. These are its formation in the 1920s and 1930s (Lukács, Korsch, Gramsci), its flourishing from the 1930s to the late 1960s (the Frankfurt School, existentialist, Freudian and structuralist Marxism), and its fragmentation after the 1970s into analytical, ecological, political, feminist and postmodern currents. It then lists the critical models these currents produced and the labels contemporary thinkers give to capitalism.

Feng contends that the early cultural turn reflected the integration of economy and culture under the logic of capital. Later schools criticised instrumental and economic rationality, consumerism and technology, and recent ones turned to micro-level political economy, neoliberalism and new imperialism. In Feng's reading, this work shows capitalism to be a changing structure and supports Marx's "two inevitables". Yet Western Marxism explains capital's control through concepts such as the one-dimensional society, the society of the spectacle and the consumer society. According to Feng, it cannot answer deeper questions of accumulation and profit maximisation, and it overlooks how this control supports new imperial hegemony.

Citing Xi Jinping on the need to study contemporary capitalism, Feng calls on Chinese Marxist scholars to study these problems in depth and to develop a Chinese discourse paradigm for studying capitalism. Read the original if you want a brief, officially aligned Chinese overview of how Western Marxism's phases and critical models are assessed.
quoteEn: Western Marxism merely explains the control exercised by the logic of capital in contemporary capitalist society as a one-dimensional society, a society of the spectacle and a consumer society, and its solution remains an adjustment within capitalism.
quoteZh: 西方马克思主义只是把当代资本主义社会的资本逻辑操控解释为单向度社会、景观社会和消费社会，其解决办法仍然是在资本主义内部进行调整。

glossary.explanation: Marx and Engels's thesis, drawn from the Communist Manifesto and Capital, that capitalism's downfall and the victory of socialism are inevitable.
The tradition begun by Lukács, Korsch and Gramsci in the 1920s and continued by the Frankfurt School and others, stressing philosophy, culture and ideology.
A term used in Chinese Marxist writing for capital's drive towards accumulation, self-expansion and profit maximisation, which shapes all areas of social life.

t: Marx's theory of "reproduction" and its social significance
zh: 马克思“再生产”理论及其社会意义
paras: Most scholarship at home and abroad reads Marx's theory of reproduction as a matter of economics. Writing in the Chinese Social Sciences Today in March 2019, Yu argues that this reading is too narrow. In Yu's account, the theory has a broader social meaning, which appears in three forms: the reproduction of human beings, the reproduction of nature, and the reproduction of social relations.

The piece begins with criticisms from Western thinkers. Yu cites Heidegger, Arendt and Baudrillard as having confined Marx's concepts of production and reproduction to technology, the maintenance of life or the framework of political economy. Yu answers these critics with Engels's remark that, on the materialist conception of history, the decisive factor is the production and reproduction of real life, not the economic factor alone. The article then sets out the three senses of reproduction and ends with two lessons for the present: good social relations and a sound relationship between humans and nature.

On the first sense, Yu says reproduction means the production, maintenance and development of living individuals, which Marx treats as the premise of history. Under capitalism this takes the form of the reproduction of labour-power, which the author calls the foundation of the system and the source of surplus value. On the second, Yu reads Marx's statement that humans "reproduce the whole of nature" as going beyond treating nature as a resource to be plundered. It points instead to a productive and ecological ethic in which humans combine the measure of the object with their own inner measure. Yu holds that Heidegger and Baudrillard misread this point. On the third, Yu draws on Marx's claim that capitalist production reproduces the relation between capitalist and worker, which the author presents as more important than its material result. Each class reproduces itself by reproducing its opposite.

Yu concludes that an economics-only reading hides the analysis of social relations and the critique of society that Marx built on this theory. Marx, Yu says, called for abolishing private property and the division of labour so as to reproduce a "real community" of free individuals. Yu adds that Marx also called for reproducing a harmonious relationship between humans and nature, under which society becomes the "completed unity of man with nature". Yu claims the theory offers guidance for building socialism with Chinese characteristics, for the Chinese Dream of the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation, and for a community with a shared future for mankind. Read the original if you want a short example of how Chinese scholars use Marx's reproduction theory to answer Heidegger, Arendt and Baudrillard and to support ecological and social-relations themes in official discourse.
quoteEn: Understanding reproduction purely from an economic angle is not only one-sided but also obscures the perspective of social-relations analysis and social critique that Marx developed through it.
quoteZh: 仅仅从经济学的角度理解再生产不仅是片面的，还会遮蔽掉马克思以此展开的社会关系和社会批判的分析视角。

glossary.explanation: The official name for the Chinese Communist Party's model of socialism since the reform era. It is presented as Marxism applied to China's conditions.
A slogan associated with Xi Jinping from 2012. It refers to national rejuvenation and the prosperity of the Chinese people.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A central goal of Party discourse. It means restoring China to national strength and international standing.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: A foreign-policy and global-governance concept promoted by Xi Jinping since about 2012. It stresses shared interests and cooperation among states.

t: The normative foundation of Marx's critique of capitalism
zh: 马克思批判资本主义的规范性基础
source: Chinese Social Sciences Today (Zhongguo shehui kexue bao), 23 April 2019
paras: Does Marx's critique of capitalism rest on a normative foundation? Zhang Shoukui takes up a dispute that has run among Anglo-American Marxist scholars since the 1970s over Marx's relation to morality and justice, and that remains unresolved. Zhang argues that such a foundation does exist, but that it is neither justice nor equality in the ordinary moral sense. It is individual freedom understood as self-realization, aimed at the condition of human emancipation in which "the free development of each is the condition for the free development of all".

The piece, a short newspaper article, first surveys four positions in Western scholarship. It then explains why individual freedom can serve as Marx's normative ground, and ends by considering what follows for Marx's aims and for current Chinese research. Zhang draws on Western commentators, including David Alan Shikiar on the "normative function" of concepts and Blackett's summary of Marx's critique as grounded in freedom and in the effect of private property on individuality and personality.

Zhang lists the four positions: an ethical demand against exploitation and injustice; purely scientific and empirical analysis; a self-aware assessment of how private ownership harms individual development; and a charge of irrationality and alienation. Zhang holds that Marx treated justice as a form of ideology, so his opposition to private property cannot rest wholly on justice. Marx's freedom, in this reading, is not self-interested "free appropriation" of external objects, as in the political economists. Owning the means of production is a precondition for freedom, not its aim, and freedom means the full and unobstructed development of a person's capacities, opposed to alienated and forced labour. Capital and private ownership therefore appear as limits on self-realization. Zhang adds that Marx shows private property to be a historical product and not a natural or eternal fact.

Zhang concludes that the decisive difference from classical liberalism lies here. Liberalism treats capital and private property as intrinsic to freedom, whereas Marx treats them as instruments for freedom under certain conditions, and finally as a constraint on it. Criticizing capital is therefore a means to human emancipation and the all-round free development of each person. Zhang calls on scholars who deepen historical materialism through the critique of capital logic to raise it to a logic of revolution, or of emancipation and individual self-realization. Read the original if you want a compact Chinese-language account of how a Chinese Marxist scholar answers the Anglo-American debate on Marx, morality and justice.
quoteEn: This normative foundation is not \"justice\" and \"equality\" in the ordinary moral-ethical sense, but \"individual freedom\" in the sense of self-realization.
quoteZh: 此种规范性基础不是一般道德伦理意义上的“正义”和“平等”，而是自我实现意义上的“个人自由”

t: The dialectic of Capital
zh: 《资本论》的辩证法
paras: This is a Chinese translation of a text by the American philosopher Allen Wood on the dialectical method of Marx's Capital. Wood argues that the work is best read as a hierarchy of theoretical models, running from very abstract models of basic social forms to fuller and more concrete ones. In his view, many familiar objections to Marx's economics come from overlooking this structure.

Wood first sketches the course of Capital: the commodity, the law of value, the value form and money, the conversion of money into capital, surplus value, the split between constant (c) and variable (v) capital, and absolute and relative surplus value. He then follows Marx through circulation in Volume II and the unified account of profit, interest and rent in Volume III. Three sections take up value and production prices, the law of value itself, and the relation between value and exploitation.

Wood contends that the law of value in Volume I is not a general theory of relative prices. It is the founding assumption of a deliberately simple model of freely reproducible commodities, which Marx then refines. Production prices in Volume III, formed through an average rate of profit, belong to a less abstract model, so the charge that the volumes contradict each other (made from Böhm-Bawerk onwards) fails. Wood nevertheless concedes that the transformation problem, raised by Bortkiewicz, points to a real defect in Marx's Volume III. He reads the apparently deductive argument for the law of value in Chapter 1 as weak at several steps, notably the premise of an equal common element in exchanged goods, and as best taken as an expository device. In his account the real grounds lie in Marx's letter to Kugelmann: allocating social labour in proportion to social need is a natural law, and under commodity production it takes the form of exchange value. Wood treats this as a historical-materialist claim tied to commodity fetishism.

Wood denies that Marx's claim that capital exploits labour depends on the labour theory of value, and he sees the neoclassical attack on that theory as aimed at discrediting surplus value. He allows that other approaches, such as Sraffa's input–output analysis, might do the same work as well or better. He adds that Marx never denied capitalists a necessary role in production. Read the original if you want a philosophically trained, Anglophone reading of the logic of Capital that separates the law of value from price theory and from the theory of exploitation.
quoteEn: Volumes I and III do not give us contradictory theories of price, but merely different patterns of commodity exchange, one more basic and abstract, the other more complex and closer to appearances.
quoteZh: 第一卷和第三卷未给我们矛盾的价格理论,而只是商品交换模式有所差异,一个更加基本和抽象,另一个更加复杂且接近于表象。

t: Investigating a missing source note in Capital
zh: 查究《资本论》 文献注释问题
paras: Volume I of Capital carries over 1,000 notes, yet a few quotations lack precise sources. Xiang Xiuli takes up one such case and argues that Engels was wrong to say that only one quotation, a passage attributed to Richard Jones, was left without a source. The article proposes a source for a long quotation that Marx left unreferenced, and that Engels also missed.

The piece, a short commentary from the Chinese Social Sciences Today in 2019, begins with the editorial history of the notes. It then turns to the unreferenced passage, which describes contradictory rulings by magistrates and differing legal practice in Yorkshire and Lancashire. It reviews how the historical-critical edition (MEGA2) and the Chinese editions treated the passage, and ends with the proposed annotation.

Xiang notes that MEGA2 marks the passage as "source could not be established", and that Chinese editions say nothing about it. Because the passage falls in Chapter 8, where Capital draws most heavily on the English Factory Inspectors' Reports, and is introduced by a phrase about manufacturers complaining, Xiang infers that it comes from those reports. No single fragment matches exactly. Xiang finds that most of the passage comes from Inspector Horner's remarks in the report to 31 October 1849, and that the remainder draws on that report and the one to 30 April 1849. Xiang says MEGA2 itself lists several sources for composite quotations.

Xiang proposes editor's notes in the relevant place in the Chinese edition of Capital, giving the page references to those reports, and suggests MEGA2 could drop its "unverified" note. Xiang compares this to the detailed note on the Chinese official Wang Maoyin, a philological contribution that originated in China. Xiang concedes that the hypothesis may be disproved and welcomes better proposals. Read the original if you are interested in Marx's editorial and textual scholarship, or want the exact source references Xiang proposes.
quoteEn: The problem here is that in Capital it is not the case that \"only one quotation has no source found\".
quoteZh: 这里的问题在于，《资本论》中并非“只有一段引文没有找到出处”。

t: Capital and the inner logic of research on Marx's political philosophy
zh: 《资本论》与马克思政治哲学研究的内在逻辑
source: Chinese Social Sciences Today (Zhongguo shehui kexue bao), 26 July 2019
paras: Gao Guangxu asks in what sense Capital can serve as an intellectual resource for research on Marx's political philosophy, a question the author treats as urgent for contemporary work in this field. The short commentary argues that reading Marx's political philosophy through Capital is not an expedient but follows necessarily from the development and the essential character of that philosophy.

The article is organised around three claims about the critique of political economy in Capital: it is the logical result of Marx's political-philosophical development, the logical precondition for advancing research on it, and the logical vehicle of its contemporary significance. Gao draws on Marx's early critique of Hegel's philosophy of right, the 1859 Preface to A Contribution to the Critique of Political Economy, the Grundrisse and Capital.

Gao argues that Marx's starting judgement, that civil society determines the state, led him from criticising Hegel's theory of the state to analysing the mode of production of material life. In Capital, the author contends, Marx shows that the political and economic logics of modernity are apparently separate but in substance coupled. The formal uniformity of capitalist exchange grounds the modern political ideas of freedom, equality and ownership and also drives their undoing, since exchange-value develops into capital and labour into wage-labour. Gao also holds that Marx's political philosophy answers the problem of the age, 'individuals ruled by abstractions', which Marx treats as rule by capital, so that capital is a political as well as an economic concept.

Gao concludes that as long as individuals remain under the rule of capital, bringing out the contemporary content of Marx's political philosophy requires a return to Capital. Read the original if you want a compact statement, in the Chinese debate on Marx's political philosophy, of why Capital should be its textual basis.
quoteEn: Interpreting Marx's political philosophy on the basis of Capital is not a contingent expedient but a necessary logic inherent in the development and theoretical essence of Marx's political thought.
quoteZh: 基于《资本论》阐释马克思的政治哲学思想不是偶然的权宜之计,而是内在于马克思政治哲学思想的发展历程和理论本质的必然逻辑。

t: A view on the "transformation" and development of Marx's early thought
st: Centred on "On the Jewish Question" and the "Introduction to A Contribution to the Critique of Hegel's Philosophy of Right"
zh: 对马克思早期思想“转变”与发展的一点看法
zhSub: 以《论犹太人问题》和《〈黑格尔法哲学批判〉导言》为中心
source: Studies on Marxism-Leninism (马克思列宁主义研究), 2019 no. 2
paras: Chinese scholars have long disputed when Marx became a Marxist. The "one-transformation" view holds that Marx completed the shift from idealism to materialism and from revolutionary democracy to communism at the end of 1843. The "two-transformation" view holds that this was only a first step, to Feuerbachian humanism and "philosophical communism", with historical materialism and scientific communism reached in 1845–46. Sun and Wang argue that both frameworks should be set aside. They propose reading Marx through two viewpoints: his unchanging overall goal of proletarian and human emancipation, and the different historical tasks he faced at each stage.

The article focuses on \"On the Jewish Question\" and the \"Introduction to A Contribution to the Critique of Hegel's Philosophy of Right\", which the two-transformation camp criticises as immature and unscientific. It first identifies two methodological errors in existing scholarship. It then traces Marx's practical trajectory from 1837 to 1843: the Doctors' Club in Berlin, the Rheinische Zeitung, and Paris. A final section distinguishes the \"historical logic\" behind the texts from their \"textual logic\".

The authors' first move is to reject two habits: judging early works against the wording of later mature texts, and inferring a \"Feuerbach stage\" or \"Young Hegelian stage\" from borrowed terms and citations. They note that Althusser and McLellan use similar methods and reach opposite conclusions. They add that quoting a thinker does not mean sharing that thinker's stance. Second, they argue that Marx's practice changed his questions. In Paris, contact with the French workers' movement and with German workers led him to the concept of the modern proletariat. The authors say his earlier conclusion that civil society determines the state had become \"outdated\" for the new problem, and his political-economic critique of civil society was not yet developed. The abstract and speculative character of the two texts is therefore explained by this gap. Third, the texts appear to move logically from religion to proletarian revolution, but the authors say this is the condensed result of Marx's earlier practice. They read his remark to Ruge about smuggling in \"the greatest amount of rationality\" as showing that the Bauer critique was only an entry point.

Sun and Wang conclude that the tendency to belittle Marx's early works, or to set a young Marx against a mature one, is mistaken. They call for studying the development of his thought through the stages of his own practice, and for grasping its essence through the constancy of his goal. Marx's thought, in their account, was enriched and advanced over his life, not overturned. Read the original if you work on the periodisation of the young Marx, the one-transformation versus two-transformation debate in Chinese scholarship, or the reading of the Deutsch-Französische Jahrbücher texts.
quoteEn: The history of thought does not develop independently of the course of human social practice; its changes and development are bound to attach to changes and development in social and historical practice.
quoteZh: 思想史不会离开人类的社会实践的进程独立地发展,它的变化和发展一定是附着在社会历史实践的变化和发展之上的。

glossary.explanation: A position in Chinese scholarship that Marx completed his qualitative shift to materialism and communism at the end of 1843, with later change being only quantitative.
A position that the 1843 shift reached only Feuerbachian humanism and philosophical communism, and that a second shift to historical materialism and scientific communism came in 1845–46.
A label applied to Marx's communism in 1843–44, said to rest on abstract philosophical reasoning rather than scientific analysis of political economy.
The Marxist doctrine of communism grounded in historical materialism and political economy, as distinct from utopian or philosophical forms.

keywords: Critique of Hegel's Philosophy of Right

t: Capital and the internal logic of research on Marx's political philosophy
zh: 《资本论》与马克思政治哲学研究的内在逻辑
source: Chinese Social Sciences Today (Zhongguo shehui kexue bao), 26 July 2019
paras: Writing in 2019, Gao Guangxu asks in what sense Capital is an intellectual resource for Marx's political philosophy, a question the author treats as urgent for contemporary research in the field. The short commentary argues that Capital's critique of political economy is the logical result of the development of Marx's political philosophy, the logical precondition for advancing research on it, and the logical vehicle of its contemporary meaning.

The piece is organised in three sections, one for each of these claims. It moves from Marx's early critique of Hegel's philosophy of right, through Capital and the 1857–58 manuscripts, to the question of why Capital still matters in an age the author describes as one of individuals ruled by abstraction.

Gao holds that Marx's critique of Hegel led him to the judgement that civil society determines the state, which directed political philosophy toward the mode of production of material life and to the critique of political economy. In Gao's reading, Capital reveals that the political and economic logics of modernity are apparently separate but in substance coupled.
