The formal homogeneity of exchange grounds modern ideas of freedom, equality and ownership, yet also undermines them, because exchange-value must develop into capital and labour into wage-labour. Gao also argues that the buying and selling of labour-power is the 'Eden' of bourgeois political ideas, whose illusions are broken once labour-power is put to use. Capital is therefore a political concept as well as an economic one.

Gao concludes that basing the interpretation of Marx's political philosophy on Capital is a necessity arising from its development and nature, not an expedient. As long as individuals remain ruled by capital, the author says, showing the contemporary meaning of Marx's political philosophy requires a return to Capital. Read the original if you want a compact statement of the case for reading Marx's political philosophy through the critique of political economy.
quoteEn: Interpreting Marx's political philosophy on the basis of Capital is not a chance expedient, but a necessary logic inherent in the development and theoretical essence of Marx's political philosophy.
quoteZh: 基于《资本论》阐释马克思的政治哲学思想不是偶然的权宜之计,而是内在于马克思政治哲学思想的发展历程和理论本质的必然逻辑。

t: Upholding and applying the scientific method of historical materialism
zh: 历史唯物主义科学方法的坚持和运用
source: China Social Sciences Today (Zhongguo shehui kexue bao), 31 May 2019
paras: This short commentary, published in 2019, asks how Xi Jinping applies the scientific method of historical materialism to major questions of Chinese history. Yang argues that since the 18th Party Congress (2012), Xi has promoted study of historical materialism and used its method to answer historical nihilism. In Yang's account, historical nihilism denies the necessity of China's socialist path, the legitimacy of Communist Party leadership and the objectivity of the nation's modern struggle for rejuvenation.

The article is organised around three methodological moves it attributes to Xi. These are starting from objective social being in understanding socialism with Chinese characteristics; grasping the periods before and after reform and opening up through the connections of the "actual historical movement"; and assessing the Party's activities and its leaders historically and concretely. A short closing paragraph sums up the contribution of Xi's statements.

On the first point, Yang holds that understanding socialism with Chinese characteristics requires letting the history of world socialism, of modern China and of the Party "speak". World socialism's five centuries show conformity to historical law; China's 170-odd years of modern history show purposiveness; and the fate of Marxism is tied to that of the Party and nation. Socialism with Chinese characteristics is therefore neither accident nor pure idea. On the second, Yang follows Xi in treating the two periods as stages of a relay race with a shared goal, premise and essence, so that neither may be used to negate the other. On the third, historical figures must be placed in their conditions: leaders should be neither deified nor wholly rejected, and the Party's mistakes should be admitted, analysed and corrected.

Yang concludes that Xi's statements deepen understanding of historical materialist method, highlight the principle of seeking truth from facts and express the Party's firm stance against historical nihilism. The piece is a compact, official-line account of how Party theory frames the continuity of Chinese history and the evaluation of its leaders. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Chinese Party scholarship justifies the unity of the pre- and post-reform periods and answers historical nihilism in 2019.
quoteEn: Ignoring the inner connection between the periods before and after reform and opening up is in fact a disrespect for historical fact.
quoteZh: 忽视改革开放前后两个历史时期的内在联系，实际是对历史事实的不尊重。

glossary.explanation: A term used in Party discourse for views seen as denying or distorting the Party's history and the legitimacy of the socialist path. It is widely used in official campaigns from the 2010s onward.
The policy of economic reform and opening to the outside world launched in 1978, which the article treats as dividing the history of the People's Republic into two periods.
The official name for the Chinese Communist Party's path and system since the reform era.
A principle associated with Mao Zedong and Deng Xiaoping that stresses basing policy and judgement on actual conditions.

t: Capital and the internal logic of research on Marx's political philosophy
zh: 《资本论》与马克思政治哲学研究的内在逻辑
source: Chinese Social Sciences Today (Zhongguo shehui kexue bao), 26 July 2019
paras: Writing in a 2019 newspaper commentary, Gao Guangxu asks in what sense Capital is an intellectual resource for research on Marx's political philosophy. Gao argues that the critique of political economy in Capital is the logical result of the development of Marx's political philosophy, the logical precondition for further research, and the logical vehicle that brings out its meaning for our own era. Reading Marx's political philosophy through Capital is, on this view, a necessity rooted in its development and nature, not an expedient.

The piece is organised in three parts, one for each of these claims. It starts from Marx's early critique of Hegel's philosophy of right and state theory, moves to the analysis of commodity form and value in Capital, and ends with the problem of the age that Capital addresses.

Gao holds that Marx's early conclusion that civil society determines the state led him to the mode of production and then to political economy. Capital, as his most systematic work in that field, is therefore the endpoint and also the starting point for understanding this development. Gao further contends that Capital shows political and economic logic to be formally separate but substantively coupled. The formal homogeneity of exchange grounds modern ideas of freedom, equality and ownership, and also undermines them, as exchange-value becomes capital and labour becomes wage labour. Gao adds that the 'Eden' of the sphere of circulation gives way to relations of domination once labour-power is used, so that capital is a political concept as well as an economic one.

Gao concludes that Capital answers a political as well as an economic question, namely the condition of 'individuals ruled by abstractions', which Gao equates with rule by capital. As long as people live under this rule, Gao argues, work on the contemporary meaning of Marx's political philosophy must return to Capital. Read the original if you want a brief statement of the case for grounding Marx's political philosophy in the critique of political economy.
quoteEn: The critique of political economy in Capital is not only an answer to the economic problems of an age dominated by capital, but even more an answer to its political problems.
quoteZh: 《资本论》的政治经济学批判不仅是对资本占统治时代的经济问题的解答,更是对资本占统治时代的政治问题的解答。

t: Staying firm in the Four-sphere Confidence and strengthening national consensus
zh: 坚定“四个自信” 增强国家共识
paras: Writing in 2019, on the eve of the 70th anniversary of the People's Republic, Jiang Yingchun asks how the national consensus built around the Four-sphere Confidence (confidence in the path, theory, system and culture of socialism with Chinese characteristics) came about and how it can be strengthened. The author argues that this consensus is a "national treasure": the necessary conclusion of world socialist practice and of China's modern history, and an inexhaustible driving force for the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. The text is a short commentary in a Party theory journal.

The article is organised in three parts, each stating how the consensus was formed: it was "fought for" (奋斗出来的), "arrived at through comparison" (比较出来的) and "sustained through persistence" (坚持出来的). The first part reviews the struggle against poverty, the Party's self-reform and the struggle against world hegemonism. The second sets out how socialism and capitalism should be compared. The third turns to ideological work.

In the first part, Jiang presents China's elimination of absolute poverty as a miracle that rests on institutional, theoretical and cultural advantages, and contrasts the Party's capacity for self-correction with the Soviet Communist Party's loss of that capacity, which the author names as a key reason for its fall. The second part holds that comparison must start from concrete facts, from the "whole of the facts" and from the will of the people. Jiang criticises those who judge China by abstract notions of "democracy" or "constitutionalism", by isolated shortcomings, or by individual will. The author calls "wholesale Westernisation" idealist, and says only the people's will, which the Party serves, yields a correct judgement of socialism's superiority.

Jiang concludes that consensus has to be sustained by persistently combining Marxism's basic principles with Chinese realities. The author calls for stronger Marxist propaganda and education, scientific criticism of erroneous social trends (liberalism, individualism, capitalism set against Marxism, collectivism and socialism) and for building the Four-sphere Confidence into philosophy and social science, moral education of the young, and economic, political, social, cultural and ecological goals. Read the original if you want an example of how Party theorists in 2019 framed ideological consensus and the comparison of socialism with capitalism.
quoteEn: We can fully say that all the development and progress achieved by new China is the result of persistence, and that the Four-sphere Confidence is a national consensus born of persistence.
quoteZh: 我们完全可以说，新中国取得的一切发展和进步是坚持的结果，“四个自信”是坚持出来的国家共识。

glossary.explanation: Confidence in the path, theory, system and culture of socialism with Chinese characteristics. The formula was developed in Party discourse under Xi Jinping after 2012, with culture added to the earlier three confidences.
The official name for China's current political and economic system and its guiding theory, associated with the reform era since the late 1970s.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A central Party goal of restoring China to national strength and prosperity, closely tied to the Chinese Dream and to the 2049 centenary target.
The official idea that the Communist Party corrects its own errors and shortcomings through internal discipline and criticism, without external checks.
An official educational principle that makes the moral and ideological formation of students the fundamental task of schooling.

t: Revisiting Marx's ecological ethics
zh: 重温马克思生态伦理思想
paras: Marking the 200th anniversary of Marx's birth, Chen Aihua rereads Marx's Economic and Philosophic Manuscripts of 1844 for the ecological ethics it contains. The author argues that these ideas matter for building ecological ethics today. They are also presented as relevant to green development, the construction of ecological civilization and a "Beautiful China".

The short commentary, first published in China Social Sciences Today in 2018, is organised around three requirements for handling the human–nature relationship. These are attention to the inner connection between humans and nature, to labour (production) as life-engendering life, and to "construction in accordance with the laws of beauty". Chen weaves in passages from Xi Jinping, including the idea that humans and nature form a "community of life".

In Chen's reading, Marx treats nature as humanity's "inorganic body", on which people depend materially and spiritually. Drawing on Marx's comparison of animal and human production, Chen holds that human production should unite the "measure of any species" with humanity's "inherent measure". Chen links today's ecological predicament to capital's logic, which pursues only growth, and cites John Bellamy Foster and Engels on one-sided production. The "laws of beauty" are then taken at three levels: the unity of naturalism and humanism, the joining of philosophy and natural science, and a proper relation between industry, people and nature.

Chen concludes that industrial development must proceed alongside systematic ecological governance, the strictest environmental protection and green ways of production and life. The author presents this as the route to a Beautiful China and a contribution to global ecological security. Read the original if you want a brief example of how Chinese commentary ties the 1844 Manuscripts to Xi Jinping's ecological thought.
quoteEn: Looking back, the ecological predicament troubling humanity today is closely bound up with the \"inherent measure\" of economic growth alone, under the operation of capital's logic.
quoteZh: 反观当代困扰人类的生态窘境，都与资本逻辑的运作下只注重经济增长的“内在尺度”密切相关。

glossary.explanation: A Chinese policy concept, prominent since the 2010s, that places environmental protection alongside economic, political, cultural and social development.
A slogan from the 18th Party Congress (2012) for a country with a clean environment, tied to ecological civilization goals.
One of the five concepts of the new development philosophy announced in 2015, stressing harmony between development and the environment.

t: How to view China's economy and how to act: assessment and policy for 2019
zh: 中国经济怎么看、怎么干
authors: Party Leadership Group of the National Development and Reform Commission
paras: Written in mid-2019 by the Party leadership group of the National Development and Reform Commission and published in Qiushi, this commentary asks how China's economic trend should be read and what should be done, given a more complex situation and US–China trade friction. Its answer is that the economy is running generally steadily, that the difficulties are mainly structural and institutional, and that the central leadership has a coherent set of policies. The authors argue that China can sustain its course if it concentrates on 'doing its own things well'.

The text has three parts. The first reviews first-quarter and early-year data, including GDP growth of 6.4%, employment, industrial capacity utilisation, credit, high-tech investment, risk control, business-environment reforms and sentiment indicators. The second part names domestic and external problems and sets out the central government's overall approach. The third lists eight concrete measures, from macro policy to livelihood issues.

The authors present the central approach as six principles: seeking progress while maintaining stability as the general tone; high-quality development as the fundamental requirement; supply-side structural reform as the main line; a strong domestic market as the focus; reform, opening up and innovation as the drive; and seizing new opportunities. They say high-quality development needs 'five strengthenings' covering indicators, policy, standards, statistics and evaluation. The eight measures include coordinated fiscal, monetary and employment policy, firm vitality, innovation, a stronger domestic market, the three tough battles (risk, poverty, pollution), balanced urban-rural and regional development, deeper reform and wider opening, and livelihood problems. The authors suggest that a large domestic market is a safeguard against external disturbance.

The authors conclude that despite trade friction, China's economy has great potential and resilience, and its long-term positive trend will not change. They attribute recent results to the Party Central Committee's leadership and timely reform and opening-up policies. Read the original if you want an official statement of China's 2019 economic assessment and policy framework, with the data and measures the authorities cited.
quoteEn: As long as we concentrate on doing our own things well, then however the external environment changes, China's economy can move steadily and far along a path of stable, healthy and sustainable development.
quoteZh: 只要我们集中精力办好自己的事，无论外部环境怎么变化，我国经济都能在平稳健康可持续发展道路上行稳致远。

glossary.explanation: An official concept, prominent since 2017, that shifts the emphasis from the speed of growth to its quality, efficiency and sustainability.
A policy line launched in 2015 that aims to improve the supply structure, for example by cutting excess capacity and reducing leverage, rather than relying mainly on stimulating demand.
The general tone of China's economic work, balancing macroeconomic stability with reform and structural advance.

glossary.literal: three major battles to storm fortifications
glossary.explanation: The official priorities of preventing major financial risks, targeted poverty alleviation and pollution control.

t: The "two inevitables" remain the major trend of world development today
zh: “两个必然”仍然是当今世界发展的大趋势
paras: Writing in Red Flag Manuscripts (Hongqi Wengao) and posted in June 2019, Zhu Bingyuan asks whether the "two inevitables" (the inevitable demise of capitalism and the inevitable victory of socialism) still describe the direction of the world. The author argues that they do. In Zhu's view, neither the collapse of the Soviet Union and the upheavals in Eastern Europe nor the recent changes in Western capitalism have altered the historical trend of socialism replacing capitalism.

The article has three parts. The first sets out the theoretical content of the "two inevitables", from the Communist Manifesto through Capital to Marx and Engels's late writings on Russia. The second traces how the idea has developed in practice, from the First and Second Internationals and the October Revolution to the Chinese revolution and the post-1991 setback. The third looks at the present: financialisation and crisis in the West, and China's rise under socialism with Chinese characteristics.

Zhu first argues that the "two inevitables" should be read together with Marx's "two never-wills" from the 1859 Preface, which stress that a social formation does not perish before its productive forces are fully developed. The author treats the latter as a supplement that makes the thesis more complete, and sees Marx's late remarks on the Russian commune and the "Caudine Forks" of capitalism as extending it to Eastern societies. Second, drawing on Deng Xiaoping, Zhu presents the Soviet collapse as a temporary reversal in a complex historical process. Third, the author describes Western capitalism as marked by financialisation, hollowing out of the real economy, polarisation, populism and recurring crises (the US government shutdown, Brexit and the "yellow vests" are cited), which Zhu calls systemic and structural, so that its basic contradictions are said to be intensifying.

Zhu concludes that China's achievements under Communist Party leadership are the most persuasive proof of the "two inevitables", and that the proposal for a community with a shared future for mankind fits both the trend of the world and the varied conditions of individual countries. The article is a statement of the official line on the continuing validity of the classical thesis. Read the original if you want a compact example of how a Chinese Marxist scholar defends the "two inevitables" against the post-1991 setback and links them to Chinese modernization-era claims about China's global role.
quoteEn: The great achievements of the cause of socialism with Chinese characteristics are the most persuasive proof of the "two inevitables"!
quoteZh: 中国特色社会主义事业取得的伟大成就，是对“两个必然”最有说服力的证明！

glossary.explanation: A Chinese shorthand for Marx and Engels's conclusion that capitalism will inevitably perish and socialism will inevitably triumph. It generalises the Manifesto's wording that the fall of the bourgeoisie and the victory of the proletariat are "equally inevitable".

Marx's statement in the 1859 Preface that no social formation perishes before all the productive forces it can contain have developed, and that new relations of production never appear before their material conditions mature.
The official name for the Chinese Communist Party's path and system since reform and opening up, which presents it as socialism adapted to China's conditions.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: A foreign-policy concept promoted by Xi Jinping, calling for shared security, development and civilisational exchange among states.

t: Promoting quality and efficiency in the poverty alleviation campaign
zh: 推动脱贫攻坚提质增效
paras: Writing in 2019, as the campaign against poverty entered what Xi Jinping called its decisive stage, Wu Fenghua and Wu Zhenlei ask how poverty alleviation can be made more effective in its final two years. They argue that the remaining tasks concern the poorest of the poor and call for a shift from quantity to quality. They also present this shift as preparation for anti-poverty work after a moderately prosperous society is built.

This is a short commentary in a Party-theory journal. It sets out six "upgrades" in turn: the focus on quality of poverty reduction, the range of people targeted, the source of motivation, the balance between development-oriented and social-security measures, the pattern of participating actors, and the way assessments are conducted. Each section is anchored in statements by Xi Jinping from 2015 to 2019.

The authors first distinguish a static and a dynamic dimension of quality. The static one is securing "two assurances and three guarantees" for the rural poor by 2020. The dynamic one is preventing relapse into poverty through strict exit standards and "look-back" checks. They then argue for widening the targets to rural households slightly above the poverty line and to urban poor groups, including migrant workers. They also urge a move from externally driven to endogenous poverty alleviation, through motivation and education, and from state-led efforts to a "government–market–community–poor household" pattern under Party leadership. On the "five batches" approach, they hold that social-security support is rightly placed last. It should expand, but not blindly: exit mechanisms are needed, and those permanently unable to work should be supported throughout.

On assessment, the authors say that evaluations have become formalistic and burdensome for localities. They propose treating assessment as a means rather than an end, simplifying procedures, and building long-term mechanisms. Counties that have shed the poverty label should keep policy, assistance and supervision stable, to avoid a "cliff effect". Read the original if you want a concise, officially aligned account of how Chinese scholars framed the policy priorities of the final phase of the poverty campaign in 2019.
quoteEn: We must raise the quality of poverty alleviation along two dimensions, the static and the dynamic.
quoteZh: 要在静态、动态两个维度提高脱贫质量

glossary.explanation: The core standard of the poverty alleviation campaign: assurance of adequate food and clothing, plus guarantees of compulsory education, basic medical care and safe housing for rural poor people.
A framework sorting poor people by remedy: development of production, relocation, ecological compensation, education, and social security as a basic safety net.

glossary.literal: building a moderately prosperous society in all respects
glossary.explanation: A Party goal for the centenary of the Party's founding in 2021, of which eliminating poverty was a key part.

t: The historical foundations of cultural confidence in the new era
zh: 新时代文化自信的历史底蕴
paras: Writing in 2019, on the eve of the 70th anniversary of the People's Republic, Li Zheng asks where the cultural confidence of the new era comes from. The article answers that it rests on three historical layers: China's excellent traditional culture, the revolutionary culture led by the Communist Party, and the advanced socialist culture of the PRC's first 70 years. Together, Li argues, these form the "historical foundations" of the Chinese nation's cultural confidence.

The article is organised in three sections that follow this sequence. The first treats the 5,000-year inheritance of traditional "cultural genes", from the dragon totem through the Xia, Shang and Zhou dynasties, the Hundred Schools of thought, and the Han, Tang, Song, Yuan, Ming and Qing periods. The second covers the Party-led New Democratic revolution, the socialist revolution of 1949–1956, and 40 years of reform and opening up. The third turns to the "re-creation" of socialist culture in the new era.

Li's central move is to treat traditional culture as necessary but insufficient. It supplies, in Li's words, the theoretical possibility of confidence, but confidence also needs practical support. Li finds that support in three "cornerstones": the New Democratic revolution, the socialist transformation, and reform and opening up. Each is said to have restored confidence that was shattered when imperialist powers broke the "Celestial Empire" in modern times. In the third section Li presents confidence in the path, theory and system of socialism with Chinese characteristics as the culmination. Here Li lists the line of theory from Mao Zedong Thought to Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, and cites constitutional provisions on the Party's leadership and the basic economic system.

Li concludes that the re-creation of socialist culture in the path, theory and institutions of socialism with Chinese characteristics has raised the Chinese nation's cultural consciousness and strengthened its confidence in path, theory, system and culture. Li also presents the Chinese system as offering developing countries a new option for modernization. Read the original if you want an example of how a Party-school-style article in 2019 derived cultural confidence from a three-part periodisation of tradition, revolution and socialist construction.
quoteEn: Excellent traditional Chinese culture, revolutionary culture and advanced socialist culture together constitute the historical foundations of the Chinese nation's cultural confidence in the new era.
quoteZh: 中华优秀传统文化、革命文化和社会主义先进文化共同构成了新时代中华民族文化自信的历史底蕴。

glossary.explanation: A concept stressed in Party discourse under Xi Jinping, referring to confidence in the value and vitality of China's own culture. It is often added to confidence in the path, theory and system of socialism with Chinese characteristics.
A metaphor from biology for the enduring core elements of a culture that are passed down and reactivated across generations. The article uses it for traditional Chinese culture.
The official name for China's path since reform and opening up. It combines Party leadership, a socialist market economy and the Party's theoretical system.
The policy launched in 1978 that introduced market-oriented economic reforms and opened China to foreign trade and investment.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's guiding ideology associated with Xi Jinping, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017 and 2018.
Mao Zedong's term for the Chinese revolution from about 1919 to 1949, led by the Communist Party against imperialism, feudalism and bureaucrat-capitalism, as a stage before socialism.

t: Guarding the cultural roots of the Chinese nation with a high degree of cultural confidence
zh: 以高度文化自信守护中华民族文化根脉
paras: Writing in Qiushi in 2019, Liu Jiayi, then Party secretary of Shandong, reports on how the province has tried to act on Xi Jinping's instructions on traditional culture. Starting from Xi's 2013 visit to Qufu, Liu argues that cultural confidence is the deepest basis of confidence in China's path, theory and system, and that Shandong, as a cradle of traditional culture and revolutionary spirit, should become a model area for displaying it.

The article is a provincial work report organised in four parts. It treats cultural confidence as rooted in excellent traditional culture, inherited through the "red gene", shown in efforts to nurture values and build character, and strengthened through exchange and mutual learning among civilizations. Each part pairs quotations from Xi with concrete Shandong programmes and figures.

Liu's central claim is that Confucianism, as the main trunk of traditional culture, and the revolutionary culture embodied in the Yimeng spirit together supply the nation's cultural confidence. Shandong's measures include a Confucian scholars programme and the World Confucian Conference, research projects and online platforms on the Yimeng spirit, a provincial traditional-culture curriculum in primary, middle and high schools, and training bases for officials' political virtue. Liu also describes the Nishan World Civilizations Forum, Nishan Bookstores in 22 countries, Belt and Road cultural activities, and a 10-billion-yuan cultural industry fund. Liu says all this must proceed under Marxist guidance, against historical nihilism and against both clinging to the past and disparaging one's own culture.

Liu concludes that Shandong will keep to the principle of creative transformation and innovative development of traditional culture, drawing on China's own past, absorbing foreign influences and facing the future. The aim is to contribute to the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation and a new chapter of advanced socialist culture. Read the original if you want a detailed, officially framed example of how a provincial Party leadership turned national cultural policy into programmes in education, cadre training, tourism, media and international outreach.
quoteEn: Openness and inclusiveness are not only an expression of cultural confidence but, even more, a driving force of cultural prosperity.
quoteZh: 开放包容既是文化自信的表现，更是文化繁荣的动力。

glossary.explanation: A concept promoted by Xi Jinping, who describes it as a more fundamental confidence underlying confidence in China's path, theory and system. It is tied to appreciation of China's civilizational heritage.

glossary.zh: 创造性转化、创新性发展
glossary.explanation: A guideline for handling traditional culture, often shortened to "the Two Creations" (两创). It calls for adapting excellent traditional elements to present needs and giving them new forms.
A Party expression for the revolutionary ideals, spirit and traditions that are meant to be passed on to later generations.

A revolutionary spirit associated with the Yimeng old revolutionary base area in Shandong, summed up by Xi Jinping as "closeness like fish and water, sharing life and death" between the army and the people. It is counted within the Party's spiritual lineage.

t: Poverty reduction with Chinese characteristics, 1978–2018
st: An analysis from the perspective of the poverty governance system and governance capacity framework
zh: 中国特色减贫实践：1978—2018
zhSub: 基于贫困治理体系和治理能力分析框架视角
source: Studies on Mao Zedong and Deng Xiaoping Theories (Mao Zedong Deng Xiaoping lilun yanjiu), 2019
paras: Writing in 2019, Ma Wenwu and Li Zhongqiu ask how China's rural poverty reduction since reform and opening up (1978) can be explained and distilled into a distinctive path. They argue that the answer lies in a poverty governance system, built on a socialist value orientation, together with a steadily growing capacity to govern poverty. The article treats the achievement as a "world poverty reduction miracle" that needs theoretical as well as empirical summary.

The authors first set out a general framework. A poverty governance system has three parts: an anti-poverty value orientation, an institutional system, and anti-poverty action, which can be direct or indirect. Governance capacity is the ability of government-led actors to confront and eliminate poverty, tested by actual changes in poverty. They then apply the framework to China's experience from 1978 to 2018, and end with poverty figures and proposals for the future.

Ma and Li describe three features of China's value orientation: a people-centred character, an emergency-relief ("救急") emphasis on the worst-off people and regions, and a developmental character that adjusts goals over time. Their account of the institutions covers a leading-group structure under the State Council, rural reforms of land, grain circulation and household registration, four successive planning stages from 1982 to 2020, and supporting fiscal, social security, responsibility and mobilisation policies. In action, targeting narrowed from the whole countryside to counties, villages and households. The authors credit strict assessment and accountability, the "Six Precisions" and the "Five Batches" for how aid is delivered. They cite UN and World Bank figures and report that, on the current standard, the poverty rate fell from 97.5% in 1978 to 3.1% at the end of 2017.

The authors conclude that success came from forming and improving a poverty governance system with Chinese characteristics. They expect that after 2020 the focus will shift to consolidating gains, preventing relapse, and moving from absolute to relative and multidimensional poverty. They propose three priorities: a national anti-poverty law, a governance system specific to ethnic-minority areas, and a more detailed poverty-standard system linked to economic development. Read the original if you want a systematic, officially aligned periodisation of China's anti-poverty policies and institutions from 1978 to 2018, with the policy documents and data that support it.
quoteEn: An important reason why China's rural anti-poverty work has succeeded is that we have formed and increasingly improved a poverty governance system with Chinese characteristics, and our poverty governance capacity has markedly increased.
quoteZh: 我国农村反贫困能够取得胜利的重要原因，在于我们形成和日益完善了中国特色贫困治理体系，贫困治理能力显著提升。

glossary.explanation: Requirements for targeted poverty alleviation, as the article lists them: precise targeting of recipients, project arrangement, use of funds, household-level measures, assignment of officials by village, and assessment of results.
Five routes out of poverty: developing production, relocation, ecological compensation, education, and social security as a last safety net.

t: On the innovation and development of the thought of building a modern socialist great power
zh: 论社会主义现代化强国思想的创新和发展
source: Journal of Ideological and Theoretical Education (思想理论教育导刊), 2019
paras: Writing in 2019, the 70th anniversary of the People's Republic, Shi Yunxia asks what is new in the goal set at the 19th Party Congress (2017) of building China into a "prosperous, democratic, culturally advanced, harmonious and beautiful modern socialist great power" by the middle of this century. Shi argues that this "great power" thought continues earlier Party thinking while advancing it. In the author's view it is a major theoretical innovation in scientific socialism, joining the theoretical logic of scientific socialism with the historical logic of Chinese social development.

The article is organised in five sections. Four trace how the thought deepens understanding of the stages of socialist development, the essential features of socialism, the scientific content of socialist modernization, and the Marxist theory of the state. These sections follow a line from Marx and Engels through Lenin, Stalin, Mao Zedong, Deng Xiaoping, Jiang Zemin and Hu Jintao to Xi Jinping. A final section turns to reform and opening up as the road to national strength.

On stages, Shi sets Lenin's and Mao's ideas of a less developed and a more developed socialism beside Deng's judgement that China is in the primary stage of socialism. Shi presents the 19th Congress timetable (basic modernization by 2035, a great power by mid-century) as the latest step in this line. On essence, Shi reads the five-part goal as extending Deng's formula of liberating and developing the productive forces toward common prosperity. On modernization, Shi argues that its deeper meaning is the modernization of the human being, linked to Marx's three stages of human development. On the state, Shi contends that Lenin's argument in The State and Revolution about the persistence of a state in the first phase of communism lays the ground for Xi's account of what kind of country China is, which the author says rebuts "China threat" theories.

Shi concludes that reform and opening up is the "key move" for achieving the Two Centenary Goals and the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. The author reviews the Third Plenum of the 18th Central Committee (2013) and Xi's 2018 speech marking forty years of reform, with its nine "musts", and holds that all of them come down to Party leadership. Read the original if you want a Party-theory account that places the modern socialist great power goal within a genealogy running from Marx and Lenin to Xi Jinping.
quoteEn: The modernization of the human being reveals a deeper essential meaning of socialist modernization, and enriches and develops the Marxist theory of social development.
quoteZh: 人的现代化——这是对社会主义现代化更深刻的本质内涵的揭示，是对马克思主义社会发展理论的丰富和发展。

glossary.explanation: The goal set at the 19th Party Congress (2017) of making China a prosperous, democratic, culturally advanced, harmonious and beautiful modern socialist country by the middle of the 21st century.
A Party judgement, associated with Deng Xiaoping after 1978, that China is in a long initial period of socialism marked by underdeveloped productive forces.
Official goals of building a moderately prosperous society by the Party's centenary (2021) and a modern socialist country by the centenary of the People's Republic (2049).

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A central official slogan, central to the Chinese Dream, for restoring China's national strength and international standing.
The policy course launched at the Third Plenum of the 11th Central Committee (1978), introducing market-oriented reforms and engagement with the world economy.

t: A community with a shared future for mankind offers Chinese wisdom for building a new world order
zh: 人类命运共同体为打造世界新秩序提供中国智慧
paras: Writing in Red Flag Manuscripts in 2019, Wang and Huang argue that Xi Jinping's idea of building a community with a shared future for mankind is a new concept that the Chinese Communist Party has contributed to contemporary humanity. In their account it expresses Chinese wisdom about world order and offers a Chinese approach to a more rational one.

The short commentary has four sections. It treats the idea as a new concept of world order, then as a set of fundamental stipulations about that order. It next presents the idea as a new yardstick for assessing global governance, and finally as a goal for human interaction.

The authors place the concept against the backdrop of "changes unseen in a century" and trace it to the Party's engagement in global governance since the 18th Party Congress (2012). They describe it as the product of combining traditional Chinese wisdom with Marxism. They argue that it rests on a scientific understanding of interdependence among nations and that its values aim at the happiness of all humanity, not at particular states. As a yardstick, they say, it means mutual respect, fairness and justice, and win-win cooperation. It rejects Cold War thinking and power politics, favours dialogue over confrontation and partnership over alliance, and holds that international rules should be written jointly by all countries.

The authors link the goal to the classical Chinese ideal of "all under heaven being for the common good" and to Marx's "association of free individuals". They conclude that it points toward a world of lasting peace, universal security, common prosperity, openness and inclusiveness, and cleanliness and beauty. They add that it will take generations to achieve. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party-affiliated scholars in 2019 presented this concept as a synthesis of Chinese tradition and Marxism.
quoteEn: This idea, which faces the whole globe and all humanity and is formed for the common interests and happiness of all, is the best ideological guide for contemporary humanity to escape governance dilemmas and crises, and in its practical aspect it supplies a new, realistic yardstick for assessing present global governance.
quoteZh: 这种面向全球和全体人类，并为了全人类的共同利益和幸福而形成的理念，是当代人类走出治理困境和危机的最好意识引领，在其现实性上为当下全球治理提供新的现实评估标尺。

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: A concept associated with Xi Jinping since the early 2010s, presented as China's vision for international relations and global governance based on cooperation and shared interests.

glossary.pinyin: bǎi nián wèi yǒu zhī dà biànjú
glossary.literal: great changes not seen in a hundred years
glossary.explanation: An official phrase used by Xi Jinping to describe the shifting global balance of power and rapid international change.
The management of transnational problems and international rules; in Chinese official discourse, a field in which China says it seeks a larger and more equitable role.

keywords: community with a shared future for mankind

t: The Communist Manifesto and the original aspiration and mission of Chinese communists
zh: 《共产党宣言》与中国共产党人的初心和使命
source: Journal of Ideological and Theoretical Education (思想理论教育导刊)
paras: Writing in 2019, Huang Rongsheng asks how the Communist Manifesto of 1848 bears on the "original aspiration and mission" of Chinese communists. The article argues that the Manifesto supplies the theoretical foundation and the guide to action for that aspiration and mission, and that its value remains undiminished in the new era of socialism with Chinese characteristics.

The article is organised in four sections. The first presents the Manifesto as the founding text of Marxism and of Marxist parties, and recounts how Lenin, Mao Zedong, Deng Xiaoping and Xi Jinping developed or applied it. The second traces how it guided the Party through revolution, construction and reform. The third examines the commitment to seek happiness for "the vast majority". The fourth turns to the Party's responsibility to pursue the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation.

In the core of the argument, Huang reads specific Manifesto propositions as having been put into practice by the Party. The historical-materialist claim that economic structure underlies political history is linked to the Party's choice of an "encircle the cities from the countryside" path, to the basic economic system of public ownership as the mainstay, and to the new development philosophy since the 18th Party Congress (2012). Its call for a decisive break with traditional ideas is tied to the Party's campaigns of ideological education, and its description of communists as the most resolute section of workers' parties is tied to Party-building and the work against corruption. The Manifesto's declaration that the proletarian movement is that of the immense majority is presented as the origin of the Party's people-centred stance and of its progress from "standing up" to "becoming prosperous" to "becoming strong".

Huang concludes that the Party's pledge to seek happiness for the Chinese people and rejuvenation for the Chinese nation inherits and develops the Manifesto's original aspiration. The article calls on present-day communists to keep to the communist ideal, the common ideal of socialism with Chinese characteristics and the Chinese Dream, and to stay true to their founding purpose. Read the original if you want an example of how Party-aligned scholarship in 2019 tied the Manifesto to the Party's "original aspiration and mission" theme.
quoteEn: The Communist Manifesto has provided a solid theoretical foundation and a guide to action for the Chinese communists' original aspiration and mission in exploring the practice of socialist modernization.
quoteZh: 《共产党宣言》为中国共产党人的初心和使命探索社会主义现代化建设的实践提供了坚实的理论基础和行动指南。

glossary.explanation: A Party slogan, prominent in 2019 in the campaign of study and education on the theme "staying true to the original aspiration and keeping the mission in mind". It is defined in the article as seeking happiness for the Chinese people and rejuvenation for the Chinese nation.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The official goal of restoring China's national strength and international standing, closely associated with Xi Jinping's Chinese Dream.
The official guideline of innovative, coordinated, green, open and shared development, put forward by the Party leadership after 2012.
A slogan associated with Xi Jinping since 2012, centred on national rejuvenation and people's well-being.

t: The precious spiritual legacy of the May Fourth Movement and its contemporary inheritance
zh: 五四运动的宝贵精神财富及其当代传承
paras: Published in Guangming Daily on the eve of the movement's centenary, this commentary asks what the May Fourth Movement of 1919 left as a spiritual legacy and how that legacy should be carried forward today. Taking its cue from Xi Jinping's call to study the movement within a "big view of history", the author argues that the May Fourth spirit of patriotism, progress, democracy and science is closely tied to the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation and must be inherited in the new era.

The piece is organised in three sections and adopts a history-of-ideas perspective. The first treats the movement as the outcome of modern China's efforts to save the nation and traces patriotism from the Paris Peace Conference to later commemorations. The second places the movement within a sequence of attempts to learn from the West and shows how it led to Marxism. The third turns to present-day implications.

In the author's account, patriotism is the first element of the May Fourth spirit. The diplomatic defeat at Paris, in which Shandong rights were handed to Japan, ended illusions about Western powers and moved advanced Chinese towards the new-democratic revolution. The author argues that the New Culture Movement had not completed the task of enlightenment, because its thinkers still trusted the victorious powers and relied on Enlightenment-era Western theory. Earlier efforts, from Lin Zexu to Sun Yat-sen, followed a logic of learning technology, theory and institutions from the West but found no workable revolutionary programme. The October Revolution brought Marxism-Leninism, and the author calls the finding of Marxism the greatest result of the movement's intellectual emancipation, preparing the ground for the founding of the Communist Party.

For the new era, the author calls for patriotism guided by Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, unwavering adherence to Marxism and Party leadership, and a people-centred approach to development. Young people, the author says, need political guidance to follow the Party and to link personal ideals to the Chinese Dream of national rejuvenation. Read the original if you want an example of how a 2019 official-academic text ties the May Fourth legacy to Party narrative and youth work.
quoteEn: The greatest result of this intellectual emancipation was that the Chinese people found Marxism.
quoteZh: 这次思想解放的最大成果，就是中国人找到了马克思主义。

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A leading official goal of restoring China's national strength and international standing after the 'century of humiliation'.
A slogan promoted by Xi Jinping since 2012, identified with national rejuvenation and people's well-being.
Mao Zedong's term for the Party-led, anti-imperialist and anti-feudal revolution in China, seen as preceding the socialist revolution.

t: Carrying forward the May Fourth spirit and creating new miracles
zh: 传承五四精神 再创伟大奇迹
paras: Writing in 2019, the centenary of the May Fourth Movement and the 70th anniversary of the People's Republic, Gao Xiang argues that a century of Chinese history offers lessons for starting a still more glorious course and creating still greater achievements. The commentary holds that the May Fourth spirit remains vital and that the Communist Party's leadership is the thread running through the period.
The piece has three parts. It first discusses the content of the May Fourth spirit, then identifies three landmark events since 1919, and finally draws lessons from the hundred years.

Gao defines the May Fourth spirit as patriotism, progress, democracy and science, and says it has taken on new meaning in pursuit of the Chinese Dream. The three events are the founding of the Party (1921), the founding of the People's Republic (1949), and reform and opening up with socialism with Chinese characteristics. Gao describes the last as a leap from standing up to becoming prosperous and then strong, and calls the new era a golden age for the nation. From this history the author draws three conclusions: Party leadership is the fundamental political guarantee of national rejuvenation; Sinicised Marxism is its scientific guide; and rejuvenation requires struggle and innovation.

Gao calls for the Party's ideological line, bold exploration and rejection of dogmatism, since China's modernization has no textbook to follow. The author presents Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era as twenty-first-century Marxism that will guide the building of a modern socialist country. Read the original if you want a concise example of how a senior CASS leader framed the May Fourth centenary in official terms.
quoteEn: Sinicised Marxism is the scientific guide for realising the great rejuvenation of the Chinese nation.
quoteZh: 中国化马克思主义是实现中华民族伟大复兴的科学指南。

glossary.explanation: A slogan popularised by Xi Jinping from 2012, equating the Dream with national rejuvenation and the people's well-being.
The policy of economic reform and opening to the outside world begun in 1978 under Deng Xiaoping.
The Party's official name for its model of socialism, combining Party leadership with a market-oriented economy, developed since reform and opening up.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's guiding ideology associated with Xi Jinping, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018.

t: The historical significance and contemporary value of the May Fourth Movement
zh: 五四运动的历史意义和时代价值
paras: Marking the centenary of the May Fourth Movement in 2019, Dong Xuewen asks what the movement meant historically and what value it holds for today's Chinese youth. The article, first published in Red Flag Manuscripts (Hongqi Wengao), argues that the movement's decisive achievement was to open the door to Marxism in China, and that this, more than any other factor, gave it a pioneering place in modern Chinese intellectual history.

Dong organises the essay in six short sections. It begins with Mao Zedong's and Xi Jinping's characterisations of the movement as an anti-imperialist, anti-feudal patriotic movement. It then discusses its significance for Chinese thought and the founding of the Communist Party, and compares the periods before and after 1919 in Mao's account of the cultural front. A section on the cultural debates of the era is followed by a discussion of what "science" and "democracy" meant, and a closing section addresses the lessons for young people in the new era.

Dong's central claim is that earlier struggles, from the Sino-Japanese War of 1894–95 to the 1911 Revolution, failed because they lacked an advanced worldview. In this account, the May Fourth Movement differed because intellectuals such as Li Dazhao, Chen Duxiu and Qu Qiubai turned to Marxism and took it to the workers, preparing the ground for the Party's founding in 1921. Dong holds that conservatives, advocates of wholesale Westernisation such as Hu Shi, and eclectics such as Liang Qichao all chose cultural directions that did not match China's social and economic trends. Only the early communists, in this reading, offered a viable blueprint. The author adds that the common shorthand of "science and democracy" hides sharp disagreements. In Dong's view, only the early communists gave these slogans real substance, through historical materialism and socialist democracy.

Dong concludes that the founding of the Party, the People's Republic and reform and opening up all show the victory of Marxism in China. The author invokes Xi Jinping's call for young people to carry on the May Fourth spirit under Party leadership and Mao's phrase "permanent struggle" as the youth movement's tradition. Dong presents the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation as demanding greater effort, guided by Marxist belief. Read the original if you want an example of how the May Fourth Movement was interpreted in official Party commentary on its 2019 centenary, with extensive quotation from Mao and Xi.
quoteEn: If the achievement of the May Fourth Movement were summed up in one sentence, it is that it opened up and pushed China's anti-imperialist, anti-feudal bourgeois-democratic revolution into a new stage.
quoteZh: 五四运动的功绩，倘用一句话来概括，那就是开启并推动中国反帝反封建的资产阶级民主革命进入到了新阶段。

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.literal: great revival of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A central Party slogan describing the goal of restoring China to national strength and prosperity. It has been closely associated with Xi Jinping's leadership since 2012.
The values the Party attributes to the 1919 movement. Xi Jinping lists them as patriotism, progress, democracy and science.
The policy of economic reform and engagement with the outside world launched in 1978 under Deng Xiaoping.

t: Mao Zedong's foundational contributions to New China's economic construction in 1949
zh: 1949年毛泽东对新中国经济建设的几个奠基性贡献
source: Studies on Mao Zedong and Deng Xiaoping Theories, 2019 no. 2
paras: Written for the 70th anniversary of the People's Republic in 2019, this article asks what laid the foundations for China's later economic development. Yang Dongquan answers that, in 1949, Mao Zedong made several foundational contributions to New China's economic construction, and that anyone studying the "Chinese path" or "Chinese model" cannot bypass them.

The article draws on Mao's 1949 telegrams, speeches, instructions and drafts, arranged in three parts. The first covers the unified domestic environment: the New Year message "Carry the Revolution Through to the End", the exposure of the Guomintang's "peace talks", the failed April negotiations and the crossing of the Yangtze. The second covers the political institutions: the political consultation system, the people's congress system and regional autonomy for ethnic minorities. The third covers the shift of the Party's work focus to cities and to economic construction, with policies on city takeover, the national bourgeoisie, North–South trade links and land reform.

Yang argues that rejecting a "divide the country at the Yangtze" settlement preserved a unified territory of 9.6 million square kilometres, with its resources, population and market. Without it, in the author's view, rival regimes would have wasted resources on arms races and been open to foreign manipulation. The political institutions, Yang says, were shown by decades of experience to be suited to China and to protect and promote economic growth. The author also reads Mao's 1949 instructions as an early statement of "taking economic construction as the centre". Examples include the March 1949 report to the Second Plenum of the 7th Central Committee, which moved the focus from countryside to city, and the telegram saying that future work centres on construction. Further examples are limiting war damage to cities, keeping existing staff employed in newly taken cities, the "four-sided and eight-directional" policy, protecting national industry and commerce, and cautious land reform that protected rich peasants.

Yang concludes that these measures gave the new state a unified environment, reliable institutions, preserved urban capital and a good start to economic recovery. By 1953, the author says, land reform had given over 300 million peasants some 700 million mu of land. Yang presents these 1949 decisions as the origin of later achievements and as an explanation for China's development. Read the original if you want a Party-historian's account, based on Mao's 1949 documents, of how the PRC's early economic policy is traced back to its founding year.
quoteEn: The raising and realisation of the idea of "carrying the revolution through to the end" not only enabled the Communist Party to defeat the Guomintang swiftly and establish people's power nationwide, but also achieved the unification of mainland China.
quoteZh: “将革命进行到底”这一思想的提出和实现，不仅使中国共产党迅速战胜了国民党，在全国范围内建立起人民的政权，而且实现了中国大陆的统一。

glossary.en: Carry the Revolution Through to the End
glossary.explanation: Title of Mao Zedong's New Year message of 1 January 1949, which rejected a negotiated halt to the civil war. The Party presented it as a call to defeat the Guomintang completely.

China's basic political system, in which congresses at each level are the organs of state power. The article says Mao backed it from 1948 as democratic centralism, in place of a bourgeois parliamentary system.

The system of consultation between the Communist Party, other parties and social groups, institutionalised through the Chinese People's Political Consultative Conference, first convened in September 1949.
The PRC's system of autonomous areas for minority nationalities within a unitary state. The 1949 Common Program adopted it in preference to a federal system based on self-determination.

glossary.en: Second Plenum of the 7th Central Committee
glossary.explanation: The Party meeting at Xibaipo in March 1949, at which Mao announced the shift of the Party's work focus from the countryside to the cities.

t: Exploring an organised rural governance strategy based on China's national conditions
st: Rethinking Mao Zedong's thought and practice of rural governance
zh: 探索基于中国国情的组织化农治战略
zhSub: 毛泽东农治思想与实践探索再思考
source: Studies on Mao Zedong and Deng Xiaoping Theories, 2019 no. 1
paras: Writing in 2019, as rural revitalization became a national strategy, Xu Junzhong asks how Mao Zedong's rural governance (nongzhi) should be reassessed after decades of reform-era criticism. The article argues that, given China's many people, scarce land and backward farming conditions, Mao's strategy of 'organising the peasants' was the only workable path. Xu holds that the difficulties of the collective period came from specific policy constraints, not from organisation as such.

The article follows Mao's strategy chronologically. It begins with the Yan'an model of the 1940s and Mao's pre-1949 statements on cooperation, then covers the cooperativisation wave of the mid-1950s through the compilation 'The Socialist Upsurge in China's Countryside' and the 1956–67 National Programme for Agricultural Development. It then treats the people's communes, and Mao's efforts in the 1960s and 1970s to defend commune and brigade enterprises. Later sections draw out five features of Mao's approach and answer current criticisms.

Xu argues that Mao treated 'many people, little land' as a resource to be mobilised through cooperation, intensive farming and diversified activity, including local industry. Mao's aim was in-situ industrialisation and urbanisation that would avoid both the Soviet collective farm and the Western path of rural decline. The five features Xu identifies are: governance subordinated to national strategy; organisation as the foundation; combining agriculture and industry; the peasants as the main actors; and peasant emancipation and improved living standards as the core value. Against the liberal 'right of exit' critique, Xu says peasants holding about three mu (roughly 0.2 hectares) each could not stand alone as independent producers, so such a right would leave them helpless. The real causes of the collective period's difficulties, in Xu's account, were the 1962 ban on commune enterprises and the 'de-commercialisation' produced by state monopoly purchase and marketing.

Xu concludes that Mao's strategy was an exploratory, trial-and-error effort whose flaws should be corrected as repair rather than dismantling. Citing Xi Jinping, Xu argues that today's smallholders still cannot join modern industrial chains or markets because they lack organisation. Effective rural governance in the new era, Xu says, requires combining organisation with marketisation. Read the original if you want a detailed, source-based defence of Mao-era rural collectivism and its relevance to rural revitalization debates.
quoteEn: The difficulties of the organised rural governance strategy did not come from organisation itself, but from policy constraints under specific historical conditions.
quoteZh: 组织化的农治战略的困境，并非来自于组织化本身，而是来自于特定历史条件下的政策约束。

glossary.explanation: The author's term for the overall management of agriculture, villages and peasants, extending beyond farm production to peasants' livelihoods and ways of life.
Mao Zedong's slogan, associated with his 1943 Yan'an speech, for gathering scattered smallholders into mutual-aid and cooperative bodies.
Large rural units set up in 1958 that combined economic management and local government and ran farming, industry, commerce, education and militia. They were dissolved after the reform period began.
A policy introduced in 1953 under which the state purchased key farm products, such as grain, at fixed prices and quantities and controlled their distribution.
Small industrial and sideline enterprises run by communes and production brigades, which later developed into township and village enterprises.
A national strategy announced at the 19th Party Congress (2017) to promote rural development and narrow urban–rural gaps.

t: Schools of socialism in the May Fourth period
zh: 五四时期的社会主义流派
paras: Mei Le asks how Marxism came to overtake other currents and become the dominant influence on Chinese thinkers after the May Fourth New Culture Movement. The short commentary argues that the answer lies largely in how rival socialisms circulated and competed in the press and in public debate during that period.

The article surveys the schools of socialism then circulating: Marxism, Guild Socialism, syndicalism, the New Village movement, cooperativism, pan-labourism, anarchism and state socialism. It then looks at two famous controversies, the 1919 debate on "problems and isms" and the socialism debate that began in 1920.

Mei notes that most schools were short-lived; besides Marxism, only Guild Socialism and anarchism had wide influence. Contemporaries, including Chen Duxiu and Zhang Dongsun, counted anarchism and state socialism as socialism, and understanding of the term was both vague and over-extended; Qu Qiubai likened it to looking at dawn mist through a gauze window. Even so, Mei says many, Marxists included, already saw Marxism as "scientific socialism". In the "problems and isms" exchange between Hu Shi and Li Dazhao, Mei argues, the limits of studying only "problems" became clear, and talk of "isms" grew. In the larger debate between Chen Duxiu and Zhang Dongsun, who openly backed Guild Socialism, the author sees the first real contest between schools. Chen's side held that capitalism's fall and socialism's rise were the world trend, and questions such as whether a capitalist stage could be skipped pushed Marxists to think in terms of national conditions.

Mei concludes that these controversies drew more people to socialism and turned it into a wave of enthusiasm, and that they helped Marxism's growing influence. The author holds that revisiting this history remains necessary. Read the original if you want a brief overview of the socialist currents and debates of 1919–1920 as presented in a Party newspaper.
quoteEn: Competition often existed among the various schools of socialism, and this competition mostly took the form of debates and polemics.
quoteZh: 社会主义各派别之间往往存在竞争的一面，而这种竞争又多是以辩论、论争的形式出现。

glossary.literal: Guild socialism (also rendered 行会社会主义, 工行的社会主义)
glossary.explanation: A British-originated current favouring worker-run guilds in industry. In China it was advocated in the early 1920s by Zhang Dongsun and others in opposition to Marxism.

glossary.literal: the dispute over problems and isms
glossary.explanation: A 1919 exchange between Hu Shi and Li Dazhao over whether to concentrate on concrete social problems or on doctrines such as socialism.
The term for Marxist socialism, distinguished in Marxist usage from other, so-called utopian or non-scientific, socialisms.

t: The Communist Party of China as the undeniable mainstay of the War of Resistance against Japan
zh: 中国共产党是无可非议的抗战中流砥柱
paras: Writing in Jiefang Daily in September 2018, Zhang Yun argues that, among the many domestic and international causes of victory in the War of Resistance against Japan, the Communist Party of China (CPC) was the "mainstay" (zhongliu dizhu) that held firm amid the storm. Zhang presents this as a response to online claims that, once the Nationalist-led frontal battlefield is assessed objectively, the Party's contribution can be belittled or denied. The author labels such claims historical nihilism and promises firm historical facts to refute them.

The commentary is organised under four headings. The first counts the Party's public anti-Japanese statements between 1931 and 1945. The second traces the Party's shifting line towards the Nationalists and the formation of the Anti-Japanese National United Front. The third describes how the Party dealt with Nationalist diehards, and the fourth reviews the armed struggle behind Japanese lines.

Zhang's first move is a self-described rough count: the Party issued 290 formal anti-Japanese positions over 14 years, 97 during the six years of partial war and 193 during the eight years of full-scale war. Zhang reads this as proof of an unwavering stance, in contrast to the Nationalist policy of non-resistance. The second move traces the policy shift from "oppose Chiang and resist Japan" to "pressure Chiang" and then "ally with Chiang". Zhang attributes it to Japan's growing aggression, the Comintern's Seventh Congress and changes in Nationalist and Soviet policy. Faced with three anti-Communist upsurges between 1939 and 1943, including the 1941 Southern Anhui Incident, the Party held the front together by the principle of struggles that are "justified, advantageous and restrained". Zhang's third move is military. Guerrilla warfare, in the author's account, dragged Japan into a protracted quagmire and made the rear-area battlefield the strategic main battlefield. The author cites 125,000 engagements, 1.713 million Japanese and puppet troops eliminated, 19 base areas, and 58–75 per cent of the Japanese invaders resisted from the stalemate stage.

Zhang concludes that, while the Nationalist frontal battlefield fought 22 major campaigns without halting the Japanese advance, the Party's rear-area battlefield created a "vast ocean" in which the enemy was trapped. In this reading the Party was an indisputable mainstay and a beacon of hope for the Chinese people. Read the original if you want to see how a 2018 Party-press commentary uses wartime statistics and United Front history to rebut revisionist assessments of the Party's role in the war.
quoteEn: It can thus be seen that the Communist Party of China was the key and decisive factor in the victory of the War of Resistance.
quoteZh: 可见，中国共产党是抗战胜利的关键性、决定性因素。

glossary.explanation: In official Chinese discourse, a label for views seen as denying or distorting the Party's revolutionary history and achievements. Critics of the term say it can be used to close off scholarly debate.
The broad political alliance, centred on Nationalist–Communist cooperation, formed in the late 1930s to resist Japan. The CPC promoted it from 1935 onwards.

glossary.literal: a rock pillar in the midstream
glossary.explanation: An idiom for a steadfast force that stands firm in turbulent times. In Party historiography it describes the CPC's role in the War of Resistance.
The January 1941 attack by Nationalist forces on the headquarters of the CPC-led New Fourth Army. It was the most serious crisis in Nationalist–Communist cooperation during the war.

t: The threefold meaning of inheriting and promoting revolutionary culture in the new era
zh: 新时代传承弘扬革命文化的三重意涵
paras: This short commentary, first published in Guangming Daily on 3 August 2018, asks what it means to inherit and promote revolutionary culture in the new era. Liu defines revolutionary culture as the cultural form created by the Communist Party and the people during the revolutionary years. The article argues that it has three meanings, and that it must be grasped in all three.

The piece is organised in three short sections. Each takes one function of revolutionary culture: as a foundation of cultural confidence, as a historical resource for consolidating the Party's governing base, and as a source of guidance for the people's spiritual home. Liu draws on statements by Xi Jinping, Deng Xiaoping and Mao Zedong, and on the Party's early rules of conduct.

On cultural confidence, Liu argues that revolutionary culture supplies spiritual nourishment, through the ideals and convictions of revolutionary forebears, and theoretical depth, because it is a result of adapting Marxism to Chinese conditions. On governance, the author holds that the mass-line experience it carries, such as the disciplines of the Jinggangshan period, offers lessons for the people-centred development philosophy and for keeping close ties between Party and people. On spiritual life, Liu notes that reform and opening up has improved material life but has also brought loss of belief, spiritual slackness and moral decline. Revolutionary culture, the article contends, shows a life of conviction under harsh conditions and can help people rebuild their spiritual world.

Liu concludes that revolutionary culture is a source of confidence, a historical resource for the Party's rule and a practical inspiration for contemporary spiritual life. The text is a brief, programmatic statement in the official register of the 19th Party Congress (2017). Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party-affiliated writing in 2018 justified the continuing relevance of revolutionary culture.
quoteEn: The formation of revolutionary culture cannot be separated from the guidance of Marxism; its core elements inherit Marxism's basic viewpoints, and it will surely provide a scientific theoretical foundation for strengthening cultural confidence in the new era.
quoteZh: 革命文化的形成离不开马克思主义的指导，其核心要素承继了马克思主义的基本观点，必将为新时代坚定文化自信提供科学的理论底蕴。

glossary.explanation: The culture created under Communist Party leadership during the revolutionary struggle. Official discourse treats it as one of three components of Chinese socialist culture, alongside excellent traditional Chinese culture and advanced socialist culture.
A concept stressed by Xi Jinping, meaning confidence in the value and vitality of China's own culture. It is presented as underlying the broader confidence in the Chinese path.
The official idea that Marxism must be combined with China's concrete realities and culture, producing theoretical results such as Mao Zedong Thought.

glossary.zh: 以人民为中心的发展思想
glossary.pinyin: yǐ rénmín wéi zhōngxīn de fāzhǎn sīxiǎng
glossary.explanation: A formulation in Xi Jinping-era Party discourse holding that development should aim at the people's wellbeing and rely on the people.

t: Mao Zedong and the mass line of the Communist Party of China
zh: 毛泽东与中国共产党的群众路线
source: Paper in Mao Zedong and the Great Rejuvenation of the Chinese Nation: proceedings of the symposium marking the 120th anniversary of Mao Zedong's birth, vol. 2 (Central Party Literature Press, 2014)
paras: Written when the 18th Party Congress (2012) had called for an educational campaign on the Party's mass line, Tian Xinming argues that the campaign should rest on a close study of Mao Zedong's thought on the subject. The article's thesis is that Mao was the founder of the Party's mass line, and that the line is a model case of the sinification of Marxism and an original achievement of Marxism adapted to the Chinese context.

The article has three parts. The first traces how the mass line was formulated in Party documents, from the 1981 historical resolution and the Party constitution (in its current wording since 1992) back to the Seventh Congress (1945) and the Eighth Congress (1956). The second examines the attitude half of the formula, "everything for the masses, everything relying on the masses". The third examines the method half, "from the masses, to the masses". Tian draws mainly on Mao's Selected Works, Liu Shaoqi's and Deng Xiaoping's reports on revising the constitution, and Party resolutions.

Tian argues that the mass line applies the Marxist principle that the people are the creators of history to all Party work. On attitude, Mao's statements from the peasant movement to the War of Resistance and the Seventh Congress are read as an expression of this historical-materialist standpoint. On method, Tian links Mao's 1943 decision on leadership to his theory of knowledge in On Practice: leaders gather scattered opinions, turn them into systematic ones, return them to the masses and test them in action. Tian rejects the reading that gives the masses practice and leaders knowledge, and notes that leaders' special functions make it easier for them to lose touch with the masses and decide wrongly. Mao's opposition to both tailism and commandism is presented as guarding against two errors: lagging behind the masses' consciousness and running ahead of it.

Tian concludes that attitude and method are inseparable and together form the complete mass line, which a 1990 Party resolution called the fundamental work line for carrying out the Party's ideological, political and organisational lines. With seeking truth from facts and independence, the mass line is described as part of the living soul of Mao Zedong Thought, and as Mao's most valuable spiritual legacy to the Party. Read the original if you want a documented account of how the mass line entered Party constitutions and how Chinese Party theorists tie it to Mao's epistemology.
quoteEn: The mass line is a model of the sinification of Marxism by Communists represented by Mao Zedong, and a major original achievement of Marxism adapted to China.
quoteZh: 群众路线是毛泽东为代表的中国共产党人把马克思主义中国化的典范，是中国化马克思主义的一个独创性重大成果。

glossary.explanation: The Party's principle of working for and relying on the people and drawing ideas from them in order to lead them. It was developed by Mao Zedong and written into the Party constitution.

glossary.zh: 毛泽东思想的活的灵魂
glossary.pinyin: Máo Zédōng sīxiǎng de huó de línghún
glossary.en: living soul of Mao Zedong Thought
glossary.explanation: A formula from the 1981 Party resolution naming three core elements of Mao Zedong Thought: seeking truth from facts, the mass line and independence.
The error of trailing behind the masses' consciousness and simply accommodating their views, which Mao contrasted with commandism.
The error of issuing orders to the masses beyond their level of consciousness and without their willing consent.
The Party's term for combining Marxism's universal principles with China's concrete conditions, associated especially with Mao Zedong.

t: Uncovering the contemporary value of Mao Zedong Thought
zh: 发掘毛泽东思想的时代价值
source: Chinese Social Sciences Today (Zhongguo shehui kexue bao), published 2018
paras: This is an interview in which Li Jie, a long-time researcher of Mao Zedong, answers four questions from reporters Chao Tianyi and Liu Fang of Chinese Social Sciences Today. The questions ask how researchers should resist historical nihilism, what in Mao Zedong Thought still matters, how to understand the Chinese Dream historically, and why Party and national history should be studied. Li's overall answer is that Mao's errors must be treated honestly but kept distinct from his achievements, and that his method and cultural thinking remain useful guides today.

The interview has four sections. The first deals with historical nihilism and Mao's late-life mistakes. The second names two legacies of Mao: his way of treating Marxism, and his reshaping of traditional culture. The third places the Chinese Dream within a "three hundred years" view of history. The fourth discusses Xi Jinping's call to study Party history and the history of the People's Republic.

On nihilism, Li argues that critics seize on Mao's late errors, inflate them into a question of character, and blame him for the acts of Lin Biao and Jiang Qing. Li holds the errors were serious and unforgivable but were not deliberate "crimes", and says Mao tried to remedy them. Li proposes arguing from facts calmly, not avoiding sensitive questions, and aiming to win public trust rather than defeat opponents. On Marxism, Li says Mao's chief legacy was applying its principles to Chinese conditions. Li summarises this as seeking truth from facts, the mass line and independence, and says the stance, viewpoint and method of Marxism matter more than fixed formulas. On culture, Li credits Mao's call for a national, popular and scientific culture, which rejects both nihilism towards tradition and wholesale Westernisation.

Li describes the first century as running from the Opium War to 1949, the second as building a modern socialist country, and the third as the pursuit of higher-level modernization and better quality. The Chinese Dream, Li says, is inclusive and different from an old imperial self-importance. Li concludes that Party and national history should be told candidly, with achievements as the mainstream and errors as a tributary, and should also serve cultural renewal by honouring heroes and ordinary workers. Read the original if you want to see how a Party historian in 2018 framed Mao's mistakes, his legacy and the Chinese Dream for a general readership.
quoteEn: Although Mao Zedong's errors were unforgivable and major ones, they were by no means deliberate crimes.
quoteZh: 毛泽东的错误尽管不可原谅、是重大错误，但决不是有意为之的罪过。

glossary.explanation: A term used in Chinese Party discourse for views seen as distorting or negating the history of the Party, socialism and revolutionary leaders. It is often applied to critical reassessments of Mao-era history.
A Maoist principle of working method: gather views "from the masses" and return policies "to the masses". The Party still presents it as a basic line of work.
A phrase associated with Mao and later with Deng Xiaoping, which the Party presents as the core of its ideological line. It means proceeding from actual conditions and testing ideas in practice.
A slogan Xi Jinping introduced in 2012, referring to the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation.

t: Eagleton's confirmation of the scientific character of Marxism
zh: 伊格尔顿对马克思主义科学性的印证
source: China Social Sciences Today (Zhongguo shehui kexue bao), 28 June 2018
paras: This short commentary, published in 2018, asks how the British critic Terry Eagleton's work bears on the scientific character of Marxism.
